The solid brick exhibited the highest thermal load, with an energy demand of 191.78 Wh·m⁻², whereas the air- and glass-wool-filled bricks reduced this value to 84.90 and 73.80 Wh·m⁻², respectively. Among the investigated PCMs, RT30 achieved the best balance between latent-heat activation and thermal regulation, with an energy demand of 77.90 Wh·m⁻² and a maximum liquid fraction of 0.45. RT26 melted completely but activated too early, while RT34 reached a maximum liquid fraction of only 0.27 and increased energy demand to 96.50 Wh·m⁻². Increasing the cavity number from 8 to 12 reduced the transmitted heat flux by up to 57.65% under the investigated configurations. Overall, glass wool provided the lowest energy demand, while PCM performance depended strongly on the compatibility between its melting range, cavity geometry, and imposed thermal cycle.

title: Spinel MnFe2O4 nanoparticles with improved surface area and charge transfer characteristics for next-generation supercapacitors
source: Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology
summary: The growing demand for sustainable and efficient energy storage devices has accelerated the development of advanced electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors. In this work, MnFe₂O₄ nanoparticles were successfully synthesized
content: The growing demand for sustainable and efficient energy storage devices has accelerated the development of advanced electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors. In this work, MnFe₂O₄ nanoparticles were successfully synthesized through a novel green co-precipitation approach using Curcuma longa extract as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of highly crystalline spinel MnFe₂O₄ with an average crystallite size of 19.9 nm and excellent phase purity. Raman spectroscopy further validated the characteristic vibrational modes of the spinel ferrite structure, while BET analysis revealed an enhanced surface area with mesoporous characteristics favorable for ion diffusion. SEM images demonstrated porous cauliflower-like interconnected morphology, and EDX confirmed the homogeneous distribution of Mn, Fe, and O elements without impurities. Electrochemical studies exhibited remarkable pseudocapacitive behavior with a high specific capacitance of 295 F g⁻¹ at 0.8 A g⁻¹ and 87.3% capacitance retention after 5000 charge–discharge cycles. Furthermore, EIS analysis revealed low charge transfer resistance and enhanced ion diffusion kinetics, confirming the strong potential of green-synthesized MnFe₂O₄ for sustainable next-generation supercapacitor applications.

title: Global distributions and environmental correlates of community leaf length and width in forests
summary: Leaf length and width are key dimensions of tree leaf size and can influence leaf boundary-layer development and leaf-environment heat exchange. However, their global patterns and environmental correlates remain poorly understood. By integr
content: Leaf length and width are key dimensions of tree leaf size and can influence leaf boundary-layer development and leaf-environment heat exchange. However, their global patterns and environmental correlates remain poorly understood. By integrating tree leaf traits and community data, we mapped community leaf length and width and identified their environmental correlates in global forests. Both community leaf length and width decreased toward higher latitudes, although leaf width showed an additional peak at mid-latitudes. These asynchronous patterns contributed to geographic variation in leaf shape, with more elongated leaves in tropical and boreal forests and relatively rounder leaves in temperate forests. Soil variables and mean annual temperature were the main correlates of leaf length, whereas leaf width was mainly associated with temperature. Our results reveal distinct environmental correlates of community leaf length and width, highlight the value of multiple leaf dimensions for predicting forest distributions and function, and identify tropical regions where additional trait data are needed to reduce uncertainty.

title: Towards standardised development of palaeofire charcoal reference sets via muffle furnace pyrolysis for Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
summary: Background The application of Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to subfossilised charcoal preserved in natural archives has been shown to be a useful technique to better understand historical fire (i.e. palaeofire) conditions.
content: Background The application of Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to subfossilised charcoal preserved in natural archives has been shown to be a useful technique to better understand historical fire (i.e. palaeofire) conditions. The reliability of FTIR analyses in palaeoecological studies is contingent on the robustness of charcoal reference sets, many of which are produced via muffle furnace pyrolysis under varying methodologies. Aim We tested how various methodological approaches influence FTIR spectral signatures, using dried plant material (leaves and branches) derived from Eucalyptus camaldulensis. Methods Methods evaluated included the preparation (e.g. milled or unmilled), containment (e.g. aluminium foil or container) and cooling (e.g. internal or external) of the modern reference material. Key results We found that methodological approaches substantially influence FTIR signatures and subsequent classification accuracies, determined via leave-one-out centroid matching, varying by nearly 30% between approaches. Conclusions We suggest that loosely containing samples in aluminium foil, using sand mediums (e.g. 50.00 ± 0.05 g and a grain size of 250–500 μm) for thermal buffering and immediately removing samples from the muffle furnace for cooling are preferred protocols for generating reference sets via muffle furnace pyrolysis. Implications This study highlights the critical importance of methodological transparency and standardised methodological protocols in developing charcoal reference sets for palaeofire analyses.

title: Proteomic profiling of Camelus dromedarius blood leukocytes using protein sequence database searches and de novo peptide sequencing
source: Journal of King Saud University - Science
summary: There is a lack of studies on the crude leukocyte proteome of camels. Therefore, we hypothesized that camel leukocytes could be a source of bioactive peptides that have not been studied before. Here, we present the first comprehensive prote
content: There is a lack of studies on the crude leukocyte proteome of camels. Therefore, we hypothesized that camel leukocytes could be a source of bioactive peptides that have not been studied before. Here, we present the first comprehensive proteomic analysis of dromedary camel crude leukocyte-derived polypeptides (CLDP) using both protein sequence database searches (PSD) and de novo peptide sequencing (DPS) to improve peptide identification and coverage. The crude protein was extracted and analyzed by LC-MS/MS, followed by identification of protein and peptide sequences through PSD and DPS. PSD identified 120 proteins based on the Camelus dromedarius and Sus scrofa databases, while DPS identified a total of 830 peptides with an average local confidence (ALC) of 95% or higher. Gene Ontology (GO) annotation and KEGG analysis highlighted terms associated with stress adaptation, extracellular signaling, and immune response. However, DPS exhibited a broader and more pronounced enrichment trend, particularly in relation to the immune system.

title: Grayscale Photomasks Enable Noncontact Optical Patterning of Hydroxypropyl Cellulose Gels for Dynamic Art
summary: ABSTRACT Hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) forms cholesteric photonic gels with dynamic structural color, but most HPC systems are tuned globally or patterned through serial fabrication. Here we report a mask‐encoded parallel photonic manufactu
content: ABSTRACT Hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) forms cholesteric photonic gels with dynamic structural color, but most HPC systems are tuned globally or patterned through serial fabrication. Here we report a mask‐encoded parallel photonic manufacturing strategy that locally regulates the reflected wavelength of acrylamide‐containing HPC (AM‐HPC) photonic gels. UV‐induced photopolymerization produces a dose‐dependent blueshift consistent with cholesteric‐pitch compression, yielding a 204 nm (662–458 nm) tuning window in 68 wt.% AM‐HPC under time‐controlled exposure and spatial features down to 50 µm. To translate this response into programmable manufacturing, we combine Gaussian‐process active‐learning calibration with an experimentally measured mask‐opacity‐to‐UV transfer function. This workflow converts two‐dimensional target wavelength fields into grayscale optical masks, enabling spatially varying UV doses to be delivered simultaneously across a continuous, unsegmented gel. A single 10 s exposure produced multilevel structural‐color images with an 85 µm mask‐pixel pitch (13 840 pixels cm − 2 ) in a continuous gel. The patterned gels retain thermally responsive structural color, allowing dynamic modulation of encoded images. These results establish a proof‐of‐concept digital‐to‐material workflow for parallel, composition‐specific programming of apparent structural color in continuous HPC photonic gels.

title: Modifications of Fiber Surface and Resin Matrix on Enhancing Interfacial Strength of UV ‐ CIPP Materials
summary: ABSTRACT Ultraviolet‐cured‐in‐place‐pipe (UV‐CIPP) technology is widely used for trenchless rehabilitation of urban pipelines. However, the multilayered liner structure is prone to debonding and delamination due to weak interfacial bonding
content: ABSTRACT Ultraviolet‐cured‐in‐place‐pipe (UV‐CIPP) technology is widely used for trenchless rehabilitation of urban pipelines. However, the multilayered liner structure is prone to debonding and delamination due to weak interfacial bonding between fibers and the resin matrix. To address this issue, microdroplet pull‐out tests were conducted on glass fiber/UV‐curable resin systems to investigate the effects of fiber surface silanization and resin matrix filler modification on interfacial properties. The surface morphology, roughness, and chemical composition of glass fibers were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Three‐point bending tests were performed on laminated specimens to validate the translation of microscale interfacial improvements to macroscopic bending performance. The preferred curing parameters were determined as 150 s and 60 mW/cm 2 . For the three strategies, interfacial shear strength (IFSS) exhibited a non‐monotonic trend with increasing modification extent. KH560 treatment for 9 h yielded a maximum IFSS of 20.63 ± 1.63 MPa among the silane‐modified groups, accompanied by an increase in surface roughness Ra from 0.273 to 0.396 nm, as revealed by AFM, and successful silane grafting, as confirmed by XPS. For resin matrix modification, the preferred MgO content was 3.5 wt%, achieving an IFSS of 20.80 ± 1.88 MPa, while the preferred nano‐SiO 2 content was 3 wt%, achieving an IFSS of 22.70 ± 1.39 MPa. The bending tests confirmed that enhanced interfacial bonding translated into improved flexural performance, with the ranking of reinforcing effectiveness consistent with the microscale results.

title: Tailoring Carbon Vacancies by Conformational Pre‐Organization Enables Hard Carbon Anodes Toward Ultra‐Long Cycle Life
summary: ABSTRACT Hard carbon is regarded as the most promising anode material for sodium‐ion batteries; however, its intrinsically sluggish kinetics and unstable electrode/electrolyte interphase during cycling fundamentally restrict its rate capabi
content: ABSTRACT Hard carbon is regarded as the most promising anode material for sodium‐ion batteries; however, its intrinsically sluggish kinetics and unstable electrode/electrolyte interphase during cycling fundamentally restrict its rate capability and cycling stability. To overcome these issues, we propose a strategy for tailoring carbon vacancies via conformational pre‐organization of the precursor architecture. Specifically, impurity atoms in the precursor serve as anchoring sites to introduce carbon vacancies that facilitate rapid Na + diffusion. Owing to their localized negative charges, these vacancies preferentially capture Na + while excluding coordinating solvents, homogenizing the interfacial electric field, and diminishing the charge‐transfer resistance. This synergistic effect reinforces interfacial stability and promotes low‐temperature ion‐transport kinetics, leading to markedly improved rate capability and cycling durability. Consequently, the optimized hard carbon anodes deliver an ultra‐long cycle life, achieving 16 000 and 10 000 cycles at 1.0 and 5.0 A g −1 , respectively. Even at −20°C, the advanced anode maintains a capacity retention of 92.40% after 800 cycles at 0.1 A g −1 , further demonstrating its excellent cycling stability. Furthermore, the full cells assembled with Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 retain 79.74% of their initial capacity after 3200 cycles at 10C. This work establishes a design paradigm for engineering hard carbon anodes with ultra‐long cycling durability.

title: Tuning the structure-piezoelectric property relationship in electrospun PLLA nanofibers through collector-induced fiber alignment
summary: Electrospinning has become one of the most common methods to fabricate piezoelectric polymer nanofibers for flexible electronics, sensors, energy harvesting devices, and bioelectronic scaffolds. Fiber alignment is one of many parameters tha
content: Electrospinning has become one of the most common methods to fabricate piezoelectric polymer nanofibers for flexible electronics, sensors, energy harvesting devices, and bioelectronic scaffolds. Fiber alignment is one of many parameters that can impact nanofiber performance attributes since alignment affects mechanical anisotropy, crystal organization, and piezoelectric response. Nonetheless, few published works provide an in-depth discussion of collector rotation speed as it impacts nanofiber alignment, leaving detailed and reproducible methods for tuning alignment-dependent piezoelectric performance largely unreported. Here, we report a standardized electrospinning protocol to reproducibly fabricate piezoelectric nanofibers with controlled alignment through tuning the speed of a rotating collector. The steps in this protocol include preparing polymer solutions, setting up an electrospinning system, determining collector speed, collecting fibers, performing optional post-processing steps, and quantitatively evaluating fiber morphology and piezoelectric response. The protocol was validated through quantification of fiber alignment using scanning electron microscopy coupled with image-based orientation metrics, and piezoelectric performance through quantification of electrical output and piezoelectric coefficients. We demonstrated that increasing collector rotation speed from 1000 to 4000 rpm reduced orientation spread from 19.57° to 11.23°, and showed this increase in alignment was associated with an increase in the effective piezoelectric coefficient (d33) from 3.37 pC/N to 5.92 pC/N and an increase in open-circuit voltage output from 15 mV to 35 mV. These results highlight how the provided protocol enables users to reproducibly tune nanofiber orientation and associated piezoelectric performance. This protocol can aid in the design of scaffolds with tunable properties, wearable sensors, and mechanically-triggered energy harvesting devices.

title: System‐Local Axes and Metabolic Reprogramming From Health to Response in House Dust Mite‐Specific Subcutaneous Immunotherapy for Allergic Rhinitis
summary: ABSTRACT Allergic rhinitis (AR) features mucosal inflammation and systemic immune activation; the coordination of local and circulating metabolism during disease and immunotherapy is unclear. We performed untargeted LC‐MS metabolomics on pa
content: ABSTRACT Allergic rhinitis (AR) features mucosal inflammation and systemic immune activation; the coordination of local and circulating metabolism during disease and immunotherapy is unclear. We performed untargeted LC‐MS metabolomics on paired plasma and nasal secretion samples from 28 house dust mite (HDM)‐induced AR patients before and after 6 months of subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT), together with 19 healthy controls. Over 1800 annotated metabolites revealed compartmentalized metabolic reprogramming in AR. Nasal secretions displayed disrupted lipid, steroid, and redox metabolism linked to epithelial injury and local inflammation, while plasma had altered nucleotide and NAD + metabolism reflecting systemic type 2 inflammatory stress. After clinically effective SCIT, metabolic profiles shifted toward healthy status, with nasal metabolites showing stronger treatment‑associated changes. Two exploratory candidate axes were observed: a plasma nucleotide/NAD + axis potentially reflecting systemic immunometabolic burden, and a nasal lipid‐steroid‐redox axis possibly linked to mucosal remission, yielding candidate features that may support future longitudinal surveillance. Combined local and systemic metabolomics reveals asynchronous yet coordinated immunometabolic remodeling throughout AR onset and SCIT intervention, providing candidate features for future development of noninvasive strategies to assess disease activity and therapeutic response.

title: Multifunctional Fe, N Co-Doped Microporous Carbons Derived from Conjugated Microporous Polymer Containing Tetraphenylethylene and Iron-Chelated 1,10-Phenanthroline Units as Platforms for CO2 Uptake, Supercapacitor, and Oxygen Evolution Reaction
summary: Abstract The development of multifunctional microporous carbons for integrated electrochemical energy storage, CO2 capture, and oxygen evolution electrocatalysis (OEECs) is an attractive approach for sustainable energy applications. In this
content: Abstract The development of multifunctional microporous carbons for integrated electrochemical energy storage, CO2 capture, and oxygen evolution electrocatalysis (OEECs) is an attractive approach for sustainable energy applications. In this work, Fe/N codoped porous carbons (TPE-PhenFe-CMP-700 and TPE-PhenFe-CMP-800) were synthesized from a tailor-made conjugated microporous polymer (CMP) precursor prepared through a Sonogashira–Hagihara cross-coupling reaction between an ethynyl-functionalized tetraphenylethylene (TPE-T) linker and an iron-chelated 3,8-dibromo-1,10-phenanthroline (Phen-Fe-2Br) monomer. The molecularly engineered precursor enables well-distributed Fe and N species throughout the carbon framework after carbonization. Among the materials obtained, TPE-PhenFe-CMP-800 exhibits a SBET of 411 m2 g–1 and a well-developed porous graphitic structure. The synergistic combination of porosity-enhanced graphitic carbon networks and the presence of Fe–N active sites endows the material with outstanding multifunctional performance. The TPE-PhenFe-CMP-800 delivers high specific capacitance (Cs) of 892 F g–1 at 0.5 A g–1, in a three-electrode supercapacitor (SCs) configuration, together with excellent CO2 adsorption of 4.01 mmol g–1 at 273 K. Furthermore, TPE-PhenFe-CMP-800 exhibits outstanding OER electrocatalytic activity, demonstrating an overpotential as low as 530 mV to reach 10 mA cm–2, along with a favorable Tafel slope of 82 mV dec–1 and an extensive electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of 76 cm2. These results demonstrate that molecular engineering of CMP precursors provides an effective strategy for constructing multifunctional Fe/N codoped porous carbons, offering a versatile platform for advanced electrochemical energy storage, CO2 capture, and electrocatalytic applications.

title: High-resolution reconstruction of redox changes using XRF core scanner: depth-transect redox changes in the Japan Sea during the Quaternary
source: Progress in Earth and Planetary Science
summary: Abstract The reconstruction of past marine bottom-water redox conditions are crucial because it reflects changes in ocean circulation, surface productivity, and the precipitation–evaporation balance. However, long-term (Myr scale), high-res
content: Abstract The reconstruction of past marine bottom-water redox conditions are crucial because it reflects changes in ocean circulation, surface productivity, and the precipitation–evaporation balance. However, long-term (Myr scale), high-resolution (mm scale), redox reconstructions remain scarce because traditional discrete-sample analyses are highly time-consuming. While the Japan Sea is known for past high-frequency fluctuations of deep-water redox conditions, the existing records are limited to the past 640 kyr at a relatively low resolution. In this study, we propose a novel method for estimating deep-water redox conditions using high-resolution XRF core scanning data and apply it to reconstruct Quaternary deep-water redox changes in the Japan Sea. First, we developed an XRF core scanner-based, high-throughput method that drastically accelerates the estimation of past deep-water oxygenation. We utilized XRF core scanner-derived Br/S, Fe/Ti, and Fe/S ratios, which are substitutes for the conventional redox-sensitive parameters C/S ratio, Fe/Al ratio, and degree of pyritization (DOP) respectively, for classification of deep-water redox conditions into four ranks. Then, we applied this method to a depth transect in the Japan Sea consisting of three sediment cores (~ 1000, ~2000, and ~3000 m water depths) from the Japan Sea. Our ultra high-resolution (mm scale) data reveal that deep-water redox conditions fluctuated from euxinic to oxic at ~cm scales. The depth-transect approach traces past expansion of oxygen minimum zone in some periods, which could be an analog for modern deoxygenation under global warming. Furthermore, in certain layers, redox conditions shifted progressively toward a less reducing state within centimeter-scale interval, which corresponds a few kyr. These fine scale redox changes could be detected only by using our new ITRAX-based redox rank classification method, because high-resolution sampling was difficult for conventional methods. Our new ITRAX-based redox rank classification method can be applied to other sediments obtained from different areas to advance our understanding of redox changes in the past.

title: Fine-tuning the energy level of defect states in doped ultrathin carbon nitride polymer for enhanced photocatalytic performance
summary: The mechanisms governing photo-induced electron behavior and its link to visible light responsiveness in graphitic carbon nitride (CN), particularly doped or defective variants, remain poorly understood. This study presents a strategy for b
content: The mechanisms governing photo-induced electron behavior and its link to visible light responsiveness in graphitic carbon nitride (CN), particularly doped or defective variants, remain poorly understood. This study presents a strategy for band structure modulation in carbon-doped CN through isomeric modulation of benzene dicarboxylic acid dopant precursors. Ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) absorption, photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations were employed to determine the energy band structure, while time-resolved spectra probed carrier dynamics across different timescales. Isophthalic acid-doped carbon nitride (IPCN) exhibits a narrowly distributed defect energy level. This manifests in a tailless UV-vis absorption profile and a sharp PL emission peak in the visible region. In contrast, terephthalic acid-doped carbon nitride (PPCN) displays multiple, continuously distributed defect levels. This results in band-edge absorption overlapping with a broad visible spectrum and a broadened PL emission peak, arising from the superposition of band-edge transitions and low-energy absorption tails. The defect levels with continuous distribution in PPCN enhance electrical conductivity but also promotes charge recombination. Conversely, the defect states in IPCN provide a suitable thermodynamic driving force for carrier migration to catalytic active site, in addition to promote spatial charge carrier separation. Consequently, visible-light CO 2 reduction and H 2 evolution activities of carbon-doped CN are markedly enhanced. This work elucidates the synergistic balance between optical absorption efficiency and charge separation performance in doped CN, providing experimental validation for the rational design of CN-based photocatalysts with superior optical and catalytic properties.

title: Organosolv lignin from corncob for developing Pickering emulsion: A comparative study of lignin nanoparticles and chitosan-coated lignin nanoparticles
summary: There is an increasing interest in the sustainable production of materials from lignocellulosic biomass due to the environmental concerns associated with non-renewable fossil resources. Lignin, an abundant biopolymer, has attracted attentio
content: There is an increasing interest in the sustainable production of materials from lignocellulosic biomass due to the environmental concerns associated with non-renewable fossil resources. Lignin, an abundant biopolymer, has attracted attention for the preparation of nanoparticles with potential applications in emulsion stabilization. In this work, organosolv lignin obtained from corncob was used to produce lignin nanoparticles (LNPs) and chitosan-coated lignin nanoparticles (chi-LNPs). LNPs were produced at lignin concentrations of 0.39 mg/mL and 3.3 mg/mL, resulting in colloidal dispersions with relatively narrow size distributions and low polydispersity index (PDI). Coating with chitosan greatly impacted the LNPs’ charge, size and PDI, increased the contact angle, but did not significantly affect surface tension. Both nanoparticle systems were subsequently evaluated as Pickering emulsion stabilizers using different oil-in-water- ratios. The results showed that both systems were effective in stabilizing the emulsions, while chi-LNPs generally produced smaller median droplet sizes, particularly at intermediate and high nanoparticle concentrations. However, no consistent trend was observed for the distribution width. Overall, these findings suggest that chitosan coating can improve the emulsifying performance of LNPs under specific formulation conditions and support the use of surface-modified LNPs as bio-based stabilizers for Pickering emulsions.

title: Pedro Carrere. Un japonista español en el México finisecular: colección, mediación y práctica artística
summary: Historiography of Japonisme in Latin America has logically prioritized the study of prominent figures such as José Juan Tablada, leaving the role of cultural mediators whose influence proved decisive yet to be examined. Among them, Pedro Ca
content: Historiography of Japonisme in Latin America has logically prioritized the study of prominent figures such as José Juan Tablada, leaving the role of cultural mediators whose influence proved decisive yet to be examined. Among them, Pedro Carrere stands out; however, his diplomatic career and collecting activities have lacked a systematic reconstruction until now. To address this gap, the present study proposes a biography constructed from archival records and an indirect approach to his figure through the analysis of testimonies, periodical sources, and, specifically, graphic materials linked to his milieu. The hypothesis posits that Carrere’s library and collection functioned as a fundamental node for the circulation of Japanese visual repertoires in late 19th-century Mexico, playing a key role in Tablada’s aesthetic formation. From this perspective, Japonisme is understood not as a passive reception of Oriental models, but as a process of mediated cultural transfer in which objects—particularly illustrated books—operate as active vectors of visual reinterpretation.

title: Prediction of dynamic retention during polymer flooding EOR in carbonate outcrops using empirical correlation
summary: Polymer retention is a critical parameter in polymer flooding and requires accurate measurement for successful field implementation. However, coreflood tests for measuring dynamic polymer retention are time-consuming, costly, and labor-inte
content: Polymer retention is a critical parameter in polymer flooding and requires accurate measurement for successful field implementation. However, coreflood tests for measuring dynamic polymer retention are time-consuming, costly, and labor-intensive, motivating the application of correlations that map readily measurable static adsorption to dynamic retention. In this study, 36 coreflooding and 36 static adsorption tests were conducted on carbonate outcrops and crushed powder, respectively, under identical conditions to determine dynamic retention and static adsorption values. Existing mathematical correlations in the literature for predicting dynamic retention, primarily developed for sandstone outcrops under single-phase conditions, were fitted to the current dataset. In addition, empirical equations and regression models were developed to predict dynamic retention values from parameters influencing polymer retention, including static adsorption values, residual oil saturation, and the size ratio factor. An 80:20 train-test split and leave-one-out cross-validation were employed to evaluate the predictive performance of the regression models. The experimental dataset showed poor agreement with the existing correlations, primarily due to differences in rock type. Further, both a simple regression equation with static adsorption as the sole influencing parameter and a multiple linear regression equation incorporating additional parameters, including residual oil saturation and the size ratio factor, were developed to predict dynamic retention. The empirical equations demonstrated a strong fit to the experimental dataset, achieving R² values of 0.93 and 0.96, respectively. All regression models performed well in predicting dynamic retention from the influencing parameters, with R² testing values of at least 0.97.

title: A melatonin textile transdermal patch based on physicochemical synergistic permeation-enhancement strategy for circadian rhythm regulation
summary: Melatonin, an endogenous circadian rhythm-regulating hormone, has faced challenges in achieving prolonged exogenous regulation due to its low oral bioavailability and short half-life. Existing transdermal strategies are difficult to balance
content: Melatonin, an endogenous circadian rhythm-regulating hormone, has faced challenges in achieving prolonged exogenous regulation due to its low oral bioavailability and short half-life. Existing transdermal strategies are difficult to balance efficacy, safety, and accessibility. To address this, we propose a physicochemical synergistic permeation-enhancement strategy and have developed a melatonin textile transdermal patch based on the synergistic action of electret and permeation enhancer. The patch is designed with a three-layer composite structure, composed of a textile-based electret backing layer, a drug-loading pressure sensitive adhesive layer containing melatonin and permeation enhancer, and a protective layer to prevent drug leakage. Electret and permeation enhancer enhance transdermal efficiency through a physicochemical synergistic permeation-enhancement strategy without disrupting the skin barrier. In vitro studies revealed that among various permeation enhancers (menthol, azone, oleic acid) and electret parameters, the combination of a −1500 V electret with 10% oleic acid exhibited the optimal synergistic effect. In vivo pharmacokinetic studies demonstrated that the patch reached a peak plasma concentration (>30 ng/mL) within 1 h and maintained effective therapeutic levels (>5 ng/mL) for up to 8 h. The patch significantly improved the sleep quality in insomniac rats, with no observed skin irritation or cytotoxicity. This study not only accomplishes an efficient, non-invasive, and parametrically tunable transdermal delivery of melatonin but also validates the feasibility of synergistic enhancement through physical field regulation and chemical permeation, thereby providing a viable strategy for developing safe and long-acting textile-based transdermal drug delivery systems aimed at neuroendocrine small-molecule hormones similar to melatonin.

title: Occupancy-driven attenuation in radiation-sensitive chromatin domains as a statistical-mechanical model of the overkill effect and RBE maximum
summary: The reduction in biological effectiveness at high linear energy transfer (LET), commonly referred to as the overkill effect, remains an active area of investigation in high-LET radiobiology. Here, we present a statistical-mechanical framewo
content: The reduction in biological effectiveness at high linear energy transfer (LET), commonly referred to as the overkill effect, remains an active area of investigation in high-LET radiobiology. Here, we present a statistical-mechanical framework in which attenuation emerges from the progressive occupancy of a finite population of radiation-sensitive chromatin domains. An effective free-energy formalism is used to describe the equilibrium occupancy state, yielding an LET-dependent occupancy fraction and an attenuation function representing the fraction of chromatin domains remaining available for the formation of additional biologically independent lethal events. The model predicts a continuous occupancy transition accompanied by a fluctuation maximum, identifying a characteristic LET range in which occupancy effects become most pronounced. When combined with a previously published LET-dependent damage-production model for carbon-ion irradiation of V79 cells, the framework predicts a maximum in lethal-lesion yield followed by a decline despite continued increases in damage production. The qualitative comparison of the RBE data in published works reveals the typical pattern of growth, peak value, and decline of the biological effectiveness, although the predicted values of the RBE continue to be lower than the experimental ones. These results suggest that finite chromatin-domain occupancy may provide a possible physical interpretation of attenuation, the overkill effect, and the emergence of an RBE maximum.

title: Point-of-use water treatment technology: Effects of increased daily production, associated risks, overall feasibility, and two post-treatment disinfection alternatives
summary: Increasing daily water production while maintaining feasible operation is still a challenge in point-of-use (POU) systems based on household slow sand filtration. This study addresses a POU system for surface water treatment constructed and
content: Increasing daily water production while maintaining feasible operation is still a challenge in point-of-use (POU) systems based on household slow sand filtration. This study addresses a POU system for surface water treatment constructed and operated for 141 days towards an initial target production of 100 L.d −1 , a volume not yet reported for that type of system. The system comprised a pre-treatment (sedimentation and blanket filtration), a household slow sand filter operated under continuous flow (HSSF-C), and two independent post-treatment units (chlorination and UV irradiation). The target production of 100 L.d −1 was maintained only on the first daily, with an average of 69 ± 17 L.d −1 , and the increased production required adjustments that extended filter run times from 3 to 30 days. Turbidity and true colour removal were 78.41 ± 21% and 48.14 ± 30% for POU with chlorination and 78.48 ± 21% and 46 ± 28% for POU with Ultraviolet (UV) irradiation unit, respectively. Escherichia coli reduction was 2.50 ± 0.37 log, regardless of the post-treatment applied. Additionally, the POU systems produced treated water with statistical differences in terms of total coliforms (3.48 ± 0.61 for chlorination and 3.70 ± 0.53 log for UV) and aerobic spore-forming bacteria (ASFB) (1.81 ± 0.73 for chlorination and 2.44 ± 0.48 log for UV). HSSF-C reduced 2.60 ± 0.17 log of Giardia lamblia cysts and 1.97 ± 0.59 log of Cryptosporidium parvum oocysts, proving to be a barrier against those protozoa. Risk assessment involving constructed structure and system operation classified the most hazards as “low” to “very high”; however, the required control measures can be simple and easily implemented by end users.

title: Impacts of Edge AI/agentic AI on supply chain management and operations research
summary: Abstract Edge AI refers to the deployment and execution of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms on decentralized, local computing devices (e.g., Internet of Things) rather than relying on centralized cloud‐based computing infrastructures
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: Abstract Edge AI refers to the deployment and execution of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms on decentralized, local computing devices (e.g., Internet of Things) rather than relying on centralized cloud‐based computing infrastructures. The literature has addressed the increasing importance of AI in supply chain and operations management (SCOM), specifically in learning‐based, generative, and agentic AI, as well as digital twins. However, the area of Edge AI has not yet received a theoretical framing and conceptualization in SCOM. In this paper, we discuss the impacts of Edge AI on SCOM. We begin with an analysis of AI in SCOM, focusing on learning‐based, generative, agentic AI, and digital twins. We then detail Edge AI's impacts on SCOM across Digital SCOR functions: orchestration, fulfillment and ordering, planning, sourcing, regeneration, synchronization, and transformation. We also analyze organizational transformations that Edge AI might trigger. Specifically, we discuss interactions of agentic AI and Edge AI, an integration of local and centralized decision‐making, and deployment scenarios of Edge AI use in SCOM, focusing on production planning and control, intralogistics, and supply chain resilience. Risks and challenges of the new technology are considered as well. Impacts of Edge AI on supply chain and operations research are discussed. We conclude that Edge AI is a crucial part of the unfolding Industry 6.0 revolution that, in combination with agentic AI, provides a technology to implement decentralized, autonomously planned and controlled supply chain, production, and logistics processes, materializing in Industry 6.0 with AI across all layers of value‐added chains.

title: Multiscale mechanobiology of circulating tumor cells: microfluidics and atomic force microscopy
source: Frontiers in Lab on a Chip Technologies
summary: Cancer progression is shaped by coupled molecular, biochemical, and mechanical changes across multiple scales, from altered signaling and cytoskeletal organization to cellular deformation, adhesion, and metastatic dissemination. Circulating
content: Cancer progression is shaped by coupled molecular, biochemical, and mechanical changes across multiple scales, from altered signaling and cytoskeletal organization to cellular deformation, adhesion, and metastatic dissemination. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are rare and heterogeneous in blood, occurring as single cells and multicellular clusters that provide access to evolving tumor phenotypes through liquid biopsy. Their apparent elasticity, deformability, adhesion, and viscoelastic behavior may reflect invasive potential, treatment response, and phenotypic state, while cytoskeletal proteins, membrane lipids, cell surface glycans, and receptors provide molecular context for these mechanical signatures. This review examines the complementary roles of microfluidics and atomic force microscopy (AFM) in multiscale CTC mechanobiology. Microfluidic platforms support label-free and affinity-based enrichment, capture, positioning, and recovery of viable cells. AFM provides localized measurements of apparent elasticity, deformation, adhesion, viscoelastic response, and nanoscale surface architecture in liquid, while functionalized probes enable molecular recognition and molecule-specific force measurements. We evaluate physical, affinity-based, cluster-preserving, open-space, and artificial intelligence-assisted microfluidic strategies together with reversible device assembly, automated AFM targeting, fluidic probes, advanced mapping modes, and treatment-response applications. Existing studies establish feasibility, including direct AFM measurements of individual patient-derived CTCs and automated analysis following microfluidic enrichment in model rare-cell mixtures. Clinical evidence remains limited, many integrated workflows rely on cultured cells or spiked samples, and within the literature identified in this review, direct AFM characterization of intact patient-derived CTC clusters was not found. Clinical translation will require confirmation of tumor identity, standardized acquisition, analysis, and reporting, increased throughput, statistical analysis that preserves the hierarchy of patients, cells, and force curves, and validation in independent patient cohorts. Integrated AFM-microfluidic platforms could extend CTC liquid biopsy beyond enumeration toward functional mechanobiological analysis relevant to metastasis, therapeutic response, and biomarker development.

title: Neurodevelopment as blueprint: biological validation of the dual-architecture AGI framework
summary: Human intelligence does not develop linearly: it follows a precise phase sequence. This article presents the hypothesis that this neurodevelopmental timeline corresponds to the dual-architecture artificial general intelligence (AGI) system
content: Human intelligence does not develop linearly: it follows a precise phase sequence. This article presents the hypothesis that this neurodevelopmental timeline corresponds to the dual-architecture artificial general intelligence (AGI) system previously proposed by the author, covering the 10 architectural components. We hypothesize that AGI development may be constrained by similar phase sequencing, address key objections (see Sections 3.1 , 5.4 , 5.5 , and 5.6 for explicit objection-response pairs) through formal arguments, and provide indirect supporting evidence for six individual mechanisms on the MuJoCo platform: four-method anti-forgetting comparison: elastic weight consolidation (EWC), synaptic intelligence (SI), memory-aware synapses (MAS), and Naive. Curiosity-driven exploration, training stability analysis, multimodal cross-prediction, and warm-start routing analysis reveal negative transfer in genuinely novel scenarios, and a multi-novelty gradient experiment spanning five gravity levels (1.0×–2.0×) identifies a crossover threshold at approximately 1.25×–1.50× gravity on HalfCheetah-v5. An appendix provides a formal mathematical theory of token migration with two formal sketches and one implication.

title: Mode‐Selective C═C and C─N Vibrational Coupling Modulates Nonradiative Decay in Regioisomeric Organic Phosphorescent Emission
summary: Structural isomerization has emerged as an effective strategy for improving the performance of organic room-temperature phosphorescent materials, but reported explanations are mainly attributed to differences in molecular packing, spin-orbi
content: Structural isomerization has emerged as an effective strategy for improving the performance of organic room-temperature phosphorescent materials, but reported explanations are mainly attributed to differences in molecular packing, spin-orbit coupling, excited-state electronic configurations, etc. The intrinsic vibrational differences encoded in the molecular structures of isomers, which may fundamentally govern triplet-state excitons' nonradiative behaviors, remain largely unexplored. Here, we construct five phosphorescent molecular structural isomerization pairs based on both purely hydrocarbon and heteroatom-containing aromatic compounds, elucidating how regioisomerization redistributes local aromatic character and skeletal rigidity, thereby selectively suppressing the dominant dissipative vibrational modes (C═C and C─N) in the triplet state. This selective vibrational restriction effectively reduces nonradiative decay loss and ultimately determines the efficiency and lifetime of triplet excitons. The representative regioisomeric phosphor further demonstrates long-lived bioimaging capability with an extended in vivo imaging window, highlighting the practical relevance of this design strategy. This work identifies dominant vibrational coordinates as the primary origin of isomer-dependent RTP behaviors and establishes a vibrationally resolved mechanistic framework for excited-state relaxation engineering.

title: Optimizing physiological performance, assimilate partitioning and productivity of late-sown wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) through mepiquat chloride application under nitrogen enrichment
summary: Introduction Late sowing constrains grain yield formation in wheat by shortening the duration of post-anthesis assimilate accumulation and limiting the effective utilization of source-derived assimilates during grain filling. Optimizing nit
content: Introduction Late sowing constrains grain yield formation in wheat by shortening the duration of post-anthesis assimilate accumulation and limiting the effective utilization of source-derived assimilates during grain filling. Optimizing nitrogen nutrition and growth regulation could help maintain physiological activity, sink development and grain productivity under late-sown conditions. Methods This two-year field study evaluated the effects of nitrogen fertilization and mepiquat chloride application on physiological responses, assimilate partitioning and grain yield of late-sown wheat in north-western India. Nitrogen treatments comprised 100% (M1), 125% (M2) and 150% (M3) of the recommended dose of nitrogen (RDN), while growth regulation treatments included an untreated control (S1), mepiquat chloride at 750 ppm at maximum tillering (S2), flag leaf (S3) and both stages (S4), and 1000 ppm at maximum tillering (S5), flag leaf (S6) and both stages (S7). Results Nitrogen fertilization significantly increased grain yield compared with 100% RDN (M1), while 125% RDN (M2) and 150% RDN (M3) produced statistically comparable grain yields during both years. Grain yield under M2 was 48.1 and 49.1 q ha -1 , compared with 43.7 and 45.7 q ha -1 under M1, representing increases of 10.1 and 7.4%, respectively, whereas M3 recorded 50.4 and 51.9 q ha -1 , corresponding to increases of 15.3 and 13.6%, respectively, over M1 during 2023–24 and 2024–25. Among growth regulation treatments, dual-stage application of mepiquat chloride at 750 ppm (S4) recorded grain yields of 50.2 and 51.8 q ha -1 during 2023-24 and 2024-25, respectively, and remained statistically comparable with the corresponding 1000 ppm treatment (S7). S4 also increased harvest index by 11.7-13.2% compared with the untreated control (S1), with values similar to S7 in both years. Discussion Higher nitrogen supply and dual-stage mepiquat chloride application were associated with improved physiological activity, sink capacity and assimilate partitioning toward grains during grain filling. These findings indicate that appropriate nitrogen management and dual-stage mepiquat chloride application can help sustain wheat productivity under delayed sowing.

title: Tracing soil–water signatures from contrasting land uses in low-flow streamwater of a mixed headwater catchment
summary: Baseflow sustains water delivery from headwater catchments during non-event conditions and low flows. However, in mixed land-use headwater catchments, how land-use-related soil–water storage signatures are represented in low-flow streamwate
content: Baseflow sustains water delivery from headwater catchments during non-event conditions and low flows. However, in mixed land-use headwater catchments, how land-use-related soil–water storage signatures are represented in low-flow streamwater and vary seasonally remain poorly understood. To address this gap, a two-year study involving monthly monitoring of a hilly purple-soil headwater catchment was conducted. We employed a combination of dissolved organic matter (DOM) fluorescence, stable water isotopes, and Bayesian mixing analysis to characterize source composition in low-flow streamwater, characterize temporal variation in dominant source signatures, and assess depth-related soil–water signatures under baseflow-dominated conditions. This study showed that orchard, sloping farmland, and paddy soil waters formed the main source-signature group, with a summed mean posterior attribution of 62.9% across the 19 retained samples, and summed monthly posterior-median attributions ranging from 52.7% to 72.8%, compared with a mean attribution of 10.7% to sampled valley shallow groundwater (monthly posterior-median range: 4.7%-26.1%). The dominant-source pattern showed seasonal variation among orchard, sloping farmland, and paddy soil waters, with estimated layer attributions favoring shallow layers (10 cm) in orchard and sloping farmland and middle layers (20–30 cm) in paddy; exploratory analyses indicated associations with bulk density and DOC. The findings indicate that different land-use types are associated with distinct soil–water storage signatures in low-flow streamwater, providing a basis for evaluating how future land-use changes may influence low-flow hydrological functioning.

title: Dry fractionation of chickpea flour: balancing protein enrichment, coproduct functionality and environmental sustainability
summary: Dry fractionation is a resource-efficient approach to produce protein-rich fractions from legumes. However, this process has mainly been optimized for protein content and yield of the fine fraction, while the functional properties of the co
content: Dry fractionation is a resource-efficient approach to produce protein-rich fractions from legumes. However, this process has mainly been optimized for protein content and yield of the fine fraction, while the functional properties of the coarse fraction have received less attention. Moreover, its environmental impact has generally been assessed in separate studies. To date, these aspects (fine fraction composition and yield, coarse fraction functionality and environmental impact) have not been considered together to optimize the dry fractionation process. This study evaluated dry fractionation of chickpea flour, performed with industrial scale equipment, under four operating conditions. The main goal was to determine to what extent a higher degree of refinement is justified when fraction composition, coarse fraction functionality and life cycle environmental impact are considered simultaneously. A clear purity-extraction efficiency trade-off was observed across all conditions: the least selective configuration achieved the highest protein extraction efficiency (59%) and fine fraction yield (36.19%) with moderate protein enrichment (36.5 g/100 g DM), while the most selective configuration reached protein content of up to 46.1 g/100 g DM but at a high cost in yield. The limited separation selectivity can be attributed, at least partly, to the overlap in particle size between starch granules and protein-rich particles in chickpea flour. The coarse fractions also differed in composition, which determined their functional properties. The coarse fraction obtained under the least selective conditions exhibited the highest extent of starch granule swelling, disruption and retrogradation during hydrothermal treatment, and formed the stiffest gel network, consistent with its elevated starch content. Life cycle assessment revealed that environmental impacts increased markedly with fractionation intensity when the whole burden was attributed to the fine fraction, decreased under mass allocation, and increased only moderately under economic allocation. This showed that the environmental performance strongly depends on how the coarse fraction is valorised. These findings highlight the three-way trade-off between protein purity, coarse fraction functional properties, and environmental sustainability, and demonstrate that coarse fraction valorisation is central to the overall viability of dry fractionation as a sustainable food ingredient production strategy.

title: Cathode Bulk Diffusion Dictates Low‐Temperature Performance in Li‐Ion Batteries: Beyond Electrolyte Engineering
summary: ABSTRACT The discharge performance limitations of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) at low temperatures (LT) remain widely debated, with competing attributions to interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics and bulk Li + diffusion. Extensive electrolyt
content: ABSTRACT The discharge performance limitations of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) at low temperatures (LT) remain widely debated, with competing attributions to interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics and bulk Li + diffusion. Extensive electrolyte engineering has been pursued, yet the intrinsic structural constraints of cathodes remain largely overlooked. Here, we apply a systematic half‐cell decoupling strategy across 36 electrolyte formulations to identify the precise rate‐determining step (RDS) in graphite (Gr), layered NCM811, and olivine LFP electrodes. Our results show that LT anodic delithiation maintains near‐theoretical lithium utilization (≈100%), confirming that full‐cell failure originates predominantly from the cathode. Notably, even with highly optimized electrolytes, cathodes exhibit a persistent capacity retention ceiling of 82%–85% for NCM811 and only 38%–48% for LFP. Distribution of capacitive times (DCT) analysis reveals that cathode performance is predominantly dominated by severely hindered bulk Li + diffusion: the solid‐state diffusion time in LFP surges from 16.2 min at RT to 104 h at −30°C. These findings conclusively establish sluggish bulk Li + diffusion as the primary kinetic bottleneck, urging a paradigm shift from electrolyte‐centric strategies toward intrinsic cathode structural engineering.

title: Surface state transport in irradiated topological insulator with hexagonal warping
summary: Abstract We investigate electronic transport in a five-region topological insulator (TI) Bi 2 Te 3 junction with hexagonal warping under the influence of circularly polarized light (CPL). The central region is irradiated by right- and left-
content: Abstract We investigate electronic transport in a five-region topological insulator (TI) Bi 2 Te 3 junction with hexagonal warping under the influence of circularly polarized light (CPL). The central region is irradiated by right- and left-handed CPL, and we systematically examine how the light modifies the transport properties of the system. Within an effective theoretical framework, we study the tunability of charge conductance and magnetoresistance (MR), highlighting the role of light in controlling quantum interference and surface-state transport in TI junctions. Our results demonstrate that CPL with different helicities and intensities serves as a powerful external tuning parameter for inducing an energy gap, controlling the conductance, and generating giant MR with a tunable sign. The interplay between optical irradiation, magnetic and electrostatic potentials, geometrical parameters, and hexagonal warping leads to highly anisotropic and energy-dependent transport characteristics. These findings highlight the potential of light-driven TI devices for optoelectronic and spintronic technologies.

title: Coupling microalgal bioremediation of recirculating aquaculture effluents with photobiological hydrogen production
summary: Recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) effluents contain substantial nutrient loads, posing a eutrophication risk to aquatic ecosystems. Microalgal bioremediation is a promising strategy, but further valorisation of this process is required
content: Recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) effluents contain substantial nutrient loads, posing a eutrophication risk to aquatic ecosystems. Microalgal bioremediation is a promising strategy, but further valorisation of this process is required. This study couples the cultivation of nitrate-utilizing Chlamydomonas reinhardtii strain CC-1690 in RAS effluent with photobiological hydrogen (H 2 ) production to achieve nutrient removal, bioenergy production, and high-quality biomass. Within 70 h, CC-1690 achieved near-complete depletion of nitrate and phosphate from the effluent. Subsequently, H 2 production was induced via carbon limitation and anoxia, yielding 49 μmol H 2 mg −1 Chl over 72 h. Although signs of physiological stress were observed, key photosynthetic subunits (PsbA, PSBO, CP47, PetB and PsaA) remained largely stable. Total lipid content increased slightly, enriched in palmitic and α-linolenic fatty acids, while protein content was unaffected. These results demonstrate that integrating H 2 production with RAS effluent remediation offers a robust approach, valorising waste into bioenergy and high-quality biomass.

title: Pharmacological and safety profile of the long-standing antileprosy drug dapsone
summary: Abstract Dapsone was the first drug to be systematically studiedfor leprosy and is the most commonly used drug for its treatment. After being used as a miracle drug for leprosy in the late 1940s and 1950s, reports of antimicrobial resistanc
content: Abstract Dapsone was the first drug to be systematically studiedfor leprosy and is the most commonly used drug for its treatment. After being used as a miracle drug for leprosy in the late 1940s and 1950s, reports of antimicrobial resistance gradually increased in the following decades, particularly because of its use at low dosages prescribed to decrease the risk of dapsone-induced hypersensitivity (DHS). Its reuse at higher dosages as part of combination multidrug therapy (MDT) for leprosy since the 1980s has contributed to a decline in its antimicrobial resistance. Concurrently, it has also received criticism because of its ability to precipitate its well-known side effects, such as hypersensitivity, anemia, and methemoglobinemia. Here, we discuss the pharmacological aspects of dapsone and attempt to elucidate the current understanding of the pharmacology of dapsone with respect to its adverse side effects.

title: Quinoa as an alternative dry season climate resilient crop in the Mekong Delta Vietnam
summary: Saline intrusion, drought, and water shortages are causing rice production losses in the Mekong River Delta dry season. Quinoa is a drought tolerant halophyte that could be an alternative crop option to rice or fallow in the dry season. The
content: Saline intrusion, drought, and water shortages are causing rice production losses in the Mekong River Delta dry season. Quinoa is a drought tolerant halophyte that could be an alternative crop option to rice or fallow in the dry season. The novelty of growing quinoa in the delta requires an understanding of variety selection and crop optimisation in conditions experienced in the dry season. A range of greenhouse and field trials screened five quinoa varieties (2-want, Sluga, Titicaca, 42- test, and Atlas) for salinity tolerance, fertiliser nitrogen response, and sowing density. The higher yielding varieties, Titicaca and 2-want, had lower biomass and improved water use efficiency in saline and water limited conditions. Nitrogen fertiliser rates of 120 kg N/ha produced the greatest biomass and yield, however lodging occurred, and the 2-want variety recorded negligible yield. Sowing densities between 15 plants/m 2 and 50 plants/m 2 had no significant effect on lodging rate and an uncharacteristic heatwave during anthesis causing no measurable yield. Though these experiments identify Titicaca as suitable variety of quinoa based on tolerance to salinity and agronomic performance, sensitivity to temperature has been identified as a risk factor. Manipulating the growing calendar so that saline and water limited tolerant varieties like Titicaca avoid peaks in temperature during anthesis may provide farmers with a suitable dry season alternative crop to rice.

title: Chloride‐Mediated Photoelectrochemical Selective Oxidation of Polyols Coupled With Hydrogen Evolution
summary: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting coupled with the oxidation of polyols into high‐value‐added chemicals is of practical significance for the upgrading of biomass and polyester plastics. However, the current polyols selecti
content: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting coupled with the oxidation of polyols into high‐value‐added chemicals is of practical significance for the upgrading of biomass and polyester plastics. However, the current polyols selective oxidation reactions suffer from harsh reaction conditions (strong basic electrolyte) and high costs of noble metal‐based catalyst via the reactive oxygen species‐mediated pathway. Herein, we for the first time demonstrate a chlorine radicals‐mediated route toward polyols oxidation under neutral conditions. As proof‐of‐concept, NiCo‐LDH‐decorated TiO 2 has been developed to promote the oxidation of ethylene glycol (EG) to glycolic acid (GA), achieving a GA production rate of 8.7 µmol cm ‒2 h ‒1 with a selectivity of 76.2% in NaCl electrolyte under irradiation, which is the highest value reported to date in PEC system. Mechanistic studies reveal that the key chlorine radicals facilitate C─H bond cleavage to form chlorinated intermediates for GA production. Additionally, we successfully coupled PEC PET‐derived EG valorization with H 2 generation from seawater, attaining GA and H 2 productivity of 30.6 and 93.9 µmol cm ‒2 , respectively. This work offers a novel perspective on polyols oxidation reaction pathway modulation and demonstrates a solar‐to‐chemical conversion approach for integrating low‐value carbon sources recycling and PEC synthesis.

summary: The data tables behind the 2026 release of the Maine Forest Dashboard (maineforestdashboard.com), the annual observational record of Maine's forests produced by the Center for Research on Sustainable Forests at the University of Maine in su
content: The data tables behind the 2026 release of the Maine Forest Dashboard (maineforestdashboard.com), the annual observational record of Maine's forests produced by the Center for Research on Sustainable Forests at the University of Maine in support of the Maine Climate Council forest indicators. Every table is a compiled reference table with its source named in the data dictionary and README: USDA Forest Inventory and Analysis design-based estimates (statewide carbon storage 2003 to 2023 with 95% confidence intervals, health and diversity indicators, county ecosystem-services estimates with sampling error), the State of Maine's Carbon Budget Version 2 (emissions and removals by sector, 2017 to 2021), Maine Forest Service wood processor and stumpage price reports (2000 to 2024), the 2024 Statewide Economic Contribution of Maine's Forest Products Sector (UMaine School of Economics and Camoin Associates), U.S. Census Bureau trade and commodity flow data, Maine DACF conserved lands, and NOAA nClimDiv statewide drought indices. No model projections are included. County values are aggregates; no plot coordinates are present. The lead graphic is the press graphic on how Maine's trees are used, 2023.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI THEORY OF PREDICTIVE CLIMATE JUSTICE AND TRANSNATIONAL CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY Re-engineering Legal Liability of Transcontinental Corporations Through Eco-Digital Governance Models

summary: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Predictive Climate Justice and Transnational Corporate Accountability (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23271861) presents a groundbreaking interdisciplinary framework transforming climate litigation from reactive post-harm adju
content: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Predictive Climate Justice and Transnational Corporate Accountability (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23271861) presents a groundbreaking interdisciplinary framework transforming climate litigation from reactive post-harm adjudication to preventive predictive accountability. It harnesses AI-powered climate modeling, satellite monitoring, and algorithmic carbon footprinting to establish legally actionable evidence of corporate climate harm before catastrophic thresholds are reached. Central is the Climate Justice Digital Accountability Index: CJDAI=(E×P×L×T×R)/[(E×P×L×T×R)+D×F+ε], where all variables are operationally defined as normalized composite indices. The complexity constant (0.01) represents the 'Heisenberg-like epistemic limit of transnational supply chains'—the irreducible uncertainty in perfectly attributing emissions to harm. Under the Weakest-Link Axiom and Asymptotic Perfection Principle (max ≈0.9901), it mathematically proves that accountability collapses without enforcement or reparation mechanisms. The theory introduces the Doctrine of Predictive Causation with Dynamic, Performance-Based Injunctions (requiring Climate Compliance Bonds rather than shutdowns), Explainable AI (XAI) Standards for admissible algorithmic evidence, and WTO-compatible Algorithmic Border Carbon Adjustments aligned with GATT Article XX and the EU's CBAM. It proposes the International Climate Accountability Tribunal (ICAT) and a Universal Climate Accountability Convention. Released under the Ferial Zayed Humanitarian License as the definitive blueprint for planetary ecological justice.

title: Ultrafast Dynamics of Competing Dimethyl Disulfide Photodissociation Pathways
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract Disulfide photochemistry impacts a wide range of chemical processes from biological UV photodamage to polymer self-healing and green photocatalysis. Despite this, the response of disulfide bonds to deep-UV light remains poorly unde
content: Abstract Disulfide photochemistry impacts a wide range of chemical processes from biological UV photodamage to polymer self-healing and green photocatalysis. Despite this, the response of disulfide bonds to deep-UV light remains poorly understood. Dimethyl disulfide serves as a model system for understanding the fundamental properties of this chemical motif, including its UV photodynamics. While 267-nm excitation exclusively cleaves the S–S bond on a subpicosecond time scale, 200 nm excites electronic states of Rydberg and antibonding character, resulting in competing C–S and S–S dissociation on an unknown time scale. Using mega-electron-volt ultrafast electron diffraction and time-resolved velocity-mapped ion imaging, we find subpicosecond as well as unexpectedly long, picosecond lifetimes. Nonadiabatic mixed quantum-classical dynamics reveal mechanisms and observables. We attribute the subpicosecond dynamics to bond dissociation on singlet states and the picosecond dynamics to dissociation after intersystem crossing. Our study reveals that deep-UV excitation in disulfide-containing molecules can induce complex, multi-time scale dynamics.

title: Forest and bioenergy expansion amplifies climate warming by accelerating regional cloud loss
summary: Abstract. Land use and land cover change (LUCC) can exacerbate cloud-mediated climate warming. However, the long-term response of cloud cover to LUCC remains underexplored, particularly regarding differences between idealized and realistic
content: Abstract. Land use and land cover change (LUCC) can exacerbate cloud-mediated climate warming. However, the long-term response of cloud cover to LUCC remains underexplored, particularly regarding differences between idealized and realistic forest expansion scenarios, as well as between forest and bioenergy expansion. Here, using simulations from the fully coupled Community Earth System Model (CESM), we demonstrate that large-scale idealized afforestation and bioenergy expansion accelerate the loss of low- and mid-level clouds while enhancing high-level clouds, thereby amplifying regional warming hotspots through intensified positive shortwave cloud radiative forcing. In contrast, realistic afforestation yields a net cooling effect. Idealized afforestation drives a pronounced decline in low-level cloud cover (1.14 times globally, 1.52 times over land), followed by bioenergy expansion (1.03 times globally and 1.23 times over land), primarily driven by reduced total precipitable water and relative humidity, as revealed by an interpretable machine learning framework, which identifies biophysical warming of the boundary layer due to albedo-driven surface heating and enhanced sensible heat flux as the dominant mechanism. Forest darkening reduces surface albedo, which increases absorbed solar radiation and elevates sensible heat, thereby drying the boundary layer and suppressing cloud formation. Conversely, realistic afforestation mitigates the loss of low- and mid-level clouds and suppresses boreal warming. Our findings indicate that more forest expansion does not always generate greater climate benefits; the climatic outcome largely depends on the type of land conversion and specific latitude bands, and highlights the critical importance of carefully selecting afforestation areas in the future to achieve positive climate benefits.

title: NeuPlume: generative inversion of atmospheric point-source emissions from sparse observations
summary: Abstract. Inverting point-source emissions from sparse atmospheric observations is difficult because emission rate, release height, wind speed, turbulence, and plume morphology can compensate for one another. We present NeuPlume, a neural-p
content: Abstract. Inverting point-source emissions from sparse atmospheric observations is difficult because emission rate, release height, wind speed, turbulence, and plume morphology can compensate for one another. We present NeuPlume, a neural-physical probabilistic inversion framework that returns an ensemble of data-compatible plume fields rather than a single point estimate. A Lagrangian stochastic model builds a scenario-specific forward library, a conditional neural field compresses the concentration fields, and a latent diffusion model learns the feasible field prior. During inversion, diffusion posterior sampling combines this prior with sparse observations to infer emission rate, effective release height, wind speed, turbulence intensity, and the full concentration field. The present implementation targets passive, low-height, near-neutral releases over flat terrain. Across six synthetic cases within this scope, NeuPlume achieves mean errors of 10.0% for emission rate and 1.4% for effective release height, outperforming Gaussian plume and mass-balance baselines under the same volumetric observation protocol. On 30 holdout cases, the nominal 68% credible interval attains 73.3% empirical coverage. As an illustrative field-transfer check, NeuPlume is applied to four UAV methane transects above a coal-mine ventilation shaft; known-U posterior intervals from three flights overlap the same-shaft hourly inventory, with diagnostics identifying wind-speed and height-boundary sensitivities under model mismatch. NeuPlume provides uncertainty-aware source-parameter constraints within the physical scope of its forward library and can be re-instantiated for other regimes by rebuilding the scenario-specific simulation ensemble and retraining the neural prior.

title: Balancing embodied and operational carbon through shading design in vertical extension retrofits
summary: The construction sector must reduce both embodied and operational carbon emissions to meet net-zero targets. While external shading can lower cooling demand, it also introduces embodied carbon through additional material use. This paper inv
content: The construction sector must reduce both embodied and operational carbon emissions to meet net-zero targets. While external shading can lower cooling demand, it also introduces embodied carbon through additional material use. This paper investigates whether operational carbon savings from façade shading can offset its embodied carbon over a 60-year building life. The Crowndale Centre in London is used as a case study of a three-storey vertical extension. Existing aluminium roofing is repurposed as external shading. Solar radiation analysis and dynamic thermal simulations using TAS are combined with life cycle assessment in OneClick LCA to evaluate operational and embodied carbon across different shading densities and material scenarios. Results show that shading reduces operational carbon; however, the embodied carbon of primary aluminium outweighs this benefit. Recycled and reclaimed aluminium achieved net carbon reductions over 60 years, with reclaimed aluminium providing the greatest whole-life carbon benefit.

title: Analysing carbon and cost of external wall materials and construction methods in the context of affordable housing in the UK
summary: The urgent need to deliver affordable housing alongside the UK’s net-zero target presents a significant challenge. While operational carbon has been widely addressed in policy and practice, embodied carbon remains comparatively overlooked d
content: The urgent need to deliver affordable housing alongside the UK’s net-zero target presents a significant challenge. While operational carbon has been widely addressed in policy and practice, embodied carbon remains comparatively overlooked despite contributing substantially to whole-life carbon emissions. This study evaluated the embodied carbon and cost performance of 31 external wall systems, categorised as Onsite, Hybrid and Modern Methods of Construction (MMC). A representative affordable housing model was assessed using Life Cycle Assessment in OneClick LCA in accordance with EN 15978 and the RICS Whole-Life Carbon Assessment for the Built Environment guidance, alongside material and labour cost modelling. Embodied carbon ranged from 65 to 300 kgCO₂e/m², while costs ranged from £113 to £266/m². Sensitivity analysis showed that biogenic carbon and Module D influenced the carbon performance of timber and biobased systems.

title: How future decarbonisation pathways affect the life-cycle carbon footprint of rooftop PVs : a UK scenario analysis
summary: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems are central to UK residential retrofit policy, yet conventional whole-life carbon assessments (WLCAs) apply static, present-day grid and manufacturing factors across multi-decade horizons, risking overstate
content: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems are central to UK residential retrofit policy, yet conventional whole-life carbon assessments (WLCAs) apply static, present-day grid and manufacturing factors across multi-decade horizons, risking overstated long-term benefit as the grid itself decarbonises. This study quantifies how future UK grid- and manufacturing-decarbonisation pathways affect the 60-year carbon footprint and payback of a 3.03kWp retrofit PV system on a UK dwelling, modelled in IESVE and an annual Excel model following EN 15978/RICS Whole Life Carbon Assessment guidance (modules A1-A5, B4, B6, C1-C4), supplemented by an EN 15804-compliant generic inventory. A static baseline is compared against three NESO Future Energy Scenarios pathways, excluding BECCS-attributed removals. The static case achieved payback in year 8 (net benefit: 19,513 kgCO2e) whereas no dynamic pathway achieved payback within 60 years, since avoided emissions fell faster (81-97%) than embodied carbon (47-61%). Findings challenge static WLCA practice for grid-displacing technologies.

title: Shifting Perspectives in Gamification Research
summary: Gamification has become an important topic in research on digital media, information systems, behavioral design, and public communication. This article uses a bibliometric-informed narrative review to examine highly cited English-language s
content: Gamification has become an important topic in research on digital media, information systems, behavioral design, and public communication. This article uses a bibliometric-informed narrative review to examine highly cited English-language studies, systematic reviews of gamification for sustainability, and Chinese research on gamified ecological science communication. It synthesizes the field's knowledge structure and theoretical development. The review identifies ten interrelated shifts. At the conceptual level, research has moved from game elements to gameful experience. At the mechanistic level, it has moved from extrinsic rewards to psychological need satisfaction and motivational affordances. At the functional level, it has moved from single outcome measures to a multilayered analysis of engagement, motivation, social interaction, experience, and awareness. Applications have also expanded across sustainability, education, health, marketing and services, organizational management, public governance, and participatory culture. Together, these shifts show that gamification research is moving beyond the question of whether particular elements work and toward an explanation of how gamification organizes motivation, interaction, emotion, identity, and social meaning in specific platform contexts. Future research should examine long-term effects and contextual variation while giving greater attention to user types, ethical risks, and computational communication methods.

title: Targeting REV7 confers cervical cancer cell radiosensitivity and ferroptosis by negatively regulating SFXN1
summary: Cervical cancer is the 4th most common malignancy in women. Radiotherapy (RT) plays an essential role in cervical cancer treatments, and this study reports the role of REV7 in cervical cancer RT. Results showed that loss of REV7 contributed
content: Cervical cancer is the 4th most common malignancy in women. Radiotherapy (RT) plays an essential role in cervical cancer treatments, and this study reports the role of REV7 in cervical cancer RT. Results showed that loss of REV7 contributed to increased the radiosensitivity of cervical cancer both in vitro and in vivo. Further molecular biology experiments demonstrated REV7-silence enhanced apoptosis, aggravated radiation-induced ROS, and accelerated ferroptosis after RT. Mass spectrometry was used to explore the candidate substrates of REV7 involved in the regulation of cervical cancer cell radiosensitivity. Mass spectrometry and co-immunoprecipitation confirmed that SFXN1 is a candidate substrate for REV7. The expression of SFXN1 was negatively regulated by REV7 in HeLa cells. Consistently, REV7 deficiency aggravated ferroptosis by increasing SFXN1. Our findings revealed that REV7 conferred radioresistance of cervical cancer cell by downregulating SFXN1 expression. Moreover, REV7 physically interacts with SFXN1 and negatively regulates its expression through an ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation pathway. In conclusion, REV7 depletion induce ferroptosis and enhance the radiosensitivity of cervical cancer cells in an SFXN1-dependent manner, indicating that targeting REV7 is a plausible candidate that possesses potential for the radiosensitization of cervical cancer.

title: Board sustainability expertise: how shareholder and employee representatives shape supervisory board practice in codetermined German firms
summary: Purpose This paper asks how sustainability expertise is constructed, distributed across shareholder and employee representatives and translated into influence through the governance channels of parity codetermined supervisory boards in Germ
