title: Physiochemical and Mechanical Performance of Portland Cement Grades Marketed in Nigeria
summary: This study presents a comparative assessment and analysis of the hydration properties of Portland cement grades 32.5 and 42.5 marketed in Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. The research was motivated by concerns over inconsistent cement q
content: This study presents a comparative assessment and analysis of the hydration properties of Portland cement grades 32.5 and 42.5 marketed in Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. The research was motivated by concerns over inconsistent cement quality and its impact on structural performance. Five (5) cement samples (A, B, C, D and E) were analyzed for chemical composition (XRF), physical properties (Blaine fineness, residue, consistency, expansion, and setting times), and mechanical properties (compressive and flexural strength at 2, 7, and 28 days). Results from Blaine values ranged from 3940 to 4480 cm²/g, showed sample D (32.5R) exhibiting the highest fineness. Setting times (initial: 133 to 155 min; final: 205 to 216 min) and expansion values (0.5 to 1.0 mm) were within permissible limits. Strength development increased with curing age, with 42.5R achieving the highest 28-day flexural strength (5.8 MPa), outperforming 32.5R (4.7 to 5.0 MPa).The findings confirm that while both cement grades meet national and international standards, 42.5 grade cements offer superior hydration performance and strength, making them more suitable for high-strength structural applications, whereas 32.5grade cements are better suited for light construction and finishing works. The research result showed analyses that falls within the acceptable range of the National and International Standards, and the coefficient of variation indicate the robustness and reliability of the result. And objectives of the assessment were fully achieved, with empirical data guide in cement selection, improving production quality, and support regulatory enforcement in Nigeria’s construction industry.

title: Toward Trustworthy and Efficient Carbon Emissions Trading: A Stable Matching and Privacy-Preserving Framework
summary: Carbon emissions trading (CET) requires not only efficient allowance allocation but also stable transactions and protection of sensitive trading information. This study proposes a trustworthy CET framework that integrates stable matching wi
content: Carbon emissions trading (CET) requires not only efficient allowance allocation but also stable transactions and protection of sensitive trading information. This study proposes a trustworthy CET framework that integrates stable matching with privacy-preserving computing. Carbon trading is modeled as a dynamic many-to-many matching problem in which reservation prices, trading quantities, and time priority are used to construct bilateral preferences, while blocking-pair elimination ensures pairwise stability. Paillier homomorphic encryption, zk-SNARKs, and blockchain are further incorporated to support secure declaration, matching, and settlement. Real-market-calibrated simulations based on China’s national carbon market show that the proposed SMCETS mechanism maintains zero blocking pairs under excess-supply, excess-demand, and equilibrium conditions, including under reservation-price perturbations and trading-quantity variations. It also achieves higher Benefit Index and total surplus values than the Vickrey and discriminatory-price auction benchmarks in the tested settings. Prototype evaluation further demonstrates practical runtime feasibility. These results suggest that stable matching and privacy-preserving technologies can be jointly incorporated into digital carbon-trading mechanisms to support more reliable and trustworthy market operation.

title: Overview and Assessment of Ship Emissions Estimation Models
source: Journal of Marine Science and Application
summary: Abstract This review provides a comprehensive comparative assessment of ship emissions estimation models across the various ship emissions estimation modelling approaches, with a focus on key approaches: top-down, bottom-up, hybrid approach
content: Abstract This review provides a comprehensive comparative assessment of ship emissions estimation models across the various ship emissions estimation modelling approaches, with a focus on key approaches: top-down, bottom-up, hybrid approaches, and emerging machine learning and artificial intelligence-based techniques as an innovative approach, offering new perspectives and solutions for the maritime industry through its powerful data analysis and pattern recognition capabilities. It delves into important ship emissions estimation models that use advanced data-driven techniques, ranging from simplified to complex, which are continually evolving to improve accuracy by incorporating real-time data, technological advancements, and the impact of environmental policies. Afterwards, this review provides an overall analysis of the ship emissions models, highlighting current research gaps in data availability and quality, challenges in selecting ship emissions estimation methods, and future research topics. Finally, it concludes with future directions in advanced machine learning methods, digital twins, advanced sensor integration, and global monitoring for precise forecasting and regulatory support, all of which are crucial for decarbonization targets.

title: Structural instability and emerging energy–GDP decoupling in Saudi Arabia: exploratory evidence and forecasting implications
summary: Energy-demand relationships in resource-dependent economies may change when macroeconomic shocks, policy reforms, and structural transformation alter consumption patterns. This study provides an exploratory assessment of structural instabil
content: Energy-demand relationships in resource-dependent economies may change when macroeconomic shocks, policy reforms, and structural transformation alter consumption patterns. This study provides an exploratory assessment of structural instability, energy–GDP decoupling, and energy-demand forecasting in Saudi Arabia using annual data from 1990 to 2023. Bai–Perron tests are applied under alternative specifications to identify endogenous changes in per capita energy consumption, while a policy-motivated test at 2016 evaluates whether the year associated with the launch of Vision 2030 is linked to a change in the energy–GDP relationship. The results indicate substantial structural instability in Saudi Arabia’s per capita energy-consumption trajectory. Major breaks are identified in the mid-1990s or early 2000s and around 2009, depending on the structural-break specification, with the 2009 breakpoint remaining robust across alternative models. In contrast, 2016 is not selected endogenously as a dominant breakpoint. A policy-motivated test at 2016 suggests a possible change in the energy–GDP relationship under conventional inference, although the evidence weakens after accounting for serial correlation. Break-adjusted cointegration results are interpreted as exploratory because of the short annual sample and uncertain integration properties. The decoupling analysis shows a descriptive change after 2016. During 2017–2023, real GDP per capita increased while per capita energy consumption declined, indicating strong decoupling. By contrast, the earlier period was characterised by strong negative decoupling. Forecasting comparisons indicate that models incorporating more recent observations produced lower forecast errors than the model estimated exclusively from pre-2016 data. Predictions incorporating realised real GDP per capita and Brent oil prices are interpreted as conditional ex post forecasts rather than fully operational ex ante forecasts. Overall, the findings provide exploratory evidence of substantial structural instability and an emerging energy–GDP decoupling pattern in Saudi Arabia. They do not establish a causal effect of Vision 2030 or demonstrate a permanent new energy regime. The results emphasise the importance of cautious interpretation, transparent data and code, and regularly updated break-aware models for energy-demand forecasting in resource-dependent economies.

title: Infrared thermographic evaluation of cleaning stone relics at tomb of Yue Fei
summary: This study investigates the efficacy and safety of steam cleaning technology for the removal of surface contaminants from stone cultural relics at the Tomb of Yue Fei, a nationally protected heritage site in China. The research focuses on c
content: This study investigates the efficacy and safety of steam cleaning technology for the removal of surface contaminants from stone cultural relics at the Tomb of Yue Fei, a nationally protected heritage site in China. The research focuses on common pollutants including dust accumulation, surface encrustation, hydro erosion, bioerosion, and anthropogenic graffiti. An evaluation method based on infrared thermography is proposed to assess cleaning effectiveness by analyzing temperature variation (T) before and after treatment. Field experiments were conducted using a steam cleaner with controlled parameters (pressure, temperature, angle, distance, and duration), and cleaning outcomes were evaluated through visual inspection, chromatic aberration measurement, and microscopic imaging. Results demonstrate that steam cleaning effectively removes most contaminants without causing significant damage to the stone substrate. The study also provides a set of recommended steam cleaning parameters for different pollutant types on limestone surfaces. The findings validate the feasibility of using infrared thermography as a non-destructive evaluation tool for cleaning efficacy, contributing to the development of standardized protocols for the conservation of stone heritage.

title: Engineering Sulfate Stability for Metal Recovery from Bauxite Residue: A Critical Review of Selective Sulfation, Roasting, Water Leaching, and Process Integration
summary: Bauxite residue is simultaneously a high-volume alkaline industrial residue and a polymetallic secondary resource containing iron, aluminum, titanium, scandium, rare earth elements, gallium, vanadium, and other potentially valuable constitu
content: Bauxite residue is simultaneously a high-volume alkaline industrial residue and a polymetallic secondary resource containing iron, aluminum, titanium, scandium, rare earth elements, gallium, vanadium, and other potentially valuable constituents. This critical narrative/process-engineering review evaluates selective sulfation as a strategy for separating target metals from the dominant Fe–Al matrix by exploiting sequential differences in sulfate formation, thermal stability, aqueous solubility, and downstream separability. The review distinguishes sulfuric-acid leaching, acid baking, sulfate-salt roasting, and sulfation–roasting–water-leaching routes mechanistically, and explicitly separates maximum extraction from maximum process selectivity. The decisive design variable is an operational thermochemical window in which undesired Fe- and, where achievable, Al-bearing sulfates are destabilized or rendered poorly leachable while Sc/REE-bearing sulfates remain recoverable by water leaching. Mineralogical association, sulfur dosage, heating rate, residence time, bed thickness, atmosphere, gas composition, cooling history, and leaching conditions jointly control this window. The review follows the process through impurity removal, solvent extraction, ion exchange, precipitation, sulfur and water recycling, residue valorization, reactor engineering, technology readiness, techno-economic analysis, and prospective life-cycle assessment. An author-developed five-level selectivity framework—formation, thermal, solubility, separation, and process selectivity—is used to normalize route comparison. The central conclusion is that selective sulfation should be designed as an integrated closed-loop separation system, with sulfur efficiency, Fe/Al rejection, product quality, off-gas control, residue usability, and scale-up robustness treated as co-equal design objectives.

title: Unions as agents for institutionalisation of labour-centred social sustainability in tourism
summary: This study examines how trade unions engage in the institutionalisation of labour-centred social sustainability in tourism, focusing on how they influence the field’s normative, regulative, and cultural-cognitive dimensions. While social su
content: This study examines how trade unions engage in the institutionalisation of labour-centred social sustainability in tourism, focusing on how they influence the field’s normative, regulative, and cultural-cognitive dimensions. While social sustainability has gained attention within environmental, social and governance (ESG) frameworks, the role of unions remains underexplored, particularly in tourism, where precarious employment persists. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 18 global union leaders and affiliates and informed by institutional theory, the study analyses how unions mobilise human rights-based framing, shape labour-related metrics and regulatory standards, and seek to shift societal expectations around decent work. Findings show that unions operate across multiple institutional domains, extending their influence beyond collective bargaining to broader field-level engagement. The study extends institutional theory by demonstrating how institutional actors actively mobilise normative, regulative and cultural-cognitive mechanisms to advance social sustainability. It further contributes to debates on the underdeveloped social dimension of ESG by highlighting the contested and political nature of defining and measuring labour-related sustainability. Unions emerge as important institutional actors in embedding labour standards within sustainability governance, while structural constraints continue to limit the realisation of labour-centred social sustainability in practice.

title: Performance testing of fabricated green-synthesised binary and ternary nanohybrids for light-induced reduction of CO2 to gaseous fuel
summary: Greenhouse gas emissions worldwide continue to rise, and rising atmospheric CO 2 is accelerating global warming and putting the 1.5 °C climate goal in jeopardy. The energy sector is still the biggest polluter because of the continued use of
content: Greenhouse gas emissions worldwide continue to rise, and rising atmospheric CO 2 is accelerating global warming and putting the 1.5 °C climate goal in jeopardy. The energy sector is still the biggest polluter because of the continued use of fossil fuels. Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction driven by solar energy provides a sustainable pathway for the transformation of CO 2 into useful fuels and chemicals. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) constitute an exciting class of materials for CO 2 capture and conversion, due to their high surface areas, tunable porosity and rich functionality. Bio-MOFs are composed of renewable biological resources and thus offer a sustainable alternative to conventional MOFs. Their structural tunability, functional diversity and self-assembly properties can improve CO 2 adsorption, selective capture in humid conditions, recyclability and industrial applicability. Thus, bio-based MOFs represent promising platforms for sustainable and efficient photocatalytic CO 2 conversion and carbon utilisation. This study explains bio-based MOF synthesis strategies and develops binary and ternary MOF nanocomposites containing metallic and metal oxide components for photocatalytic CO 2 reduction under halogen-lamp irradiation, followed by analysis of the reaction products. The synthesised materials were comprehensively characterised using FE-SEM/EDS, XRD, UV–Vis DRS, FTIR, PL, Mott–Schottky analysis, XPS, and BET surface area analysis to evaluate their morphological, structural, elemental, optical, electronic, surface-chemical, and textural properties. The composites were then tested for reduction reactions under visible light irradiation and quantified using gas chromatography (GC). Furthermore, Design of Experiments (DOE) using the two-factorial method was applied to optimise process parameters.

title: Global evidence on energy transition and climate vulnerability through systematic review
summary: Over the last decade, the number of studies showing a link between energy transition and climate vulnerability has increased significantly. Globally, energy transition is an important component of the climate system and plays a key role in
content: Over the last decade, the number of studies showing a link between energy transition and climate vulnerability has increased significantly. Globally, energy transition is an important component of the climate system and plays a key role in economic development. There is a large body of literature on energy transition and climate vulnerability individually, but limited studies have used multiple factors to analyse both. What remains unclear is whether these two systems interact and influence each other. In recent years, especially after 2022, some studies have begun to consider multidimensional measures of climate vulnerability or climate risk, such as composite indices that incorporate exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. The paper aims to critically review the insufficient and highly inconsistent approaches used to establish a relationship between energy transition and climate vulnerability. Data for the study are collected using the Scopus database. This study adopted the PRISMA framework and conducted a bibliometric analysis of 76 studies. This study reviews existing studies on the relationship between energy transition and climate vulnerability, identifies major research themes, and highlights important research gaps for future studies. The review highlights that carbon emission reduction is considered the main indicator of environmental performance, with limited focus on climate vulnerability using multidimensional measures such as exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. The review shows four major thematic areas in the existing literature, with the largest proportion of studies focusing on policy, economic, and institutional dimensions, followed by climate risk and vulnerability, energy transition and environmental outcomes and emerging research areas. The findings also reveal that the literature remains fragmented, with limited integration of energy transition and climate vulnerability within a unified analytical framework. Furthermore, the review identifies significant research gaps, particularly in sub-national analyses and the use of comprehensive climate vulnerability indicators.

title: People are good at stewardship
summary: Abstract Environmental sciences and policy have long been framed on the premise that environmental harm is an expression of human nature rather than a product of specific historical and political arrangements. This framing has shaped a gene
content: Abstract Environmental sciences and policy have long been framed on the premise that environmental harm is an expression of human nature rather than a product of specific historical and political arrangements. This framing has shaped a generation of interventions designed to constrain human behaviour rather than enable human capacity. We argue for a different starting point that the capacity to live in generative, reciprocal relationships with the rest of nature is one of our defining strengths as a species and that the evidence for this claim is now extensive, cross‐disciplinary and consequential. We recommend reorienting both research and practice around the acknowledgement that environmental degradation is not a human baseline to be incrementally mitigated, but a historically recent pathology rooted in settler and extractive colonialism, industrial capitalism and the deliberate dismantling of Indigenous and other local governance systems. Recentring the human capacity for stewardship shifts the primary focus of the pro‐environmental enterprise from mitigating a flaw to enabling a human strength. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

title: Fluorination: A strategy to tune the interactions of molecules and nanoscale systems with biological matter
summary: Fluorination has become a key molecular engineering strategy in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine, enabling the fine tuning of the physicochemical and biological properties of therapeutic molecules and drug delivery systems. The unique c
content: Fluorination has become a key molecular engineering strategy in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine, enabling the fine tuning of the physicochemical and biological properties of therapeutic molecules and drug delivery systems. The unique characteristics of fluorine, including its small steric footprint, high electronegativity, and exceptional strength of the C-F bond, enhance metabolic stability, modulate lipophilicity and acidity, and improve pharmacokinetic profiles. Beyond these well-established effects, fluorination has emerged as a tool for controlling the assembly and biological behavior of nanocarriers. Fluorinated biomolecules, polymers, dendrimers, and lipid-based systems often display improved colloidal stability, reduced nonspecific protein adsorption, enhanced cellular uptake, and efficient endosomal escape, ultimately leading to superior intracellular delivery of nucleic acids, proteins, and other therapeutic cargoes. Here we summarize recent advances in the fluorination of both therapeutic cargoes and delivery carriers, emphasizing how different fluorination strategies, including single fluorine atoms, trifluoromethyl groups, linear perfluoroalkyl chains, and emerging short branched fluorinated motifs, can be exploited to optimize drug delivery performance. Attention is devoted to the relationship between fluorinated molecular architectures, self-assembly, and bio-nano interactions that govern biological activity. Furthermore, the advantages and limitations of current fluorination approaches are discussed. Finally, we highlight the need for a deeper mechanistic understanding of how fluorinated moieties interact with proteins and biological membranes. Advanced physicochemical techniques, including neutron and X-ray scattering and reflectometry, are expected to provide fundamental insights into these processes, enabling the rational design of more effective, safer, and environmentally sustainable fluorinated therapeutics and nanomedicines.

title: [18F]ApaScan: A 2-Pyridinylbenzimidazole PET Tracer with Highly Selective Binding to Human Aldosterone-Producing Adenoma Tissue
summary: Abstract Aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) is overexpressed in aldosterone-producing adenomas (APAs) and represents a promising PET target for the noninvasive localization of APA lesions in primary aldosteronism. To address this need, we synth
content: Abstract Aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) is overexpressed in aldosterone-producing adenomas (APAs) and represents a promising PET target for the noninvasive localization of APA lesions in primary aldosteronism. To address this need, we synthesized and evaluated 2-pyridinylbenzimidazole analogues for their ability to bind to human APA (hAPA) tissue. Based on initial binding assays, five analogues were selected and radiolabeled with fluorine-18 for autoradiographic and saturation binding studies. Among them, [18F]3 ([18F]ApaScan) exhibited high-affinity binding to hAPA homogenates (KD = 8.4 nM) with no measurable specific binding to normal adrenal (hNA) homogenates, demonstrating excellent tissue selectivity for hAPA over hNA. Quantitative autoradiography using [18F]3 further confirmed a high hAPA-to-hNA tissue binding ratio of 18. In normal rats, [18F]3 displayed rapid adrenal uptake, efficient clearance without prolonged retention, and no skeletal accumulation. Taken together, these results suggest that [18F]3 has the potential to be developed into a PET tracer for localizing APAs in primary aldosteronism.

title: 31) Water-Energy-Compute Optimization Framework for Sustainable U.S. AI Data Center Infrastructure
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The growth of AI data centers in the United States raises electricity demand and, through cooling and power generation, water consumption. Energy, water, carbon, thermal safety, compute cost and service availability are coupled: a cooling m
content: The growth of AI data centers in the United States raises electricity demand and, through cooling and power generation, water consumption. Energy, water, carbon, thermal safety, compute cost and service availability are coupled: a cooling mode that saves electricity may consume water, and a mode that saves water may raise electricity use and carbon emissions. This study investigates how AI data centers can optimize compute performance while reducing electricity and water consumption without compromising availability.

title: A Coupled Data Assimilation Method for Visibility and Relative Humidity CAOP v1.0 module within the WRFDA v4.3 framework: Improving both PM 2.5 and Humidity Forecasts
summary: Abstract. High precision prediction of near-surface PM2.5 mass concentration is critical for effective air quality management and mitigating health risks. While Data assimilation (DA) of the aerosol mass concentration or the aerosol optical
content: Abstract. High precision prediction of near-surface PM2.5 mass concentration is critical for effective air quality management and mitigating health risks. While Data assimilation (DA) of the aerosol mass concentration or the aerosol optical properties (AOP) observation optimizes the initial conditions of an atmospheric chemistry prediction model and improves aerosol prediction skill, the potential of assimilating surface visibility remains constrained by the overlooked regulatory effect of relative humidity (RH) on visibility variance. To address this, we developed a coupled DA method of AOP and RH (CAOP v1.0) within the WRFDA (version 4.3) framework. Four parallel experiments were conducted across mainland China in December 2020: a control experiment and three DA experiments. Results demonstrate that assimilating visibility alone (VisOnly) reduced RMSE by 21 % for visibility and 9 % for PM2.5, validating the CAOP module. Furthermore, DA of both visibility and RH – whether performed simultaneously but independently in the VisRH_Indp experiment or via the coupled scheme in the VisRH_Copl experiment – effectively corrected the PM2.5 analysis bias originating from background RH deviations. The coupled scheme (VisRH_Copl) achieved superior performance, lowering PM2.5 RMSE by 17 % compared to 16 % in the independent run (VisRH_Indp). Crucially, the CAOP scheme more efficiently leveraged visibility data to constrain the RH field, improving the RH forecast correlation coefficient by 25 % (versus 23 % in the VisRH_Indp). This study confirms that visibility observations substantially enhanced RH analysis and demonstrated that the coupled DA method outperforms independent DA approaches for joint PM2.5 and RH forecasting.

title: How does digital government affect high-quality employment? Evidence from China
summary: Governments around the world are actively promoting the construction of digital government to improve the public service value and serve the economic and social development more effectively. This study aims to explore the impact of digital
content: Governments around the world are actively promoting the construction of digital government to improve the public service value and serve the economic and social development more effectively. This study aims to explore the impact of digital government on macro high-quality employment (MQE) and the influencing mechanism in the context of developing countries facing severe employment problems. We develop a six-dimensional MQE index system and use two-way fixed effects (FE) model and U-test method to explore the nonlinear relationship between digital government and MQE. The main findings are as follows. First, the level of MQE is constantly improving, but there are great differences between provinces. Second, there is a significant U-shaped relationship between the digital government and MQE; that is, when the digital government development index has not exceeded the critical value, it has an inhibiting effect on MQE, and when the digital government development index reaches the critical value, the digital government will have a promoting effect on the improvement of MQE. Third, the improvement effect of digital government on MQE is mainly achieved through enhancing the digital industrialization scale and promoting economic development. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that in the eastern and central regions, in provinces with high human capital level, digital government and MQE show a U-shaped relationship, but in the western regions and provinces with low human capital level, the U-shaped relationship is not significant. From the perspective of different MQE dimensions, digital government has a significant non-linear effect on both the quantity and quality of employment. Therefore, the government should accelerate the development of digital government beyond the critical level to promote MQE and people’s well-being.

title: Entrepreneurship development, corruption perception, and sustainable development outcomes in emerging economies: the moderating role of digital financial inclusion
summary: Abstract Background Sustainable development remains uneven across emerging economies despite continuing efforts to strengthen entrepreneurship, governance institutions, and financial inclusion. Existing evidence provides limited understandi
content: Abstract Background Sustainable development remains uneven across emerging economies despite continuing efforts to strengthen entrepreneurship, governance institutions, and financial inclusion. Existing evidence provides limited understanding of whether access-oriented digital financial inclusion conditions the association between entrepreneurship development and sustainability performance across heterogeneous emerging-economy settings. Methods This study examines the relationships among entrepreneurship development, corruption perception, institutional quality, digital financial inclusion, and sustainable development outcomes using a balanced panel of 60 emerging economies over 2009–2024, comprising 960 country-year observations. Sustainable development is measured by the SDG Index Score, while digital financial inclusion is proxied by adult account ownership at a financial institution or mobile-money-service provider. Two-way fixed-effects estimation with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors provides the principal associational estimates. Panel threshold regression and panel quantile regression assess nonlinear and distributional heterogeneity, dynamic system-GMM provides supplementary dynamic evidence, a source-observed sensitivity analysis evaluates dependence on constructed annual observations for entrepreneurship and digital financial inclusion, and time-aware XGBoost–SHAP analysis assesses nonlinear predictive relationships. Results The principal estimates show no statistically significant positive association between entrepreneurship development and sustainable development outcomes, while the Corruption Perceptions Index is also statistically insignificant. Institutional quality, digital financial inclusion, industry value added, and population growth are positively associated with sustainable development outcomes, whereas inflation shows a negative but comparatively weak association. Contrary to the proposed moderation hypothesis, the entrepreneurship–digital financial inclusion interaction is negative and statistically significant in the principal model, while the corresponding interaction is statistically insignificant in the source-observed and dynamic specifications. The threshold analysis identifies a digital financial inclusion threshold of approximately 62.99%, but entrepreneurship is not statistically significant either below or above the threshold, precluding interpretation of the threshold as a beneficial policy benchmark. Quantile estimates further show negative entrepreneurship coefficients across the 25th, 50th, and 75th conditional quantiles, while institutional quality and digital financial inclusion remain positively associated with sustainable development. The source-observed sensitivity analysis preserves the principal conclusions concerning entrepreneurship, corruption perception, and moderation. XGBoost–SHAP additionally identifies population growth as the most influential nonlinear predictor in the temporally held-out samp

title: How directionality emerges through frame layering: An analysis of Swedish research and innovation policy on agri-food
summary: Transforming agri-food systems is widely seen as necessary to address overlapping ecological and social crises. Public research and innovation policy is a central mechanism through which such transformations are steered, yet it is often art
content: Transforming agri-food systems is widely seen as necessary to address overlapping ecological and social crises. Public research and innovation policy is a central mechanism through which such transformations are steered, yet it is often articulated in ways that obscure the normative commitments legitimising particular pathways. Using critical frame analysis and drawing on debates around directionality and the contrasting paradigms of sustainable intensification and agroecology, we analyse Swedish agri-food research and innovation policy from 2017 to 2025. We ask how problems and solutions are framed across successive levels of policy articulation, and what this implies for directionality. The policies comprise two national strategies, two action plans, two strategic research agendas and 21 funding calls. The findings show that directionality is not the property of any single instrument or policy level but emerges through frame layering across levels. In this way, diversity at one level can partially compensate for closure at another. We argue that directionality is therefore a relational and partly emergent property of how frames are layered. Hybrid framings, whose paradigm alignment depends on operationalisation, define challenges and solutions in broader terms that ease political friction at the cost of directional clarity. The paper offers a layered account of directionality and shows how critical frame analysis can surface the normative commitments embedded in research and innovation policy.

title: From Peroxides to Qubits: Using Glow-Stick Chemistry to Introduce Excited States, Conical Intersections, and Quantum Computing to Undergraduates
summary: Glow sticks provide a familiar and visually striking entry point to chemiluminescence and excited-state chemistry. We present a self-contained computational teaching module that uses peroxide bond breaking to introduce multireference electr
content: Glow sticks provide a familiar and visually striking entry point to chemiluminescence and excited-state chemistry. We present a self-contained computational teaching module that uses peroxide bond breaking to introduce multireference electronic structure, conical intersections, and quantum computing. In a Jupyter/Google Colab notebook, students first stretch the O–O bond of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and observe the emergence of biradical character. They then examine 1,2-dioxetane as a tractable model for cyclic-peroxide decomposition, using state-averaged complete active space self-consistent field (SA-CASSCF) calculations to explore near-degenerate electronic states and examine the local conical topology of an S0/S1 intersection. The resulting active-space problem is then represented on a quantum simulator using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and the subspace-search VQE (SSVQE), and finally extended to state-averaged orbital-optimized VQE (SA-OO-VQE), in which the orbitals are optimized as well. The activity emphasizes that quantum algorithms are motivated by the structure of challenging multireference problems rather than presented as immediate replacements for classical methods. Designed for one 2–3 h laboratory session or two 75-min recitations, the module requires no advanced quantum mechanics or computer-science background and includes learning objectives, assessment questions, implementation guidance, and a complete tested notebook.

title: Soil amendments for cost-effective tropical forest restoration
summary: Introduction: Low-cost soil amendments hold promise for improving assisted forest restoration outcomes and reducing dependence on emission-intensive inputs, yet rigorous field-based comparisons of novel and standard amendments, including co
content: Introduction: Low-cost soil amendments hold promise for improving assisted forest restoration outcomes and reducing dependence on emission-intensive inputs, yet rigorous field-based comparisons of novel and standard amendments, including cost-effectiveness, remain rare. Objectives: We evaluated seedling performance and cost-effectiveness under three novel soil amendments: nutrient-rich agricultural biowaste (composted coffee pulp), native soil microbiome inoculation (live primary forest soil), and locally sourced effective microorganisms (LEM), against commercial fertilizer and an unamended control. Methods: Treatments were tested on one early-successional (Croton tenuicaudatus) and one late-successional (Persea caerulea) seedling species. We assessed survival, relative growth rate, root mass fraction, soil and foliar nutrients, and cost-effectiveness (USD/kg plant carbon gain/ha) over the first year on degraded tropical pasture. Results: Coffee pulp was the most effective amendment, significantly enhancing soil and foliar nutrients (particularly in Croton), matching fertilizer in Croton growth rate (0.182 vs. 0.160), improving survival by 13–19% over control and LEM treatments for both species, and reducing cost per unit carbon gain by up to 92% (Croton) and 68% (Persea) relative to controls. Native soil microbiome inoculation significantly enhanced Croton growth and cost-effectiveness relative to controls); LEM had no significant effect on growth or survival and significantly increased costs per unit plant carbon gain relative to other amendments for both species. Conclusions: Composted coffee pulp and native soil microbiome inoculation improved first-year seedling performance and cost-effectiveness on degraded tropical pasture, with coffee pulp more cost-effective than commercial fertilizer; LEM provided no benefit. Implications for Practice: • Composted coffee pulp and other nutrient-rich agricultural biowastes significantly improve seedling performance and offer a scalable, low-cost alternative to emission-intensive synthetic fertilizers on degraded tropical land. • Inoculation with live forest soil may also improve seedling growth, survival and restoration cost-effectiveness. • We do not recommend LEM as a direct soil amendment as it may increase costs without ecological benefit. • Soil amendments are a small share of total restoration costs but can greatly improve cost-effectiveness and should be evaluated with financial as well as ecological metrics. • Future work should test more biowastes and soil microbiome inoculum sources and match amendments to species traits.

title: Project Report: Revitalising degraded freshwater wetlands in the Lower Loddon landscape
summary: Here, we investigated the efficacy of freshwater wetland restoration through rewetting and revegetation to mitigate carbon emissions and increase soil carbon sequestration and storage in the Lower Loddon landscape in north-western Victoria,
content: Here, we investigated the efficacy of freshwater wetland restoration through rewetting and revegetation to mitigate carbon emissions and increase soil carbon sequestration and storage in the Lower Loddon landscape in north-western Victoria, Australia. To do so, we monitored greenhouse gas fluxes (i.e., carbon dioxide [CO₂], methane [CH₄], and nitrous oxide [N₂O] fluxes), soil organic carbon and nitrogen stocks, soil moisture contents, and soil water holding capacities at four wetland sites (each site contained one restored and one degraded control site) before and after restoration.

title: Beyond gene signatures: a mechanism-based framework for cuproptosis susceptibility in non-small cell lung cancer at the metabolism–immunity interface
summary: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has become a biomarker-driven disease, yet durable control remains limited by therapeutic resistance, metabolic heterogeneity, and incomplete predictors of response. Cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of
content: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has become a biomarker-driven disease, yet durable control remains limited by therapeutic resistance, metabolic heterogeneity, and incomplete predictors of response. Cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death linked to mitochondrial respiration and lipoylated TCA-cycle proteins, offers a potential metabolic layer for patient stratification. However, the current NSCLC literature is dominated by cuproptosis-related gene scores, lncRNA models, and immune-association signatures. These studies are useful for hypothesis generation but rarely demonstrate copper flux, FDX1 dependence, lipoylated DLAT/DLST engagement, iron-sulfur cluster protein loss, or pathway-specific pharmacodynamics. We therefore organize the NSCLC literature using a mechanistic evidence matrix that separates transcriptomic association, copper-access enrichment, mitochondrial-dependence evidence, canonical target engagement, and clinical pharmacodynamic confirmation. Rather than proposing a new molecular subtype or diagnostic label, we conceptualize cuproptosis susceptibility as a continuous, mechanism-based construct defined by copper access, TCA/OXPHOS dependence, lipoylated substrate burden, detoxification capacity, and immune context. This framework reframes cuproptosis from universal copper toxicity to a conditional therapeutic vulnerability. Its clinical value will depend on biomarker-enriched trials with pharmacodynamic confirmation rather than retrospective gene signatures alone.

title: Holey Graphyne as a Promising Cathode Material for Aluminum-Ion Batteries: A First-Principles Study
summary: Abstract Aluminum-ion batteries are among the most efficient battery technologies owing to the abundance of aluminum and its trivalent redox properties. However, their practical application remains limited by the poor longevity of cathode m
content: Abstract Aluminum-ion batteries are among the most efficient battery technologies owing to the abundance of aluminum and its trivalent redox properties. However, their practical application remains limited by the poor longevity of cathode materials. In this study, we investigate the potential of the two-dimensional porous carbon allotrope holey graphyne (HGY) as a cathode material for aluminum-ion batteries. Density functional theory calculations are employed to systematically examine the interaction of AlCl4 species with HGY and assess its potential for AlCl4 storage. The results indicate that AlCl4 on the HGY surface has an adsorption energy of −1.59 eV, suggesting significant energetic stability of the adsorbate system. The monolayer HGY provides a specific capacity of 372 mAh g–1, substantially higher than that of graphite (70 mAh g–1) and graphene (155 mAh g–1). Furthermore, the calculated average open-circuit voltage of the HGY cathode is approximately 2.25 V, higher than that of graphite (2.00 V). Additionally, the low diffusion barrier of 0.04 eV indicates high mobility of AlCl4 on the HGY surface, suggesting rapid ion transport and favorable fast-charging capability. These findings highlight the significant potential of HGY as an effective cathode material for aluminum-ion batteries.

title: AZƏRBAYCANDA BƏRPA OLUNAN ENERJİ İNVESTİSİYALARININ İQTİSADİ ARTIMA TƏSİRİ
source: Journal of Science and Innovative Technologies
summary: A S Ə Tədqiqatın məqsədi -bərpa olunan enerji investisiyalarının Azərbaycanın iqtisadi inkişafına təsirini ekonometrik metodlar əsasında qiymətləndirmək, enerji sektorunda struktur transformasiyasının makroiqtisadi artımdakı rolunu müəyyənl
content: A S Ə Tədqiqatın məqsədi -bərpa olunan enerji investisiyalarının Azərbaycanın iqtisadi inkişafına təsirini ekonometrik metodlar əsasında qiymətləndirmək, enerji sektorunda struktur transformasiyasının makroiqtisadi artımdakı rolunu müəyyənləşdirmək və yaşıl enerji investisiyalarının iqtisadi şaxələndirmə strategiyasındakı yerini əsaslandırmaqdır.Tədqiqatın metodologiyası -2005-2024-cü illəri əhatə edən illik statistik məlumatlar əsasında zaman sırası üzrə çoxdəyişənli reqressiya modeli qurulmuşdur.Real ÜDM-in illik artım tempi asılı dəyişən kimi götürülmüş, bərpa olunan enerji investisiyaları əsas izahverici dəyişən kimi modelə daxil edilmişdir.Sabit kapital qoyuluşları, karbon emissiyaları və ümumi enerji istehlakı nəzarət dəyişənləri kimi istifadə olunmuş, dəyişənlərin stasionarlığı Augmented Dickey-Fuller testi ilə yoxlanılmışdır.Tədqiqatın tətbiqi əhəmiyyəti -nəticələr enerji və investisiya siyasətinin formalaşdırılması və iqtisadi şaxələndirmə strategiyasının təkmilləşdirilməsi üçün praktik əsas yaradır.Tədqiqatın nəticələri -əldə edilmiş nəticələr göstərir ki, enerji sektorunda investisiyaların struktur dəyişməsi iqtisadi artımın dinamikasına əhəmiyyətli təsir göstərir və yaşıl enerji sektorunun genişlənməsi daha dayanıqlı inkişaf modelinə keçidi stimullaşdırır.Tədqiqatın orijinallığı və elmi yeniliyi -bərpa olunan enerji investisiyalarının Azərbaycan iqtisadiyyatı kontekstində zaman sırası ekonometrik model çərçivəsində sistemli və kompleks qiymətləndirilməsi, enerji strukturu, investisiya və ekoloji amillərin vahid empirik model daxilində qarşılıqlı təsirinin təhlil edilməsidir.

title: Addressing Climate Resilience and Environmental Sustainability Approach: A Focus on Innovative Trends, Environmental Policies, and Preventive Measures
summary: Climate change is considered the major environmental challenge facing the world today. It affects the environment in many ways, including changes in ecosystems, rising temperatures, drought, melting of ice caps, rise in sea level, flooding,
content: Climate change is considered the major environmental challenge facing the world today. It affects the environment in many ways, including changes in ecosystems, rising temperatures, drought, melting of ice caps, rise in sea level, flooding, loss of biodiversity, and many more. Recent developments in biotechnology have contributed positively to mitigating climate change and adaptation. Biotechnology offers a wide range of approaches to increase climate resilience and restore the ecosystem. It improves agricultural yield and food security. Modern Biotechnology, including genetic engineering and CRISPR technology, has produced modified stress-resistant crops with high yield that significantly reduce the adverse effects of climate change. Conventional biotechnology contributed to enhancing soil productivity, greenhouse gas emissions, carbon sequestration through microbial biotechnology, the production of biofuel, and reducing pollution. Planning and monitoring strategies for environmental management and restoration further increased awareness among communities, empowering them in their role to foster environmental sustainability. Smart manufacturing and intelligence can accelerate progress towards a more sustainable and climate-resilient future.

title: Last orders? Pub closures, policy and the future of the public house in the UK
summary: The public house occupies a dual position in British society as both vital social infrastructure and a significant contributor to the hospitality economy. Yet the sector is experiencing a post-pandemic ‘perfect storm’, with closures acceler
content: The public house occupies a dual position in British society as both vital social infrastructure and a significant contributor to the hospitality economy. Yet the sector is experiencing a post-pandemic ‘perfect storm’, with closures accelerating despite sustained consumer demand. This critical review argues that the crisis reflects a policy paradox: government rhetoric celebrates pubs as community hubs, while fiscal and regulatory arrangements treat them primarily as alcohol-based commercial enterprises. Drawing on academic research, industry evidence and recent policy developments, the paper examines structural drivers of decline, including the financialised debt models of large pub-owning companies and the ‘Prime Land Paradox’, whereby the redevelopment value of pub sites may exceed their value as trading businesses. It also highlights varied trajectories: pubs of different formats face common pressures, while outcomes depend on ownership, debt exposure, location, property values and capacity to adapt. The resilience of some micropubs and community-owned venues further complicates any simple distinction between thriving gastropubs and declining wet-led locals. The paper concludes with targeted recommendations to stabilise the sector and protect pubs’ social value as accessible ‘third places’.

title: A co-simulation and optimization framework for synergistic switchable building envelopes toward carbon reduction in hot-summer and warm-winter regions
summary: Conventional static building envelopes, characterized by fixed thermal and optical properties, cannot adapt to dynamic climatic variations, thereby limiting their carbon-reduction potential in regions with complex climates. Although individ
content: Conventional static building envelopes, characterized by fixed thermal and optical properties, cannot adapt to dynamic climatic variations, thereby limiting their carbon-reduction potential in regions with complex climates. Although individual switchable building envelope (SBE) technologies have demonstrated significant energy-saving potential, the synergistic simulation and coordinated control of multi-component SBE systems remain a critical challenge due to nonlinear thermal interactions and heterogeneous control logics. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel co-simulation and optimization framework that integrates three heterogeneous SBE technologies, including a thermally responsive switchable roof, a thermochromic-photovoltaic (PV) switchable window, and a switchable heat-pipe wall, within a unified modeling environment. A high-fidelity platform coupling EnergyPlus and Python is established to resolve hour-by-hour state transitions and dynamic boundary conditions. A single-objective genetic algorithm is then employed to concurrently optimize key thermophysical and control parameters, such as optical transmittances, solar absorptivity, and temperature setpoints, to minimize annual operational carbon emissions. Applied to a typical residential building in Guangzhou (hot-summer and warm-winter region), the synergistic SBE system achieves an annual carbon reduction rate of 48.9%, equivalent to 5.5 kgCO₂/m 2 . Beyond macro-level savings, quantitative temporal analyses reveal a demand-driven regulation pattern: the switchable roof, PV window, and heat-pipe wall autonomously maintain their performance-favorable states (e.g., heat dissipation, shading, and active heat-transfer) for 66%, 29%, and 30% of the year, respectively, with switching frequency proportions below 10.1%. This research provides a robust computational methodology and quantitative insights for the performance-driven design of next-generation climate-responsive building envelopes.

title: From Public to Private Governance, and Back—Eco‐Modulation as De‐Privatization in Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)
summary: ABSTRACT The European Union is advancing circular economy policies, aimed at reducing the environmental impacts of products across their life‐cycles. Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) exemplifies this strategy. It privatizes the end‐of
content: ABSTRACT The European Union is advancing circular economy policies, aimed at reducing the environmental impacts of products across their life‐cycles. Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) exemplifies this strategy. It privatizes the end‐of‐life management of products to their producers, seeking thereby to incentivize the producer to design environmentally more sustainable products. However, EPR has failed to deliver significant improvements in product design. This article examines the EU's attempts to strengthen eco‐design in EPR through ‘eco‐modulation’. Applying the theory of competence‐and‐control, the article argues that the introduction of eco‐modulation will destabilize the public‐private balance in EPR, shifting EPR back from private towards public governance. This de‐privatization is expected to refine EPR's role within the EU's policy mix. Our findings thus offer insights for the development of EPR‐related circular economy policies, while also contributing to theories of privatization.

title: Beyond static cross-sectional views: unraveling the spatiotemporal evolution of the carbon footprints of China's mainstream photovoltaic systems
summary: Conventional life cycle assessments often lack temporal dimension and spatial variation. This study incorporates temporal dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and technological diversity to reveal the spatiotemporal evolution of the carbon foot
content: Conventional life cycle assessments often lack temporal dimension and spatial variation. This study incorporates temporal dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and technological diversity to reveal the spatiotemporal evolution of the carbon footprints of China's PV systems, quantify the mitigation effects of key drivers, and assess the PV systems' cumulative net emission reduction benefits. The results show that the carbon footprint of 1 kWp annually installed PV system declined from 1481.34–1837.15 kg CO 2 -eq in 2011 to 1060.98–1271.45 kg CO 2 -eq in 2022. Technological progress contributed almost three times that of grid decarbonization to carbon mitigation in the module manufacturing stage. Over the same period, the life cycle carbon emission per kWh generated from annually installed PV also decreased, from 70.53–75.39 g CO 2 -eq to 50.52–52.17 g CO 2 -eq, with substantial inter-provincial variation. Due to the continued influence of legacy systems installed in earlier years with higher embodied emissions, the average carbon intensity of the in-operation PV fleet remained higher than that of newly installed systems. In terms of net mitigation performance, China's operating PV fleet reached a structural turning point in 2017, when cumulative emission reductions first exceeded cumulative emissions. Scenario analysis indicates that a synergistic pathway combining efficiency improvements with grid decarbonization is critical for optimal mitigation outcomes. These results highlight the need for China to boost PV manufacturing and generation efficiency while optimizing their spatial layout. The framework developed herein can offer multi-dimensional, dynamic perspectives to underpin differentiated policy design.

title: ASSESSMENT OF ADAPTIVE RE-USE AS A STRATEGY FOR SUSTAINABLE REAL ESTATE DEVELOPMENT IN NIGERIAN CITIES
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Earth Science
summary: This study examined the applicability of adaptive reuse as a strategy for improving the functionality and sustainability of existing buildings. The study focused on identifying the major features and components applicable to adaptive reuse
content: This study examined the applicability of adaptive reuse as a strategy for improving the functionality and sustainability of existing buildings. The study focused on identifying the major features and components applicable to adaptive reuse and assessing their relevance to contemporary property development. Data were obtained from practicing Estate Surveying and Valuation firms in Lagos with a total response of 172 which was then analysed using descriptive statistics, particularly frequency, percentage, weighted mean score and standard deviation. The findings revealed that several adaptive reuse features, including flexible space tilization, improvement of building services, retention of existing building components and incorporation of sustainable design principles were applicable to existing buildings. The study further established that adaptive reuse can extend the useful life of buildings, reduce demolition & construction waste, promote more efficient utilization of existing infrastructure amongst others. However, factors such as renovation costs, building condition, regulatory requirements, technical expertise and compatibility of proposed uses may constrain its implementation. The study thus concludes that adaptive reuse provides a viable approach to sustainable property development when supported by appropriate feasibility assessment, regulatory frameworks, financing and professional expertise. Thus, the study recommended greater consideration of adaptive reuse in property development and urban regeneration programmes.

title: Advances in process integration and heat exchanger network design: Toward intelligent, sustainable, and low-carbon industrial systems
summary: The role of process integration in improving industrial energy efficiency, is increasingly important, especially in response to fossil fuel depletion and environmental concerns. This paper provides comprehensive review that focusses on exam
content: The role of process integration in improving industrial energy efficiency, is increasingly important, especially in response to fossil fuel depletion and environmental concerns. This paper provides comprehensive review that focusses on examining the heat and resource recovery process through Process Integration. The review comprehensively examines systematic process integration methodologies, including heat integration through heat exchanger network (HEN) design, water pinch analysis (mass integration), and integrated industrial decarbonization strategies. It synthesizes recent advances in energy, water, and resource integration to enhance process efficiency, minimize environmental impacts, and promote sustainable industrial systems. Additionally, the study highlights how modern tools such as process optimization techniques, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced materials further improve efficiency and innovation in process industries. Industrial applications are emphasized, showing that process integration helps industries reduce CO 2 emissions, improve sustainability, and maintain profitability in complex economic conditions.

title: Assessment of strategies to enhance the performance of a glow plug-assisted methanol engine
summary: This study presents a comprehensive investigation of a glow plug (GP)‑assisted methanol compression ignition engine operating at a high compression ratio (CR) of 19. Engine performance and emissions were evaluated under idle, mild, and high
content: This study presents a comprehensive investigation of a glow plug (GP)‑assisted methanol compression ignition engine operating at a high compression ratio (CR) of 19. Engine performance and emissions were evaluated under idle, mild, and high‑load conditions by systematically investigating the effects of injection strategy, nozzle number, and nozzle hole diameter, and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR). At high load, combustion was mainly governed by autoignition, reducing the role of GP‑initiated flame propagation. A split injection strategy with a reduced pilot fraction and delayed main injection was identified as an effective approach to suppress excessive maximum pressure rise rate (MPRR) while maintaining high indicated thermal efficiency (ITE) through optimized combustion phasing. With a fixed total nozzle flow area, varying the number of holes had a limited influence on overall performance; however, at a constant nozzle diameter, increasing the number of holes led to poorer mixture formation and higher incomplete combustion losses. At idle and mild loads, the 9‑hole injector consistently delivered higher ITE. For idle operation, the injection timing needed to be adjusted according to intake pressure to ensure stable ignition and efficient combustion. At mild load, coordinating the injection strategy with EGR was crucial for simultaneously controlling NO x emissions and MPRR while improving ITE. Compared with the baseline piston, the higher‑CR piston combined with optimized injection and EGR strategies improved ITE by approximately 1.2% at idle and 1.4% at high load. These findings provide valuable guidance for developing next‑generation carbon‑neutral engines powered by e‑methanol.

title: Key Projects and Design Strategies in Energy-Efficient Contemporary Architecture
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The built environment accounts for approximately 39% of global energy-related carbon dioxide emissions and over 36% of final energy consumption worldwide. In response to pressing climate imperatives, contemporary architecture has undergone
content: The built environment accounts for approximately 39% of global energy-related carbon dioxide emissions and over 36% of final energy consumption worldwide. In response to pressing climate imperatives, contemporary architecture has undergone a paradigm shift from conventional resource-intensive design toward ultra-low-energy, net-zero, and energy-positive building standards. This paper conducts a rigorous comparative analysis of iconic energy-efficient architectural projects utilizing the standardized IMRaD (Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion) research framework. By evaluating landmark international case studies—including The Edge (Amsterdam), Powerhouse Brattørkaia (Trondheim), Bullitt Center (Seattle), Pearl River Tower (Guangzhou), and the Bahrain World Trade Center (Manama)—this study synthesizes the core mechanisms bridging passive architectural strategies (building orientation, high-performance thermal envelopes, natural ventilation) and active technological innovations (Building-Integrated Photovoltaics [BIPV], geothermal energy loops, and IoT-driven smart automation). Quantitative metrics demonstrate that the synergistic implementation of these approaches can achieve operational energy reductions exceeding 70% relative to regional baseline standards, while generating substantial surplus energy. Finally, the study evaluates technical, financial, and policy barriers and proposes actionable frameworks for adapting green building methodologies to hot, arid continental climates such as Central Asia.

title: The politics of baselines: A political feasibility framework for energy and climate scenarios
summary: Energy, transport, and climate scenarios rely on assumptions about future taxes, subsidies, and regulations, but such policy trajectories are rarely screened for political feasibility before they enter models. This paper addresses this ofte
content: Energy, transport, and climate scenarios rely on assumptions about future taxes, subsidies, and regulations, but such policy trajectories are rarely screened for political feasibility before they enter models. This paper addresses this often-neglected step in scenario design by developing a political feasibility framework to help modellers define and compare contested policy trajectories before quantification. Building on the distinction between outside and inside views of feasibility, the framework proceeds in two steps. First, it scopes a limited set of plausible trajectories using historical precedent, institutional practice, and actor commitments. Second, it evaluates them across five feasibility dimensions informed by institutional theory and political economy. The framework is demonstrated using a Swedish rail-demand forecast from 1999, in which a flat real road fuel tax path was used in the adopted-policy baseline. The case illustrates how seemingly neutral baseline assumptions embed political judgements and how a structured feasibility assessment can make alternative policy trajectories explicit and comparable. A simplified demand model is used to simulate the effect of alternative tax trajectories on rail demand. The framework offers scenario teams and modellers a practical approach to selecting and documenting policy assumptions based on political feasibility across adopted-policy, planned-policy, and exploratory scenario settings.

title: Laser micro drilled glass semipermeable membranes for microfluidic blood oxygenators
summary: Abstract Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-saving therapy for patients with severe respiratory failure, but current technology remains limited by hemocompatibility challenges. We previously developed microfluidic oxygenat
content: Abstract Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-saving therapy for patients with severe respiratory failure, but current technology remains limited by hemocompatibility challenges. We previously developed microfluidic oxygenator prototypes utilizing rigid, flat-plate silicon membranes with etched micropores to improve blood flow dynamics and hemocompatibility. However, fabrication of the micropores with deep reactive ion etching (DRIE) is costly and limits scalability. In this study, we report the development of a low-cost alternative semipermeable membrane composed of laser micro drilled borosilicate glass bonded to a thin, gas-permeable polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layer. Uniform arrays of through-pores (10 μm diameter, 20 μm pitch) were successfully fabricated through the full 400 μm thickness of the glass substrate, achieving near-vertical sidewalls and robust mechanical integrity. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed precise pore geometry and uniform distribution. Oxygen transfer performance was evaluated using a benchtop flow circuit under varying sweep gas pressures and water flow rates. Compared to prior PDMS-on-silicon membranes, the glass-based membranes demonstrated improved oxygen transfer (volume percent: 0.59 ± 0.13% [laser micro drilling] versus 0.28 ± 0.09% [DRIE]) due to elimination of non-porous support regions. Importantly, laser micro drilling reduced projected membrane fabrication costs by more than an order of magnitude (estimated membrane costs for a 4000 cm 2 neonatal oxygenator: $100,000 [DRIE] versus $8500 [laser micro drilling]), supporting the feasibility of scaling toward clinically relevant ECMO devices.

title: Effect of Carboxymethyl Chitosan and Genipin on the Structural, Water Uptake, and Thermomechanical Properties of Zein‐Based Biodegradable Materials
summary: ABSTRACT Zein is an insoluble prolamin protein extracted from different by‐products of the corn industry. More recently, the thermoplastic behavior and ability to melt when heated displayed by zein/glycerol blends (zein/Glycerol) have highl
content: ABSTRACT Zein is an insoluble prolamin protein extracted from different by‐products of the corn industry. More recently, the thermoplastic behavior and ability to melt when heated displayed by zein/glycerol blends (zein/Glycerol) have highlighted its use in versatile plastic thermal processing techniques. In this study, the effect of additives that may reinforce the resulting materials is examined. A water‐soluble chitosan derivative, carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCH), was included in zein/CMCH/Glycerol systems to assess the feasibility of complexation between zein and CMCH as a way to tune the hydrophilicity and mechanical properties of the material. Additionally, genipin (GNP), a natural cross‐linker, was added either to zein/Glycerol or zein/CMCH/Glycerol systems to reinforce the mechanical properties. In this context, Young's modulus ( E ) increased from around 16 to 40 MPa when GNP was added at 0.5 mM, while maintaining its water uptake (WUC) around 170%. The joint role of CMCH and GNP was only synergistic at low GNP concentrations (0.01 mM). However, at high GNP concentrations (0.5 mM), no enhancement of the mechanical properties was observed, despite the greater thermal resistance. Thus, the properties of zein‐based materials can be improved by selecting a suitable GNP concentration, which facilitates the development of bioplastics with specific applications.
