title: Unsteady airfoil aerodynamics in attached flow: From unsteady thin-airfoil theory to wind turbine implementation
summary: Abstract. Attached-flow unsteady aerodynamics form the foundation of the dynamic stall models used in wind turbine aerodynamic and aeroelastic codes. These conditions are particularly important over the outboard blade region, which dominate
content: Abstract. Attached-flow unsteady aerodynamics form the foundation of the dynamic stall models used in wind turbine aerodynamic and aeroelastic codes. These conditions are particularly important over the outboard blade region, which dominates power production and aerodynamic loading. In this region, the angle of attack and relative velocity are unsteady while the flow remains predominantly attached. A complete engineering model for unsteady airfoil aerodynamic loads combines several distinct elements, including airfoil polar lookup, attached-flow shed wake memory, non-circulatory loads, consistent definitions of force magnitude and direction, and, subsequently, separated-flow dynamics. Although the underlying theory is classical, to the authors' knowledge, existing descriptions do not provide a complete and internally consistent route for implementing these attached-flow contributions in wind turbine aerodynamic solvers. This work addresses this gap by focusing on the attached-flow component and presenting all attached-flow contributions in the form of lift, drag, and moment coefficients for implementation in generalized lifting-line methods, including blade-element momentum (BEM), lifting-line (LL), and actuator-line (AL) methods. The formulation is designed for combination with 2-D airfoil polars obtained from measurements or computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Starting from the classical dimensional loads of unsteady thin-airfoil theory, the circulatory and non-circulatory contributions are derived in coefficient form, and the implications of the associated modeling choices are clarified. In particular, the shed wake memory is formulated using the downwash velocity rather than the angle of attack as the aerodynamic state variable. Because the 2-D theory is classical, verification focuses on its rotor-level implementation. The coned straight blade case provides a cross-method benchmark and quantifies the errors in rotor-integrated thrust and power caused by omitting three required contributions that are often omitted. Among these, the lift direction projection contribution has the largest influence on power. Omitting the mid-chord heaving acceleration contribution eliminates the non-circulatory normal force cancellation and produces a thrust error. The zero-onset flow vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) case verifies that, in the ideal thin-airfoil limit, all circulatory and non-circulatory contributions cancel, resulting in zero total rotor torque.

title: Reconciling economic development, energy access, and decarbonization in Africa’s renewable energy transition: a bibliometric review
summary: Africa’s position in the global energy debate is marked by a persistent imbalance. The continent contributes only a small share of global CO 2 emissions, but it remains highly exposed to climate change and still faces deep energy-access def
content: Africa’s position in the global energy debate is marked by a persistent imbalance. The continent contributes only a small share of global CO 2 emissions, but it remains highly exposed to climate change and still faces deep energy-access deficits. For this reason, the renewable energy transition in Africa cannot be read only as a decarbonization agenda. It also raises questions of development, affordability and reliability. This article reviews how these issues have been treated in the scientific literature through a bibliometric analysis of 107 Scopus-indexed documents published between 2010 and 2025. Using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix, the paper examines publication trends, influential works, scientific actors, collaboration patterns and keyword structures. The results point to four main clusters: Technological Decarbonization and Energy Systems; Green Finance and Economic Development; Energy Access, Poverty and Security; and Emissions, Efficiency and Socioeconomic Co-benefits. These clusters do not form separate debates. Rather, they show that the literature increasingly frames Africa’s renewable energy transition as a trilemma in which economic development, energy access and decarbonization must be considered together. The review also identifies remaining gaps, particularly in the measurement of energy access and renewable energy, the treatment of financing and governance constraints, the use of stronger causal methods, and the integration of energy justice, gender and digital inclusion into transition research.

title: Petrol Ürünleri İthalatının Tahmininde Geleneksel, Hibrit ve Meta-Sezgisel Yaklaşımlar: SARIMA, RF-LSTM ve DE-HW Modellerinin Karşılaştırılması
summary: Bu çalışma, Türkiye’nin 2030 Sürdürülebilir Kalkınma Amaçları doğrultusunda ekonomik ve çevresel sürdürülebilirlik planlamalarına katkı sağlamak amacıyla, 27.10 GTİP kodlu petrol ürünleri ithalat miktarını 2030 yılına kadar tahmin etmeyi ve
content: Bu çalışma, Türkiye’nin 2030 Sürdürülebilir Kalkınma Amaçları doğrultusunda ekonomik ve çevresel sürdürülebilirlik planlamalarına katkı sağlamak amacıyla, 27.10 GTİP kodlu petrol ürünleri ithalat miktarını 2030 yılına kadar tahmin etmeyi ve farklı tahmin modellerinin performanslarını karşılaştırmayı amaçlamaktadır. 2007–2026 dönemine ait aylık ithalat verileri kullanılarak Mevsimsel Otoregresif Entegre Hareketli Ortalama (SARIMA), Diferansiyel Evrim algoritmasıyla optimize edilmiş Holt-Winters (DE-HW) ve derin öğrenme tabanlı Hibrit Rastgele Orman–Kısa Uzun Vadeli Bellek (RF-LSTM) modelleri uygulanmıştır. Model performansları Kök Ortalama Kare Hata (RMSE), Ortalama Kare Hata (MSE), Ortalama Mutlak Hata (MAD) ve Ortalama Mutlak Yüzde Hata (MAPE) ölçütleriyle değerlendirilmiştir. Bulgular, Hibrit RF-LSTM modelinin eğitim ve doğrulama setlerinde sırasıyla %7 ve %5 MAPE değerleriyle en yüksek tahmin performansını sağladığını göstermiştir. Elde edilen 2030 tahminleri, enerji ithalatı bütçe yönetimi, lojistik planlama ve stratejik rezerv kapasitesinin belirlenmesine yönelik politika kararları için veri temelli bir çerçeve sunmaktadır.

title: STRATEGIES FOR ACHIEVING SUSTAINABILITY IN DESIGN-DRIVEN FOOD PACKAGING: A MULTI-CASE EVALUATION WITHIN A CIRCULAR ECONOMY FRAMEWORK
source: International Journal of African Research Sustainability Studies
summary: This study investigates how design-driven strategies enhance sustainability in food packaging within a circular economy framework. It identifies how design choices mediate environmental performance, usability and consumer behaviour, moving
content: This study investigates how design-driven strategies enhance sustainability in food packaging within a circular economy framework. It identifies how design choices mediate environmental performance, usability and consumer behaviour, moving beyond material substitution as the sole sustainability strategy. A qualitative multi-case study using secondary data was adopted, supported by a design-based evaluation matrix applied to five packaging types (bioplastic tray, paper carton, glass jar, reusable modular container and compostable pouch). Thematic analysis compared cases across environmental, functional and behavioural dimensions using a transparent 0–3 scoring rubric. Design effectiveness depends less on material novelty and more on systemic compatibility with recovery infrastructures and user interaction. Packaging featuring intuitive functionality (resealability, clear disposal cues) and closed-loop integration achieved higher sustainability scores. Glass jars and reusable containers demonstrated superior circular-economy alignment; biobased and compostable materials underperformed due to infrastructural and behavioural constraints. The study introduces a design-based evaluation matrix integrating behavioural, functional and environmental criteria, offering a practical decision-support tool for designers, policymakers and waste managers. Reliance on secondary data and five cases limits generalisability. Future work should combine life-cycle metrics with primary consumer insights.

title: Arquitectura colectiva de su tiempo que buscó en el rural, crear comunidad
summary: Un viaje de ida y vuelta. Una invitación a retornar al momento proyectual, colándonos en el pensamiento de dos arquitectos que se aproximaron a un conjunto histórico consolidado como palimpsesto: Fregenal de la Sierra. Ahí descubriremos las
content: Un viaje de ida y vuelta. Una invitación a retornar al momento proyectual, colándonos en el pensamiento de dos arquitectos que se aproximaron a un conjunto histórico consolidado como palimpsesto: Fregenal de la Sierra. Ahí descubriremos las narrativas que les guiaron en la concepción de esta arquitectura residencial colectiva, poco común en contextos rurales y su firme deseo de servir a la sociedad, construyendo una nueva manera de habitarla desde una nueva comunidad.

title: Synergistic evolution of wind turbine design and AI infrastructure: A perspective on policy and future directions
summary: The world is undergoing simultaneous digital and energy revolutions. Rising energy demand, together with rapid expansion of digital infrastructure, is reshaping the relevance and design priorities of modern renewable energy systems. Among t
content: The world is undergoing simultaneous digital and energy revolutions. Rising energy demand, together with rapid expansion of digital infrastructure, is reshaping the relevance and design priorities of modern renewable energy systems. Among these, wind energy remains a major renewable resource, with continuous developments in turbine design, simulation, control, and deployment strategies. This perspective highlights the co-evolution of wind turbine research and computational infrastructure, particularly in the context of artificial intelligence, graphics processing units, application-specific integrated circuits, and high-performance computing. It briefly reviews wind turbine simulation approaches, from early analytical models to modern high-fidelity large-eddy simulations. The article also discusses system-level improvements and policy measures required to support renewable energy integration, grid planning, and sustainable digital growth. This perspective argues that wind-energy development and AI infrastructure are undergoing a mutually reinforced co-evolution, linking advances in computational methods and hardware with AI-enabled wind-system design while creating new requirements for renewable generation, grid integration, and energy-system planning. Overall, it emphasizes the need for coordinated energy and computing strategies to address future decarbonization challenges.

title: The eagle as an agricultural ally: quantifying the predation of medically significant snakes and public perception gaps in the Thar Desert
summary: Introduction Effective raptor conservation in human-dominated landscapes requires understanding both biological realities and local socio-ecological perceptions. This study investigated the dietary ecology and community perception of the sh
content: Introduction Effective raptor conservation in human-dominated landscapes requires understanding both biological realities and local socio-ecological perceptions. This study investigated the dietary ecology and community perception of the short-toed snake eagle ( Circaetus gallicus ) in the agropastoral landscapes of the Thar Desert, India. Methods Autonomous nest camera monitoring was used to observe a single representative breeding pair during the chick-provisioning phase. Concurrently, a structured survey of 87 local community members assessed traditional ecological knowledge and socio-cultural perceptions across different age cohorts and livelihoods (traditional pastoralists and agriculturalists). Results Camera monitoring recorded 62 prey deliveries, revealing similar proportions of snakes (order Ophidia) and large desert lizards (order Lacertilia) during the observation period. Baseline perceptions were highly positive, with strong consensus on the eagle’s cultural value (median=4.0, IQR=1.0) and conservation importance. Furthermore, respondents demonstrated an acute awareness of the eagle’s role as a biological snake controller (median=3.67, IQR=1.0). However, quantitative analysis revealed a highly significant ecological blind spot (p<0.001) regarding the raptor’s reliance on desert lizards, with widespread lack of awareness (median=1.0) cutting equally across all generations and livelihood groups. Discussion To foster long-term coexistence, we recommend an “agricultural ally” conservation framework. By actively integrating empirical nest camera evidence with the community’s existing spiritual ethos of compassion ( Jeev-Daya ), conservationists can bridge this cognitive gap. Demonstrating that culturally revered snake controllers depend fundamentally on lizards can transform local perspectives on native open scrublands, protecting these critical habitats from industrial fragmentation.

title: Optimal Allocation of Medium-Voltage Distributed Generation Under Uncertain Load Conditions
source: London Journal of Research In Computer Science and Technology
summary: Electrical power distribution systems are constantly expanding, and their complexity is increasing due to factors such as the growth and unpredictability of electricity demand driven by population growth and industrial development. The inte
content: Electrical power distribution systems are constantly expanding, and their complexity is increasing due to factors such as the growth and unpredictability of electricity demand driven by population growth and industrial development. The integration of renewable energy sources into the electrical matrix helps meet this demand and reduce losses, but issues like voltage variation can affect distribution system performance. This work addresses the integration of distributed generation in medium voltage electrical distribution systems, focusing on loads under. Using metaheuristic approaches, the study explores solutions for operational challenges, including the implementation of an optimization algorithm, the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), in an IEEE 123-bus distribution system. The results highlight the effectiveness of metaheuristic in optimizing the allocation of energy sources, contributing to a more efficient and sustainable integration of distributed generation in distribution systems.

title: THE LEGISLATIVE POWER IN THE EUROPEAN UNION
summary: The process of European integration has been characterized by an institutional structure distinct from that of other international organizations. Moreover, its evolution has brought it closer to the model found in nation-states. This is evi
content: The process of European integration has been characterized by an institutional structure distinct from that of other international organizations. Moreover, its evolution has brought it closer to the model found in nation-states. This is evident in the distribution of powers —particularly regarding legislative authority— as the system has shifted from a model where the body representing the Member States held full decision-making power to one in which legislative authority is shared between the Council and the European Parliament, featuring characteristics of a bicameral legislative model. The current legal system in the European Union was defined by the Lisbon Treaty. Which enabled the generalization of the codecision procedure, now officially called the ordinary legislative procedure. Through this mechanism, the institution elected by universal and direct suffrage by European citizens fulfils its role as a parliament—namely, exercising legislative power—, although shared with the Council.

title: Urbicidal planning: Managing risk in “dangerous” cities
summary: The term “urbicide” has been used to describe the physical and material destruction of cities, specifically as a means to annihilate the material foundations of heterogeneity. Yet the act of physical destruction often works in tandem with p
content: The term “urbicide” has been used to describe the physical and material destruction of cities, specifically as a means to annihilate the material foundations of heterogeneity. Yet the act of physical destruction often works in tandem with parallel practices of construction that seek to create alternative urban futures. In this paper, we argue that “urbicidal planning” is a recurring logic of planning practice even in cases that do not involve the wholesale destruction of infrastructure. Often, such planning rests on a socio-spatial discourse that targets specific racial, ethnic, or social groups and their corresponding geographies as threats to political and developmental goals. It is therefore a preventative logic of city-making that rests on the eradication of particular urban risks, motivated by the need to pacify or eliminate the present and future dangers of the city. Moreover, it is a preemptive form of eradication that is often dissociated across time and space. We demonstrate these arguments through two illustrative vignettes: the policies and practices of the French protectorate in Morocco in the early 20th century and those of foreign humanitarian and military actors in Haiti during the United Nations’ peacekeeping operation in the beginning of the 21st century.

title: Analisis Dinamis Pengaruh Variasi Tekanan Hidrolik terhadap Tegangan dan Arus Motor Main Inlet Valve di PLTA Orya Genyem
summary: Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Air (PLTA) memiliki sistem operasi yang bergantung pada keandalan berbagai peralatan utama, salah satunya Main Inlet Valve (MIV) yang berfungsi mengatur aliran air menuju turbin. Sistem hidrolik pada MIV berperan d
content: Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Air (PLTA) memiliki sistem operasi yang bergantung pada keandalan berbagai peralatan utama, salah satunya Main Inlet Valve (MIV) yang berfungsi mengatur aliran air menuju turbin. Sistem hidrolik pada MIV berperan dalam menghasilkan gaya aktuasi, sehingga perubahan tekanan hidrolik dapat memengaruhi beban kerja motor penggerak. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh variasi tekanan hidrolik terhadap tegangan dan arus motor Main Inlet Valve pada PLTA Orya Genyem. Penelitian menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan pendekatan korelasional berdasarkan data pengukuran langsung tekanan hidrolik, tegangan motor, dan arus motor pada variasi tekanan 10–20 MPa. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi, wawancara, pengukuran lapangan, dan studi literatur. Data dianalisis menggunakan analisis deskriptif dan regresi linear sederhana untuk mengetahui hubungan antara tekanan hidrolik dengan parameter kelistrikan motor. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa peningkatan tekanan hidrolik menyebabkan peningkatan arus motor dari 7,11 A pada tekanan 10 MPa menjadi 11,85 A pada tekanan 20 MPa, sedangkan tegangan motor mengalami penurunan relatif kecil dari 392,00 V menjadi 387,67 V. Analisis regresi menunjukkan hubungan yang sangat kuat antara tekanan hidrolik terhadap arus motor dengan nilai R² sebesar 0,9919 dan terhadap tegangan motor dengan nilai R² sebesar 0,9888. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa tekanan hidrolik berpengaruh terhadap kinerja kelistrikan motor MIV, terutama terhadap perubahan arus, sehingga pemantauan tekanan hidrolik dan arus motor dapat digunakan sebagai indikator evaluasi kondisi operasi dan pencegahan gangguan sistem.

title: Surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization of hybrid thermoelectric–liquid battery thermal management systems
summary: Battery thermal management is critical for ensuring the safety, performance, and longevity of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles. This study presents a hybrid battery thermal management system (BTMS) integrating thermoelectric coole
tags: Thermal management of electronic devices and systems
content: Battery thermal management is critical for ensuring the safety, performance, and longevity of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles. This study presents a hybrid battery thermal management system (BTMS) integrating thermoelectric coolers (TECs) with serpentine mini-channel cold plates for cylindrical lithium-ion battery packs. A system-level multi-objective optimization framework combining a genetic algorithm with an artificial neural network surrogate model is developed to simultaneously minimize maximum cell temperature, temperature difference, total power consumption, and system mass. Three representative designs were identified from the resulting Pareto front, and the knee-point design was selected for detailed evaluation, achieving a maximum temperature of 28.88 °C, a temperature difference of 2.04 °C, a power consumption of 64.27 W, and a system mass of 2.42 kg, representing reductions of 10.45 %, 14.51 %, 15.98 %, and 1.82 %, respectively, compared to a baseline design. Independent CFD re-evaluation of several Pareto-optimal solutions, including the selected design, confirms the surrogate model’s predictive accuracy, and sensitivity analysis identifies TEC input current as the strongest driver of thermal performance. Under both the NEDC and the WLTC, the optimized BTMS maintains stable thermal performance, with maximum temperature and temperature difference increasing by only 2.45 °C/1.25 °C and 1.58 °C/0.99 °C, respectively. The hybrid configuration also reaches a safe operating temperature approximately 53 % faster than the baseline following elevated initial conditions and remains robust under elevated coolant inlet temperatures (up to 45 °C) and high discharge rates (up to 2C). The proposed framework contributes to improving the thermal management of battery energy storage systems, with practical implications for electric vehicle range and battery longevity.

title: Cellulose-Based Nanosponges with PEDOT:PSS as Pressure Sensors with Tunable Elasticity: A Study on Modulation of Mechanical Properties and Pressure Response
summary: Abstract This study investigates the suitability of sustainable, highly porous nanosponges, composed of TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibers (TOCNF) and branched polyethylenimine (bPEI, cross-linker), as scaffolds for PEDOT:PSS poly(3,4-ethy
content: Abstract This study investigates the suitability of sustainable, highly porous nanosponges, composed of TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibers (TOCNF) and branched polyethylenimine (bPEI, cross-linker), as scaffolds for PEDOT:PSS poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrenesulfonate dip coating to design piezoresistive pressure sensors. The mechanical properties of the nanosponges were tuned by introducing citric acid (CA) as a co-cross-linker, varying its content from 0% to 18% relative to the moles of primary amines of bPEI. The resulting devices functioned effectively as pressure sensors, with the best performance achieved at 3% CA. This configuration operated reliably up to 200 kPa and reached a sensitivity of 1.96 × 10–3 mA·kPa–1. These findings confirm the promising performance of cellulose-based nanosponges and pave the way for their integration into lightweight and environmentally friendly pressure sensors.

title: Edge‐Based Information‐Centric Networking for Enhanced Message Discrimination in Vehicular Ad‐Hoc Networks
summary: ABSTRACT Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) are central to Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), but practical deployment remains constrained by communication latency, scalability, and privacy requirements. This study develops an edge‐b
content: ABSTRACT Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) are central to Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), but practical deployment remains constrained by communication latency, scalability, and privacy requirements. This study develops an edge‐based Information‐Centric Networking (ICN) framework integrated with blockchain technology. Raspberry Pi units equipped with cameras perform real‐time incident detection and classification using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and You Only Look Once v8 (YOLOv8). Frame extraction, noise reduction, and data augmentation increased the reported detection accuracy from 70% to 97%. Severity‐based incident prioritization reduced latency to 112 ms in low‐density networks and 128 ms in high‐density networks, while packet loss decreased from 12.12% to 6.34% and throughput increased from 600 to 700 Mbps. The ICN layer also enabled high‐priority alerts to reach vehicle dashboards in less than 1 s. The evaluated configuration scaled to 400 mobile routers and 20 access points while maintaining low latency and stable communication. These findings indicate that the proposed architecture can support real‐time, secure, and efficient vehicular communication in ITS environments.

title: Reproducible AES-128 Benchmarking and Security-Assessment Boundary for Resource-Constrained IoT Environments
source: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
summary: To meet the constraints of resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices, the encryption mechanism must provide confidentiality while adding little complexity and memory usage. This work presents a reproducible Advanced Encryption S
content: To meet the constraints of resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices, the encryption mechanism must provide confidentiality while adding little complexity and memory usage. This work presents a reproducible Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) -128 performance benchmarking and security boundary analysis for constrained IoT applications. Before any benchmarking, the AES-128 implementation was tested against a standard cryptographic test vector. Encryption and decryption were verified based on the successful plaintext recovery. To enhance methodological rigour and reproducibility, the experimental design used 250 runs over four IoT-relevant payload sizes (16 bytes, 1 KB, 10 KB, and 1 MB) executed in a controlled execution environment. The evaluation consisted of performance metrics that include encryption time, decryption time, execution stability, standard deviation and memory variation, analysed in a controlled execution environment. Results show that while AES-128 exhibits stable run-to-run timing for small and medium payloads, execution overhead and timing variance increased for 1 MB workloads in the implementation presented using Python. It also points out that process-level memory profiling is limited for small workloads since they are impacted by noise and variability in the measurement. Reduced-key brute-force attack analysis is shown only as a pedagogical example of key-space growth and makes no claim about the security of full AES configurations. Likewise, side-channel attack concerns are qualitatively addressed because attack analysis was performed. The study provides an AES-128 benchmarking methodology for IoT security evaluation that is statistically founded and fully reproducible.

title: Global Lithium Dynamics: Us-China Geopolitical Competition and Its Implications on Energy Security in South Asian Region
summary: This paper examines the implications of U.S.–China geopolitical competition over lithium resources for energy security, with a focus on South Asia. Home to nearly 25% of the world's population, South Asia is a developing region facing risin
content: This paper examines the implications of U.S.–China geopolitical competition over lithium resources for energy security, with a focus on South Asia. Home to nearly 25% of the world's population, South Asia is a developing region facing rising energy demands driven by economic growth. Lithium is a critical resource due to its central role in rechargeable batteries used in electric vehicles, smartphones, laptops, and renewable energy storage systems, supporting the global shift from petroleum to clean energy. The lithium-ion battery market has expanded rapidly, becoming one of the fastest-growing raw material markets worldwide. Reflecting its strategic importance, lithium was declared essential to U.S. economic and national security in 2018, and to the European Union's industrial strategy in 2020. This shift has intensified U.S.–China competition over lithium production, processing, and supply chains, influencing energy security, trade, and pricing dynamics in South Asia. The paper assesses how this rivalry may shape regional development.

title: A Blackbox Access to Load Forecasting Models Is All You Need to Breach Privacy
source: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data
summary: Machine learning and deep learning models play a crucial role in optimizing smart grid operations. While offering valuable utility, concerns arise regarding their exposure of sensitive information. Previous studies have focused on optimizin
content: Machine learning and deep learning models play a crucial role in optimizing smart grid operations. While offering valuable utility, concerns arise regarding their exposure of sensitive information. Previous studies have focused on optimizing load forecasting models, such as Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), overlooking their associated risks of revealing private information about the consumer. Existing privacy preservation studies have focused mainly on addressing risks associated with classification models, but similar concerns may exist in their load forecasting counterparts. In this paper, we investigate potential data leakage from deep learning-based load forecasting models. Our study analyzes the ability of personalized forecasting models to leak global properties about the consumer. We present a novel property inference attack tailored for forecasting models that can be executed in a black box setting, with only query access to the target model. We demonstrate that black box access to an LSTM model can reveal sensitive information about the user, with the attack achieving results comparable to having direct access to the data (with the difference being as low as 1% in Area Under the ROC Curve). This highlights the necessity of securing access to forecasting models with the same level of diligence as the data itself.

title: Hybrid quantum learning based fault detection method for an active distribution system
summary: Abstract Modern distribution systems with integrated renewable energy sources exhibit complex fault behaviour due to inverter-based generation and bidirectional power flow, making conventional protection methods less reliable. This paper pr
content: Abstract Modern distribution systems with integrated renewable energy sources exhibit complex fault behaviour due to inverter-based generation and bidirectional power flow, making conventional protection methods less reliable. This paper presents a PMU-based fault detection framework for active distribution networks using hybrid quantum machine learning (QML) techniques. A modified IEEE 34-bus system with solar photovoltaic and wind distributed generation units is modelled, and faults are systematically created near the DG locations with wide variation in fault type, location, and fault resistance. PMU-measured voltage and current phasors are processed using symmetrical component analysis to extract compact numerical features representing peak magnitudes and phase angles of sequence components. Two hybrid QML models, namely Quantum Random Forest (QRF) and Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC), are developed within a unified modular framework. In the QRF model, quantum computation is employed for nonlinear feature transformation, followed by classical ensemble learning for classification. In the VQC model, parameterized quantum circuits learn nonlinear decision boundaries through variational optimization. The performance results show a clear difference between QRF and VQC. QRF gives stable and reliable fault detection with high precision, but VQC performs better overall. The VQC testing accuracy reached 99.8%, with precision of 99.7%, recall of 100%, and an F1-score of 99.9%. These results were achieved through the consideration of SMOTE for class balancing and feature selection for enhanced model performance. When compared with classical and deep learning approaches, the advantage of using numerical PMU data with hybrid quantum learning becomes more evident, especially since no image-based signal conversion is required. Overall, hybrid QML can be considered as a useful technique for advanced protection system.

title: Renewable expansion and storage for energy resilience under megadrought conditions: A regional optimization study of the Biobío power system in Chile
summary: This dataset contains the processed input data, Calliope model configuration files, scenario definitions, scripts, and selected outputs supporting the study “Renewable expansion and storage for energy resilience under megadrought conditions
content: This dataset contains the processed input data, Calliope model configuration files, scenario definitions, scripts, and selected outputs supporting the study “Renewable expansion and storage for energy resilience under megadrought conditions: A regional optimization study of the Biobío power system in Chile”. The dataset supports the reproduction of the baseline, megadrought, renewable expansion, and fossil-free scenarios evaluated in the study. The energy system model was implemented in Calliope v0.6.8 and complemented with geospatial preprocessing in QGIS.

title: Operational assessment of deep learning-based multi-horizon wind speed forecasting for wind energy applications
summary: Accurate multi-horizon wind speed forecasting is important for wind energy operation, yet forecast reliability generally decreases as the prediction horizon increases. This study evaluates LSTM, GRU, and BiLSTM models using 10-min meteorolo
content: Accurate multi-horizon wind speed forecasting is important for wind energy operation, yet forecast reliability generally decreases as the prediction horizon increases. This study evaluates LSTM, GRU, and BiLSTM models using 10-min meteorological measurements from the Abhar Wind Farm, Iran. The models were compared at horizons from 10 min to 24 h, and GRU was selected for extended analysis based on competitive accuracy and lower parameter count. Using an independent full-year test dataset, GRU achieved RMSE values of 0.903 and 3.885 m/s at 10 min and 24 h, respectively. Although absolute accuracy deteriorated with horizon, RMSE skill relative to persistence increased from 4.85% to 22.49%. Operational Accuracy Ratio analysis across ±0.5–±2.0 m/s tolerances confirmed consistent horizon-dependent degradation. Seasonal evaluation showed the same general trend throughout the year. The results demonstrate the importance of forecast horizon in operational wind speed forecasting.

title: Impact of sub-hourly wind dynamics on green hydrogen yield and electrolyser lifetime
summary: Direct wind-to-hydrogen systems, in which a wind farm supplies power to an electrolyser without a firm grid connection, must accommodate the full variability of the wind resource, yet many existing techno-economic and design studies rely on
content: Direct wind-to-hydrogen systems, in which a wind farm supplies power to an electrolyser without a firm grid connection, must accommodate the full variability of the wind resource, yet many existing techno-economic and design studies rely on input data with temporal resolutions of several minutes to one hour. This coarse averaging can mask short-term power fluctuations that drive electrolyser performance, cycling and degradation. This paper presents a novel wind-to-electrolyser model that synthesises effective wind speed suitable for a power curve wind model at 1 Hz, combining low-frequency trend variation, mesoscale wind speed changes and Kaimal turbulence, validated against aeroelastic simulations. The resulting power output is supplied to a PEM electrolyser model incorporating bank-level thermal dynamics and steady-state, cyclic and on/off degradation, enabling the effect of wind-power variability on long-term electrolyser performance to be quantified. Using 10-year simulations of a wind farm at a site in Orkney, Scotland, two scenarios are investigated: the effect of wind farm size (1–10 turbines) and input temporal resolution (1 s, 1 min, 10 min) on power variability, degradation and hydrogen production; and the effect of turbine configuration for a fixed installed capacity (three 5 MW turbines versus one 15 MW turbine). Results show that coarser temporal resolution substantially overestimates hydrogen production, particularly for small wind farms, where 10-minute-averaged data increase predicted output by up to 428% relative to 1 s data, primarily due to underestimated on/off and cyclic degradation. Aggregating turbines and, to a lesser extent, using larger rotors both smooth the power input and reduce this sensitivity, though the effect remains significant even for 10-turbine farms. These findings demonstrate that high-frequency wind power variability must be explicitly considered in the design and performance assessment of wind-to-hydrogen systems.

title: A novel in-situ electric heating high-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage system for renewable energy curtailment accommodation
summary: The volatility and intermittency of renewable energy power generation such as wind and solar energy have led to a severe electricity curtailment problem. As a seasonal thermal storage technology featuring large capacity and low cost, High-T
content: The volatility and intermittency of renewable energy power generation such as wind and solar energy have led to a severe electricity curtailment problem. As a seasonal thermal storage technology featuring large capacity and low cost, High-Temperature Aquifer Thermal Energy Storage (HT-ATES) provides an effective solution for renewable energy accommodation. However, traditional HT-ATES systems suffer from low thermal recovery efficiency due to buoyancy flow induced by hot water injection, which restricts their large-scale application. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel in-situ electric heating HT-ATES method that directly heats the aquifer matrix by leveraging the uniform heating characteristic of solid electric heating technology. An electro-thermal-fluid multi-physics coupled numerical simulation model was established, and its reliability was verified via scaled-down experiments. Simulation results show that the thermal recovery efficiency of a single module of the novel HT-ATES system is significantly higher than that of the traditional system; after 90 days of operation, the average temperature of recovered hot water reaches 84.65 °C, and the energy storage capacity per unit aquifer volume is increased by approximately 57.1% compared with the ground heat exchanger method. Finally, the system configuration was optimized through parameter sensitivity analysis, and the potential of the novel HT-ATES system to accommodate renewable energy curtailment was verified based on the electricity curtailment data of a wind farm in Northeast China.

title: APPLICATION OF DOUBLE SKIN GLASS FACADE TO ENHANCE THERMAL COMFORT IN THE DESIGN OF RAILWAY TERMINAL BUILDING BAUCHI, NIGERIA
source: International Journal of African Research Sustainability Studies
summary: The quest to enhance indoor comfort has led to substantial innovation of building envelopes which is considered a viable option for buildings to work with climate by responding to heat gains. The use of Double Skin Glass Façade (DSGF) can l
content: The quest to enhance indoor comfort has led to substantial innovation of building envelopes which is considered a viable option for buildings to work with climate by responding to heat gains. The use of Double Skin Glass Façade (DSGF) can lower the amount of heat gained via building envelopes however, most of the studies on DSGF where carried in cold climates. In this study, the effect of the DSGF cavity depth, envelope type, material and configuration on thermal comfort in wet, dry climate of Bauchi is evaluated. Using the chosen case study of railway buildings, the buildings were simulated, temperatures were measured, and an Autodesk Revit 2017 reference base case model was created. After performing a thermal simulation of the base case, cavity depths and envelope material configurations were changed, put into use, and thermally simulated using Design Builder to produce annual and monthly internal temperatures for the peak wettest months (April, March, and May). Results from the Simulations of the optimized model indicates that DSGF model having a cavity depth of 300mm with fully glazed envelope of 6mm thick Low-E glass coating with box window DSF, a reduction in temperature of 4.620, 4.290, and 4.040. Subsequently, the research findings indicate that integrating a DSGF model with adequate selection of cavity depth and envelope material choice has led to a notable reduction in internal temperatures thereby, reducing dependency on mechanical system whilst enhancing building performance, suggesting its effectiveness in improving thermal comfort within the proposed railway station building.

title: Toward real-time wave forecasting via data-driven reduced-order modeling with data assimilation
summary: Reliable wave forecasts are a cornerstone of coastal risk management and offshore operations, yet operational products remain expensive to generate at high resolution and can be insufficiently calibrated for decision-making under uncertaint
content: Reliable wave forecasts are a cornerstone of coastal risk management and offshore operations, yet operational products remain expensive to generate at high resolution and can be insufficiently calibrated for decision-making under uncertainty. We present a hybrid forecasting framework that couples data-driven reduced-order modeling with sequential data assimilation to produce flow-dependent, spatially coherent ensembles of significant wave height over the North Sea. The approach learns a nonlinear manifold of sea-state variability with a convolutional autoencoder trained on WAM wave model, then advances the system in a delay-embedded latent space using a control-aware linear dynamical model driven by low-dimensional controls extracted from wind forecasts. Uncertainty is propagated with an ensemble formulation, and buoy observations are assimilated using a deterministic ensemble square-root filter with innovation-based adaptive inflation to maintain reliability during energetic events. The proposed system reproduces the timing and magnitude of storm growth–peak–decay across the buoy network, while preserving physically consistent basin-scale storm footprints in reconstructed fields. Errors are spatially organized and regime dependent, concentrating near storm maxima where wind–wave misalignment, swell influence, and representativeness effects are strongest, but the assimilation layer mitigates drift and reduces persistent offsets without introducing spatial artifacts. Beyond forecasting, we introduce an observability metric derived from the posterior latent covariance and the decoder sensitivity, yielding time-varying maps that identify where additional in-situ measurements would most reduce forecast uncertainty. The introduced method provides a computationally efficient, uncertainty-aware alternative that bridges physics-based spectral modeling and purely data-driven prediction for operational decision support.

title: МОДЕЛЮВАННЯ ТЕПЛОВИХ ПРОЦЕСІВ ГІБРИДНОГО ГЕЛІОКОЛЕКТОРА
summary: Запропоновано вдосконалену конструкцію гібридного теплового фотоелектричного геліоколектора (ГТФГК). Для нього розроблено комп'ютерну модель разом із тепловим акумулятором (ТА). Модель створено в середовищі SolidWorks, а теплові процеси роз
content: Запропоновано вдосконалену конструкцію гібридного теплового фотоелектричного геліоколектора (ГТФГК). Для нього розроблено комп'ютерну модель разом із тепловим акумулятором (ТА). Модель створено в середовищі SolidWorks, а теплові процеси розраховано в модулі Flow Simulation. Вона дає змогу визначити теплофізичні характеристики колектора та окреслити шляхи вдосконалення його конструкції. За результатами моделювання отримано часові залежності температури теплоносія на вході та виході геліоколектора, а також температури в тепловому акумуляторі. Визначено миттєву питому теплову потужність і теплову ефективність системи «гібридний геліоколектор – тепловий акумулятор». Встановлено, що розроблена конструкція з прозорим покриттям має достатню теплову продуктивність у перетворенні сонячної енергії на теплову. Отримані результати підтверджують перспективність цієї технології для стабільного енергозабезпечення. Сучасні екологічні виклики підкреслюють необхідність ефективного застосування відновлюваних джерел енергії, особливо сонячної. Реалізація сталого розвитку та виконання умов енергетичної стратегії вимагають вдосконалення технологій використання сонячної енергії.

title: LAND USE CONVERSION AND ITS IMPACT ON SOCIO ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN NORTHERN NIGERIAN URBAN CENTRES
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Earth Science
summary: This paper highlights the impact of land use conversion on the socio-economic development in Northern Nigerian Urban Centers. The problems associated with land use conversion in the study area range from traffic congestion leading to lack o
content: This paper highlights the impact of land use conversion on the socio-economic development in Northern Nigerian Urban Centers. The problems associated with land use conversion in the study area range from traffic congestion leading to lack of parking space, to shortage of residential accommodation resulting from incessant land use conversion from residential to commercial use. Other challenges are pollution emanating from high traffic, overstretched infrastructure like power, water, roads, drainage, and other problems such as inaccessibility and lack of open space. Data were collected through document review on the factors of land use conversion, the socio-economic benefits of land use conversion and the challenges resulting from land use conversion in the study area. Finally, the study recommends sustainable solutions such as urban renewal programme aimed at phasing out all commercial activities that are not in conformity with planning specifications, re-planning of the area, creation of commercial hub, empowerment of the inhabitants and sanction of illegal conversion were proffered among others. This will aid and lead to having an environment that is convenience, functional, economic and aesthetic for living and working.

title: Smart city cloud-IoT analysis with spatio-temporal attention and uncertainty-aware spectral signal denoising
summary: The deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in smart cities has generated massive amounts of energy consumption data, creating strong potential for intelligent energy demand forecasting. Noisy sensor readings, missing data, and
content: The deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in smart cities has generated massive amounts of energy consumption data, creating strong potential for intelligent energy demand forecasting. Noisy sensor readings, missing data, and complex temporal dependencies have prevented conventional deep learning methods from achieving higher prediction accuracy. To address this challenge, this paper presents an innovative approach for accurate energy demand forecasting: the Smart City Cloud-IoT Spatio-Temporal Attention Network with Uncertainty-Aware Spectral Signal Denoising (SCC-IoT-STAN-USSD). Firstly, IoT energy consumption data are preprocessed through Bayesian Boundary Trend Filtering (BBTF) to remove noise measurement, fill in missing data, and retain significant temporal patterns. Then, an Amplitude-Preserving Adaptive Synchro squeezed S-Transform (APST) is used to acquire time–frequency representations from the filtered signals. The above features are then analyzed using the Spatio-Temporal Attention Network (STAN) to extract spatial correlation and long-term temporal dependencies for accurate forecasting. In addition, the Uncertainty-Aware Spectral Signal Denoising (USSD) method improves prediction accuracy by reducing uncertainty during the process of model optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a prediction accuracy of 98.20%, MAE of 0.31, RMSE of 0.24, MAPE of 2.14%, SMAPE of 1.98%, R 2 score of 0.992, and energy efficiency of 97.84%, thus surpassing the performance of ANN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM, GNN, and recently proposed methods. Additionally, statistical significance testing, regression analysis, and ablation tests show the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Deployment-time action correction for steady-state reinforcement learning-based optimal power flow
summary: This paper addresses the problem of constraint violations in reinforcement learning (RL) for power-system operation, with application to steady-state optimal-power-flow tasks. While RL-based controllers can achieve competitive reward perfor
content: This paper addresses the problem of constraint violations in reinforcement learning (RL) for power-system operation, with application to steady-state optimal-power-flow tasks. While RL-based controllers can achieve competitive reward performance, they may produce actions that violate operational constraints, limiting their practical applicability in steady-state optimal-power-flow (OPF) tasks. We investigate a deployment-time safety framework in which a continuous constraint-violation surrogate is learned directly from state–action–violation samples generated by the power-system simulator. Once the nominal Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) policy has been trained, it remains fixed, and candidate actions are corrected by minimizing their deviation from the original policy output while penalizing the violation predicted by the learned surrogate. The correction is performed directly over the nonlinear surrogate using projected gradient descent, and linear and quadratic penalty formulations are empirically compared. The framework is evaluated on two complementary OPF-Gym benchmarks, EcoDispatch and MaxRenewables, which differ in their optimization objectives, network topologies, actuator compositions, and control dimensionalities. Large-scale out-of-sample simulations show substantial reductions in the frequency and severity of constraint violations relative to nominal SAC, Lagrangian-penalty SAC, Recovery RL, and linearized correction baselines; across both benchmarks, the exact-gradient variants substantially reduce physical constraint violations relative to nominal SAC and the linearized correction strategies. In EcoDispatch, these feasibility improvements are additionally achieved while maintaining reward performance close to the underlying SAC controller. The results demonstrate the potential of simulator-driven deployment-time action correction for improving the empirical feasibility of RL-based OPF decisions without retraining the nominal policy or requiring the analytical OPF constraints to be exposed in differentiable form.

title: Universal Design Principles as a Framework for Inclusive Architectural Practice: A Structured Approach to Architectural Decision Making
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
summary: Universal Design (UD) has gained increasing attention in architectural practice because buildings are used by people with diverse physical, sensory, cognitive and functional capacities. However, the established principles of Universal Desig
content: Universal Design (UD) has gained increasing attention in architectural practice because buildings are used by people with diverse physical, sensory, cognitive and functional capacities. However, the established principles of Universal Design are often presented as general guidance or applied through individual accessibility provisions, with limited direction on how they can inform coordinated architectural decisions. This study addresses this gap by developing a practice-oriented framework for translating Universal Design principles into inclusive architectural practice. A qualitative literature synthesis was adopted, drawing on peer reviewed journal articles, scholarly publications and relevant institutional materials addressing Universal Design, inclusive architecture, accessibility, circulation, environmental usability and related aspects of the built environment. The selected literature was purposively analysed through thematic synthesis to identify recurring user requirements, design requirements and architectural responses associated with the seven Universal Design principles. The findings indicate that Universal Design principles relate to recurring requirements concerning access, spatial organisation, circulation, environmental communication, safety, adaptability and physical effort. The analysis further shows that individual architectural decisions may respond to several Universal Design principles simultaneously, supporting an integrated approach rather than isolated accessibility provisions. Based on these relationships, the study proposes a framework structured around five components: User Need, Design Requirement, Universal Design Criterion, Architectural Response and Inclusive Performance. The framework provides architects, educators and other built environment professionals with a structured means of relating user requirements to design decisions and considering their expected contribution to inclusive building use. Its application has implications for architectural education, professional practice, design review and accessibility assessment. The study concludes that advancing Universal Design in architectural practice requires greater attention to the translation of established principles into coordinated design decisions. As a literature derived framework, its application across different building types and user contexts requires further empirical testing.

title: Phenotypic and genotypic assessment of antimicrobial and biocide resistance in enterobacteria from anaerobic digestion of dairy waste: implications for environmental and public health
source: World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology
summary: Abstract Antimicrobial-resistant bacteria in agricultural waste represent a critical One Health concern. Anaerobic digestion of livestock waste is widely promoted; however, the fate of antimicrobial resistance and biocide tolerance in full-
content: Abstract Antimicrobial-resistant bacteria in agricultural waste represent a critical One Health concern. Anaerobic digestion of livestock waste is widely promoted; however, the fate of antimicrobial resistance and biocide tolerance in full-scale systems remains unclear, constraining safe digestate reuse. This study assessed phenotypic and genotypic resistance in Escherichia coli-like enterobacteria isolated from effluent and biofertilizer in a full-scale dairy anaerobic digestion system. A total of 173 isolates were screened for antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs), antimicrobial susceptibility, multidrug resistance (MDR), and biocide inhibition-zone responses. No diarrheagenic virulence genes were detected. At least one screened ARG was detected in 91.0% of effluent and 83.3% of biofertilizer isolates. qacE∆1 was the most frequent marker and occurred significantly more often in effluent (70.8%) than biofertilizer isolates (44.0%; q = 0.00291). Phenotypic resistance to at least one antimicrobial was observed in 27.0% and 34.5% of effluent and biofertilizer isolates, respectively, while MDR occurred in 2.2% and 9.5% ( p = 0.0521). tet(a) carriage was strongly associated with tetracycline resistance (OR = 20.9; q < 0.001). H 2 O 2 inhibition zones were significantly smaller among biofertilizer isolates, whereas Lactic Acid (LA) yielded 6-mm measurements in all isolates and in the reference strain. These findings demonstrate that anaerobic digestion does not fully eliminate culturable resistant enterobacteria and underscore the need for integrated resistance monitoring in dairy-waste management.

title: Bayesian‐Based Mixed‐Integer Optimization for Resonance Fatigue Testing of Large‐Scale Wind Turbine Blades
summary: ABSTRACT Fatigue testing of large wind turbine blades is a critical step in ensuring their operational reliability, however, repeatedly developing loading fixtures for different test phases (such as static and fatigue testing) often entails
content: ABSTRACT Fatigue testing of large wind turbine blades is a critical step in ensuring their operational reliability, however, repeatedly developing loading fixtures for different test phases (such as static and fatigue testing) often entails significant time and financial costs. To achieve reusability of test loading fixtures and comply with the strict load conservative envelope principle specified in the standards, this paper proposes a method for optimizing full‐scale structural fatigue test loading schemes for blades based on Bayesian optimization and mixed‐integer nonlinear programming (MINLP). This method treats the mounting positions of the exciter and counterweight in the fatigue test loading scheme as discrete variables, and optimizes the excitation force amplitude, the mass of the loading saddle at the excitation point, and the mass of the counterweight as continuous variables. In the mixed optimization of discrete and continuous variables, the static test loading points are treated as discrete candidate positions for the fatigue test equipment. The base mass of each static test loading saddle is used as the lower bound for the corresponding mass variable. In the dynamic model optimized for flapwise direction, the stiffness softening effects caused by pre‐bending and geometric nonlinearity is considered. The rationality of the optimized loading scheme was verified through full‐scale structural fatigue testing of 100‐meter‐class wind turbine blades. The results indicate that the optimized loading scheme achieved a global safety envelope for the target design bending moment in both flapwise and edgewise fatigue tests. The maximum positive deviation of the measured bending moment in the flapwise and edgewise directions was controlled at approximately 8.6% and 16.4%, respectively, meeting the certification requirements for equivalent fatigue damage specified in the IEC 61400–23 standard. This optimization method provides a technical framework for designing loading schemes for full‐scale structural fatigue testing of large wind turbine blades that combines theoretical accuracy with cost‐effectiveness. It can effectively reduce the preparation time for large‐scale blade fatigue testing and ensure the rationality of certification.

title: Quality Tools for Managing Construction Projects
summary: This latest edition continues to offer valuable insights into the utilization and implementation of a variety of quality tools and techniques throughout the various stages of construction projects. Specifically, it emphasizes three key qual
content: This latest edition continues to offer valuable insights into the utilization and implementation of a variety of quality tools and techniques throughout the various stages of construction projects. Specifically, it emphasizes three key quality management processes: planning quality, performing quality assurance, and conducting quality control. Quality Tools for Managing Construction Projects, Second Edition , explores various quality tools used in the construction industry, including classic tools of quality, management and planning tools, process analysis tools, innovation and creation tools, lean tools, cost of quality, quality function deployment, Six Sigma, and TRIZ. It covers project management, risk management, procurement, safety management, quality assessment, monitoring, training, customer satisfaction, and quality auditing. New sections include Q 4.0 Transformation, Scope and Schedule Management, Supply Chain Management, Quality Auditing, and Sustainable Requirements. The book is intended for use by quality managers, project managers, construction managers, and design professionals working on construction projects, as well as academics and professionals preparing for certification examinations.

title: What matters for wind farm layout optimization? An assessment based on the effective layout distance
summary: Abstract. Wind farm layout optimization is one of the main phases of offshore wind farm design and involves a wide range of implementation choices, spanning aspects such as flow modeling, data selection, and objective definition. This study
content: Abstract. Wind farm layout optimization is one of the main phases of offshore wind farm design and involves a wide range of implementation choices, spanning aspects such as flow modeling, data selection, and objective definition. This study quantifies the impact of 18 different implementation choices across 9 categories on the results of wind farm layout optimization. The comparison is performed using both a conventional approach based on performance metrics and the concept of effective layout distance, a novel metric introduced to measure differences between sets of layouts based solely on turbine positions. The results show that the hyperparameter values of the optimization algorithm, the choice of wake model, the use of cost of valued energy as objective, and the adoption of a control co-design approach have a high impact on the optimal layouts and therefore require careful consideration during problem formulation. In contrast, choices such as rotor averaging models and the use of revenues based on varying electricity prices as objective have a negligible effect on the resulting layouts and can therefore be selected based on simplicity and computational efficiency.

title: İmalat İşletmelerinde Talep Yanıtı Uygunluğunun CRITIC–MARCOS Yaklaşımıyla Değerlendirilmesi
summary: Elektrik sistemlerinde esneklik ihtiyacının artması, imalat işletmelerinin talep yanıtı programlarına katılım uygunluğunun sistematik biçimde değerlendirilmesini gerekli kılmaktadır. Yüksek elektrik tüketimi tek başına yeterli olmadığından,
content: Elektrik sistemlerinde esneklik ihtiyacının artması, imalat işletmelerinin talep yanıtı programlarına katılım uygunluğunun sistematik biçimde değerlendirilmesini gerekli kılmaktadır. Yüksek elektrik tüketimi tek başına yeterli olmadığından, veri kalitesi, yük profili ve fiili yanıt performansı birlikte ele alınmalıdır. Bu çalışmada, açık erişimli gerçek bir endüstriyel elektrik tüketimi ve talep yanıtı veri seti kullanılarak CRITIC–MARCOS tabanlı çok kriterli bir karar destek yaklaşımı önerilmiştir. 10 imalat işletmesi, tüketim büyüklüğü, yük profili, veri güvenilirliği ve talep yanıtı performansını temsil eden 7 kriterle değerlendirilmiştir. Kriter ağırlıkları CRITIC yöntemiyle belirlenmiş, uygunluk sıralaması MARCOS yöntemiyle elde edilmiştir. En yüksek ağırlık C5 eksik veri oranında (0,1656) hesaplanmıştır. Çelik-2, 0,9124 skoruyla en uygun; Dövme-2 ise 0,3385 skoruyla en düşük uygunluğa sahip alternatif olmuştur. CBL ve kapasite karşılama oranına ilişkin duyarlılık analizinde ana model ile tüm senaryolar arasındaki Spearman sıra korelasyonu 0,988 bulunmuştur. Bulgular, veri güvenilirliği ve fiili yanıt performansının uygunluk değerlendirmesinde belirleyici olduğunu göstermektedir.

title: INTEGRATSIYALASHGAN ENERGETIKA MODELLARI UCHUN MA’LUMOTLARNI TEKSHIRISH VA UYG‘UNLASHTIRISH: NASA POWER VA ERA5 MA’LUMOTLARI MISOLIDA
summary: The article investigates the validation, standardization, and harmonization of meteorological data from different sources for long-term modeling of renewable energy systems. A methodological workflow is proposed that includes preliminary qu
content: The article investigates the validation, standardization, and harmonization of meteorological data from different sources for long-term modeling of renewable energy systems. A methodological workflow is proposed that includes preliminary quality control, unit standardization, temporal synchronization, spatial matching, and statistical assessment using RMSE, MAE, and Bias. NASA POWER and ERA5 data for August 2026 were compared for Tashkent, Samarkand, Bukhara, Karshi, and Navoi using three key parameters: solar radiation, air temperature, and wind speed. The relative mean absolute difference for solar radiation ranged from 2.79% to 3.82%, indicating relatively close agreement between the two data sources. RMSE values ranged from 1.03 to 3.06 °C for air temperature and from 0.84 to 1.91 m/s for wind speed. The results demonstrate that agreement between data sources varies considerably by meteorological parameter and that each parameter should therefore be validated separately before being incorporated into integrated energy models. The proposed approach provides a methodological basis for the subsequent comparison and harmonization of international datasets with national observations and for the development of a consistent input dataset for renewable energy modeling.

title: Wealth and weight revisited: A Bayesian model averaging approach to the Obesity Kuznets Curve
source: The European Journal of Health Economics
summary: The substantial literature on the existence of an inverted U-shaped relationship between obesity prevalence and economic growth, known as the Obesity Kuznets Curve (OKC), has yielded mixed evidence due to uncertainty in model and variable s
content: The substantial literature on the existence of an inverted U-shaped relationship between obesity prevalence and economic growth, known as the Obesity Kuznets Curve (OKC), has yielded mixed evidence due to uncertainty in model and variable selection. We address this using a comprehensive panel of 84 countries from 2000 to 2020. Our Two-Way Fixed Effects (TWFE) models suggest the OKC follows an inverted-N shape, suggesting multiple transition points in the obesity-wealth nexus. To account for model uncertainty, we employ Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) against a large set of potential determinants. The inverted-N shape remains robust, with BMA identifying key predictors across economic, sociocultural, and environmental domains. Our results suggest that a single 'turning point' oversimplifies the obesity transition, and that targeted interventions must account for the multi-stage nature of economic development.

title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
summary: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to asse
content: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. Most studies examine short-term, individual-level responses, limiting inference on long-term effects. Impacts vary widely by stressor, taxon, and biological outcome. Invertebrates often show positive responses linked to reef effects, though key functional traits are vulnerable. Fish responses are largely neutral except under noise, while marine mammals exhibit the most consistent negative impacts. The impact score developed here highlights taxon-specific vulnerability and offers a scalable risk-assessment tool for data-poor regions. The review calls for standardized, long-term field monitoring to support OWF expansion while safeguarding biodiversity.

title: A Current-Scaling Strategy for Droop-Controlled Grid-Forming Inverters in Off-Grid Systems
summary: The progressive replacement of synchronous generation by inverter-based renewable energy resources is altering the dynamical structure of modern power systems, reducing system strength due to the inertia curtailment. In this context, grid-f
content: The progressive replacement of synchronous generation by inverter-based renewable energy resources is altering the dynamical structure of modern power systems, reducing system strength due to the inertia curtailment. In this context, grid-forming inverters have emerged as a fundamental technology capable of establishing voltage and frequency in inverter-dominated grids. However, their effective deployment is intrinsically dependent on the control framework that must guarantee stability, robustness, and interoperability under complex and uncertain operating conditions. The most adopted grid-forming control strategy is droop control. This work presents a proportional scaling strategy in the inner current loop for droop-controlled grid-forming inverters, which preserves the current angle, reducing only its magnitude if a large disturbance occurs. Moreover, an innovative grid-forming controller parametrization procedure based on hybrid jellyfish search and particle swarm optimizer is also provided. This methodology avoids empirical tuning and allows incorporating system constraints in the controller tuning procedure. Hardware-in-the-loop results demonstrate high performance of the optimized droop under nominal operation, load variation, black-start, and faults.

title: Institutional-based social network resources, social resource orchestration competence, and business growth of manufacturing small and medium enterprises: evidence from Kenya
summary: Introduction The sustainable growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in manufacturing in developing economies depends significantly on how firms harness institutional social networks as strategic resources. Despite growing schol
content: Introduction The sustainable growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in manufacturing in developing economies depends significantly on how firms harness institutional social networks as strategic resources. Despite growing scholarship on social capital and firm performance, the mechanisms by which institutionally based social network resources — comprising regulatory, normative, and cultural-cognitive networks — translate into business growth remain insufficiently theorised. Specifically, the moderating role of social resource orchestration competence (SROC) in converting institutional network resources into firm growth value has not been empirically examined among Kenyan manufacturing SMEs. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 393 purposively selected respondents — comprising business owners, heads of operations, and heads of finance — drawn from Kenya Association of Manufacturers (KAM)-registered manufacturing SMEs across 14 sub-sectors in Nairobi County, Kenya. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) was conducted in SmartPLS 4.0, preceded by Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) to establish reliability and validity. Convergent and discriminant validity, as well as collinearity, were assessed using established thresholds before path analysis was conducted. Results Direct path analysis confirmed significant positive associations of regulatory ( β = 0.332, p < 0.05), normative ( β = 0.285, p < 0.05), and cultural-cognitive resource networks ( β = 0.162, p < 0.05) with SME growth. When SROC was introduced as a moderator, it emerged as the dominant growth factor ( β = 0.543, p < 0.05). SROC significantly amplified the association of regulatory resource networks with SME growth ( β = 0.162, p < 0.05) and attenuated the contribution of cultural-cognitive networks ( β = −0.429, p < 0.05), while having no significant moderating effect on normative resource networks. Discussion These findings advance Social Exchange Theory by offering preliminary evidence that the economic value of institutional network exchanges varies with the firm's SROC. The study introduces the Social Exchange Orchestration Grid (SEOG) — a novel theoretical framework that maps the differential economic value of institutional network archetypes against SROC — providing manufacturing SME managers with a strategic tool for prioritising institutional network investments. Implications for SME policy in sub-Saharan Africa are discussed, with an emphasis on building orchestration capabilities as a potentially more critical investment than network acquisition per se .

title: Optimizing Network Capacity for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Using V2G Technology and Renewable Energy Sources
summary: This paper presents an integrated framework for optimizing the capacity of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) operating within distribution networks. Capacity is maxi- mized through integration of RES, reactive power compensa- tion d
content: This paper presents an integrated framework for optimizing the capacity of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) operating within distribution networks. Capacity is maxi- mized through integration of RES, reactive power compensa- tion devices (RPCs), Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology. A key feature of the proposed model is the use of V2G technology not only for active power regulation but also for elimination of har- monic oscillations. The developed multi-objective optimization model aims to reduce energy losses and operating costs while simultaneously improving voltage stability. It was tested on an IEEE-33 test scheme, adhering to specifi ed constraints.

title: Land concentration and large renewable energy projects
source: Documentos de trabajo/Documento de trabajo - Banco de España, Servicio de Estudios
summary: This paper examines how land ownership concentration shapes the deployment of large-scale renewable energy projects across six European countries (Spain, Germany, France, Italy, Belgium and the Netherlands). Using a 5×5 km grid-cell framewo
content: This paper examines how land ownership concentration shapes the deployment of large-scale renewable energy projects across six European countries (Spain, Germany, France, Italy, Belgium and the Netherlands). Using a 5×5 km grid-cell framework with cadastral parcel data, we show that cells with a higher share of area in large parcels (= 10 ha) are substantially more likely to host mega photovoltaic (PV) plants (= 50 ha), with a standardized semi-elasticity of 68% in the pooled sample, consistent across all six countries. Land concentration also drives aggregate solar deployment: a one-standard-deviation increase raises expected PV hectares within a grid cell by 62%, an effect driven almost entirely by the mega-plant margin. By contrast, the effect on wind parks is weaker and heterogeneous, consistent with wind requiring less contiguous land assembly than solar. A specificity test and decomposition analysis corroborate that the assembly mechanism operates specifically at the mega-plant margin, and a horse race between cadastral concentration and farm operational size establishes that ownership, not farming scale, is the operative mechanism. A finer 500 m grid within-municipality analysis corroborates the effect of land concentration on mega PV plants and further reveals that it is attenuated in irrigated areas, where higher agricultural rents raise landowner reservation values. We rationalize these patterns with a conceptual framework in which solar assembly requires unanimous consent from a set of landowners whose number falls with parcel size, while wind requires only a subset. Our findings reveal that land ownership structure is a decisive factor in the energy transition: fragmentation impedes large-scale deployment, while concentration enables it but channels its benefits toward a few large landowners, potentially deepening rural grievances and local opposition.

title: Government Interventions and Protected Cultivation: A Central Rajasthan Perspective
summary: Protected cultivation using polyhouses, shade nets, drip irrigation, and greenhouse farming has emerged as a key strategy to boost productivity, reduce climate risks, and raise farmer incomes. To promote adoption, the Government of India an
content: Protected cultivation using polyhouses, shade nets, drip irrigation, and greenhouse farming has emerged as a key strategy to boost productivity, reduce climate risks, and raise farmer incomes. To promote adoption, the Government of India and Rajasthan have introduced schemes like NHM, RKVY, and MIDH, offering subsidies, credit support, and training. For the analysis of the objectives of Government Policies, Subsidies, and Support Programs were examined relevant to Horticulture and Protected Cultivation in Central Rajasthan. Semi-arid Central Rajasthan, with erratic rainfall and poor soils, has been a focus under the National Horticulture Mission (NHM) through subsidies, training, and technical support. Farmer feedback indicated 62.56% learned of NHM via government extension services, while 12.42% were informed by peers. Over half had limited prior knowledge of protected cultivation, yet all attended training. NHM subsidies covering 51–75% of initial investment enabled polyhouse establishment, resulting in higher yields, improved produce quality, and better market access. Challenges included high initial costs, technical gaps, maintenance issues, and lack of collateral (27.53%). To improve sustainability, the study recommends advanced training, timely financial support, quality input access, and technical advisory networks. Strengthening cooperatives, market linkages, infrastructure, tailored credit, and insurance, supported by research, awareness campaigns, and monitoring, will enhance adoption and ensure long-term viability for sustainable horticultural development in Central Rajasthan.

title: Complejidad económica y mercadotecnia sostenible: estrategias de diversificación exportadora verde en Hidalgo
summary: This study aimed to identify green export diversification opportunities in the state of Hidalgo, Mexico, and integrate them with sustainable marketing strategies to strengthen their insertion into international markets. Drawing on economic
content: This study aimed to identify green export diversification opportunities in the state of Hidalgo, Mexico, and integrate them with sustainable marketing strategies to strengthen their insertion into international markets. Drawing on economic complexity theory and the Greenplexity approach, average exports, product affinity, and product complexity were analyzed. Three diversification strategies were designed: maintenance, related capabilities, and trade inertia. The results show 34 products with real export potential, with particular relevance in the electric vehicle value chain. Positioning the state of Hidalgo under a sustainable territorial branding narrative (“Hidalgo Verde”) is recommended, to legitimize and showcase these products within the energy transition.

title: Plasma Catalysis for Green Chemistry and Co2 Conversion
summary: The ever-growing CO2 levels in the atmosphere along with the pressing need to move away from traditional carbon-intensive chemical production necessitate breakthrough technologies beyond conventional thermal catalysis. Plasma catalysis, whi
