Furthermore, key bottlenecks are identified, current mitigation strategies are assessed, and priority research directions are outlined for advancing the sustainable "photosynthesis" of plastic waste.

title: Modeling freshwater use for direct lithium extraction from geothermal brines in the Salton Sea
summary: Abstract Global lithium demand is projected to more than double by 2035, to about 715 kt per year (3.8 Mt LCE per year) under the IEA Stated Policies Scenario, intensifying the need for new, sustainable extraction routes. Direct lithium ext
content: Abstract Global lithium demand is projected to more than double by 2035, to about 715 kt per year (3.8 Mt LCE per year) under the IEA Stated Policies Scenario, intensifying the need for new, sustainable extraction routes. Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from geothermal brines is of particular interest because co-location with closed-loop geothermal operations avoids the large land footprint of evaporitic ponds and the carbon intensity of hard-rock mining. The Salton Sea Known Geothermal Resource Area (SS-KGRA) hosts geothermal operations with co-located pilot-scale DLE facilities, making it among the advanced regions for geothermal lithium extraction. Though these operations are expected to reduce land and carbon intensity, they require freshwater inputs across multiple unit operations; this demand has been reported only as facility-wide aggregates, without process-level resolution, despite potential US operations existing in an arid region constrained by agricultural water use. Existing estimates do not track the internal fate of process water, which determines the net volume drawn from external sources. Herein, we present LiHydroSim, a process-based model that translates publicly available process descriptions into a facility-level freshwater balance through a three-layer architecture separating gross unit-operation demand, internal recovery, and net external supply. Applied to a representative adsorption-based facility processing 7000 gallons per minute of geothermal brine, the model estimates net external freshwater demand of 1719 acre-feet per year (152 m3 t −1 lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE); 0.12 AF/t LCE), below the 189–355 m3 t −1 LCE (0.15–0.29 AF/t LCE) reported by Salton Sea developers, consistent with auxiliary demands outside the process boundary. The eluant for lithium elution dominates the water balance, accounting for 92% of gross internal process-water demand, while internal recycling offsets roughly one third of that gross demand. Total demand depends mainly on eluant volume: across two patent-specified operating modes, it ranges from 870 to 1719 acre-feet per year.

title: Steering smart farming technology adoption toward a safe and just operating space
summary: Abstract Smart farming is transforming agricultural systems. Innovations such as precision farming, robotics, and AI-driven applications are known as agriculture’s fourth revolution which may provide socioeconomic, and environmental benefit
content: Abstract Smart farming is transforming agricultural systems. Innovations such as precision farming, robotics, and AI-driven applications are known as agriculture’s fourth revolution which may provide socioeconomic, and environmental benefits. However, adoption rates remain below socially desirable levels due to, amongst others, a lack of return relative to required risks, and costs. We propose the “Safe and Just Operating Space” (SJOS) concept as a normative framework to steer regional and sector-specific policy incentives toward the most impactful technologies regarding urgent socio-environmental needs. This is the first time that the SJOS concept is applied to designing regional policies to induce the most impactful smart farming. Proposing a new type of decision-making framework is highly relevant to policymakers, researchers, and industry stakeholders interested in policies to govern novel technologies. Our blueprint outlines the application, discusses the advantages and limitations, and highlights the required research needs for policy implementation. Four implementation steps are required to apply the SJOS concept to smart technology in agricultural systems: 1) downscaling and disaggregating environmental and socio-economic conditions to define case-specific regional Safe and Just boundaries for the agricultural sector, 2) scoring the regional status quo, 3) evaluating individual smart technologies in terms of the different Safe and Just indicators, and 4) creating the Safe and Just synthesis to enable technology prioritization and target-oriented policy action. Our framework is globally applicable and ensures that technology deployment is effective in terms of timing, location, and application, enabling the attainment of a socially desirable level of technology use.

title: Regional economic impacts and emission responses under solar radiation modification
summary: Abstract Solar Radiation Modification (SRM) has been proposed as a potential tool to limit increases in global or regional temperatures caused by anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. While previous research has extensively examined the c
content: Abstract Solar Radiation Modification (SRM) has been proposed as a potential tool to limit increases in global or regional temperatures caused by anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. While previous research has extensively examined the climate system's response to various SRM strategies, as well as their aggregate economic consequences, the spatial distribution of economic impacts has received less attention. In this study, we use NorESM2-DIAM---an Earth System Model coupled to a high-resolution integrated assessment model---to assess the economic impacts, measured in GDP per capita, in an idealised SRM scenario where incoming solar radiation is reduced by 1%. Our results suggest that, relative to a baseline without SRM, most countries experience economic gains under SRM, with only a few countries facing negative impacts. Low-income countries tend to see the largest benefits, reducing disparities in GDP per capita across countries relative to the baseline. However, reduced damages and smaller disparities in GDP per capita are accompanied by a “moral hazard” effect, in that SRM leads to higher emissions, which may in turn cause additional adverse effects not captured here. These findings highlight potential trade-offs between economic benefits, the distribution of economic impacts, and increased emissions relevant for SRM governance.

title: Growing More While Emitting Less? Decoupling US Agricultural Production and Greenhouse Gas Emissions
summary: ABSTRACT We decompose state‐level US agricultural greenhouse gas emissions growth into output growth, input emission intensity, and total factor productivity (TFP). Combining EPA emissions data with USDA productivity accounts over 1990–2015
content: ABSTRACT We decompose state‐level US agricultural greenhouse gas emissions growth into output growth, input emission intensity, and total factor productivity (TFP). Combining EPA emissions data with USDA productivity accounts over 1990–2015, we find that TFP growth historically slowed emissions but has recently weakened. Declining input emission intensity, concentrated in the Southeast, has become the dominant mitigating factor. Further decomposition suggests that land productivity gains are more closely linked to emission reductions than labor productivity gains.

title: Investissement Agricole, Conditions Climatiques et Production Alimentaire en Afrique : Une Analyse des Effets Non Linéaires du Climat sur Données de Panel
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Résumé : Cette étude répond au manque d’analyses examinant conjointement l’investissement agricole et les non-linéarités climatiques en Afrique. Elle analyse la relation entre l’investissement agricole, les conditions climatiques et la prod
content: Résumé : Cette étude répond au manque d’analyses examinant conjointement l’investissement agricole et les non-linéarités climatiques en Afrique. Elle analyse la relation entre l’investissement agricole, les conditions climatiques et la production alimentaire dans un panel cylindré de onze pays africains sur la période 1996–2022. L’échantillon comprend l’Afrique du Sud, le Cameroun, l’Égypte, l’Éthiopie, le Kenya, le Mali, le Maroc, le Nigéria, l’Ouganda, la Tanzanie et la Tunisie, sélectionnés selon la disponibilité continue des données. L’investissement agricole est mesuré par la formation brute de capital fixe agricole, tandis que la température moyenne et les précipitations annuelles représentent les conditions climatiques. L’analyse repose principalement sur un modèle à effets fixes avec des erreurs standards de Driscoll-Kraay robustes à l’hétéroscédasticité, à l’autocorrélation temporelle et à la dépendance transversale. Les résultats montrent que l’investissement agricole est positivement et significativement associé à la production alimentaire. Dans l’estimation principale, une hausse de 1 % de la FBCF agricole est associée à une augmentation d’environ 0,140 % de l’indice de production alimentaire. Aucun effet non linéaire robuste n’est identifié pour la température. En revanche, le test de Lind et Mehlum (2010) confirme, dans la spécification principale, une relation en U inversé entre les précipitations et la production alimentaire : la relation est positive jusqu’à un seuil estimé à environ 733 mm par an, puis devient négative. Ce résultat pluviométrique doit toutefois être interprété comme conditionnel à l’estimateur retenu, puisqu’il n’est pas confirmé par les estimations PCSE et FGLS. Les résultats soulignent l’importance de l’investissement productif et de politiques de gestion de l’eau adaptées aux conditions nationales. Mots-clés : investissement agricole, production alimentaire, conditions climatiques, non-linéarité, Afrique. Classification JEL : C23, O13, Q18, Q25, Q54. Type du papier : Recherche empirique. Abstract: This study addresses the lack of research jointly examining agricultural investment and climate nonlinearities in Africa. It analyzes the relationship between agricultural investment, climatic conditions, and food production using a balanced panel of eleven African countries over the period 1996–2022. The sample comprises Cameroon, Egypt, Ethiopia, Kenya, Mali, Morocco, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, Tunisia, and Uganda, selected according to the continuous availability of data. Agricultural investment is measured by agricultural gross fixed capital formation, while mean temperature and annual precipitation represent climatic conditions. Arable land, agricultural employment, and fertilizer use are included as control variables in the empirical specifications. The empirical analysis primarily relies on a fixed-effects model with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors robust to heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, and cr

title: Assessment of Electricity Generation Potential from Residual Gases of Continuous Wood Carbonization Using a Techno-economic Framework
summary: Brazil is the world's largest producer of charcoal, with production primarily directed toward industrial applications, notably charcoal-based steelmaking. Nevertheless, conventional batch carbonization technologies release substantial amoun
content: Brazil is the world's largest producer of charcoal, with production primarily directed toward industrial applications, notably charcoal-based steelmaking. Nevertheless, conventional batch carbonization technologies release substantial amounts of residual gases directly into the atmosphere, resulting in substantial energy losses, air pollution, and environmental degradation, as these gases include significant fractions of methane, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide, among others. These losses are mainly associated with the widespread use of large rectangular masonry kilns, which hinder the recovery and utilization of carbonization gases. Such gases contain approximately 50% of the wood's initial energy; thus, given the large production of charcoal in Minas Gerais, they can represent a considerable energy potential for the state. This study evaluates the feasibility of recovering energy from wood carbonization gases using a continuous carbonization reactor ("Lambiotte" type). Owing to continuous operation, this technology enables improved energy utilization through a gas recovery system that supplies part of the carbonization process's energy demand while directing the remaining fraction to electricity generation. The analyzed reactor has a nominal charcoal production capacity of 20 tons/day and provides up to 1.95 MWh of thermal power from residual gases. Electricity generation from the recovered gases was assessed using two conversion technologies: a conventional steam Rankine cycle and an Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC), which achieved electrical efficiencies of 9.5% and 17.7%, respectively. The techno-economic analysis identified the steam Rankine cycle as the most economically viable option under the evaluated conditions, yielding a specific electricity generation of 130 kWh/ton of charcoal for a gravimetric charcoal yield of 33%. For a higher charcoal yield of 42%, the specific electricity generation decreased to 62 kWh/ton. The results demonstrate that continuous carbonization technology is well-suited for large-scale charcoal production in Brazil. In addition to producing superior-quality, homogeneous charcoal, the process enhances overall energy efficiency by converting residual gases into electricity. Furthermore, the controlled combustion of these gases significantly reduces emissions of highly polluting compounds, such as CH4 and CO, thereby mitigating greenhouse gas emissions, particularly methane, which remain among the most critical environmental challenges of the charcoal industry.

title: Biogas purification and enrichment: sustainability metrics analysis of dry anaerobic digester with cashew apple bagasse substrate
summary: Abstract This study hypothesizes that cashew apple bagasse‐based anaerobic digestion, combined with biochar purification, enhances biogas quality and sustainability. This study aims to investigate the performance and sustainability of a bio
content: Abstract This study hypothesizes that cashew apple bagasse‐based anaerobic digestion, combined with biochar purification, enhances biogas quality and sustainability. This study aims to investigate the performance and sustainability of a biochar‐based biogas purification technology using cashew apple bagasse as a substrate, with a focus on environmental and energy benefits. The experimental result was the production of 53.7 L of biogas. Thus, the anaerobic digestion of 1 ton of cashew apple bagasse could generate 70 m 3 of biogas with a methane concentration of 63%, which could subsequently be purified to produce 44 m 3 of CH 4 . The purification process effectively increased the methane content from 71% to 78% by the 22nd day, using a 50:50 mixture of activated carbon and zeolites. Sustainability analysis indicated that the cashew apple bagasse‐based biogas purification process achieved a Path2Green score of 0.412, outperforming Study 1 (0.447) and Study 2 (0.232), while matching Studies 3 and 4 (0.447). Regarding the AGREE metric, the process scored 0.50, surpassing Study 2 (0.58) but falling slightly behind Studies 3 and 4 (0.58 each). For the GAPI metric, the process earned a score of 74, higher than Study 2 (85) yet lower than Studies 1, 3, and 4 (85 each). Overall, the results demonstrate the method's alignment with green chemistry principles and its potential for sustainable biogas purification.

title: Nepalese Calamity of 2026: Manmade or Climate Driven
summary: The flash floods of August 26, 2026, along the Nepal-Tibet border are one of the most devastating Himalayan disasters since the 2015 earthquake. Some believe that the event was driven by anthropogenic activities. Others attribute it to clim
content: The flash floods of August 26, 2026, along the Nepal-Tibet border are one of the most devastating Himalayan disasters since the 2015 earthquake. Some believe that the event was driven by anthropogenic activities. Others attribute it to climate change. To have greater clarity of the primary cause and to draw lessons for the future, this paper examines the catalysts behind the disaster. Although the primary geological event may have been rooted in climate change, the catastrophic scale of downstream destruction seems to have been greatly amplified by manmade vulnerabilities. Unplanned development leading to high density of downstream settlements, unabated infrastructure activities in the seismically weak Himalayas, and proliferation of high-risk hydropower infrastructure in narrow valleys significantly multiplied the economic and human toll. Hence, the calamity cannot be categorized as purely natural or manmade but a compound one, where climate-induced cryospheric instability collided with systemic failures in climate-resilient engineering and transboundary early-warning systems. The study concludes with policy recommendations for transboundary disaster risk reduction in the warming Himalayas.

title: Multi-period Optimization of Sugarcane, Corn, and Agave Biorefineries for Sustainable Aviation Fuel Production in Brazil
summary: The decarbonization of the aviation sector represents one of the most significant challenges in the global energy transition due to its dependence on high energy-density liquid fuels and limited electrification alternatives. This study deve
content: The decarbonization of the aviation sector represents one of the most significant challenges in the global energy transition due to its dependence on high energy-density liquid fuels and limited electrification alternatives. This study develops a multi-period mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model to evaluate the technical, economic, and environmental feasibility of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production via the alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) route in Brazil, using ethanol derived from sugarcane, corn, and agave. The model integrates mass and energy balances, regional logistics, hydrogen supply alternatives, capital and operating costs, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions within a unified optimization framework aimed at maximizing net present value (NPV). The optimized system produces 8.20 Mt of SAF annually alongside bioethanol, gasoline, diesel, biomethane, and other co-products, requiring substantial biomass inputs exceeding 15 million hectares of cultivated land. The calculated minimum selling price (MSP) of 0.947 USD/L is positioned at the lower end of the range reported in the literature (0.87–2.74 USD/L), indicating competitive economic performance relative to other feedstocks and technological pathways. Environmentally, the system emits 34.36 MtCO2e/year but avoids 93.58 MtCO2e/year, resulting in a net reduction of 59.22 MtCO2e/year. Transportation emissions represent only 0.31% of total emissions. When contextualized within Brazil’s 2035 climate targets (0.85–1.05 GtCO2e/year), the net mitigation achieved corresponds to approximately 5.6–7.0% of the projected national emissions level. These results suggest that large-scale SAF deployment via integrated ATJ pathways could play a substantial role in supporting national decarbonization strategies, although biomass demand and land-use implications remain critical considerations.

title: Source tracking and transmission of antibiotic resistance genes mediated by core microbiota in black soldier fly larvae bioconversion of doxycycline‐contaminated hen manure
summary: Black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) bioconversion of doxycycline-contaminated hen manure raises concerns about antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) transmission. Although core microbiota in gut may participate in ARG dynamics, the relative contribu
content: Black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) bioconversion of doxycycline-contaminated hen manure raises concerns about antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) transmission. Although core microbiota in gut may participate in ARG dynamics, the relative contributions of microbiota from manure and baseline larval gut to the BSFL gut resistome remain unclear. Using metagenomics, amplicon sequencing, and cultivable bacteria analysis, we found that: (1) Providencia, Klebsiella, Enterococcus, and Escherichia-Shigella dominated the BSFL gut and served as primary ARG hosts; (2) Fecal filtrate intervention drastically altered gut microbiota and ARG profiles, suppressing Klebsiella (by 95.56%) and Escherichia-Shigella (to < 0.5%) while enriching Providencia (3.53 fold increase) and Enterococcus, with increased ARGs such as tet(59) and qnrD1. Long-read metagenomic analysis indicated that viable manure-borne bacteria, rather than cell-free fecal filtrate, delivered structurally intact ARG-MGE units as key carrier of mobile resistance cassettes; (3) Source tracking (FEAST) assigned the majority of ARBs (> 90%) and their ARGs in the BSFL gut to the baseline BSFL gut source, with manure-derived ARBs contributing 4.80%. Culture-based 16S rRNA gene homology provided evidence consistent with possible manure-to-gut transfer of selected Escherichia-Shigella and Enterococcus. The BSFL gut resistome was more strongly associated with the baseline BSFL microbiota than with manure, but manure still represented a detectable source of ARB and ARG introduction. FEAST source assignments should be interpreted as composition-based bioinformatic estimates rather than definitive proof of origin, due to lack of direct functional tracing. These findings have critical implications for assessing the ecological safety of BSFL-based waste valorization.

title: Development of Intelligent Adaptive Control for Solar-SEIG Powered Battery Charging Station
summary: Abstract This paper presents the design and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) implementation of a smart adaptive control strategy for a renewable-integrated electric vehicle (EV) charging station. The primary objective of this work is to develop a
content: Abstract This paper presents the design and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) implementation of a smart adaptive control strategy for a renewable-integrated electric vehicle (EV) charging station. The primary objective of this work is to develop a reliable, grid-compliant, and power-quality-enhanced charging station capable of operating under dynamic and critical load conditions. The proposed system integrates a solar photovoltaic (PV) array, a self-excited induction generator (SEIG) driven by a hydro turbine, battery storage, multiple EV charging ports, a critical load, and a three-phase utility grid. An adaptive least mean absolute third (ALMAT) filter-based control algorithm is employed to generate reference source currents, enabling effective harmonic mitigation, load balancing, and power factor correction. The system operates in both standalone and grid-connected modes, ensuring uninterrupted power supply during night time and optimal energy utilization during day time through battery storage and grid export. A bidirectional converter is used to support different types of EV charging requirements. Experimental validation using OPAL-RT demonstrates that the proposed control strategy achieves unity power factor, maintains total harmonic distortion within IEEE 519 limits, and ensures stable system performance under varying operating conditions. The results confirm that the developed charging station enhances power quality, improves system reliability, and supports sustainable and economical EV charging, making it suitable for practical deployment in renewable energy-based transportation charging station.

title: Ultrafine Ru Nanoparticles Supported on Layered Double Hydroxide-Derived MgAl Mixed Oxides for Durable Bi-Reforming of Methane
summary: Abstract The sustainable conversion of methane and carbon dioxide into syngas via bi-reforming of methane (BRM) represents a promising strategy for greenhouse gas mitigation and carbon resource utilization. However, catalyst deactivation ca
content: Abstract The sustainable conversion of methane and carbon dioxide into syngas via bi-reforming of methane (BRM) represents a promising strategy for greenhouse gas mitigation and carbon resource utilization. However, catalyst deactivation caused by coke accumulation and sintering of active metals remains a major challenge for achieving efficient and durable BRM processes. Herein, ultrafine Ru nanoparticles (NPs) supported on Mg3AlOx mixed oxides derived from layered double hydroxides (denoted as Ru/MAO) were fabricated via an ultrasound-assisted reduction. The optimal 0.2Ru/MAO catalyst exhibits superior catalytic activity and remarkable long-term stability for 250 h at 800 °C. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the ultrafine Ru NPs (∼1.1 nm) possessing electron-deficient characteristics regulate the adsorption strength of CHx intermediates, thereby suppressing excessive methane cracking and the formation of inert carbonaceous species. Meanwhile, the abundant basic sites on the Mg3AlOx support promote CO2 adsorption and activation, facilitating CO2-assisted carbon oxidation and removal during reaction. Furthermore, the strengthened interfacial interaction between Ru NPs and Mg3AlOx effectively inhibits Ru sintering under high-temperature conditions. A synergistic combination of in situ spectroscopic characterization and theoretical calculations further demonstrate the crucial roles of HCOO* and CHO* intermediates in suppressing coke accumulation and mitigating catalyst deactivation.

title: Experimental Characterization of Vacuum-Retention Behavior in FDM-Printed Enclosures for Adaptive Building-Facade Applications
summary: Abstract Achieving structural hermeticity in Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) components is essential for vacuum-based smart facade applications. This study presents a rigorous methodological evaluation of vacuum retention in 3D-printed comp
content: Abstract Achieving structural hermeticity in Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) components is essential for vacuum-based smart facade applications. This study presents a rigorous methodological evaluation of vacuum retention in 3D-printed composite enclosures using four material types: PET-CF, PETG, PLA-Aero, and PLA Basic. A pressure-decay testing protocol, aligned with BS EN 1779 and ASTM F2095 standards, was developed to characterize leak kinetics under controlled depressurization. Our results demonstrate that carbon-fiber reinforced PET (PET-CF) provides superior airtightness, maintaining a vacuum level below the instrumentation's detection threshold (<3.75•10⁻⁴ mbar•L•s⁻¹).Conversely, standard polylactic acid (PLA) and foaming variants exhibit significant timedependent leakage. Through annotated microstructural analysis, we identify inter-layer fusion quality and localized seam integrity as the primary determinants of hermetic performance. This work provides a validated framework for optimizing additive manufacturing parameters to ensure the airtightness of functional building components, contributing to the development of high-performance, energy-efficient building envelopes.

title: Effect of ionic liquid–functionalized graphene oxide loading on CO
summary: Graphene oxide (GO)/Pebax-1657 mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) have been well-recognized as a cost-effective solution for carbon capture. Nonetheless, their separation performance is often compromised by GO aggregation and the formation of in
content: Graphene oxide (GO)/Pebax-1657 mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) have been well-recognized as a cost-effective solution for carbon capture. Nonetheless, their separation performance is often compromised by GO aggregation and the formation of interfacial voids. To overcome these challenges, this study focused on the development of ionic liquid functionalized GO (IL-GO) by covalently functionalizing GOs with 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)-imide ([BMIM][Tf2N]) ionic liquid (IL) via a two-steps approach. The CO2 separation performance of the MMMs incorporating with IL-GOs was examined across different loadings (0.2 – 2.0 wt.%). Notably, the 0.5 wt.% IL-GO/Pebax MMM demonstrated the most promising results, achieving a CO2 permeability of 154.07 Barrer and a CO2/CH4 selectivity of 58.50 under the investigated single gas conditions, indicating its potential for CO2 separation.

title: Adaptive Uncertainty-Guided Surrogates for Efficient phase field Modeling of Dendritic Solidification
summary: Abstract The high computational cost of phase field simulations remains a major limitation for predicting dendritic solidification in metals, particularly in additive manufacturing, where microstructural control is critical. This work inves
content: Abstract The high computational cost of phase field simulations remains a major limitation for predicting dendritic solidification in metals, particularly in additive manufacturing, where microstructural control is critical. This work investigates alternative strategies for surrogate modeling of dendritic solidification using uncertainty-driven adaptive sampling with XGBoost and CNNs, including a self-supervised strategy, to efficiently approximate the spatio-temporal evolution while reducing costly phase field simulations. The proposed adaptive strategy leverages model uncertainty, approximated via Monte Carlo dropout for CNNs and bagging for XGBoost, to identify high-uncertainty regions where new samples are generated locally within hyperspheres, progressively refining the spatio-temporal design space and achieving accurate predictions with significantly fewer phase field simulations than an Optimal Latin Hypercube Sampling optimized via discrete Particle Swarm Optimization (OLHS-PSO). The framework systematically investigates how temporal instance selection, adaptive sampling, and the choice between domain-informed and data-driven surrogates affect spatio-temporal model performance. Evaluation considers not only computational cost but also the number of expensive phase field simulations, surrogate accuracy, and associated $CO_2$ emissions, providing a comprehensive assessment of model performance as well as their related environmental impact.

title: Forging Sustainable Research: Integrating Sustainability into Neuroscience Education
summary: The health and wellbeing of living organisms and the environment are irrevocably interconnected. Animals constantly shape the environments in which they live, and environmental factors, in turn, shape the minds and behaviours of animals. Th
content: The health and wellbeing of living organisms and the environment are irrevocably interconnected. Animals constantly shape the environments in which they live, and environmental factors, in turn, shape the minds and behaviours of animals. The emerging discipline of environmental neuroscience studies this reciprocal interaction and offers a unique opportunity to integrate sustainability into undergraduate training. Here, we present and evaluate Forging Sustainable Research, an interdisciplinary undergraduate course that integrates teaching of neuroscience, biology, psychology, environmental science, and sustainable development. Students explore how research in these fields can be interlinked 24 and re-oriented towards addressing emerging environmental challenges. In parallel, students learn how to measure and mitigate the environmental impact of research activities. Student feedback suggests that the course is effective at raising awareness and understanding of sustainability in research, while also enhancing student perception of their own ability to promote positive change. As climate and ecosystem change impact all sectors, sustainability awareness in academic and professional spaces is increasingly sought after. Students in the course therefore receive training in transferable skills relevant for diverse career paths. In the long term, this course may serve as model for direct integration of sustainability training into undergraduate curricula in the natural sciences.

title: Strategic Innovation in the Bakery Industry Through Underutilized Bioresources: A Narrative Review of Nutritional Enhancement, Circular Economy Approaches, Consumer Acceptance, and Industry 4.0 Technologies
summary: The bakery industry is undergoing paradigm shifts due to increased customer demand for healthy foods, sustainable manufacturing techniques and innovations. At the same time, growing concerns about food waste, environmental harm and the depl
content: The bakery industry is undergoing paradigm shifts due to increased customer demand for healthy foods, sustainable manufacturing techniques and innovations. At the same time, growing concerns about food waste, environmental harm and the depletion of natural resources are driving increasing interest in the use of underutilized bioresources in food systems. Fruit and vegetable processing waste, cereal waste, leguminous bioresources, wasted coffee grounds, etc., might be promising bioresources with a considerable potential in boosting the nutritional and functional quality of bakery products and being in line with the principles of circular economy. The present narrative review aims to provide an overview of the available literature on incorporating underutilized bioresources into bread products, with respect to nutritional enhancement, sustainability, consumer acceptance and competitive advantages. In this study, emerging breakthroughs in fiber enrichment, protein augmentation, antioxidant optimization, alternative flour use and waste valorization will be discussed. It also explores the effects of Industry 4.0 technology on sustainable bakery innovation, including artificial intelligence, blockchain systems, automation, robots and smart packaging technologies. A review of published research reveals that underutilized bioresources can enrich baked items with dietary fiber, protein, antioxidants, and other micronutrients, and can also help minimize food waste. However, optimal utilization of underutilized bioresources faces many problems, such as sensory qualities, legislative compliance, production scale-up, and consumer perception. The role of sustainability communication, sustainability branding and digital technology in consumers’ decision-making is increasing. This analysis gives a multi-disciplinary viewpoint on sustainable bakery innovation and identifies potential research avenues on precision formulation, digitalisation, life cycle assessment and consumer product design.

title: Understanding, measuring, and projecting technology growth in energy transitions
summary: Meeting climate targets depends on how fast low-carbon technologies replace fossil fuels. Wind and solar power are now among the cheapest sources of new electricity, which many take to mean their growth will be rapid, seamless and uniform.
content: Meeting climate targets depends on how fast low-carbon technologies replace fossil fuels. Wind and solar power are now among the cheapest sources of new electricity, which many take to mean their growth will be rapid, seamless and uniform. Techno-economic models, in which deployment is largely cost-driven, project much the same. But how does growth actually unfold, and how far ahead can it be anticipated?This thesis shows that growth instead proceeds in four phases – formative, accelerating, steady, and slowdown – each shaped by drivers and barriers that shift as technology and policy co-evolve. It develops tools that analyse growth as it unfolds, without imposing a fixed shape or destination, and locate shifts between phases directly in deployment data. The findings contradict three common assumptions. Growth does not follow a simple S-curve: for wind and solar, initial acceleration typically ends at around 3% of a country's electricity generation, far earlier than an S-curve's midpoint implies, giving way to prolonged steady growth punctuated by stalls and re-accelerations. Learning rates are not constant: across 145 cost series, the cost decline per doubling of deployment steepens as technologies mature, yet annual cost reductions slow, because each doubling takes longer. And technologies do not spread evenly: across more than 90 technologies in over 200 countries, later adopters pass through the phases in less time but deploy more slowly and saturate lower, consistent with a weaker capacity to absorb new technologies.A hindcast-validated probabilistic model, PROLONG, projects a baseline for what is likely given the growth observed across countries, rather than what is cost-optimal or required by a target. Its central projections for wind and solar grow much like the IPCC's 2 °C-compatible pathways, and faster than current policy scenarios. The COP28 pledge to triple renewables by 2030 sits near its 95th percentile, and would require major economies to accelerate wind and solar growth by 1.4 to 5 times. Together these findings replace a smooth, cost-driven picture with a phase-based one, in which barriers change from phase to phase rather than fading as technologies become cheap, and the support that sustains growth evolves with them.

title: Chemical Looping Reforming of Methane Coupled with CO2 Splitting Using a Sol–Gel-Derived LaFe0.4Co0.6O3 Oxygen Carrier
summary: Abstract Chemical looping reforming of CH4 coupled with CO2 splitting (CLRCS) is an attractive technology that enables covalorization of CO2 and CH4 to high- value syngas. In CLRCS, oxygen carriers shuttle oxygen from CO2 to CH4, enabling s
content: Abstract Chemical looping reforming of CH4 coupled with CO2 splitting (CLRCS) is an attractive technology that enables covalorization of CO2 and CH4 to high- value syngas. In CLRCS, oxygen carriers shuttle oxygen from CO2 to CH4, enabling selective methane partial oxidation and CO2 splitting. However, rational optimization of perovskite oxygen carriers is pivotal to advancing this technology. Herein, a set of Co-doped LaFeO3 perovskite oxygen carriers (LaFe1–xCoxO3, x = 0–1) were synthesized via an optimized sol–gel method. The catalytic performances of materials were measured in a fixed-bed reactor at 750–950 °C, complemented by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) characterizations for structural analysis. Among all tested samples, LaFe0.4Co0.6O3 achieves superior performance at 850 °C, with 92% CH4 conversion and ∼90% syngas selectivity (H2/CO ≈ 2). Moderate Co incorporation remodels the Fe-centered perovskite lattice, which appeared to tune the material redox properties. By contrast, excessive Co doping (x > 0.6) deteriorates regeneration capacity and cyclic stability. Catalytic behavior is highly sensitive to the oxidant atmosphere: CO2 and H2O as mild oxidants are hypothesized to preserve the oxygen carrier in a favorable incompletely oxidized state for selective reforming, whereas O2 causes overoxidation, restricting CH4 conversion to 60% and syngas selectivity to 10%. Moreover, optimizing the inlet CO2 concentration further modulates the redox state of LaFe0.4Co0.6O3. Benefiting from optimized oxidation protocols, the material retained steady performance over 100 redox cycles, sustaining 96–98% CH4 conversion, 92.9–95.4% CO selectivity, 93.9–96.8% H2 selectivity, and 91–93% CO2 utilization efficiency. This study proposes plausible design guidelines for perovskite oxygen carriers tailored to sustainable syngas synthesis via CLRCS and provides fundamental structural and operational references for future reactor scale-up and renewable-energy matching of this carbon capture process.

title: Ghana's Net-Zero Transition Implication for Land and Water Use
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This report applies the Climate, Land, Energy and Water systems (CLEWs) Framework using the OSeMOSYS Linear Programming Energy System Model to compare two net-zero pathways for Ghana over 2023–2063: a Net-zero scenario and a Net-zero plus A
content: This report applies the Climate, Land, Energy and Water systems (CLEWs) Framework using the OSeMOSYS Linear Programming Energy System Model to compare two net-zero pathways for Ghana over 2023–2063: a Net-zero scenario and a Net-zero plus Afforestation scenario.

title: Greening cities to ensure biosphere functional integrity: Insights from Rotterdam and Lagos
summary: The Earth Commission has proposed that 20-25% of every square kilometre of managed lands, including in cities, be reserved for nature to ensure its local functioning and human wellbeing -biosphere functional integrity boundary (BFI). This r
content: The Earth Commission has proposed that 20-25% of every square kilometre of managed lands, including in cities, be reserved for nature to ensure its local functioning and human wellbeing -biosphere functional integrity boundary (BFI). This research adopted a multi-method justice-oriented approach grounded in the Earth System Justice framework to assess the challenges and opportunities of implementing this proposed biosphere functional integrity boundary in Rotterdam and Lagos. We conclude: (a) This proposed scientific boundary precedes global policy but complements the EU's voluntary urban greening guidelines. (b) Good quality green is inequitably distributed in case study countries for different reasons. (c) Combining existing large-scale planning and subsidizing small-scale greening efforts should enable Rotterdam to achieve the boundary, despite risks of gentrification, inequitable access, and poor-quality green. For Lagos, development imperatives compete with existing greening. (d) This research has enhanced Earth system justice and its 9 criteria for just boundaries. We believe that adopting a contextually relevant BFI boundary may enable equitable distribution of good quality and accessible green especially for the people who need it most.

title: STREAMS: An open-source screening life cycle assessment tool for UASB-based wastewater treatment — Inventory development and case-study application in a tropical setting
summary: Wastewater treatment plants consume energy and emit greenhouse gases, and in tropical and subtropical regions, where upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) reactors prevail, the destination given to the biogas largely determines the climate
content: Wastewater treatment plants consume energy and emit greenhouse gases, and in tropical and subtropical regions, where upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) reactors prevail, the destination given to the biogas largely determines the climate burden. The environmental performance of UASB reactors coupled with trickling filters (TF), vertical-flow constructed wetlands (VF-CW) or polishing ponds (PP) has not been compared through a single transparent inventory. This study delivers a gate-to-gate operational life cycle inventory for these configurations and their by-product routes; STREAMS, an open-source web application built on that inventory; and a case study of ten operational scenarios at a full-scale WWTP in Campo Grande, Brazil. Impacts were assessed across seven categories using ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H) with Ecoinvent 3.9.1 in the Brazilian regionalization. Data quality was scored with the pedigree matrix and propagated through Monte Carlo iterations under dependent sampling. Replacing the open flare with enclosed combustion and energy recovery reduced global warming by 56% to 92%, although no scenario reached a net credit once the gas engine conversion efficiency was applied. A trickling filter raised global warming by a factor of 1.6, whereas a VF-CW reduced freshwater eutrophication by 55% at thirteen times the land requirement. No configuration performed best in every impact category: UASB with VF-CW and an enclosed flare is indicated where phosphorus discharge governs, and UASB-only with an enclosed flare where climate mitigation governs. The inventory and the source code are open, so utilities can repeat the comparison with local data.

title: When simulator experiences shape later choices: Measuring behavioural spillover on travel preferences
source: Transportation Research Part D Transport and Environment
summary: Behavioural spillover, where one behaviour affects others, non-targeted behaviours, is widely studied in psychology but underexamined in transport, despite its potential to improve sustainability. We offer a novel contribution by combining
content: Behavioural spillover, where one behaviour affects others, non-targeted behaviours, is widely studied in psychology but underexamined in transport, despite its potential to improve sustainability. We offer a novel contribution by combining an immersive and feedback-supported driving simulator experiment with stated choice (SC) components before and after the simulator to test spillover effects on preferences for travel time and carbon emissions. Our design captures how real-time, experience-based feedback, augmented by personalised driving advice, influences behaviour. We find evidence of behavioural shifts, and a link between those shifts in SC preferences and behaviour in the simulator. Crucially, we reveal substantial heterogeneity in responses, underscoring the need to move beyond homogeneous assumptions, with a strong impact of messaging on eco-driving. The relative importance of CO 2 emissions increased by 52.89% following the driving simulator intervention among respondents receiving eco-driving advice, compared with an increase of 31.73% among those who experienced the intervention without advice. The findings highlight the potential for immersive simulator experiences and personalised eco-driving advice to influence short-term environmental preferences and provide a foundation for future research on behavioural spillover in transport.

title: Trends in greenhouse gas emissions from China’s municipal solid waste sector at urban and county levels: key drivers and mitigation strategies
summary: Significant changes have occurred in China’s municipal solid waste (MSW) management methods over the last two decades, yet comprehensive assessments of greenhouse gas (GHG) emission patterns and their driving factors remain limited. In this
content: Significant changes have occurred in China’s municipal solid waste (MSW) management methods over the last two decades, yet comprehensive assessments of greenhouse gas (GHG) emission patterns and their driving factors remain limited. In this study, GHG emissions from the urban and county-level MSW disposal sector in China during 2006–2023 were quantified using the IPCC methodology, and the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) was applied to identify key drivers. Urban and county-level emissions followed different temporal trajectories, with the transition in county-level MSW management occurring later than in urban areas. Total emissions peaked at 134.06 Mt CO 2 -eq in 2019 and remained relatively stable thereafter, while the national average emission intensity declined over the study period. The dominant emission source gradually shifted from landfill to incineration, and this transition occurred earlier in urban areas. Multi-scale spatial heterogeneity was evident, with emission hotspots progressively shifting from eastern and southern coastal regions toward inland areas. Compared with urban areas, county-level waste disposal showed greater mitigation potential due to less developed treatment infrastructure. LMDI results showed that waste generation intensity and treatment structure contributed negatively to emission changes, whereas economic development and population contributed positively to emission changes. These findings support differentiated mitigation strategies for urban and county MSW disposal in China, emphasizing source reduction, system-level optimization, energy efficiency improvement, and regional coordination.

title: Ammonia-assisted carbonation of NaCl-rich produced-water brine: CO2 uptake, sodium conversion, and recoverable salt formation
source: Case Studies in Chemical and Environmental Engineering
summary: Saline brines generated during oilfield-produced-water treatment are difficult to manage and remain underused as resource-recovery feedstocks. This study evaluated ammonia-assisted Solvay-type carbonation of a field-derived NaCl-rich produc
content: Saline brines generated during oilfield-produced-water treatment are difficult to manage and remain underused as resource-recovery feedstocks. This study evaluated ammonia-assisted Solvay-type carbonation of a field-derived NaCl-rich produced-water brine using a laboratory bubble-column reactor. Controlled synthetic-solution experiments were used to examine how ammoniation and NaCl concentration affected liquid-phase total carbon (TC), while produced-water experiments quantified apparent dissolved-sodium conversion and recovered-solid characteristics. Among the tested produced-water conditions, the highest apparent Na + conversion was 47% at a nominal NH 3 concentration of 6.5 M. In synthetic solutions, ammoniation increased liquid-phase TC accumulation, whereas increasing NaCl concentration reduced the TC response, consistent with ionic-strength and salting-out effects. XRD identified NH 4 HCO 3 as the dominant crystalline phase in the recovered solid, with overlapping reflections permitting only qualitative assignment of possible minor Na-bearing bicarbonate/carbonate and residual chloride contributions. FTIR supported bicarbonate/carbonate functionality, and SEM–EDS showed a heterogeneous C-, O-, and N-rich solid with spatially variable Na and Cl. The results demonstrate the feasibility of ammonia-assisted carbonation for apparent sodium conversion in a real produced-water brine, while showing that product selectivity, ammonia partitioning and recovery, and complete Na/C/N mass balances are central to further process development.

title: Marine arsenate evolution during Proterozoic oxygenation events and implications for biological phosphate metabolism
summary: Abstract Earth’s atmosphere and oceans experienced two major episodes of ocean-atmosphere oxygenation that transformed the planet and shaped the evolution of the oxygen-rich biosphere between 2.45 and 0.541 billion years ago (Ga). These cha
content: Abstract Earth’s atmosphere and oceans experienced two major episodes of ocean-atmosphere oxygenation that transformed the planet and shaped the evolution of the oxygen-rich biosphere between 2.45 and 0.541 billion years ago (Ga). These changes increased the abundance of oxidized chemicals in seawater, but their distribution and effects on the availability and utilization of essential nutrients remain poorly understood. Here we show that these oxygenation events were accompanied by stepwise increases in marine arsenate content—a toxic compound that closely resembles phosphate and interferes with its biological use. Arsenate concentrations rose during the first global oxygenation event and again after the end of the Sturtian global glaciation. Our results suggest that seawater contained much higher arsenate relative to phosphate than today for much of early Earth’s history, likely restricting biological access to phosphate. After the Sturtian glaciation, increasing phosphate availability lowered the arsenate-to-phosphate ratio, reducing arsenate toxicity and enabling more efficient phosphate use in shallow coastal seas, thereby supporting the expansion of oxygen-dependent life.

title: From acidic extreme environments to agriculture: a multi-stress-tolerant Talaromyces pseudofuniculosus enhances soybean growth under abiotic stress
summary: Extremophilic fungi are a relatively unexplored source of stress-resilient microbes for sustainable agriculture. Here, we describe Talaromyces pseudofuniculosus FAR, isolated from the highly acidic site of Piccolo Inferno in southern Italy
content: Extremophilic fungi are a relatively unexplored source of stress-resilient microbes for sustainable agriculture. Here, we describe Talaromyces pseudofuniculosus FAR, isolated from the highly acidic site of Piccolo Inferno in southern Italy and identified by ITS and β-tubulin (BenA) sequencing. Despite its origin from an extreme environment, T. pseudofuniculosus FRA remained fully functional under non-stress conditions and displayed tolerance to salinity and heavy metals while maintaining key plant growth-promoting traits, including phosphate solubilization, auxin-related compound production and hydrolytic activities. In soybean (Glycine max L.), the live fungus promoted plant growth under both non-stress conditions and agriculturally relevant salinity and copper stress, and successfully colonized the roots. A cell-free extracellular extract (exCFS) promoted early seedling development in vitro, but its effects were not sustained in pot experiments. GC-MS analysis provided a qualitative characterization of the extracellular metabolite profile and revealed condition-dependent differences between control, NaCl and CuSO4; growth conditions, indicating environment-dependent modulation of fungal metabolism. Overall, these findings highlight the physiological and metabolic plasticity of T. pseudofuniculosus FRA and support its potential as a fungal biostimulant for saline- and metal-impacted agricultural soils.

title: Hop ( Humulus lupulus L.) Residual Biomass: Attributes, Past Experiences and Opportunities for Future Utilization
summary: Hop (Humulus lupulus L.), a perennial climber plant, has a significant agricultural and industrial presence, primarily valued for its cones in the beer brewing industry. However, the residual biomass, comprising leaves and bines, is often u
content: Hop (Humulus lupulus L.), a perennial climber plant, has a significant agricultural and industrial presence, primarily valued for its cones in the beer brewing industry. However, the residual biomass, comprising leaves and bines, is often underutilized. Research has highlighted the vast utilization potential of this biomass, which can be effectively utilized as a source of bio-fertilizers through bio-composting, and traditionally for medicinal and fodder purposes, too. Additionally, hop residual biomass has been identified as a potential bast-fiber crop, comprising phloem fibers and woody core. The structural carbohydrates in the hop stem, including cellulose, can have great potential for pulping and production of nanocellulose. Furthermore, the phloem fibers can be used as a filler in natural fiber‑reinforced composites, influencing their mechanical properties. The annual discharge of hop residual biomass in the European Union alone is estimated to be around 100,000–120,000 tons, underscoring the need for sustainable utilization strategies. This review highlights the importance of utilizing hop biomass residues as a raw material for a range of applications. Additionally, by developing efficient processing technologies, the full potential of hop residual biomass can be unlocked, reducing waste and promoting a more circular and sustainable economy.

title: Combustion-derived air pollution and heat from gas-fired appliances in commercial kitchens can exceed health-based guidelines
summary: Abstract Commercial kitchens may expose an estimated 15.7 million U.S. workers to elevated air pollution and heat, yet real-world measurements are limited and no prior study has compared commercial kitchens with gas-fired appliances to full
content: Abstract Commercial kitchens may expose an estimated 15.7 million U.S. workers to elevated air pollution and heat, yet real-world measurements are limited and no prior study has compared commercial kitchens with gas-fired appliances to fully electric ones. We monitored pollutants and temperature in 27 commercial kitchens in California, Pennsylvania, and New York, including 24 natural gas- or propane-fired and 3 fully electric, during both work and idle periods. We measured nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), carbon monoxide (CO), carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), methane (CH 4 ), benzene, and temperature at five locations within each kitchen relevant for chefs and cooks. During work hours, NO 2 measured immediately outside ventilation hoods and in ambient kitchen areas exceeded the US EPA and world health organization 1 h guidelines (100 ppbv) in 17 of 24 (70%) kitchens with gas-fired appliances, reaching a maximum of >1000 ppbv in four kitchens. In total, we captured ∼170 work hours where the 1 h NO 2 guideline was surpassed outside hoods or in ambient areas. CO levels also exceeded the California 1 h guideline (20 ppm) outside of hoods and in ambient kitchen areas for ten hours in three kitchens with gas-fired appliances, whereas benzene exceeded the California 1 h exposure guideline (8.4 ppb) for 12 h in five different kitchens. Likewise, 13 of 19 (68%) fossil-fueled kitchens exceeded OSHA’s proposed high-heat trigger of 90°F (32.2 °C), with 10 recording maximum temperatures above 100°F (37.8 °C). Overall, workers in ∼70% of kitchens with gas-fired appliances we sampled faced routine exposures to pollution and heat that exceeded health-based guidelines despite ventilation systems. None of the electric kitchens exceeded pollutant or temperature thresholds. While we frequently observed high pollutant concentrations during work hours, two-thirds of fossil-fueled kitchens exhibited higher median concentrations of NO 2 , CO, CO 2 , CH 4 , and benzene overnight when ventilation was off but pilot lights remained lit. This finding has implications for cleaning and prep crews and for co-occupants in mixed-use buildings.

title: Investigating perspectives and emotions on climate change among children and adolescents in San Cristóbal, Galápagos
summary: An estimated one billion children live at extremely high risk of adverse effects from climate change. Even when children are not exposed to direct physical impacts, the existential threat of climate change can have a psychological impact by
content: An estimated one billion children live at extremely high risk of adverse effects from climate change. Even when children are not exposed to direct physical impacts, the existential threat of climate change can have a psychological impact by creating a stressor that exacerbates underlying mental health disorders or contributes to the development of new disorders. Children and adolescents worldwide are experiencing high rates of fear and worry related to climate change, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Despite this disparate impact, most studies on this topic have been conducted in the Global North. The Galápagos Islands are part of a medium-income nation and will face stark impacts of climate change in the coming decades. Currently, it is unknown how the threat of climate change is affecting the mental health of the children living in the islands. To address this gap, we conducted semi-structured, qualitative interviews with children and adolescents on the island of San Cristóbal to determine their thoughts, perspectives, and understanding of climate change ( N = 30). These interviews also required participants to draw what they expect the island to look like in 100 years. We identified major themes from the interview transcripts and drawings, including the children’s personal identification with nature, feelings of anger and frustration, and feelings of sadness and loss regarding climate change. The findings from this study will inform interventions to promote emotional resilience among the children in San Cristóbal, as well as educational initiatives to address knowledge gaps.

title: Consolidated geographic and petrophysical dataset for potential underground hydrogen storage focusing on the Global South
summary: Abstract As we move towards a green energy future, comprehensive site characterisation data for energy storage is critical for modelling, policy and guiding investment decisions. In this work, we present a dataset of 518 sub-surface formati
content: Abstract As we move towards a green energy future, comprehensive site characterisation data for energy storage is critical for modelling, policy and guiding investment decisions. In this work, we present a dataset of 518 sub-surface formations spread across 34 countries with an emphasis on the under-explored Global South. Criteria relating to geological suitability and techno-economic feasibility from a wide range of data sources are collected from existing literature in a unified dataset. Scientific publications, industry reports, technical reports and national databases are all considered. Entries to the dataset are compiled with dates, source publications, geographic locations and operating statuses alongside site characteristics. The subsurface structures compiled include hydrocarbon fields, aquifers and salt caverns. Major limitations to consider are poor coverage in Africa & Northern South America, and restricted validation options. No assessments on site feasibility are made, and the data is entirely secondary in nature. This dataset aims to provide the groundwork for further studies in Underground Hydrogen Storage (UHS) adoption by providing input data for preliminary site selection frameworks, system modeling and policy decisions.

title: Diagnosing systematic overestimation and feature dependencies in data-driven predictions of urban CO₂ emissions in China
summary: Machine learning is increasingly used to simulate and predict complex urban phenomena, such as CO₂ emission patterns in cities. However, the effectiveness, biases, and uncertainty of these predictive models are not well understood. This stu
content: Machine learning is increasingly used to simulate and predict complex urban phenomena, such as CO₂ emission patterns in cities. However, the effectiveness, biases, and uncertainty of these predictive models are not well understood. This study systematically evaluates 18 different machine learning algorithms using a rich dataset of county-level CO₂ emissions in China from 2001 to 2020, incorporating 41 diverse features spanning socioeconomic, environmental, and energy consumption factors. The analysis reveals a widespread issue: nearly all models, regardless of type, tend to systematically overestimate emissions in Chinese county-level cities across both space and time. By isolating the effects of feature selection and quantifying uncertainty through bootstrap resampling, the research demonstrates that aggressive dimensionality reduction often harms model performance, while retaining a high number of features is crucial for capturing the true complexity of urban emissions. Tree-based models, such as CatBoost and LightGBM, outperform others in accuracy and uncertainty quantification. These findings highlight the urgent need for the scientific and policy communities to prioritize diagnosing and correcting systematic biases in machine learning models, rather than focusing solely on improving accuracy, to ensure reliable guidance for urban carbon management and climate policy.

title: Ecological connections and territorial planning: potentialities and contradictions
summary: Ecological connectivity is recognized in the literature as a vital factor for reestablishing biodiversity patterns and for mitigating the impacts of climate change. In 2017, the 20 municipalities of the Metropolitan Region of Campinas (RMC)
content: Ecological connectivity is recognized in the literature as a vital factor for reestablishing biodiversity patterns and for mitigating the impacts of climate change. In 2017, the 20 municipalities of the Metropolitan Region of Campinas (RMC) in southeastern Brazil entered into a Term of Agreement to implement an ecological connectivity initiative called the Reconecta Project. This article seeks to identify and analyze the relationships between the project's proposed route and the territorial planning mechanisms established by Brazilian legislation. The methodology employed involved overlaying various informational layers to establish numerical relationships between land use, the territorial planning system established by the three federal levels of government, and the project itself. The findings reveal that the Reconecta Project is located within a landscape matrix that is not conducive to ecological connectivity, as it contains few forest fragments. Although legal land-use planning mechanisms have been adopted, their potential has not been fully realized.

title: Tetranuclear Copper Cluster of N2O Reductase: A Distinctive Copper–Sulfur Metallocluster
summary: Abstract Copper is an essential element involved in several cofactors and organometallic compounds used as catalysts. Although most biological copper centers contain one to three copper ions, nature has evolved a unique tetranuclear copper–
content: Abstract Copper is an essential element involved in several cofactors and organometallic compounds used as catalysts. Although most biological copper centers contain one to three copper ions, nature has evolved a unique tetranuclear copper–sulfur cluster that has attracted the attention of both biochemists and inorganic chemists. This multinuclear copper center has only been observed in one enzyme, nitrous oxide reductase, which catalyzes the reduction of nitrous oxide to dinitrogen, the final step of the denitrification pathway. The structural, spectroscopic, and kinetic properties of this [4CuS] cluster have been the subject of extensive investigation, revealing that it exists in two distinct forms within the enzyme, CuZ[4Cu:2S] and CuZ*[4Cu:1S], with different oxidation states, spectroscopic signatures, and catalytic properties. These features are discussed together with recent advances in understanding the biosynthesis and assembly of this cluster. Inorganic chemists have synthesized a variety of structural and functional models of the CuZ cluster, although none fully reproduces the electronic structure and catalytic efficiency of the native active center. This review discusses the interplay between biological and synthetic studies, illustrating how advances in one field continue to inspire progress in the other while identifying the challenges that must be overcome to achieve truly functional biomimetic catalysts.

title: The Double Dividend of Automation: How Do Industrial Robots Affect Energy and Carbon Intensity?
summary: This paper investigates the effect of industrial robot deployment on energy and carbon intensity, using data from 60 countries over the period 2000–2019 and employing both homogeneous and heterogeneous panel data methods. The findings indic
content: This paper investigates the effect of industrial robot deployment on energy and carbon intensity, using data from 60 countries over the period 2000–2019 and employing both homogeneous and heterogeneous panel data methods. The findings indicate that robot deployment decreases energy and carbon intensity, thereby improving efficiency in both domains. These effects are particularly pronounced at higher intensity levels, underscoring the critical role of robots in enhancing environmental and energy performance.

title: Evaluation of risk scenarios in Ecuador using Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite remote sensing, ERA5-Land climate data, and XGBoost
summary: The present study aims to develop and optimize a spatial risk scenarios model for forest fires in Ecuador through the integration of machine learning and satellite remote sensing.To this end, 103,224 historical records of thermal anomalies
content: The present study aims to develop and optimize a spatial risk scenarios model for forest fires in Ecuador through the integration of machine learning and satellite remote sensing.To this end, 103,224 historical records of thermal anomalies captured by the VIIRS sensor were processed, along with five continuous meteorological variables from the ERA5-Land global reanalysis, spatial coordinates (latitude and longitude), and temporal indicators (month of the year), spanning the period between 2015 and 2025.The methodology was based on the construction of a 5-kilometer resolution spatial grid coupled with the XGBoost classification algorithm, designed to efficiently manage class imbalance in the face of extreme climate events.The computational system achieved an accuracy level of 81% on the test set, validating its robustness with a true positive rate of 0.86 and an area under the ROC curve of 0.8382.Furthermore, the feature importance analysis determined that precipitation deficits and seasonal timing act as the primary drivers of ignition risk, exerting a significantly greater influence than surface temperature, concluding that this scalable and open-access tool allows for high-precision mapping of vulnerable areas in the Andean and coastal regions through scenario-based experiments, aiming to optimize the distribution of state preventive resources against the constant threat of global warming.

title: Trade in Low‐Carbon Technologies: The Role of Climate and Trade Policies
summary: ABSTRACT Curbing carbon emissions to meet the targets set in the Paris Agreement requires the deployment of low‐carbon technologies (LCTs) at a global scale. This paper assesses the role of climate and trade policies in fostering LCT diffus
content: ABSTRACT Curbing carbon emissions to meet the targets set in the Paris Agreement requires the deployment of low‐carbon technologies (LCTs) at a global scale. This paper assesses the role of climate and trade policies in fostering LCT diffusion through trade. Leveraging a comprehensive database of climate policies and a new database identifying trade in LCTs and the tariffs applied to these goods, this paper shows that the introduction of new climate policies has a positive and significant impact on LCT imports. Zooming into specific climate policies, the paper finds that, except for non‐binding ones, all climate policies stimulate LCT imports. The paper also highlights the role of trade policies as an engine of LCT diffusion—reductions in tariffs applied to LCT goods have a sizable impact on LCT imports. On the flip side, results suggest that more protectionist measures would impede the spread of LCTs.

title: Climate change response in the region
summary: The European Arctic’s response to climate change is the main topic of this chapter, with a focus on how Arctic countries have developed and implemented adaptation and mitigation strategies over time. It aims to provide a comparative evaluat
content: The European Arctic’s response to climate change is the main topic of this chapter, with a focus on how Arctic countries have developed and implemented adaptation and mitigation strategies over time. It aims to provide a comparative evaluation of national approaches to climate governance and assess how well they handle the social and gendered dimensions of climate change. The chapter looks at Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, and Iceland individually, tracking the development of their national climate plans, significant policy frameworks, institutional frameworks, and adaption strategies. Chapter is also focuses on how gender views are incorporated into climate and adaptation strategies, as well as how much policy frameworks take equality, participation, representation, and inclusion into account. The analysis shows that while the European Arctic states have created more complete frameworks for climate policy, there is still unequal integration of gender and broader societal factors. The chapter emphasises the significance of shifting from environmental and economic concerns to more inclusive and gender-sensitive climate policy, stressing on both the advantages and disadvantages of current approaches to climate governance.

title: Analysis of institutional governance for the development of climate-smart agriculture in Sistan and Baluchestan Province, Iran
summary: The present study aimed to analyze the role of institutional governance in developing climate-smart agriculture (CSA) in Sistan and Baluchestan Province, Iran. Given the intensification of challenges caused by climate change and weaknesses
content: The present study aimed to analyze the role of institutional governance in developing climate-smart agriculture (CSA) in Sistan and Baluchestan Province, Iran. Given the intensification of challenges caused by climate change and weaknesses in institutional coordination, the successful implementation of CSA policies requires identifying key actors and assessing the quality of their relationships. The research was an applied study conducted using a descriptive-analytical method. Through direct observation and unstructured interviews with experts and key informants (32 individuals), 48 institutions and active associations related to CSA were identified in the province, and their links and interactions were analyzed using social network analysis (SNA). The results indicated that institutional coherence was at a moderate to relatively high level across four networks: agricultural productivity improvement, adaptation to climate change, greenhouse gas mitigation, and CSA. Furthermore, the Agricultural Jihad Organization (AJO), the Governor’s Office (Provincial Government) (GO), the General Directorate of Natural Resources and Watershed Management (NRWM), the Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines, and Agriculture (CCIMA), and the General Directorate of Environmental Protection (EP) were identified as the key actors with the highest centrality and social influence. The findings suggest that effective CSA development governance requires strengthening horizontal and vertical connections among governmental, scientific, financial, and civil institutions to prevent duplication and improve synergy in policymaking and the implementation of adaptive programs. By emphasizing institutional analysis, this research provides a framework for better understanding climate-based governance networks, which can be applied to other regions with similar conditions.

title: A multi-measure adaptation method for temporal coordination under drought–flood transition risks
source: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction
summary: Rapid drought–flood transitions create short-term conflicts between drought mitigation and flood-control measures, while fixed decision modes may not adapt as risk evolves. This study develops a prediction–decision coupling framework that i
content: Rapid drought–flood transitions create short-term conflicts between drought mitigation and flood-control measures, while fixed decision modes may not adapt as risk evolves. This study develops a prediction–decision coupling framework that integrates Transformer-based precipitation forecasting with the NK model to evaluate the synergistic performance of DRR measure portfolios under evolving risks. The Transformer model generates daily precipitation quantile forecasts from historical meteorological data and employs the transition risk index (TRI) to characterize probabilistic DFAA risk states. These states are incorporated into the NK model to compare independent decision-making (IDM), continuously coordinated decision-making (CDM), and temporally coordinated decision-making (TCDM). A case study of Huangshan City identifies increasing drought-to-flood risk in mid-June 2024 and a weak flood-to-drought signal in mid-July. Under non-modular dependencies, TCDM exceeds IDM and CDM by 10.17% and 2.00%, respectively, in cost-adjusted performance. Sensitivity analyses indicate that this advantage depends on coordination and switching costs. The results suggest that coordination intensity and measure priority should vary with risk phase, transition direction, measure dependencies, and forecast uncertainty, providing portfolio-level support for adaptive drought–flood risk reduction.

title: AntimicrobialResistanceinaChangingClimate:Evidence,CausalPathways, and Prevention Strategie
source: Pakistan Journal of Medical & Cardiological Review
summary: Background: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and climate change are both significant global health threats increasingly recognized as mechanistically interconnected. This review critically synthesises evidence on the potential for climate-rel
content: Background: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and climate change are both significant global health threats increasingly recognized as mechanistically interconnected. This review critically synthesises evidence on the potential for climate-related hazards (temperature, heatwaves, flooding and drought) to alter and intensify AMR via biological, environmental and health-system pathways, and evaluates the causal strength and implications for prevention. Methods: This critical narrative review involved a structured literature-identification and updating process, critically appraising systematic and scoping reviews, primary ecological and genomic studies, modelling analyses, and authoritative One Health reports through August 2026, organized by hazard and pathway rather than paper by paper. Results: Association of temperature with AMR is one of the most consistent and replicated findings across ecological studies in the United States, Europe and China, and is supported by a large multi-country genomic analysis of Salmonella resistance genes. This relationship is not generalizable: at least one adjusted analysis found no significant temperature-resistance association, highlighting the organism- and context-specific nature of the relationship. Resistant pathogens and resistance genes are mobilized in the environment during flooding, but there is limited direct evidence of this leading to increased clinical infection. Ecological study design, residual confounding and limited data availability in South Asia, including Pakistan, limit causal inference across hazards. Evidence assessing climate-specific AMR prevention interventions remains limited. Conclusions: Climate change must be considered as a potential contributing and amplifying factor for AMR, rather than a proven independent cause. Climate-informed surveillance is a priority for LMICs, including Pakistan, for One Health AMR strategies.

title: Soil Carbon Sequestration Potential of Climate-Smart Agronomic Practices: A Critical Review
source: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology
summary: Agricultural soils can contribute to climate mitigation through management that increases organic carbon inputs, limits avoidable losses and sustains favourable conditions for carbon retention. Yet higher soil carbon concentrations, larger
content: Agricultural soils can contribute to climate mitigation through management that increases organic carbon inputs, limits avoidable losses and sustains favourable conditions for carbon retention. Yet higher soil carbon concentrations, larger stocks relative to conventional management and additional atmospheric carbon removal are not interchangeable outcomes. This critical narrative review evaluates the sequestration potential of cover cropping, diversified rotations, residue retention, reduced tillage, organic amendments, biochar, balanced nutrient management, water management and agroforestry in predominantly mineral agricultural soils. Verified scholarly literature with publication coverage through 30 July 2026 was synthesised according to intervention mechanisms, measurement validity, temporal persistence and whole-system greenhouse gas consequences. The most consistent evidence supports maintaining or increasing plant-derived inputs and combining compatible practices, rather than assuming that disturbance reduction alone produces substantial whole-profile gains. Cover crops commonly increase topsoil carbon, but responses depend on biomass production, growing windows, water availability and nitrogen management.
