content: Abstract. This paper presents sparse gradient descent as a solution for variable selection in convex piecewise linear regression where the model is given as the maximum of [Formula: see text]-affine functions [Formula: see text] for [Formula: see text]. Here, [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text] denote the ground-truth weight vectors and intercepts. A nonasymptotic local convergence analysis is provided for Sp-GD under sub-Gaussian noise when the covariate distribution satisfies the sub-Gaussianity and anticoncentration properties. When the model order and parameters are fixed, Sp-GD provides an [Formula: see text]-accurate estimate given [Formula: see text] observations, where [Formula: see text] denotes the noise variance. This also implies the exact parameter recovery by Sp-GD from [Formula: see text] noise-free observations. Since optimizing the squared loss for sparse max-affine is nonconvex, an initialization scheme is proposed to provide a suitable initial estimate within the basin of attraction for Sp-GD, i.e., sufficiently accurate to invoke the convergence guarantees. The initialization scheme uses sparse principal component analysis to estimate the subspace spanned by [Formula: see text], then applies an [Formula: see text]-covering search to estimate the model parameters. A nonasymptotic analysis is presented for this initialization scheme when the covariates and noise samples follow Gaussian distributions. When the model order and parameters are fixed, this initialization scheme provides an [Formula: see text]-accurate estimate given [Formula: see text] observations. A new transformation named Real Maslov Dequantization (RMD) is proposed to transform sparse generalized polynomials into sparse max-affine models. The error decay rate of RMD is shown to be exponentially small in its temperature parameter. Furthermore, theoretical guarantees for Sp-GD are extended to the bounded noise model induced by RMD. Numerical Monte Carlo results corroborate theoretical findings for Sp-GD and the initialization scheme.

title: Fault-tolerant execution of error-corrected quantum algorithms
summary: Scaling up quantum algorithms to tackle high-impact problems in science and industry requires quantum error correction and fault tolerance. While progress has been made in experimentally realizing error-corrected primitives, the end-to-end
content: Scaling up quantum algorithms to tackle high-impact problems in science and industry requires quantum error correction and fault tolerance. While progress has been made in experimentally realizing error-corrected primitives, the end-to-end execution of logical quantum algorithms using only fault-tolerant (FT) components has remained out of reach. We demonstrate the FT and error-corrected execution of two quantum algorithms, the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm applied to the Poisson equation, on Quantinuum H2 and Helios trapped-ion quantum processors using the $[[7,1,3]]$ Steane code. For QAOA circuits on 5 and 6 logical qubits, we show performance improvements from increasing the number of QAOA layers and the number of $T$ gates used to approximate logical rotations, despite increased physical circuit complexity. We further show that QAOA circuits with up to 8 logical qubits and 9 logical $T$ gates perform similarly to unencoded circuits. For the largest QAOA circuits we run, with 12 logical (97 physical) qubits and 2132 physical two-qubit gates, we still observe better-than-random performance. Finally, we show that adding active QEC cycles and increasing the repeat-until-success limit of state preparation subroutines can improve the performance of a quantum algorithm, thereby demonstrating critical capabilities of scalable FT quantum computation. Our results are enabled by an FT logical $T$ gate implementation with an infidelity of $\sim 2.6(4)\times10^{-3}$ and dynamic circuits with measurement-dependent feedback. Our work demonstrates near-break-even performance of complex, error-corrected algorithmic quantum circuits using only FT components.

title: Exact analytical PGSE signal for diffusion confined to a cylindrical surface using a spectral Laplacian formalism
summary: Abstract Objective. To derive an exact analytical expression for the diffusion MRI signal arising from diffusion confined to a cylindrical surface under finite rectangular pulsed-gradient spin-echo (PGSE) gradients, and to develop computati
content: Abstract Objective. To derive an exact analytical expression for the diffusion MRI signal arising from diffusion confined to a cylindrical surface under finite rectangular pulsed-gradient spin-echo (PGSE) gradients, and to develop computationally efficient strategies for repeated model evaluations. Approach. The Bloch–Torrey equation was solved using a spectral matrix formalism of the Laplace operator in the eigenbasis of the cylindrical surface. The resulting signal is expressed as a product of non-commuting matrix exponentials and is valid for arbitrary rectangular gradient durations and separations, without approximations to the diffusion propagator or spin phase distribution. A reduced real spectral basis was introduced to decrease the dimensionality of the problem. Accelerated implementations based on Strang splitting and Gauss–Legendre quadrature were developed for repeated signal evaluations and computation of the spherical mean. The analytical signal was validated against Monte Carlo diffusion simulations. Main results. The exact formulation showed excellent agreement with Monte Carlo simulations over a wide range of cylinder radii and acquisition parameters. The spectral expansion converged rapidly with mode order, and the reduced basis substantially decreased computational cost without loss of accuracy. The accelerated implementations provided large additional speed-ups while retaining controllable errors relative to the exact solution. Significance. The proposed framework extends exact finite-pulse solutions of the Bloch–Torrey equation to diffusion confined to cylindrical surfaces and provides practical implementations for directional and orientationally averaged diffusion MRI signals. It therefore offers an approximation-free reference for assessing faster signal approximations and for applications requiring large numbers of model evaluations.

title: Pourquoi et comment innover autrement ? L’innovation responsable à impact : un agenda de recherche pour les sciences de gestion
summary: Le dogme de l’innovation intensive se heurte désormais aux dégradations croissantes que cette course engendre sur l’environnement naturel, l’obsolescence des compétences et à la perte de sens pour les salariés. Il faut donc innover autremen
content: Le dogme de l’innovation intensive se heurte désormais aux dégradations croissantes que cette course engendre sur l’environnement naturel, l’obsolescence des compétences et à la perte de sens pour les salariés. Il faut donc innover autrement et repenser l’innovation en intégrant les impacts sociétaux. Mais pourquoi et comment faire ? L’objectif de cet article est de proposer un agenda de recherche pour les sciences de gestion pour refonder la gestion des innovations à impact. En premier lieu, il s’agit de comprendre comment l’innovation est aujourd’hui cadrée, les impensés que ce cadrage produit et les impacts indésirables provoqués. En deuxième lieu, temps, il s’agit d’étudier et théoriser les pratiques d’innovation responsables à impact dans leur diversité, tout en proposant un cadre intégrateur. Enfin, en troisième lieu, nous esquissons des pistes pour changer les cadres cognitifs de l’innovation à impact, à savoir adopter une responsabilité projective, repenser l’instrumentation gestionnaire et mettre en cohérence les politiques publiques. Codes JEL : O30, O31, O32, O33, O35

title: Strategi Sistemik Starbucks dalam Mempertahankan Eksistensi dan Ekspansi di China Tahun 2017-2025
summary: Globalization has driven multinational corporations to expand into various countries, including the food and beverage (F&B) sector, which is heavily shaped by local cultural and consumer dynamics. As one of the world's largest coffeehouse c
content: Globalization has driven multinational corporations to expand into various countries, including the food and beverage (F&B) sector, which is heavily shaped by local cultural and consumer dynamics. As one of the world's largest coffeehouse chains, Starbucks faces significant challenges in maintaining its presence and expanding its market share in China. This study examines the strategies Starbucks has used to contend with local competitors such as Luckin Coffee, as well as shifting consumer behaviors and rising consumer nationalism in China. To address these pressures, Starbucks has implemented a comprehensive localization strategy. The company has launched product innovations based on local flavors and developed "heritage stores" to honor local culture. It has also expanded into lower-tier cities to capture new market potential. Meanwhile, it has strengthened digital capabilities by integrating with domestic e-commerce ecosystems to improve consumer access. To appeal to the younger generation, Starbucks has adapted its business model by emphasizing digitalization and introducing more affordable promotions. These measures have driven significant growth in both store counts and total assets. However, intense price competition has caused revenue to stagnate in recent years. Ultimately, Starbucks's long-term viability in China hinges on its ability to keep adapting to market disruptions and shifting local preferences.

title: Authentic Leadership, Psychological Capital, and Meaningfulness of Work: Predicting Generation Z Employees' Mental Well-Being
source: Jurnal Relevansi Ekonomi Manajemen dan Bisnis
summary: This study examined the effects of authentic leadership and psychological capital on the mental well-being of Generation Z employees and investigated the mediating roles of psychological capital and meaningfulness of work. Given Generation
content: This study examined the effects of authentic leadership and psychological capital on the mental well-being of Generation Z employees and investigated the mediating roles of psychological capital and meaningfulness of work. Given Generation Z’s increasing presence in the workforce and concerns regarding employee well-being, this study employed a quantitative approach using a cross-sectional survey of 300 Generation Z employees in Batam, Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.0. The structural model demonstrated substantial explanatory power for mental well-being (R² = 0.747), with predictive relevance indicated by Q² = 0.582. Authentic leadership positively affected mental well-being (β = 0.485, p < 0.001) and psychological capital (β = 0.563, p < 0.001), but did not significantly affect the meaningfulness of work (β = 0.068, p = 0.235). Psychological capital significantly mediated the relationship between authentic leadership and mental well-being (β = 0.215, p < 0.001), whereas meaningfulness of work did not (β = 0.015, p = 0.246). The findings highlight the importance of authentic leadership in strengthening psychological resources associated with Generation Z employees’ mental well-being and provide implications for leadership development in organizations.

title: Evaluation of Management Accounting Implementation in Supporting MSME Operational Efficiency (Krutukan MSME Case Study)
source: Indonesian Journal of Islamic Economics and Finance
summary: MSMEs have an important role in the economy, but they still face limitations in cost management, financial recording, and operational planning. This condition causes cost information to not be fully used as a basis for decision-making and e
content: MSMEs have an important role in the economy, but they still face limitations in cost management, financial recording, and operational planning. This condition causes cost information to not be fully used as a basis for decision-making and efficiency improvement. This study aims to evaluate the implementation of management accounting in supporting operational efficiency in Krutukan MSMEs, especially in recording and managing costs, determining selling prices, production planning, and cost control. This study uses a qualitative approach with a single intrinsic case study method and involves one main informant, namely the owner of Krutukan MSMEs. Data was obtained through observation for two days, in-depth interviews with MSME owners, and documentation, then analyzed using the interactive model Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña through the stages of coding, categorization, theme formation, data presentation, and verification. The results of the study show that management accounting is applied only through cost recording, raw material needs planning, expenditure control, and the use of cost information in determining selling prices. However, recording is still done manually and costs have not been classified systematically. Simulations show that expenditure-based HPP that does not include all BOP of Rp. 8,000 per package increased to Rp. 9,500 per package after the full cost calculation approach included a BOP of Rp. 150,000, so that the previous HPP was lower than Rp. 1,500 per package. The study concluded that operational efficiency can be improved through cost classification, simple budgeting, systematic HPP calculation, and digitization of financial records.

title: What “Digitization” Means for the Limbe Deep Sea Port (Cameroon) Project: Definitions, Components, Pathways, and Implications
summary: Digitization in the deep sea port context is often invoked as shorthand for technological modernization, yet its operational meaning and implications vary widely by place. This paper explicates what “digitization” means for the Limbe Deep S
content: Digitization in the deep sea port context is often invoked as shorthand for technological modernization, yet its operational meaning and implications vary widely by place. This paper explicates what “digitization” means for the Limbe Deep Sea Port in Cameroon by situating the concept within port operational processes, stakeholder relationships, governance environments, and socioeconomic constraints specific to Limbe and comparable West/Central African ports. Drawing on an interdisciplinary desk-based literature review of academic studies, international agency reports, industry white papers, and regional policy documents, the study adopts a conceptual-analytical approach to define digitization as the systematic conversion and integration of analogue and paper-based port procedures into interoperable digital systems that enable real-time data exchange, automated workflows, evidence-based decision-making, and secure electronic transactions across the port ecosystem. The paper disaggregates digitization into technological (TOS, PCS, VTMS, IoT, analytics, blockchain, cybersecurity), organizational (process re-engineering, governance, procurement), human factors (skills, roles, change management), and regulatory (single window, data governance) dimensions. It identifies measurable indicators to assess progress—transaction digitalization rate, vessel turnaround time, dwell time, customs clearance time, system uptime, and workforce certification rates—and outlines likely benefits (efficiency, transparency, environmental monitoring, regional connectivity) and risks (digital divides, cyber threats, governance bottlenecks, finance constraints). The analysis highlights contextual enablers and barriers for Limbe, including infrastructure, institutional capacity, financing options, and regional integration imperatives. The paper concludes with policy and operational recommendations that prioritize staged interventions—low‑complexity quick wins, mid‑term integration, and long‑term smart-port capabilities—anchored in inclusive governance, blended finance, workforce development, and cyber resilience. The findings aim to provide a clear, practical, and academically grounded definition of digitization tailored to Limbe’s developmental and geopolitical realities. Keywords: Limbe Deep Sea Port; port digitization; Port Community System; Terminal Operating System; Cameroon; smart ports; maritime governance

title: Exploraciones digestivas. La relación estética y conceptual entre cine y performance en la película Crímenes del futuro de David Cronenberg
source: H-ART Revista de historia teoría y crítica de arte
summary: The paper argues that the film Crimes of the Future opens up a critical dialogue on the relationship between the body and technology through two controversial figures in the world of performance art: Orlan and Stelarc. The tensions arising
content: The paper argues that the film Crimes of the Future opens up a critical dialogue on the relationship between the body and technology through two controversial figures in the world of performance art: Orlan and Stelarc. The tensions arising from this relationship are framed by the premise that the evolution of bodies is not to be found in the body-machine hybridisation and prosthetics; rather, it lies in the mysterious rebellion of the organs: the organ in question—or rather, the system in conflict—is here the digestive system. Digestion is therefore explored as the film’s acoustic identity, as an aesthetic experience, and as the conceptual framework for the analytical writing of this text.

title: Climate policies and adaptive capacities: a cross-analysis of sectoral, intersectoral, and international actions
summary: Against intensifying climate risks, this study compares the associations of sectoral, cross-sectoral, and international climate policies with annual changes in adaptation readiness. Using an unbalanced panel of 59 countries from 2002 to 202
content: Against intensifying climate risks, this study compares the associations of sectoral, cross-sectoral, and international climate policies with annual changes in adaptation readiness. Using an unbalanced panel of 59 countries from 2002 to 2022, it estimates OLS and SUR models with policy–income interactions and assesses robustness through Mundlak and dynamic GMM specifications. Cross-sectoral policies display the most consistent positive association with readiness improvements, although Wald tests show no statistically significant difference between their coefficients and those of sectoral policies. The two approaches therefore appear complementary rather than substitutable. International policies are mainly associated with improvements in lower-income countries, and their contribution weakens as income rises. The findings emphasize cross-sectoral coordination, sector-specific expertise, sustained implementation, and strategies adapted to national economic and institutional capacities.

title: THE STATE OF AVAILABLE ENVIRONMENT AS FACTOR OF MOBILITY OF PEOPLE WITH DISABILITY IN MODERN RUSSIA
source: Problems of Social Hygiene Public Health and History of Medicine
summary: The accessibility of social environment for people with disabilities is major condition of social rehabilitation and increasing their individual social mobility based on equal possibilities. By means of social mobility, people with disabili
content: The accessibility of social environment for people with disabilities is major condition of social rehabilitation and increasing their individual social mobility based on equal possibilities. By means of social mobility, people with disability receive access to various public benefits and possibility to lead comprehensively rich life. However, in Russian regions barriers of social environment remain to be significant. The study of accessibility of objects and spaces for low-mobile categories of the disabled was carried out in 2025 in conditions of the Murmansk Oblast. The data concerning partial accessibility of environment (accessibility index for all observation elements is 0.28, where 1 represents full accessibility and -1 represents complete inaccessibility) was obtained. However, in a comprehensive assessment of the accessibility of the environment when constructing logistics routes for the spatial mobility of people with disabilities, a lower value (index -0.27) was obtained. However, under complex assessment of accessibility of environment during construction of logistic routes for spatial mobility of people with the disability lesser value was received (index -0.27) demonstrating partial inaccessibility of spatial infrastructural environment. The main reason is fragmentation and randomness of location of accessible objects and absence of available routes to them. The results of the study point to necessity of integrated making of accessible environment, providing conditions for mobility at all stages of movement of people with disability and for all categories of disability. The results of the study can be useful under making accessible environment on territories of the Subjects of the Russian Federation.

title: Does sustainable finance strengthen corporate governance? Evidence from ASEAN banks
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe growing global demand for the integration of strong corporate governance in the banking industry is essential for enhancing financial performance. However, the interactive role of sustainable
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe growing global demand for the integration of strong corporate governance in the banking industry is essential for enhancing financial performance. However, the interactive role of sustainable finance in strengthening governance mechanisms remains relatively underexplored. This study aims to examine whether adopting sustainable finance practices strengthens corporate governance mechanisms in the banking sector in ASEAN countries during the period 2018–2022. Utilizing the Fixed Effects Model, this study presents a notable finding. The results indicate that the interaction between management scores and green bonds has a positive and significant effect on Return on Assets, whereby a 5% increase in green bonds exposure raises ROA by 0.248, but exerts a negative effect on Return on Equity, with a decrease of 0.340 for every 1% increase. In contrast, the interaction between shareholder scores and green bonds has a negative and significant impact on ROA, with a decline of 0.223 for each 5% increase, while positively influencing ROE by 0.222 for every 1% increase. This study confirms that green bonds asymmetrically moderate the relationship between corporate governance and banking performance, in which management-oriented governance enhances asset efficiency but suppresses ROE, whereas shareholder-oriented governance reduces ROA while improving ROE. Conceptually, green bonds function as a balancing mechanism between corporate governance and banking performance, whereby managerial governance improves asset efficiency at the expense of equity returns, while shareholder-based governance enhances ROE with the trade-off of lower ROA.

title: Empowering Green Womenpreneurs: Qualitative Interview Dataset of Women Entrepreneurs in Brazil's Beauty Sector, 2024-2025
summary: This dataset contains qualitative interview data collected as part of the Empowering Green Womenpreneurs research project, funded by the UK Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC). The project investigates the experiences of women entre
content: This dataset contains qualitative interview data collected as part of the Empowering Green Womenpreneurs research project, funded by the UK Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC). The project investigates the experiences of women entrepreneurs in Brazil, with a particular focus on sustainability, circular economy practices, and the challenges and opportunities associated with developing environmentally sustainable businesses. The dataset comprises 26 semi-structured interviews conducted online with women entrepreneurs operating micro and nano enterprises across different sectors in the state of São Paulo, Brazil, between May and August 2025. Interviews explored participants' entrepreneurial journeys, business models, sustainability and circular economy practices, barriers and enablers to business development, innovation, access to finance, and institutional support. The interviews were conducted in Portuguese, audio-recorded with participants' informed consent, transcribed verbatim, and anonymised prior to analysis. The dataset provides rich qualitative evidence on women-led entrepreneurship, sustainable business practices, gender-related challenges, and entrepreneurial ecosystems in an emerging economy. It offers valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners interested in entrepreneurship, gender, sustainability, circular economy, and inclusive economic development.

title: Institutional risk, finance, and the limits of techno-economic optimality in green hydrogen deployment
summary: Green hydrogen is widely positioned as a key option for deep decarbonization, yet large-scale deployment remains limited despite growing techno-economic potential. This review examines how non-technical conditions influence the feasibility
content: Green hydrogen is widely positioned as a key option for deep decarbonization, yet large-scale deployment remains limited despite growing techno-economic potential. This review examines how non-technical conditions influence the feasibility of green hydrogen business models, using the Netherlands as an illustrative case. A review-driven mixed-methods framework integrates evidence from a systematic literature review, semi-structured expert interviews, and an established hourly-resolved techno-economic optimization model to examine how policy design, investment risk, infrastructure constraints, and demand formation influence both the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) and deployment feasibility. A multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) is employed to synthesize qualitative and quantitative evidence and prioritize the principal drivers and barriers identified across the different sources. The synthesized evidence, supported by the illustrative techno-economic analysis, indicates that LCOH values below €6 kg −1 are attainable under favorable assumptions, including low renewable electricity prices, reduced weighted average cost of capital (WACC), and access to underground hydrogen storage. However, regulatory fragmentation, grid congestion, weak demand coordination, and limited institutional legitimacy substantially constrain the realization of such conditions in practice. The findings demonstrate that techno-economic assessments alone may overestimate the deployability of green hydrogen when institutional risk and market coordination challenges are not explicitly considered. The proposed integrative framework provides a structured approach for assessing hydrogen market readiness in early-stage European contexts and supports the alignment of techno-economic competitiveness with governance capacity, investment conditions, and social acceptance.

title: Preferences for digital health services among patients with chronic kidney disease: a discrete choice experiment
summary: Background Digital health technologies offer novel approaches for chronic kidney disease management. However, quantitative evidence on patient preferences for digital health services remains limited. There is a critical need for more eviden
content: Background Digital health technologies offer novel approaches for chronic kidney disease management. However, quantitative evidence on patient preferences for digital health services remains limited. There is a critical need for more evidence on the sustainability and optimization of chronic kidney disease management in China, especially from the demand side. Policymakers require detailed data on the needs of chronic kidney disease patients regarding digital health services. Methods A discrete choice experiment was conducted to measure the preferences of people with chronic kidney disease. Participants were recruited face-to-face in Sichuan Province, China, and completed an anonymous electronic questionnaire on-site. The mixed logit model evaluated participants’ preferences for six attributes, estimating willingness to pay and relative importance, and performing subgroup analysis based on the initial model results. Results A total of 322 patients completed the questionnaire (mean age 49.8 years; 55.3% female). Out-of-pocket cost was the most influential attribute (relative importance 50.8%), followed by healthcare provider type (17.2%) and consultation frequency (10.0%). Patients preferred the combination of an attending nephrologist and a clinical nurse specialist (coefficient = 0.716; 95% CI, 0.510–0.921) and a higher consultation frequency (coefficient for five consultations per month = 0.414; 95% CI, 0.208–0.620). Willingness to pay for the combined provider team was 52.99 yuan. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested possible differences in preferences by sex, age, disease duration, and comorbidity type, but most formal between-group comparisons were not statistically significant and were unadjusted for multiple testing. Conclusion Out-of-pocket cost is the primary determinant of digital health service selection among patients with chronic kidney disease. The type of healthcare provider is critical for service appeal. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested possible preference differences across patient groups, indicating that stratified or preference-sensitive service designs may merit further investigation. Future research should examine whether aligning digital health services with patient preferences is associated with improved engagement or outcomes in real-world settings.

title: ISLAMIC BANKING, SUKUK AND FINANCIAL-CENTRE STRATEGY IN UZBEKISTAN (2022–2033)
summary: On 29 June 2026 Uzbekistan began permitting full-scale Islamic banking by statute, a step few countries of the former Soviet space have taken. This article examines how the country moved from isolated microfinance experiments to Law No. ZRU
content: On 29 June 2026 Uzbekistan began permitting full-scale Islamic banking by statute, a step few countries of the former Soviet space have taken. This article examines how the country moved from isolated microfinance experiments to Law No. ZRU-1126 of 27 March 2026, and what that change means for banks, capital markets and the planned Tashkent International Financial Centre (TIFC). Using official statements, Central Bank of Uzbekistan statistics, World Bank/IMF assessments and the reports of the Eurasian Development Bank, the Islamic Development Bank Institute and LSEG, the study assembles a dated chronology, quantifies the conventional banking base on which Islamic finance will be built, and compares forecasts of Islamic assets and sukuk volumes with current actual activity. The central finding is a large gap between regulatory ambition and market reality: Islamic financial services provided by microfinance organisations totalled only UZS 11.2 billion in the first quarter of 2026, whereas the banking sector held UZS 1,016.6 trillion in assets on 1 August 2026. The article concludes that the pace of bank licensing and sukuk issuance, rather than legislation itself, will decide whether the dual system becomes economically significant before 2033

title: Ghana Climate Finance and Macrofiscal Context: OECD Commitments (2000-2024) with World Bank, IMF, Ghana Debt and GCF Records.
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset provides a curated compilation of Ghana’s climate-related development finance and macroeconomic context, designed to support research on financing instruments, creditor composition, concessional lending and sovereign debt. The
content: This dataset provides a curated compilation of Ghana’s climate-related development finance and macroeconomic context, designed to support research on financing instruments, creditor composition, concessional lending and sovereign debt. The climate-finance component contains 2,719 OECD recipient-perspective commitment records covering 2000–2024. A cleaned version excludes one flagged exact duplicate, leaving 2,718 records across the full period and 2,587 records within the principal analytical window of 2010–2024. Records retain provider names, financial instruments, flow classifications, climate objectives, activity descriptions, amounts and source references. The compilation also includes 19 World Development Indicators series, with coverage extending back to 1983 where available; IMF financing-arrangement history from a snapshot dated 31 August 2024; Ghana Ministry of Finance public-debt observations preserved by report vintage; selected Green Climate Fund project approvals, instruments and disbursement events; and a documentary register, pilot evidence notes and qualitative coding protocol. Selected project and documentary material extends beyond 2024 and is identified as contextual evidence. It includes the original research workbook, CSV snapshots of all 18 worksheets, eight derived data tables, a data dictionary, methodological documentation, source-specific rights statements and file checksums. A Python reproduction script regenerates the cleaned records, annual and subperiod summaries, provider-coverage tables, concentration measures and robustness comparisons without external dependencies. All eight derived CSV files reproduce byte for byte. Climate-finance amounts represent reported commitments rather than national receipts, expenditure or sovereign liabilities. Provider coverage and climate-attribution methods vary across years. Missing values are preserved, overlapping public-debt vintages remain separate, and regional project totals are not assigned wholly to Ghana. Documentary pilot findings are preliminary secondary interpretations rather than a completed qualitative analysis.

title: The Law Wants to be Formal
summary: This Article examines the relationship between legal formalism and the institutional significance of different areas of law, arguing that formalism tends to migrate toward the legal domains most central to a system’s self-conception and leg
content: This Article examines the relationship between legal formalism and the institutional significance of different areas of law, arguing that formalism tends to migrate toward the legal domains most central to a system’s self-conception and legitimacy. Through a comparative analysis of English and American law, the Article contends that the two systems, once grounded in a shared tradition of formalist private law, diverged significantly following the influence of legal realism and the rise of the administrative state. In the United States, realism weakened confidence in private law as an autonomous and conceptually coherent body of doctrine, leading courts and scholars to recast contract, tort, equity, and unjust enrichment in more functional and policy-oriented terms. As private law became less central to the legal system, formalist reasoning migrated to areas such as statutory interpretation, constitutional structure, jurisdiction, standing, and procedural doctrine. In England and other Commonwealth jurisdictions, by contrast, realism exerted less influence, allowing private law to remain comparatively formalized and doctrinally central. The Article traces these developments through comparative studies of contract formation, unjust enrichment, constructive trusts, tort duty, statutory interpretation, procedural standing, and governmental liability. It argues that formalism persists because legal systems require a credible distinction between constrained judicial decisionmaking and unconstrained political policymaking. When one area of law is perceived as too open-ended or policy driven to sustain that distinction, formalist analysis relocates to other legal fields capable of performing that legitimating function. The Article concludes that legal realism did not eliminate formalism from American law but instead shifted its center of gravity from private law to the doctrines governing legislative interpretation, judicial power, and procedural administration, while English law largely retained private law as the principal site of formal legal reasoning.[This abstract was written by Microsoft Copilot, a generative artificial intelligence.]

title: Populism and sustainable marketing practices: Insights from consumer-packaged goods manufacturers’ new product launches
source: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
summary: Abstract While sustainable marketing practices have traditionally been grounded in stakeholder capitalism, the rise of anti-climate-action populism presents new challenges to firms’ sustainable strategies. Drawing on resource dependence the
content: Abstract While sustainable marketing practices have traditionally been grounded in stakeholder capitalism, the rise of anti-climate-action populism presents new challenges to firms’ sustainable strategies. Drawing on resource dependence theory, this study argues that anti-climate-action populism prompts firms to reduce sustainable marketing practices, specifically the use of environmentally friendly packaging in new product launches. However, we propose that subnational formal and informal institutions, such as economic freedom and cultural tightness, attenuate this effect. To test these hypotheses, we employ a quasi-natural experimental design, using the announcement of the United States’ exit from the Paris Agreement to analyze its impact on sustainable marketing practices, based on a global sample of product launches by consumer-packaged goods manufacturers. Our difference-in-differences analysis supports these hypotheses. This study advances the understanding of the dynamic relationship between populism and subnational institutions, highlighting how different institutional pillars shape firms’ sustainable marketing strategies.

title: Selling Spirituality
summary: Selling Spirituality offers a critical analysis of the rise of spirituality as a powerful commodity in the global marketplace. It shows how spirituality is big business, examining how spiritual discourses, practices, and institutions have b
content: Selling Spirituality offers a critical analysis of the rise of spirituality as a powerful commodity in the global marketplace. It shows how spirituality is big business, examining how spiritual discourses, practices, and institutions have been reshaped by neoliberal forces. This expanded second edition provides significant updates to the book in light of developments from the previous decades, particularly the consolidation of neoliberalism through digital technologies, emerging AI and platform capitalism. Building on the original analysis of the privatisation of religion and the privatisation of welfare, the authors introduce a third privatisation: the outsourcing of attention, affect and mental resilience to spiritualised techniques of self-regulation amid conditions of precarity, algorithmic governance and informational overload. Four new chapters examine neoliberalism as a quasi-religious orthodoxy; the commodification of Christian prayer and interiority; mindfulness as a technology of attention within the attention economy; and the dangers of individualised green spirituality in responding to climate crisis. Substantially revised chapters address psychology, Asian philosophies, and spiritual consumer industries. Across these contexts, the book argues that contemporary spirituality increasingly manages distress and anxiety while obscuring the structural sources of social and mental suffering. This insightful book will be of great interest to students and scholars in religious studies, philosophy, cultural studies, sociology, political theory, and environmental humanities. It will also be of interest to readers concerned with neoliberalism, mental health, digital capitalism, mindfulness, and the contemporary politics of well-being.

title: Association of maternal educational attainment with preterm birth and low birth weight: A systematic review and meta-analysis
summary: BACKGROUNDMaternal educational attainment is an important socioeconomic indicator associated with health literacy, healthcare access, and health-related behaviors.However, its association with preterm birth and low birth weight (LBW) varies
content: BACKGROUNDMaternal educational attainment is an important socioeconomic indicator associated with health literacy, healthcare access, and health-related behaviors.However, its association with preterm birth and low birth weight (LBW) varies across populations, educational classifications, and study settings. AIMTo determine the associations of maternal educational attainment with preterm birth and LBW. METHODSPubMed, Web of Science, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 6, 2026, for observational studies examining maternal education in relation to preterm birth or LBW.Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.Random-effects models pooled odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI).Heterogeneity, subgroup analyses, leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, and potential small-study effects were evaluated.The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024576198). RESULTSThirty-seven studies involving 30432601 births were included; 24 contributed to preterm birth analyses and 17 to LBW analyses, with four reporting both outcomes.For ≥ 12 years vs < 12 years of maternal education, higher attainment was associated with lower odds of preterm birth (OR = 0.82, 95%CI: 0.75-0.89)and LBW (OR = 0.83, 95%CI: 0.71-0.98).Heterogeneity was considerable for preterm birth (I² = 99.3%) and LBW (I² = 5 / 55 97.9%).Subgroup estimates varied by region, economic setting, and study design.Leave-one-out analyses did not materially alter the overall direction of associations. CONCLUSIONHigher maternal educational attainment was associated with lower odds of preterm birth and LBW, although substantial heterogeneity limits causal interpretation and generalizability.

title: Making Shrimp in Moral Economies: Time, Ethics, and Labor in a Global Supply Chain
summary: ABSTRACT This article is part of the special issue 'Morality at Work: Ethnographies of Labor and Ethics' edited by Michael Vine and Sarah Winkler‐Reid. This article explores how future‐oriented temporalities shape people's labor experiences
content: ABSTRACT This article is part of the special issue 'Morality at Work: Ethnographies of Labor and Ethics' edited by Michael Vine and Sarah Winkler‐Reid. This article explores how future‐oriented temporalities shape people's labor experiences and ethical subjectivities within the global supply chain of brown shrimp. Drawing on ethnographic research with Dutch fishers, Moroccan shrimp peelers, and European processing managers, it traces how embedded notions of risk, luck, and destiny mediate workers' engagement with the uncertainty of the future. Processing company managers in Europe employ risk management practices to assert control over volatile markets, while North Sea fishers rely on notions of luck to navigate the unpredictability of fishing. In Moroccan peeling factories, workers often invoke destiny when making sense of their precarious working conditions. This article argues that attention to these divergent orientations toward the future offers critical insight into the moral economies that drive different forms of work under global capitalism.

title: Exploring Poverty Penalties in Water and Housing Services and Their Influence on the Economic Decision-Making of Slum Households in Dhaka
summary: The disparate prices of access to key services are becoming increasingly relevant factors in urban poverty in the Global South, whereas little effort has been made to understand the combined effects of various service deprivations on househ
content: The disparate prices of access to key services are becoming increasingly relevant factors in urban poverty in the Global South, whereas little effort has been made to understand the combined effects of various service deprivations on household economic decisions. The paper explores the interactions between water and housing poverty penalties on the livelihoods and economic decision-making of slum dwellers in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The study combined an exploratory sequential mixed methods design, which uses 30 in-depth household interviews with a survey of 100 slum households in four settlements in Dhaka North and Dhaka South City Corporations. The results show that the poor households face a compounded poverty penalty, with insecure housing and lack of water resources imposing disproportionately heavy financial burden and implementing decreased possibilities of investment in savings, education, health, and livelihood. Households currently spend 32.7 % of monthly income on rent and water, which is above known affordability levels, and 75 % of households report having no saving ability. Correlation analysis also shows that households with low income have greater relative burdens and housing and water penalties reinforce one another. This research builds on the poverty penalty theory in the context of extending it to the issue of urban inequality, informal system of service provision and sustainable livelihoods in growing urban cities across the world. The findings suggest that water and housing poverty penalties interact to constrain household livelihood choices and reduce opportunities for saving, education, health expenditure, and productive investment.

title: Vendor Selection Risk and Organizational Performance in Corporate Institutions in Taraba State: The Impact of Incompetent External Service Providers
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: This study examined vendor selection risk and organisational performance in corporate institutions in Taraba State, focusing on incompetent external service providers. Specifically, it assessed vendor competence, due diligence, selection tr
content: This study examined vendor selection risk and organisational performance in corporate institutions in Taraba State, focusing on incompetent external service providers. Specifically, it assessed vendor competence, due diligence, selection transparency, favoritism, and vendor performance monitoring. The study was anchored on Transaction Cost Economics, Stakeholder Theory, and Agency Theory. A survey research design was adopted, using primary data from selected corporate institutions. Logit regression was employed for analysis. Findings revealed that all five vendor selection risk factors had statistically insignificant effects on organisational performance, despite positive and negative relationships. The study concluded that vendor selection risk factors did not significantly influence organisational performance. It recommended strengthening vendor assessment, due diligence, transparency, fairness, and continuous performance monitoring.
