summary: Pedicle screw loosening remains a challenge for surgeons and patients. We propose using hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers to enhance the bone fixation of pedicle screws. Polylactide (PLA) anchors with various
content: Pedicle screw loosening remains a challenge for surgeons and patients. We propose using hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers to enhance the bone fixation of pedicle screws. Polylactide (PLA) anchors with various designs were fabricated using additive manufacturing, while simvastatin- and bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanofibers were prepared through coaxial electrospinning. The effects of PLA anchors and drug/biomolecule-loaded PLGA nanofibrous membranes on improving the pullout strength of pedicle screws from artificial bones were investigated. The in vitro release characteristics of simvastatin and BMP-2 from the nanofibers were evaluated using high-performance liquid chromatography and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, while the in vivo elution of simvastatin was assessed in a rabbit model with histological examinations. The results demonstrate that electrospun drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers, when wrapped around pedicle screws, enhance the screws’ pullout strength. Additionally, the nanofiber/screw system provides a sustained release of simvastatin and BMP-2 for over 30 days in vitro and 4 weeks in vivo. Histological analysis also confirmed the biocompatibility of nanofibrous anchors. Hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers show potential for improving screw fixation and serving as a platform for extended drug delivery.

title: Ocean-sourced CO2 Boosts Radiolytic Oxidants at Europa’s Chaos
summary: Abstract James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations of Europa’s leading hemisphere reveal enhanced CO 2 abundances over equatorial chaos terrains where the subsurface ocean is thought to have breached the ice shell. Hydrogen peroxide, s
content: Abstract James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations of Europa’s leading hemisphere reveal enhanced CO 2 abundances over equatorial chaos terrains where the subsurface ocean is thought to have breached the ice shell. Hydrogen peroxide, synthesized radiolytically by Jovian magnetospheric charged particles impinging on Europa’s ice, is also elevated in these geologically active regions, spatially coinciding with CO 2 . This correlation implicates CO 2 in H 2 O 2 synthesis, consistent with laboratory experiments showing increased radiolytic peroxide yields in carbon-bearing ices. Our radiolysis model – which incorporates charged-particle precipitation through electromagnetic fields accounting for Europa’s interaction with Jupiter’s magnetosphere – predicts enhanced H 2 O 2 on the leading hemisphere equatorial regions. The relative dearth of energetic electrons in this region shields peroxide from destruction, leaving a notably higher abundance towards the leading apex compared to the mid-latitude regions or the trailing side. Integrating the inferred CO 2 abundance and the associated boost in peroxide yield, we show that ocean-derived CO 2 acts as a multiplier, further elevating H 2 O 2 concentrations within the fractured surfaces of Tara and Powys Regiones. Together, these results imply that geologic resurfacing at Europa’s chaos terrains and precipitating radiation conspire to contribute to the excess peroxide observed by JWST, with endogenic CO 2 amplifying oxidant production in these potentially ocean-linked regions.

title: A review of phase-change display: materials, architectures, driving, and applications
summary: The rapid advancement of next-generation display technologies has driven an increasing demand for devices that simultaneously offer ultrahigh resolution, high refresh rates, and ultralow power consumption. Phase-change materials (PCMs) unde
content: The rapid advancement of next-generation display technologies has driven an increasing demand for devices that simultaneously offer ultrahigh resolution, high refresh rates, and ultralow power consumption. Phase-change materials (PCMs) undergo reversible structural transitions between amorphous and crystalline states, accompanied by pronounced changes in optical constants. This process is inherently nonvolatile and requires no sustaining bias, resulting in near-zero static power consumption. These properties have established PCMs as a highly competitive platform for next-generation display technologies. However, several critical challenges remain, including limited color gamut coverage, insufficient cycling endurance, and difficulties in pixel-level addressing, all of which continue to hinder the practical deployment of PCM-based displays. This review provides a systematic overview of phase-change display technologies, organized along four interconnected dimensions: materials, device architectures, driving schemes, and applications. The microscopic mechanisms and optimization strategies governing switching speed, energy consumption, and cycling stability are first summarized. The optical modulation principles of thin-film interference structures, subwavelength metasurfaces, and multimodal hybrid devices are then reviewed. The multilevel grayscale control strategies of electrothermal and laser-based driving schemes are subsequently compared. Representative applications, including reflective, transmissive, and holographic displays, are also surveyed. This review aims to establish a coherent framework spanning from material fundamentals to device architectures and application development, providing a structured reference for advancing PCM-based displays toward high-performance and practical implementation.

title: All-optical 2D perovskite photodetector arrays for pixelated long-wave infrared imaging
summary: Abstract Infrared detection and imaging are important for applications including thermal monitoring, night vision, environmental sensing, and molecular identification. All-optical mid-wave infrared (MWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) detec
content: Abstract Infrared detection and imaging are important for applications including thermal monitoring, night vision, environmental sensing, and molecular identification. All-optical mid-wave infrared (MWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) detection offers a compelling alternative to conventional infrared detectors by enabling non-contact photothermal sensing without needing electronic readout circuitry. Here, we demonstrate pixelated LWIR imaging using solution-processed two-dimensional metal-halide perovskites (2D-MHPs), whose strong electron-phonon interaction produces a large temperature coefficient of reflectance in the visible wavelength range. By integrating (PEA) 2 PbI 4 films with LWIR-absorbing SiNₓ membranes, we realize centimeter-scale imagers capable of detecting 9.5-µm LWIR light with sensitivity down to ~20 pW·µm⁻². To mitigate lateral thermal diffusion that limits spatial fidelity, we introduce a structured-probe illumination scheme, and we further develop a fully pixelated imager with thermally isolated membrane-disc arrays. This design effectively eliminates pixel-to-pixel crosstalk and enables high-resolution optical readout using a silicon-based CMOS camera. These advances establish 2D-MHP-based all-optical thermal imaging as a scalable, low-cost platform for LWIR sensing, with strong potential for extension to far-infrared and terahertz detection.

title: Hylocereus undatus peel extract and ZnO nanoparticles suppress cancer through apoptosis and Wnt/β-catenin inhibition
summary: Abstract Cancer treatment faces the challenge of multidrug resistance and systemic cytotoxicity. This study explores the anticancer potential of Hylocereus undatus peel extracts and their biogenically synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (Z
content: Abstract Cancer treatment faces the challenge of multidrug resistance and systemic cytotoxicity. This study explores the anticancer potential of Hylocereus undatus peel extracts and their biogenically synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). Total phenolics, flavonoids and GC–MS profiles of the extracts were determined. Then, ZnO NPs were synthesized by using aqueous and n-hexane extracts and characterized by FTIR, Zeta Potential, XRD, SEM, EDX, and TEM. Among all tested formulations, ZnO NPs-AE (derived from the aqueous extract) showed the strongest antitumor activity, both in cell culture (Caco‑2 and HepG2) and in the Ehrlich ascites carcinoma mouse model. In MTT assays, ZnO NPs-AE was highly cytotoxic to Caco‑2 and HepG2 cells (IC₅₀ = 9.22 and 12.93 µg/mL, respectively) and performed on the same level as doxorubicin ( p < 0.05). It also showed a more favourable selectivity profile, being less toxic to normal colon fibroblasts (CCD‑18Co; IC₅₀ = 32.35 µg/mL) than to Caco‑2 cells (IC₅₀ = 9.22 µg/mL), which was better than doxorubicin. Consistent with this, ZnO NPs-AE reduced the proportion of cells in G2/M phase (7.39% compared with 12.65% in untreated cells) and increased total apoptosis to 25.98% in Caco‑2 cells. Molecularly, it up-regulated caspase-3 (6.15-fold), down-regulated topoisomerase II (0.33-fold) and suppressed the Wnt/β catenin axis. Consistently, ELISA quantification of Axin2 and Cyclin D1 in Caco‑2 cells confirmed down‑regulation of these Wnt/β‑catenin targets in parallel with the decrease in β‑catenin protein. In vivo, ZnO NPs-AE (5 mg/kg) reduced EAC volume to 89.36%, normalized hepatic/renal biomarkers, improved lipid profiles, and alleviated oxidative stress by elevating GSH, CAT, and SOD levels, while reducing MDA, alongside histopathological improvements. Overall, ZnO NPs-AE represents a promising, well tolerated biogenic nanoplatform for targeted cancer therapy.

title: Overshoot and the Cryosphere: Averting Global Meltdown
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The Implications of Temperature Overshoot, Peak and Decline for the Cryosphere Exceeding the 1.5°C Paris Agreement target will bring large and in many cases irreversible impacts from the Earth’s melting ice sheets, permafrost, glaciers, sea
content: The Implications of Temperature Overshoot, Peak and Decline for the Cryosphere Exceeding the 1.5°C Paris Agreement target will bring large and in many cases irreversible impacts from the Earth’s melting ice sheets, permafrost, glaciers, sea ice and polar oceans. These losses can still be limited if overshoot is kept to a minimum by deep emissions reductions followed by scaled-up carbon drawdown. Overshoot and the Cryosphere: Averting Global Meltdown sets out the global impacts of ice loss with overshoot, exploring which ones are locked in – and how more urgent climate action can still stop or slow the worst of this damage, delivering vital evidence ahead of COP31 in Türkiye. The report lays out out actionable solutions to bring temperatures back down from overshoot. Renewable energy and battery technologies are booming, reliance on coal and oil is slowing, and climate policies have cut emissions in many places. Successful policies now need to be scaled up to reduce emissions by at least 5% per year, starting now, reaching net zero greenhouse gas emissions by mid-century. The report emphasizes that there can be no delay in phasing out fossil fuels to retain the possibility of bringing temperatures down in the future by drawing down carbon. Doing so will have tangible benefits for future generations including: • Slowing down the rate of sea-level rise to an ‘adaptable’ level. Even though several meters of sea level rise are already locked in for many centuries due to the long-term retreat of polar ice sheets, how fast it will happen matters greatly to coastal communities on the frontline of climate change today. • Potentially halting and partially reversing glacier, snowpack and sea ice loss. A return to 1.5°C and below would initiate some sea ice and glacier re-growth within decades to centuries, and potentially re-establish healthy snowpack levels. • Limiting the damage from impacts such as the destabilization of permafrost, which can lead to tragic events such as that seen in Nepal and also emits carbon as it thaws. This climate feedback loop would leave even more CO2 to be removed from the atmosphere later. Produced by the International Cryosphere Climate Initiative (ICCI) in coordination with the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), Overshoot and the Cryosphere: Averting Global Meltdown brings together an international team of over 80 polar and mountain scientists and serves a thematic companion report to UNEP’s Limiting Overshoot Spotlight Report, the first of its kind from a UN agency. Overshoot and the Cryosphere was jointly released with the latest installment of the similarly peer-reviewed State of the Cryosphere 2026: The Cost of Overshoot on November 2, 2026.

title: TH-positive pulmonary nerve fiber-epithelial interaction promotes adipose thermogenesis in male mice
summary: Cold exposure activates sympathetic neurons in adipose tissue to maintain thermal homeostasis. However, whether sympathetic activation in non-adipose tissues contributes to cross-organ regulation of adipose thermogenesis remains unclear. He
content: Cold exposure activates sympathetic neurons in adipose tissue to maintain thermal homeostasis. However, whether sympathetic activation in non-adipose tissues contributes to cross-organ regulation of adipose thermogenesis remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate the activation of TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers (TPNFs) by cold exposure, which further promotes adipose thermogenesis. Specifically, cold exposure activates TPNFs that innervate bronchial Club cells in the lung and leads to a reduction in Secretoglobin family 3A member 1 (SCGB3A1) expression via Adrenergic Receptor β2 (ADRB2). SCGB3A1, a Club cell-specific secretory factor, binds the choline transporter SLC44A2 on adipocytes to restrict choline uptake and impair thermogenic activation. Meanwhile, TPNFs activation induces NGF secretion from Club cells, which in turn strengthens TPNFs innervation of Club cells in a feedforward loop. Importantly, the stimulation of this mechanism via tracheal infusion of the ADRB2 agonist norepinephrine (NE) enhances thermogenesis in mice. Jiang et al. reveal a lung–adipose communication pathway in which cold-activated TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers regulate Club cell SCGB3A1 secretion to control adipocyte choline uptake and thermogenesis.

title: Alkyl Imidazolium Cation-Supported Poly(terphenyl- co -fluorene isatin) Anion Exchange Membrane for Anion Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
summary: Abstract Anion exchange membrane (AEM) is the core component of alkaline fuel cells. Current research still faces bottlenecks such as the difficulty in synergizing ion conductivity and alkali stability, and the inhibition of reaction kineti
content: Abstract Anion exchange membrane (AEM) is the core component of alkaline fuel cells. Current research still faces bottlenecks such as the difficulty in synergizing ion conductivity and alkali stability, and the inhibition of reaction kinetics by adsorption of ionomer catalysts. In this work, a new ether-free poly(terphenyl-co-fluorene isatin) polymer backbone was developed. Alkyl imidazole with a unique π-conjugated delocalized structure was selected as a cation to develop a series of imidazole cation-loaded comb-shaped poly(terphenyl-co-fluorene isatin) polyelectrolytes (PTFI-IZ-n). The additional hydrophobic structure on the imidazole cation provides a driving force for the self-assembly of ion clusters. PTFI-IZ-8 AEM exhibits the most developed phase separation morphology and exhibits a high OH– conductivity of 140.61 mS/cm at 80 °C. The long comb-like alkyl chain in PTFI-IZ-8 AEM effectively protects the stability of the cation. After 1200 h in 2 M NaOH at 80 °C, the ion conductivity only decreased by 10.32% and the tensile strength decreased by 11.05%. The peak power density of H2–O2 AEMFC based on PTFI-IZ-8 can reach 1.03 W/cm2 at 80 °C, providing a new strategy for the design of high-performance anion exchange membranes.

title: A data-driven predictive system for shellfish biotoxin risk assessment
source: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
summary: Diarrhetic shellfish poisoning (DSP) toxins pose a major threat to the aquaculture industry and public health. Traditional monitoring methods suffer from delays and high costs, and intelligent early warning systems are urgently needed. The
content: Diarrhetic shellfish poisoning (DSP) toxins pose a major threat to the aquaculture industry and public health. Traditional monitoring methods suffer from delays and high costs, and intelligent early warning systems are urgently needed. The study utilised machine learning to predict shellfish biotoxin levels in shellfish by integrating multiple data sources, including phytoplankton monitoring, climatic variables, and historical toxin records. Data from seven shellfish production areas in Northern Ireland from 2011 to 2021, covering DSP-OA + dinophysistoxins and AZAs toxin concentrations, seven phytoplankton taxa or taxonomic groups, and three climatic variables was used to inform the model. Using the Lale Machine learning framework, the study constructed 42 initial modelling scenarios across regions, shellfish species, and toxin combinations. SHAP analyses quantified feature contributions and identified the main predictors across the retained scenarios. After data filtering and performance screening, model performance varied across the region-species combinations. The final regression models showed limited predictive performance, while the classification models showed stronger performance for the two evaluated region-species combinations, Belfast mussels and Dundrum mussels, with F1 scores of 0.766 and 0.950. The results of the study show predictive potential for toxin occurrence at the next sampling occasion, although further validation is required before operational early-warning application.

title: Properties and microstructure of Ca-rich slag-based mortar prepared with a one-part sodium carbonate–silica fume solid activating blend
summary: Sodium carbonate (Na 2 CO 3 , SC)-activated slag systems typically exhibit slow setting, delayed hardening, and limited early-age strength, whereas the activation of cement-containing Ca-rich precursors can induce rapid setting without a co
content: Sodium carbonate (Na 2 CO 3 , SC)-activated slag systems typically exhibit slow setting, delayed hardening, and limited early-age strength, whereas the activation of cement-containing Ca-rich precursors can induce rapid setting without a corresponding increase in early-age strength. In this study, a one-part SC–SF solid activating blend was employed, in which silica fume (SF) partially replaced SC. The influence of the solid activating blend-to-precursor mass ratio (A/P) and the sodium carbonate-to-silica fume mass ratio (N/S) on flowability, setting behavior, and mechanical properties of cement-containing Ca-rich slag-based mortars was systematically investigated. Microstructural characterization was conducted to examine the associated phase assemblage and microstructural features. The results indicated that, in the pure SC-activated system, flowability initially increased slightly and then decreased as A/P increased, whereas setting time progressively shortened. In contrast, partial replacement of SC with SF at suitable proportions markedly enhanced flowability, prolonged setting time, and promoted early-age strength development. At an A/P of 0.3, the SC–SF mortar with an N/S of 1.0 exhibited approximately 36.7% higher flowability, an extended setting time from 29 to 133 min, and a 151.9% increase in 3-day compressive strength relative to the pure SC mixture. The 28-day and 56-day compressive strengths were further improved by 24.6% and 29.1%, respectively. Microstructural analyses at A/P = 0.3 and 28 d showed that, compared with the pure SC mixture, specimens with partial replacement of SC by SF exhibited weaker carbonate-related diffraction features and a more continuous and compact gel-like matrix in the observed regions. Overall, appropriate adjustment of the sodium carbonate and silica fume dosages can improve the flowability, setting behavior, and mechanical properties of the mortar, providing a useful reference for the mixture design and further investigation of one-part sodium carbonate-activated systems.

title: Antioxidant metabolites from the endophytic fungus Aspergillus spelaeus
summary: Five undescribed compounds, including two drimane-type sesquiterpenoids, asperdrimanes A and B ( 1 and 2 ), and three amide compounds, asperspamides A–C ( 3 – 5 ), together with four known metabolites 6 – 9 , were isolated from the fungus A
content: Five undescribed compounds, including two drimane-type sesquiterpenoids, asperdrimanes A and B ( 1 and 2 ), and three amide compounds, asperspamides A–C ( 3 – 5 ), together with four known metabolites 6 – 9 , were isolated from the fungus Aspergillus spelaeus GDGJ-286. By extensively analyzing NMR, LC–MS/MS, Marfey's method, and X-ray crystallography, the structures were characterized successfully. Asperdrimanes A and B ( 1 and 2 ) are drimane-type sesquiterpenoids characterized by a spiro- β -lactone moiety. Asperspamide B ( 4 ) exhibited exceptional antioxidant capacity in ABTS, FRAP, and DPPH tests, along with significant neuroprotective effects in a hydrogen peroxide-induced PC12 cell oxidative injury model, demonstrating strong anti-apoptotic and anti-necrotic properties. These findings highlight asperspamide B’s potential as a lead compound for developing antioxidant agents.

title: Mitochondrial Pathophysiology of Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: From Quality Control Failure to Emerging Therapies
summary: Chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is increasingly understood as a disorder of cardiac energy conversion in which mitochondria fail both as the principal source of ATP and as regulators of calcium handling, redox b
content: Chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is increasingly understood as a disorder of cardiac energy conversion in which mitochondria fail both as the principal source of ATP and as regulators of calcium handling, redox balance, cell survival and sterile inflammation.This narrative review synthesizes evidence published between 2021 and 2026 on mitochondrial pathophysiology in HFrEF, with emphasis on human myocardium and cardiovascular aging.Human studies converge on a reproducible energetic signature: a 20% reduction in the phosphocreatine to ATP ratio, depletion of the adenine nucleotide pool, a collapse of creatine kinase flux, reduced fatty acid import and oxidation, glycolysis uncoupled from glucose oxidation, increased ketone and lactate consumption, defective branched-chain amino acid catabolism, hyperacetylation of mitochondrial enzymes and myocardial iron deficiency.These lesions are coupled to failure of mitochondrial quality control (fragmentation, cristae

title: Lead-free soft hybrid materials for piezoelectric sensors: A paradigm shift from toxic lead-based ceramics to sustainable electronics
summary: The development of piezoelectric materials has significantly transformed modern electronic and sensing technologies, and their use has extended from extremely precise actuators to wearable self-powering devices. But the problem is that thes
content: The development of piezoelectric materials has significantly transformed modern electronic and sensing technologies, and their use has extended from extremely precise actuators to wearable self-powering devices. But the problem is that these materials are commonly made out of lead-based ceramics, and for example, lead zirconate titanate (PZT) contains 60% of lead. Such materials entail great risks to the environment and people's health. This extensive paper elaborates on the evolution of lead-free soft hybrid piezoelectric materials with special emphasis on bismuth iodide-based organic-inorganic hybrids that can be a safe choice of the electronic sensor market of tomorrow. The latest breakthrough research demonstrates that owing to a well-planned halogen bonding between the organic and the inorganic components of the material, there occurs a slight structural instability which in turn opens the way to the improved piezoelectric performance thus making the piezoelectric coefficients comparable to those of commercial PZT with zero toxic lead content (d 3 3 =161.5 pm/V). This review connects developments in sensing mechanisms, material chemistry, crystal engineering, wearable electronics, energy harvesting, and medical implants.

title: Thermochemical upgrading of cereal brans into pyrolytic chars for solid fuel applications
summary: Abstract The growing production of cereals in Europe generates large quantities of milling by-products, including cereal brans, whose valorisation is important in the context of circular bioeconomy and renewable energy production. Although
content: Abstract The growing production of cereals in Europe generates large quantities of milling by-products, including cereal brans, whose valorisation is important in the context of circular bioeconomy and renewable energy production. Although brans are commonly used in food and feed chains, low-grade or surplus fractions may require alternative management pathways. This study evaluated the potential of selected cereal brans, namely spelt, oat, wheat, rye, barley, durum wheat, triticale and millet brans, as feed-stocks for the production of pyrolytic char intended for energy recovery. The brans were pyrolysed at 500 °C, and the resulting chars were assessed in terms of solid yield, ash content, higher heating value and energy-related indicators. The char yield ranged from 30.27 to 37.04%, depending on the feedstock. Pyrolysis increased the higher heating value from 16.58 to 22.80 MJ/kg in raw brans to 24.45–30.15 MJ/kg in the corresponding chars, confirming the effectiveness of carbonisation in improving the energy density of the solid product. However, ash content also increased markedly, from 3.69 to 7.36% in raw brans to 11.41–23.31% in the chars, indicating that mineral concentration is a key constraint for combustion-oriented applications. The integrated evaluation of heating value and ash load showed that oat, rye and durum wheat chars offered the most favourable balance between high energy content and relatively low ash burden. To conclude, cereal brans can be considered promising feedstocks for thermochemical upgrading into charcoal-like solid fuels, particularly when they are unsuitable for food or feed uses.

title: Observation of light-induced Haldane gap in graphene
summary: Abstract Symmetry and topology, encoded in electronic wavefunctions, play a central role in the electronic properties and emergent phenomena of quantum materials. While these properties are conventionally determined by the equilibrium Hamil
content: Abstract Symmetry and topology, encoded in electronic wavefunctions, play a central role in the electronic properties and emergent phenomena of quantum materials. While these properties are conventionally determined by the equilibrium Hamiltonian, strong optical fields offer a fundamentally different route by reshaping the Hamiltonian on ultrafast timescales, turning symmetry and topology into dynamically controllable degrees of freedom. Graphene provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing this concept, where circularly polarized light has long been predicted to dynamically break time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and open a topologically nontrivial gap at the Dirac point. Despite extensive experimental efforts, direct observation of this Dirac gap—the defining spectroscopic signature of the dynamical TRS-breaking induced topological phase—has remained missing. Here we directly observe this light-induced Dirac gap in monolayer graphene. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the gap emerges simultaneously with the optical field and exclusively under circularly polarized driving, directly linking its opening to dynamical TRS breaking. Together with Floquet theory, we identify the gap with a light-induced Haldane mass and reveal the associated nontrivial Floquet Berry curvature and Chern topology. By demonstrating dynamical TRS breaking in a prototypical non-magnetic material, our results establish optical driving as a route to ultrafast engineering of symmetry and topology, opening opportunities for dynamically tunable quantum matter beyond equilibrium.

title: Short-term interaction of Fe(II)–GMZ bentonite under hydro-thermo-mechanical conditions
summary: The interface reaction between the bentonite buffer barrier and the metal disposal canister is one of the key factors affecting the long-term safety of high-level radioactive waste geological disposal repository. To investigate the short-te
content: The interface reaction between the bentonite buffer barrier and the metal disposal canister is one of the key factors affecting the long-term safety of high-level radioactive waste geological disposal repository. To investigate the short-term interactions between Fe(II) corrosion products and Gaomiaozi(GMZ) bentonite under low-to-moderate temperature and confining pressure, GMZ bentonite is selected as the test material. An independently developed THCM reaction platform is used to conduct Fe(II)-bentonite contact reaction experiments under different Fe(II) concentrations, temperatures, confining pressures and solution conditions. The ion composition of the suspension after the reaction and the changes in the solid-phase mineral structure are analyzed by atomic absorption spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. The results showed that contact with Fe(II) caused a rapid redistribution of aqueous cations, including an increase in the Na⁺ concentration, which is consistent with cation exchange involving the montmorillonite. Increasing the reaction time and temperature affected the aqueous ion composition and the local hydration and bonding environments of the solid phase. However, the XRD and FTIR results don’t provide conclusive evidence for structural Fe incorporation or montmorillonite-to-illite transformation. These findings provide laboratory-scale information on the short-term interaction between Fe(II)-bearing solutions and GMZ bentonite powder, while further validation using highly compacted bentonite is required before extrapolation to repository buffer conditions.

title: Corneal epithelial signals remodel bacterial physiology and extracellular vesicle cargo in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus epidermidis
summary: Host–microbe communication at the ocular surface is bidirectional, yet the reciprocal effects of corneal epithelial signals on bacterial physiology remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how corneal epithelial-derived exosomes and
content: Host–microbe communication at the ocular surface is bidirectional, yet the reciprocal effects of corneal epithelial signals on bacterial physiology remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how corneal epithelial-derived exosomes and bacteria–epithelium co-culture influence Pseudomonas aeruginosa , a major opportunistic ocular pathogen, and Staphylococcus epidermidis , a common member of the ocular surface microbiota. Bacterial responses were assessed by transcriptomic and functional analyses, while bacterial extracellular vesicles released during epithelial interaction were characterized by proteomics and RNA sequencing. Corneal epithelial-derived exosomes reduced bacterial growth and increased epithelial adhesion in both species, while enhancing biofilm formation in P. aeruginosa . Bacteria–epithelium co-culture induced substantially broader responses than exposure to epithelial-derived exosomes alone. In P. aeruginosa , epithelial interaction reorganized quorum-sensing, motility, iron-acquisition, phenazine and biofilm-associated pathways, resulting in reduced motility and pyocyanin production, increased pyoverdine production and enhanced biofilm formation. In S. epidermidis , epithelial interaction was associated with reduced expression of several virulence factors associated with cytotoxicity and inflammatory responses, upregulation of genes associated with surface interaction and protein export, and decreased biofilm biomass. In both species, epithelial interaction also induced extensive remodeling of bacterial extracellular vesicle protein and RNA cargo, which did not simply mirror the corresponding intracellular bacterial profiles. These findings demonstrate that corneal epithelial signals actively drive species-specific bacterial adaptation and vesicular remodeling. Together with previous evidence of bacteria-to-epithelium signaling, they support a dynamic model of bidirectional interkingdom communication at the ocular surface.

title: Metabolic regulation of oocyte developmental competence: cellular cooperation, developmental transitions, and human evidence
source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
summary: Oocyte metabolism supports meiotic maturation and prepares the cytoplasm for fertilization and early cleavage. These functions depend on the exchange of substrates with cumulus cells, mitochondrial activity and organization, redox balance,
content: Oocyte metabolism supports meiotic maturation and prepares the cytoplasm for fertilization and early cleavage. These functions depend on the exchange of substrates with cumulus cells, mitochondrial activity and organization, redox balance, and the use of metabolites in biosynthesis and chromatin regulation. This narrative review examines how these processes contribute to developmental competence, drawing on mammalian perturbation studies and human oocyte, cumulus-cell, follicular-fluid and embryo studies. Animal experiments show that disturbed substrate use or organelle organization can impair development despite meiotic progression or little change in total adenosine triphosphate (ATP) content. They also reveal dose- and stage-dependent responses to metabolic supplementation. Human studies identify related molecular and optical changes, particularly during reproductive aging, but the biological meaning of a measurement depends on the sampled cell, developmental stage and experimental conditions. Direct oocyte profiling, associated follicular samples and embryo measurements therefore address different questions. The Goldilocks concept helps frame the possibility that both insufficient activity and excessive demand can accompany developmental failure; it does not establish a common metabolic threshold for clinical selection. We discuss metabolic interventions as tests of mechanism and distinguish developmental rescue in experimental systems from benefit in vitro fertilization. The central challenge is to determine which metabolic changes contribute to loss of competence and which arise as responses to aging, culture or developmental arrest.

title: Ultrasmall Superparamagnetic Fe3O4 Nanoparticles Green-Synthesized with Cosmos caudatus : Phytochemical Surface Coordination and Suppression of MCF-7 Migration
summary: Abstract Phytochemical-mediated synthesis of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPION) is dominated by a narrow set of plant substrates, and extending this chemical space to phylogenetically distinct species remains an open questio
content: Abstract Phytochemical-mediated synthesis of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPION) is dominated by a narrow set of plant substrates, and extending this chemical space to phylogenetically distinct species remains an open question. Herein, we report the first application of Cosmos caudatus Kunth leaf extract, rich in quercetin glycosides, catechins, and chlorogenic acid, to the green sonochemical synthesis of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (CC-SPION), benchmarked against an extract-free control (Bare-SPION). Acoustic cavitation combined with phytochemical reduction produced a crystalline inverse-spinel iron oxide in 25 min at near ambient temperature. TEM revealed near-monodisperse, semispherical primary particles of 7.30 ± 0.88 nm smaller than green-synthesized iron oxides in related studies; the TEM primary-particle diameter (7.30 nm) and XRD crystallite size (7.25 nm) were in close agreement, with FE-SEM reporting larger drying-induced aggregates (7.7–17.5 nm). Multipeak XRD analysis showed the crystallite size fell from 11.61 nm (Bare-SPION) to 7.25 nm (CC-SPION). Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) corroborated the elemental compositions, whereas Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) substantiated the existence of Cosmos caudatus chemicals within the nanoparticle composition. This coordinated phytochemical corona raised the zeta-potential magnitude from −20.4 to −42.5 mV, conferring electrosteric stabilization (PDI ≈ 0.08). VSM confirmed superparamagnetism at 298 K (Ms = 43.99 emu/g; with no coercivity and remanence). CC-SPION was noncytotoxic to HEK-293 and MCF-7 cells across 31.25–500 μg Fe/mL (ISO 10993–5; viability ≥70%), reduced MCF-7 wound closure over 24–48 h, and showed dose-dependent cell association/localization. These findings establish C. caudatus sonochemistry as a route to mechanistically well-defined ultrasmall biocompatible SPION for prospective MRI and antimigratory applications.

title: Kinetic Multi-reaction Model of Platinum Nanoparticle Oxidation and Cathodic Dissolution in a Wide Potential Window
summary: Abstract Mathematical modeling provides a powerful framework for understanding and mitigating degradation in catalyst materials such as platinum nanoparticles. A hallmark of platinum degradation during voltage cycling is the appearance of t
content: Abstract Mathematical modeling provides a powerful framework for understanding and mitigating degradation in catalyst materials such as platinum nanoparticles. A hallmark of platinum degradation during voltage cycling is the appearance of two distinct maxima in the dissolved Pt concentration: a smaller peak upon increasing potential and a larger peak upon decreasing potential. To explain this observation, we propose a kinetic multi-reaction model of Pt nanoparticle oxidation and dissolution, which describes dissolution as an interplay between direct electrochemical dissolution, passivation of the Pt surface, and the electrochemical dissolution of Pt oxides. The model is calibrated using cyclic voltammograms and time traces of Pt ion concentrations measured for two Pt catalyst samples with different nanoparticle sizes and different supports (carbon-supported 3 nm and unsupported 30 nm particles). The model results show very good agreement with the experimental data and indicate that the dissolution dynamics are indeed governed by oxide surface passivation and dissolution. Furthermore, comparison of results for different catalysts shows that the observed differences in Pt dissolution arise not only from variations in reaction rates on particles of different sizes but also from differences in the catalysts’ microscopic structure, which significantly influence Pt loss through diffusion.

title: YOLOv8-CNR: a lightweight fire and smoke detection model for forest fire scenarios based on improved YOLOv8
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: Introduction To address irregular morphology and drastic scale variations of flame and smoke targets in forest fire detection, and the difficulty of lightweight models in balancing accuracy and real-time performance, this paper proposes YOL
content: Introduction To address irregular morphology and drastic scale variations of flame and smoke targets in forest fire detection, and the difficulty of lightweight models in balancing accuracy and real-time performance, this paper proposes YOLOv8-CNR based on improved YOLOv8n. Methods The model optimizes backbone, neck, and loss function: C3_ConvNeXtv2 enhances flame texture and smoke edge representation; RepNCSPELAN4 strengthens multi-scale flow and small-target smoke features; SIoU improves localization of irregular targets. Results On M4SFWD with its trajectory-level split, YOLOv8-CNR achieves 79.8% mAP50 and 39.4% mAP50-95 with 2.52 M parameters, improving 7.5 and 2.6 percentage points over tuned YOLOv8n, at 238.1 FPS. This split eliminates near-duplicate frame leakage across subsets. Because the test set consists entirely of six Scene 4 camera runs that are absent from both training and validation, the M4SFWD results are interpreted as controlled comparisons under a scene-held-out setting rather than same-distribution generalization. Cross-dataset transfer is further evaluated through zero-shot transfer: trained only on M4SFWD, the model achieves 78.3 and 82.7% mAP50 on SMOKE_dataset and FLAME_dataset, respectively. Retrained on these datasets, it achieves 90.2 and 90.4% mAP50, demonstrating favorable real-world applicability. Ablation experiments show complementary and partially overlapping effects among the three modules, with the complete model achieving a 2.6 percentage point improvement in mAP50-95 over the baseline. Discussion The proposed model improves overall and smoke-related precision and recall, while flame precision slightly decreases (81.1% vs. 82.4%), flame mAP50-95 increases from 42.0 to 45.2%. This method provides an efficient solution for real-time flame and smoke detection in complex forest scenarios.

title: Genomic and ecological specialization of Methanobrevibacter species shape human methane emission and overall gut ecosystem function
summary: Abstract Methane is a unique archaeal metabolite that links gut microbial ecology to host physiology. Although intestinal methane production varies by several orders of magnitude between individuals and has been associated with gastrointest
content: Abstract Methane is a unique archaeal metabolite that links gut microbial ecology to host physiology. Although intestinal methane production varies by several orders of magnitude between individuals and has been associated with gastrointestinal transit and disease states, the ecological and functional determinants underlying this variation remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate breath methane phenotyping with shotgun metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, comparative genomics, cultivation and stable-isotope tracing in 80 deeply characterized individuals to determine the species-level and functional basis of human gut methanogenesis. Breath methane levels strongly reflected archaeal abundance but could not fully explain methane emission; species-resolved profiling revealed that methane emission represents distinct archaeome states rather than differences in methanogen quantity alone. High methane emitters were dominated by Methanobrevibacter smithii and M. intestini, whereas low emitters harbored a previously uncharacterized Methanobrevibacter lineage (M. sp900766745), for which we propose the name Candidatus Methanobrevibacter hominipaucus sp. nov. Comparative genomics revealed that M. sp900766745 represents a metabolically streamlined lineage lacking several methyl-compound utilization pathways and displaying reduced substrate acquisition capacity. Communities of low-emission individuals exhibited reduced microbial transcriptional activity and accumulated incompletely processed dietary metabolites, indicating lower fermentative turnover and altered hydrogen flux.

title: Tracking deep-time environmental stability exposes a global conservation gap
summary: Abstract Continents drift across latitudinal climate zones that are themselves shifting as Earth's climate evolves [1-5]. The relative speed of these two motions (tectonic versus climatic velocity) determines how much climate change a given
content: Abstract Continents drift across latitudinal climate zones that are themselves shifting as Earth's climate evolves [1-5]. The relative speed of these two motions (tectonic versus climatic velocity) determines how much climate change a given landmass experiences over geological time: where plates and climate zones move in concert, local climates can remain stable for millions of years, allowing lineages to persist and diversify. However, whether this interplay has shaped deep-time environmental stability and, in turn, present-day biodiversity patterns remains untested. Here, using a Lagrangian framework to track land parcels through 60 million years of palaeogeographic, palaeoclimatic, and palaeoproductivity reconstructions, we show that in amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals, species richness increases with the time a parcel has spent within a stable environmental envelope. This accumulation shows no sign of saturation, instead accelerating across nearly all combinations of taxonomic group and environment. Integrating stability along tectonic trajectories identifies modern macroevolutionary refugia (>20 Myr of cumulative stability). Of these refugia, 77.9% lack legal protection---rising to 91.5% in Asia---and just 2.1% fall within strictly protected areas. Refugia are only modestly better protected than unstable land (22.1% versus 15.8%), with over three-quarters of this difference driven by the weakest protection tiers. Having assembled while their environments moved at centimetres to metres per year, these biotas face present-day climate velocities of hundreds of metres to kilometres per year [6, 7], a kinematic debt that protecting static coordinates alone cannot address.

title: Probing Bimetallicity in Catalytic Systems: A Practical Tutorial on Advanced Analytical Tools
summary: Abstract Bimetallic catalysts provide a versatile platform for tuning catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability through metal–metal interactions, electronic modification, geometric/ensemble effects, and dynamic restructuring under reac
content: Abstract Bimetallic catalysts provide a versatile platform for tuning catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability through metal–metal interactions, electronic modification, geometric/ensemble effects, and dynamic restructuring under reaction conditions. However, establishing their working structure is challenging because the two metals may form alloys, solid solutions, intermetallic phases, Janus particles, core–shell structures, segregated domains, or partially oxidized surface species. This Tutorial Review introduces advanced analytical tools and complementary computational approaches for assessing bimetallicity, emphasizing the capabilities and limitations of each method. The discussion first outlines the structural complexity of bimetallic catalysts and the thermodynamic and kinetic factors that influence alloying, segregation, particle size, and surface composition, including the dynamic evolution of subnanometer-sized clusters. It then compares bulk, surface-sensitive, local-coordination, imaging, and adsorbate-probe methods, including X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), selected-area electron diffraction (SAED), infrared spectroscopy, chemisorption, temperature-programmed desorption/reduction (TPD/TPR), and in situ/operando approaches. Representative studies demonstrate why individual signatures, such as diffraction peak shifts, binding energy changes, lattice fringes, or CO adsorption bands, should not be interpreted in isolation. A dedicated Perspective distinguishes structural evidence of bimetallicity from demonstrations of catalytic synergism and discusses how controlled comparisons link working-state descriptors with kinetic and performance metrics, including turnover frequency, apparent activation energy, reaction order, selectivity, stability, and regenerability. Overall, this Tutorial Review provides a practical framework for selecting complementary characterization methods and building reliable structure-kinetics-performance relationships to guide bimetallic catalyst design.

title: Preparation of a high specificity imidacloprid monoclonal antibody and its application in homogeneous fluorescence immunoassay based on hydrogel beads assembling CdSe/ZnS quantum dots
summary: Abstract The risk associated with imidacloprid (IMI) residues necessitates the development of highly sensitive detection methods for ensuring food safety. In this study, IMI-hapten is synthesized via the reaction of IMI with β-mercaptopropi
content: Abstract The risk associated with imidacloprid (IMI) residues necessitates the development of highly sensitive detection methods for ensuring food safety. In this study, IMI-hapten is synthesized via the reaction of IMI with β-mercaptopropionic acid, and used to prepare immunogen, coating antigen, and IMI monoclonal antibody (IMI-mAb). An indirect competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ic-ELISA) is established, yielding a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 0.34 µg L -1 and a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.04 µg L -1 . To further enhance sensitivity and analytical efficiency, fluorescent hydrogel beads are engineered by embedding CdSe/ZnS quantum dots (QDs) into biocompatible chitosan hydrogel matrices. A homogeneous fluorescence immunoassay is subsequently established, relying on the competitive interaction between an antigen-conjugated quenching probe (AgNPs@IMI-OVA) and an antibody-labeled signal probe, which modulates the fluorescence intensity accordingly. Compared with conventional ELISA, this assay exhibits remarkable superiority, which achieves a LOD of 5.62×10 − 4 µg L -1 (representing over a 70‑fold enhancement), eliminates tedious washing steps, and completes the entire assay within 20 min. Validation using spiked fruit and vegetable samples confirms the method’s high specificity and reliability, demonstrating its great potential for the rapid screening of IMI residues in agro-products.

title: A general, non-energetic formation route to carboxylic and fatty acids in the interstellar medium
summary: Abstract Carboxylic acids have been detected in the interstellar medium, and biologically relevant fatty acids have been identified on meteorites. However, their formation routes under interstellar conditions and possible delivery to planet
content: Abstract Carboxylic acids have been detected in the interstellar medium, and biologically relevant fatty acids have been identified on meteorites. However, their formation routes under interstellar conditions and possible delivery to planetary surfaces to act as molecular building blocks for the origin of life remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate a general, non-energetic, condensed-phase formation route to carboxylic acids under astrophysical, low-temperature conditions, through the interaction of aldehydes and either O-atoms or hydroxyl radicals. This general acid formation route was investigated and confirmed experimentally through the use of infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry, and theoretically through the use of hybrid density functional theory and coupled cluster calculations. The finding of a non-energetic formation route from aldehydes to acids and the pathway to form biologically relevant fatty acids under interstellar conditions indicates that such molecules could form and subsequently be inherited into stellar systems, thus potentially contributing to the origin of life.

title: Robotic winding of wet-spun fibers for biofabrication of aligned, perfusable, muscle-based tissue
summary: Structural alignment of muscle and integrated vasculature enables the function of geometrically complex tissues in the body, such as the gastroesophageal junction and the ventricles. However, replicating this complexity is an ongoing challe
content: Structural alignment of muscle and integrated vasculature enables the function of geometrically complex tissues in the body, such as the gastroesophageal junction and the ventricles. However, replicating this complexity is an ongoing challenge. Described here is the wet-spun & robotically articulated placement (WRAP) method for deposition of aligned cellular fibers on scaffolds, resulting in large structures fabricated from the inside-out. WRAP enables complex, multi-oriented muscle and vascular placement by creating a continuous cellular fiber through wet spinning, and then using a robotic arm programmed with a set of tissue profiles to maneuver the fiber around an organ scaffold. Wet-spun fibers, consisting of muscle cells combined with endothelial cell fibers via double-core spinning, exhibited the ability to mature, align, contract, and initiate tubulogenesis, creating perfusable fibers. Further, the robotic arm could accurately create physiologically relevant fiber patterns with high precision. The potential to generate perfusable blood vessels alongside functional muscle is paramount to fabricating muscle-based constructs. The WRAP method offers a high throughput and versatile solution to the scale-up problem plaguing the biofabrication of muscle-based tissues.

title: A multi-technical method for the taxonomic identification and production history of three medieval gilt leathers from the Palacio de Viana in Córdoba
summary: Abstract Gilt leather was an artistic representation made on skin that became widely popular in the late 15th century and, especially, in the first half of the 16th century. It was a carved leather whose main decoration was gilding and pain
content: Abstract Gilt leather was an artistic representation made on skin that became widely popular in the late 15th century and, especially, in the first half of the 16th century. It was a carved leather whose main decoration was gilding and painting, often with additional engravings and embossing. Its elitist character and the social recognition it acquired turned this object into a symbol of cultural identity. Nevertheless, understanding the complex production techniques requires an overview not limited to written sources, especially with regard to the nature of the hide. We applied Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry (ZooMS) using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionisation trapped ion mobility time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-timsTOF) to three gilt leathers from the Palacio de Viana leather collection (Córdoba, Spain). Using minimal amounts of sample, the three objects were established to derive from sheepskin. This technique also allowed us to estimate the peptide deamidation levels, found to be higher than those estimated in parchment. This likely reflects the aggressive chemical treatment of leather and its preservation history. The combination with a scanning electron microscope analysis fitted with an energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) detector contributes to the reconstruction of their production history.

title: Modeling Decadal Organosulfates in Particulate Matter to Improve Estimations of Aerosol Hygroscopicity in the United States
summary: Abstract Organosulfates (OSs) can comprise a substantial fraction of secondary organic aerosol and exhibit significantly different hygroscopicity than inorganic sulfates, yet their spatiotemporal prevalence and climatic impacts remain poorl
content: Abstract Organosulfates (OSs) can comprise a substantial fraction of secondary organic aerosol and exhibit significantly different hygroscopicity than inorganic sulfates, yet their spatiotemporal prevalence and climatic impacts remain poorly constrained because speciated measurements are sparse and common chemical transport models do not explicitly represent OS formation. This study develops a flexible and robust modeling framework to quantify isoprene-derived OS (iOS) concentrations and OS impacts on aerosol hygroscopicity (κ) across the contiguous United States (U.S.) for summers spanning 2013–2022. Using the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model with updated iOS chemistry, simulations reproduce Interagency Monitoring of Protected Visual Environments (IMPROVE) network-derived organosulfur and inorganic sulfate and agree with speciated iOS measurements from filter analyses. OS concentrations are elevated in the eastern U.S., with summertime mean values up to 0.51 μg m–3. OS formation produces a net 5.6% decrease in κ (direct OS contribution, +2.8%; indirect, −8.4% via sulfate reduction). We apply an interpretable machine-learning surrogate to identify predictive features associated with OS variability and enable efficient estimation without rerunning CMAQ. These results provide the first observation-validated, high-spatial-coverage OS reconstruction and nationwide quantification of OS-driven κ changes, underscoring the importance of representing OS formation and expanded observations to improve aerosol-cloud radiative effect assessments.

title: Synthesis and Engineering of Bio-Based Porous Organic Polymers for Gold Recovery
summary: The development of functional porous materials from renewable resources offers a promising strategy to reduce reliance on fossil-derived feedstocks and advance sustainable materials technologies. Here, we report the facile synthesis of bio-
content: The development of functional porous materials from renewable resources offers a promising strategy to reduce reliance on fossil-derived feedstocks and advance sustainable materials technologies. Here, we report the facile synthesis of bio-based porous organic polymers (bioPOPs) through the polycondensation of vanillin-derived organic dialdehydes and inexpensive diamine monomers. The synthetic approach demonstrates good generality, enabling vanillin-derived monomers bearing different functional substituents (H, OH, CH3, OCH3, and NO2) to be converted into bioPOPs with high specific surface areas of up to 523 m2/g and abundant microporosity. Furthermore, cellulose nanofibers (CNF) were employed as templates for the in situ interfacial polymerization of bioPOPs on their surfaces, allowing the resulting hybrid nanofibers to be processed into freestanding composite films. Benefiting from their rich microporosity and abundant nitrogen-containing functional groups, both pristine bioPOPs and CNF@bioPOP composite films exhibited efficient [AuCl4]- capture from aqueous solutions, with adsorption capacities of up to 1093 mg/g, rapid adsorption kinetics, and excellent selectivity over competing metal ions. More importantly, the materials demonstrated highly efficient and selective gold recovery from real electronic waste leachate, highlighting their potential for preciousmetal recovery from secondary resources. The freestanding composite films further offer advantages for practical separation applications through their processability and potential integration into continuous flow systems. Overall, this work demonstrates the transformation of renewable resources into functional porous materials for precious-metal recovery from secondary waste streams, establishing a fully sustainable and circular approach to resource utilization.

title: Spatial dynamics of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in an urban environment and associated impacts on air quality
summary: Abstract. Urban air pollution, affecting residents and commuters alike, depends considerably on volatile organic compounds (VOCs) due to their toxicity and potential to form secondary pollutants. The distribution and composition of urban VO
content: Abstract. Urban air pollution, affecting residents and commuters alike, depends considerably on volatile organic compounds (VOCs) due to their toxicity and potential to form secondary pollutants. The distribution and composition of urban VOCs reflect their emission as well as transport and atmospheric removal and formation processes. Hence, the VOC burden can differ substantially on small spatial scales. Aiming at investigating whether and how a large street canyon with dense traffic influences the air quality of adjacent neighbourhoods, we conducted trailer-based mobile measurements of nitrogen oxides, ozone, and VOCs in the city of Munich, Germany in September 2023. VOCs were measured using a highly resolved proton transfer reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometer (PTR-ToF-MS). To support different statistical analyses, the study area was divided into grid cells. A distinct separation of the VOC pool into traffic-related, biogenic, and functionalized compounds was achieved by hierarchical cluster analysis, ultimately assisting non-target analyses. The spatial variability was characterized by a combination of hierarchical cluster analysis, k-means analysis, and non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS). We show for exemplary locations that small-scale variations of some of the less abundant but highly reactive VOCs emitted by traffic (e.g. aromatics, alkenes) induce statistically significant spatial differences in terms of oxidant reactivities and the potential for the formation of aerosols or ozone. Finally, the variability-lifetime relationships of the VOC groups were analysed, revealing that the variability of the traffic-related VOCs was more tightly linked to local source strength compared to the biogenic and functionalized VOCs, and supporting their respective allocation.

title: Efficient and stable inverted RGB quantum-dot-electrolyte LEDs for active-matrix displays
summary: Quantum dots (QDs) are promising for optoelectronic applications, and the exploration of QD-electrolyte (QE) may endow distinctive optical and electronic characteristics. However, the performance of red QE-based light-emitting diodes (QE-LE
content: Quantum dots (QDs) are promising for optoelectronic applications, and the exploration of QD-electrolyte (QE) may endow distinctive optical and electronic characteristics. However, the performance of red QE-based light-emitting diodes (QE-LEDs) is limited, and green/blue QE-LEDs have not been reported. Here, we report an inverted architecture that eliminates solvent compatibility issues, enabling efficient and stable red/green/blue (RGB) QE-LEDs. By doping an ionic liquid into QDs, an electrolyte emitting layer (EML) enhances charge injection and transport. Additionally, an insulating layer is placed between the EML and the electron transport layer, suppressing excessive electron leakage. The red QE-LED exhibits a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.2% and a T95 lifetime of 13,100 h at 1000 cd m−2, surpassing previous best red QE-LEDs. The green QE-LED shows an EQE of 20.3% and a T95 lifetime of 14,400 h at 1000 cd m−2. Notably, the blue QE-LED possesses an EQE of 13.5% and a T95 lifetime of 244.5 h at 1000 cd m−2, representing a record stability for solution-processed blue LEDs without light-outcoupling technologies. Furthermore, we develop RGB active-matrix displays, exhibiting excellent stability and uniformity. The results unlock potential opportunities to develop QE-based devices for next-generation high-performance electroluminescence devices and optoelectronic technologies. Quantum-dot electrolyte light-emitting diodes promise new optoelectronics, but efficient green and blue devices remain elusive. Ren et al. developed an inverted, ion-enhanced architecture enabling efficient, stable full-color devices and displays.

title: Microbiome-mediated effects of Bacillus subtilis inoculants on rice straw decomposition, residue chemistry, and nutrient release in double-cropping paddy fields
summary: Returning rice straw to fields is key for sustainable agriculture, yet its slow decomposition conflicts with tight schedules in double-cropping rice systems. Whether laboratory-effective microbial inoculants can consistently enhance straw d
content: Returning rice straw to fields is key for sustainable agriculture, yet its slow decomposition conflicts with tight schedules in double-cropping rice systems. Whether laboratory-effective microbial inoculants can consistently enhance straw decomposition and nutrient turnover in the field remains unclear. We conducted a two-season field experiment using nylon-mesh bags that prevented direct mixing of straw from soil-applied inoculants (laboratory-developed decomposing inoculant, LABIN; conventional commercial decomposing inoculant, COMIN, both Bacillus subtilis-based), thereby evaluating their primarily indirect effects via stimulation of the indigenous soil microbiome. Neither inoculant significantly increased net dry matter loss in either season ( p >0.05). However, LABIN exerted profound effects on nutrient release dynamics, it markedly elevated phosphorus release in the late-season period and persistently drove greater lignin degradation as well as unique structural alterations within straw residues, which was verified via Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). LEfSe analysis identified enrichment of putative decomposer taxa such as Vicinamibacter and Candida tropicalis , without affecting alpha diversity. Collectively, these results indicate that LABIN did not accelerate overall mass loss under conditions of limited direct inoculant–straw contact. Nevertheless, it altered straw residue chemistry and nutrient release, likely through selective shifts in the soil microbial community. This finding provides proof-of-concept evidence for a primarily indirect, microbiome-mediated mode of action of LABIN in paddy systems.

title: Thiolate addition to withaferin A: a GFN2-xTB and DFT study of site-selective glutathione conjugation
summary: Abstract Withaferin A (WFA), the major steroidal lactone of Withania somnifera , alkylates cysteine residues in vimentin, Hsp90 and IKKβ. Glutathione (GSH), the cell’s most abundant thiol, serves as the initial step in detoxifying electroph
content: Abstract Withaferin A (WFA), the major steroidal lactone of Withania somnifera , alkylates cysteine residues in vimentin, Hsp90 and IKKβ. Glutathione (GSH), the cell’s most abundant thiol, serves as the initial step in detoxifying electrophiles. The carbon that interacts with it determines both the rate of clearance and the extent to which a compound remains to alkylate proteins. It is unquantified at any of WFA’s four electrophilic carbons: the ring-A enone (C3), the side-chain lactone (C24) and the epoxide carbons (C5, C6). This study computes conformer-ensemble free energies with GFN2-xTB in implicit water with quasi-RRHO corrections, scans the C–S approach coordinate at each site, and recalibrates with M06-2X single point calculations on truncated models. Nucleophiles were modelled as thiolates and adducts as anions; the isolable species is the neutral protonated conjugate. Addition is most exergonic at C3-α (ΔG = − 11.7 kcal mol⁻¹), then C6 (− 8.9), C5 (− 8.3) and C24 (+ 0.2 to − 4.4). Site-specific DFT corrections invert this ordering toward the epoxides. A def2-TZVP check shifts every correction by about + 7.8 kcal mol⁻¹, removing the sign difference between reaction classes but, because it is uniform, leaving the ranking intact: the inversion is robust to basis set though the corrections are not. No Hessian-verified saddle was located, so no activation energy is reported; C3 has no interior scan maximum whereas both methods place one at the epoxide, supporting kinetic control without establishing it. The methanethiolate probe reproduced glutathionate’s site preference but inverted its facial preference, α by 7.0 against β by 13.3 kcal mol⁻¹, so minimal-thiol screening ranks sites dependably, faces unreliably.

title: Precursor-Dependent Performance of Low-Silicate-Modulus Industrial Byproduct-Based Geopolymers
summary: This study examined 16 alkaline-activated paste formulations using granulated blast-furnace slag (GBFS) and fly ash from Çatalağzı (CAT), Kemerköy (KEM), and Kangal (KAN). Four nominal silicate moduli (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8) were tested, w
content: This study examined 16 alkaline-activated paste formulations using granulated blast-furnace slag (GBFS) and fly ash from Çatalağzı (CAT), Kemerköy (KEM), and Kangal (KAN). Four nominal silicate moduli (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8) were tested, with the water content of each precursor being adjusted using a Vicat-based consistency criterion. All specimens were heat-treated at 60 °C for 24 hours. The density, ultrasonic pulse velocity, and mechanical performance of the specimens were assessed in relation to the composition, fineness, and morphology of the precursors. The water-to-binder ratios ranged from 0.251–0.259 for CAT to 0.688–0.699 for KAN. GBFS achieved peak compressive and flexural strengths of 82.25 and 4.91 MPa, respectively, at a nominal modulus of 0.6 with a maximum ultrasonic pulse velocity of 3.65 km/s. CAT performed best at a modulus of 0.6, while KEM achieved its highest mechanical performance at a modulus of 0.4. KAN exhibited a loss-on-ignition of 9.60%, high water demand, bleeding, declining density, and low strength. Its density decreased by 8.45% between days 1 and 28, but this does not directly correlate with porosity. Differences in water content complicate strength comparisons across precursors, while changes in alkaline dosage limit the interpretation of modulus effects. Therefore, the best-performing formulations depend on the consistency and curing conditions used. These results highlight the importance of considering activator composition, precursor properties, and water demand together.

title: Utility-Gated Personalized Federated Forecasting for Peak-Constrained Building Energy Management
summary: Abstract Distributed building energy management depends on forecasts, yet federated forecasting is commonly evaluated without testing the decisions that those forecasts support. This study examines whether selective, communication-efficient
content: Abstract Distributed building energy management depends on forecasts, yet federated forecasting is commonly evaluated without testing the decisions that those forecasts support. This study examines whether selective, communication-efficient collaboration improves both load prediction and battery operation. The proposed UtilityGossipmethod maintains separate private and collaborative low-rank adapters at each node. A peer adapter is incorporated only when randomized cross-fitting on local held-out data indicates a meaningful reduction in forecast error. Evaluation on public electricity and solar benchmarks covers longer horizons, alternative network topologies, node failures, and transmit-time noise. At the 96-step horizon, the method reduces Solar-Energy mean squared error by 1.59% relative to local training and avoids the greater than 3% degradation caused by unconditional federation on Electricity, using half the communication of federated averaging. Operational value is assessed by replaying every forecast source through the same frozen battery policy for a held-out week. An external projection prevents coordinated charging from increasing the running no-storage district peak. The proposed forecast supports a 19.34% cost reduction relative to no storage, and diagnostic replays confirm that forecast timing affects dispatch. Its additional control gain over a strong local forecast is not statistically resolved. The results support selective federation for distributed forecasting but show that lower prediction error does not necessarily yield proportional energy savings.

title: Disclosing compound and cascading climate risks in food system portfolios
summary: Climate change, and associated increased weather variability and extreme events, will have a major impact on food systems and consequently on financial institutions with a large portfolio in food system investments. Without taking appropria
content: Climate change, and associated increased weather variability and extreme events, will have a major impact on food systems and consequently on financial institutions with a large portfolio in food system investments. Without taking appropriate risk mitigation measures, climate-related shocks across food systems will adversely affect these financial institutions. Through various transmission mechanisms of the food and financial systems, this can have consequences for the wider economy. The financial sector has gradually come to understand that climate change will seriously impact food systems, which are often high-input intensive, with substantial uncertainty and tail-risk. There is growing evidence that climate change events and their impacts manifest in complex, non-linear, non-uniform ways, often through compound and cascading climate risks. Climate change has the greatest impact in the primary stage of a food system in which production depends on growing conditions during the season. Compound risks arise from the simultaneous or sequential occurrence of multiple climate hazards, such as heatwaves coinciding with droughts, amplifying overall impacts (e.g., reduced crop yields). Cascading risks emerge when climate-related impacts propagate through interconnected social, economic, and natural systems, crossing the agricultural sector and borders, thus triggering wider chains of consequences. In this article we will lay out how climate risk assessment (CRA) frameworks are integrated into financial sector regulation and into the corresponding industry standards (including the standards for agricultural portfolios). We start with the global CRA frameworks and then zoom into the various EU policy instruments to address climate-related financial sector risks. Subsequently, we focus on the implementation of CRA frameworks. While the CRA frameworks do not explicitly mention compound and cascading risks, further reading in professional literature illustrates how to include these risk types through scenario analysis. Therefore, the scope of the subsequent analysis is to link compound and cascading risks with scenario analysis. We conclude that there is currently limited rigor in incorporating compound and cascading climate risks into CRA frameworks and disclosures, although the topic is emerging. This calls for deeper engagement in the coming years, from regulators financial industry, food system actors and academia.

title: Harnessing GIS to map trawl fishing grounds and reduce carbon footprint along India’s west coast
summary: Aim: This study examines the spatial and temporal dynamics of key commercial fish species along the west coast of India through GIS-based mapping, aiming to reduce the environmental footprint of trawl fisheries by optimizing fishing effort,
content: Aim: This study examines the spatial and temporal dynamics of key commercial fish species along the west coast of India through GIS-based mapping, aiming to reduce the environmental footprint of trawl fisheries by optimizing fishing effort, minimizing scouting time, and lowering carbon emissions. Methodology: Data from customised logbooks for each fishing operation were geo-referenced using recorded latitude–longitude coordinates to delineate the spatial extent of fishing grounds. Spatial analysis and map generation were conducted using ArcGIS, while Visual Basic 6 was used for database management and query execution. The datasets were used to generate thematic layers, shapefiles, and feature classes for spatio-temporal analysis of fishing activities and species distribution. Results: Three commercially important species/groups—Trichiurus lepturus, Nemipterus spp. (N. japonicus and N. randalli), and Lagocephalus inermis—showed consistent occurrence within trawling grounds, with clear seasonal fluctuations in abundance. Peak abundances of Nemipterus spp. in January and October and Lagocephalus inermis in January and May, indicating persistent species–habitat associations across seasons. Interpretation: The findings of this study highlight the utility of participatory GIS-based mapping in identifying productive fishing grounds and supporting adaptive, season-specific fisheries management, and conservation planning. Practically, the spatial information generated can help fishers reduce scouting time, fuel consumption, and operational costs by targeting areas of consistent abundance, thereby also contributing to lower greenhouse gas emissions from trawling operations. Key words: Climate change, CO2 emission, Fisheries, Fishing grounds, Mitigation, Trawl

title: CO2 confinement by a novel molecular spring architecture via reactive molecular dynamics
summary: Abstract In this study, we propose a novel framework with a hybrid molecular spring architecture based on a spiral/helical-type nanostructure supported by slab layers and bridged by organic linkers. Hierarchically, the framework consists of
content: Abstract In this study, we propose a novel framework with a hybrid molecular spring architecture based on a spiral/helical-type nanostructure supported by slab layers and bridged by organic linkers. Hierarchically, the framework consists of symmetrical nickel (Ni)-doped α-Al 2 O 3 slabs, a sulfur-rich helical cage, and multifunctional 2,5-dimercaptoterephthalic acid (DMBDC) organic linkers. Ni/α-Al 2 O 3 supported, DMBDC bridged and helical pillared framework (SL-HPF) contributed to dynamic structural stability, the synergistic role of interfacial coupling and molecular confinement through reactive force field (ReaxFF) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The CO 2 confinement performance of SL-HPF was analysed by atomic arrangements via MD trajectories, self-diffusion coefficient (D), radial distribution functions (RDF), gas viscosity measurements. To isolate the contribution of the helical cage, a control system was conducted on pure Ni/α-Al 2 O 3 slabs. The D and gas viscosity of CO 2 for only control system are 1.451 × 10 –7 m 2 s −1 and 0.0163 Js m −3 , respectively. In contrast, the SL-HPF exhibited an enhanced molecular trapping because CO 2 molecules systematically penetrated the helical cage due to strong confinement effects. For SL-HPF, D and local fluid viscosity of CO 2 were calculated as 1.812 × 10 –8 m 2 s −1 and 0.0347 Js m −3 , respectively. Structural localization was further validated by a highly dense S-C pair RDF correlation peak at 1.8 Å within the helical cage. These results demonstrate that the synergy between catalytic metal sites, elastic organic springs, and high-affinity sulfur vacancies in the helical cage can successfully immobilize gas molecules through molecular trapping rather than chemical bond disruption. This work presents a novel molecular spring design and hybrid framework for next-generation environmental remediation technologies.

title: Toxic ecologies and harm stabilization: a critical realist account of social-ecological harm at Nairobi’s Dandora Dumpsite
summary: Urban waste systems can reproduce severe harm even where it is extensively documented and repeatedly targeted by policy. This article asks how unjust human-nature relations become stabilized as routine under these conditions, using a critic
content: Urban waste systems can reproduce severe harm even where it is extensively documented and repeatedly targeted by policy. This article asks how unjust human-nature relations become stabilized as routine under these conditions, using a critical realist analysis of Nairobi's Dandora Dumpsite. It proposes the concept of toxic ecology, an emergent configuration in which contaminants, infrastructures, institutions, and everyday practices cohere into durable patterns of exposure and inequality. A mixed-genre documentary corpus is synthesized through structured extraction and retroduction to identify recurring regularities and infer a conjunctural configuration of six interacting mechanisms, spanning responsibility diffusion, regulatory deferral, infrastructural lock-in, normalization, unequal valuation, and de facto control.
