content: Rare sugars, monosaccharides that occur only rarely in nature, exhibit physicochemical and biological properties distinct from those of naturally abundant sugars such as D-glucose. Their widespread utilization has been hindered by limitations in existing production methods, which rely primarily on equilibrium-constrained biocatalytic cascades or on synthetic approaches requiring multiple steps or organic reagents. Here we show the one-pot heterogeneous catalytic epimerization of methyl glucosides into rare sugar derivatives over supported Ru catalysts under hydrogen atmosphere in water. Among the supported metals examined, Ru uniquely promotes regioselective stereoinversion of 1- O -methyl β-D-glucopyranoside at the C3 position to produce 1- O -methyl β-D-allopyranoside without requiring additional reagents or multistep reactions. Isotopelabeling experiments reveal that dehydrogenation and hydrogenation proceed substantially faster than net epimerization, identifying surface-confined molecular rotation of a keto intermediate as the rate-determining step. Computer simulations further show that the experimentally observed regioselectivity originates from the low rotational free energy barriers and relatively high stability of the keto intermediate on the Ru surface. These findings identify molecular rotational dynamics on catalyst surfaces as a governing principle for stereochemical inversion reactions.

title: Clarifying the Use of Reflection Coefficient (%) in Guided Wave Testing Reports: Why Reflection Coefficient and Not Reflectivity
summary: Guided Wave Testing (GWT) is a long-range ultrasonic inspection technique widely used for measuring pipelines and other elongated structures. As an ultrasonic method, it measures the amplitude of reflected mechanical waves. However, a persi
content: Guided Wave Testing (GWT) is a long-range ultrasonic inspection technique widely used for measuring pipelines and other elongated structures. As an ultrasonic method, it measures the amplitude of reflected mechanical waves. However, a persistent usage error exists in portions of the guided wave testing community: the use of the term reflectivity (%) to describe the amplitude of reflected signals in inspection reports. In wave physics, reflectivity is defined as the ratio of reflected wave energy to incident wave energy and is equal to the square of the reflection coefficient. The reflection coefficient, by contrast, describes the ratio of reflected amplitude to incident wave amplitude at the reflector location — and this is the parameter that ultrasonic instruments actually measure. Using reflectivity (%) where reflection coefficient (%) is physically correct introduces a fundamental inconsistency that distorts defect severity estimates and undermines inspection transparency. This paper clarifies the physical definitions of reflection coefficient and reflectivity, demonstrates the numerical consequences of confusing these two parameters in GWT reports, and presents evidence from a published ASTM standard and field inspection data that confirm the amplitude-based interpretation. The paper concludes that guided wave testing reports must use reflection coefficient (%) on a calibrated Time-Corrected Gain (TCG) plot in order to meet the standards of transparent and quantitative inspection reporting.

title: A Review of Starch‐Based Bioplastics From Plant and Agro‐Based Sources: Extraction, Characterization, and Applications
summary: ABSTRACT The persistence of nonbiodegradable petrochemical plastics, which can endure for centuries, poses ecological challenges. Their accumulation and toxic emissions during disposal contribute to plastic pollution, an escalating environm
content: ABSTRACT The persistence of nonbiodegradable petrochemical plastics, which can endure for centuries, poses ecological challenges. Their accumulation and toxic emissions during disposal contribute to plastic pollution, an escalating environmental and public health concern. Starch‐based bioplastics are promising because they are low‐cost, recyclable, and available from plant sources and agricultural waste, including potato, corn, rice, wheat, cassava, banana peel, jackfruit seed, mango seed, avocado seed, and lucuma seed. Bioplastics are a sustainable alternative. This study shows the methods for extracting starch from various feedstocks and examines the roles of starch gelatinization and plasticization in film development. The impact of common plasticizers (particularly sorbitol and glycerol) and natural, organic, and inorganic fillers is examined in relation to structure‐property trade‐offs. Natural extracts, essential oils, and other bioactive components can modify mechanical, barrier, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties of starch‐based films. Surface morphology, structural, functional, mechanical, and thermal characterizations are frequently used for bioplastic analysis. The strength and decomposition of the composites were confirmed by mechanical and soil biodegradation tests, and the composites regularly improved performance. Starch‐based bioplastics can substitute petrochemical‐based plastics, reducing environmental issues.

title: Revealing Phase-Controlled Surface Structure in PtNi Nanocatalysts via In-situ Gas Cell Transmission Electron Microscopy
summary: The rational design of catalysts capable of efficiently utilizing CO2 is critical for sustainable chemical processes. The Super-dry reforming of methane (Super-DRM), which couples dry reforming of methane (DRM) with the reverse water gas sh
content: The rational design of catalysts capable of efficiently utilizing CO2 is critical for sustainable chemical processes. The Super-dry reforming of methane (Super-DRM), which couples dry reforming of methane (DRM) with the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reactions, offers a promising route to maximize CO2 conversion. Modulating the crystal phase of nanocatalysts offers a powerful strategy to enhance catalytic performance, yet the relationship between bulk phase and catalytic behavior remains poorly understood. A significant obstacle in resolving this issue is obtaining atomic-level insights on the surface structure of phase-controlled catalyst under reaction conditions. In this study, we employ in-situ gas cell transmission electron microscopy to investigate the surface structure of faceted PtNi nanoparticles during Super-DRM at moderate temperatures (550 ℃). Atomic-resolution in-situ observations reveal that the reaction environment induces a pronounced nickel segregation and subsequent coke formation on the surface of disordered A1-PtNi nanoparticles. In contrast, the ordered L10 phase exhibits remarkable resistance to such segregation on its {111} facets. This structural rigidity effectively suppresses coke formation and lowers the kinetic barrier for CH4 activation by 27 kJ/mol compared to the disordered phase. Complemented by in-situ spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, our findings demonstrate that the bulk crystal ordering acts as an anchor for surface structures, governing the catalytic behaviors. This study unveils a direct atomic-level link between crystal ordering, surface reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering valuable design principles for robust intermetallic catalysts in CO2 utilization.

title: In Vitro and In Vivo Evaluation of Green-Synthesized ZnO Nanoparticle-Reinforced Hydroxyethyl Cellulose Biocomposite Derived from Sugarcane Bagasse Cellulose for Skin Tissue Repair
summary: Sustainable bioactive wound dressings have attracted considerable attention for enhancing skin tissue regeneration. In this research, sugarcane bagasse (SCB)-derived cellulose was converted into hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) and blended with
content: Sustainable bioactive wound dressings have attracted considerable attention for enhancing skin tissue regeneration. In this research, sugarcane bagasse (SCB)-derived cellulose was converted into hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) and blended with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), Type A gelatin and succinic acid (SA) to fabricate crosslinked nanobiocomposite hydrogel films reinforced with Aloe vera -mediated zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). The hydrogels were prepared by solution casting and characterized by FTIR, XRD, FESEM and TGA. Structural characterisation showed homogeneous dispersion of ZnO NPs throughout the polymer network, with a mean particle diameter of approximately 72 nm. The optimized HEC/PVA/Succinic acid/Gelatin/ZnO NPs (HPSGZ) biocomposite demonstrated a tensile strength of 12.30 ± 0.03 MPa (n = 3), a water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) of 2340 ± 5 g m⁻² day⁻¹, together with a swelling ratio of 1140 ± 5% at pH 7.4, demonstrating favorable moisture management. The hydrogel exhibited pronounced antibacterial efficacy toward Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli , enhanced antioxidant activity, excellent hemocompatibility and >95% Vero cell viability after 72 h. In vivo evaluation demonstrated approximately 96 ± 2% wound closure within 12 days, accompanied by accelerated tissue regeneration. These findings indicate that the developed HPSGZ nanobiocomposite offers a sustainable and effective platform for advanced wound management.

title: Drinking-Water 4,4′-Methylenedianiline Establishes a Longitudinally Tractable Mouse Model of Cholestatic Liver Injury
summary: Longitudinal studies of liver injury require models that can be maintained with simple administration, low procedure-related stress, and acceptable survival. Drinking-water thioacetamide (TAA-DW) is useful for this purpose, but it mainly pr
content: Longitudinal studies of liver injury require models that can be maintained with simple administration, low procedure-related stress, and acceptable survival. Drinking-water thioacetamide (TAA-DW) is useful for this purpose, but it mainly produces centrilobular hepatocellular injury. Few drinking-water models are available for cholestatic liver injury. Here, we tested whether 4,4'-methylenedianiline (MDA), a known bile-duct-damaging hepatotoxicant, can be used to build a practical drinking-water model of cholestatic liver injury in mice. Male C57BL/6JJcl mice received MDA in drinking water for up to 28 days. A route- and administration-schedule-matched TAA-DW model was used as a reference. Drinking-water MDA (MDA-DW) caused sustained ALT elevation without observed mortality under the tested regimen. Compared with TAA-DW, MDA-DW produced stronger cholestatic biochemical features, including increased ALP, TBIL, and TCHO. Histology showed bile duct hyperplasia with degeneration, periportal/peribiliary fibrosis, and scattered focal hepatocellular necrosis. Whole-slide image analysis supported the distinct lesion distribution between MDA-DW and TAA-DW. Early time-resolved multimodal profiling showed model-specific responses: MDA-DW showed ALT elevation around Days 2-3, increased CD8-positive T cells on Day 8, and enrichment of fibrinolysis-related gene sets, whereas TAA-DW showed a sharp early injury peak and transient eosinophil increase. Impact Statement: This study expands the range of drinking-water liver injury models by providing a low-mortality MDA-DW model with cholestatic liver injury. The model offers a simple platform for time-resolved studies of liver injury progression, tissue remodeling, and model-specific inflammatory responses.

title: Storage, Connectivity, and Stream Drying in Headwater Systems: Modeling Across Hydrogeomorphic Features
summary: Abstract Headwater streams play a critical role in the physical, chemical, and biological functions of downstream waters. However, predicting their specific impact on a landscape scale remains a grand challenge, prompting the development of
content: Abstract Headwater streams play a critical role in the physical, chemical, and biological functions of downstream waters. However, predicting their specific impact on a landscape scale remains a grand challenge, prompting the development of the river corridor framework to integrate the study of stream channels and hyporheic zones with that of adjacent hillslopes and riparian zones. To operationalize this framework and better explore hydrologic fluxes, the intermediate hydrogeomorphic feature (HGF) scale was recently defined to discretize the river corridor into quantifiable and repeatable compartments. In this study, we used process‐based modeling within and across HGFs to evaluate hydrologic connectivity, storage, streamflow, and drying. We used the Advanced Terrestrial Simulator to model hydrologic fluxes in an experimental watershed in the Coastal Plain of the southeastern United States, where we delineated incised, intact riparian, and wetland HGFs along three streams. Among HGFs, incised channels gained the most water from the subsurface, wetland HGFs maintained the highest water tables, and intact riparian HGFs frequently went dry. Incised and wetland HGFs generated the majority of discharge throughout the year, but dry season discharge was dominated by streamflow gains in incised HGFs. Together, these results suggest that stream incision increases downstream connectivity and export, whereas wetland HGFs increase watershed capacity for storage. Our findings highlight the role of geomorphic structure in driving spatial patterns of drying, storage, and connectivity. Given the pervasiveness of stream incision across anthropogenically impacted systems, our results provide a basis for identifying locations significant to watershed‐scale hydrologic export or retention.

title: Sulfation enabled dynamic activation and single-atom extraction against SO2 poisoning
summary: The sulfate formation from the residual SO2 in the industrial exhaust has long been recognized as the primary cause of sulfur poisoning in the oxidative removal of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Contrary to the conventional understandin
content: The sulfate formation from the residual SO2 in the industrial exhaust has long been recognized as the primary cause of sulfur poisoning in the oxidative removal of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Contrary to the conventional understanding, here we showed in situ sulfation enables dynamic activation of Pt1/MnxTi1-xO2 single atom catalysts against sulfur poisoning, forming dynamically Pt1/MnSO4 with highly active Pt1-SO4 motif that results in excellent benzene oxidation of 6.3×10-6 mol·g-1 cat·s-1 in presence of 100 ppm SO2 at 240 °C, and unprecedented SO2-resistant stability up to 300 h. State-of-the-art in situ characterizations along with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, clearly revealed dynamic transformation of two distinct sulfur oxo-salts from chemisorbed (SO3)ads sulfite to SO42- sulfate during reaction and their specific role in SO2 resistant benzene oxidation. The as-formed (SO3)ads adsorbates blocked the Pt sites on MnxTi1-xO2 consequently resulting in irreversible deactivation. In contrast, in situ sulfation promoted the dynamic activation of poisonous (SO3)ads into SO42- sulfate, and simultaneously enables Pt single-atom extraction from MnxTi1-xO2 onto the as-formed MnSO4 sulfate. In situ DRIFTS measurements further revealed that the square-planar Pt1-SO4 motif on the as-formed Pt1/MnSO4 can effectively prevent the SO2 adsorption, preserving highly exposed Pt single-atom sites for deep oxidation of benzene to carboxylate. This work provides dynamic insights for sulfation of Pt single-atom catalyst against SO2 poisoning, and benefits the general design of Pt1-SO4 motif for SO2 resistant oxidation of a broad range of VOCs, including benzene, propane and ethylene.

title: Responses of functional trait networks and hub traits of submerged macrophytes to water depth variation in an impounded lake of the South‑to‑North Water Transfer Project, China
summary: Trait network analysis have been widely used to unravel the effects of variable environments on submerged macrophytes communities. However, few studies focused on the response of submerged macrophytes to variable water depths in impounded l
content: Trait network analysis have been widely used to unravel the effects of variable environments on submerged macrophytes communities. However, few studies focused on the response of submerged macrophytes to variable water depths in impounded lakes from a whole plant trait network perspective. Here, we carried out a field study aimed to evaluate variation of functional traits, detect hub traits and clarify trait network topologies among different water depths. Overall, our results showed that internodes number, plant height，root number, stem diameter, rhizosphere diameter, root weight, specific leaf area, carbon content and phosphorus content significantly differed among different water depths. From shallow to deep water depth, the hub traits of submerged macrophytes communities gradually shift from resource-acquisitive traits to resource-conservative traits in response to light attenuation. The functional trait network exhibited high edge density and average clustering coefficient, low average path length and tight assemblages of three modules, indicating high-efficiency traits cooperation and resource acquisition at moderate water depth. This study explored the changing patterns and determinants of trait networks along water depth gradients to improve our understanding of ecological rules regulating trait correlations.

title: Chemoreceptor TRPγ coordinates locomotor activity via regulating intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis in Drosophila
summary: Abstract Chemosensation underlies animal behavioral adaptation in ever-changing environments. As a member of the canonical transient receptor potential (TRP), TRPγ orchestrates the chemosensation and the adaptive behavior via fine motor con
content: Abstract Chemosensation underlies animal behavioral adaptation in ever-changing environments. As a member of the canonical transient receptor potential (TRP), TRPγ orchestrates the chemosensation and the adaptive behavior via fine motor control in Drosophila. Yet, how TRPγ senses and transduces chemical cues has been elusive. Here, we explored cryo-EM structures of dTRPγ in both apo and camphor-bound states, with resolutions of 2.18 Å and 3.44 Å, respectively, thereby capturing ligand-induced pore dilation. Through analysis of dTRPγchannel structure, we further identified two allosteric Ca2+-sensing modules: an activating site embedded within the voltage-sensor-like domain (VSLD) and an inhibitory site coordinated by the intracellular ankyrin repeat domain (ARD) and coiled-coil domain (CCD). These spatially segregated sensors convert cytoplasmic Ca2+ into opposing gating signals, maintaining calcium homeostasis via a dual-feedback manner. In vivo, this bidirectional regulation directly controls locomotor kinematics by modulating stride length and velocity, while mutants with lost Ca2+ regulatory functions exhibit impaired locomotor activity. Together, our findings reveal that dTRPγ acts as an independent ion channel, integrating environmental cues with ionic dynamics to drive adaptive behavior.

title: Fe/Cu Bimetallic Particles for Trichloroacetaldehyde Dechlorination: From Parameter Effects to Reusable Catalysis with Mechanistic Insights
summary: Abstract Iron/copper (Fe/Cu) bimetallic particles have demonstrated high activity for the dechlorination of trichloroacetaldehyde (TCAL). To enhance the dechlorination efficacy, a systematic evaluation of key operational parameters—such as
content: Abstract Iron/copper (Fe/Cu) bimetallic particles have demonstrated high activity for the dechlorination of trichloroacetaldehyde (TCAL). To enhance the dechlorination efficacy, a systematic evaluation of key operational parameters—such as chelator concentration, bimetal dosage, copper loading, and initial pH—is essential. The Fe/Cu bimetallic composites were synthesized and applied under optimized conditions (25 g/L Fe/Cu, EDTA/Cu molar ratio of 1:10, 1% Cu loading, initial pH 8). The materials were characterized before and after reaction using SEM-EDS, XRD, and XPS. Reaction intermediates were analyzed by gas chromatography with a micro electron capture detector (GC-μECD) to propose a degradation pathway. Under optimal conditions, a high TCAL removal rate of 98.18% and a dechlorination efficiency of 38.70% were achieved within 48 hours. Material characterization confirmed an iron-core structure with surface-deposited copper, which facilitated synergistic galvanic corrosion and improved surface reactivity. The degradation was attributed to hydrogen radicals (H•), the reducing power of Fe⁰ and Fe²⁺, and the adsorption by iron oxides (Fe₂O₃ and FeOOH). The Fe/Cu catalyst exhibited excellent recyclability over five cycles, and the degradation kinetics followed a pseudo-first-order model.

title: Maize–potato intercropping enhances aggregate stability and AMF diversity in red soils of Southern China
source: Soil Science Society of America Journal
summary: Abstract Background and Aims Enhancing the stability of soil aggregates can slow down soil erosion. However, the stabilization mechanisms of soil aggregates under different planting patterns and growth stages of maize ( Zea mays L.) and pot
content: Abstract Background and Aims Enhancing the stability of soil aggregates can slow down soil erosion. However, the stabilization mechanisms of soil aggregates under different planting patterns and growth stages of maize ( Zea mays L.) and potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.), specifically in relation to the role of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF), remains limited in the southwest region of China. The major objective of this study was to determine the changes of soil nutrient content, enzyme activity, glomalin-related soil protein (GRSP) content, AMF community and characteristics of soil aggregates and their interrelationship under different planting patterns and growth stages of maize and potato. Methods A long-term positioning experiment commenced in 2018. Three treatments of maize monoculture, potato monoculture and maize-potato intercropping were established. Non-rhizosphere soil samples were collected at three distinct growth stages for each crop: for maize, these stages were jointing (T1), tasseling (T2), and maturity (T3); for potato, the stages were seedling (T1), peak flowering (T2), and maturity (T3). The analysis focused on changes in soil nutrient content, GRSP content, enzyme activity, and characteristics of soil aggregates. Additionally, the AMF community in both rhizosphere and non-rhizosphere soils was analyzed during the T2 stage of maize and potato. Results The results showed that: (1) Across crop growth periods, the mean weight diameter ( MWD ) of non-rhizosphere soil was highest under maize and potato intercropping at T2 (1.02), followed by potato intercropping at T3 (0.98). (2) Compared with monoculture, the intercropping of maize and potato significantly enhanced the activities of urease (URE), invertase (INV), and catalase (CAT) in the rhizosphere soils of both crops at the T2 stage. Meanwhile, this intercropping pattern also increased the proportion of soil aggregates > 2 mm and the MWD in the non-rhizosphere soils of the two crops, with the magnitude of these improvements ranged from 10.98% to 88.84%. Additionally, potato intercropping increased the relative abundance of unclassified_f__Gigasporaceae and Gigaspora , as well as the Shannon index of the AMF community in rhizosphere soil at T2 stage. (3) During the T2 period, the activities of INV and CAT in rhizosphere soil was significantly higher than in non-rhizosphere soil of maize monoculture and potato intercropping. Conclusion Redundancy analysis revealed the following key finding: During the T1 stage, environmental factors had no significant effect on the stability of non-rhizosphere soil aggregates. At T2, INV, Gigaspora and Diversispora were the primary drivers of non-rhizosphere soil aggregate stability, while CAT and Diversispora dominated the regulation of rhizosphere soil aggregate stability. In the T3 stage, total glomalin-related soil protein (T-GRSP) and CAT were the main factors affecting non-rhizosphere soil aggregate stability. Further structural equation mode

title: Enhancing feasibility of cost-optimal energy systems in surrogate-assisted design optimization
summary: Energy system design optimization often incurs high computational cost, which limits applications such as uncertainty analysis and interactive decision support. Surrogate models reduce this cost by emulating expensive original models. In su
content: Energy system design optimization often incurs high computational cost, which limits applications such as uncertainty analysis and interactive decision support. Surrogate models reduce this cost by emulating expensive original models. In surrogate-assisted design optimization (SADO), an upper-level optimization algorithm searches over designs while surrogate models emulate operational optimizations to evaluate each design. Existing SADO studies rarely enforce feasibility, defined here as the ability of an energy system to satisfy all demand constraints.This study quantifies how the choice of a feasibility predictor influences the cost and feasibility of designs obtained from SADO applied to a convex energy system model. We compare three feasibility predictors: two artificial neural networks and a convex hull predictor that classifies feasibility by membership in a feasible input space. We embed each predictor into SADO and evaluate predicted designs by their cost and feasibility when re-evaluated in the operational optimization.The results show that the feasibility predictor strongly affects both cost and feasibility of designs. SADO with neural-network-based feasibility predictors achieves feasible designs consistently only if oversizing is enforced. In contrast, SADO with the convex hull predictor yields guaranteed feasible designs by construction and produces designs whose objective values are typically within 2 % of the cost-optimal solution. This improved feasibility comes at the expense of increased computational cost compared to neural-network-based feasibility predictors. Overall, these results establish feasibility prediction as a critical design choice in SADO and identify geometric feasibility predictors as robust alternatives to data-driven surrogate models for convex energy system models.

title: Organic Electrochemical Transistor Arrays With Integrated Lipid‐Sealed Femtolitre Chambers For Simultaneous Electrical and Optical Detection of Membrane Protein Activity
summary: ABSTRACT We report a scalable method for fabricating arrays of fifty‐two ion‐sensitive PEDOT:PSS organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) on glass coverslips, each incorporating an integrated fluoropolymer microwell sealed with a lipid b
content: ABSTRACT We report a scalable method for fabricating arrays of fifty‐two ion‐sensitive PEDOT:PSS organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) on glass coverslips, each incorporating an integrated fluoropolymer microwell sealed with a lipid bilayer for simultaneous electrical and fluorescence microscopy studies of membrane proteins. The architecture addresses a key limitation of existing OECT arrays by providing every transistor with an independent fluid reservoir sealed by its own isolated segment of lipid bilayer, thereby confining membrane protein diffusion to a defined sensing region. Microwells containing a dye‐labeled 50 mM KCl solution were sealed with lipid bilayers and overlaid with a dye‐free 100 mM KCl solution. Following addition of α‐hemolysin, formation of heptameric pores enabled K + ions to diffuse into the microwells and dye molecules to diffuse out, producing concurrent decreases in transistor conductance and fluorescence intensity. This integrated platform combines electrical and optical readout within independently addressable sensing sites and provides a versatile, scalable foundation for larger transistor arrays and the investigation of diverse membrane proteins reconstituted into lipid bilayers.

title: Modular Biofabrication of Functional Skeletal Muscle Incorporated with Endothelialized Microvascular Seed‐Derived Lumenized Microvessels
summary: The clinical translation of engineered skeletal muscle (eSM) for volumetric muscle regeneration is hindered by the challenge of establishing a functional vascular network capable of sustaining its high metabolic demand and ensuring graft su
content: The clinical translation of engineered skeletal muscle (eSM) for volumetric muscle regeneration is hindered by the challenge of establishing a functional vascular network capable of sustaining its high metabolic demand and ensuring graft survival. Here, we present a bottom-up biofabrication strategy to generate a pre-vascularized in vitro eSM model through the modular assembly of independently matured muscle and vascular compartments. C2C12 myoblasts were encapsulated within core-shell fibers using rotary wet-spinning (RoWS), yielding anisotropically aligned, multinucleated, and contractile myofibers expressing myosin heavy chain and sarcomeric α-actinin. In parallel, gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)-based microvascular seeds (µVS), pre-endothelialized with human umbilical vein endothelial cells, were engineered to guide rapid and structurally stable vascular formation while preventing uncontrolled capillary self-organization. Fully endothelialized µVS were incorporated into a pro-angiogenic bioink and processed via RoWS to generate tubular vascular fibers with physiological diameters (100-200 µm) and continuous CD31-positive lumens. After independent maturation, muscle and vascular constructs were bioassembled into a hierarchically organized tissue and co-cultured. By decoupling myogenic and angiogenic differentiation, this strategy overcomes medium incompatibility typical of conventional co-cultures, preserving compartment-specific architecture and function and establishing a versatile platform for muscle-vascular modeling and translational muscle repair.

title: Layer-by-layer water filling in molecular-scale capillaries monitored by AFM
summary: Abstract Under ambient humidity, water spontaneously condenses in pores only a few nanometers in size, making nanoscale capillarity central to numerous natural phenomena and technological applications. At these dimensions, water may no long
content: Abstract Under ambient humidity, water spontaneously condenses in pores only a few nanometers in size, making nanoscale capillarity central to numerous natural phenomena and technological applications. At these dimensions, water may no longer be treated as a continuous fluid, yet the consequences of molecular discreteness for capillary condensation and filling remain poorly understood. Here we study two-dimensional (2D) nanocapillaries fabricated by van der Waals assembly and, using atomic force microscopy (AFM), monitor their wall deformations during humidity-driven water uptake. We observe two distinct regimes: layer-by-layer filling of flexible capillaries and abrupt filling of more rigid ones. Flexible walls deform in ≈3 Å steps, consistent with the entry of individual molecular layers of water. The different filling regimes are explained by a competition between wall deformation energy and oscillatory wall-water interactions. These results, together with the theoretical framework developed here, show how molecular discreteness can profoundly affect ubiquitous capillary phenomena, with wall rigidity determining whether this discreteness is exposed or hidden within an apparently classical, Kelvin-like response.

title: Strategic heteroatom doping enhances the sensitivity of covalent organic frameworks for ciprofloxacin detection
summary: Abstract Ciprofloxacin water pollution from poor waste management poses serious ecological and public health risks. In this research, we investigated the adsorption capacity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) doped with heteroatoms such
content: Abstract Ciprofloxacin water pollution from poor waste management poses serious ecological and public health risks. In this research, we investigated the adsorption capacity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) doped with heteroatoms such as nitrogen, phosphorus, sulfur, and silicon to enhance their ability to adsorb ciprofloxacin. Using density functional theory (DFT) with the ꞷB97XD/6-311G(d) level of theory. This study included structural analysis, electronic properties, spectral analysis, topological studies, and adsorption energy investigations to provide a comprehensive understanding of the COF-ciprofloxacin interaction. The results revealed that the bare COF was strongly chemisorbed with ciprofloxacin, with an adsorption energy of -1.088 eV. Conversely, doping COFs with nitrogen alone or in combination with sulfur and silicon significantly improved chemisorption, with adsorption energies of -1.116 eV, (N-COF-CFN) -1.415 eV, (N-COF-S-CFN), and − 1.687 eV (N-COF-Si-CFN). These findings suggest that specific heteroatom doping can significantly enhance the adsorption capacity of COF for ciprofloxacin.

title: Heterogeneous Decarbonization: Technology-Specific Renewable Shocks and Asymmetric Emissions Responses Across the Global Economy
summary: Abstract Climate policy often assumes that renewable energy deployment produces similar emission reductions across countries, despite major differences in grid flexibility and fuel substitution capacity. Using the GTAP-E-Power computable ge
content: Abstract Climate policy often assumes that renewable energy deployment produces similar emission reductions across countries, despite major differences in grid flexibility and fuel substitution capacity. Using the GTAP-E-Power computable general equilibrium framework calibrated to eight global regions and twenty-two sectors, together with panel data for 59 countries from 2000 to 2023, this paper examines how technology-specific renewable shocks affect emissions, production, and welfare. The results reveal a heterogeneous rebound problem in which developing economies with rigid grids experience emissions declines of 16–33% through output contraction, while advanced economies substitute toward fossil generation, producing rebound effects of up to 39% under solar shocks. Solar shocks generate the strongest rebounds, while firm zero-emission baseload contractions intensify coal substitution. Demand-side efficiency policies generate substantial welfare gains but impose negative spillovers on trade-exposed regions. Fixed-effects and Bayesian Ridge methods consistently confirm a robust emissions-reducing effect of renewable energy deployment, with a fixed-effects elasticity of -0.30 and a Bayesian Ridge posterior mean of -0.40. JEL Classification: Q43 , Q53 , Q58 , F18 , C68

title: Sequential preparation of styrene/vinyltriethoxysilane-derived precursors for hybrid and porous materials
summary: Abstract Converting sequence-prepared copolymer precursors into hybrid and porous materials remains challenging because alkoxysilane condensation can reduce structural definition during isolation and processing. Here, styrene/vinyltriethoxy
content: Abstract Converting sequence-prepared copolymer precursors into hybrid and porous materials remains challenging because alkoxysilane condensation can reduce structural definition during isolation and processing. Here, styrene/vinyltriethoxysilane (VTES)-derived precursors were prepared by sequential anionic polymerization and transformed into polysiloxane-containing hybrids by acid-catalyzed sol–gel treatment. FTIR and SEC/GPC of the soluble fraction are consistent with incorporation of VTES-derived units, although the isolated products are better regarded as operational sequential precursors than as rigorously defined diblock copolymers. After acid treatment, SAXS, SEM, TGA, DSC, and ²⁹Si MAS NMR indicate weakly ordered nanostructured hybrids with short-range compositional correlations, multiscale heterogeneity, and extensively condensed T²/T³ silsesquioxane environments. Exploratory post-treatments showed moderate porosity after calcination of the 1:1 hybrid (51.7 m² g⁻¹) and substantially higher surface area after carbonization of the 7:3 hybrid followed by HF etching (561.9 m² g⁻¹). These results establish the feasibility of the precursor-to-material route while showing that processing-induced condensation limits rigorous structure-property assignment.

title: Full Scan Enhanced Dynamic Range MS Improves Metabolite Coverage and Cancer Cell Line Discrimination in Untargeted Metabolomics
summary: Abstract Metabolite detection with mass spectrometry (MS) in untargeted metabolomics is limited by the wide concentration range of metabolites, where high-abundance ions can restrict the detection of low-abundance features. Full Scan enhanc
content: Abstract Metabolite detection with mass spectrometry (MS) in untargeted metabolomics is limited by the wide concentration range of metabolites, where high-abundance ions can restrict the detection of low-abundance features. Full Scan enhanced Dynamic Range (eDR) MS addresses this limitation by partitioning the MS1 mass range into multiple subscans and mass windows, reducing ion competition during accumulation. Here, we systematically evaluated different eDR acquisition strategies for untargeted metabolomics. Across four hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines, Full Scan eDR MS increased detectable compounds up to ∼3.5-fold compared with Full Scan MS and improved signal-to-noise ratios of low-abundance compounds. Among equidistant configurations, 12 windows yielded the highest compound count, while custom window distributions enabled targeted enhancement of selected mass regions. In particular, allocating narrower windows to the low-m/z region selectively increased the detection of low-mass compounds. Increased MS1 coverage also translated into deeper MS2 coverage and increased metabolite identifications. This expanded coverage included cancer-relevant metabolites and improved the detection of metabolic differences between cancer cell lines. Overall, Full Scan eDR MS provides a flexible strategy to increase analytical depth in untargeted metabolomics while maintaining data quality. Customization of window size and distribution enables targeted expansion of the dynamic range within predefined mass regions, allowing MS acquisition to be tailored to sample composition and metabolites of interest.

title: Graphene oxide with tailored low thermal conductivity by defect engineering, for thermal insulation
summary: The present study suggests a viable strategy for the development of next-generation nanomodified materials, exhibiting tunable intrinsic thermal management properties by adjustment of physicochemical aspects of graphene oxide (GO) dopants.
content: The present study suggests a viable strategy for the development of next-generation nanomodified materials, exhibiting tunable intrinsic thermal management properties by adjustment of physicochemical aspects of graphene oxide (GO) dopants. Starting from a modified Hummers-based synthesis route, two complementary defect engineering strategies were investigated for suppressing thermal transport, namely lateral size control by mechanical treatment such as ultrasonication and defect introduction by oxygen plasma. The Raman ID/IG defect index was increased with both sonication duration and oxygen plasma exposure, confirming the progressive introduction of structural defects. Hybrid treatments yielded synergistic enhancements in the defect index, with values reaching 20% higher than the as-synthesized nanocarbon. Thermal conductivity, measured under the Transient Plane Source configuration exhibited plausible reductions in value, of ca. 26%, comparable with the value measured for an independent graphene oxide variant, stemming from oxidation of pristine graphene nanoplatelets. The finding demonstrates that chemical oxidation is equally effective to mechanical treatment for thermal transport suppression. While the two defect engineering pathways operate through distinct and complementary mechanisms, namely edge-related phonon scattering for mechanical treatment and basal-plane sp³ defect introduction for chemical treatment, their synergistic combination in the hybrid approach is envisioned to achieve further reductions in thermal conductivity.

title: Correlative Operando X‐Ray Imaging and Diffraction Revealing Mechanical Failure Pathways in Lithium Metal Sulfide‐Based All‐Solid‐State Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) employing sulfide solid electrolytes and lithium metal anodes offer a promising route toward high energy density and improved safety. However, their practical implementation is hindered by coupled
content: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) employing sulfide solid electrolytes and lithium metal anodes offer a promising route toward high energy density and improved safety. However, their practical implementation is hindered by coupled electro‐chemo‐mechanical interfacial instabilities, which evolve across multiple length scales and remain poorly understood under operating conditions. Here, we present a multimodal operando characterization approach combining X‐ray computed tomography (XCT), X‐ray diffraction (XRD), and stack pressure monitoring to elucidate degradation mechanisms in LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) | Li 6 PS 5 Cl (LPSC) | Li cells. By correlating particle‐level morphology with lattice‐scale structural and strain evolution, this approach provides a unified multiscale description of interfacial degradation. Simultaneous operando XCT and XRD measurements reveal reversible ∼6% volume changes in NCM811 particles during (de‐)lithiation, while spatially resolved XRD uncovers heterogeneous lithiation and depth‐dependent electrochemical activity across the cathode. Partial relaxation of interfacial microstrain is linked to oxidative decomposition of LPSC. At the LPSC|Li interface, operando XCT visualizes crack formation, lithium infiltration, and progressive contact loss caused by plating‐induced stress, ultimately leading to mechanical disconnection and short‐circuiting at higher current densities. These mechanically induced degradation processes are partially reversible during lithium stripping. This multimodal operando framework provides critical insights into degradation pathways and design principles for mechanically robust sulfide‐based ASSBs.

title: Engineering an Enzymatically Active Granular Matrix for On‐Chip Modeling of Bone‐Like Mineralization
summary: Controlled biomineralization is central to engineering physiologically relevant hard-tissue models, yet achieving spatially organized, three-dimensional (3D) mineral deposition in microfluidic on-chip systems remains challenging. While cell
content: Controlled biomineralization is central to engineering physiologically relevant hard-tissue models, yet achieving spatially organized, three-dimensional (3D) mineral deposition in microfluidic on-chip systems remains challenging. While cell-based bone-on-chip platforms offer biological complexity, they couple mineral initiation to matrix remodeling and paracrine signaling, complicating isolation of the earliest biochemical drivers of mineralization. Inspired by bottom-up synthetic biology, we engineered an enzymatically active granular matrix that recapitulates a key osteogenic function within a perfusable 3D microenvironment. Alkaline phosphatase (ALP), the key driver of native bone formation, was covalently conjugated to poly(ethylene glycol)-based (PEG) microgels via thiol-ene photochemistry, retaining over 90% of its initial activity after 24 h. These monodisperse microgels were assembled into a jammed, perfusable matrix on-chip, enabling independent control over enzyme loading and substrate delivery. The system supported in situ mineralization (24-48 h), yielding a calcium-deficient, poorly crystalline apatite-like phase characteristic of early-stage bone mineral. We demonstrate 3D localization of enzymatic activity to the granular matrix, which, coupled with interstitial perfusion, enabled mineral formation whose spatial distribution depended on the perfusion regime. This mechanistically defined, acellular platform provides a tunable foundation for investigating ALP-driven 3D mineralization and establishes a modular route toward hybrid biosynthetic models of (patho)physiological tissue mineralization.

title: Inverse-IMPRESSION: A Graph-Based Platform for Molecular Structure Elucidation from Experimental NMR Spectroscopic Properties
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Here, we present a platform built on our inverted graph transformer network, IMPRESSION-G2, which can accurately and rapidly reconstruct molecular bonding directly from experimental nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopic in
content: Abstract Here, we present a platform built on our inverted graph transformer network, IMPRESSION-G2, which can accurately and rapidly reconstruct molecular bonding directly from experimental nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopic information. It comprises three interconnected stages: a one-shot model that reads in NMR parameters and uses these to predict bond connectivity between atoms; a structure correction stage that corrects the predicted structures by removing uncertain bonds and iteratively reassigning them; and noise-augmented multishot prediction, generating an ensemble of candidate structures, which are ranked to identify the best-fit structure. By integrating a range of 1H and 13C NMR data, including two-dimensional (2D) experiments such as COSY, HSQC, and HMBC, the inverse-IMPRESSION platform correctly identifies the structures of 77.8% of molecules with up to 30 heavy atoms (H, C, N, O, and F) using simulated NMR data, and 11 of 19 (58%) molecules using experimental NMR data. The experimental structures solved are representative of the complex structures in synthetic and natural products that routinely challenge chemists, assessed by high nSPS scores (greater than 40) for successfully elucidated structures and molecular weights of up to 480 Da. The inverse-IMPRESSION framework thus provides a highly effective approach for automated molecular structure elucidation by using graph-based machine learning on experimental data.

title: Ion-bombardment-engineered PTFE for tunable contact electrification: From enhanced triboelectricity to antistatic functionality
summary: Contact electrification plays a dual role in modern technologies, serving as the fundamental mechanism for triboelectric energy harvesting while simultaneously causing electrostatic discharge (ESD) that threatens the reliability of advanced
content: Contact electrification plays a dual role in modern technologies, serving as the fundamental mechanism for triboelectric energy harvesting while simultaneously causing electrostatic discharge (ESD) that threatens the reliability of advanced electronic manufacturing. Although fluoropolymers such as polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) are widely utilized owing to their strong tribonegative characteristics, practical strategies for continuously tuning their triboelectric behavior from charge accumulation to charge dissipation remain limited.Here, we demonstrate an ion-bombardment-assisted surface engineering approach that enables tunable control of contact electrification in PTFE through dose-dependent modification of surface chemistry and electronic structure. Nitrogen ion irradiation induces progressive defluorination and structural reconstruction of PTFE, leading to the formation of conjugated carbon domains with varying degrees of connectivity. At low ion doses, isolated conjugated domains promote triboelectric charge accumulation, resulting in a 200% enhancement of triboelectric output compared with pristine PTFE. In contrast, increasing ion dose forms interconnected conductive pathways that facilitate charge dissipation, suppressing triboelectric voltage by up to 95%. Comprehensive physicochemical analyses reveal that the transition from triboelectric enhancement to antistatic behavior originates from the evolution of conjugated carbon structures and their associated charge transport characteristics. This work establishes ion bombardment as a facile and scalable surface engineering strategy for regulating contact electrification in fluoropolymers and provides a practical platform for both electrostatic discharge mitigation and triboelectric energy-harvesting applications.

title: A statistical framework for laser-induced subsurface modification and cracking in 4H-SiC
summary: Abstract Laser slicing of 4H-SiC enables low-kerf wafer separation, but reproducible subsurface crack formation remains challengingbecause the modified layer is buried, defect-sensitive, and statistically variable. Here, nanosecond laser-in
content: Abstract Laser slicing of 4H-SiC enables low-kerf wafer separation, but reproducible subsurface crack formation remains challengingbecause the modified layer is buried, defect-sensitive, and statistically variable. Here, nanosecond laser-induced subsurfacemodification and cracking in commercial n-type 4H-SiC are described probabilistically rather than through deterministicthresholds. Incident fluence, pulse-to-pulse pitch, and focal depth below the surface were varied systematically, and image-derived outcomes were classified as modification onset, crack onset, or stable crack formation. Weibull analysis was used todescribe the probability of each outcome, while binomial confidence intervals and bootstrap resampling were used to quantifyuncertainty. Modification formed within a comparatively narrow fluence band across all tested depths and pitches. Pulse pitchemerged as the primary parameter governing the transition from modification to cracking. At smaller pitch, stable crackingbecame probable within the same fluence interval as modification, whereas at larger pitch a statistically separable fluencerange produced modification without subsequent cracking. Cross-sectional SEM supported the corresponding morphologicalprogression from void-like or elliptical modifications to wedge-like, crack-forming inclusions. This combined statistical andmorphological analysis captures both systematic parameter trends and excursions among nominally identical conditions,providing a basis for selecting more reproducible crack-forming process windows for 4H-SiC wafer slicing.

title: A strategy for synergistic photothermal-photocatalytic: contactless photocatalytic reactor for CO2 reduction with seawater or wastewater into HCOOH
summary: Abstract Herein, a synergistic photothermal-photocatalytic strategy is developed by designing a contactless photocatalytic reactor that concurrently synchronizes and enhances mass transfer while expanding the scope of usable water sources.
content: Abstract Herein, a synergistic photothermal-photocatalytic strategy is developed by designing a contactless photocatalytic reactor that concurrently synchronizes and enhances mass transfer while expanding the scope of usable water sources. Specifically, heat radiation-induced evaporation is exploited to accelerate the transport of both reactants and products, thereby relaxing the purity requirements for the water feedstock and sustaining efficient CO₂ reduction rates even with seawater and wastewater. Importantly, the diffusion rates of vaporized H₂O and CO₂ reach the same order of magnitude, effectively eliminating the mass-transfer mismatch. Under full-spectrum irradiation in a reactor with a 1 cm² irradiation area, the CO₂-to-formic acid production rates using pure water, simulated seawater, and simulated wastewater reach 680.7, 645.3, and 663.0 µmol g⁻¹ h⁻¹, respectively. This work not only demonstrates the valorization of wastewater resources but also opens a new avenue for integrated photocatalysis and photothermal conversion.

title: Co-fermentation of yeast CECA and PL09 modulates antioxidant activity, volatile and metabolic profiles of highland barley bran
summary: Highland barley bran (HBB) is a nutrient-rich by-product whose food application is limited by poor flavor and palatability. This study compared glucose-supplemented HBB fermented for 24 h with CECA, PL09, or their 1:1 mixed culture using HS
content: Highland barley bran (HBB) is a nutrient-rich by-product whose food application is limited by poor flavor and palatability. This study compared glucose-supplemented HBB fermented for 24 h with CECA, PL09, or their 1:1 mixed culture using HS-SPME-GC–MS and untargeted metabolomics. Among the fermented treatments, CP24 showed the highest total phenolic and flavonoid colorimetric indices, while its in vitro DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities reached 30.37% and 54.98%, respectively. CP24 also exhibited a distinct VOC profile, with isoamyl acetate and ethyl hexanoate reaching eOAVs of 30.96 and 38.60, respectively, although their sensory contributions require validation. Metabolomics identified 42 and 227 differential metabolites relative to C24 and P24, and correlation analysis revealed statistical associations between selected metabolites and VOCs. These findings characterize the treatment-dependent chemical and metabolic differences in fermented HBB and support its further evaluation in cereal foods.

title: Advancements in optical fiber coatings and functionalization for chemical and biological sensing applications
summary: Recent advances in optical fiber engineering have enabled the transformation of conventional fibers into sophisticated platforms for chemical and biological sensing. Innovations in coating technologies-incorporating polymers, metals, nanopa
content: Recent advances in optical fiber engineering have enabled the transformation of conventional fibers into sophisticated platforms for chemical and biological sensing. Innovations in coating technologies-incorporating polymers, metals, nanoparticles, and hybrid nanocomposites, have significantly enhanced light-matter interactions at the fiber interface, thereby improving analytical sensitivity and performance. Polymeric coatings provide chemical tunability and mechanical flexibility, while metallic films enable plasmonic-based refractive index sensing with high responsiveness. In parallel, the integration of nanoparticles and nanocomposite materials introduces tailored optical properties and multifunctional behavior, expanding the capabilities of fiber-based sensing systems. Complementary surface functionalization strategies, including self-assembled monolayers and molecular imprinting have further advanced the field by enabling the controlled immobilization of biorecognition elements such as enzymes, antibodies, and aptamers. These approaches confer high selectivity and stability, facilitating the development of next-generation optical fiber sensors for the detection of gases, volatile organic compounds, biomarkers, pathogens and genetic targets. This review summarizes recent progress in coating materials, surface functionalization methods, and optical transduction mechanisms for fiber-optic chemical and biological sensors. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationship between coating morphology, sensing performance, and practical challenges including coating instability, signal drift, reproducibility, and operation in complex sample environments. Emerging trends in distributed sensing and artificial intelligence-assisted signal processing are also discussed as promising directions for next-generation intelligent optical fiber sensing systems.

title: Light Alkali Metal Functionalized Two‐Dimensional C 5 N Monolayers for Enhanced Hydrogen Storage
summary: This work presents a comprehensive computational investigation of a novel two‐dimensional (2D) organic carbon nitride (C 5 N) monolayer for hydrogen (H 2 ) storage applications. Van der Waals‐corrected density functional theory calculations
content: This work presents a comprehensive computational investigation of a novel two‐dimensional (2D) organic carbon nitride (C 5 N) monolayer for hydrogen (H 2 ) storage applications. Van der Waals‐corrected density functional theory calculations reveal that pristine C 5 N interacts weakly with H 2 molecules, thereby limiting its storage capability. To address this limitation, the C 5 N monolayer is functionalized with light alkali metals M (M = Li, Na, and K) to enhance its adsorption performance. Energetic analysis demonstrates that C 5 N can stably accommodate up to six metal dopants, with average binding energies of −2.88, −1.84, and −1.80 eV per dopant for Li, Na, and K, respectively. These values are significantly stronger than the corresponding cohesive energies of the dopants, thus preventing metal aggregation. The thermal stability of the functionalized systems is confirmed through ab initio molecular dynamics simulations at 300 K. Electronic structure and charge analysis, based on projected density of states and Bader charge calculations, indicate charge transfer values of 0.99, 0.99, and 0.85 electrons per dopant from Li, Na, and K to the C 5 N monolayer, respectively. This charge transfer leads to enhanced polarization, reduced bandgap, and improved H 2 adsorption performance. Each metal dopant can adsorb up to eight H 2 molecules, leading to a maximum storage capacity of 48 H 2 molecules per unit cell. The corresponding gravimetric densities are 9.42, 8.61, and 7.93 wt% for the Li‐, Na‐, and K‐functionalized C 5 N systems, respectively, with moderate average adsorption energies (−0.16 to −0.17 eV/H 2 ) that are suitable for reversible H 2 storage. Thermodynamic analysis under practical fuel‐cell operating temperature and pressure conditions further confirms the favorable H 2 adsorption/desorption behavior of the functionalized C 5 N systems. The reversibility of the designed materials is evaluated through desorption temperature and recovery time calculations, indicating efficient H 2 release kinetics. In addition, volumetric storage performance is assessed through density‐to‐volume ratio analysis. Overall, these results highlight alkali metal‐functionalized C 5 N monolayers as promising candidates for efficient and reversible H 2 storage applications.

title: Advanced modeling of the mechanical behavior of natural fiber-reinforced earthen bricks: A second-order gradient theory approach
summary: Flax fiber-reinforced earthen bricks offer a sustainable alternative to conventional masonry but exhibit complex mechanical behavior due to their heterogeneous microstructure. This study addresses this challenge by combining experimental th
content: Flax fiber-reinforced earthen bricks offer a sustainable alternative to conventional masonry but exhibit complex mechanical behavior due to their heterogeneous microstructure. This study addresses this challenge by combining experimental three-point bending tests with a multiscale numerical framework based on gradient elasticity theory. We first implement first-order gradient elasticity using Code\_Aster and an in-house FFT-based code to compute the effective stiffness tensor $\mathbb{A}^{0,0}$. This approach yields relative errors of 3\% and 4\% for bricks reinforced with 16 and 64 long fibers, respectively, compared to experimental data. To improve accuracy, we extend the framework to second-order gradient elasticity, incorporating size effects and non-local interactions through higher-order tensors $\mathbb{B}^{0,1}$ and $\mathbb{C}^{0,0}$. The refined model reduces relative errors to below 0.1\%, demonstrating its robustness in capturing microstructural phenomena. Our findings confirm that second-order gradient theory significantly enhances predictive accuracy for fiber-reinforced composites and validate the potential of flax-reinforced earthen bricks as eco-friendly construction materials.

title: AKARI near-infrared spectroscopy of circumstellar hydrocarbon dust associated with young stellar objects
source: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
summary: Abstract We investigate the processing of the circumstellar polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) associated with young stellar objects (YSOs) through their stellar activities. We analyze the AKARI near-infrared (2.6–4.4$\, \mu {\rm m}$ )
content: Abstract We investigate the processing of the circumstellar polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) associated with young stellar objects (YSOs) through their stellar activities. We analyze the AKARI near-infrared (2.6–4.4$\, \mu {\rm m}$ ) long-slit spectral data of 10 YSOs, focusing on the aromatic feature at a wavelength of 3.3$\, \mu {\rm m}$ and the aliphatic features at 3.4–3.6$\, \mu {\rm m}$. The spectral fitting results show large variations from target to target in the flux ratio of the aliphatic to aromatic features, the shape of the aliphatic feature profile, and the central wavelength of the aromatic feature. In particular, ${\rm HD}\,\,97048$ and Elias 1 show strong aliphatic features at wavelengths longer than 3.5$\, \mu {\rm m}$, which is consistent with the hydrogenated nanodiamond features reported in previous studies. We find that the properties of the hydrocarbon dust vary under the influence of the YSO activity, where the degree of dust processing is likely to be related to the age of the YSO and the amount of the circumstellar dust. In addition, correlation is observed between the variations of the H$_2$O and CO$_2$ ice features and the aliphatic feature profiles, suggesting connection between the formation of CO$_2$ ice and the processing of aliphatic hydrocarbons. Finally, we find a significant correlation between the variations in the central wavelength of the aromatic feature and the shape of the aliphatic feature profile. These findings may be consistent with a tentative scenario in which circumstellar PAHs are converted to nanodiamonds through irradiation by high-energy particles produced by YSO activity.

title: Solid-State, Rapid Mechanochemical Pathway for Zinc Phthalocyanine-Embedded Schiff-Base Polymer-TiO2 Nanocomposite for LED Assisted Efficient Photochemical Remediation of Hexavalent Chromium
summary: Abstract The processing and elimination of heavy metals and toxic components from water is indispensable due to its potentially hazardous and carcinogenic impacts on the well-being of people and the environment. Successful heavy metals and
content: Abstract The processing and elimination of heavy metals and toxic components from water is indispensable due to its potentially hazardous and carcinogenic impacts on the well-being of people and the environment. Successful heavy metals and toxic components mitigation ensures adequate water quality for consumption, prevents ingestion in to living organisms, and limits the contamination of the environment. The present work details the development of a zinc phthalocyanine based polymeric Schiff-Base encapsulated TiO 2 (ZnPc_SB@TiO 2 ) nano-composite via solid-state, mechanochemical pathway for the effective photochemical remediation of Cr(VI) in the presence of energy efficient LED as source of visible light. To comprehensively understand the structure, size, morphology, and optical properties of the newly synthesized photoactive materials, they were subjected to Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and Solid-state diffuse reflectance spectrophotometer characterization. The photoreduction of Cr(VI) was carried out under the impact of a 100 W LED as visible light source to investigate the photocatalytic competence of TiO 2 and ZnPc_SB@TiO 2 . The implications of several factors on the photocatalytic performance, such as photocatalyst dosage, interaction time, pH of the medium, and photocatalyst re-usage, are investigated. The photocatalytic activity for Cr(VI) photochemical remediation was found to be 88% for ZnPc_SB@TiO 2 where as TiO 2 alone exhibited less than 10%. The findings suggested that photosensitization of TiO 2 with ZnPc_SB significantly boosted photocatalytic activity for Cr(VI) photochemical remediation.

title: Bidentate Click-Functionalized Thermoplastic Polyurethane for Modular Immobilization of PEGylated Compounds: Mirabegron as a Proof-of-Concept
summary: Abstract Thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) is widely used in the development of biomedical devices, due to its excellent physicochemical properties; however, its chemical inertness limits its application in drug-immobilization systems. Here,
content: Abstract Thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) is widely used in the development of biomedical devices, due to its excellent physicochemical properties; however, its chemical inertness limits its application in drug-immobilization systems. Here, we report the development of a postfabrication “TPU-click platform” utilizing a novel bidentate polyethylene glycol (PEG) linker [N-(aminooxy-PEG2)-N-bis(PEG3-propargyl)]. To ensure biomedical suitability, surface activation was achieved using a nontoxic bismuth-based catalyst. The bidentate architecture provides dual orthogonal alkyne sites, enabling the copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) of complex molecules with enhanced theoretical payload capacity and versatility. Mirabegron was selected as a representative molecule to demonstrate the platform’s versatility. Surface modification was confirmed using multiple characterization techniques. ATR-FTIR spectroscopy revealed characteristic bands associated with isocyanates (2260–2270 cm−1), alkyne groups (2200–2500 cm−1), and ether bonds (1000–1100 cm−1). XPS (C 1s, N 1s, and O 1s) showed changes in surface elemental composition consistent with successful functionalization. SEM revealed variations in surface topography, while water contact angle values increased from 75.6° ± 1.04 to 122.58° ± 5.17, indicating a transition in wettability behavior attributable to changes in surface chemistry. Finally, the antioxidant capacity (59.67 ± 4.46 Trolox equivalents) supported the chemical feasibility of immobilizing PEGylated mirabegron and a broad range of PEGylated therapeutic molecules on TPU. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report describing a TPU-click platform employing a bidentate PEG linker and Mirabegron PEGylation. This platform opens new opportunities for the development of drug-functionalized biomedical devices.

title: Deliverable 2.1 – Recycling Technologies and Resulting Products
source: Organic Eprints (International Centre for Research in Organic Food Systems, and Research Institute of Organic Agriculture)
summary: The objective of this deliverable was to provide an up-to-date overview on NRTs, including information on resource streams, processing steps and resulting products as a basis for discussing which nutrient inputs can be compatible with organ
content: The objective of this deliverable was to provide an up-to-date overview on NRTs, including information on resource streams, processing steps and resulting products as a basis for discussing which nutrient inputs can be compatible with organic farming. A database with 218 entries covering 14 classes of resource streams and 14 NRT classes was compiled based on the Fertitec project, a catalogue provided by the European Sustainable Phosphorus Platform and additional products from other projects. Elements considered important for the acceptability in organic farming such as process type, additives, nutrient solubility and carbon preservation were included in addition to information on raw material, process steps, chemical composition and pollutants. The compilation includes NRTs applicable to agricultural waste streams, by-products from food processing as well as municipal wastes. The different NRT classes and process types showed trade-offs between nutrient recovery, carbon preservation and contaminant removal. This compilation of NRTs can now be used to discuss the priorities in case of conflicting principles.

title: Facile green synthesis of Cu₂O nanoparticles using Azadirachta indica extract and evaluation of their activity against Staphylococcus aureus
summary: Copper(I) oxide (Cu₂O) nanoparticles were synthesized using Azadirachta indica (neem) leaf extract as a reducing and stabilizing agent. Previous reports on neem-mediated synthesis have mainly dealt with CuO or metallic Cu nanostructures; bu
content: Copper(I) oxide (Cu₂O) nanoparticles were synthesized using Azadirachta indica (neem) leaf extract as a reducing and stabilizing agent. Previous reports on neem-mediated synthesis have mainly dealt with CuO or metallic Cu nanostructures; but the present study targets the Cu₂O phase and evaluates its activity against Gram-positive bacterium, Staphylococcus aureus . The synthesis was carried out in water at 60 °C without using any toxic chemicals. The nanoparticles were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), UV-Vis spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis. XRD indicated crystalline cubic Cu₂O, UV-Vis spectroscopy showed a broad absorption maximum at 601 nm (about 2.06 eV), and SEM showed agglomerated particles made up of nanoscale primary particles. Activity against S. aureus was evaluated by the disc diffusion method. The nanoparticles resulted in increased zones of inhibition with concentration (2.5 ± 0.2, 2.7 ± 0.05 and 2.9 ± 0.15 mm at 0.5, 1 and 2 mg/mL, respectively), when compared with 2.5 ± 0.1 mm for tetracycline (10 µg) and no inhibition for the negative control (0.5% DMSO). The comparison with tetracycline was qualitative. Overall, the study presents a simple green route to synthesis of Cu₂O nanoparticles that inhibit S. aureus in vitro; and findings of antibacterial activity and its possible scope for related use.

title: Role of bio-polymeric binders on combustion and fire suppression performance of KNO3/KClO4–3,5 DNB pyrotechnic composite
summary: Traditional pyrotechnic composites (PCs), often synthesized with epoxy or other synthetic binders, can combust at temperatures up to ​ 2100 °C, creating secondary fire and explosion risks. This study examines how renewable, cost-effective b
content: Traditional pyrotechnic composites (PCs), often synthesized with epoxy or other synthetic binders, can combust at temperatures up to ​ 2100 °C, creating secondary fire and explosion risks. This study examines how renewable, cost-effective binders: starch, guar gum, tannic acid, and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose affect the combustion behavior, exothermicity, temperature profiles, and fire-suppression performance of PCs in a 4.57 kW n-heptane pool fire. Characterization of the aerosol particulates was performed using XRD, FTIR, and SEM. SEM-EDX and DSC for the PCs. PC-1, with a linear burning rate (LBR) of 10.05 ± 2.158 mm/s, extinguished the fire within 5 s and generated the highest ignition temperature (210 °C), whereas PC-4 and PC-5 with LBRs of 9.3 ± 0.742 mm/s and 9.7 ± 0.693 mm/s, respectively showed a noticeable decrease in ignition temperatures (184 °C and 182 °C, respectively) and suppressed the fire within 7 s and 5 s, respectively. It can be concluded that starch-based PC exhibited optimal fire performance parameters, making it a promising bio-based binder for the KNO 3 -KClO 4 -3, 5 DNB pyrotechnic composition.

title: A Novel Fe3O4-Coated Activated Carbon Catalyst for Drinking Water Disinfection and Toxic Disinfection Byproduct Control
summary: Abstract Traditional drinking water disinfectants such as chlorine not only deactivate pathogenic microorganisms in source water but also react with dissolved organic matter (DOM) from natural and anthropogenic sources, leading to the forma
content: Abstract Traditional drinking water disinfectants such as chlorine not only deactivate pathogenic microorganisms in source water but also react with dissolved organic matter (DOM) from natural and anthropogenic sources, leading to the formation of numerous toxic halogenated disinfection byproducts (DBPs). The strong oxidants generated through catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) by iron oxide (Fe3O4) are proposed to reduce dissolved organic carbon (DOC), a DBP precursor, as well as to disinfect pathogens in drinking water treatment. This study aims to synthesize a novel Fe3O4-coated granular activated carbon (GAC) catalyst enabling simultaneous removal of DOC in water, mitigation of the formation of toxic halogenated DBPs such as trihalomethanes (THMs), and disinfection of waterborne pathogens. The experimental results demonstrated that synthesized Fe3O4-GAC enables us to effectively catalyze the rapid decomposition of H2O2 (7 times faster than Fe3O4 alone), reduce DOC (53%), limit THM formation (below the detection limit), and inactivate E. coli (>99.9%) in water. This research demonstrates that Fe3O4-GAC has high potential to be used as a green, cost-effective catalyst for drinking water treatment.

title: A mMono-Bac1.0 system for recombinant adeno-associated virus vectors with higher flexibility, throughput and yield
summary: Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) holds immense promise for therapeutic applications, but high production costs limit its widespread clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for manufacturing breakthroughs. Here, we establish a mo
content: Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) holds immense promise for therapeutic applications, but high production costs limit its widespread clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for manufacturing breakthroughs. Here, we establish a modular Mono-Bac system with the p24 -NanoLuciferase (Nluc) reporter Bacmid for rAAV production, named mMono-Bac1.0, enhancing manufacturing flexibility, throughput and yield simultaneously. The system introduces two key technology to the pFD/Cap-(ITR-GOI)-Rep transfer vector-based Mono-Bac framework. First, a modular pGB-AAV Donor construction strategy enables one-step all-in-one AAV transfer vector assembly and effortless switching of capsids or GOIs, thus facilitating high-throughput combinatorial production. Second, an engineered p24 -Nluc Bacmid enables rapid (<5 min) quantification of infectious recombinant baculovirus (rBV) titers and real-time monitoring of Nluc activity in culture supernatants to determine the optimal harvest point (log RLU ~ 6.5), thereby maximizing rAAV yield. This system has the potential to advance baculovirus expression vector (BEV)-based rAAV manufacturing into a data-driven era, supporting efficient industrial-scale production.

title: Zinc Chloride–Polyethylene Oxide Gel Polymer Electrolytes for Wearable and Flexible Energy Storage Applications
summary: ABSTRACT We prepared and evaluated the properties of hydrated ZnCl 2 ‐Polyethylene oxide (PEO) gel polymer electrolyte (H‐GPE) for flexible electrochemical capacitors (FEC). The FEC was developed using the H‐GPE and a multi‐layer graphene s
content: ABSTRACT We prepared and evaluated the properties of hydrated ZnCl 2 ‐Polyethylene oxide (PEO) gel polymer electrolyte (H‐GPE) for flexible electrochemical capacitors (FEC). The FEC was developed using the H‐GPE and a multi‐layer graphene sheet as an electrode for wearable and flexible energy storage applications. The electrochemical performance of the fabricated H‐GPEs with different ZnCl 2 :PEO ratios were evaluated. Three compositions, namely 60:40, 70:30, and 80:20 wt.%, were investigated and denoted as FEC1, FEC2, and FEC3, respectively. Among these, the FEC2 sample exhibits comparatively higher specific capacitance (7.374 µF.cm −2 ) values compared to FEC1 (5.840 µF.cm −2 ) and FEC3 (2.280 µF.cm −2 ) at a current density of 0.2 µA.cm −2 . The device developed with 70% ZnCl 2 exhibited the highest specific capacitance among the tested compositions, indicating the most favorable overall electrochemical behavior, consistent with the combined FTIR and electrochemical results. Further, the electrochemical performance of FEC2 is examined at various temperatures (−10 to 50°C), and it reveals that the specific capacitance of FEC increases with temperature. The mechanical flexibility studies show that the current response decreases as the bending angle increases, from 30° to 180°. The observed performance reveals the possible application of this H‐GPE along with new active electrode materials in FEC devices for low‐powered electronics.

title: Integrated recovery of rare earth elements and transition metals from spent NiMH batteries
summary: Abstract Spent nickel-metal hydride batteries are concentrated secondary resources rich in transition metals (TM) and critical rare earth elements (REE). This study compares two integrated hydrometallurgical routes exploiting different solu
content: Abstract Spent nickel-metal hydride batteries are concentrated secondary resources rich in transition metals (TM) and critical rare earth elements (REE). This study compares two integrated hydrometallurgical routes exploiting different solution chemistries: (i) sulfuric-acid leaching followed by bulk REE precipitation and (ii) methanesulfonic-acid (MSA) leaching followed by targeted oxidative removal of Ce. In the sulfate route, TM dissolution was favored (approximately 98% Ni at 60 °C), whereas REE extraction remained within approximately 40–60% over the investigated temperature range. La extraction further decreased to approximately 42% at 3 mol.L −1 H 2 SO 4 , consistent with the limited solubility of REE sulfate species. Following leaching and pH adjustment, the precipitation percentages of La, Ce, and Nd exceeded 98%. In the MSA route, the high solubility of metal methanesulfonates prevented this sulfate related limitation and enabled approximately 95–99% extraction of La, Ni, and Co at 60 °C, together with near-complete La dissolution at a 1/30 g.mL −1 solid-to-liquid ratio. Subsequent addition of 6 vol.% H 2 O 2 at pH 4 resulted in 94% Ce removal, consistent with selective oxidative precipitation, while most other metals remained predominantly in solution. The sulfate route therefore introduces TM–REE selectivity during leaching and enables collective REE recovery, whereas the MSA route prioritizes comprehensive dissolution and postpones selectivity to a targeted downstream step. These results show that the preferred route depends on the desired product streams: early group separation and bulk REE recovery, or near-complete metal dissolution followed by Ce-first separation.

title: Tree species composition and nutrient uptake influence soil nutrient availability, even under contrasted levels of water availability
summary: Temporal asynchrony within a vegetation period, such as when mixing trees with contrasting leaf phenology (i.e. deciduous and evergreen species), may play an important role in accelerating belowground nutrient cycling in mixed-species fores
content: Temporal asynchrony within a vegetation period, such as when mixing trees with contrasting leaf phenology (i.e. deciduous and evergreen species), may play an important role in accelerating belowground nutrient cycling in mixed-species forests. However, forests are increasingly impacted by drought, and how mixing effects may be modified by changes in water availability is unknown. Using an 11-year-old experimental plantation in southwestern France, we tested the interactive effect of stand composition (monocultures of each Pinus pinaster and Betula pendula, and the mixture of the two species) and water availability (via irrigation) on various belowground processes.
