We quantified soil nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) availability with ion-exchange resins in the growing vs dormant periods, net mineralization with an in situ soil incubation method every 4-6 weeks from April to September, and N uptake by trees using two in situ 15 N soil labeling campaigns, one at budburst and one at peak leaf expansion in summer. The methods were implemented at several time points, in order to elucidate potential temporal complementarity in the mixture. We found differences in soil nutrient availability between different species compositions, with pure pine generally having higher mineral N, and pure birch having higher available P under high water availability. These differences were unlikely due to increases in net nutrient mineralization, as these rates were similar among treatments. Instead, differences in tree growth and canopy covering between species compositions, and thus different nutrient uptake needs may be the main drivers for the soil nutrient availability trends. The 15 N labeling experiment revealed a competitive advantage for pine in the mixture at budburst, with higher N uptake than pine in monocultures, without negatively impacting birch uptake. This advantage was then lost once birch's leaves were out in the early summer. We conclude that the timing of nutrient needs and uptake of species within a mixture, such as between a broadleaf deciduous and an evergreen conifer, may be a stronger driver than mineralization for soil nutrient availability in a mixture, even under two contrasted levels of water availability.

title: Skin-mimetic adaptive gradient electrode for ambulatory noninvasive brain-computer interfaces
summary: Noninvasive brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) need stable, comfortable electrodes for long-term wear. Current rigid or uniformly soft electrodes suffer from scalp mismatch, causing motion artifacts and short operation times. Inspired by huma
content: Noninvasive brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) need stable, comfortable electrodes for long-term wear. Current rigid or uniformly soft electrodes suffer from scalp mismatch, causing motion artifacts and short operation times. Inspired by human skin’s gradient structure, we created a skin-mimetic adaptive gradient electrode (AGE). Based on the Marangoni effect, we induced heterogeneous crosslinking in the hydrogel within a gradient temperature field. This yields an electrode with a gradual stiffness change—soft at the scalp interface and firm at the circuit connection—along with a gradient pore structure for sustained electrolyte release. This design enabled stable, high-quality EEG recording for over 8 h during free movement and over 14 h at rest, maintaining >94% typing accuracy. This work demonstrated the potential of gradient-designed hydrogels toward noninvasive BCIs in freely moving practicality.

title: Urban ecological resilience in the digital era: the role of data factor marketization and spatial spillovers
summary: As data becomes an increasingly important production factor in the digital economy, its role in shaping environmental outcomes has attracted growing attention. This study examines how data factor marketization affects urban ecological resil
content: As data becomes an increasingly important production factor in the digital economy, its role in shaping environmental outcomes has attracted growing attention. This study examines how data factor marketization affects urban ecological resilience. Using a spatial difference-in-differences model and panel data from 282 Chinese cities between 2010 and 2022, we find that data factor marketization significantly enhances ecological resilience and generates positive spatial spillovers, although these effects are mainly concentrated within a relatively short geographic range. The effect operates through three main pathways: green innovation, efficient resource allocation, and industrial upgrading through digital transformation. The results also reveal substantial heterogeneity: eastern and western cities benefit more than central ones, and resource-based cities respond more strongly, likely due to their stronger demand for structural transformation. In addition, cities with stronger digital foundations derive greater ecological benefits from the reform, highlighting the conditioning role of digital development in shaping policy effectiveness. These findings advance understanding of how data factor allocation supports environmental adaptation and underscore the importance of digital infrastructure and institutional capacity. Policy efforts should prioritize data institutionalization, digital inclusion, and targeted support for digitally lagging and resource-dependent cities to better translate data reforms into ecological gains.

title: Bioprocessing of Damaged Wheat Grain Into PHB Using Lactobacillus Fermentation Following Optimized Acid Hydrolysis
summary: ABSTRACT This study establishes a sustainable strategy for poly(3‐hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) biosynthesis by utilizing damaged wheat grain (DWG) as an alternative, non‐food agro‐industrial substrate. The integrated approach involves the systema
content: ABSTRACT This study establishes a sustainable strategy for poly(3‐hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) biosynthesis by utilizing damaged wheat grain (DWG) as an alternative, non‐food agro‐industrial substrate. The integrated approach involves the systematic optimization of HCl‐mediated hydrolysis followed by microbial fermentation using Lactobacillus species. Hydrolysis parameters, including time, acid‐to‐sample ratio, HCl concentration, and substrate loading, were evaluated to maximize reducing sugar (RS) release while suppressing the formation of fermentation inhibitors. Optimal nutrient recovery was achieved at 45 min, 20% w/v acid‐to‐sample ratio, 6% w/v HCl, and 20% w/w substrate loading, yielding 336.66 ± 1.14 mg glucose equivalent/g RS and 4.67% ± 0.07% w/w protein. Under these optimized conditions, inhibitory concentrations of acetic acid, formic acid, furfural, and 5‐HMF were effectively restricted to 2.36, 6.95, 0.49, and 1.17 mg/g, respectively. Subsequent fermentation of the refined hydrolysate by a consortium of Lactobacillus plantarum , Lactobacillus murinus , and Lactobacillus casei was conducted. At 30°C with a 6% inoculum level over 96 h, FH12 achieved a maximum PHB titer of 1.85 ± 0.42 g/L. These results demonstrate the potential of converting low‐value agro‐wastes into biopolymers via optimized lactic acid bacteria fermentation, providing a viable pathway for circular bioeconomy applications.

title: Interaction effects between fungi and hydrogel antifungal coating under microgravity-induced diffusion limitation
summary: The long-term performance of antifungal coatings in microgravity is critical for spacecraft applications, yet how altered mass transport regulates fungus–coating interactions and coating degradation remains unclear. Here, a hydrogel antifun
content: The long-term performance of antifungal coatings in microgravity is critical for spacecraft applications, yet how altered mass transport regulates fungus–coating interactions and coating degradation remains unclear. Here, a hydrogel antifungal coating (SDM) on aluminium alloy coupons was evaluated against Aspergillus brasiliensis during a 90-day parallel experiment conducted aboard the China Space Station (CSS) and under ground conditions. We reveal that microgravity-induced diffusion limitation does not simply enhance or suppress antifungal performance but reshapes fungus–coating interfacial interactions. Restricted transport reduced fungal colonisation, while incomplete hydration-layer formation under microgravity resulted in a lower anti-biofilm adhesion rate (52.83%) than that under ground conditions (57.44%). Meanwhile, fungal stress adaptation increased organic acid production, but limited interfacial transport reduced the accumulation and action of corrosive metabolites, mitigating coating degradation. Consistent with this mechanism, chemical structure analysis showed attenuated carbonyl-related degradation signals in space-exposed coatings, whereas ground coupons exhibited more pronounced structural deterioration. These findings reveal a diffusion-controlled mechanism governing the antifungal and degradation behaviour of functional coatings under microgravity.

title: Acceleration of Hydrogen Evolution Reaction via Tuning Plasmon Mode
summary: This chapter demonstrates that HER rate can be systematically modulated by engineering the optical mode of periodic Ag disk arrays fabricated on glassy carbon substrates by electron beam lithography. FDTD simulations confirmed that SLR mode
content: This chapter demonstrates that HER rate can be systematically modulated by engineering the optical mode of periodic Ag disk arrays fabricated on glassy carbon substrates by electron beam lithography. FDTD simulations confirmed that SLR modes produce a spatially delocalized electric field across the periodic array, distinct from the highly localized LSPR field, with multi-order polariton modes emerging depending on structural geometry. Reflectance spectroscopy under 75 MPa validated the calculated optical modes and confirmed structural stability during HER. A video-based bubble analysis method was developed to quantify local HER rates, revealing that structures supporting SLR modes resonant with the relevant potential region exhibit significantly enhanced reaction rates. These findings establish a direct correlation between specific polariton modes and electrochemical reactivity, providing rational design guidelines for polariton-enhanced catalysis on non-catalytic electrodes.

title: Amphiphilic block co-polymer infused bismuth vanadate as an adsorbent for azo-rubine dye: Synthesis, characterization and application studies
summary: Dye pollution is one of the major concern in this modern society. This communication aims to synthesize a high-functionality adsorbent for the detoxification of discharged dyes. Here we report, a polymeric material derived from a kind of am
content: Dye pollution is one of the major concern in this modern society. This communication aims to synthesize a high-functionality adsorbent for the detoxification of discharged dyes. Here we report, a polymeric material derived from a kind of amphiphilic block co-polymer (stearylmethacrylate -b- acryl amide) infused Bismuth Vanadate (BiVO 4 ) prepared on the basis of SET-LRP method, which makes the water free from such kind of toxic material by simple binding. Well-defined amphiphilic block copolymer was effectively synthesized via living radical polymerization (LRP) on the surface of stearyl methacrylate (SMA) possessing hydrophilic groups as monomer in presence of Copper(0) as catalyst. The process exhibited characteristics of a controlled radical polymerization, as indicated by the linear kinetic plot of versus conversion, despite some loss of chain-end control at higher conversions. The amphiphilic block copolymer was successfully synthesized and generally characterized by GPC and in addition, TGA, 1 H NMR provides confirmational evidence for the synthesized block copolymer. The results indicate that the polymeric material immobilized with different % of BiVO 4 displayed excellent sorption capacity for the specific organic dye. Contact angle measurements provide additional evidence for the wettability and sorption. The high initial removal capacity of the organic dye is primarily facilitated by the hydrophobic domains of the polymer matrix, while electrostatic interactions and π–π* stacking between the dye and the polymer functional groups may also serve as secondary contributing factors. Results demonstrated that the polymer-infused BiVO₄ exhibited significantly improved adsorption performance compared to pristine BiVO₄, owing to synergistic interactions between the inorganic matrix and amphiphilic polymer chains.

title: Metabolic cascades drive spatial prebiotic fermentation in a defined gut consortium
summary: Dietary fiber deficiency shifts the gut microbiota to degrade host mucus, compromising intestinal homeostasis. Mechanistically linking in vitro metabolic dynamics of fiber degradation to in vivo outcomes remains challenging due to a lack of
content: Dietary fiber deficiency shifts the gut microbiota to degrade host mucus, compromising intestinal homeostasis. Mechanistically linking in vitro metabolic dynamics of fiber degradation to in vivo outcomes remains challenging due to a lack of representative model systems. Introducing spatial mucin structures to a defined Oligo-Mouse-Microbiota (OMM12) in vitro consortium allowed us to recapitulate the spatio-temporal dynamics of xylooligosaccharide (XOS) processing in gnotobiotic mice. XOS supplementation rapidly established a stable community state in vitro and in vivo across compositional, metabolic and transcriptional levels. XOS supplementation established distinct functional guilds: Bifidobacterium animalis and Blautia coccoides partitioning xylose and arabinose catabolism, whilst profiting from XOS degradation by Bacteroides caecimuris. Along the colonic axis, a spatial XOS gradient exposes Bl. coccoides's substrate preference for xylose and drives longitudinal functional adaptations. Altogether, our predictive platform proves that regional microenvironments govern prebiotic efficacy, highlighting spatial cascades as essential parameters for targeted microbiome interventions.

title: Enhanced Flame Retardancy and Mechanical Properties of Thermoplastic Vulcanizate by a Multi‐Piperazine/Melamine Vinylphosphonate System
summary: ABSTRACT To meet the dual demands for flame retardancy and mechanical performance of thermoplastic vulcanizate (TPV), two vinylphosphonate‐containing flame‐retardant products, designated as tris(vinylphosphonate salt) of phenylsilane tris(p
content: ABSTRACT To meet the dual demands for flame retardancy and mechanical performance of thermoplastic vulcanizate (TPV), two vinylphosphonate‐containing flame‐retardant products, designated as tris(vinylphosphonate salt) of phenylsilane tris(piperazine) (NV) and melamine vinylphosphonate (MV), were prepared and combined to construct an intumescent flame‐retardant system. NV and MV were compounded at different mass ratios, and the 6NV/4MV ratio showed the most favorable overall flame‐retardant performance. At a loading of 24 wt.% (6NV/4MV), the modified TPV exhibited an LOI value of 26.5% and achieved UL‐94 V‐0 ratings at both 3.2 and 1.6 mm thicknesses. Cone calorimeter tests showed substantial reductions in peak heat release rate, peak smoke production rate, total heat release, and total smoke production, together with an increased char residue. SEM‐EDS analysis indicated enhanced retention of phosphorus‐containing species in the condensed phase and the formation of a relatively compact char layer for the 6NV/4MV formulation. At 20 wt.% loading, the tensile strength and elongation at break of 6NV/4MV/TPV increased by 27.5% and 8.3%, respectively, compared with neat TPV. FTIR analysis revealed that the C = C‐related absorption band nearly disappeared after thermal processing, indicating thermally induced changes in the unsaturated groups. This change may have contributed to partial crosslinking among the components. Overall, compositional regulation of the binary NV/MV system provided a favorable balance among flame retardancy, mechanical‐property retention, and durability under water exposure.

title: Cell Spreading-Enhanced Electron-Transfer Electrochemical Cytosensor Enabling Single-Cell Detection
summary: Achieving single-cell detection with electrochemical cytosensors remains challenging, owing to a poor understanding of how electroactive redox probes generate measurable signals near large, insulating cells. Here, we validate a cell–electro
content: Achieving single-cell detection with electrochemical cytosensors remains challenging, owing to a poor understanding of how electroactive redox probes generate measurable signals near large, insulating cells. Here, we validate a cell–electrode interfacial electron-transfer effect, in situ visualizing that the measurable current signal originating from redox probes located at the cell–electrode adjacent interface, rather than from those distributed on the cell surface. Notably, cell spreading enlarges this cell-adjacent interface, thereby enabling effective current amplification. Guided by this effect, we design an integrated cytosensor platform that combines a highly conductive lamellar reduced graphene oxide (RGO)/Ti3C2Tx electrode chip, which facilitates lamellipodia-driven cell spreading, with a high peroxidase-activity FeCN single-atom nanozyme. This platform exhibits a 7.6-fold signal enhancement over conventional chips and a detection limit of 0.03 cells mL−1, allowing a resolvable current response from a single cell on the 2 cm2 large-sized chip. Furthermore, it demonstrates potential feasibility for clinical detection of circulating tumor cells, achieving 96% specificity and 87% sensitivity across 55 blood samples in distinguishing cancer patients from healthy controls. This work establishes a cell spreading-enhanced electron-transfer paradigm and advances electrochemical cytosensing toward high-performance liquid biopsy applications. Electrochemical cytosensors have emerged as powerful tools for single-cell analysis, but generating robust signals from individual cells remains a major challenge. The authors uncover a cell-electrode interfacial electron-transfer effect, in which only redox probes at the cell-electrode interface contribute to measurable currents. Exploiting this mechanism, they develop a cell spreading-enhanced electron-transfer (SEET) cytosensor and apply it to circulating tumor cell detection in 55 patient samples, achieving 96% specificity and 87% sensitivity.

title: In Situ Assembled Carboxyl‐Functionalized Hexaazatrinaphthylene Enables Accelerated Li + Transport and Localized FEC Enrichment in Silicon Anodes
summary: ABSTRACT Rational interfacial regulation is critical to resolving the structural instability of high‐performance silicon (Si) anodes for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). Here, a molecular interphase engineering strategy based on hexaazatrinaph
content: ABSTRACT Rational interfacial regulation is critical to resolving the structural instability of high‐performance silicon (Si) anodes for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). Here, a molecular interphase engineering strategy based on hexaazatrinaphthylene tricarboxylic acid (HATNTA), a carboxyl‐functionalized derivative of hexaazatrinaphthylene (HATN), is proposed to regulate the interfacial chemistry of Si anodes. The π‐conjugated framework provides abundant polar nitrogen sites (C═N) that may facilitate Li + coordination. The carboxyl groups incorporated into HATNTA enable localized fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) enrichment, thereby steering the interfacial reaction pathway toward the formation of a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). The resulting interphase suppresses excessive electrolyte decomposition and mitigates electrode swelling and structural degradation during prolonged cycling. The Si‐HATNTA anode achieves an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 92.56%. It exhibits a rate capability of 1122 mAh g −1 at 5 A g −1 and maintains 1341 mAh g −1 after 200 cycles at 1.0 A g −1 . The NCM811//Si‐HATNTA full cell retains 70.49% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles at 0.2 C. This work provides a molecular design strategy for stabilizing Si anodes through interfacial chemistry regulation.

title: Spatial multi-omics of mouse incisor mesenchyme reveals metabolic remodeling during the MSC-to-TAC transition
summary: The continuously growing mouse incisor provides a useful model for investigating stem cell niche organization and the MSC-to-TAC transition because it contains spatially distinct mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-enriched and transit-ampl
content: The continuously growing mouse incisor provides a useful model for investigating stem cell niche organization and the MSC-to-TAC transition because it contains spatially distinct mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-enriched and transit-amplifying cell (TAC)-enriched compartments and abundant TAC populations. However, the metabolic programs associated with MSCs and their transition to TACs within the native tissue environment remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated region-resolved transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics with single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize metabolic remodeling associated with the MSC-to-TAC transition in the mouse incisor pulp. We found that the MSC-enriched apical pulp was enriched for molecular features associated with fatty acid β-oxidation and ketone body metabolism, whereas the TAC-enriched mitotic pulp showed molecular signatures associated with the tricarboxylic acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation, and nucleotide biosynthesis. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed lower mRNA-protein concordance in the MSC-enriched apical pulp, consistent with a contribution of post-transcriptional regulation, whereas the TAC-enriched mitotic pulp showed tighter mRNA-protein coupling. Metabolite profiling further showed higher abundance of acyl-carnitines and ketone bodies in the MSC-enriched apical pulp and higher abundance of glutamine, aspartate, and purine intermediates in the TAC-enriched mitotic pulp. Pseudotime analysis suggested coordinated changes in transcriptional programs related to fatty acid oxidation, mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, and nucleotide synthesis along an MSC-to-TAC trajectory. Collectively, our study establishes a region-resolved multi-omics atlas of metabolic remodeling associated with the MSC-to-TAC transition in the mouse incisor and provides insights into the metabolic features associated with stem cell activation, progenitor expansion, and tissue homeostasis in the native dental stem cell niche.

title: Submission to EPBC portal 26 Oct 2026, re Woodside's proposed sub-marine CCS storage Environmental Impact Statement.
summary: ABSTRACT: This submission highlights that Woodside company neglected (apparently on purpose) to model for the impact of a condensed CO2 spill at their proposed "carbon capture" and processing plant near to Scott Reef complex, or from their
content: ABSTRACT: This submission highlights that Woodside company neglected (apparently on purpose) to model for the impact of a condensed CO2 spill at their proposed "carbon capture" and processing plant near to Scott Reef complex, or from their proposed extensive pipeline CO2 transport network. Despite this omission, they are preparing an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS). Such an EIS, without reference to this specific modelling would be inadequate and invalid. Furthermore, Australia's government, despite some pretence of being environmentally responsible, has to date failed to include endangered coral species on the EPBC Act list, which may appear to let them off the hook when it comes to responsibilities regarding offshore mining and carbon capture and storage (CCS) projects. This submission focuses on the impacts that a major CO2 spill or a series of lesser spills would have in the vicinity of Scott Reef, in particular looking at the impact of the resulting plume(s) of carbonic acid on coral species, including numerous critically endangered species (including EPBC Act-listed species), and on biodiversity and marine species in general, including many vulnerable, endangered and critically endangered species (including numerous EPBC Act-listed species). It then calculates the volume and likely movement (and therefore spread) of CO2 that Woodside has claimed it will store beneath the sea, which is likely to lead to spills. In truth, very little is known about the aquifer where it is claimed CO2 would be stored, other than, for instance, it is said to have a smaller capacity volume than the total amount of CO2 planned for the site, and is said to be full of salt water. In contact with CO2, the water steadily becomes carbonic acid; this at any concentrated strength, has a corrosive effect on corals, reef structures, the sea floor, and a fatal effect on all local species, whether plant or animal. Even in a much diluted strength, it would contribute substantially to ocean acidification. Factors such as the seismic activity in the region, subsidence which would occur in conjunction with gas extraction, and the risks to the reefs and to species from a CO2 spill at or near the storage site, or an oil spill, compound the problem. Scott Reef complex is a biodiverse, relatively pristine reef system, that includes a number of rare and endangered corals and other species. Along with the nearby Serangapatam Reef, it is among Australia's 17 recognised reef systems, and has recently been given (as of October 2026) a Critically Endangered ecosystem listing with the IUCN's Red List. Alternative methods for retaining atmospheric carbon include cultivation of sea-grass meadows, afforestation and reafforestation of biodiverse forests, the use of trickle-through semi-permeable dams along sloped water courses in arid and semi-arid regions, and avoiding emissions in the first place.

title: Quantifying opportunities of reducing 2 footprint of dairy farms with different on-site renewable generation and regional 2 grid mix
source: Strathprints: The University of Strathclyde institutional repository (University of Strathclyde)
summary: Dairy farms have been increasing their reliance on electric machinery such as vacuum pumps and water heaters in the milking parlours, resulting in increased energy demand and increased carbon footprint [3]. To reduce their carbon emissions
content: Dairy farms have been increasing their reliance on electric machinery such as vacuum pumps and water heaters in the milking parlours, resulting in increased energy demand and increased carbon footprint [3]. To reduce their carbon emissions and ensure compliance with future net zero policies [2], accurate measurement of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions is essential. This paper aims to support how the farms should be categorising and quantifying their carbon footprint output via reassessing the values from national scale to regional.

title: Land-use change CO2 emissions (ELUC) data for the Global Carbon Budget 2026
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Description This dataset provides estimates of net land-use change CO2 emissions (ELUC) and their component fluxes from the three bookkeeping models used in the Global Carbon Budget 2026 (GCB2026): BLUE (Hansis et al., 2015), LUCE (Qin et a
content: Description This dataset provides estimates of net land-use change CO2 emissions (ELUC) and their component fluxes from the three bookkeeping models used in the Global Carbon Budget 2026 (GCB2026): BLUE (Hansis et al., 2015), LUCE (Qin et al., 2024), and OSCAR (Gasser et al., 2020). Peat drainage emissions are from FAO (Conchedda and Tubiello, 2020), LPX-Bern (Lienert and Joos, 2018; Müller and Joos, 2021), and ORCHIDEE-PEAT (Qiu et al., 2021), and peat fire emissions are from GFED5.1 (van der Werf et al., 2025). The dataset further includes the data underlying Figure 8 of GCB2026, including estimates from national greenhouse gas inventories (NGHGIs) and atmospheric inversions. The dataset also includes global and gridded estimates of the environmental contribution to ELUC (δL), which is the difference in ELUC between a simulation with transient carbon densities and a simulation with pre-industrial carbon densities. The reported net ELUC estimates already include the environmental contribution (δL). Net ELUC and its component fluxes are available as global and national annual time series for 1850–2025. Net ELUC is also available as gridded annual time series (0.25° resolution) for 1959–2025. The data describe CO2 emissions and removals expressed as mass of carbon (C). For ELUC and its component fluxes, positive values denote emissions and negative values denote removals. The sign convention for δL is explained below. Empty cells in .xlsx files denote missing values. The dataset contains 20 files: One .xlsx file with global estimates for BLUE, LUCE, and OSCAR (units: PgC/yr = GtC/yr) Fourteen .xlsx files with country-level estimates for BLUE, LUCE, and OSCAR, one for each of the net and component fluxes listed below (units: TgC/yr) Two NetCDF files with gridded net ELUC estimates for BLUE and LUCE (units: tC/ha/yr, referring to total grid-cell area) One .xlsx file with the data underlying Figure 8 of GCB2026 (units: PgC/yr = GtC/yr) One .xlsx file with the global estimates of the environmental contribution to ELUC (δL) (units: PgC/yr = GtC/yr) One NetCDF file with the gridded estimates of the environmental contribution to ELUC (δL) (units: tC/ha/yr, referring to total grid-cell area) Global, country-level, and gridded data The dataset includes the following net and component fluxes. The identifiers shown in monospace are used in the corresponding country-level filenames and as worksheet names in the file with global estimates. “SC” denotes shifting cultivation, and “nonforest” refers to shrub and herbaceous vegetation: net-eluc (net ELUC): Net CO2 emissions from land-use change. clearing-allveg-total (deforestation and clearing of other vegetation (total)): Total CO2 emissions from deforestation and the clearing of shrub and herbaceous vegetation, including both permanent clearing and clearing within shifting cultivation cycles. regrowth-allveg-total ((re-)growth of forest and other vegetation (total)): CO2 removals through the growth and regrowth

title: Global Steel Decarbonization under Policy, Technology, and Resource Constraints: A Process-Unit Agent-Based Model
summary: Abstract Deep decarbonization of steel requires low-emission technologies to be deployed through a long-lived and heterogeneous asset fleet without disrupting steel supply. We developed a country-resolved agent-based model that follows glob
content: Abstract Deep decarbonization of steel requires low-emission technologies to be deployed through a long-lived and heterogeneous asset fleet without disrupting steel supply. We developed a country-resolved agent-based model that follows global steel process units annually from 2023 to 2060. Units choose among continued operation, renewal, retrofit, conversion, retirement, and new construction, subject to construction time, linked upstream capacity, national production pathways, and annual supplies of scrap, hydrogen, natural gas, and pellets. Four scenarios distinguish stronger climate policy from improved technology and resource availability. Global process-chain CO2 emissions decline by 67–79% by 2060, reaching 0.476–0.737 Gt. The integrated case achieves the lowest emissions, but the two-component interventions do not independently outperform the reference case. Stronger policy changes when assets enter a finite transition queue, whereas technology and material conditions determine whether replacement routes can be built and operated at that time. By 2060, Scrap-EAF supplies 74–80% of crude steel, but residual unabated blast furnaces and coal-based direct reduction keep national steel pathways above their allocated levels in many countries. Deep decarbonization, therefore, depends on coordinating asset turnover, construction, and complementary material systems, rather than on technology availability or carbon-price pressure alone.

title: Symmetry in Thermal Fluid Sciences and Energy Applications
summary: Symmetry is a fundamental notion in thermal-fluid sciences and energy applications and an important tool for understanding the properties of complex systems. Thermal and fluid processes are applied in several modern energy use technologies,
content: Symmetry is a fundamental notion in thermal-fluid sciences and energy applications and an important tool for understanding the properties of complex systems. Thermal and fluid processes are applied in several modern energy use technologies, basically consisting of the complex multidimensional interaction of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics. A comprehensive analysis involves vector and scalar quantities in the flow field, where symmetry is highly considered in order to simplify geometric parameters. These requirements therefore are also applied to experimental techniques, and the interconnection between experimental analysis and numerical simulation of processes is an important field. Thus, there is a wide range of symmetry solutions for this research area, the results of which contribute to the development of science and fast information for decision-making in industry.

title: Limited effect of basalt amendment and mycorrhizal inoculation on soil chemical properties and maize growth on a nutrient-rich soil
summary: Abstract Enhanced weathering (EW) of silicate minerals has emerged as a promising carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy, with potential benefits for soil fertility and crop performance. However, the soil processes that determine these co-be
content: Abstract Enhanced weathering (EW) of silicate minerals has emerged as a promising carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy, with potential benefits for soil fertility and crop performance. However, the soil processes that determine these co-benefits remain poorly constrained. In particular, interactions between basalt amendments and soil biota such as arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) may influence nutrient mobilization and plant uptake, but these effects have rarely been quantified. In a 113-day mesocosm experiment with Zea mays using a Belgian, sandy loam soil, we investigated the effect of basalt and AMF inoculation on soil properties, nutrient and heavy metal availability, and crop yield and quality. We also assessed potential AMF-driven bio-weathering via cation mass balance and pore water dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), pH, and alkalinity measurements. Basalt application, but not AMF, improved soil pH, cation exchange capacity, base saturation, and generally increased exchangeable Ca and Mg, whereas most other nutrients in the pore water remained unaffected. Crop yield and quality were largely unaltered by basalt or AMF, except for an increase in plant Mg with basalt application. Moreover, heavy metal availability and plant uptake were also generally unaffected, with the notable exception of soil pore water and corn Ni, which increased with basalt. These results suggest that risk for heavy metal contamination is not generic but may arise under specific environmental conditions. Finally, despite a synergistic effect of basalt and AMF on pore water DIC, we found no indication that AMF enhanced basalt weathering rates. Overall, AMF had limited influence on soil fertility indicators and crop performance. Basalt application improved key soil chemical indicators and increased the exchangeable fractions of Ca and Mg, demonstrating its role as a soil improver. Unlike several studies conducted in more acidic soils, these chemical enhancements did not increase maize growth here, indicating that the agronomic benefits of basalt are context-dependent.

title: Multimodal training in reconfigurable brain-inspired iontronic networks
summary: Inspired by the brain, we propose an iontronic physical alternative to traditional digital neural networks. We theoretically study microfluidic networks in which nodes are connected by conical electrolyte-filled channels that act as memrist
content: Inspired by the brain, we propose an iontronic physical alternative to traditional digital neural networks. We theoretically study microfluidic networks in which nodes are connected by conical electrolyte-filled channels that act as memristive iontronic synapses. Their electrical conductance is not only tunable via the channel geometry, but also depends on electrical, chemical, and mechanical signals. Leveraging this multimodal responsiveness, we demonstrate that small networks can be trained to perform nonlinear tasks. The network performs forward passes physically via ionic relaxation, while training combines this physical evolution with numerical gradient descent. We theoretically demonstrate that this system can perform tasks like input-output mapping and linear regression with bias. Moreover, we show that the circuit can be reconfigured to perform different objectives via adjusting the pressures on the nodes, paving the way for soft adaptable materials that compute and learn without conventional electronics.

title: Magneto-optical properties of the neutral silicon-vacancy center in diamond under extreme isotropic strain fields
summary: The neutral silicon--vacancy (SiV$^{0}$) center in diamond combines inversion symmetry with optical emission, making it a robust quantum emitter resilient to stray electric fields. Using first-principles density-functional theory, we quanti
content: The neutral silicon--vacancy (SiV$^{0}$) center in diamond combines inversion symmetry with optical emission, making it a robust quantum emitter resilient to stray electric fields. Using first-principles density-functional theory, we quantify its response to isotropic strain spanning strong compression and tensile regimes (effective hydrostatic pressures of approximately $-80$ to $180$~GPa). The coexistence of doubly degenerate $e_g$ and $e_u$ levels produces a structural instability captured by a quadratic product Jahn--Teller model. Under isotropic compression, the zero-phonon line blue-shifts nearly linearly while the $E_g$ phonon stiffens, suppressing vibronic instabilities and reducing Jahn--Teller quenching. Consequently, the Ham-reduced excited-state spin--orbit splitting increases substantially and the dark--bright vibronic gap widens. In contrast, isotropic tensile strain enhances vibronic effects and induces symmetry breaking beyond a critical strain, with tunneling-mediated dynamical averaging at the onset. Throughout the symmetry-preserving regime, parity remains well defined, so isotropic strain alone does not activate the dark transition. Charge-transition levels indicate photostability of the emission deep into the compressive regime, and near the highest photostable deformation ($\sim 100$~GPa), the radiative lifetime increases due to a reduced transition dipole moment despite the increasing optical energy. These trends yield compact calibration relations linking optical and spin observables to isotropic strain and establish SiV$^{0}$ as a symmetry-protected, strain-tunable quantum emitter operating into the multi-megabar-equivalent regime.

title: Failure Impact and Uncertainty Impact Metrics for Hybrid-Electric Turboprop Development
summary: This paper introduces two new metrics, Failure Impact (FI) and Uncertainty Impact (UI), to address the limitations of traditional evaluation methods like Technology Readiness Level (TRL) and Integration Readiness Level (IRL) in the developm
content: This paper introduces two new metrics, Failure Impact (FI) and Uncertainty Impact (UI), to address the limitations of traditional evaluation methods like Technology Readiness Level (TRL) and Integration Readiness Level (IRL) in the development of hybrid-electric turboprop aircraft. These metrics, scored on a 1-9 scale, quantify the severity of component failures and the impact of uncertainties. The study applies these metrics to a 50-passenger hybrid-electric turboprop, focusing on four critical components: battery, motor, inverter, and thermal management system (TMS). Using a Multi-Attribute Decision-Making (MADM) framework, the paper evaluates these components under four strategic scenarios: Balanced, Safety-First, Maturity-Focused, and Uncertainty-Reduction. The results from various MADM methods, including MAUT, AHP, BWM, and TOPSIS, consistently identify the battery as the highest priority for testing and resource allocation due to its high FI and UI scores. The TMS consistently ranks as the second priority. The rankings of the motor and inverter vary depending on the strategic focus, particularly under the Uncertainty-Reduction scenario. A non-compensatory method, ELECTRE III, provided a contrasting ranking by placing the battery last due to its extreme risk scores triggering vetoes. The study concludes that the Best-Worst Method (BWM) is particularly well-suited for aerospace applications due to its simplicity and consistency.

title: Projected Disc-type Phase-change Memory for Analog In-Memory Computing
summary: Abstract Resistive memory technologies offer a compelling advantage for in-memory computing. However, realizing a device architecture that simultaneously achieves high computational precision, efficiency, and density has remained elusive du
content: Abstract Resistive memory technologies offer a compelling advantage for in-memory computing. However, realizing a device architecture that simultaneously achieves high computational precision, efficiency, and density has remained elusive due to inherent trade-offs among these performance metrics. Here, we introduce a compact phase-change memory device architecture that combines an ultra-confined active switching volume for enhanced electro-thermal efficiency with a non-insulating thin film that suppresses temporal conductance fluctuations. We analytically model and back-end integrate these devices into crossbar arrays. Even with conventional, undoped phase-change materials, the device architecture enables a computational precision approaching 6 bits, low conductance values below 50 μS with an adequate conductance window, and a viable pathway toward sub-100 μA programming currents under nominal operating voltages.

title: การประเมนการกกเกบคารบอนของตนไมในพนทโรงเรยนในเมองสการเปนเมองสเขยว กรณศกษาเทศบาลเมองแมโจ จงหวดเชยงใหม

summary: This study assessed the carbon sequestration capacity and developed a comprehensive tree database for eight school sites in Maejo Municipality, Chiang Mai province, Thailand, with a total area of 97.55 rai (15.60 ha). The research employed
content: This study assessed the carbon sequestration capacity and developed a comprehensive tree database for eight school sites in Maejo Municipality, Chiang Mai province, Thailand, with a total area of 97.55 rai (15.60 ha). The research employed field inventory methods. The diameter at breast height (DBH) and height of the trees were recorded from January to April 2025. Then biomass (both aboveground and belowground) and carbon storage were evaluated based on allometric equations and carbon fraction. A geographic Information System (GIS) database was developed, and stakeholder interviews were conducted to evaluate carbon storage potential and identify management challenges. The inventory documented 1,802 trees comprising 1,383 common trees, 408 palms, and 11 bamboo clumps. Total carbon storage across all eight school sites was 427.70 tonnes of carbon (equivalent to 1,568.22 tonnes of CO2eq), yielding a carbon density of 4.38 tonnes C/rai (27.38 tonnes C/ha). This value aligns well with the international benchmark for urban educational institutions of primary and secondary schools. The study identified key management challenges, including structural risks to buildings, allergen concerns, pest management, and debris handling. The findings emphasize the need for integrated urban planning that coordinates educational institutions, municipal authorities, and community networks initiatives to optimize carbon sequestration.
