title: Regulatory risk perception and corporate financialization: evidence from China
summary: Abstract This paper investigates the effect of regulatory risk perception on corporate financialization in China. Using the method of keyword search, we quantify regulatory risk perception in China based on the text data of listed companies
content: Abstract This paper investigates the effect of regulatory risk perception on corporate financialization in China. Using the method of keyword search, we quantify regulatory risk perception in China based on the text data of listed companies’ annual reports. With the sample of Chinese A-share companies from 2011 to 2024, we find robust evidence that regulatory risk perception significantly curbs corporate financialization. Meanwhile, our results also indicate that this effect is stronger in non-SOEs (non-state-owned enterprises), firms at the maturity and decline stages, and firms with lower risk preference and lower market position. Finally, we propose that easing financing constraints, reducing corporate tax avoidance and alleviating corporate credit mismatches are plausible channels through which regulatory risk perception decreases corporate financialization. Overall, we shed light on the real effects of regulatory risk perception and the determinants of corporate financialization.

title: Modular Direct Solar-To-Green Hydrogen Innovation
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract This paper presents an innovative Modular Direct Solar-to-Green Hydrogen technology, which combines solar photovoltaic (PV) and electrolyzer functionalities in a single panel. The PV- Integrated Electrolysis (PVIE) system produces
content: Abstract This paper presents an innovative Modular Direct Solar-to-Green Hydrogen technology, which combines solar photovoltaic (PV) and electrolyzer functionalities in a single panel. The PV- Integrated Electrolysis (PVIE) system produces hydrogen directly from sunlight and water in a modular, highly efficient manner, enabling very low production cost compared to conventional approaches. Additionally, a simulated based case study will illustrate its benefits for oil terminal facilities, particularly to power remote, off-grid ship loading pumps at Single Point Mooring (SPM). This study evaluates a PV-Integrated Electrolysis (PVIE) system that merges photovoltaic and electrolytic technologies into a single panel device. When exposed to sunlight, the panel immediately generates hydrogen through the electrolysis of water. Unlike conven tional electrolyzers, which depend on grid interconnection and require significant land area, the modularity of the PVIE system enables hydrogen production at or near the point of use. To assess the effectiveness and scalability of this technology, simulation models are utilized, focusing on scenarios relevant to offshore terminals and remote locations. The analysis provides insights into how the PVIE solution addresses the demands of future markets. Conventional solar-powered electrolysis processes suffer cumulative efficiency losses due to DC/AC conversions, transmission losses, grid interfacing, and thermal losses. They also have limited Solar-to-Hydrogen (STH) conversion efficiency to just 16% with traditional approaches. These inefficiencies, combined with high capital and operational expenditures, coupled with reliance on grid electricity, make the conventional electrolysis prohibitively expensive, and result in projected green hydrogen costs exceeding USD 4/kg by 2030. Since hydrogen is a major cost component for other green transportation fuels such as Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), these products also remain financially inaccessible. In contrast, the PV-Integrated Electrolysis (PVIE) system eliminates multiple conversion stages by integrating photovoltaic generation and electrolysis at the panel level. Results indicate Solar-to-Hydrogen (STH) efficiencies exceeding 21%, representing a significant improvement over traditional design and reducing infrastructure capital expenditures. The modular, panel-based manufacturing approach reduces balance-of-plant requirements, land footprint, and grid dependency. Cost projections indicate the potential to achieve large-scale hydrogen production costs at or below USD 1/kg without subsidies, significantly improving the commercial feasibility of green hydrogen for clean fuels, energy storage, and power generation. The novel aspect of this paper is showcasing PV-Integrated Electrolysis (PVIE) architecture that enables hydrogen production wherever sunlight and water are available. title: Upstream-Integrated Microalgae Biorefinery for CO2 Utilisation and Premium Bioproduct Generation: A Market-Matched Pilot Basis
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract An abstract of record proposed a 33,000 t/yr Nannochloropsis biorefinery in the Abu Dhabi interior returning USD 85 to 100 million per year at a 12 to 16% internal rate of return. This paper reports that those figures do not hold,
content: Abstract An abstract of record proposed a 33,000 t/yr Nannochloropsis biorefinery in the Abu Dhabi interior returning USD 85 to 100 million per year at a 12 to 16% internal rate of return. This paper reports that those figures do not hold, identifies the cause as one of scope rather than estimating accuracy, and replaces the case with a market-matched basis that closes on stated conditions. The original plant was sized by its carbon target: a 60,000 t/yr carbon dioxide (CO2) utilization objective fixed biomass output near 33,000 t/yr, which fixed an eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) volume of 1,300 to 1,650 t/yr. Against a global EPA and docosahexaenoic acid supply of order 160,000 t/yr, of which algal sources contribute approximately 12,000 t/yr, that volume does not enter the premium market so much as overwhelm it. The surplus falls to feed parity, where revenue of USD 21 to 48 million per year cannot cover operating expenditure of USD 50 to 55 million, still less USD 150 to 300 million of installed capital. A carbon-utilization target constrains a design; it cannot size one. Scale offers no relief, because cultivation cost scales with cultivation area at an exponent of unity and amortizing costs saturate by approximately 10 ha. The correction is grade and volume rather than size. A market-matched basis of 3,000 t/yr of dry biomass on 38 to 48 ha is developed to the same maturity, producing two products only: a polar-lipid EPA oil for the nutraceutical market and a defatted protein meal. Installed capital is USD 26 to 64 million, annual operating cost USD 6.8 to 11.7 million, and revenue USD 10.0 to 13.5 million, carried at a cooling duty this paper shows to be a lower bound. The case returns capital at a commercially meaningful rate above approximately 5.5% EPA of dry weight, a value above the 4 to 5% reference range for the genus but inside the 5 to 7% reported for screened high-EPA isolates, unmeasured for the thermotolerant strain this site requires, and dependent on holding the culture nutrient-replete. Establishing it is the primary objective of the staged program proposed here.

title: Integrated MMV Baseline Deployment for Co2 Storage in the UAE: Enabling Site Certification, Risk Management and Carbon Crediting
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract The deployment of Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) at commercial scale requires robust Measurement, Monitoring, and Verification (MMV) programs to establish pre-injection conditions, support storage assurance, and demonstrate the l
content: Abstract The deployment of Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) at commercial scale requires robust Measurement, Monitoring, and Verification (MMV) programs to establish pre-injection conditions, support storage assurance, and demonstrate the long-term containment of injected CO2. This paper presents the development and implementation of a comprehensive MMV baseline program for a geological CO2 storage site in Abu Dhabi, UAE. The baseline program was designed using a risk-based approach and integrated atmospheric, groundwater, and passive seismic monitoring systems to characterize environmental and subsurface conditions prior to CO2 injection. The monitoring network was deployed across a remote desert environment and supported by a vendor digital platform for data acquisition, quality assurance, traceability, and long-term data management. Initial baseline datasets were generated to establish reference conditions and capture natural variability, providing the foundation for future anomaly detection, storage performance assessment, and containment verification throughout the storage lifecycle. A key component of the program was the consolidation of diverse monitoring datasets into a unified digital ecosystem, enabling standardized workflows, metadata management, cross-disciplinary data integration, and audit-ready traceability. By integrating environmental, geophysical, and operational datasets within a single framework, the platform supports efficient data traceability and auditability, facilitates regulatory reporting, and provides a transparent basis for independent verification and certification activities. The project demonstrated that effective MMV implementation requires more than the deployment of monitoring technologies alone. Successful delivery depended on risk-based monitoring design, proactive stakeholder engagement, close coordination with technology vendors, and operational flexibility to address deployment challenges associated with a remote desert operating environment. The experience confirms that MMV baseline acquisition should commence during the early stages of CCS project development to ensure adequate characterization of natural conditions prior to injection. The integrated monitoring and digital traceability framework established through this program provides a scalable and auditable model for future CCS projects, supporting storage assurance, regulatory compliance, certification readiness, and emerging carbon market requirements across the UAE and wider region.

title: ESG Ratings and Corporate Sustainable Growth Under Financing Constraints: A Dual-Route Mechanism of Green Technological Innovation and Resource Improvement
summary: Under China’s dual-carbon and high-quality development goals, this study examines whether and how third-party ESG ratings are associated with corporate sustainable growth, defined as the internally financeable growth rate of Higgins. Using
content: Under China’s dual-carbon and high-quality development goals, this study examines whether and how third-party ESG ratings are associated with corporate sustainable growth, defined as the internally financeable growth rate of Higgins. Using 25,683 firm-year observations of Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2022 and Huazheng ESG ratings, of which only seven of the nine levels (C to A) are observed, we estimate a moderated mediation model (Hayes Model 21). A one-level rating upgrade is associated with a 1.42 percentage-point-higher sustainable growth rate (1.69 points when profitability controls mechanically linked to the dependent variable are excluded), and a one-standard-deviation increase corresponds to 10.5% of the standard deviation of the growth rate. The association holds under instrumental-variable estimation, propensity-score matching, firm fixed effects and alternative measures. Green technological innovation, measured by green patent applications, partially mediates the relationship, but the indirect effect (0.0020) accounts for only 14.2% of the total effect; supplementary tests suggest that lower financing costs and reduced operating and crash risks are potential complementary channels behind the direct effect. Financing constraints weaken the first stage of the green technological innovation route, whereas a stronger market competitive position strengthens the second stage; the conditional indirect effect under low constraints and a strong position (0.0029) is 2.25 times that under the opposite conditions. The associations are stronger for non-state-owned, growth-stage and heavily polluting firms. The findings are consistent with a dual-route view in which ESG ratings relate to sustainable growth through both an innovation route and a resource-improvement route, each with distinct boundary conditions.

title: Harmonizing Repeated Multi-Platform Optical and LiDAR Observations for Continental-Scale Terrestrial Carbon Cycle Data Assimilation.
summary: Accurate monitoring of terrestrial carbon has attracted considerable attention due to the impacts of rapid climate change, disturbance, and land use on carbon storage and the growth of new global carbon markets and reporting requirements. W
content: Accurate monitoring of terrestrial carbon has attracted considerable attention due to the impacts of rapid climate change, disturbance, and land use on carbon storage and the growth of new global carbon markets and reporting requirements. While uncertainties in C estimates remain nontrivial, crucial opportunities exist to reduce uncertainty by rigorously harmonizing models and monitoring through data assimilation (DA). LiDAR has received considerable attention for its potential to inform carbon monitoring, and while there have been a number of papers on how to initialize models using LiDAR data, it has yet to be integrated into DA systems. In this study, we integrate GEDI LiDAR into an established DA system that already assimilates optical observations of aboveground biomass (AGB) and leaf area index (LAI), microwave soil moisture (SM), and ground-based soil organic carbon (SOC) to constrain C cycling processes across the entire North American continent. Notably, this is the first time both optical and LiDAR AGB products have been iteratively harmonized within a DA system. Results show that by assimilating both optical and LiDAR observations, we reduced the uncertainty in woody biomass by 63.7% relative to unconstrained model simulations and 18% relative to our previous DA system, and achieved an average RMSE reduction of 38.3 kg/m2 across five AGB products. Importantly, LiDAR reduces DA biases in high AGB regions where optical AGB estimates were exhibiting saturation. Analysis further identified the leading factors driving spatial error patterns within the DA system to be data quality, cloud coverage, and elevation. Overall, by bridging the spatial and temporal limitations of individual satellite products, this approach offers a practical, generalized workflow for high-resolution terrestrial carbon MRV in complex, dynamic ecosystems.

title: The Impact of Executives’ Overseas Background on Corporate ESG: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Companies
summary: Within the dual background of the “dual carbon” strategy and the standardized development of ESG in capital markets, exploring the driving mechanisms of corporate ESG performance is crucial, for promoting the sustainable operation of listed
content: Within the dual background of the “dual carbon” strategy and the standardized development of ESG in capital markets, exploring the driving mechanisms of corporate ESG performance is crucial, for promoting the sustainable operation of listed companies. This research takes Chinese A-share listed companies, from 2009 to 2023, as the research sample and, empirically analyzes the impact of executives’ overseas background on corporate ESG performance, based on upper echelons theory. The findings are concluded as follows: executives’ overseas background can boost a company’s overall ESG score, and remains valid after a series of robustness tests; mechanism tests indicate that executives’ overseas background can enhance corporate governance, thus improving corporate ESG performance; heterogeneity analysis indicates that this effect is more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, mature enterprises, and enterprises with lower levels of green innovation. This research provides empirical evidence for enterprises to optimize management configuration and improve ESG governance.

title: Analysis of Influencing Factors of Electric Vehicle Purchase Intention based on Product Attributes and Market Environment
summary: In order to achieve green and low-carbon development and energy structure transformation, China promoted the development of electric vehicles (EVs) greatly and implemented a series of policies to stimulate the consumption of the EV market.
content: In order to achieve green and low-carbon development and energy structure transformation, China promoted the development of electric vehicles (EVs) greatly and implemented a series of policies to stimulate the consumption of the EV market. Existing studies focus on the impact of consumers’ perception on purchase intention mostly. Based on product attributes and market environment, this study analyses the sales situation and product characteristics of EVs in China in 2026 through One-Way Analysis of Variance (One-Way ANOVA) and Quantile Regression model (QR model), covering 500 samples. There are significant differences in sales between different brands, and the type of EV and whether there are government incentives do not have a significant impact on purchase intention. The number of charging stations and energy consumption have a significant impact on low sales vehicles and medium sales vehicles separately, and there exists heterogeneity. Battery capacity, vehicle range, charging time, average EV price, market adoption rate, and CO2 reduction have little impact on purchase intention, which shows that the explanatory power of product parameters and market environment declines.

title: Unmasking the Impacts of Monetary Policy Rate, Reserve Requirements, Open Market Operations, and Liquidity Ratio on Financial Stability in the Nigerian Banking Sector
summary: This study examines the dynamic relationship between monetary policy instruments and financial stability in the Nigerian banking sector over the period 1992–2024. Specifically, it investigates the relationships between the monetary policy r
content: This study examines the dynamic relationship between monetary policy instruments and financial stability in the Nigerian banking sector over the period 1992–2024. Specifically, it investigates the relationships between the monetary policy rate (MPR), cash reserve ratio (CRR), open market operations (OMO), and liquidity ratio (LRA), using the banking-sector Z-score as a proxy for financial stability and controlling for money supply relative to gross domestic product (M2/GDP) and the exchange rate (EXR). The study employs the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) framework to examine short-run dynamics and long-run relationships. The reported unit-root test results indicate a mixture of I(0) and I(1) variables, supporting the suitability of the ARDL approach, provided that no variable is integrated of order two. The bounds-test results indicate a long-run relationship across the four model specifications, with F-statistics of 5.873 for MPR, 4.925 for CRR, 4.381 for OMO, and 5.104 for LRA, all exceeding the reported 5% upper critical bound of 4.35. The reported long-run estimates show positive and statistically significant associations for MPR and OMO, whereas CRR is statistically insignificant and LRA has a negative and statistically significant coefficient. Money supply relative to GDP is positive and significant in the CRR and OMO specifications, while the exchange rate has negative and statistically significant coefficients in the MPR and LRA specifications. In the short run, changes in MPR and OMO are positively associated with financial stability, while changes in LRA and the exchange rate exhibit negative associations in their respective models; CRR is statistically insignificant. The error-correction coefficients are negative and statistically significant across all four specifications, indicating adjustment towards the estimated long-run relationships. Preliminary diagnostic tests do not identify significant residual normality, serial-correlation, functional-form or heteroscedasticity problems at the 5% level. However, the CUSUMSQ results for the OMO model indicate unusual residual behaviour around 2001 that warrants further investigation. The findings suggest that the estimated relationships between monetary policy instruments and banking-sector stability differ across specifications. Nevertheless, the absence of the original estimation dataset and workfile means that these results require reconstruction and independent verification before definitive empirical conclusions and policy recommendations can be established.

title: Thin markets, thick subsidies: local competition and the incidence of heat pump grants
source: London School of Economics and Political Science Research Online (London School of Economics and Political Science)
summary: We study how local supply shapes the incidence and quantity response of clean-technology subsidies. In October 2023, the UK government increased the grant for air-source heat pumps from #5,000 to #7,500 in England and Wales, while Scotland
content: We study how local supply shapes the incidence and quantity response of clean-technology subsidies. In October 2023, the UK government increased the grant for air-source heat pumps from #5,000 to #7,500 in England and Wales, while Scotland left its policy unchanged. Using 260,000 certified heat pump installation records in a difference-in-differences comparison of Northern England with Scotland, we find that the grant increase raised monthly installations by 24%, adding roughly 7,200 units over 20 post-reform months. Reported pre-grant installation costs fell by about #830, so household out-of-pocket payments declined by more than the #2,500 grant increase. The quantity expansion and the cost reduction were larger in local areas with more competition prior to the policy. Supply adjusted through local installer entry, wider geographic reach among existing installers, and a shift toward smaller, higher-efficiency heat pumps. While changes in heat pump size and model mix explain roughly half of the unconditional cost drop, within-installer-and-model price cuts account for a quarter of the average decline and half of the additional price drop in more competitive markets. Combining these estimates with engineering-based carbon abatement yields a marginal value of public funds of 2.1, rising to 2.5 in markets one standard deviation above mean competition.

title: Modeling branch diameter in Larix olgensis using living branches, knot profiles and stem scars: climate–soil associations
summary: Branch diameter (BD) strongly influences crown architecture, knot formation and wood quality, yet BD development is commonly modeled using living branches alone, leaving the diameter attained by dead branches at growth cessation insufficien
content: Branch diameter (BD) strongly influences crown architecture, knot formation and wood quality, yet BD development is commonly modeled using living branches alone, leaving the diameter attained by dead branches at growth cessation insufficiently represented. Here, we developed a BD model as a function of branch age for Larix olgensis by combining living first-order branch measurements with longitudinal knot profiles and external stem-scar diameters. Data from 60 felled trees in 19 plots were used to estimate age-related BD curves and to evaluate the roles of branch position, tree form, climate and soil factors. Candidate growth functions were compared, extended with environmental covariates and fitted within a nonlinear mixed-effects framework to account for plot- and tree-level variation. BD followed a nonlinear age-related trajectory, with rapid early enlargement followed by gradual stabilization. The Mitscherlich function was selected as the base model, and its performance improved after incorporating branch insertion height, height-diameter ratio, mean warmest-month temperature (MWMT), soil organic carbon and a product of mean annual precipitation and cation exchange capacity (MAP × CEC). The final mixed-effects model increased adjusted R 2 from 0.801 to 0.936 and reduced RMSE from 3.145 to 2.087 mm. Simulations indicated that BD was larger for branches located higher on the stem and under higher MWMT conditions, but smaller in trees with higher height-diameter ratios. The MAP × CEC term described variation in simulated BD across combinations of precipitation and soil conditions. The model provides age-related estimates of branch size that can inform wood-quality assessment and pruning decisions when considered alongside stand age, live-crown retention and management costs.

title: Taxation as a Tool for Environmental Protection in Uganda: A critical policy review with special reference to carbon-credit taxation
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Environmental taxation can influence production and consumption while generating resources for public services, yet revenue collection alone does not demonstrate environmental protection. This article critically examines taxation as an envi
content: Environmental taxation can influence production and consumption while generating resources for public services, yet revenue collection alone does not demonstrate environmental protection. This article critically examines taxation as an environmental policy instrument in Uganda, with particular attention to carbon-credit transactions. It uses a structured narrative review of selected legislation, official publications and economic literature available up to 1 November 2026. The analysis distinguishes taxes on pollution, taxes affecting environmentally harmful products, administrative charges and the taxation of income from environmental activities. The findings identify a mismatch between readily administered tax bases and the environmental damage that policy seeks to reduce. Carbon-market governance has become more explicit under Uganda's 2025 regulations, but the corresponding-adjustment fee must be distinguished from income tax, value added tax and community benefit sharing. Illustrative models demonstrate how demand responsiveness, project scale and the choice between gross and net tax bases affect outcomes; these models are not estimates of Uganda's actual environmental impacts or tax liabilities. The article proposes coordinated fiscal guidance, transparent project accounting, proportionate administration, distributional protection and independent environmental monitoring. It concludes that environmental effectiveness depends on the relationship between tax design, credible enforcement, accessible alternatives and verified ecological results, rather than the environmental label attached to a revenue instrument.

title: Hematological and Serum Biochemical Profiles of Hubbard Broiler Chickens Fed Fermented Brewers Dried Grain as Replacement for Maize
summary: A 42-days trial evaluated the effects of replacing maize with fermented brewers dried grain (FBDG) on hematology, serum biochemistry, and electrolyte profiles of broiler chickens. 300 one-day-old Hubbard broiler chicks were assigned to five
content: A 42-days trial evaluated the effects of replacing maize with fermented brewers dried grain (FBDG) on hematology, serum biochemistry, and electrolyte profiles of broiler chickens. 300 one-day-old Hubbard broiler chicks were assigned to five treatments (6 replicates of 10 birds each) under a Completely Randomized Design (CRD). Diets were formulated isonitrogenous and isocaloric according to NRC requirements. Treatment 1 (control) contained no FBDG, while T2, T3, T4, and T5 replaced maize with FBDG at 5 %, 10 %, 15 %, and 20 %, respectively. Solid-state fermentation significantly upgraded raw BDG: Crude Protein (18.0 to 27.1%), Ash (5.08 to 6.89%), and Metabolizable Energy (1980 to 2980 kcal/kg) increased, whereas Crude Fiber (16.0 to 10.01%) and Ether Extract (4.98 to 3.91%) decreased. Hematological indices (PCV, Hb, RBC, MCV, MCH, MCHC, WBC) were significantly higher (P<0.05) in FBDG groups (T2–T5) than T1. Similarly, serum total protein, albumin, globulin, calcium, phosphorus, potassium, and bicarbonate were elevated in T2–T5 relative to T1. Conversely, serum AST, ALT, ALP, urea, creatinine were not significantly affected. In conclusion, solid-state fermentation enhances the bio-nutritional value of BDG, and replacing maize up to 20% with FBDG improves oxygen-carrying capacity, protein metabolism, mineral balance, and hypocholesterolemic status without inducing hepato-renal stress.

title: Application of digitaltechnologiesin the postal logistics sector in Vietnam:Current status, challenges, and solutions
source: Ministry of Science and Technology Vietnam
summary: Digital transformation is becoming a crucial driver for innovating operational models in the postal logistics sector.The robust growth of e-commerce, the digital economy, and the increasing demands for speed and service quality have created
content: Digital transformation is becoming a crucial driver for innovating operational models in the postal logistics sector.The robust growth of e-commerce, the digital economy, and the increasing demands for speed and service quality have created an urgent need for logistics enterprises to apply digital technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data, cloud computing, and automation.In Vietnam, the digital transformation in the postal logistics industry has achieved some results; however, there are still many limitations in technological infrastructure, data connectivity, human resources, and the level of technology adoption among enterprises.Based on the synthesis and analysis of domestic and international specialised studies and reports, this research evaluates the current status of applying digital transformation technology in the postal logistics sector in Vietnam.Simultaneously, it proposes development orientations and solutions according to the roadmap to 2030 and the vision to 2045.Digital transformation not only improves operational efficiency and reduces logistics costs but also lays the foundation for building a smart postal logistics ecosystem that meets the development requirements of the digital economy.

title: Perceived environmental responsibility, green brand image, and green trust: asymmetric moderating roles of green self-concept consistency and green skepticism among electric-motorcycle users
summary: Background Perceived Environmental Corporate Social Responsibility (ECSR) signals environmental priorities, but consumers may interpret this signal differently when judging brand image and trust. We examine how green skepticism and green se
content: Background Perceived Environmental Corporate Social Responsibility (ECSR) signals environmental priorities, but consumers may interpret this signal differently when judging brand image and trust. We examine how green skepticism and green self-concept consistency (GSCC) moderate these associations among electric-motorcycle users. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted from 29/06/2026 to 28/07/2026, following the institutional ethical clearance issued on 25 June 2026, among 502 consenting adult electric-motorcycle owners or active users in Greater Jakarta, Indonesia, recruited through purposive sampling. Six focal associations specified in the broader research framework were reported from SmartPLS 4 estimates using 5,000 bootstrap subsamples, two-tailed tests, and a 5% significance level. Separate composite-score analyses served as robustness checks. Results Perceived ECSR was positively associated with green brand image (β = 0.353, t = 9.363, p < 0.001) and green trust (β = 0.287, t = 7.030, p < 0.001); green brand image was associated with green trust (β = 0.319, t = 6.959, p < 0.001). Green skepticism weakened the ECSR–trust association (β = −0.125, p = 0.011). GSCC weakened the direct ECSR–trust association (β = −0.118, p = 0.002) but strengthened the ECSR–image association (β = 0.141, p < 0.001). The supplementary indirect ECSR → green brand image → green trust association was positive (β = 0.113, p < 0.001). Conclusions Perceived ECSR is associated with two distinguishable outcomes: environmental brand meaning and relational credibility. Identity fit shows opposing moderation patterns for image and direct trust, while skepticism weakens the direct trust association. The cross-sectional design does not establish causal or temporal effects.

title: Sustainable postharvest management of fruits: Bridging biology, technology and policy
summary: Postharvest loss remains a major barrier to agricultural productivity, yet proven technologies and interventions exist to reduce it. Globally, an estimated 14% of food is lost between harvest and retail (FAO, 2019), while a further 19% of t
content: Postharvest loss remains a major barrier to agricultural productivity, yet proven technologies and interventions exist to reduce it. Globally, an estimated 14% of food is lost between harvest and retail (FAO, 2019), while a further 19% of the food available to consumers is wasted in retail, food service, and households (UNEP, 2024). Fruits and vegetables are among the most perishable agricultural commodities, and their high-water content, fragile tissues, and vulnerability to mechanical injury and decay lead to value-chain losses of 20% - 50%, depending on the crop and region (Khan et al., 2024). Where fruit is lost depends on where it is grown. In developing regions, losses occur early, on farms and during handling, because cold storage facility is scarce and produce passes through thousands of unconnected smallholders. In developed economies, losses occur later, at retail and household levels, driven by overproduction, strict cosmetic standards and consumer behavior (Khan et al., 2024). Globally, these losses cost hundreds of billions of dollars annually. Due to this, growers earn less, consumers pay more, and the land, water and energy used to produce the fruit gets wasted. Although logistics plays pivotal role in post-harvest loss reduction, however, it explains only part of the problem. Understanding quick fruit deterioration needs looking at biology. Physiological and biochemical processes going on within fruit are important in fruit spoilage. Senescence is not a simple decay, but a firmly regulated process in which ethylene plays a central role. In climacteric fruits, ethylene biosynthesis and signalling trigger a burst of respiration that drives ripening, while non-climacteric species follow quieter, ethylene-independent cues feeding into much the same genetic machinery (Tipu and Sherif, 2024). As senescence proceeds, reactive oxygen species accumulate faster than the fruit's antioxidant enzymes can neutralise them, causing lipid peroxidation and membrane damage. Simultaneously, enzymes such as polygalacturonase and cellulase break down the pectin and hemicellulose that give tissue its structure, explaining why ripe fruit softens. Chlorophyll degrades, other pigments accumulate, water is lost through transpiration, and starch converts into sugar, rewriting colour, texture, and flavour within days. Ethylene and abscisic acid pathways, alongside carbohydrate and ROS metabolism, remain the principal molecular drivers of this decline across both fruit classes (Storch et al., 2025). Every serious postharvest intervention such as cold chain, packaging, coating, or biocontrol agent, works by interrupting one of these triggers rather than masking its effects. Conventional refrigeration is the obvious starting point, but it is energy intensive, still largely dependent on hydrofluorocarbons, and out of reach for smallholders without reliable grid access. title: Cold Atmospheric Plasma for Breast Cancer Therapy: Mechanisms, Preclinical Evidence, and Translational Challenges
summary: ABSTRACT The burden of breast cancer remains high as it is the most prevalent malignancy among women, with therapeutic success often limited by drug resistance, treatment toxicity, and tumor heterogeneity. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP), a p
content: ABSTRACT The burden of breast cancer remains high as it is the most prevalent malignancy among women, with therapeutic success often limited by drug resistance, treatment toxicity, and tumor heterogeneity. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP), a partially ionized gas enriched with reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS), and electromagnetic waves, has emerged as a promising preclinical anticancer strategy with selctively killing. Here, we review the mechanisms of CAP action against breast cancer, including RONS‐mediated oxidative stress, mitochondrial disruption, apoptosis, immunogenic cell death, and suppression of metastatic and angiogenic pathways. Notably, preclinical studies indicate that CAP can target therapy‐resistant breast cancer stem‐like cells and may sensitize aggressive subtypes, particularly triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC). Synergistic combinations with drug therapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and surgery further support its therapeutic potential as an adjunctive strategy in preclinical breast cancer research. Advances in delivery platforms, such as plasma‐activated media and hydrogels, may help address CAP's instability and improve local delivery. Despite promising preclinical results, clinical translation faces barriers such as the short half‐life of RONS, device standardization, and unresolved immunomodulatory effects. Further standardized in vivo studies and breast‐cancer‐specific clinical trials are required before CAP can be considered clinically ready for breast cancer therapy.

title: The Broad Ecological Range of Salmonella enterica Serotype Typhimurium Is Associated With Genomic Diversification
summary: ABSTRACT Salmonella Typhimurium is a versatile foodborne pathogen with a broad ecological range, making it an ideal model to better understand pathogen adaptations that allow them to infect multiple hosts and persist across environments. He
content: ABSTRACT Salmonella Typhimurium is a versatile foodborne pathogen with a broad ecological range, making it an ideal model to better understand pathogen adaptations that allow them to infect multiple hosts and persist across environments. Here, we analysed 595 genomes of S. Typhimurium representing three food animal sources (bovine, swine, and poultry) and one non‐food animal source (wild birds). We found that S. Typhimurium from food animal sources generally had a more open pangenome and harboured more antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Notably, swine isolates exhibited the most open pangenome and the highest prevalence of ARGs, patterns that were associated with a greater presence of mobile genetic elements, particularly plasmids. Despite similar core genome sizes, S. Typhimurium from different sources displayed distinct patterns of positive selection in the core genome that varied in frequency and targeted functional categories. In contrast, although accessory genome sizes varied substantially across sources, the frequency of positive selection remained similar. Using machine learning, we identified source‐predictive genetic variants, many of which are associated with stress‐response functions. These findings suggest that gain and loss of accessory genes and positive selection acting on core genes support differential adaptation in S. Typhimurium, potentially contributing to its broad ecological range.

title: Liquidité boursière et valorisation des actions sur les marchés financiers frontières d'Afrique subsaharienne : proposition d'un dispositif de recherche exploratoire
source: Revue Internationale des Sciences de Gestion
summary: Cette étude explore, à travers un dispositif de recherche mixte, le lien potentiel entre liquidité boursière et valorisation des actions sur quatre marchés frontières d'Afrique subsaharienne (BRVM, NSE, NGX, GSE). Partant d'une littérature
content: Cette étude explore, à travers un dispositif de recherche mixte, le lien potentiel entre liquidité boursière et valorisation des actions sur quatre marchés frontières d'Afrique subsaharienne (BRVM, NSE, NGX, GSE). Partant d'une littérature contradictoire sur la prime d'illiquidité, il propose un cadre conceptuel articulant cinq facteurs explicatifs (liquidité, gouvernance actionnariale, ouverture aux investisseurs étrangers, risque de change, intégration financière) et une variable secondaire, la pérennité de la cotation. L'étude combine une phase qualitative (entretiens semi-directifs) pour identifier les mécanismes perçus par les acteurs de marché, et une phase quantitative purement descriptive pour documenter les régularités entre liquidité et valorisation, sans viser de relation causale. Le périmètre, la période d'étude et l'opérationnalisation des variables sont précisés pour garantir la reproductibilité. L'article se termine par des propositions de recherche, dont les implications restent discutées de manière strictement conditionnelle aux résultats futurs.

title: L'intelligence écologique et la consommation verte : le rôle médiateur de la conscience environnementale
source: Revue Internationale des Sciences de Gestion
summary: Cette étude examine l’effet de l’intelligence écologique sur la consommation verte, en intégrant la conscience environnementale comme mécanisme intermédiaire. Elle répond au décalage persistant entre connaissance des enjeux écologiques et a
content: Cette étude examine l’effet de l’intelligence écologique sur la consommation verte, en intégrant la conscience environnementale comme mécanisme intermédiaire. Elle répond au décalage persistant entre connaissance des enjeux écologiques et adoption effective de comportements responsables. Une enquête quantitative menée auprès de 300 répondants a été analysée par la méthode PLS-SEM. Les résultats montrent que le modèle explique 54,8 % de la variance de la consommation verte. La conscience environnementale présente l’effet le plus important sur celle-ci (f² = 0,732), devant l’intelligence écologique (f² = 0,190). Ces résultats soulignent que la compréhension des enjeux écologiques ne suffit pas à elle seule et que leur intériorisation sous forme de conscience environnementale joue un rôle central dans l’adoption de comportements de consommation durable.

title: Efficient Synthesis, Anticancer Evaluation, and Molecular Docking Studies of New Triazole‐aryl‐Ester Hybrids of β‐Himachalene as Potent Inducers of Apoptosis
summary: ABSTRACT A novel series of aromatic ester‐1.4‐disubstituted‐1,2,3‐triazole hybrids containing himachalene was efficiently synthesized by a regioselective copper‐catalyzed azide‐alkyne cycloaddition between an azidomethyl‐himachalene derivat
content: ABSTRACT A novel series of aromatic ester‐1.4‐disubstituted‐1,2,3‐triazole hybrids containing himachalene was efficiently synthesized by a regioselective copper‐catalyzed azide‐alkyne cycloaddition between an azidomethyl‐himachalene derivative and various propargylated esters. These compounds were characterized by NMR and HRMS analyses. The Hemisynthesized products were studied for their in vitro cytotoxicity against four cancer cell lines (HT‐1080, A‐549, MCF‐7, and MDA‐MB‐231). Most of the tested compounds showed moderate to significant activities with IC 50 values ranging from 8.06 to 47 µM on all cancer cell lines. Notably, compound 6d, with a 4‐methoxy substituent, was the most potent against HT‐1080 and MCF‐7 cells. The mechanism of action study revealed that compound 6d induced apoptosis through caspase‐3/7 activation and cell cycle arrest at G0/G1. These results were confirmed by in silico molecular docking investigations, which demonstrated that compound 6d had a strong binding affinity toward caspase‐3/7 (‐8.6 kcal/mol), much higher than the co‐crystallized ligand. Key hydrogen bonds with ARG207 and SER205, π‐cation interaction with ARG207, π – π stacking with HIS121 and TYR204, and hydrophobic interactions with MET61 and PHE128 were all present in its well‐balanced interaction profile. These interactions give the ligand a molecular basis for its increased biological activity and aid in its stable position inside the active site.

title: A disproportionality analysis of dual bronchodilators based on the FAERS
summary: Abstract Objective To detect adverse event (AE) signals for dual bronchodilators using the Food and Drug Administration(FDA) Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), assess their potential safety risks, and inform pharmacovigilance. Methods
content: Abstract Objective To detect adverse event (AE) signals for dual bronchodilators using the Food and Drug Administration(FDA) Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), assess their potential safety risks, and inform pharmacovigilance. Methods AE reports pertaining to dual bronchodilators were retrieved from the FAERS for the period covering the fourth quarter of 2013 through the fourth quarter of 2025. Signal detection was subsequently conducted using both the Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) and the Multi‑Item Gamma Poisson Shrinker (MGPS) method. Results From the FAERS database, the numbers of AE reports with umeclidinium/vilanterol, indacaterol/glycopyrronium, tiotropium/olodaterol, glycopyrronium/formoterol, and aclidinium/formoterol as primary suspected drugs were 1,674, 674, 572, 102, and 52, respectively; the corresponding numbers of detected AE signals were 140, 111, 64, 30, and 10; and the numbers of involved system organ classes (SOCs) were 19, 16, 15, 12, and 7, respectively. Conclusion The AEs of dual bronchodilators were predominantly observed in the SOCs of respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders, cardiac disorders, and infections and infestations, etc. The distribution of AE signals and serious adverse events(SAEs) varied across the five drugs. Accordingly, individualized drug selection is advised in clinical practice, with special attention to early risk monitoring in elderly patients and those with compromised baseline cardiopulmonary function.

title: BARREIRAS E OPORTUNIDADES EM MODELOS DE NEGÓCIO CIRCULARES: EVIDÊNCIAS DE UMA REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA DA LITERATURA INTEGRADA À META-ANÁLISE

summary: A Economia Circular (EC) propõe ciclos fechados de materiais, mantendo recursos em uso pelo maior tempo possível e minimizando a geração de resíduos (Kirchherr; Reike; Hekkert, 2017).Sob esse viés, o Brasil aprovou em 2025 o Plano Nacional
content: A Economia Circular (EC) propõe ciclos fechados de materiais, mantendo recursos em uso pelo maior tempo possível e minimizando a geração de resíduos (Kirchherr; Reike; Hekkert, 2017).Sob esse viés, o Brasil aprovou em 2025 o Plano Nacional de Economia Circular (PNEC), ampliando a demanda por investigações acadêmicas capazes de articular frameworks de modelos de negócios circulares que suportem sua implementação em diversos setores produtivos, além da necessidade de mapear possíveis barreiras e oportunidades para o desenvolvimento das práticas de economia circular (Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços, 2025).Nesse contexto, a literatura destaca que práticas de Economia Circular, como logística reversa, produção limpa, recuperação de materiais e integração colaborativa da cadeia de suprimentos, podem ser compreendidas como ações e estratégias gerenciais que operacionalizam a transição de modelos lineares para modelos circulares, atuando como mecanismos operacionais que viabilizam circularidade, enquanto os modelos de negócio circulares representam estruturas de criação, entrega e captura de valor baseadas na lógica circular (Aarikka-stenroos et al., 2022;Ostermann et al., 2021;Pieroni et al., 2021).Sob a perspectiva da Engenharia de Produção, a implementação desses modelos envolve gestão de operações, projeto de produtos e processos, cadeia de suprimentos, gestão de resíduos, eficiência produtiva e tecnologias habilitadoras da Indústria 4.0 (Jabbour et al., 2019;Mattos;Albuquerque, 2018).Embora exista vasta literatura sobre modelos de negócio circulares e práticas de economia circular, os estudos ainda são predominantemente qualitativos e fragmentados, limitando a consolidação empírica das relações entre os fatores que influenciam sua implementação (Pieroni et al., 2019;Whalen, 2019).Consequentemente, permanece limitada a compreensão sobre a magnitude, consistência e variabilidade dos efeitos associados às barreiras e oportunidades identificadas na literatura (Kirchherr; Van Santen, 2019).Nesse contexto, emerge a seguinte questão de pesquisa: quais são as barreiras e oportunidades identificadas na literatura para o desenvolvimento de modelos de negócio circulares e qual é a magnitude e a variabilidade dos efeitos dessas variáveis sobre sua implementação?Tendo como objetivo geral, identificar e sistematizar as barreiras e oportunidades relacionadas aos modelos de negócio circulares, bem como analisar quantitativamente a magnitude das relações entre variáveis por meio de meta-análise, title: Women’s Environmental Stewardship in a Matrilineal Society: The Role of Bundo Kanduang in Green Economy Development
summary: Abstract Background The transition toward a sustainable green economy requires inclusive community participation, particularly women’s involvement in environmental and socio-economic governance. In the Minangkabau matrilineal society of Wes
content: Abstract Background The transition toward a sustainable green economy requires inclusive community participation, particularly women’s involvement in environmental and socio-economic governance. In the Minangkabau matrilineal society of West Sumatra, Indonesia, Bundo Kanduang represents women’s cultural authority and social leadership within family and community structures. Despite increasing global attention to gender and sustainability, few studies have examined how indigenous matrilineal values contribute to environmental stewardship and the development of a green economy in local communities. This study explores the multidimensional role of Bundo Kanduang in supporting sustainable development practices within Minangkabau society. Methods This study employed a qualitative research design using narrative interviews with 98 married Minangkabau women aged 25–45 years residing in Lubuk Minturun Village, Koto Tangah District, Padang City, West Sumatra, Indonesia. Data were analyzed thematically to identify women’s contributions across household economic activities, social participation, and environmental management practices within the context of green economy development. Results The findings reveal that Bundo Kanduang plays a significant role in promoting sustainable household economies through adaptive income-generating activities and resource management practices. Participants also demonstrated active engagement in community-based social initiatives and environmental stewardship, including waste management, coastal environmental preservation, and the transmission of ecological values within families and communities. The integration of matrilineal cultural values into women’s environmental leadership strengthens community resilience and supports localized green-economy practices. Study Limitations This study has several limitations. First, it was conducted as a qualitative single-case study in Lubuk Minturun Village, Padang City; therefore, the findings are context-specific and should not be interpreted as statistically representative of all Minangkabau women or matrilineal communities in Indonesia. Second, the study relies substantially on participants’ narratives and interpretations of their everyday economic, social, cultural, and environmental practices, which may be influenced by recall and social desirability. Third, although interviews, questionnaire-guided qualitative prompts, observations, community discussions, and documentary materials were used to strengthen triangulation, the study does not quantitatively measure the environmental or economic outcomes associated with the reported practices. Consequently, the findings demonstrate culturally embedded practices that are consistent with principles of environmental stewardship and green economy development rather than establishing a causal effect of Bundo Kanduang on green economy outcomes. The single-site design and purposive qualitative focus also limit transferability beyond the study

title: PERCEPÇÃO DE QUALIDADE NO SETOR AUTOMOTIVO BRASILEIRO: IMPACTOS DA ELETRIFICAÇÃO E DAS MONTADORAS CHINESAS
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: Fernando Tobal Berssaneti (USP)O setor automotivo brasileiro está em um período de transformação estrutural, marcado pela transição dos veículos a combustão interna (ICE) para os veículos eletrificados (EV) e pela rápida ascensão das montad
content: Fernando Tobal Berssaneti (USP)O setor automotivo brasileiro está em um período de transformação estrutural, marcado pela transição dos veículos a combustão interna (ICE) para os veículos eletrificados (EV) e pela rápida ascensão das montadoras chinesas, que em 2024 responderam por mais de 70% das vendas de elétricos e híbridos plug-in no país.Esse movimento desafia os referenciais clássicos da gestão da qualidade, historicamente ancorados em atributos mecânicos e na conformidade com especificações técnicas.Este estudo analisa como essa dupla transição vem redefinindo a percepção de qualidade do consumidor brasileiro e seus impactos para a gestão da qualidade no setor.Foi realizado uma pesquisa de métodos mistos, com 182 respondentes, combinando análise quantitativa (boxplots e correlação de Spearman) e qualitativa (análise de conteúdo de 144 verbatins), estruturada em cinco pilares de percepção dos EVs e quatro dimensões avaliativas das montadoras chinesas.Os resultados indicam uma redefinição seletiva e incremental dos critérios de qualidade: a tecnologia emerge como principal diferencial dos EVs, mas é a qualidade funcional e econômica (ρ = 0,514) que mais se associa à intenção de compra.Entre as marcas chinesas, qualidade percebida e custo-benefício impulsionam a confiança, embora o risco quanto à durabilidade persista mesmo entre os consumidores mais propensos à aquisição, revelando que a reinserção dessas marcas no mercado brasileiro ainda enfrenta resistências.

title: The Externalities of ChatGPT in Labor Markets, Productivity, and Resource Allocation
source: International Journal of Finance Insurance and Risk Management
summary: Purpose: The rapid development and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, particularly ChatGPT, have significantly influenced various sectors of the economy by reshaping labor markets, productivity, and resource a
content: Purpose: The rapid development and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, particularly ChatGPT, have significantly influenced various sectors of the economy by reshaping labor markets, productivity, and resource allocation.This study aims to examine the extent to which the widespread use of ChatGPT generates both positive and negative externalities in these three areas and to provide a multifaceted assessment of its broader economic impact. Design/Methodology/Approach:The study adopts a secondary-data research approach based on a systematic evaluation of academic studies, institutional reports, and other credible sources concerning ChatGPT and generative AI.The analysis examines the changes associated with ChatGPT in labor markets, productivity, and resource allocation.Economic models, theoretical reasoning, and the concept of externalities are employed to identify and evaluate the positive and negative consequences associated with the adoption and use of technology.Findings: The findings indicate that ChatGPT generates important positive externalities by increasing productivity through the rapid generation of ideas and solutions and by facilitating more efficient and streamlined communication.It also improves the utilization of labor by automating repetitive tasks and supporting decision-making processes.In addition, ChatGPT can contribute to more efficient resource allocation by reducing certain forms of waste and inefficiency and by facilitating rapid access to relevant information.However, the analysis also identifies significant negative externalities.These include potential productivity losses resulting from inaccurate information and quality concerns, job displacement associated with automation and skills mismatches, challenges related to worker retraining and labor-market adjustment, and environmental pressures arising from the increasing resources required to support AI technologies.Practical Implications: The findings highlight the need for firms, workers, and policymakers to adopt a balanced approach to the implementation of ChatGPT.Organizations should establish appropriate mechanisms for verifying AI-generated information, invest in employee training and reskilling, and use AI in ways that complement rather than unnecessarily replace human capabilities.Policymakers should strengthen AI literacy, support labormarket adaptation and retraining, and develop appropriate measures to address the social and environmental costs associated with large-scale AI adoption.Such measures can help maximize the economic benefits of ChatGPT while reducing its negative
