Besides containing valuable hydrocarbons, waste lubricating oil also contains sulfur compounds and heavy metals that may reduce fuel quality and cause environmental pollution. This study evaluates the recovery of waste lubricating oil through a pyrolysis–distillation process assisted by activated carbon derived from low-rank coal from East Kalimantan, Indonesia. The activated carbon was synthesized through carbonization and chemical activation and characterized using iodine number analysis to determine its adsorption capability. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was applied to optimize pyrolysis temperature and activated carbon dosage in order to maximize liquid yield and contaminant removal efficiency. The synthesized activated carbon exhibited an iodine number of 1163.51 mg/g. Optimization predicted optimum conditions at 416.54 °C and 12.87 wt.% activated carbon dosage, producing 89.67% liquid yield and approximately 76% contaminant removal efficiency. Experimental validation confirmed the model prediction, resulting in 88% liquid yield with satisfactory fuel characteristics.

title: Beyond Corporate Responsibility: Reassessing the Financial Implications of Sustainability for Dividend Policy
summary: Corporate sustainability has increasingly become an important consideration in corporate financial decision-making, particularly in relation to dividend policy and shareholder returns. However, existing empirical evidence on this relationsh
content: Corporate sustainability has increasingly become an important consideration in corporate financial decision-making, particularly in relation to dividend policy and shareholder returns. However, existing empirical evidence on this relationship remains fragmented and contradictory. This study examines the sustainability–dividend policy nexus through a combined bibliometric analysis and critical literature review. Data were retrieved from Scopus and comprised 150 peer-reviewed articles published between 2005 and 2025. Using the Bibliometrix package in R, the study investigates publication trends, influential authors, journals, countries, collaboration networks, and thematic developments. The critical review further evaluates the relationship's underlying mechanisms and contextual conditions. The findings indicate that corporate sustainability generally supports higher and more stable dividend payments through improved profitability, reduced information asymmetry, and lower agency costs. However, this relationship is conditional upon sustainability measurement, ownership structure, financial constraints, and institutional characteristics. Notably, externally verifiable sustainability initiatives, particularly eco-labelling certifications and green bonds, demonstrate more consistent positive associations with dividend outcomes than broad ESG scores. The bibliometric analysis reveals growing scholarly interest since 2018, while highlighting the fragmented and underdeveloped connection between sustainability and dividend policy. By integrating signaling, and stakeholder perspectives, this study clarifies existing empirical inconsistencies and provides insights into how credible sustainability practices can support dividend distributions and long-term shareholder value.

title: Tata Kelola Bioenergi Pongamia Berbasis Komunitas di Wilayah Kepulauan Kering Indonesia Timur
summary: This study examines how knowledge of Pongamia (Pongamia pinnata), community governance, and feedstock readiness may be connected to support community-based bioenergy. A bibliometric mapping of 2,208 unique records retrieved through Elicit a
content: This study examines how knowledge of Pongamia (Pongamia pinnata), community governance, and feedstock readiness may be connected to support community-based bioenergy. A bibliometric mapping of 2,208 unique records retrieved through Elicit and Dimensions was complemented by a focused thematic synthesis of 32 articles (29 from the main corpus and three external contextual studies). Title–abstract mapping identified four broad thematic domains encompassing agroecology, community governance, bioenergy, and engineering. However, only a small share of the assembled corpus explicitly addresses Pongamia; consequently, thematic separation should not be generalized as fragmentation of the entire global literature. The thematic synthesis indicates that willingness to participate depends on planting material, extension support, trusted organizations, and credible economic benefits. The article develops preliminary design principles connecting seed resources, nurseries, participation, institutional arrangements, processing, and market access. The proposed framework is a literature-informed proposition rather than an empirically validated model for Lembata.

title: Effect of Agaricus bisporus extract on gene expression of some virulence genes of Aspergillus flavus
summary: Aspergillus flavus is a common filamentous fungus as well as an opportunistic pathogen of crops. The capability of fungi to infect plants relied on particular genes differentiating pathogenic fungi from their nonpathogenic counterparts. Thi
content: Aspergillus flavus is a common filamentous fungus as well as an opportunistic pathogen of crops. The capability of fungi to infect plants relied on particular genes differentiating pathogenic fungi from their nonpathogenic counterparts. This investigation aims to study the effect of Agaricus bisporus extract on the gene expression of Lipase, Aflatoxin and Metalloprotease of four highly pathogenic isolates of Aspergillus flavus in Iraq. Nine isolates were obtained from infected walnut fruits and their diagnosis was confirmed by morphological and molecular methods. The quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) for gene detection showed that the isolates (A. flavus 1, A. flavus 4, A. flavus 7 and A. flavus 8) were characterized by positive results for all virulence genes. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry analysis of the alcoholic extract of A. bisporus showed that it contains many common compounds in high concentration in the form of esters, fatty acids, derived alcohols and ketones, as well as some aromatic compounds, all of which have varying effects in inhibiting fungal growth. The results of qRT-PCR for gene expression revealed a fundamental down regulation for the expression of lipase, aflatoxin and metalprotease genes. Lipase and metalprotease genes showed highly significant difference (P≤0.01) in gene expression for two isolates (A. flavus 4 and A. flavus 8) for lipase and Metalprotease genes while Aflatoxin gene revealed highly significant difference (P≤0.01) in three isolates (A. flavus 4, A. flavus 7 and A. flavus 8). Elucidating the molecular techniques which control the secondary metabolism of toxin-producing fungi can make it possible to deliberately silence the genes implicated, thereby planned inhibition of these fungi and reducing their virulence.

title: Integrating Research and Project-Based Learning: A Competency-Oriented Teaching Reform for the Civil Engineering Materials Course
source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
summary: Given the broad scope of the Civil Engineering Materials course, the close relationship between material properties and engineering applications, and the constraints imposed by curing ages on cementbased materials testing, this study develo
content: Given the broad scope of the Civil Engineering Materials course, the close relationship between material properties and engineering applications, and the constraints imposed by curing ages on cementbased materials testing, this study develops a research-integrated and project-based teaching reform framework through literature analysis and curriculum design, drawing on the theories of constructive alignment, project-based learning, and research-based learning. Representative research cases are selected and adapted into undergraduate projects with clearly defined variables, experimental tasks, and expected deliverables. Taking low-carbon cement mortar mix design as an example, an eight-week instructional module is designed to encompass research question formulation, mix design, specimen preparation, performance testing, and multi-criteria engineering evaluation. Five competency dimensions are identified, including application of materials knowledge, experimental design, data analysis and interpretation, sustainable engineering decisionmaking, and engineering communication. Alignment is established among project-level competency objectives, learning activities, and assessment evidence, supported by an analytic scoring rubric and mechanisms for process-based assessment and feedback. The proposed framework emphasizes the integration of research questions into course activities, coordination between experimental curing periods and instructional schedules, and evidence-based assessment of student competencies, providing a reference for curriculum reform in civil engineering materials and related courses.

title: Green and Digital Trade Between Viet Nam and Japan Through Technology Specialisation and Supply Chain Concentration
summary: Green and digital goods are central to the energy transition, yet the structure of their trade between Viet Nam and Japan has received little attention. This study aims to show how four established trade indicators, read jointly, distinguis
content: Green and digital goods are central to the energy transition, yet the structure of their trade between Viet Nam and Japan has received little attention. This study aims to show how four established trade indicators, read jointly, distinguish product groups by export specialisation, market complementarity, bilateral trade balance, and sourcing concentration. Using six-digit trade data from the World Integrated Trade Solution (WITS) and UN Comtrade for 2018–2023, it applies the Revealed Comparative Advantage index (RCA), the Trade Complementarity Index (TCI), the Grubel–Lloyd index (GL), and the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI) of Japan’s import sources to six groups: low-carbon technology goods, environmental goods, lithium-ion battery supply chain goods, industrial robots, semiconductors, and 3D printing goods. The configurations differ by group. In industrial robots, both countries show revealed specialisation, and gross bilateral trade is almost balanced. In environmental goods, Viet Nam’s export structure moved closer to Japanese import demand before revealed specialisation emerged. In semiconductors, Vietnamese specialisation coexists with unbalanced bilateral trade. Product-level checks show that the group-level HHI understates the concentration in battery goods, whereas the semiconductor result depends on the treatment of “Other Asia, n.e.s.”. The contribution is configurational: the indicator combinations show where evidence on value added, capability formation, and dependence is most needed.

title: Transforming modern drug discovery with molecular modeling and artificial intelligence
summary: Background: Techniques such as Molecular Modeling and Artificial Intelligence in drug discovery have revolutionized the field by improving target identification, virtual screening, lead optimization, and toxicity prediction. Although many c
content: Background: Techniques such as Molecular Modeling and Artificial Intelligence in drug discovery have revolutionized the field by improving target identification, virtual screening, lead optimization, and toxicity prediction. Although many computational techniques exist, the literature offers few systematic, comprehensive reviews of molecular modeling combined with AI-driven techniques. This article evaluates the application of molecular modeling technologies, such as Quantum Mechanics, Molecular Mechanics, Molecular Dynamics, molecular docking, and computer-aided drug design, using AI methods. Methodology: The author conducted a narrative review based on published information from scientific literature databases such as PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Results and Discussion: Molecular modeling enables structural and mechanistic models of ligand–target binding, while AI accelerates virtual screening, de novo molecular design, ADMET prediction, and lead optimization. Novel technologies such as AlphaFold, graph neural networks, and generative AI are expanding applied computational drug design. Nevertheless, several challenges remain, including data quality, model interpretability, external validation, dataset bias, overfitting, limited experimental validation, and translational reliability. Conclusion: Integrating molecular modeling and AI technologies represents a major step toward faster, more economical drug discovery processes. Future success will depend on increased use of standardized datasets, the development of explainable AI, and thorough experimental validation.

title: Market orientation and green technology adoption in agricultural enterprises: A serial mediation model of organizational learning capability and policy utilization capability
summary: Green and low-carbon development has become an important embodiment of China's path to becoming a strong agricultural country. How to enable agricultural enterprises to better adopt green technologies and conduct production and operation wi
content: Green and low-carbon development has become an important embodiment of China's path to becoming a strong agricultural country. How to enable agricultural enterprises to better adopt green technologies and conduct production and operation with the concept of sustainable development has become a key link. This article utilizes a structural equation model (SEM) to analyze the role paths and mediating effects of organizational learning ability and policy orientation in agricultural enterprises' market orientation and willingness to adopt green technologies[ The definition of green technology in this paper refers to Guo Kesha, Tian Xiaoxiao. Green technology and green transformation of industrial development mode [J]. Tianjin Social Sciences, 2024 (02) :99-107, including green manufacturing (production) technology and green service technology.]. The results show that market orientation, organizational learning ability, and policy effectiveness have significant direct positive impacts on the willingness to adopt; market orientation has a significant positive impact on agricultural enterprises' organizational learning ability, organizational learning ability has a significant positive impact on policy orientation, and market orientation has a significant positive impact on policy effectiveness; the results of mediation analysis also indicate that learning ability has a significant mediating effect between market orientation and willingness to adopt, and policy effectiveness has a significant mediating effect between market orientation and willingness to adopt. Through difference analysis, it is believed that the mediating effects of the three paths are equally important, and organizational learning ability and policy effectiveness play a partial mediating role in agricultural enterprises' willingness to adopt green technologies. Based on this, policy suggestions are proposed to improve enterprises' own organizational learning ability, increase the promotion of policies related to green technologies, improve relevant policies for the application of green technologies, and increase research and development efforts for green technologies.

title: Why Are There So Many Power Laws in Economics?
summary: Power law distributions are ubiquitous in socioeconomic contexts. While their general properties are well understood, it is often less clear why they regularly appear in empirical data. What are the generative mechanisms leading to power la
content: Power law distributions are ubiquitous in socioeconomic contexts. While their general properties are well understood, it is often less clear why they regularly appear in empirical data. What are the generative mechanisms leading to power law distributions and why do we so often observe such distributions in socioeconomic contexts? This paper aims to partly fill this gap by discussing two candidate mechanisms, cumulative advantage and random multiplication, that appear regularly, but in variegated forms, in political economy arguments. These mechanisms do not only seem especially relevant for understanding power law distributions in socioeconomic contexts, but can also be captured in simple formal setups. On this basis, we identify core formal properties and explore how these mechanisms can be mapped to real-world problems and processes. In addition, we discuss the relation of power laws and their generative mechanisms to related concepts relevant in heterodox economics, like path dependence, cumulative processes, power asymmetries or non-ergodicity.

title: Differentiating Climate Efficiency in Agrifood Systems: A Stylised Simulation Model With Carbon Opportunity Costs
summary: ABSTRACT The agrifood system generates around one‐third of global greenhouse gas emissions, driven by land use and land‐use change. Existing policy assessments focus on net emissions changes, overlooking efficiency losses within market dyna
content: ABSTRACT The agrifood system generates around one‐third of global greenhouse gas emissions, driven by land use and land‐use change. Existing policy assessments focus on net emissions changes, overlooking efficiency losses within market dynamics and the carbon sequestration potential of land. This study enhances agrifood policy assessment by extending ex‐post model reporting and differentiating efficiency changes on the supply and demand side. As proof of concept, a simplified partial equilibrium model with two regions and two commodities simulates different taxation and subsidisation schemes. Incorporating carbon opportunity costs to capture land's carbon sink capacity alters efficiency rankings of production sites and commodities and changes the assessment of policies' climate impacts. Disaggregating climate efficiency into supply and demand side reveals efficiency losses obscured when assessing solely net emission changes. Accounting for carbon opportunity costs and differentiating between supply‐ and demand‐side efficiency reveals effects that net emission reporting does not capture and can, thus, inform policy design. This contribution is best read as a methodological proof of concept. Additionally, we describe the steps and the challenges to integrate the developed framework into a full‐scale simulation model for applied policy analysis.

title: Biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland
summary: Abstract Halting biodiversity loss requires systematic action from all sectors of society. The public sector is a significant actor globally in creating markets for goods and services, public procurement representing on average 13–20% of na
content: Abstract Halting biodiversity loss requires systematic action from all sectors of society. The public sector is a significant actor globally in creating markets for goods and services, public procurement representing on average 13–20% of national gross domestic product. In this study, we assessed the biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland in 2022. We applied the consumption-based biodiversity footprint model BIOVALENT, where data from EXIOBASE and LC-IMPACT databases are combined to connect economic activities in the value chains of procured goods and services with the resulting biodiversity impact. Our results indicate that (i) largest contributors to the biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland in 2022 were construction and maintenance services (19%), utilities consisting of water and energy consumption and rentals of real estate (15%), health and social services (11%), and medical and care supplies (10%); (ii) the greatest potential in mitigating the biodiversity footprint lies in construction and maintenance, utilities, medical and care supplies, machines and appliances, and accommodation and catering services; and (iii) according to the model on average over 90% of the biodiversity footprint was located overseas. These insights from our analysis can be used for guiding strategic prioritization, more detailed assessments, and mitigation actions towards most impactful procurement categories. The considerable role of the value chain in the harmful biodiversity impacts calls for significant changes in the public procurement practices, given their influence throughout production systems and consumption patterns.

title: Space economy and strategic development in ASEAN pathways to 2035
summary: The ASEAN space economy is entering a rapid growth phase toward 2035, alongside a global market projected to reach USD 1.8 trillion. ASEAN’s share is expected to scale to approximately USD 80–200 billion, driven by three key engines: Earth
content: The ASEAN space economy is entering a rapid growth phase toward 2035, alongside a global market projected to reach USD 1.8 trillion. ASEAN’s share is expected to scale to approximately USD 80–200 billion, driven by three key engines: Earth Observation (EO) commercialization, SATCOM expansion via high-throughput systems, and rising demand for ISR and Space Domain Awareness (SDA). EO in Southeast Asia alone is projected to triple to USD 45 billion by 2030. Thailand is positioned as a regional hub through THEOS-2, Thaicom platforms, national space policy, and a multi-orbit spaceport strategy enabling upstream and downstream integration. Using a bottom-up forecast model aligned with the Space Capacity Ladder (SCL), ASEAN is expected to sustain a 4.4–11.1% share of the global space economy by 2035, led by Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.

title: From Electrification on Component-Level to Software-Defined Vehicles: The Role of Modular Smart Corner Systems in Next-Generation Electric Vehicle Architecture
summary: Abstract The transition to software-defined vehicles (SDVs) necessitates a paradigm shift in both control strategies and vehicle architecture. The EU-funded SmartCorners project addresses this challenge by developing integrated smart corner
content: Abstract The transition to software-defined vehicles (SDVs) necessitates a paradigm shift in both control strategies and vehicle architecture. The EU-funded SmartCorners project addresses this challenge by developing integrated smart corner systems (SCS), which combine in-wheel motor (IWM) propulsion, brake-by-wire, active suspension actuator, and steer-by-wire functionality in a single module. These SCS are embedded within a highly adaptable skateboard chassis architecture, enabling scalable deployment across diverse vehicle platforms. The SmartCorners project targets to demonstrate significant advancements, including improvement in real-world driving range, reduction of component and system costs, an increasement in interior volume, and a development time drop of the EV systems enabled by digital-twin-based design methodologies. Beyond these performance gains, SmartCorners establishes the foundational principles of modularity, adaptability, and software integration that underpin the evolution toward SDVs. These achievements highlight a critical bridge between electrified component innovation and the holistic software-defined mobility systems of the future.

title: Raw sugarcane bagasse hydrochar outperforms carbon nanotubes in microbial fuel cell power generation
summary: Abstract The commercialization of microbial fuel cells (MFCs) is currently limited by the high cost of standard electrode materials like carbon nanotubes (CNTs). This study introduces a high-performance, low-cost alternative: sugarcane baga
content: Abstract The commercialization of microbial fuel cells (MFCs) is currently limited by the high cost of standard electrode materials like carbon nanotubes (CNTs). This study introduces a high-performance, low-cost alternative: sugarcane bagasse hydrochar. We evaluated raw (RSBH), phosphated (PSBH), and sulfonated (SSBH) hydrochars as symmetric electrodes against a commercial CNT control. While acid functionalization enhanced thermal stability and char yields, the unmodified hydrochar yielded the most striking electrochemical results. Ni-RSBH achieved a peak power density of 1008 mW/m2, quadrupling the performance of the commercial Ni-CNT (235 mW/m2). Post-operation analysis revealed that Ni-RSBH developed exceptional biofilm compatibility, with anodic capacitance surging to 51.03 F/g compared to just 3.01 F/g for Ni-CNT. Although the phosphated variant (Ni-PSBH) offered superior voltage stability (0.68–0.71 V), the raw hydrochar provided the optimal balance of conductivity and biological activity. These findings demonstrate that minimally processed agricultural waste can outperform engineered nanomaterials, presenting a scalable, circular-economy solution for bioelectrochemical systems.

title: A 3D Multitask Graph Neural Network Framework for Ames Mutagenicity Prediction
summary: The long, complex, and costly process of drug development makes early, reliable toxicity assessment a central challenge in pharmaceutical research. Accurately predicting drug-induced toxicity and mutagenicity is crucial for guiding decision
content: The long, complex, and costly process of drug development makes early, reliable toxicity assessment a central challenge in pharmaceutical research. Accurately predicting drug-induced toxicity and mutagenicity is crucial for guiding decision-making and reducing late-stage attrition. Deep learning approaches can predict the results of the Ames mutagenicity test, a standard screening method; however, most existing models rely on molecular descriptors that limit structural representation, lack interpretability, and do not account for Ames results of individual bacterial strains. Graph neural networks (GNNs) are chemically intuitive and overcome these limitations. This work presents a deep learning, multitask GNN model for predicting Ames mutagenicity. The proposed approach outperforms existing models, including those from the Ames/QSAR International Challenge. Furthermore, the model is highly interpretable. Explainability analysis of atom-level contributions reveal that the model is capable of learning known structural alerts associated with mutagenicity, along with additional molecular patterns and three-dimensional structural properties. Importantly, these insights are captured in a strain-specific manner, highlighting the value of a multitask approach. Finally, the model is able to identify previously unreported molecular substructures potentially associated with mutagenicity, supporting its utility in drug design and development.

title: Electricity retail pricing as incentives for load optimization in Vietnam
summary: Abstract Vietnam’s pathway to net-zero emissions by 2050 has so far relied primarily on large-scale renewable energy investments, with limited use of demand-side management. This study evaluates how alternative retail electricity pricing sc
content: Abstract Vietnam’s pathway to net-zero emissions by 2050 has so far relied primarily on large-scale renewable energy investments, with limited use of demand-side management. This study evaluates how alternative retail electricity pricing schemes - flat tariffs, Time-of-Use (TOU), Critical Peak Pricing (CPP), and a TOU-CPP hybrid - shape demand flexibility, system costs, emissions, consumer welfare, and reliability in Vietnam. The analysis uses SWITCH 2.0, an integrated capacity expansion and dispatch model with an iterative demand-response module, to Vietnam’s electricity system in 2050. Relative to flat pricing, the modeled TOU designs reduce total system costs by up to 15% and CO2 emissions by 17.2-37.5%, while increasing consumer welfare. Consecutive TOU blocks capture substantial benefits, whereas adding CPP produces little additional improvement. Endogenous block assignment achieves the lowest system cost and reduces storage investment, but does not yield the lowest emissions or highest consumer welfare. Sensitivity analysis confirms lower unit costs and emissions and higher consumer welfare under consecutive TOU than under matched flat-pricing cases across seven demand-response parameter combinations. However, the magnitude of these benefits depends strongly on the share of load available for within-day rescheduling. Demand shifting toward solar-rich hours also changes transmission utilization, relieving pressure on some corridors while increasing it elsewhere. The findings support a staged transition toward TOU pricing with simple consecutive blocks, accompanied by enabling technologies and coordinated transmission planning. The results represent conditional system-level outcomes rather than estimates of realized consumer responses or distributional effects.

title: Distributed small-reservoir pumped-storage hydropower in Europe: a GIS screening under drawdown and karst constraints
summary: Continental pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) atlases omit schemes built from small reservoirs, although such sites could provide distributed flexibility. We screen this resource across 37 European countries, detecting closed depressions and
content: Continental pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) atlases omit schemes built from small reservoirs, although such sites could provide distributed flexibility. We screen this resource across 37 European countries, detecting closed depressions and water bodies and pairing upper and lower reservoirs under land-use, protection and grid-distance constraints. The reproducible workflow uses open pan-European data, a hybrid terrain stack (FABDEM; national lidar in Norway and Sweden) and an explicit allowable water-level variation for lake volume. At a 5-km grid distance and 1-m drawdown, exact maximum-weight matching gives an all-size screened bound of 2.57 TWh; excluding mapped-karst footprints for purpose-built reservoirs and sites above 2500 m leaves 0.58 TWh, of which a 21 115-site portfolio capped at 100 MWh per site stores 0.40 TWh (0.24 TWh, EU-27). Replacing FABDEM by national lidar cuts Norway’s and Sweden’s screened energy with 72% each (328.7 to 92.1 and 67.3 to 18.5 GWh): usable lake volume barely moves ( − 0.4 %), but pairs containing a dry basin collapse because that basin binds. A Sobol analysis makes maximum pair distance and karst treatment the joint controls (total effects 0.49 and 0.48). This is an exploratory first screening, not deployable capacity: it ranks where national feasibility studies should look, and their constraints can only reduce it.

title: Mechanical deterioration and damage evolution of coal specimens under drying–wetting cycles
summary: Abstract Utilizing underground mine reservoirs for pumped storage power stations represents a highly promising approach for large-scale energy storage. However, the long-term exposure of coal pillar dams to drying-wetting cycles (DWC) poses
content: Abstract Utilizing underground mine reservoirs for pumped storage power stations represents a highly promising approach for large-scale energy storage. However, the long-term exposure of coal pillar dams to drying-wetting cycles (DWC) poses a severe risk of structural instability. This study investigated the mechanical degradation and damage mechanisms of coal specimens, leveraging triaxial loading coupled with acoustic emission (AE) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) monitoring. The results indicated that the compressive strength and cohesion underwent non-uniform, multi-stage degradation with increasing DWC, with the most acute deterioration occurring after the first cycle. AE monitoring revealed that with increasing DWC, the frequency of high-amplitude AE events escalated, and their peaks shifted forward. Concurrently, the overall b -value exhibited a downward trend. Analysis of the RA-AF characteristics confirmed that the proportion of shear fracture events escalated significantly with increasing DWC, triggering a failure mode transition from micro-tensile cracking to macro-shear sliding. NMR testing showed that the T 2 spectra exhibited a predominantly unimodal distribution, with micropores dominating the pore network. Under the action of DWC, the dissolution and spalling of hydrophilic minerals drove the transformation of internal micropores and mesopores into macropores. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for the stability assessment of underground reservoir-based PHES systems.

title: Water-soluble titanium(IV) tris-catecholate metal coordination complex as a highly negative negolyte for alkaline aqueous redox flow battery
summary: The titanium(IV) tris-catecholate metal coordination complex (Ti(cat) 3 ) is investigated as a negolyte candidate for alkaline aqueous flow batteries. The Ti(cat) 3 complex exhibits a low redox potential of −1.13 V versus the standard hydro
content: The titanium(IV) tris-catecholate metal coordination complex (Ti(cat) 3 ) is investigated as a negolyte candidate for alkaline aqueous flow batteries. The Ti(cat) 3 complex exhibits a low redox potential of −1.13 V versus the standard hydrogen electrode, which enables a high cell potential (>1.6 V) when paired with ferro-/ferricyanide. Electrochemical studies show that the redox potential of Ti(cat) 3 is pH-independent, but that highly alkaline conditions (pH > 12) significantly reduce its electrochemical behaviour. The apparent capacity fade of the battery is strongly correlated to parasitic hydrogen evolution that causes electrolyte imbalance and results in non-intrinsic capacity decay. The battery exhibits an intrinsic capacity fade of 2.51% per day at 50 mA/cm 2 . The influence of the charge and discharge cut-off voltage is investigated and evaluated by using in-situ measurements of the redox potential and pH. Here, it is found that the discharge cut-off voltage can minimize the degradation of the Ti(cat) 3 complex, and that tuning this parameter reduces the intrinsic capacity fade to 0.31% per day at 30 mA/cm 2 . These findings highlight both the opportunities and the challenges of the Ti(cat) 3 complex as a low-potential negolyte candidate for high-voltage aqueous batteries.

title: Government Failure and Corporate Reform
summary: Corporate law has been racked by a decades-long debate. Shareholder primacy theorists suggest that corporate leaders should focus exclusively on maximizing financial returns to shareholders, while stakeholder governance theorists suggest th
content: Corporate law has been racked by a decades-long debate. Shareholder primacy theorists suggest that corporate leaders should focus exclusively on maximizing financial returns to shareholders, while stakeholder governance theorists suggest that corporate leaders should consider a broader range of concerns such as impacts on workers and the environment. Though the battle has been fought intensely on many fronts for years, there is one area of apparent agreement. Most commentators view stakeholder governance as a kind of second-best regulation. Ideally, the government would tend to worker and environmental concerns through real regulations, imposing financial penalties on corporations that behave in socially destructive ways. Corporate leaders could then focus on financial returns, given the knowledge that bad behavior would not be profitable. It is only when the government fails in its basic task by refusing to issue or enforce necessary regulations that it becomes necessary for corporations to balance different concerns internally. But although it seems to be a point of broad agreement, the idea that stakeholder governance is a response to government failure is incomplete. This Article unpacks that claim and reveals its shortcomings. It is far from obvious whether the government's refusal to regulate in a space is a failure or simply a result of the democratic process given widespread disagreement. And even an "ideal" government would face limitations in its ability to drive good outcomes. Statutes and regulations are inherently limited tools, and there are many areas such as speech and dignitary interests where the government cannot interfere or provide an adequate solution. Understanding these shortcomings deepens the analysis of the relationship between corporate governance and the political process and reveals fresh insights about the debate between shareholder primacy and stakeholder governance.

title: Получение карбоната кальция с заданными свойствами крупности как фактор эффективной утилизации техногенного гипсосодержащего сырья
summary: This study focuses on developing a method for utilizing phosphogypsum, a large-tonnage waste product from phosphate raw material processing, whose disposal sites are sources of complex negative impacts on the environment. As a promising app
content: This study focuses on developing a method for utilizing phosphogypsum, a large-tonnage waste product from phosphate raw material processing, whose disposal sites are sources of complex negative impacts on the environment. As a promising approach to the utilization of gypsum-containing waste, the study considers the interaction of phosphogypsum with a sodium carbonate solution (carbonate conversion), which yields calcium carbonate, a marketable product referred to as phosphochalk. Existing technologies typically produce a fine-grained material, which hinders filtration and restricts the potential applications of phosphochalk. This study aims to determine the carbonate conversion parameters that enable the production of phosphochalk with tailored particle size characteristics while maintaining a high degree of feedstock conversion. A series of single-factor experiments was carried out to evaluate the influence of reaction conditions – temperature, Na2CO3 concentration in the carbonate solution, liquid-to-solid (L:S) ratio, and phase contact time – on the conversion of CaSO4·2H2O. The results showed that raising the conversion temperature to 90-100 °C and increasing the L:S ratio to 10 promote intensive nucleation of CaCO3 crystals and the formation of large agglomerates. A Na2CO3 concentration of 250 g/dm3 and a phase contact time of up to 3 h together yield phosphochalk with a particle size of D90 = 45 μm at a conversion degree of 98.8 %. In terms of its characteristics, the resulting product is suitable for use in the metallurgical industry as a raw material for flux production, which demonstrates its competitiveness in the secondary raw materials market. The recommendations developed in this work enable the design of a low-waste technology for processing technogenic raw materials, consistent with the principles of sustainable development and helping to reduce the environmental burden.

title: Integrating Safety and Sustainability: A Grid-Independent Ultralight Quadricycle for Secure Urban Mobility
summary: Abstract Light electric vehicles (LEVs) offer sustainable urban mobility through low energy consumption and compact design. However, broader adoption requires integrating energy autonomy and road safety assessments into the initial design p
content: Abstract Light electric vehicles (LEVs) offer sustainable urban mobility through low energy consumption and compact design. However, broader adoption requires integrating energy autonomy and road safety assessments into the initial design phase. This study introduces a novel combined evaluation of grid independence and crash safety for a pedal-assisted quadricycle featuring vehicle-integrated photovoltaics (VIPV). A Florence-based case study first optimises geometry and VIPV placement to maximise solar yield under urban conditions. Second, simulations quantify occupant injury risk in heterogeneous traffic with increasing LEV market penetration, addressing the scarcity of real-world crash data. Results show that roof-oriented VIPV and parking-agnostic geometry significantly reduce external charging reliance. Concurrently, safety analyses confirm the vehicle’s suitability for low-speed environments, specifically 30 km/h zones. This research establishes a generalisable methodology: while calibrated on Florence’s topology and solar irradiance, the framework provides a scalable tool to minimise grid dependency and enhance safety across diverse climatic and traffic contexts.

title: Accelerating Public Charging Infrastructure: Micro-Level Approach Enables Efficient Planning of Charging Locations Based on Suitability of Public Space
summary: Abstract Expanding public electric-vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure is a pressing municipal need, yet planning is slowed by site-specific public-space constraints. To address this challenge, we developed a method that considers all poss
content: Abstract Expanding public electric-vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure is a pressing municipal need, yet planning is slowed by site-specific public-space constraints. To address this challenge, we developed a method that considers all possible sites for charging infrastructure in public space and conducts a suitability analysis based on potential conflicts, including preservation orders, overlays with bike lanes, and vegetation protection. Our method incorporates demand data to identify hotspots for infrastructure placement. A buffer-based analysis is applied to each suitable site, assigning the best-scoring locations. We applied our method to a neighborhood in Berlin, Germany, and obtained a selection of sites that meet demand without generating conflicts in public space. This study delivers a high-resolution output and a flexible framework for diverse urban settings, making the charging infrastructure expansion process more efficient.

title: Получение удобрений из отходов различного генезиса для рекультивации нарушенных земель и благоустройства территорий
summary: This study addresses the loss of land for other uses resulting from economic activities and waste disposal, highlights the need to develop alternative fertilizers suitable for the biological stage of land reclamation and subsequent landscap
content: This study addresses the loss of land for other uses resulting from economic activities and waste disposal, highlights the need to develop alternative fertilizers suitable for the biological stage of land reclamation and subsequent landscaping, and examines the resource potential of industrial wastes for producing nutrient amendments. The most promising waste processing approaches involve producing sewage sludge-based fertilizers through composting with other industrial wastes of various origins. A combined computational and experimental approach was used to develop composting mixtures, enabling optimization of the C:N, moisture content, and pH while incorporating visual assessments during laboratory trial mixing. The fertilizers produced were assessed qualitatively and quantitatively for veterinary, sanitary, hygienic, toxicological, and agrochemical parameters in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. A plant growth experiment using artificial soil demonstrated their effectiveness in improving key plant productivity parameters, including seed germination, plant biomass, and maximum plant height. Potential factors limiting fertilizer application were identified as toxic element contents and possible imbalances between moisture retention and air exchange caused by reduced soil substrate density at high fertilizer mass fractions. These findings confirm the feasibility of reusing wastes of various origins to restore land quality and expand the range of alternative fertilizers.

title: Химический состав и экологический ущерб отходов цианирования Берикульского золотоизвлекательного завода (Кемеровская область)
summary: The article presents the results of a comprehensive study of the stored waste from the Berikul gold mining plant (Kemerovo Region), using geochemical, geophysical, and econometric methods. Using electrical tomography method, geoelectric sec
content: The article presents the results of a comprehensive study of the stored waste from the Berikul gold mining plant (Kemerovo Region), using geochemical, geophysical, and econometric methods. Using electrical tomography method, geoelectric sections (transverse and along the dam’s contour) and a 3D model of the storage facility were constructed; they describe the location of zones with a specific electrical resistance varying within the range of 3-800 Ohm·m, which makes it possible to determine the configuration of conductive zones in the internal structure. From the stored waste, which has a thickness of 5-7 m, mineralized water filters into the underground horizons, resulting in the formation of a depression characterized by an electrical resistivity (ER) of ~200 Ohm·m, which is significantly lower than the ER of the surrounding rocks. The zone of reduced resistance extends deeper than 40 m, which clearly indicates the vertical spread of the drainage system, possibly along a weakened zone in the granodiorite massif. Additionally, the formation of highly conductive areas is clearly visible on resistance maps up to 20-40 m. Samples of solid matter and water were taken from the resulting small bodies of water to determine their chemical composition. The stored waste is characterized by a contrasting composition in different parts of the storage facility; accordingly, both the physicochemical parameters and the ability of elements to transfer into solutions vary over a wide range. The majority of the waste material produces an acidic reaction in the pore waters and has a high mineralization. Water extracts from the samples cakes indicate a significant proportion of easily soluble compounds in the waste material. The content of metals and metalloids in water from surface ponds (maximum Fe 7800, Al 590, Zn 160, As 1600, Be 0.022 mg/l) indicates a high environmental hazard posed by these waste materials, while also suggesting the potential attractiveness of the site for the further recovery of useful components. An assessment has been carried out of the damage caused by the storage facility to water bodies within its influence zone – 470 million rubles.

title: Перспективы использования отходов содового производства в различных отраслях
summary: This paper presents a review and analysis of scientific articles and patents addressing the disposal and processing of soda production waste. Examples of methods for reducing the toxicity of sludge, using waste in construction (including ro
content: This paper presents a review and analysis of scientific articles and patents addressing the disposal and processing of soda production waste. Examples of methods for reducing the toxicity of sludge, using waste in construction (including road construction), and processing it into chemical compounds are provided. Particular attention is paid to the use of sludge for soil reclamation. The ammonia-soda process (the Solvay process) for producing soda ash is the predominant method worldwide. A significant drawback of this process is the generation of hazardous production waste, which necessitates compliance with environmental requirements and regulations during storage and processing. Russian practices for managing soda production waste lag behind European ones due to low prices for primary natural raw materials, the heterogeneity of waste composition and properties, the need for preliminary waste treatment, and the low level of environmental payments by enterprises for waste disposal. Tightening environmental safety requirements for soda ash production waste and the high cost of maintaining settling ponds are driving the development of processing methods. The choice of processing method depends on the plant᾽s location, energy capacity, and the company᾽s financial condition. The use of sludge in the production of building materials is limited by the presence of chloride ions, small particle size, thixotropic properties of the material, and variability in sludge composition. Road construction is the most promising avenue in terms of disposal volumes and the use of waste without additional treatment. The use of waste for land reclamation requires a selective approach to site selection and additional research. Despite the wide range of possible applications for soda production waste, the problem of its disposal remains pressing. This is due to the volumes of soda production and the resulting waste, as well as the need for financial investment to implement disposal methods

title: การสงเสรมกญชงเปนพชทางเลอกเพอบรรเทาปญหาไฟปาและเสรมสรางรายได: กรอบแนวคดการออกแบบเชงนโยบายจงหวดแมฮองสอน
source: Warasan Wichai Lae Songserm Wichakan Kaset
summary: Mae Hong Son (MHS) Province in northern Thailand constantly faces social and environmental crises caused by forest fires. This study designed policies to integrate hemp into the agricultural extension system to mitigate land preparation bur
content: Mae Hong Son (MHS) Province in northern Thailand constantly faces social and environmental crises caused by forest fires. This study designed policies to integrate hemp into the agricultural extension system to mitigate land preparation burning. A survey of 200 households from three communities, in-depth interviews, focus group discussions (FGDs), and observations were conducted. The results showed that forest fires cause distinct impacts on livelihoods, health, and the environment, while existing control measures are insufficient. Hemp products have significant potential as an inclusive alternative for income enhancement and value-added product development. A Social Return on Investment (SROI) of 2.5:1 illustrated significant economic and social benefits. This framework shifts toward livelihood-based mitigation, demonstrating that integrating a structured hemp value chain into agricultural extension services can effectively reduce burning and enhance community resilience in MHS.
