title: Ancient human occupation alters modern forest traits, structure and biomass in neotropical forests.
summary: There is considerable debate as to how extensively neotropical forests were shaped by ancient people. This uncertainty has implications for the global carbon cycle because forest plots may be disproportionately located in formerly occupied
content: There is considerable debate as to how extensively neotropical forests were shaped by ancient people. This uncertainty has implications for the global carbon cycle because forest plots may be disproportionately located in formerly occupied areas, potentially biasing estimates of tropical forest growth and carbon uptake. Ground measurements within the formerly occupied Maya city of Xmakabatun (400BCE to 800CE), now covered by forest, revealed significantly higher forest biomass, modified leaf traits, and distinct species composition on archaeological structures (i.e. ancient buildings) relative to control and former agricultural areas. We then used GEDI and trait-based remote sensing across the broader region to show that forest regions with greater quantities of known archaeological settlement also had significantly higher biomass and modified leaf traits. We next extend this approach to the Amazon basin, where ancient land-use histories are less certain. Using similar remote sensing techniques, we found that forests near Amazonian Dark Earth (terra preta) sites (N=503) were shorter but had slightly more foliage (~6%), whereas forests near geoglyphs (N=961) were taller but had much less bulk (20%) than the control forest plots. From these relationships, we estimate that ancient human occupation has increased modern Amazonian biomass by, on average, 2.8±1.6%, an amounts equivalent to ~1% of global above-ground biomass. Together, these results demonstrate that ancient land use has left detectable legacies in the traits and structure of modern forests and suggest that remotely sensed biomass and/or leaf trait datasets may also provide a tool for regional-scale archaeological mapping.

title: Phylogeny and intraspecific variability dominate nitrogen fixer biomass responses to nitrogen enrichment
summary: Anthropogenic nitrogen (N) enrichment profoundly influences the growth of N-fixing plants, but the drivers underlying their highly variable biomass responses remain poorly quantified. Through a meta-analysis of 2,110 paired observations acr
content: Anthropogenic nitrogen (N) enrichment profoundly influences the growth of N-fixing plants, but the drivers underlying their highly variable biomass responses remain poorly quantified. Through a meta-analysis of 2,110 paired observations across 76 N-fixing plant species from 121 experiments, we demonstrate that N enrichment increases N-fixing plant biomass by 14.2% on average, with responses ranging from −99.4% to 1301.3%. Intraspecific variability (26.9%; i.e., variation among individuals within species) and plant phylogeny (21.1%) represent substantial yet frequently overlooked sources of uncertainty in biomass responses of N-fixing plants to N enrichment, even though environmental conditions (climatic and edaphic factors) and experimental design (N enrichment rate and duration) account for a significant portion of biomass response variation. Intraspecific variability, phylogeny, and experimental design collectively explain a larger proportion of variance in root than in shoot biomass responses, whereas environmental conditions show the opposite trend. These results provide quantitative evidence that phylogeny and intraspecific variability are indispensable for accurately predicting the response of N-fixing plants to global change. Nitrogen enrichment alters the growth of nitrogen-fixing plants, but responses vary widely. This meta-analysis shows that phylogeny and intraspecific variation are major contributors to that variability.

title: Ionic Liquids‐Mediated Decarboxylation Reactions
summary: ABSTRACT Decarboxylation is a key process in organic chemistry, wherein a carboxyl group is removed in the form of carbon dioxide. Due to cutting‐edge research in the field of decarboxylation, the green chemistry matrices involving methods
content: ABSTRACT Decarboxylation is a key process in organic chemistry, wherein a carboxyl group is removed in the form of carbon dioxide. Due to cutting‐edge research in the field of decarboxylation, the green chemistry matrices involving methods have always attracted chemists. Recently, ionic liquids (ILs) demonstrated a very efficient role for the decarboxylation reactions with their unbeatable properties, like negligible vapor pressure and their tunable nature, which can be adjusted to help in dissolving substrates. The adjustable properties of ILs further express them as designer solvents, and additionally, their hydrogen‐bonding capabilities speed up the organic reactions, leading to enhanced performances. Their nonvolatile nature further makes them eco‐friendly and easy to handle, as the product gets separated effortlessly, and hence can be recycled and reused. Current review focuses on the investigation studies articulating ILs in decarboxylation reactions, with scaffolds bearing carboxyl groups such as carboxylic acids, β ‐keto acids, malonic acids, and aromatic carboxylic acids. Basically, ILs are a big step forward in decarboxylation chemistry offering a flexible and eco‐friendly platform. The ongoing research is bound to uncover even more exciting possibilities for sustainable synthesis, making ILs an eco‐friendly tool in modern organic chemistry.

title: Transport and fate of bacteria through porous medium: a review
summary: Groundwater contamination due to the presence of pathogenic bacteria may pose a threat to community well-being and could lead to outbreaks of waterborne diseases. These bacteria can move from their accidental/anthropogenic release point to
content: Groundwater contamination due to the presence of pathogenic bacteria may pose a threat to community well-being and could lead to outbreaks of waterborne diseases. These bacteria can move from their accidental/anthropogenic release point to groundwater through infiltered rainwater and contaminate the aquifer. On the other hand, the efficient transportation of bacteria through the sub-surface medium increases the possibility of successful bioaugmentation. Therefore, understanding the fate and mechanism of transport of bacteria through the sub-surface medium is important in the context of both groundwater risk assessment and bioremediation. This review summarizes the various studies conducted on bacterial transportation and which demonstrate the usefulness of both experimental and theoretical approaches. The review addresses the complex interactions between a porous medium and the mechanisms of bacterial transport through experimental as well as modelling approaches.

title: Energy Balance Closure and Thermophysical Property Uncertainty in Spent NiMo and NiMoV Catalyst Recovery: Heat Effects, Thermal Integration, and Predictive Reliability—A Critical Review
summary: Spent nickel–molybdenum (NiMo) and nickel–molybdenum–vanadium (NiMoV) hydroprocessing catalysts combine valuable metals with oils, coke, sulfides, and complex oxide supports. Their recovery routes integrate thermal pretreatment, oxidative o
content: Spent nickel–molybdenum (NiMo) and nickel–molybdenum–vanadium (NiMoV) hydroprocessing catalysts combine valuable metals with oils, coke, sulfides, and complex oxide supports. Their recovery routes integrate thermal pretreatment, oxidative or alkaline roasting, aqueous separation, and product finishing, but energy claims are often incomparable because boundaries, reference states, thermophysical assumptions, and unmeasured heat losses differ. This critical review develops a property-consistent framework for steady-state and transient energy-balance closure, evaluates sensible and latent heat and reaction enthalpy contributions, and connects thermal integration to uncertainty-aware route assessment. The review critically evaluates a predominantly 2020–2026 bibliography supplemented with a directly relevant route model and foundational reconciliation literature; evidence is evaluated by relevance and transferability rather than assumed uniform quality. The proposed framework distinguishes metered utilities, calculated stream enthalpies, reaction heat, and residual losses; specifies minimum reporting data for solids, gases, and aqueous streams; and integrates reconciliation, sensitivity analysis, and uncertainty propagation. The principal conclusion is that credible energy comparisons require closed elemental and phase inventories, consistent enthalpy reference states, and explicit uncertainty intervals before heat recovery or route superiority can be claimed.

title: Photosynthetic markers reveal recovery of Pisum sativum from pathogen infection following fungicide treatment
summary: Many plant-pathogen interactions can severely compromise plant growth and productivity, highlighting the need for effective strategies to prevent or mitigate infection and limit disease progression. Pathogen infection disrupts photosynthesi
content: Many plant-pathogen interactions can severely compromise plant growth and productivity, highlighting the need for effective strategies to prevent or mitigate infection and limit disease progression. Pathogen infection disrupts photosynthesis and carbon metabolism; however, the physiological consequences of fungicides, both beneficial and potentially phytotoxic, remain insufficiently characterised despite their widespread use in crop protection. After preliminary experiments in Arabidopsis thaliana , we investigated the impact of Ascochyta pisi infection on Pisum sativum and evaluated the efficacy of tebuconazole applied preventively or curatively. Determining the best time to apply the fungicide to the crops appears to be crucial. Photosynthetic function was assessed by PAM chlorophyll fluorometry, and pigment content and the abundance of selected chloroplastic proteins (cFBP1, TRX f, PsaC, D1/PsbA, and LHCII) were also determined. Infection caused a marked decline in Y(II) photosynthetic performance, accompanied by cFBP1 and TRX f decreased, and an induction of PsaC (PSI), the D1/PsbA protein (PSII), and LHCII. Curative tebuconazole application partially restored photosynthetic and metabolic functions, whereas preventive treatment did not fully counteract infection-induced alterations. Principal component analysis, integrating all measured variables, clearly separated the treatments and supported a stronger curative than preventive effect of the fungicide under the conditions tested. This combined physiological and biochemical approach enables robust comparisons across treatments and helps identify trade-offs between disease suppression and host performance. Overall, these results provide an integrative and quantitative framework using an effective and reliable methodology for assessing plant physiological responses to biotic stress and inform more sustainable crop protection strategies, particularly under increasing climate pressure in Mediterranean agroecosystems.

title: Methods for theoretical simulation of microvascular networks
summary: The microcirculation consists of an extensive network of small blood vessels. It is responsible for transport of substances including oxygen, nutrients and waste products to all parts of the body. Microcirculatory function can be studied ex
content: The microcirculation consists of an extensive network of small blood vessels. It is responsible for transport of substances including oxygen, nutrients and waste products to all parts of the body. Microcirculatory function can be studied experimentally using microscopic imaging techniques. However, many aspects of microvascular function are difficult to observe directly, and theoretical models and simulations have made valuable contributions to our understanding of the microcirculation. Here we review several theoretical approaches for investigating several key aspects of microvascular networks, including blood flow in microvessels, exchange of oxygen and other substances between blood and tissue, short-term local regulation of blood flow, and long-term structural adaptation and remodeling, including angiogenesis. A recurrent theme is the impact of the heterogeneous structure of the networks on the functional properties of the microvasculature. This heterogeneity arises from geometrical constraints and from the stochastic nature of microvessel growth. Theoretical simulations can be used to investigate how active mechanisms of flow regulation and remodeling can compensate for the inherent heterogeneity, and how failure of these mechanisms can contribute to impaired tissue function in diseases.

title: Aranya Kanda In Ramayana: The Moral Foundation for Sustainable Forest Governance in Contemporary World
summary: Abstract Due to evolving significance to Indian Knowledge System; Ramayana has been subject for researchers for getting better solutions for Legal Systems in contemporary era. The Socio-Legal approaches in the form of Philosophy discussed i
content: Abstract Due to evolving significance to Indian Knowledge System; Ramayana has been subject for researchers for getting better solutions for Legal Systems in contemporary era. The Socio-Legal approaches in the form of Philosophy discussed in Ramayana are evident to show the wisdom of Author of Ramayana-Sage Valmiki. On the backdrop of Sustainable Development in contemporary era, Ramayana is rich heritage of Ecological Wisdom playing a role of lighthouse to guide for better governance of Environment. Out of Seven parts of Ramayana; Aranya Kanda – the ‘Book of Forest’ highlights the relationship between Human Being and Forest. Author here, tries best to analyse the nexus between notions of Environmental Law and Sustainability in contemporary era & Aranya Kanda in Ramayana. Author has done comparative analysis of Forest management Practices implied in the Aranya Kanda and modern strategies of Community Forestry, Sacred Groves and Sustainable Livelihood to attain ecological harmony. This research studies the ecological ethics in Aranya Kanda to form philosophical basis of existing socio-legal systems governing forestry. This research contends that Aranya Kanda is philosophical basis for ecological perspective-a notion which has close nexus with modern concepts of Conservation ethics and Participatory Forest Governance. This research creates further scope for other disciplines that how traditional narratives can be implemented in reality for better environmental management. It offers a transdisciplinary framework that bridges classical philosophy, environmental humanities, and forest ecology.

title: How Metal-to-Linker Ratio and Concentration Govern the Nucleation Mechanism of MOF-5-inspired Crystals: Insights from Multiscale Modeling
summary: Predicting whether a computationally designed metal organic framework can be synthesized remains difficult.While efforts developing predictive viability of synthesis metrics have focused on inherent thermodynamic stability, not much focus h
content: Predicting whether a computationally designed metal organic framework can be synthesized remains difficult.While efforts developing predictive viability of synthesis metrics have focused on inherent thermodynamic stability, not much focus has been placed on kinetics, nucleation mechanisms, and how these are impacted by synthesis conditions.Using the well-known MOF-5 in DMF system as a case study, we combine Hamiltonian replica exchange, coarse-grained molecular dynamics, unsupervised clustering, minimum free energy path (MFEP) analysis, and microkinetic modeling to examine how metal-to-linker ratio and linker concentration reshape the pathway, energetics, and kinetics of nucleation.At 20 mM linker concentration, we find that excess metal clearly thermodynamically and kinetically favors the formation of a crystalline nucleus, whereas stoichiometric metal-to-linker ratio and excess linker favor large amorphous aggregates.At excess metal conditions, we find that increasing concentration from 20 mM to 160 mM maintains thermodynamic favorability for the ordered nucleus but accelerates the pathway toward it.Within the concentration range tested, as concentration increased, aggregation also became more pronounced, and the dominant barrier became associated with healing instead of growth steps.Additionally, the nucleus yield and formation rate increased monotonically with concentration, albeit with clearly diminishing gains between 80 mM and 160 mM (well below the linker solubility limit).These results offer a plausible mechanistic rationale for the empirical preference for excess metal during MOF-5 synthesis and suggest that the benefits of higher precursor concentration diminish well before the linker solubility limit is reached.

title: Blue Bonds and Ocean Sustainability: Evidence from selected African countries
summary: Abstract This study examines the nexus between blue bond issuance and ocean sustainability in selected African countries. Ocean sustainability is a major concern in Africa, as catalytic projects aimed at guaranteeing a blue economy are scar
content: Abstract This study examines the nexus between blue bond issuance and ocean sustainability in selected African countries. Ocean sustainability is a major concern in Africa, as catalytic projects aimed at guaranteeing a blue economy are scarce and require substantial financing. The issue of blue bonds, a variation of blue finance, could be a plausible solution to finance ocean sustainability needs. Despite their importance, blue bonds face persistent barriers in the African context; therefore, they have been issued in only three countries to date: Seychelles, Gabon, and Cape Verde. Panel data from these countries for the years 2018–2023 were analysed using fixed-effects regressions. The study found that blue bond issuance is positively and significantly related to the ocean health index, implying that projects focused on ocean sustainability can be financed viably through blue bond proceeds. The growth rate of the gross domestic product was positive and significant, indicating that economic growth increases the sustainability of the oceans. Regulatory quality was significantly negative, indicating that ineffective regulatory enforcement stifles progress towards improving ocean sustainability. The proxies for carbon dioxide emissions and inflation were positively associated with ocean sustainability. There are several implications of these findings. Firstly, there is a need for the development of African capital markets to accommodate innovative financing through blue bonds to finance ocean sustainability-related projects. Secondly, African national governments must invest in financial infrastructure to support the development of the blue bond market and ensure robust institutional and capital market regulatory frameworks that align with international standards.

title: Quantitative Analysis of Spatiotemporal Asymmetric Dynamic Changes and Driving Mechanisms of Carbon Storage in the Huaihe River Basin
summary: Exploring the dynamic evolution of carbon storage plays a crucial role in maintaining ecological stability in river basins. This paper takes the Huai River Basin as the research object and uses the PLUS model to predict land use changes und
content: Exploring the dynamic evolution of carbon storage plays a crucial role in maintaining ecological stability in river basins. This paper takes the Huai River Basin as the research object and uses the PLUS model to predict land use changes under different development scenarios in the future. Based on the predicted results and meteorological, ecological and other data, the InVEST model was coupled to analyze the spatiotemporal changes of carbon storage under different scenarios in the future. The driving mechanism of carbon stock evolution within the watershed was ultimately analyzed using the GeoDetector model. The results show that (1) the land use pattern of the basin remained generally stable from 2000 to 2023, with cropland as the dominant land use type, impervious surfaces continuously expanding, and the areas of cropland, forestland, and grassland generally decreasing; (2) carbon storage in the basin generally showed a slowly declining trend, exhibiting a spatial pattern of high in the south and low in the north and high in the west and low in the east; (3) natural factors such as the DEM and slope have the greatest impact on the spatial distribution of carbon storage, the interactions among multiple factors are significantly enhanced, and the influence of socio-economic factors has gradually strengthened; and (4) by 2030, carbon storage increases under all scenarios, with the largest increase under the ecological protection scenario and the smallest under the economic development scenario. The results can provide a scientific basis for land use optimization, carbon sink enhancement, and ecological protection under the dual-carbon goals.

title: Estimation of biomass and carbon accumulation capacity of Peruvian Amazon rainforests under a climate change context
summary: Aim of study: The study assesses the carbon potential of forests in the Peruvian Amazon, focusing on modeling carbon within a climate change mitigation framework to improve our understanding of the regional capacity to store in forest ecosy
content: Aim of study: The study assesses the carbon potential of forests in the Peruvian Amazon, focusing on modeling carbon within a climate change mitigation framework to improve our understanding of the regional capacity to store in forest ecosystems. Area of study: San Martín Region, Peruvian Amazon. Material and methods: A total of six forest sites in the Amazonas region, located within San Martín and Loreto districts, were assessed. Structural measurements were recorded for all the trees and allometric equations were applied to estimate biomass. Additionally, altitude was recorded and its relationship with carbon storage was analyzed. Main results: The highest tree density was found in El Varillal and Ojo del Agua forests with 360 and 332 trees ha-1, respectively. Ahuihua and El Varillal forests showed the largest total height and diameter values. The accumulated carbon was greater in Ahuihua and Bajo Huallaga forests both the aboveground and belowground with values of 405.07 t ha-1 and 51.85 t ha-1, and 201.46 t ha-1 and 27.59 t ha-1, respectively. These forests also had the largest structural mean values of basal area, total height, dominant height, and diameter at breast height. The altitude variable was negatively related to aboveground and belowground carbon. Research highlights: The type of forest and the management practices play a crucial role for carbon accumulation both in the aboveground and belowground biomass. The basal area was the variable that most contributed on carbon accumulation. Understanding the carbon dynamic in forests provides essential information for the implementation of accurate management practices and conservation efforts.

title: Reclamation of Galamsey Land is Not Land Restoration: The Land Beyond Agriculture
summary: Agriculture is not the only imperative for land reclamation. In Ghana, conflation of disapproval, and clarion call for compulsory reclamation of ‘galamey’-degraded arable lands, by the moral society and eco-conscious minority in order to su
content: Agriculture is not the only imperative for land reclamation. In Ghana, conflation of disapproval, and clarion call for compulsory reclamation of ‘galamey’-degraded arable lands, by the moral society and eco-conscious minority in order to sustain biodiversity, agricultural productivity, environmental safety, and public health is muffled by the oratory artifice of utilitarians (both utilitarian narrowness and indifference) and the financial might of political financiers fronting for international gold merchants. The coup de grace is delivered by unpatriotic, unethical, and compromised environmental scientists and scholars whose acquiescence legitimized the false scientific narrative of synonymy of land reclamation to land ecosystem restoration. The error builds complacency that weakens collective revulsion for the insensate destruction of nature by illegal small-scale gold mining; believing that, remedy lies in merely covering up dugouts or levelling up degraded areas and re-vegetating them. Neither ignorance nor conceptual oversight is an alibi; the interchangeable use of land reclamation and land restoration is a veneer by insincere political actors to shirk responsibility for a national course, and sophism by opportunistic scientists and scholars to plunder and pillage national resources in a course which does not fully address a national tragedy! Presently (2026), the ever-changing estimated cost of reclaiming a hectare of galamsey-degraded arable land is $48 thousand; $264 million for the over 5 500 hectares degraded so far. But, the overall national conservative budgetary estimate for reclamation and short-term restoration (for arable purpose only) of the same 5 500-plus hectares, is a whopping $17 billion! Yes, degraded lands must be reclaimed at all cost but, further efforts must be expended to attain land ecosystem restoration in the end. Land reclamation is only the important first step in the long journey to land ecosystem restoration; it is not an end in itself. This is the thesis of this scientific master piece.

title: A Morphological Dual-Staining Framework for Standardized Detection of Cell Death in the Microalga Dunaliella salina
summary: Abstract The absence of a simple, universal protocol to detect algal cell death is a major bottleneck in aquatic ecology and carbon cycle research. This study bridges this gap by establishing a practical diagnostic framework based on parall
content: Abstract The absence of a simple, universal protocol to detect algal cell death is a major bottleneck in aquatic ecology and carbon cycle research. This study bridges this gap by establishing a practical diagnostic framework based on parallel 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) and iodine staining, concurrently probing the two pillars of photoautotrophic vitality—metabolic activity (via respiratory electron transport) and photosynthetic storage integrity. Using the halotolerant, wall-less model Dunaliella salina , we applied the method to environmentally relevant stressors. It clearly distinguished viable cells and consistently classified four distinct death phenotypes: apoptosis-like, necrotic, plasmolysis, and a novel secretion-type death from microbial fouling. Notably, light-induced necrosis exhibited morphological hallmarks of singlet oxygen-mediated killing, analogous to Type II Photodynamic Therapy. Crucially, identical death signatures were detected in natural populations from Maharloo Hypersaline Lake, confirming ecological validity. Beyond providing a robust, field-adaptable toolkit, our findings expose a critical disciplinary gap: the lack of standardized nomenclature and diagnostic criteria for cell death in carbon-fixing unicellular organisms. As these organisms mediate nearly half of global carbon fixation, quantifying their mortality is essential for improving carbon fixation and growth models, accurately predicting carbon fluxes, assessing the resilience of aquatic carbon sinks, and evaluating climate change impacts. We therefore propose an international consortium on Cell Death in Carbon-Fixing Unicellular Organisms to standardize definitions of cell death phenotypes, unify methodologies through this dual-staining protocol, explicitly incorporate mortality into carbon fixation and growth models, and translate laboratory-based viability metrics into predictive tools for ecosystem- and photobioreactor-scale carbon management. Our framework provides the essential methodological foundation for this global standardization effort.

title: Review of the Current Research Status of Thermal Management Systems for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
summary: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFCs) is a key technology for the efficient conversion of clean energy, and the thermal management system is a critical auxiliary system for PEMFCs. This paper reviews the multi-field applications of PE
tags: Thermal management of electronic devices and systems
content: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFCs) is a key technology for the efficient conversion of clean energy, and the thermal management system is a critical auxiliary system for PEMFCs. This paper reviews the multi-field applications of PEMFCs thermal management in areas such as combined heat and power (CHP) and waste heat power generation. It focuses on three major technical aspects: cell system cooling technology, ultra-low temperature vehicle cold-start, and stack waste heat recovery. The advantages and disadvantages of various research methods are compared and analyzed, and the current research status and future trends are summarized.

title: Species- and region-specific growth curves, forest age (2020), and disturbance trends for French forests at 30 m resolution
summary: Abstract. Spatially explicit biomass growth curves data that jointly resolve tree species, stand age and disturbance regime are scarce, particularly at fine spatial resolutions. We present five consistent data products for metropolitan Fren
content: Abstract. Spatially explicit biomass growth curves data that jointly resolve tree species, stand age and disturbance regime are scarce, particularly at fine spatial resolutions. We present five consistent data products for metropolitan French forests around 2020, derived from a 30 m dominant-species map, the 30 m FORMS-B satellite above-ground biomass (AGB) map and the Landsat-based European Forest Disturbance Atlas: (1) 290 AGB growth curves for 28 species categories across 11 large ecological regions; (2) a 30 m forest age map for 2020 covering 17.01 Mha of forests, obtained by inverting these curves against the AGB map; (3) 3,752 harvest and natural disturbance rates and patch sizes, with their 1999–2024 trends; (4) 3,752 event-based disturbance severities (AGB loss per disturbed hectare); and (5) 1,874 rotation periods from National Forest Inventory (NFI) plot samples remeasurements. Products 3–5 cover 28 species categories across 86 small ecological regions. These cover the species×region combinations present in French forests, not the full combinatorial grid. Not all 28 species categories occur in every ecological region; the totals reflect strata with forest area only. All products include uncertainties and gap-filling flags. Growth curves match National Forest Inventory-derived curves for early growth (+12±15 %, 95 % CI) but give a higher asymptotic biomass (+22±18 %) and a later half-saturation year (+33±23 %), partly reflecting differences in the representation of age extremes, as NFI measurements exclude trees <7.5 cm in diameter and we aggregate stands >60 years into a single age class. The age map matches the NFI nationally aggregated age distribution (median offset −2 [−20 to +42] yr). The 2020 harvested area (44±6 kha) and the resulting AGB loss (2.5±0.3 MtC.yr−1) are of the same order as independent clear-cut estimates (62 kha from the NFI; ~3 MtC.yr−1 from satellite-mapped clear-cuts over 2018–2024). The Landsat disturbance product captures only stand-replacing and high severity events and underestimate selective logging and diffuse mortality. These products can be combined directly to model forest carbon dynamics at species and regional resolution. All data are openly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23499335 (Pellissier-Tanon et al., 2026).

title: Characterizing hydrogen-diesel dual-fuel combustion in a commercial heavy-duty vehicle
summary: Hydrogen-diesel dual-fuel (H₂DF) combustion is a promising pathway for reducing CO₂ emissions from conventional diesel engines, particularly in heavy-duty applications. However, most existing studies are based on engine dynamometer experime
content: Hydrogen-diesel dual-fuel (H₂DF) combustion is a promising pathway for reducing CO₂ emissions from conventional diesel engines, particularly in heavy-duty applications. However, most existing studies are based on engine dynamometer experiments under idealized steady-state conditions, leaving gaps in understanding the constraints of real-world operation and implementation. This study addresses these gaps through an experimental investigation of a retrofit H₂DF system implemented on a commercial heavy-duty vehicle. The objective is to identify the governing factors and mechanisms of H₂DF combustion and their relationships with engine operating parameters under representative conditions. A research vehicle equipped with a retrofit H₂DF system, where hydrogen is injected upstream of the intake manifold, was tested on a chassis dynamometer under steady-state conditions to compare H₂DF and conventional diesel operation and to identify H₂DF combustion regimes. The vehicle was then evaluated under real-world traffic conditions to assess in-use performance and compare results with steady-state testing. Five distinct H₂DF combustion regimes were identified and mapped, providing a generalized framework for characterizing H₂DF combustion under varying operating conditions. The governing factors and transition thresholds between regimes were determined, defining the operational space and associated trade-offs among emissions and efficiency. In on-road tests, H₂DF operation achieved an overall 22±5% reduction in tailpipe CO₂ emissions relative to diesel operation at an average hydrogen energy fraction (HEF) of 18%, with no significant effect on fuel efficiency or tailpipe NOₓ emissions, while particulate matter emissions remained below the detection limit in both fuel modes. Steady-state chassis dynamometer testing was found to represent overall trends in brake-specific CO₂ and engine-out NOₓ with respect to engine torque at a given engine speed during real-world operation. However, deviations arise because steady-state testing does not capture instantaneous variations in HEF and equivalence ratios, nor the nonlinear dependence of NOₓ formation and engine efficiency on these operating parameters. This study provides a unique H₂DF dataset from both chassis dynamometer and real-world testing, advancing understanding of retrofit H₂DF operation in commercial diesel engines. The findings inform H₂ injection strategy optimization, while the proposed combustion regime framework supports future investigations into H₂DF combustion mechanisms.

title: Hudson River Estuary sediments contain high fractional abundances of preserved globothalamean foraminiferal organic linings at Piermont, New York
summary: Foundational to an estuarine ecosystem is the composition of its sediments, with benthic foraminifera serving as a key component. While it is common to find intact and deformed tests, foraminiferal organic linings (FOLs; foraminifera whose
content: Foundational to an estuarine ecosystem is the composition of its sediments, with benthic foraminifera serving as a key component. While it is common to find intact and deformed tests, foraminiferal organic linings (FOLs; foraminifera whose tests dissolved) are not always present in sediment samples. Identifying where FOLs are preserved is a necessary first step towards determining what promotes their development and burial. Here we document the prevalence of globothalamean FOLs in the Hudson River Estuary (HRE) at the Pier in Piermont, New York, USA. We also identified six agglutinated foraminifera species and successfully imaged foraminifera that were collected while in the process of losing their tests. There are a multitude of factors that can lead to test dissolution with FOL preservation, but most are related to suboptimal growth conditions. While the HRE has a history of sediment pollution, studies utilizing foraminifera or FOLs to study the modern benthic environment are not common. Our study provides some of the first evidence for FOLs preserved in the HRE. This exploratory work is a critical step towards utilizing foraminifera as a proxy for benthic conditions, with specific recommendations for future FOL sampling to monitor sediment conditions in the HRE.

title: Diversified cropping rotation increases soil carbon sequestration via fungal-mediated necromass production and mineral association
summary: Crop diversification boosts soil organic carbon (SOC) storage, yet uncertainty persists regarding its effects on molecular SOC composition. Using a 43-year field trial in fluvo-aquic soil, we contrasted conventional wheat-rice (ConCrop) ver
content: Crop diversification boosts soil organic carbon (SOC) storage, yet uncertainty persists regarding its effects on molecular SOC composition. Using a 43-year field trial in fluvo-aquic soil, we contrasted conventional wheat-rice (ConCrop) versus diversified rice/wheat – cotton/barley – maize/faba bean rotations (DivCrop). We demonstrated DivCrop elevated SOC by 9.6% (0–15 cm) and 15% (15–30 cm). DivCrop alleviated C-nitrogen co-limitation, stimulating 150% greater microbial growth and 47% higher C use efficiency. This coincided with restructured microbial communities shifting toward fungal dominance and increased functional capacity. Community transplantation assays confirmed increased adaptation for efficient C processing. Diversification accelerated lignin decomposition (plant-derived C reduced by 19–35%) and redirecting C flow toward fungal necromass (20–44% of total microbial necromass). Consequently, mineral-associated organic C increased 48–69%, with short-term formation efficiency rising 98–160% via reactive iron oxide interactions. Diversification thus shifts plant-derived recalcitrance towards mineral-stabilized microbial products in low-SOC soils, reshaping SOC composition toward climate-resilient agriculture. Crop diversification increased soil organic carbon by 10–15%, boosted microbial growth and carbon-use efficiency, shifted communities toward fungi, and raised mineral-associated carbon by 48–69%, based on a 43-year field trial and community transplantation assays.

title: Forest fragmentation susceptibility assessment using the weight of evidence model in Mizoram, India
summary: Forest fragmentation represents one of the major threats to biodiversity and ecosystem sustainability. Despite having the highest proportion of forest cover percentage to total geographical area among Indian states, forest fragmentation sus
content: Forest fragmentation represents one of the major threats to biodiversity and ecosystem sustainability. Despite having the highest proportion of forest cover percentage to total geographical area among Indian states, forest fragmentation susceptibility in Mizoram remains a serious concern. The present study assesses forest fragmentation susceptibility in the state of Mizoram using RS-GIS based Weight of Evidence model (WOE). LULC maps for 2005 and 2025 were generated using Landsat-5 and Landsat-9 imageries, and the Landscape Fragmentation Tool (LFT v2.0) was used to delineate the fragmentation classes. Seven causative factors, viz. altitude, slope, aspect, distance to roads, distance to streams, distance to agricultural land, and distance to built-up areas were incorporated into the WOE Model. A multicollinearity analysis was conducted which confirmed the suitability of the selected variables (VIF < 5). The results reveal that nearly 41.06% of the study area falls under moderate to very high forest fragmentation susceptibility categories. Areas located close to built-up and agricultural land, and lying on gentle slopes at elevations between 1000 and 2000 m are more prone to fragmentation. Areas near roads (< 1000 m) and streams (< 500 m) were found to be susceptible to fragmentation indicating the influence of anthropogenic activities and landscape accessibility on forest fragmentation patterns. The model was validated using the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve and achieved a good predictive accuracy, with an Area Under Curve (AUC) value of 0.831. The findings bring into light the need for targeted conservation and management interventions, particularly in areas experiencing increasing anthropogenic pressure from agricultural and built-up expansion. The generated susceptibility provides a valuable decision-support framework for policymakers and planners to mitigate future fragmentation and ensure long-term sustainability of Mizoram’s forest ecosystems.

title: Impacts of glacial meltwater on ocean continental shelf regimes around Antarctica
summary: As the Antarctic ice sheet melts in response to climate change, freshwater is released into the ocean over the continental shelf, altering its hydrographic properties, stratification and circulation. This can, in turn, affect melting of Ant
content: As the Antarctic ice sheet melts in response to climate change, freshwater is released into the ocean over the continental shelf, altering its hydrographic properties, stratification and circulation. This can, in turn, affect melting of Antarctic ice shelves by modifying the delivery of oceanic heat to sub-ice-shelf cavities. To study the response of the ocean to enhanced Antarctic meltwater, we use an equilibrated 1° global ocean-sea ice configuration with relatively realistic continental shelf regimes. We conduct three freshwater perturbation experiments of increasing complexity covering the period 1990-2100. Our results show that meltwater injection reduces wintertime convection around Antarctica, by strengthening vertical stratification. Consequently, Dense Shelf Water (DSW) is no longer renewed while Circumpolar Deep Water (CDW) is no longer ventilated on the shelf. CDW thus permanently intrudes onto the lower part of the continental shelf, causing warming there. However, this response depends strongly on how the meltwater perturbation is implemented: warming and CDW intrusion on the shelf are largely mitigated under a realistic forcing design, in which meltwater is distributed vertically and horizontally and the latent heat of fusion is accounted for. Under this realistic forcing, shelf bottom waters warm only slightly (+0.1°C on average in 2100), whereas coastal surface injection causes strong warming (+0.7°C). Further, DSW formation proves more resilient under more realistic forcing, but ultimately ceases under all meltwater injection scenarios considered. These results indicate that models using simplified meltwater anomaly forcing likely exaggerate both continental shelf warming and DSW decline.

title: Multivariate Phenotypic Diversity, Phenological Plasticity and Quantitative Drought Tolerance Indices in Sweet Sorghum (Sorghum Bicolor L. Moench) Under Contrasting Water Regimes
source: International Journal of Chemistry and Technology
summary: Water scarcity poses a major constraint to sweet sorghum productivity in semi-arid regions. In this study, 256 sweet sorghum genotypes were evaluated under well-watered (WW) and water-deficit (WD) conditions to assess agro-morphological div
content: Water scarcity poses a major constraint to sweet sorghum productivity in semi-arid regions. In this study, 256 sweet sorghum genotypes were evaluated under well-watered (WW) and water-deficit (WD) conditions to assess agro-morphological diversity, phenological plasticity, and quantitative drought tolerance. Significant phenotypic variation was observed across all measured traits. Under WW, the average growth duration was 106.4 ± 1.07 days (range: 93–127 days), whereas drought stress slightly extended the growth cycle to 108.2 ±1.22 days under WD, accompanied by an increased coefficient of variation (18.01%). Plant height ranged from 94.5 to 362.1 cm under WW (population mean: 224.8 ± 2.16 cm) and declined to a maximum of 343.6 cm under WD (mean: 208.5 ± 2.24 cm). High broad-sense heritability (H2) coupled with high genetic advance as percent of mean (GAM > 20 %) was recorded for phenological duration and stem diameter, indicating strong genetic control despite drought-induced developmental plasticity. Multivariate ordination and plasticity trade-off analyses revealed that drought response is governed by two distinct functional axes: vegetative vigor paired with stress tolerance, and structural robustness aligned with juice quality, driven by an inverse coordination between vertical elongation and radial stem expansion. Quantitative drought evaluation using Drought Susceptibility Index (DSI) and Stress Tolerance Index (STI) effectively separated high absolute growth from true relative stress tolerance. Applying a multi-trait selection rule identified 14.8 % of the population as elite performers. Genotypes such as X012 and X066-1 exhibited superior drought tolerance (DSI < 0.50, STI > 1.25), maintaining structural stability and high sugar accumulation (Juice Brix > 16.5 %) under water stress. Overall, these findings demonstrate substantial phenotypic diversity and provide reliable selection metrics for breeding drought-adapted and bioenergy-efficient sweet sorghum germplasm.

title: Ultra-swelling pH-responsive hybrid hydrogel for oral heparin delivery
summary: Oral delivery of heparin remains challenging because of poor stability and limited site-specific release within the gastrointestinal tract. Herein, an ultra-swelling pH-responsive hybrid hydrogel based on chitosan, acrylic acid, and 2-hydro
content: Oral delivery of heparin remains challenging because of poor stability and limited site-specific release within the gastrointestinal tract. Herein, an ultra-swelling pH-responsive hybrid hydrogel based on chitosan, acrylic acid, and 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) was developed through low-temperature redox-initiated graft copolymerization and statistically optimized using a Box–Behnken design. The effects of the monomer-to-chitosan ratio, initiator concentration, and crosslinker content on hydrogel performance were systematically evaluated. Structural, morphological, and thermal characteristics were confirmed by FTIR, XRD, SEM, DSC, and TGA analyses. The optimized hydrogel exhibited a highly porous architecture and an exceptional swelling ratio exceeding 4000% under near-neutral conditions while maintaining limited swelling in acidic media. Heparin loading and in vitro release studies demonstrated minimal drug release at gastric pH and rapid, sustained release at neutral to mildly alkaline pH, reflecting the transition from stomach to intestinal environments. The combination of statistical optimization, pronounced pH responsiveness, and selective heparin release highlights the advantages of this hydrogel over conventional formulations. These findings establish the optimized chitosan-g-poly(AA-co-HEMA) hydrogel as a promising platform for oral delivery of heparin and other pH-sensitive therapeutics requiring controlled gastrointestinal release.

title: Contrasting Controls on Air–Sea CO 2 Fluxes in the Pearl River Estuary and Adjacent Coastal Waters Under Typhoon Intensification and Track Shifts: A Modeling Study
summary: Abstract Northwest Pacific typhoons frequently affect the northern South China Sea, but their impacts on air‐sea CO 2 flux (FCO 2 ) in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE) and adjacent coastal waters remain poorly constrained. We used a coupled ph
content: Abstract Northwest Pacific typhoons frequently affect the northern South China Sea, but their impacts on air‐sea CO 2 flux (FCO 2 ) in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE) and adjacent coastal waters remain poorly constrained. We used a coupled physical‐biogeochemical model to simulate Typhoon Hato (2017) and conducted sensitivity experiments with intensified winds and northward‐shifted tracks to quantify their effects on FCO 2 variability. Hato converted both regions into pronounced CO 2 sources, with mean estuarine FCO 2 increasing ∼15× relative to pre‐typhoon conditions. During the event, FCO 2 variability was governed primarily by air‐sea partial pressure difference of CO 2 (Δ p CO 2 ); in coastal waters it arose mainly from vertical mixing of DIC, whereas in the estuary it reflected TA advection. Wind‐intensification experiments showed that FCO 2 increased nonlinearly with wind speed. In coastal waters, the drivers of FCO 2 anomaly (ΔFCO 2 ) shifted toward a dominance of the gas transfer velocity (k), whereas estuarine anomalies remained jointly controlled by gas transfer velocity and non‐thermal p CO 2 ( p CO 2_noSST ); sea surface temperature (SST) effects remained secondary. Track‐shift experiments redistributed process importance. In coastal waters, the contribution from the gas transfer ( k ) term declined and enhanced p CO 2_noSST moderated ΔFCO 2 peaks, whereas in the estuary an increased SST contribution and reduced k‐term contribution amplified peak variability. This paper shows that extreme typhoons trigger brief, intense nearshore CO 2 outgassing pulses, and that future intensity increased and track shifts may reshape FCO 2 magnitude and controls, increasing coastal carbon‐budget uncertainty.

title: Decoupling of spatiotemporal variations of lake CO2 emissions in China: Inconsistency between seasonal and spatial dominant factors
summary: Lake CO 2 emissions have become a critical component shaping the stability of terrestrial carbon sinks and regional carbon budgets, yet existing studies often neglect the spatial heterogeneity and scale effects of the explanatory variables,
content: Lake CO 2 emissions have become a critical component shaping the stability of terrestrial carbon sinks and regional carbon budgets, yet existing studies often neglect the spatial heterogeneity and scale effects of the explanatory variables, resulting in substantial uncertainties in the assessment of lake CO 2 emissions. In this study, we examined seasonally dominant explanatory variables and their scale-dependent spatial associations with lake CO 2 fluxes across China. The results showed that lake CO 2 fluxes exhibited a spatiotemporal pattern, with higher mean values in winter (−0.36 to 10.53 mmol m −2 d −1 ; 1.54 ± 1.45 mmol m −2 d −1 ) and lower values in summer (−0.40 to 7.00 mmol m −2 d −1 ; 1.01 ± 1.32 mmol m −2 d −1 ; p < 0.001); annual mean values were highest in the Northeast Plain and Mountain Lake Zone (2.27 ± 1.55 mmol m −2 d −1 ) and lowest in the Inner Mongolia-Xinjiang Lake Zone (0.63 ± 0.69 mmol m −2 d −1 ). The global spatial autocorrelation of CO 2 fluxes strengthened from spring to winter (Moran's I = 0.348–0.411). The multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) model achieved the best goodness of fit in all seasons (R 2 = 0.68–0.86), effectively capturing the spatial heterogeneity of the explanatory variables. Lake area exhibited the highest explanatory power in spring and winter (Q = 0.489 and 0.287, respectively), whereas DO ranked highest in summer and autumn (Q = 0.381 and 0.196, respectively). OPGD interaction detection showed that nonlinear enhancement was the predominant interaction type, suggesting that spatial heterogeneity in CO 2 fluxes reflects the joint influence of multiple explanatory variables. Scale-effect analysis based on MGWR bandwidths revealed that lake attributes (lake area, average depth, and average discharge) exhibited broad-scale effects, with relatively stable influences across larger spatial ranges (bandwidths: 159–181 km). In contrast, water quality indicators (DO and NH 4 + ) and climatic factors (PRE and SSR) showed localized effects due to their smaller bandwidths (23–40 km). The detector analysis further identified high-emission zones associated with small lakes and conditions of low DO, underscoring the necessity of differentiated management for small waterbodies and environmentally sensitive regions in lake‑carbon governance. Overall, this study demonstrates that explicitly incorporating spatial heterogeneity and multiscale effects is essential for accurately assessing lake CO 2 emissions and for designing spatially and seasonally targeted carbon-mitigation strategies.

title: LED-infused photoperiod and light intensity regulation on morpho-physiological attributes, productivity, quality and resource use efficiency in french bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.)
summary: Abstract Photoperiod and light intensity are critical environmental factors influencing the growth, development of higher plants. To evaluate their effects on french bean, an experiment was conducted at the University of Agricultural Scienc
content: Abstract Photoperiod and light intensity are critical environmental factors influencing the growth, development of higher plants. To evaluate their effects on french bean, an experiment was conducted at the University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru, Karnataka. The study comprised five infused photoperiod regimes, namely 4 h (8:00 AM–12:00 Noon), 6 h (8:00 AM–2:00 PM), 8 h (8:00 AM–4:00 PM), 10 h (8:00 AM–6:00 PM), and 12 h (8:00 AM–8:00 PM), along with ambient light as the control. In each photoperiod treatment, ambient sunlight was supplemented with LED illumination at a constant light intensity. The results revealed that french bean plants grown under infused photoperiod exhibited significantly greater leafiness than those grown under ambient light alone (33–41% at 20 DAS and 19–70% at 40 DAS). Enhanced leaf development resulted in substantial improvements in photosynthetic rate (65–87% and 47–97%) and instantaneous water use efficiency (77–102% and 43–116%). Consequently, dry matter accumulation increased by 5–30% under the infused photoperiod regimes compared with the control. The improved physiological performance translated into remarkable enhancements in yield-attributing traits and seed yield (29–100%) over ambient light-grown plants. Furthermore, exposure to elevated photoperiods at a constant light intensity improved seed quality by increasing protein and fat contents, while also enhancing nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium uptake by plant. These findings demonstrate the potential of photoperiod manipulation through supplemental lighting to improve productivity, quality, and resource use efficiency in french bean cultivation.

title: Genotype x environment interaction for stomata traits in a rice recombinant inbred population
summary: Drought is a major abiotic constraint limiting global rice ( Oryza sativa L.) production. While stomatal traits are linked to drought adaptation, their environmental stability and breeding utility are poorly understood. This study evaluated
content: Drought is a major abiotic constraint limiting global rice ( Oryza sativa L.) production. While stomatal traits are linked to drought adaptation, their environmental stability and breeding utility are poorly understood. This study evaluated 272 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) derived from an IRRI 154/NERICA 4 cross under well-watered and reproductive-stage drought-stress conditions across four seasons (2022WS - 2024DS) to quantify genotype-by-environment (G×E) interactions for four stomatal characteristics (density, area, length, and width) on both leaf surfaces. Significant genotypic variation and pronounced transgressive segregation were observed for all traits. While reproductive-stage stress reduced mean grain yield by 84.6%, stomatal density remained numerically stable across moisture regimes. Conversely, cell dimensions exhibited high plasticity, driving a 20.5% reduction in abaxial stomatal area and a 17.2% reduction in length to facilitate rapid closing kinetics. Combined multi-environment analysis revealed that while raw grain yield heritability dropped to 0.39 under stress due to seasonal masking, abaxial stomatal density and area preserved exceptionally robust combined heritability (H 2 , 0.92 and 0.99, respectively). Stomatal traits displayed weak direct correlations with final grain yield, indicating they function as upstream components of stress resilience rather than direct drivers of sink capacity. Crucially, these findings demonstrate that breeders can focus exclusively on abaxial stomatal density under well-watered conditions as a unified, high-heritability proxy for large-scale germplasm screenings. This operational shortcut captures baseline genetic variation while completely avoiding stress-induced leaf deformations, offering a highly scalable, high-throughput pathway to accelerate climate-resilient rice development.

title: Post‐Mining Conservation Measures for Erosion Control: A Global Assessment of Their Effectiveness on Runoff and Soil Erosion Reduction
summary: ABSTRACT Mining activities severely disturb land surfaces and hydrological processes, intensifying hillslope erosion and soil loss. To evaluate the effectiveness of post‐mining restoration measures and identify the factors regulating their
content: ABSTRACT Mining activities severely disturb land surfaces and hydrological processes, intensifying hillslope erosion and soil loss. To evaluate the effectiveness of post‐mining restoration measures and identify the factors regulating their performance, we compiled a global dataset of runoff and soil erosion yield from 58 studies spanning multiple mine types, climatic zones, and restoration practices, and conducted a weighted meta‐analysis using random‐effects models. Overall, restoration measures reduced runoff by 49.0% and soil erosion yield by 67.6%, with consistently greater reductions in soil erosion. Combined measures were most effective, whereas soil amendment alone showed the weakest runoff reduction (21.1%). Runoff reduction increased with restoration duration, while soil erosion control was strong initially but showed a transient decline before recovering. Restoration effectiveness also varied substantially among mine types and environmental conditions. Soil erosion reduction was more sensitive than runoff to climatic and topographic factors, with higher rainfall intensity and steeper slopes generally weakening both runoff and soil erosion control. Slopes longer than 15 m sharply reduced soil erosion control (56.9% vs. > 70% on shorter slopes). Vegetation cover further revealed contrasting responses: runoff reduction plateaued at approximately 40% cover, whereas soil erosion reduction continued to increase up to 80%–100% cover. These findings demonstrate that post‐mining restoration effectiveness is jointly regulated by restoration strategy, recovery duration, and site conditions, highlighting the need for context‐specific combinations of restoration measures, vegetation targets, and landform configurations.

title: Eichhornia crassipes management in a eutrophic reservoir: Cover reduction, rapid recolonization, and cyanobacterial dynamics
summary: Abstract Mechanical harvesting is widely used to control Eichhornia crassipes in reservoirs, yet its performance is judged by biomass removed rather than the reduction and stabilization of plant cover. We integrated a 129 month Sentinel-1 t
content: Abstract Mechanical harvesting is widely used to control Eichhornia crassipes in reservoirs, yet its performance is judged by biomass removed rather than the reduction and stabilization of plant cover. We integrated a 129 month Sentinel-1 time series derived using U-Net segmentation with harvesting records and water quality monitoring to evaluate harvest campaigns, recurrent expansion and phytoplankton responses in a 177 ha eutrophic tropical urban reservoir. Harvesting effort was not proportional to cover change: campaigns with comparable biomass removal produced contrasting outcomes. Cover reductions were followed by recolonization, with the two fastest episodes doubling reservoir scale cover in 19 and 20 days. Expansion was fastest after low cover phases and declined as open water surface became occupied, whereas harvesting imposed a weaker constraint on cover gain. At the reservoir outlet, higher cover was associated with lower cyanobacterial density and dominance during the dry season, while chlorophyll-a remained unrelated to cover. Station specific Random Forest models interpreted with explainable AI (SHAP) retained true color and macrophyte cover as main predictors of cyanobacterial density. These findings distinguish three dimensions often conflated in macrophyte management: operational effort, spatial outcome and ecological state. Harvested biomass should therefore be treated as an effort metric, whereas net cover change, residual cover and rebound provide direct measures of management performance. Combining deep learning satellite mapping, operational records, explainable machine learning and in situ monitoring can support adaptive harvesting, but durable control will also require reductions in nutrient and suspended solid loads.

title: Utilizing calcite‐bound phosphate to reconstruct historical phosphorus loading to marl lake ecosystems
summary: Abstract Reconstructing historical phosphorus (P) concentrations in lakes has been a long‐standing problem for paleolimnology. The most commonly applied method is the use of diatom‐inferred total P models, but there are well‐documented limi
content: Abstract Reconstructing historical phosphorus (P) concentrations in lakes has been a long‐standing problem for paleolimnology. The most commonly applied method is the use of diatom‐inferred total P models, but there are well‐documented limitations to these approaches. Authigenic calcite co‐precipitated with P is a promising geochemical indicator of ambient P conditions in the water column through time. We tested two approaches for isolating the P content associated with authigenic calcite. The first capitalizes on a well‐known sequential extraction method but incorporates a physical separation to increase the specificity of the extraction. The second uses scanning electron microscopy and energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy (SEM‐EDS) to target P concentrations of authigenic calcite. These methods were evaluated using calcite‐rich sediments from Utah Lake in north‐central Utah, USA. Utah Lake is a eutrophic lake with a well‐documented increase in P pollution due to rapid population growth and wastewater inputs. Both methods showed increased up‐core concentrations of calcite‐P that match historical P loading records; however, a relatively high P detection limit reduced the effectiveness of the semi‐quantitative SEM‐EDS method. Overall, we demonstrate that the methods outlined here are feasible for reconstructing historical P concentrations in lakes with sufficient sedimentary authigenic calcite and appropriate sedimentary environments.

title: Assessment of Dietary Sources in a Tropical Coastal Fish (Blackspotted Croaker Protonibea diacanthus)
summary: Abstract Energy and nutrients from rivers and coastal floodplains are widely recognised as key drivers of productivity in coastal marine food webs, but these inputs may increase productivity for some species while having negligible or negat
content: Abstract Energy and nutrients from rivers and coastal floodplains are widely recognised as key drivers of productivity in coastal marine food webs, but these inputs may increase productivity for some species while having negligible or negative effects on others. Understanding the sources of nutrition supporting commercially important fishes is therefore critical for effective management. Here, we quantify the relative contribution of terrestrial, freshwater, and marine resources to the diet of the marine sciaenid Protonibea diacanthus in the wet–dry tropics of northern Australia. Bulk stable isotopes (δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N, δ³⁴S) and compound-specific stable isotope analysis of essential amino acids (δ¹³C) were used to resolve trophic pathways, alongside microbial source tracking to assess the influence of freshwater and marine water sources at aggregation sites. Across all approaches, results consistently indicated a dominant reliance on marine-derived resources. Mixing models identified marine sources, particularly marine fish, as the primary contributors to diet, while CSIA-AA independently demonstrated that carbon supporting P. diacanthus was overwhelmingly marine in origin. There was little evidence of freshwater or terrestrial influence in either trophic pathways or microbial assemblages, regardless of season or proximity to river outflows. These findings contrast with studies of other tropical fisheries species that show strong positive relationships with freshwater flow, and suggest that the nutrition of P. diacanthus is supported primarily by marine trophic pathways rather than riverine subsidies. This study highlights the need for caution when generalising the role of freshwater inputs across species and emphasises the importance of species-specific trophic dynamics in coastal ecosystem management.

title: Research on urban landscape ecological restoration and spatial renewal in the context of climate change
summary: The compounding effects of urbanization and climate change are accelerating the ecological degradation of urban landscapes, with persistent intensification of the heat island effect, increasingly frequent extreme waterlogging events, and gr
content: The compounding effects of urbanization and climate change are accelerating the ecological degradation of urban landscapes, with persistent intensification of the heat island effect, increasingly frequent extreme waterlogging events, and growing habitat fragmentation. Based on landscape ecology and resilient city theory, this study constructs an integrated research framework of “climate diagnosis — ecological restoration — spatial renewal — coupled assessment,” and proposes a Dynamic Climate-driven Ecological Vulnerability Response Matrix (DCEVR), a multi-scale blue-green coupled restoration technology integration system (BGCE), and climate-adaptive spatial renewal strategies underpinned by the Dual-Element Synergistic Benefit Assessment Model (DESBM). Indicator weights in the DCEVR are determined through an entropy-weight–AHP composite method, while the BGCE weight coefficients (α, β, γ) are scenario-specific values derived from climate scenario simulation. Drawing on ecological monitoring and spatial implementation data from the core area of Chengdu’s Jincheng Greenway between 2019 and 2023 — using three parallel benchmark scenarios (restoration-only, renewal-only, and coordinated implementation) constructed from real spatial subdivisions of the 133 km² study area — the study finds that, relative to the renewal-only baseline, deep coupling of ecological corridor restoration with low-carbon spatial restructuring is associated with an improvement of 27.3% in the city’s comprehensive climate resilience index, and that blue-green system collaborative intervention yields significant gains in microclimate regulation efficiency. All comparative claims reflect observed differences between spatial benchmark zones rather than experimental controls; causal attribution should be interpreted with appropriate caution. The research provides theoretical support and methodological reference for urban ecological governance and spatial planning practice.

title: Spatio‐Temporal Assessment of the Complementarity Between Hydroelectric, Wind and Solar Energy Sources for Northeastern Brazil
summary: ABSTRACT The growing participation of variable renewable sources in the Brazilian electricity system makes it necessary to understand how their different spatial and seasonal patterns can contribute to the stability of energy supply. In thi
content: ABSTRACT The growing participation of variable renewable sources in the Brazilian electricity system makes it necessary to understand how their different spatial and seasonal patterns can contribute to the stability of energy supply. In this context, the study evaluated the seasonal dynamics and spatiotemporal complementarity among hydropower, wind and solar resources in Northeast Brazil (NEB), between 1999 and 2022, with a focus on long‐term strategic planning. Initially, hierarchical cluster analysis was applied to monthly fields of precipitation, solar irradiation and wind speed at 100 m, allowing regions with homogeneous temporal patterns to be delineated. Five homogeneous precipitation regions (P1–P5), five solar irradiation regions (S1–S5) and four wind speed regions (W1–W4) were identified. The relationship between precipitation regimes and inflow to Sobradinho was also examined, with inflow adopted as the hydropower component (H1) because it integrates the basin response and represents the water inflow to the reservoir. The integration of hierarchical cluster analysis with compromise programming made it possible to simultaneously quantify the complementarity among hydropower, wind and solar resources, expanding the assessment beyond exclusively bivariate approaches. The combinations of W1, S1–S5 and H1 fell within the moderate complementarity range and showed better results than configurations involving W2, although the degree of complementarity varied among years. The alternation between the seasonal cycles of these resources reduces the coincidence among their periods of relatively lower availability, which may contribute to the diversification of the regional electricity mix, the stability of renewable supply and energy security in long‐term strategic planning.

title: Decomposition and mycorrhizal suppression of saprotrophs remain stable after wildfire and clearcut disturbance in boreal forests
summary: Boreal forests store a large portion of global terrestrial carbon, primarily in soils, yet their sensitivity to environmental changes remains uncertain. Disturbance is one major agent of change, with dominance shifting from wildfire to fore
content: Boreal forests store a large portion of global terrestrial carbon, primarily in soils, yet their sensitivity to environmental changes remains uncertain. Disturbance is one major agent of change, with dominance shifting from wildfire to forest management over the past century. Mycorrhizal suppression of saprotrophic decomposition may be an important control on boreal soil carbon storage, but its occurrence and magnitude remain uncertain. Additionally, the distinct impacts of wildfire and clearcutting on decomposition and soil microbial communities remain largely unexplored. We quantified mycorrhizal suppression of saprotrophs and decomposition in needle and humus litter through a root-exclusion experiment in 31 sites across wildfire (4-375 yr since disturbance) and clearcut chronosequences (1-109 yr since disturbance) in northern Sweden. Mycorrhizas suppressed decomposition by 15.5 ± 5.9% overall, with no consistent change over time after disturbance. This pattern was linked to absolute fungal abundance but not to other microbial community shifts, soil temperature or soil moisture. Decomposition rates were stable across time since disturbance for all substrates and disturbance types. Our findings improve understanding of mycorrhizal-decomposition interactions and highlight the need to further explore key fungal traits and compositional changes, especially at the soil surface, that regulate carbon storage dynamics in boreal soils.

title: Paulownia biomass under drought and salinity: From stress adaptation to functional materials and biorefinery valorization
summary: As semi-arid and salt-affected landscapes expand under climate change and land degradation, interest has increased in fast-growing woody biomass that can support both land rehabilitation and material production.Paulownia species and commerc
content: As semi-arid and salt-affected landscapes expand under climate change and land degradation, interest has increased in fast-growing woody biomass that can support both land rehabilitation and material production.Paulownia species and commercial hybrids are frequently promoted for these purposes because of their rapid juvenile growth, coppicing capacity, and lignocellulosic composition.Reported performance, however, varies substantially across genotypes, sites, and management regimes.This review evaluates the biological basis, establishment requirements, drought and salinity responses, wood and fiber properties, functional-material applications, and integrated biorefinery pathways of Paulownia spp.Field observations, controlled stress experiments, wood-characterization results, and laboratory processing studies are interpreted separately through a genotype × environment × management (G×E×M) framework.The specific synthesis is a proposed evidence chain from site and genotype through feedstock properties to end use: field evidence can inform plantation feasibility, whereas processing results establish candidate applications but cannot establish the advantages of stress-grown biomass without paired feedstock measurements.Field studies support substantial variation in growth with water supply, drainage, soil condition, and genotype, but available studies do not establish a universal drought or salinity threshold or a consistently abrupt response.Selected hybrids perform well in particular managed trials; comparative superiority across environments and lower invasion risk remain unverified for many clones.Low wood density constrains some structural and volumetric fuel applications, while laboratory fractionation and biochar studies show process feasibility under specified conditions, not industrial superiority or a demonstrated benefit of stress-grown feedstock.Paulownia is thus a management-dependent candidate for site-matched biomass production.This review distinguishes comparatively supported site and material constraints from hypotheses about genotype-specific stress limits and integrated biorefinery value.Field validation, genetically identified planting material, measured soil and water conditions, feedstock characterization, and comparative process assessment are required before regional or industrial recommendations can be made.

title: The Composite: Interface Matching across the Chrysene Arc, and the Resolution of Its Obstructions
summary: This paper establishes the formal interface composition of the chrysene protocell arc, verifying how the sequence of transitions from bulk stock separation to vessel division concatenates into a single valid finite execution. Across this un
content: This paper establishes the formal interface composition of the chrysene protocell arc, verifying how the sequence of transitions from bulk stock separation to vessel division concatenates into a single valid finite execution. Across this unbroken chemical pathway, a substituted chrysene stock separates itself from a polyaromatic bulk, is admitted with its carbon traced atom by atom, draws on a single material pool shared among competing uses, encloses an integrated nucleic-acid strand, builds an ordered chrysene lattice in the lumen where a twelve-axiom framework finds its model, and culminates in a vessel that divides. To connect each stage's output to the next stage's input as a complete atom map, the atom-tracing framework defines an interface as a tuple of fields — atoms with their origin labels, resources, location, charge, orientation, environment, and phase — and establishes that a chain of transitions forms a valid finite execution when adjacent stages match on every shared coordinate. Evaluating these interface equalities across the full sequence yields a rigorous biconditional: the chain concatenates into a valid finite execution precisely when the 17 conditions enumerated here hold, each an explicit equality between the quantities of connected stages. Of these conditions, 11 hold directly and 2 are unified under explicit conventions. The carbon formula of the separation stage reproduces three of the four terms of the 810-carbon assembly on which the atom-by-atom accounting is demonstrated, reflecting their shared foundation in the underlying substitution balances. Polarity descriptions across the corpus align in the same way: the resource-allocation analysis designates a species by its broad class, while the separation analysis specifies its ordering within that class. Two additional interface fields are formalized here to complete the specification, both uniquely determined by the structure of the system. The atom-tracing framework requires an origin label to be carried per site rather than per molecule, fixing the label set at 26 members — 18 core positions and 8 arm positions — across the bulk-core and oxalate origins, and the separation stage's carbon formula reflects this exact partition. Six invariants are verified atom by atom across the five transitions of the separation sequence, and the location field is defined relative to a control volume. Four remaining conditions are harmonized by aligning parameter regimes and notation across the corpus. The material ledger is governed by the integrated-cycle demand table, whose requirement at a genome length of L = 200 base pairs is 15231 units, incorporating a catalyst term without a separate bud-fraction term. This reference frame unifies the resource-pool figure of 42200 and the lumen-lattice figure of 14705: the membrane's share is 86.3 per cent, and the 83.5 per cent figure corresponds to that table's L = 735 row paired with the L = 200 pool. The final three conventions establish a

title: A Novel Approach Combining Mechanism and Machine Learning to Unravel Oxidant-Driven Formation Regimes of α-Pinene-Derived Oxygenated Organic Molecules (OOMs)
summary: Abstract. Monoterpene oxidation produces oxygenated organic molecules (OOMs) that act as secondary organic aerosol precursors, but the roles of ozone (O3) and the hydroxyl radical (OH) in their ambient formation are hard to separate because
content: Abstract. Monoterpene oxidation produces oxygenated organic molecules (OOMs) that act as secondary organic aerosol precursors, but the roles of ozone (O3) and the hydroxyl radical (OH) in their ambient formation are hard to separate because the two oxidants co-vary. We fitted an ensemble of tree-based regression models to one month of online mass-spectrometric measurements at a coastal background site in eastern China and ranked the predictors of four OOM classes defined by hydrogen content (H14–H20) using Shapley additive explanations. Within the fitted models, ozone accounts for 70.8–79.4 % of the relative predictive importance and OH for 20.6–29.2 %. The balance shifts along the series, the class retaining the hydrogen count of the parent monoterpene depending most strongly on ozone and the most saturated class most strongly on OH. The ozone response is not uniform: below about 62 ppb (62.0–63.6 ppb across the four classes) the models extract little ozone signal, whereas above this level ozone becomes a strong positive predictor for all four classes. Three independent checks support this pattern (Appendix B). Both the weights and the transition level derive from a single campaign and are site-specific; the analysis can be repeated wherever these variables are measured.

title: Characterising roadside ecosystems using the SEEA Ecosystem Condition Typology: towards a core set of biophysical variables
summary: Roadsides represent one of the most extensive anthropogenic networks globally, yet no integrative framework currently supports their systemic ecological characterisation and condition assessment. These areas can mitigate the environmental i
content: Roadsides represent one of the most extensive anthropogenic networks globally, yet no integrative framework currently supports their systemic ecological characterisation and condition assessment.
