These areas can mitigate the environmental impacts of roads; yet this potential requires a clearer understanding of their functioning. While the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting – Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA-EA) framework and its Ecosystem Condition Typology (ECT) have been applied to coastal, forest and freshwater ecosystems, roadsides remain largely unaddressed within this framework, as they are primarily regarded as extensions of transport infrastructure rather than as distinct ecosystems. This study presents the first application of the SEEA-ECT to roadside ecosystems, combining a compartmental systems perspective with a systematic literature review for the 1950- 2024 period of 97 peer-reviewed studies. Thirty key biophysical variables are identified and organised across five compartments — air, soil, water, flora and fauna — and classified according to ECT physical, chemical, compositional, structural and functional state classes. Results reveal consistent anthropogenic pressure gradients extending from the road edge outwards, cross-compartment interactions driven by biogeochemical cycling, hydrological dynamics and microtopographic control and the central role of soil and flora as intermediary nodes linking pressures to ecosystem responses. Building on these findings, a preliminary core set of 10 biophysical variables is proposed, combining literature-based prioritisation with considerations of ecological relevance and complementarity across ECT classes. This set provides an initial basis for roadside ecosystem condition monitoring and requires further field validation. This framework offers a transferable and internationally standardised foundation for evidence-based roadside management, ecosystem condition accounting and sustainable infrastructure planning.

title: Flavour instability and aroma profiles of non-alcoholic beers across production principles and beer styles
summary: Flavour instability is a major quality challenge in non-alcoholic beers (<0.5 vol.% alcohol), as their reduced Ethanol content alters aroma retention, antioxidative capacity, and ageing pathways compared with conventional beer. Consequently
content: Flavour instability is a major quality challenge in non-alcoholic beers (<0.5 vol.% alcohol), as their reduced Ethanol content alters aroma retention, antioxidative capacity, and ageing pathways compared with conventional beer. Consequently, non-alcoholic beers are often more susceptible to flavour deterioration during storage.In this study, the aroma composition, sensory profile, and ageing behaviour of 45 commercial non-alcoholic beers from 30 breweries were investigated. Samples were grouped into physically dealcoholised, stopped fermentation, alternative yeast, and hybrid beers. Aroma compounds and ageing-relevant aldehydes were analysed in fresh and forced-aged samples, complemented by trained-panel sensory evaluation. In addition, ageing potential was assessed through alkaline-induced release of aldehydes from bound states.Distinct differences between production principles were observed. Biologically produced non-alcoholic beers, particularly stopped-fermentation beers, exhibited higher wort-like character, elevated concentrations of Strecker aldehydes, and larger pools of releasable aldehydes. In contrast, physically dealcoholised beers generally showed lower initial aldehyde concentrations but often experienced the strongest increases in ageing-related compounds during forced ageing. Across all production principles, Strecker aldehydes and Furfural increased markedly during ageing and were identified as major contributors to flavour deterioration. The alkaline release approach revealed a substantial aldehyde-related ageing potential exceeding the Aldehyde increases observed during forced ageing, indicating the presence of both bound aldehydes and matrix-dependent formation pathways. Hybrid beers displayed the most favourable ageing behaviour, combining comparatively low aldehyde concentrations with the smallest sensory deterioration after ageing.Overall, flavour instability was influenced more strongly by production principle than by beer style, demonstrating that technology selection is a key determinant of long-term sensory quality in non-alcoholic beers. These findings highlight the importance of production-specific strategies to improve flavour instability and shelf life.

title: Practice and Research on the "Reaching New Heights" Action for Enhancing Young Employees' Comprehensive Quality in the Construction of a New-Type Power System
summary: With the in-depth advancement of the dual-carbon strategy and the accelerated construction of a new-type power system, the green, digital and intelligent transformation of the power industry continues to deepen, and industry formats, techni
content: With the in-depth advancement of the dual-carbon strategy and the accelerated construction of a new-type power system, the green, digital and intelligent transformation of the power industry continues to deepen, and industry formats, technical systems and job requirements are being iteratively upgraded, setting new standards for the comprehensive quality and professional competence of young employees. Young employees are the core reserve force for the development of power enterprises, and their comprehensive quality bears directly on the safe and stable operation of the power grid, the quality of energy supply and the long-term development of enterprises. At present, the young workforce in the power industry is troubled by a weak theoretical foundation, a single skill structure, and insufficient safety risk control, innovation transformation and physical and mental adaptability, while the traditional talent cultivation model is rigid, its mechanisms are fragmented, its evaluation is one-dimensional and its resource allocation is uneven, which restricts the growth and development of young employees. In response, power enterprises have innovatively carried out the "Reaching New Heights" action to improve young employees' comprehensive quality, integrating modern talent management concepts, building a five-in-one cultivation system covering moral cultivation, safety, skills, innovation and physical and mental health, and creating a refined, digital, closed-loop and collaborative model of talent cultivation. Based on the requirements of new-type power system construction and combined with the characteristics of power positions and the growth patterns of young people, this paper defines the core connotation of young employees' comprehensive quality, analyzes the shortcomings of that quality and the pain points of traditional cultivation, systematically explains the innovative system and practical paths of the "Reaching New Heights" action, reviews its implementation results and existing problems, and proposes long-term optimization countermeasures. This study constructs a young talent cultivation system suited to the new-type power system, fills gaps in industry talent cultivation, and forms a replicable and promotable model for improving young employees' quality and building the workforce, thereby providing solid talent support for the growth of young people and the high-quality development of the power industry.

title: Manganese-dependent ammonium oxidation associated with sulfur redox cycling in lake sediments
summary: Abstract The release of fixed nitrogen as dinitrogen gas (N2) back to the atmosphere plays a major role in global nitrogen cycling. One major pathway of N2 production is anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox). Anammox is often considered a
content: Abstract The release of fixed nitrogen as dinitrogen gas (N2) back to the atmosphere plays a major role in global nitrogen cycling. One major pathway of N2 production is anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox). Anammox is often considered a nitrite-dependent process, despite the fact that other electron (e) acceptors such as metal oxides are more abundant in various natural settings. Here we present experimental evidence for a two-step relay process of manganese [Mn(IV)]-dependent ammonium oxidation associated with a functionally novel bacterial lineage in a lake system. We observe that the process proceeds through two steps: ammonium acts as the initial e-donor to reduce sulfate to sulfide, followed by the oxidation of sulfide with Mn(IV) as the terminal e-acceptor. This two-step relay process is associated with Ca. Thiovibrio sp. TH_142, a functionally novel bacterium belonging to the order Desulfobulbales, which relies on reduction of Mn(IV) for energy conservation. From the genome of Ca. Thiovibrio sp. TH_142, we identify genes responsible for manganese reduction (dmsE and mtrB) and sulfide oxidation (tusA, dsrEFH and dsrL). We also identify genes associated with sulfate reduction (sat, aprAB and dsrABC) and a functionally unknown protein structurally similar to hydrazine synthase. These results expand the current view of microbial-mediated ammonium transformations under anoxic conditions, paving the way for understanding the coupled nitrogen, sulfur and manganese cycles in warming, less oxygenated aquatic ecosystems.

title: Synthetic Textile Microfibers as Emerging Pollutants: A Critical Review of Environmental and Health Consequence
source: Journal of Indian Association for Environmental Management (JIAEM)
summary: Microfiber pollution is a serious environmental problem that has been created by on-going commercial use of synthetic textiles for clothing. When washed, these textiles release tiny pieces of plastic also known as microfibers. Many of these
content: Microfiber pollution is a serious environmental problem that has been created by on-going commercial use of synthetic textiles for clothing. When washed, these textiles release tiny pieces of plastic also known as microfibers. Many of these fibers enter into waste or treatment plants and then into the aquatic environment where they cause harm to human health and marine ecosystems. The negative impacts from microfiber pollution (air quality, water and energy consumption and chemical pollution due to detergent) are covered in this study. Moreover, the uptake of microfibers by swallowing or breathing in is extremely harmful to health. There are several action steps that can be taken to minimize this pollution, such as the use of sustainable textiles, changing washing routines and the use of microfiber collection machines. Moreover, structural changes (such as public educative campaigns, policy campaigns) to increase greatly the development should be realized. This study highlights solutions that can be undertaken to address the problem of microfiber pollution and safeguard the planet and public health. The above terms refer to the defining features of microfibers: Micro-sized, Microfiber pollution, The impact on your health – Health hazard and Microfiber-catching equipment – The equipment designed to catch the microfibers.

title: Distinct Structural Trajectories of Dissolved Organic Matter Across the Yangtze River Estuary
summary: Abstract The Yangtze River Estuary (YRE) serves as a critical land‐ocean interface where hydrodynamic mixing and biogeochemical processes jointly regulate dissolved organic matter (DOM) cycling. However, the structural variability of DOM ac
content: Abstract The Yangtze River Estuary (YRE) serves as a critical land‐ocean interface where hydrodynamic mixing and biogeochemical processes jointly regulate dissolved organic matter (DOM) cycling. However, the structural variability of DOM across estuarine gradients remains poorly understood. Here, untargeted metabolomics was applied to investigate the structural diversity and spatial variation of DOM in surface waters across the freshwater, transition and adjacent marine zones of the YRE. Among 17,506 quality‐filtered molecular features, 1,422 were annotated and classified into 14 superclasses, dominated by organoheterocyclic compounds (24.8%), benzenoids (17.4%), and lipids/lipid‐like molecules (16.1%). Multivariate analyses revealed clear compositional differentiation among hydrographic zones, with phosphate identified as the strongest environmental factor associated with DOM composition. Phosphorus‐containing DOM declined significantly from freshwater to the transition zone, suggesting combined influences of sediment resuspension and microbial utilization. Trend‐based classification identified four major molecular trajectories across the estuarine gradient: increasing, decreasing, U‐shaped, and unimodal patterns. These trajectories were mainly represented by benzenoids, organoheterocyclic compounds, lipids and lipid‐like molecules, and phenylpropanoids and polyketides, indicating pronounced restructuring of aromatic, heterocyclic, and lipid‐associated compounds during land‐to‐ocean transport. A subset of these compounds may originate from anthropogenic sources, highlighting complex source contributions and transformation pathways. Co‐occurrence network analysis further revealed selective associations between low‐abundance bacterial taxa and differential DOM clusters, supporting a potential role of heterotrophic remineralization in shaping molecular patterns. Overall, this study provides new insights into DOM transformation mechanisms at the land‐ocean interface and underscores the importance of molecular‐level approaches for understanding coastal carbon cycling.

title: Soil microbial and nematode community responses associated with aerial thiacloprid spraying history in Pinus tabulaeformis forests of the Qinling Mountains
summary: BACKGROUND: Aerial insecticide application is an important component of pine wilt disease vector control, yet few studies have examined whether belowground communities across multiple taxa differ consistently among forests with contrasting
content: BACKGROUND: Aerial insecticide application is an important component of pine wilt disease vector control, yet few studies have examined whether belowground communities across multiple taxa differ consistently among forests with contrasting management histories. We compared unsprayed Pinus tabulaeformis forests (Control) with forests last sprayed with thiacloprid approximately 2 years (AST-2) or 4 years (AST-4) before sampling in the eastern Qinling Mountains. Soil was collected at 0-10 and 10-20 cm depth from three independent plots per category. Amplicon sequencing was used to compare community composition, diversity and ordination patterns. RESULTS: Bacterial communities were dominated by Acidobacteriota, Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota, whereas Ascomycota and Basidiomycota predominated among fungi. Bacterial and fungal communities showed clearer separation among spraying-history categories in ordination space than the overall nematode community, which overlapped more extensively. Plant-parasitic nematodes showed some separation among categories. Bacterial and nematode Shannon diversity showed no consistent increase or decrease across spraying histories, whereas fungal Shannon diversity was generally higher in AST-2. CONCLUSION: Differences among forests with contrasting spraying histories were expressed primarily in community composition, with contrasting patterns among nematode feeding guilds. These findings can inform the monitoring of belowground communities in forests subject to chemical pest management. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Children as Canaries in the Data Centers: A Case Study of Discovery Elementary in Loudoun County, Virginia
summary: Discovery Elementary School in Ashburn, Virginia, enrolls 639 children from prekindergarten through fifth grade and sits within half a mile of 11 data centers, with two more under construction and as many as 264 diesel backup generators per
content: Discovery Elementary School in Ashburn, Virginia, enrolls 639 children from prekindergarten through fifth grade and sits within half a mile of 11 data centers, with two more under construction and as many as 264 diesel backup generators permitted nearby. This case study runs the assignment test from the author’s Children as Canaries series, a sequence of four questions that separates the sentinel claim into sentinel proper, targeted selection, and captive absorption, on that school while the exposure is ongoing. Selection fails, because no one chose these children. A specified property of childhood is present: children take in more air per unit of body weight while their lungs are still developing, and diesel and traffic pollution at school has been associated with new asthma, airway inflammation, and lower academic performance. The sentinel reading still fails in practice, because no published record shows the air at the school being measured, and an October 2026 systematic review found no study of observed health outcomes near any data center. The case assigns to captive absorption. Virginia compels attendance, and the exposure differential is a product of location. The regulatory record then shows that every instrument adopted in Virginia runs forward, commissions a study, or penalizes a past violation. The 2026 generator statute reaches only permit applications filed on or after July 1, 2026, after the monitoring, health assessment, and school notice provisions of the introduced bill were dropped, and a September 2026 executive order orders a review. Federal rules allow each emergency engine 100 hours a year of testing and maintenance with no condition on when. California’s airborne toxic control measure for stationary diesel engines, as amended in 2011, bars nonemergency operation, including testing, of emergency engines already in use within 500 feet of school grounds between 7:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. on school days. The remedy for captivity therefore already exists in a form that reaches engines already installed. The assignment points to measuring the air at the school rather than the children in it, moving routine testing out of school hours, and putting sites with compulsory attendance first in any retrofit program.

title: Evaluating Recent Trends in Mixed Layer Depth Around the Kerguelen Plateau
summary: Abstract The Kerguelen Plateau in the Southern Indian Ocean sustains intense phytoplankton blooms through local iron enrichment. Changes in mixed‐layer depth (MLD) can therefore affect regional ecosystem functioning and air–sea carbon excha
content: Abstract The Kerguelen Plateau in the Southern Indian Ocean sustains intense phytoplankton blooms through local iron enrichment. Changes in mixed‐layer depth (MLD) can therefore affect regional ecosystem functioning and air–sea carbon exchange. Using 17 years (2007–2023) of observations from animal‐borne sensors and Argo floats, we reconstruct monthly MLD from sparse in situ data using principal components analysis through conditional expectation (PACE). The method is evaluated using GLORYS and a masked version reproducing the observational sampling pattern. The reconstruction captures the dominant seasonal cycle and leading spatial pattern of MLD variability. The masked‐reanalysis experiment shows that broad interannual fluctuations are more stable than fitted trends, which are particularly sampling‐sensitive. We examine these trends to determine whether the observational record supports sustained MLD change or instead reflects sampling‐induced variability. We find a deeper‐MLD region over and west of the Kerguelen Plateau, surrounded by a shallower‐MLD region and bounded to the north by the deep mixing band. Observation‐based trend estimates for 2007–2023 indicate a weak summer deepening tendency of about , consistent with GLORYS but not statistically significant. A winter shallowing tendency is obtained from the sparse reconstructions; however, it is mostly a result of poor data sampling. In the early 1990s, bottle profiles from the KERFIX station give deeper MLD than at the nearest grid point in 2007–2023, in winter and summer, but this contrast is difficult to interpret as a long‐term trend. Overall, the results suggest that domain‐wide MLD has not changed significantly around the Kerguelen region in the last two decades.

title: Synthetic auxotrophy reveals metabolic regulation of plasma cell generation, affinity maturation, and cytokine receptor signaling
summary: ABSTRACT The efficiencies with which activated B lymphocytes proliferate and develop into antibody (Ab)-secreting plasma cells are critical determinants of adaptive humoral immunity and sustain certain autoimmune diseases. Specific pathways
content: ABSTRACT The efficiencies with which activated B lymphocytes proliferate and develop into antibody (Ab)-secreting plasma cells are critical determinants of adaptive humoral immunity and sustain certain autoimmune diseases. Specific pathways in intermediary metabolism, or their substrate supply, influence lymphocyte differentiation and function. We now show that although stringent restriction of glutamine supply decreases proliferation and differentiation of B cells into plasma cells, glutaminolysis - a major means of metabolism of this amino acid - was only conditionally crucial in B cells and the Ab responses derived from them. Strikingly, Gls , the gene encoding the main glutaminase of lymphocytes, promoted anti-NP Ab responses at the primary and recall phases if either glucose uptake into B cells or pyruvate into their mitochondria was also impaired but otherwise was dispensable. This synthetic auxotrophy, i.e., conditional requirement of glutaminase for processes in addition to survival and proliferation, involved support to a progressive expansion of mitochondrial respiration followed by plasma cell differentiation. Surprisingly, impairment of glutaminase and the mitochondrial pyruvate channel decreased IL-21 stimulation of STAT3 phosphorylation as well as interferon stimulation of STAT1 activation. Together, our findings establish not only a powerful collaboration of metabolic pathways in programming increased respiration and the development of Ab-secreting cells, but also reveal modulation of cytokine receptor signaling by metabolism.

title: Selection of High Yielding and Quality Linseed Genotypes through Productivity andBiochemical Study
summary: Edible oil demand in Bangladesh is increasing rapidly, highlighting the need to enhance domestic oilseed production. Linseed, an underutilized oilseed crop, offers potential for improving oilseed self-sufficiency in the country. However, im
content: Edible oil demand in Bangladesh is increasing rapidly, highlighting the need to enhance domestic oilseed production. Linseed, an underutilized oilseed crop, offers potential for improving oilseed self-sufficiency in the country. However, improving its productivity requires the identification of high yielding superior genotypes. This study was conducted to screen linseed genotypes for high yield and quality based on yield performance and biochemical traits. Ten linseed genotypes were evaluated using Randomized Complete Block Design with three replications. Data were recorded on plant height, primary branches plant−1, capsules plant−1, seeds capsule−1, seed yield plant−1, 1000-seed weight, biological yield, seed yield, harvest index, oil content and the composition of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids. Yield components, seed yield, oil content and fatty acid composition were significantly varied in different linseed genotypes except seeds capsule−1. The maximum seed yield (1.45 t ha−1) was recorded in KUSHTIA-2, while the minimum seed yield (1.00 t ha−1) was recorded in NILA. The order of linseed genotypes based on seed yield was KUSHTIA-2 > LIN 1903 > GOPALGANJ > WB > BD 10703 > KUSHTIA-1 > BD 10705 > LIN C 2017 > CHAPAI > NILA. Maximum oil content (44.44%) was recorded in WB and the minimum (42.18%) was recorded in CHAPAI. Based on oil content, the order of linseed genotypes was WB > KUSHTIA-1 > LIN C 2017 > GOPALGANJ > KUSHTIA-2 > LIN 1903 > BD 10703 > NILA > BD 10705 > CHAPAI. Genotypes WB, KUSHTIA-2, LIN 1903 and BD 10703 had comparatively better fatty acid content as compared to other genotypes. The superior genotype(s) identified require further multi-environment evaluation to confirm their yield stability and oil content. Such validation would facilitate their effective utilization in linseed improvement programs and sustainable cultivation across diverse agro-climatic conditions of Bangladesh. Bangladesh Agron. J. 2026, 29(1): 1–10

title: Magnetic levitation and spatial superposition of a nanodiamond with a current-carrying chip
summary: We propose a current-carrying-chip scheme for generating spatial quantum superpositions using a levitating nanodiamond with a built-in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre defect. Our setup is quite versatile and we aim to create the superposition
content: We propose a current-carrying-chip scheme for generating spatial quantum superpositions using a levitating nanodiamond with a built-in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre defect. Our setup is quite versatile and we aim to create the superposition for a mass range of $10^{-19}~{\rm kg}< m< 10^{-15}~{\rm kg}$ and a superposition size ${\cal O}(10) {\rm μm} < Δx < {\cal O}(1){\rm nm}$, respectively, in $t\leq 0.1$s, depending on the position we launch from the center of the diamagnetic trap. We provide an in-depth analysis of two parallel chips that can create levitation and spatial superposition along the $x$-axis, while producing a very tight trap in the $y$ direction, and the direction of gravity, i.e., the $z$ direction. Numerical simulations demonstrate that our setup can create a one-dimensional spatial superposition state along the x-axis. Throughout this process, the particle is stably levitated in the z-direction, and its motion is effectively confined in the y-direction for a Gaussian initial condition. This setup presents a viable platform for a diamagnetically levitated nanoparticle for a table-top experiment exploring the possibility of creating a macroscopic Schrödinger Cat state to test the quantum gravity induced entanglement of masses (QGEM) protocol.

title: Contribution of fine roots on carbon allocation patterns in Norwegian forests
summary: Abstract. Boreal forests play a key role in the global carbon (C) cycle, with fine root production and turnover contributing to belowground C fluxes and inputs to soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. However, fine root biomass and production a
content: Abstract. Boreal forests play a key role in the global carbon (C) cycle, with fine root production and turnover contributing to belowground C fluxes and inputs to soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. However, fine root biomass and production are difficult to quantify and introduce uncertainty in estimates of net primary production (NPP), limiting the assessment of C allocation patterns in boreal forests. The objective of the present study was to assess how different fine root modelling approaches influence estimates of NPP, gross primary production (GPP), carbon use efficiency (CUE), and belowground C allocation to fine roots in Norwegian boreal and nemo-boreal forests. Using Norway’s national forest resource map together with MODIS remote sensing data, we estimated fine root biomass and production using three approaches that differed in how foliage biomass was derived: two based on leaf area index (from MODIS or the forest resource map) and one based on allometric biomass equations. These approaches were combined with alternative fine-root turnover rates and foliage-to-fine-root biomass ratios. Mean NPP derived from the forest resource map ranged from 318 to 243 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ across young to mature forests. In Norway spruce and Scots pine forests, NPP increased during early stand development, peaked between 50 and 80 years, and declined with increasing age. Comparison against European MODIS NPP revealed that tree growth alone accounted for 16 % of MODIS NPP, while including fine root and understory NPP contributions increased total NPP by roughly 3–5 times, depending on the fine root estimation method. CUE ranged from 0.30 to 0.63, showing age-related declines and species-level variation, with the lowest values in mature Norway spruce forests. Our analysis sheds light on the role of fine root biomass and production in forest C budgeting and their influence on NPP, CUE, and belowground C allocation. Excluding fine roots creates a major gap in forest C analyses and we conclude that the choice of method for fine root estimation has a strong impact on regional NPP and its component fluxes. Estimates of forest CUE may guide management by identifying areas with low efficiency, where interventions may enhance C sequestration.

title: A global eddy-collocated temperature and salinity profile dataset (v1.0): integrating multiplatform in situ observations with satellite-tracking mesoscale eddies
summary: Abstract. Mesoscale eddies are a fundamental component of ocean circulation and play a crucial role in shaping the three-dimensional distribution of ocean temperature and salinity. However, observational constraints have long limited system
content: Abstract. Mesoscale eddies are a fundamental component of ocean circulation and play a crucial role in shaping the three-dimensional distribution of ocean temperature and salinity. However, observational constraints have long limited systematic, global-scale quantification of eddy-induced thermohaline variability. Here, we present a global eddy-collocated historical temperature and salinity profile dataset spanning 29 years (1993–2021), constructed by integrating in situ hydrographic profile observations with satellite-derived mesoscale eddy tracking products. The dataset contains 2.35 million quality-controlled temperature-salinity profiles, each collocated with the nearest mesoscale eddy on the sampling day that may have influenced the observed water column. The profiles provide broad global coverage, with most 2°×2° grid boxes containing more than 150 observations, enabling statistically robust analyses from regional to global scales. Validation against well-documented regional eddy signatures shows that the dataset consistently reproduces well-established eddy-induced temperature and salinity anomaly structures across diverse ocean regions. Example applications demonstrate the dataset’s capability to investigate the spatial heterogeneity and vertical extent of eddy-induced thermohaline anomalies, eddy impacts on mixed-layer depth and stratification, eddy contributions to subsurface extreme temperature events, and eddy-driven heat and material transports. This dataset provides a comprehensive observational foundation for advancing quantitative assessments of mesoscale eddy impacts on regional to global ocean physical environment, heat budgets, and climate change.

title: Shell hash promotes growth in Pacific littleneck clams ( Leukoma staminea ) by altering pore water chemistry
summary: Abstract. Bivalves that build calcium carbonate skeletons are at particular risk from ocean acidification, and mitigation strategies will be needed to keep coastal populations healthy. It can be energetically costly for organisms like clams
content: Abstract. Bivalves that build calcium carbonate skeletons are at particular risk from ocean acidification, and mitigation strategies will be needed to keep coastal populations healthy. It can be energetically costly for organisms like clams and mussels to build their shells under low pH conditions, and acidification can lead to shell dissolution. Adding crushed shells (shell hash) to beach sediments, a practice used by some Indigenous communities and aquaculturists, may mitigate the negative effects of ocean acidification by altering the chemistry of the pore fluids they live in. We tested the hypothesis that mixing shell hash into the sediment improves the growth and physiology of infaunal Pacific littleneck clams (Leukoma staminea). Juvenile clams (pre-sexual maturity) were raised for 90 days under four conditions: control seawater with sediment, acidified seawater with sediment, control seawater with sediment plus shell hash, and acidified seawater with sediment plus shell hash. Pore water and overlying seawater were sampled three times a week for pH, alkalinity, salinity, temperature, and dissolved oxygen. Clam shell weight, soft tissue weight, and new shell growth were measured, and mantle tissue RNA was collected for gene sequencing after three months. Our results demonstrate that the addition of shell hash increased the pH of porewater relative to the control, and animals exposed to acidified water plus shell hash grew larger than animals exposed to acidified water alone. Gene expression profiling suggests that animals in acidified seawater with shell hash were largely indistinguishable from animals in non-acidified water. Our experimental results suggest that adding shell hash to sediments alters the chemistry of pore fluids, thus buffering against acidic conditions that can negatively affect the growth of economically and culturally important shellfish like littleneck clams.

title: A crown story: how tree size and structure drive maple syrup yields
summary: ABSTRACT Maple syrup production is strongly influenced by spring weather conditions, particularly the frequency and intensity of freeze–thaw cycles. However, marked individual differences in sap and sugar yields persist among trees growing
content: ABSTRACT Maple syrup production is strongly influenced by spring weather conditions, particularly the frequency and intensity of freeze–thaw cycles. However, marked individual differences in sap and sugar yields persist among trees growing under similar stand conditions, indicating additional tree-level sources of variation. This study aimed to explain inter-individual variability in maple yields in commercial high-vacuum syrup production using structural, morphological, and growth characteristics. We used terrestrial light detection and ranging to derive variables describing crown, stem, and whole-tree size, biomass, and structure in 38 mature sugar maples. We related these variables to individual yields, including sap volume, sugar content, and syrup production. Our models explained substantial inter-individual variability: 52% in sap sugar content, 44% in sap volume, and 47% in syrup production. Laterally expanded crowns were associated with higher sap sugar content, as were lower growth rates in the first 25 mm of wood. Sap volume was highest in large, heavily branched trees with crowns extending vertically along the stem. Projected crown surface area was the strongest predictor of syrup yield, with an estimated increase of 250 mL per 5.6 m 2 . These findings highlight the importance of multidimensional crown development in maximizing individual yields in maple syrup production.

title: Impacts of the heterogeneous ammonia uptake on air quality in the North China Plain
summary: Abstract. Previous studies have revealed that the heterogeneous uptake of ammonia (NH3) on secondary organic aerosols (SOA) profoundly influences the NH3 budget, nitrate aerosol chemistry, and the regional PM2.5 burden, also constituting an
content: Abstract. Previous studies have revealed that the heterogeneous uptake of ammonia (NH3) on secondary organic aerosols (SOA) profoundly influences the NH3 budget, nitrate aerosol chemistry, and the regional PM2.5 burden, also constituting an important source of nitrogen-containing organic compounds (NOCs). However, current regional modeling efforts are hindered by large uncertainties in uptake coefficients (γ) and a persistent lack of field-based observational constraints. In this study, we incorporate a first-order reactive NH3 uptake mechanism into the WRF-Chem model to evaluate its impacts on air quality and NOCs over the North China Plain (NCP) during November 2017, with a wide range of the uptake coefficient from 10-5 to 10-3. When simulations are constrained with available observations in the NCP, we conclude that the uptake coefficient of 10-5 is characterized as a conservative upper-bound estimate for this heterogeneous process. Sensitivity simulations with the uptake coefficient of 10-5 reveal that the uptake reaction decreases NH3 concentrations by 0.62 % and inorganic aerosol and PM2.5 concentrations by less than 0.06 %, but contributes 1.2 μg m-3 of NOCs in the NCP. This study suggests that the uptake reaction might be a vital path for NOCs formation, but its impact on air pollutants concentrations is insignificant.

title: Cross-linked chitosan-nicotinic acid beads (CLC-NAB)—a novel adsorbent for the removal of Hg(II) ions from aqueous medium
summary: Abstract An adsorbent, cross-linked chitosan-nicotinic acid beads (CLC-NAB) were fabricated in a sustainable green method and used effectively for the selective adsorption of mercury(II) from aqueous solutions. The CLC-NAB were characterize
content: Abstract An adsorbent, cross-linked chitosan-nicotinic acid beads (CLC-NAB) were fabricated in a sustainable green method and used effectively for the selective adsorption of mercury(II) from aqueous solutions. The CLC-NAB were characterized by swelling study, FTIR spectroscopy, SEM and elemental analysis. Optimum conditions for the adsorption process were determined by varying various operational parameters including initial pH, adsorbent dosage, initial mercury(II) concentrations, contact time, temperature. Kinetic studies showed that the mercury adsorption is best described by both pseudo-second-order and intra particle diffusion kinetic model. The adsorption experimental data were well fitted to Redlich-Peterson isotherm model and the monolayer adsorption capacity is 1060.2 mg/g. The values of the thermodynamic parameters (ΔG˚ and ΔH˚) revealed that the adsorption was spontaneous in nature and endothermic. Complete removal of toxic mercury(II) ions was attained by using 150 beads at pH 5. 1 M NaCl and 1 M NaNO 3 were utilised as desorbing agents to completely desorb mercury ions from CLC-NAB. Overall, cross-linking with nicotinic acid improves chitosan's adsorption performance. Therefore, the environment-friendly CLC-NAB with good stability can be used as a promising adsorbent for the removal of mercury(II) from aqueous solutions.

title: Contrasting stages of agricultural abandonment reflected in carbon pools, greenhouse gas fluxes, and soil biogeochemistry at two drained peatlands
summary: Peatland drainage has led to significant soil carbon (C) losses, contributing to global greenhouse gas emissions. While rewetting is a key climate mitigation strategy, many abandoned, previously drained peatlands undergo secondary successio
content: Peatland drainage has led to significant soil carbon (C) losses, contributing to global greenhouse gas emissions. While rewetting is a key climate mitigation strategy, many abandoned, previously drained peatlands undergo secondary succession by shrubs and trees, forming wet woodlands. The climatic and biogeochemical implications of this encroachment remain poorly understood, particularly on drained, nutrient-enriched peat soils. This study investigated C stocks and turnover processes in a temperate peatland across two stages of abandonment: a recently abandoned grassland and a site abandoned 75 years ago, now encroached by dense willow shrubland. We assessed above- and belowground biomass and soil C stocks, in situ CO2 and CH4 fluxes, soil temperature, water table depth (WTD), and soil and groundwater geochemistry. Laboratory soil incubations evaluated site-specific response of soil C flux to moisture and temperature. The results indicate that willow encroachment was associated with substantially greater biomass C storage (sevenfold higher level) and higher soil C stocks than the grassland (56.2 ± 4.92 vs. 36.5 ± 1.70 kg C m⁻²), as well as a deeper peat layer. While both sites remained deeply drained on an annual basis (annual mean WTD >30 cm), the willow shrub exhibited lower soil respiration under variable soil moisture content than the grassland did in the laboratory incubations, suggesting long-term biogeochemical adaptation and enhanced soil C recalcitrance. Lower porewater N and higher Fe and P concentrations at the willow shrub indicate potential for nutrient retention and reduced leaching. Additionally, a first attempt to estimate C loss through ecosystem respiration (Reco) at the willow shrub suggested that Reco was substantially higher for the grassland than the willow shrub (3.50 ± 0.40 vs 2.83 ± 0.72 kg C m-2 yr-1). These findings suggest that wet woodland encroachment can support C retention and environmental buffering on drained peat soils. However, where abandoned soils stay deeply drained – such as the willow shrub where the water table approached terrain only four times during the measurement year, more intensive rewetting efforts remain essential to restore peatland functioning as a C sink.

title: Combatting deforestation through trade: The EU's unilateral and regional approaches
source: Review of European Comparative & International Environmental Law
summary: Abstract Global deforestation, primarily driven by agricultural expansion, exacerbates climate change and biodiversity decline, prompting concerted international efforts to combat it. As a major destination for key deforestation‐linked comm
content: Abstract Global deforestation, primarily driven by agricultural expansion, exacerbates climate change and biodiversity decline, prompting concerted international efforts to combat it. As a major destination for key deforestation‐linked commodities and their derived products, the EU has significantly contributed to forest loss worldwide. In response, the EU's Deforestation Regulation, adopted in 2023, and its renewable energy regime concerning biofuels aim to ensure the sustainability of supply chains and reduce the EU's deforestation footprint. This unilateral framework, affecting imports and domestic sales, is subject to World Trade Organization (WTO) scrutiny. In parallel, the EU's regional trade agreements (RTAs) increasingly incorporate forest‐ and climate‐related commitments. Through a primarily doctrinal lens, this article examines such a dual‐track policy in light of recent WTO rulings in EU—Palm Oil and new developments in the EU's RTA practice, including under the EU–Mercosur agreement, concerning environmental sustainability. The article argues that, while the WTO legal system permits a risk‐based anti‐deforestation approach in principle, the EU's policy should be implemented with sufficient flexibility, meaningful engagement with partner countries and stronger coordination between the unilateral and regional tracks to ensure its trade‐law consistency and improve its environmental effectiveness.

title: Sinking Silicates. I. Characterizing the Benchmark System Containing the T0 Brown Dwarf CWISEJ210640.16+250729.0 using JWST
summary: Abstract In this study, we present the full (97.3% complete) 0.8–12.5 μ m spectral energy distribution (SED) of an L/T transition object, CWISE J210640.16+250729.0 (CW 2106), using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). We provide a full ch
content: Abstract In this study, we present the full (97.3% complete) 0.8–12.5 μ m spectral energy distribution (SED) of an L/T transition object, CWISE J210640.16+250729.0 (CW 2106), using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). We provide a full characterization of the host star’s elemental abundances and age. We empirically derive the bolometric luminosity (≈ −4.825 dex) of CW 2106, and obtain estimates of its mass ( M ≈ 50–62 M Jup ), radius ( R ≈ 0.83–0.87 R Jup ), effective temperature ( T eff ≈ 1213 K), and surface gravity ( log g ≈ 5.28 dex). We find the near-infrared (near-IR) spectrum (0.8–2.5 μ m) is best reproduced with cloudy atmospheric models while the mid-infrared (mid-IR) spectrum (5–12.5 μ m) is best reproduced with cloudless models. This suggests a cloud layer restricted to only the deepest observable parts of the atmosphere and is qualified by the lack of a 9 μ m silicate feature. Making use of the Mg/Si ratio of the primary, alongside thermochemical models, we predict the clouds in CW 2106 to be composed primarily of enstatite (MgSiO 3 ), removing ∼23% of the bulk oxygen out of the atmosphere. Future retrieval studies will be able to help investigate the existence and full impact of these cloud species.

title: Diversity of planetary origins and compositions traced by stellar abundance differences among co-natal star systems
summary: So called co-natal stars are wide binaries that form from the same molecular cloud and are expected to share the same stellar composition. However, observations indicate stellar abundance differences in a small fraction of these co-natal sy
content: So called co-natal stars are wide binaries that form from the same molecular cloud and are expected to share the same stellar composition. However, observations indicate stellar abundance differences in a small fraction of these co-natal systems. These stellar abundance differences have been attributed to the ingestion of planets by their host stars. In this study, we analyze a previous sample of co-natal stars to determine the composition of the planets that had been ingested by their host stars. The abundance differences in these co-natal pairs come in different flavours, where systems can show a positive abundance difference of the refractory elements (Fe, Mg, Si) paired with a positive, zero, or negative abundance difference of volatiles (O, C, S). Positive trends of refractory and volatile abundance differences can be explained (at minimum) by the ingestion of a single planet by one of the stars. However, positive trends of refractory abundance differences paired with zero or negative abundance differences of oxygen and carbon imply that both stars are required to ingest planets formed at different locations (i.e. interior or exterior to the water and/or carbon grain evaporation front). Furthermore, some systems show a sulfur abundance difference that is a factor of a few lower than the abundance difference of Fe, Si, and Mg, even though sulfur is mostly accreted via the moderately volatile compound FeS. We show that this can be explained by the migration of one of the planets across the FeS evaporation front, where the planet first accretes large amounts of sulfur with the solids and then no sulfur, while still accreting the other refractory elements before being ingested by its host star. Our study shows that the planetary compositions derived from the detailed stellar abundances are sufficient to explain the measured abundance differences of co-natal stars, giving us a handle on the composition of exoplanets. At the same time it implies very different planetary compositions caused by the different formation location of these planets, in agreement with planet formation models dedicated to the formation of inner super-Earths and sub-Neptunes.

title: Spatiotemporal Coastal Air-Quality Contrasts under Transboundary Influence: Sentinel-5P CO and NO₂ over Prince Edward Island (Canada) and Massachusetts (U.S.)
summary: Coastal and island airsheds experience compound pressures from local emissions and long-range transport, yet multi-year comparisons between lower-emission island receptors and densely urbanized coastal jurisdictions remain limited. Using Pr
content: Coastal and island airsheds experience compound pressures from local emissions and long-range transport, yet multi-year comparisons between lower-emission island receptors and densely urbanized coastal jurisdictions remain limited. Using Prince Edward Island (PE), Canada, and Massachusetts (MA), U.S., a lower-emission island and a densely urbanized coastal state, we analyse Sentinel-5P TROPOMI observations from 2019 to 2024 to compare column behaviour of CO and NO₂, pollutants with contrasting atmospheric lifetimes. The results show that (1) CO exhibits closely synchronized jurisdiction-scale behaviour consistent with a strong regional-background influence, including elevations in 2023, with closely similar province/state means and overlapping 95% confidence intervals; (2) NO₂ exhibits opposing seasonal regimes, with PE summer-elevated (mean summer ≈ 7.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol m⁻²) and MA winter-elevated (≈4.2 × 10⁻⁵ mol m⁻²), producing a counterintuitive PE > MA annual mean despite higher localized urban peaks in MA; (3) spatial maps show compact corridor-associated NO₂ hotspots in MA versus a comparatively more spatially diffuse NO₂ pattern in PE; and (4) exploratory concordance with independent external evidence shows construct-dependent correspondence across pollutants and jurisdictions. The six-year temporal and spatial patterns support a screening-versus-compliance framework in which satellite columns can help prioritize season-specific ground monitoring, identify candidate corridors for follow-up, and support smoke-event screening, while exposure assessment and regulatory compliance remain based on validated surface observations or appropriately validated fused products. The findings therefore support summer NO₂ monitoring priorities in PE and winter corridor monitoring in MA and provide a transferable screening framework for other coastal and island jurisdictions.

title: Optimizing yield and water productivity in arid Northwest China: A source-sink perspective on drip-fertigated potatoes
summary: Water and nitrogen (N) availability regulate assimilate production (source) and accumulation (sink), ultimately determining potato yield and water productivity (WP c ). However, previous studies have primarily focused on final yield or stat
content: Water and nitrogen (N) availability regulate assimilate production (source) and accumulation (sink), ultimately determining potato yield and water productivity (WP c ). However, previous studies have primarily focused on final yield or static source-sink relationships, whereas the temporal dynamics of biomass allocation under different irrigation regimes and N rates remain unclear. This study quantified the effects of soil wetted proportion (P), irrigation frequency (F), and N rate on sink/source ratio dynamics, yield, WP c and tuber quality in arid Northwest China. Three-year field experiments evaluated three P levels (P1: 35%, P2: 55% and P3: 75%) in 2014–2015, and three irrigation frequencies (F1: once every 2 days, F2: once every 4 days and F3: once every 6 days) combined with three N rates (140, 220, 300 kg ha −1 ) in 2018. The results indicated that increasing P or reducing F resulted in a higher late-stage sink/source ratio. However, correlation analysis revealed that while an elevated sink/source ratio during the early-to-mid growth stages was positively associated with final yield and crop evapotranspiration, it exhibited a significant negative correlation with tuber starch and protein contents. To balance this allocation, the P2 (55%) treatment effectively maintained source-sink coordination, resulting in yield and WP c that were significantly increased by 15.5% and 22.8% relative to those under P3 in 2015. In 2018, the highest yield and WP c were recorded under the F1N3 treatment, whereas low-frequency irrigation restricted total dry matter accumulation and limited the crop's yield response to high N inputs. Consequently, based on an entropy-weight TOPSIS comprehensive evaluation, regulating spatial soil moisture through a moderate wetted proportion (P2), and adopting high-frequency irrigation (F1) with adequate nitrogen (N3), represent a promising agronomic strategy for achieving comprehensive multi-criteria performance under the tested conditions.

title: Effects of Daily Light Integral and Flower Thinning on Growth, Fruit Production, and Sugar Composition of ‘Kuemsil’ Strawberries in a Vertical Farm
summary: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) production in a vertical farm requires coordinated management of the light supply and reproductive growth to improve the yield and fruit quality.This study evaluated the daily light integral (DLI; 15,
content: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) production in a vertical farm requires coordinated management of the light supply and reproductive growth to improve the yield and fruit quality.This study evaluated the daily light integral (DLI; 15, 17.5, and 20 mol•m -2 •d -1 ) and flower thinning (3, 5, and 7 flowers per inflorescence) in 'Kuemsil' strawberries during 83 days of reproductive growth.Increasing the DLI shifted fruit production toward larger fruits and increased the number of marketable fruits, defined as fresh weight > 10 g and soluble solids content ≥ 10 °Brix.The soluble solids content ranged from 10.1 to 11.8 °Brix and was significantly lower at DLI 15 than at DLI 20.A sugar analysis showed greater sucrose content at DLI 20, whereas fructose and glucose decreased.Flower thinning alone did not significantly affect the marketable fruit number across DLI levels, although retaining three to five flowers per inflorescence supported fruit quality under DLI 20.Overall, a DLI of 20 mol•m -2 •d -1 with three to five flowers per inflorescence was the most effective treatment combination for improving marketable production and sweetness-related characteristics of 'Kuemsil' strawberries under controlled indoor cultivation.

title: Combined climate change and arsenic pollution increases rice cadmium with little effect on micronutrients
summary: (Background and Aims) Rice production faces the dual threat of increasing soil As contamination and climate change. Each stressor can alter micronutrient (e.g. Fe, Zn) and toxin (e.g., Cd) plant uptake and internal translocation. Yet, the c
content: (Background and Aims) Rice production faces the dual threat of increasing soil As contamination and climate change. Each stressor can alter micronutrient (e.g. Fe, Zn) and toxin (e.g., Cd) plant uptake and internal translocation. Yet, the combined effects of soil As contamination and climate change factors on the nutritional quality and safety of rice grain remain poorly elucidated. (Methods) A full-factorial pot experiment growing rice under two soil As levels (low-As, high-As) and four climate conditions (today; elevated CO2 (+435 ppm CO 2 ); elevated temperature (+5° C); future (combined elevated CO 2 and temperature)) was performed. (Results) Grain Fe decreased slightly with soil As contamination and was barely altered by future climate conditions. Grain Zn and Cd both decreased with soil As contamination and increased with future climate. For grain Zn, the decrease with As contamination led to an overall decrease (by 25%) with combined soil As contamination and future climate. For Cd, increased concentrations under future climate outweighed the effect of soil As, leading to two-fold increased grain concentrations with As contamination and future climate combined. (Conclusion) Our results provide insight into the processes controlling Fe, Zn, and Cd in rice grown in polluted systems threatened by climate change, and highlight the critical importance of multifactorial, mechanistic studies.

title: Hydrate formation at sea-level lowstands during glacial cycles: Temporal constraints from overpressure evolution
summary: Marine gas hydrate is a huge carbon sink on Earth. Understanding how past climate change affected it is crucial for predicting its environmental impacts in a warmer future. A major challenge, however, is that the hydrate formation time in g
content: Marine gas hydrate is a huge carbon sink on Earth. Understanding how past climate change affected it is crucial for predicting its environmental impacts in a warmer future. A major challenge, however, is that the hydrate formation time in geological systems remains poorly constrained. Previously, we could only infer the formation time of gas hydrates formed within the past tens of thousands of years. Here, we present a novel approach and the first successful attempt to date hydrates formed in the geological past using overpressure evolution in overlying sediments. Overpressures of ~0.58 MPa and ~0.5 MPa were observed in hemipelagic deposits overlying a hydrate-bearing sand in the updip and downdip directions, respectively, in the Qiongdongnan Basin, South China Sea. The inferred high pore pressures caused an abnormally high porosity of ~70% at ~136 m below the seafloor. Overpressure evolution during sedimentation shows that updip hydrates formed at ca. 135 ka, coinciding with the formation time of earliest cold seep in this region, and downdip hydrates formed at ca. 110 ka. Both formations occurred during sea-level lowstands and were separated by an ~25 k.y. interval matching glacial cycle. We interpret that sea-level falls triggered upward migration of deep gas, successively inducing hydrate formation across the sand. Thus, sea-level falls may not only dissociate shallow-water hydrates but also promote new hydrate formation in deep-water settings by solidifying gas that migrated from below into the overlying sedimentary system. Gas hydrate may be a carbon sink rather than the seeping methane source proposed by the “clathrate gun hypothesis” during sea-level lowstands.

title: Lithium: the protective cation singled out by Alzheimer’s disease
summary: Lithium is a mood stabilizer that is most prescribed in psychiatry for managing mental disorders.Many findings indicate that lithium is also neuroprotective in various neurodegenerative diseases.In particular, lithium has been of great inte
content: Lithium is a mood stabilizer that is most prescribed in psychiatry for managing mental disorders.Many findings indicate that lithium is also neuroprotective in various neurodegenerative diseases.In particular, lithium has been of great interest as an affordable but still effective treatment for Alzheimer's disease (AD), due to its diverse neuroprotective actions and mechanistic overlap with key AD pathways, such as A production and tau modification.While the multifaceted activities may result from lithium's inhibitory action on two key enzymes, glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK-3) and inositol monophosphatase (IMPase), recent findings suggest that selective lithium depletion in neurons mediated by amyloid deposits may be a key pathological trigger in AD and supplementation with lithium orotate, a lithium salt with reduced amyloid binding, may even reverse brain damage and prevent cognitive decline.In this study, we review the neuroprotective properties of lithium, its known mechanisms of action, and discuss its therapeutic potential in AD, a topic that has been debated for decades.[BMB Reports 2026; 59(10)

title: Wood-derived biochar as a potential sustainable alternative to lichens for monitoring airborne potentially toxic elements
summary: In this study, we evaluated two wood-derived biochars (BCH) as passive monitoring matrices for atmospheric PTEs, benchmarking their performance against the epiphytic lichen Evernia prunastri (L.) Ach. The materials were first characterized
content: In this study, we evaluated two wood-derived biochars (BCH) as passive monitoring matrices for atmospheric PTEs, benchmarking their performance against the epiphytic lichen Evernia prunastri (L.) Ach. The materials were first characterized in terms of elemental composition, surface chemistry (XPS), specific surface area (BET), and morphology (SEM). They were then exposed in outdoor and indoor campaigns, representative of combined wet and dry deposition outdoors and predominantly dry deposition indoors. Exposure settings were selected to capture contrasting deposition regimes and to enable an overall (setting-agnostic) comparison of matrix sensitivity, not to rank settings by contamination. The accumulation of As, Cd, Cu, Zn, Ni, Pb, Cr, and Sb was quantified by ICP-MS and interpreted using the Exposure-to-Control (EC) ratio and the Pollution Load Index (PLI). Calculated as the geometric mean of EC ratios, PLI summarized the relative multi-element accumulation response of each matrix. Accumulation patterns varied among elements and exposure settings. BCH2 showed the highest overall PLI, although BCH1 had the largest BET surface area (62.1 m 2 g -1 , compared with 37.8 for BCH2 and 30.1 for the lichen), indicating that surface area alone does not explain the observed accumulation patterns. Outdoor magnetic measurements showed a larger absolute increase in mass-specific susceptibility in BCH2 (64.0 × 10 -9 m 3 kg -1 ) than in the lichen (10.6 × 10 -9 m 3 kg -1 ). However, the high intrinsic magnetic background of BCH2 resulted in substantially lower relative magnetic contrast, limiting its suitability for magnetic biomonitoring. Overall, the results support the potential of biochar as a complementary matrix for chemical monitoring of atmospheric PTEs, including indoor settings.

title: Integrated Nitrogen, Farmyard Manure, and Vermicompost Improve Barley Productivity in the Central Highlands of Ethiopia
summary: Soil fertility depletion caused by declining organic matter and imbalanced nutrient inputs is a major constraint to barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) production in the Ethiopian highlands. A field experiment was conducted during the 2022/2023 mai
content: Soil fertility depletion caused by declining organic matter and imbalanced nutrient inputs is a major constraint to barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) production in the Ethiopian highlands. A field experiment was conducted during the 2022/2023 main cropping season at Holeta Agricultural Research Center, Ethiopia, to evaluate the effects of integrating nitrogen fertilizer, vermicompost, and farmyard manure on soil properties and barley productivity under a randomized complete block design with three replications. Initial soil analysis indicated clay-textured, moderately acidic soil with low organic carbon (1.22%), total nitrogen (0.12%), and available phosphorus, confirming nutrient limitations in the study area. Integrated nutrient application significantly (P < 0.05) improved soil chemical properties, yield components, and grain yield compared with sole application of organic or inorganic fertilizers. The combined application of 75% recommended vermicompost and 75% recommended nitrogen fertilizer produced the highest grain yield (4545.59 kg ha⁻ 1 ), followed by 75% farmyard manure combined with 75% nitrogen fertilizer. Yield improvement was associated with increased spike length, grains per spike, and aboveground biomass production. Vermicompost-based treatments showed relatively greater yield advantages than farmyard manure treatments, likely due to faster nutrient mineralization and improved nutrient availability. Economic analysis also indicated higher net returns and marginal profitability under integrated nutrient management treatments. The results demonstrate that combining organic amendments with mineral nitrogen improves soil fertility and barley productivity and provides a sustainable nutrient management strategy for food barley production in the Ethiopian highlands.

title: Topsoil chemical differentiation in mapped brown forest soil units of Southern Bulgaria
summary: hemical differentiation within the uppermost centimetres of mineral soil is rarely resolved in regional surveys, because sampling depths of 0–20 cm average across the layer in which surface accumulation actually occurs. This study compares
content: hemical differentiation within the uppermost centimetres of mineral soil is rarely resolved in regional surveys, because sampling depths of 0–20 cm average across the layer in which surface accumulation actually occurs. This study compares two successive topsoil intervals, 0–5 and 5–10 cm, at fifteen sampling points distributed across the Western Rhodopes in Southern Bulgaria, all located within areas mapped as brown forest soils. Twenty-nine samples were analysed for soil reaction, the components of the sorption complex, organic carbon, humus and total nitrogen. The upper interval contained approximately 53% more organic carbon (3.48 versus 2.28%) and 70% more total nitrogen (2.17 versus 1.28 g kg−1) than the interval immediately below it, and both contrasts remained significant after false discovery rate adjustment under parametric and distribution-free tests alike. Soil reaction was slightly lower at the surface (6.50 versus 6.66), a difference that was statistically supported but quantitatively small, with a 95% confidence interval reaching only -0.29 pH units. The components of the sorption complex–total exchange capacity, exchangeable calcium and magnesium, hydrolytic acidity and base saturation–showed no significant differentiation between the two intervals. Expressed as stratification ratios, organic carbon and nitrogen gave mean values of 1.67 and 1.87, whereas exchange capacity, base saturation and pH all gave ratios close to unity. Surface accumulation of organic matter and nitrogen therefore proceeds without a corresponding reorganisation of the exchange complex, and a 0–10 cm composite would have concealed the greater part of it.

title: Advanced Heat Transfer
summary: Advanced Heat Transfer , Fourth Edition provides a comprehensive source for analyzing heat transfer problems across a wide range of modes and applications in energy systems, including conduction, convection, radiation, phase change, and che
content: Advanced Heat Transfer , Fourth Edition provides a comprehensive source for analyzing heat transfer problems across a wide range of modes and applications in energy systems, including conduction, convection, radiation, phase change, and chemically reactive flows with heat transfer. The fourth edition introduces significant updates, including new content on historical perspectives of heat transfer, experimental methods, measurement uncertainties, and solidification processing of materials. It expands upon the coverage of advanced cooling techniques for electronics, waste heat recovery, and microchannel heat exchangers. New case studies explore topics such as optimization of electronic assemblies, directional solidification, heat recovery in industrial applications, and neural networks. This book is intended for senior undergraduate and graduate mechanical, aerospace, and chemical engineering students taking courses in Heat Transfer, Multiphase Heat Transfer, and Advanced Thermodynamics. A Solutions Manual, PowerPoint Lecture Slides, and Figure Slides are available for adopting instructors. The eBook+ version of this book features new interactive learning features, including multiple-choice and true/false quizzes, flashcards, and links to video and audio lectures.

title: ANALISIS CADANGAN KARBON PADA DUKUH DI DESA SUNGAI ALANG KECAMATAN KARANG INTAN
summary: The dynamics of mixed garden land cover are often influenced by pressures from human activities, such as land expansion for monoculture farming, large – scale plantations, or settlements, which lead to the loss of the forest's ability to ab
content: The dynamics of mixed garden land cover are often influenced by pressures from human activities, such as land expansion for monoculture farming, large – scale plantations, or settlements, which lead to the loss of the forest's ability to absorb carbon, thereby directly impacting global climate change. One of the ways to mitigate climate change and global warming is by preserving the ecological functions of absorbing and storing carbon, which can be achieved through maintaining and protecting forest vegetation from damage. This study aims to analyze the estimated carbon stock in the soil surface within Dukuh, Sungai Alang Village, Karang Intan District, Banjar Regency. Data collection was conducted at the sapling, pole, tree, and necromass growth levels using a non-destructive method. Sampling of understory vegetation and litter was carried out using a destructive method, followed by oven-drying in the laboratory. The results of this study indicate that the estimated total biomass aboveground is 1,477.072 tons/ha, with an estimated total carbon stock aboveground of 694.220 tons/ha. The pole level has an estimated total biomass of 123.051 tons/ha and a carbon stock of 57.834 tons/ha. The tree level has an estimated total biomass of 1,353.465 tons/ha and a carbon stock of 636.130 tons/ha. The litter layer has an estimated total biomass of 0.350 tons/ha and a carbon stock of 0.160 tons/ha. The understory vegetation has an estimated total biomass of 0.176 tons/ha and a carbon stock of 0.082 tons/ha. Deadwood has an estimated total biomass of 0.030 tons/ha and a carbon stock of 0.014 tons/ha

title: Evolution towards functional stability of buried wood in an anoxic Lab Wood Vault for durable carbon dioxide removal
summary: Wood harvesting and storage (WHS) via Wood Vaulting is an emerging carbon dioxide removal method. Its effectiveness hinges on long-term wood preservation but currently our process understanding is limited. A major type of Wood Vault aims to
content: Wood harvesting and storage (WHS) via Wood Vaulting is an emerging carbon dioxide removal method. Its effectiveness hinges on long-term wood preservation but currently our process understanding is limited. A major type of Wood Vault aims to create anoxic (oxygen-free) condition to stop biological degradation. Here we study wood preservation inside a ‘Lab Vault’ where wooden discs are buried under a layer of clay to seal off air with subsequent monitoring of gas concentrations. Our results show 3 stages of gas evolution: (1) Aerobic decomposition: O 2 decreased from 21 to 0% by the consumption of a small amount of organic matter in 10 days, replaced by CO 2 ; (2) Anaerobic decomposition in the next 1.5 months, with CH 4 increased from 0.0002% to 0.2%; (3) A ‘deep anoxic state’ where both aerobic and anaerobic decomposition stop or slow down drastically with zero oxygen and negligible CH 4 generation while CO 2 remains high. The third stage signifies a ‘functional stability’ where wood degradation stops completely. However, long-term maintenance requirement of anoxic condition on millennial timescales cannot be directly inferred from the short-term experiment because anoxic condition was initially created by wood decay. Our experiment suggests that Wood Vault is fundamentally different from landfill, which is often used as a reference in commercial implementation standards. Our results provide direct observational evidence of the initial biophysical processes underlying durable wood preservation, as well as targets for engineering design and monitoring and verification for biomass burial as a climate solution.

title: Time-Dependent Expression of Photosynthetic Genes in C3 and C4 Halophytes in Response to Osmotic and Ionic Components of Salinity
summary: Abstract The temporal dynamics (3, 6 h, 1–4 days) of photosynthetic gene transcripts accumulation in response to salinity (400 mM NaCl) in C 3 halophyte Chenopodium quinoa Willd. and C 4 halophyte Salsola komarovii (Iljin) Akhani & Roalson
content: Abstract The temporal dynamics (3, 6 h, 1–4 days) of photosynthetic gene transcripts accumulation in response to salinity (400 mM NaCl) in C 3 halophyte Chenopodium quinoa Willd. and C 4 halophyte Salsola komarovii (Iljin) Akhani & Roalson were studied. Analysis of changes in water content, sodium accumulation, and antioxidant enzymes activity made it possible to separate the responses to the osmotic and ionic components of salinity in time. Three stages of response to salinity were identified: early response (3–6 h), sodium accumulation stage (1–2 days) and toxic ionic effect (3–4 days). At the early stage of salinity, osmotic stress was detected only in the C 3 halophyte, which led to a decrease in water content and in the expression of rbcL , psbA and PnsB5 genes. At the sodium accumulation stage, both species showed an increase in psbA expression, which was accompanied by increased PGR5 expression in C 3 species. The toxic effect of Na + led to an increase in expression of psbA , as well as PGR5 and PnsB5 genes of both pathways of cyclic electron transport (CET) photosystem I (PSI) in the C 3 halophyte with increased sodium flow through the leaf. Overall, genes encoding Rubisco, PSII components, and two CET PSI pathways were more sensitive to salinity in C. quinoa than in S. komarovii . This reflects differences in tolerance to osmotic and ionic stress in these species, possibly driven by both the C 4 carbon concentration mechanism in S. komarovii , which promotes more efficient water use, and the salt-excreting ability of C. quinoa , which results in high Na + flux through the leaf.

title: Burn intensity regulates post-fire effects on soil N 2 O emissions: A grassland soil pyrocosm study
summary: Post-fire soil emissions of nitric oxide (NO) and nitrous oxide (N 2 O) are important ecosystem nitrogen (N) loss pathways, but their flux dynamics vary widely across studies, making generalizations challenging. Natural variation in burn in
content: Post-fire soil emissions of nitric oxide (NO) and nitrous oxide (N 2 O) are important ecosystem nitrogen (N) loss pathways, but their flux dynamics vary widely across studies, making generalizations challenging. Natural variation in burn intensity—or heat energy released during combustionm—may help resolve this variability by mediating the soil physicochemical and biological drivers of these emissions. Here, we used an experimental "pyrocosm" system to evaluate how varying burn intensity influences post-fire NO and N 2 O emissions using soil from a Southern California grassland across 18 weeks. Over several months, we measured soil NO and N 2 O fluxes alongside soil pH, extractable nitrate (NO 3 - ) and ammonium (NH 4 +), net NH 4 + production, net nitrification, soil carbon (C) pools, microbial biomass C, and the potential activities of five extracellular hydrolytic enzymes under Control, Low- (100.1 ± 20.0 o C peak soil temperature at 5 cm depth), and High-intensity (243.8 ± 7.4 o C peak soil temperature at 5 cm depth) burns. Soil NO emissions were not significantly affected by burn intensity. In contrast, N 2 O emissions tripled under low burn intensity relative to unburned controls, but did not differ from controls at high burn intensity. This stimulation of N 2 O emission under low burn intensity was driven by increased denitrification, as supported by elevated soil pH and labile C availability, and an 88% reduction in net nitrification that signaled active NO 3 - consumption. Under high burn intensity, however, severe loss of microbial biomass, soil C, and NO 3 - constrained denitrification, with rising hydrolytic enzyme activities over time suggesting C limitation. Together, these findings demonstrate that post-fire N 2 O emissions reflect a fire intensity-dependent balance between microbial mortality and resource limitation, helping to explain divergent N emissions across ecosystems.

title: Glutamate-1-semialdehyde aminotransferase is redox regulated by a TRX f/m-NTRC module coordinating chlorophyll biosynthesis and photosynthesis in pea
summary: Pea ( Pisum sativum ) is a major global legume whose productivity depends on photosynthesis. Chlorophyll, essential for photosynthesis, is synthesized via tetrapyrrole biosynthesis (TBS), where 5-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) is the sole metabo
content: Pea ( Pisum sativum ) is a major global legume whose productivity depends on photosynthesis. Chlorophyll, essential for photosynthesis, is synthesized via tetrapyrrole biosynthesis (TBS), where 5-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) is the sole metabolic precursor. Glutamate-1-semialdehyde aminotransferase (GSAAT) plays a significant role in ALA formation, yet its precise role and regulation in pea are currently unknown. In this study, a single PsGSA gene was identified in pea, phylogenetically explained by the loss of a duplicated lineage during legume evolution. PsGSA is leaf-enriched, light-responsive, and encodes a chloroplast-localized protein. Silencing PsGSA severely impaired GSAAT activity, ALA-synthesizing capacity, chlorophyll biosynthesis, and photosynthesis, and triggered feedback down-regulation of other TBS genes. GSAAT activity is redox-regulated, with Cysteine 169 and Cysteine 191 forming a regulatory disulfide bond that modulates its activity. In addition, NADPH-dependent thioredoxin reductase C (NTRC), thioredoxin (TRX) f, and TRX m function as an integrated module that interacts with GSAAT. In vitro , the module synergistically reduced and reactivated oxidized GSAAT more efficiently than any single component. In pea, simultaneous silencing of all three genes caused pronounced GSAAT oxidation, activity decrease, chlorophyll deficiency, and photosynthetic decline, whereas single silencing NTRC or double silencing TRX f and TRX m showed milder phenotypes, indicating functional complementarity within the module. Our findings demonstrate that TRX f, TRX m, and NTRC act as an integrated redox module to precisely control GSAAT activity, thereby ensuring efficient TBS and photosynthesis in pea, and provide insights into target orchestration by the chloroplast redox system.

title: Practical approach to the fish health consultation
summary: Background : There are an estimated 100 million pet fish living in homes across the UK; given the widespread popularity of fish as pets, it is not surprising that many owners seek veterinary care for their aquatic companions. Aim of the art
content: Background : There are an estimated 100 million pet fish living in homes across the UK; given the widespread popularity of fish as pets, it is not surprising that many owners seek veterinary care for their aquatic companions. Aim of the article : This article provides readers with a comprehensive guide to approaching fish cases in first‐opinion practice, focusing on the common diseases found in koi and goldfish. Additionally, it highlights effective diagnostic and therapeutic treatments that can be applied in these cases.

title: Integrated fertilizer management and agrometeorological conditions associated with yield and nutritional quality of Boro rice
summary: Increasing rice production while improving grain nutritional quality is essential for global food security. We hypothesized that integrated fertilizer management combined with a suitable rice variety would enhance grain yield, nutrient upta
content: Increasing rice production while improving grain nutritional quality is essential for global food security. We hypothesized that integrated fertilizer management combined with a suitable rice variety would enhance grain yield, nutrient uptake, and nutritional quality compared to conventional fertilizer management, while agrometeorological conditions would help explain variations in crop performance. Accordingly, this study evaluated the effects of rice variety and integrated fertilizer management on growth, yield, nutrient uptake, and grain nutritional quality of Boro rice and examined their associations with agrometeorological variables. BRRI dhan89 outperformed BINA dhan10, exhibiting greater plant height and superior yield attributes. BRRI dhan89 produced the highest grain yield with 75% chemical fertilizers plus 25% cow dung, whereas BINA dhan10 produced the lowest grain yield under the control treatment. Nutrient analyses revealed that BINA dhan10 had higher calcium, magnesium, iron, zinc, and starch content, whereas BRRI dhan89 had elevated levels of nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulfur, and protein. Combining 75% chemical fertilizers with 25% cow dung was associated with higher macro- and micronutrient uptake and improved grain nutritional characteristics. Grain yield was positively correlated with grain nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and sulfur concentrations. Moreover, grain yield was positively associated with sunshine duration and air temperature but negatively associated with relative humidity.
