The highest benefit-cost ratio (2.02) was observed in BRRI dhan89 with the combination of 75% chemical fertilizers and 25% cow dung. Post-harvest soil analysis showed higher soil organic carbon and selected available nutrient concentrations under integrated fertilizer management. Under the conditions evaluated, application of 75% of the recommended chemical fertilizer rates with 25% cow dung, particularly in BRRI dhan89, was associated with greater grain productivity and nutrient uptake, along with favorable grain nutritional characteristics. However, further multi-location and multi-season studies are needed to validate the wider applicability of these findings.

title: Dose-dependent growth and gene expression in marine prokaryotes in response to glacial and non-glacial iron-rich colloids from Kerguelen Island (Southern Ocean)
summary: Abstract Iron (Fe) plays a central role in regulating prokaryotic carbon (C) metabolism through complex processes. In Fe-limited limited ocean regions, new sources can influence prokaryotic activity thereby modulating the microbially mediat
content: Abstract Iron (Fe) plays a central role in regulating prokaryotic carbon (C) metabolism through complex processes. In Fe-limited limited ocean regions, new sources can influence prokaryotic activity thereby modulating the microbially mediated cycling of carbon. However, while accelerated glacial melting delivers substantial quantities of Fe-rich material to the ocean, the bioavailability of glacial Fe remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the response of marine prokaryotes to Fe contained in the colloidal fraction (20–200 nm size fraction) originating from the Cook Ice Cap on Kerguelen Island (Southern Ocean). We assessed growth and gene transcriptional responses to dose-dependent additions of Fe-rich colloids from two sources, glacial meltwater and a non-glacial origin. The two colloid types resulted in dose-dependent, but contrasting growth responses. Increasing additions of glacial colloids resulted in a reduction in prokaryotic growth and the opposite pattern was observed with non-glacial colloids. Transcriptional profiles revealed an increasing trend in Fe-limitation, as evidenced by transcripts of the glyoxylate shunt, as a function of the addition of either colloid type. We further observed a dose-dependent increase in transcripts of aromatic compound degradation only in the non-glacial colloid incubations, suggesting that these Fe-rich colloids could also provide C. These results point to the key role of C regulating prokaryotic growth in response to Fe-rich colloids. The quantitative transcriptional responses observed provide insights to the nutritional status of prokaryotes and to compounds and pathways involved in processing Fe-rich colloids.

title: Natural fire-derived charcoal resembles high-temperature biochar in regulating soil CO2 emissions from a subtropical plantation soil
summary: Char is a carbon (C)-rich pyrogenic material generated either during natural fire events (natural charcoal) or through the thermochemical conversion of plant biomass (engineered biochar). However, whether these two types of char have compar
content: Char is a carbon (C)-rich pyrogenic material generated either during natural fire events (natural charcoal) or through the thermochemical conversion of plant biomass (engineered biochar). However, whether these two types of char have comparable effects on soil CO 2 emissions remains unclear. In this study, we conducted a 30-day incubation experiment to compare the effects of charcoal produced from Pinus massoniana bark during broadcast burning and engineered biochars produced from the same feedstock at 300, 500, and 900 °C (B300, B500, and B900) on soil CO 2 emissions, physicochemical properties, and bacterial diversity and composition. The addition of B300 significantly increased soil CO 2 emissions ( p < 0.05), whereas B500, B900, and charcoal had no significant effects. B300 addition markedly increased the relative abundances of Proteobacteria and Cyanobacteria while decreasing those of Acidobacteriota, Chloroflexi, and Verrucomicrobiota ( p < 0.001). Mixed-effects models accounting for treatment variation showed that soil pH was negatively associated with cumulative CO 2 emissions, whereas Proteobacteria exhibited a positive association. Random forest analysis identified Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota as potential predictors of cumulative CO 2 emissions, although these relationships require further validation. In contrast, natural fire-derived charcoal caused minimal changes in bacterial community composition. Overall, our findings demonstrate that high-temperature biochars (>500 °C) exhibit similar effects on soil CO 2 emissions and bacterial community to natural charcoal in subtropical plantation soils, highlighting their potential as functional analogues of fire-derived charcoal.

title: MSPRP: multi-granularity symptom-aware probabilistic representation prompting for target-domain-free plant disease detection
summary: Introduction Existing vision-language zero-shot anomaly detection methods have mainly been validated on industrial datasets and often suffer from lesion-scale variations, domain shifts, and complex background interference when directly appl
content: Introduction Existing vision-language zero-shot anomaly detection methods have mainly been validated on industrial datasets and often suffer from lesion-scale variations, domain shifts, and complex background interference when directly applied to field plant images. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MSPRP, a multi-granularity symptom-aware probabilistic representation prompting method for target-domain-free plant disease detection. Methods Based on frozen CLIP encoders, MSPRP introduces three modules: the Multi-Granularity Symptom-Aware Module (MGSAM) performs learnable hierarchical fusion and spatial-channel symptom attention on multi-layer patch features, the Uncertainty-Aware Prompt Flow Module (UPFM) models healthy/diseased prompts as probabilistic representations to improve prompt adaptability, and the Adaptive Cross-Modal Prototype Aggregation Module (ACPAM) aggregates suspected symptom prototypes from high-response patches to reduce background interference in image-level disease scoring. The model is trained only on the industrial MVTec AD dataset and tested on target agricultural datasets without target-domain training. Results A field Polygonatum odoratum disease dataset is also constructed as an evaluation benchmark. Experimental results show that MSPRP achieves the best average AUROC and AP among methods that do not use target agricultural training images. Ablation results verify the contribution of each module. Discussion Overall, MSPRP provides a target-domain-free computational methodology for field plant disease discrimination without target agricultural training images or target-domain pixel-level lesion annotations.

title: Sports Matter
summary: This engaging book explores how advances in materials have transformed the way sports are played. It traces the adoption of new materials across a range of popular sports, showing how innovations in equipment have influenced performance, te
content: This engaging book explores how advances in materials have transformed the way sports are played. It traces the adoption of new materials across a range of popular sports, showing how innovations in equipment have influenced performance, technique, safety, and even the evolution of the games themselves. Alongside the history and development of each sport—including the emergence of new sports from established ones—the book outlines how rules have changed over time. It also examines the discovery, development, and structure of the materials used in sporting equipment, explaining the properties that make them suitable for particular applications and comparing them with alternative materials. Each chapter concludes by considering how future innovations may continue to shape the game. The book is a valuable resource for general readers, sports enthusiasts, and anyone interested in the science behind sporting equipment.

title: Fabrication of mesoporous monolithic titania–carbon hybrids with superior performance in removing strontium species from aqueous effluents
summary: Radioactive waste management in a safe, easy, and cost-effective manner is a critical imperative for the global environment. Removal of radioactive strontium ( 90 Sr) from contaminated water, such as seawater (high-salinity matrices), with
content: Radioactive waste management in a safe, easy, and cost-effective manner is a critical imperative for the global environment. Removal of radioactive strontium ( 90 Sr) from contaminated water, such as seawater (high-salinity matrices), with high efficiency and selectivity remains a critical challenge. Here, we report a one-pot sol-solvothermal synthesis of a titania-carbon composite monolith (TCCM) based on in situ carbonization. The TCCM exhibited many advantages, including a high specific surface area (138.2 m 2 g -1 ) and a narrow pore size distribution (6.2 nm). The results indicated that this batch adsorption study showed a maximum Sr 2+ adsorption capacity of 77.3 mg g -1 at pH 6–9. The fabricated material demonstrates high selectivity, removing 86% of Sr 2+ (9.5 mg g -1 ) from authentic Red Sea seawater. Kinetics follow the pseudo-second-order model (R 2 = 0.992), and the Langmuir isotherm confirms monolayer chemisorption. Furthermore, the TCCM retains 89.2% of its initial capacity after six regeneration cycles, outperforming many reported composites. Thus, TCCM is a durable, highly selective, and reusable strontium sorbent in complex aqueous environments.

title: Volcanic CO2 as a non-linear geochemical transfer signal
summary: Introduction Volcanic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is widely used to infer deep magmatic degassing, but the flux measured at the surface is filtered by hydrothermal storage, chemical reactions, pathway permeability, and environmental forcing. Met
content: Introduction Volcanic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is widely used to infer deep magmatic degassing, but the flux measured at the surface is filtered by hydrothermal storage, chemical reactions, pathway permeability, and environmental forcing. Methods In this study, a low-dimensional geochemical transfer theory links dissolved magmatic carbon, mobile exsolved CO2, hydrothermal pressure, aqueous and mineral carbon storage, and connected-fracture permeability. Local linearization quantifies the frequency-dependent gain and delay of a mobile-gas perturbation transmitted to the surface, together with barometric admittance. A reduced nonlinear realization provides synthetic checks of direct, buffered, delayed, and pathway-controlled responses; frequency-specific recovery, parameter-sensitivity, and time-step analyses show how these responses depend on storage and pathway time scales. A published-data test using 30 Solfatara surveys evaluates whether the sampled flux distributions can be explained using a single multiplicative amplitude factor. Results The direct-proxy interpretation is recovered only when hydrothermal retention is weak, pathway conductance is approximately stationary, and atmospheric forcing is small. Both ordinary least-squares and robust Theil–Sen estimates show upper-quantile scaling shallower than the unit slope required by that null model (for Q 95 , slopes of 0.28 and 0.46, with Theil–Sen 95% interval 0.10–0.88). Discussion The result indicates non-uniform scaling of the sampled flux distribution, consistent with changes in spatial distribution and pathway contribution in addition to bulk amplitude. The theory therefore converts a qualitative source-versus-pathway ambiguity into explicit transfer regimes, local observation degeneracies, and measurement requirements within one physically interpretable geochemical structure.

title: Tree and neighborhood damage have distinct effects on delayed mortality after a severe hurricane
summary: Tropical forest resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration depend on tree survival. Disturbance events, such as hurricanes, generate distinct forms of damage at the individual-tree and neighborhood scale, providing a unique setting
content: Tropical forest resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration depend on tree survival. Disturbance events, such as hurricanes, generate distinct forms of damage at the individual-tree and neighborhood scale, providing a unique setting to disentangle the causal contributions of mortality drivers. Leveraging post-hurricane census data for nearly 4000 trees in the Luquillo Forest Dynamics Plot, Puerto Rico, we used a causal inference framework combined with Bayesian multilevel models to estimate the effect of individual- and neighborhood-scale damage on delayed tree mortality following Hurricane Maria (2017). Individual damage effects depended on species identity and tree size. Stem break emerged as the most lethal form of damage across the community. Neighborhood damage was associated with elevated mortality following Hurricane Maria, independent of focal tree damage. This effect was strongest among large trees, consistent with disproportionately high physiological stress resulting from greater inherent metabolic demands, refoliation energy costs, and evapotranspiration following canopy recovery. Severe biomass loss (> 75% crown loss) buffered large trees from negative neighborhood effects, revealing a positive pruning effect on survival. Our study advances mechanistic understanding of delayed tree mortality, while also suggesting how mortality patterns may shift with expected increases in disturbance severity under a warming climate.

title: Resource availability reshapes clonal recovery and trait coordination across fragment configurations of Salvinia natans
summary: Abstract Background Clonal aquatic plants can regenerate from fragments, but how light and nutrient availability influence recovery across fragment configurations remains poorly understood. We conducted a four-week factorial experiment with
content: Abstract Background Clonal aquatic plants can regenerate from fragments, but how light and nutrient availability influence recovery across fragment configurations remains poorly understood. We conducted a four-week factorial experiment with the floating fern Salvinia natans , combining two light levels, two nutrient levels and three configurations: light fragmentation (LF; two three-node fragments), moderate fragmentation (MF; three two-node fragments) and severe fragmentation (SF; six single-node fragments). Initial total node number was standardized across configurations, with five replicate pots per treatment combination. We measured growth, biomass allocation and frond-specific metabolism, and examined trait coordination using plant trait multilayer networks (PTMNs). Results Under high-light, nutrient-rich conditions, MF produced more frond pairs and ramets and accumulated more dry weight than LF or SF. Under low light, dry-weight accumulation remained low and differences among configurations narrowed. High light combined with low nutrients was associated with higher carbohydrate concentrations and a greater submerged-frond to floating-frond dry-weight ratio. PTMNs showed contrasting patterns of trait coordination: LF had the greatest cross-layer connectivity, MF the strongest local clustering, and SF the highest module interlayer association. Carbohydrate traits and biomass allocation occupied central network positions, with the leading hubs differing among configurations. Conclusions The growth advantage of MF depended on resource availability. Fragment configurations were also associated with distinct relationships among carbohydrate status, tissue allocation and clonal growth. These findings show that recovery responses differed in both growth performance and the coordination of traits across functional layers.

title: O DESMATAMENTO NA AMAZÔNIA BRASILEIRA E SUAS CONSEQUÊNCIAS NA CAPTAÇÃO DOS BENEFICIOS CLIMÁTICOS NO ANTROPOCENO
source: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável
summary: Este artigo faz abordagem sobre a região Amazônica e suas principais características na época geológica do Antropoceno, no período de 1988 a 2023 a partir de dois principais pontos sobre a floresta amazônica brasileira: o desmatamento colet
content: Este artigo faz abordagem sobre a região Amazônica e suas principais características na época geológica do Antropoceno, no período de 1988 a 2023 a partir de dois principais pontos sobre a floresta amazônica brasileira: o desmatamento coletado por meio de sensoriamento remoto por satélite e coleta de dados in situ na floresta; e as consequências climáticas na escala global, regional e local na captação dos benefícios para a floresta no estado do Pará na relação floresta-clima. O objetivo é compreender as razões do desmatamento e os benefícios do carbono na relação floresta-clima. Sendo assim, os descritores utilizados através da metodologia de revisão da literatura, são aplicados, e que diversos autores demonstram como a colaboração efetiva entre cientistas e formuladores de políticas pode levar a uma conservação bemsucedida. Com isso a pesquisa tem como resultado fornecer um guia para ampliar os esforços de conservação florestal para a Amazônia em geral. Finalmente, olhamos para o futuro da pesquisa sobre florestas na Amazônia e destacamos algumas vias mais interessantes para trabalho sustentável como os benefícios climáticos.

title: Indonesia’s Palm Oil Trilemma: Reconciling Biodiesel Expansion, Export Competitiveness, and Supply Resilience under Climate and Governance Constraints
source: Journal of Business Research and Reports
summary: Indonesia’s palm oil sector is being asked to serve an expanding domestic energy market while sustaining food and oleochemical supply, export competitiveness, rural livelihoods, and ecological integrity. This interpretive qualitative litera
content: Indonesia’s palm oil sector is being asked to serve an expanding domestic energy market while sustaining food and oleochemical supply, export competitiveness, rural livelihoods, and ecological integrity. This interpretive qualitative literature review examines the resulting policy trilemma using peer-reviewed research published during 2020-2026 and the IPOSS fourth-quarter 2026 industry outlook as a contextual, explicitly prospective source. The analysis differentiates observed evidence from institutional forecasts, policy announcements, and conceptual scenarios. It synthesises eight interconnected themes: stock-flow consistency; biodiesel allocation and fiscal costs; climate-related production lags; smallholder yield gaps and replanting; commodity pricing and fiscal instruments; welfare distribution; deforestation-related market governance; and adaptive policy coordination. The synthesis indicates that additional domestic biodiesel demand can support energy substitution while raising the opportunity cost of exports and the exposure of levy-financed incentives to commodity price cycles. Weather risks, delayed biological yield responses, constrained smallholder finance, and traceability demands further limit simple supply-side solutions. We propose an integrated decision architecture combining equivalent-unit physical accounting, reserve and food-security safeguards, risk-sensitive biodiesel support, productivity-led expansion without deforestation, and inclusive market access. Five conditional scenarios clarify where policy complementarities are possible and where trade-offs remain unavoidable. The analysis does not claim new econometric estimates or validate IPOSS forecasts. Rather, it identifies measurable policy thresholds, evidence limitations, and a research agenda for jointly assessing energy security, trade value, public finances, farmer welfare, and ecological boundaries.

title: Outdoor PM2.5 Chemical Components and Risk of Lung Cancer in a Large Prospective U.S. Cohort
summary: Abstract Regional heterogeneity in the association between fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and lung cancer suggests that PM2.5 components may differentially influence risk. We used a spatiotemporal model to estimate historical (2000–2004) r
content: Abstract Regional heterogeneity in the association between fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and lung cancer suggests that PM2.5 components may differentially influence risk. We used a spatiotemporal model to estimate historical (2000–2004) residential outdoor PM2.5 component concentrations (sulfate, ammonium, nitrate, black carbon, organic matter, mineral dust, sea salt) for participants from the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study. We used Cox models to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals (HR [CI]) of associations per interquartile range of PM2.5 components and common copollutant nitrogen dioxide (NO2) with lung cancer, overall and by histologic subtype. We fitted single-pollutant models and then specified the multipollutant mixture using elastic net regression. From the start of follow-up in 2010 through 2018, 8565 lung cancer cases were diagnosed among 364,842 participants. In single-pollutant models, sea salt (HR = 1.02 [1.00–1.04]) was associated with overall lung cancer risk; sea salt (HR = 1.04 [1.00–1.07]) and black carbon (HR = 1.05 [1.00–1.10]) with adenocarcinoma; and ammonium (HR = 1.10 [1.00–1.21]), sulfate (HR = 1.15 [1.04–1.27]), organic matter (HR = 1.06 [1.01–1.12]), and black carbon (HR = 1.09 [1.01–1.17]) with squamous cell carcinoma. NO2 was associated with increased risk overall and adenocarcinoma. In mixture models, NO2 (HR = 1.08 [1.03–1.13]) and sea salt (HR = 1.04 [1.01–1.07]) were associated with adenocarcinoma, and sulfate was marginally associated (HR = 1.14 [0.98–1.13]) with squamous cell carcinoma. We found no clear associations with small cell tumors. These findings suggest that certain PM2.5 components play a role in lung cancer subtype etiology. Given the limited number of existing studies, replication of these findings in diverse geographic locations is an important next step.

title: Input uncertainty overshadows cropland greenhouse gas accounting and mitigation tracking
summary: Abstract Tracking agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation to achieve the Paris Agreement goal requires robust emission baselines. Here we test the impact of choice of input datasets on emission baselines. We tested 1,284 source-specifi
content: Abstract Tracking agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation to achieve the Paris Agreement goal requires robust emission baselines. Here we test the impact of choice of input datasets on emission baselines. We tested 1,284 source-specific input-dataset combinations across11,100 gridded emission maps through an IPCC Tier 1/2 framework at 5 arcmin resolution, covering cropland GHG from nitrogen inputs (synthetic fertilizer, manure and crop residues), rice paddies, and drained peatland, to characterize the dataset-driven uncertainty. The range of total emissions across input datasets was 1.9 Gt CO2eq yr-1, comparable to the central estimate of total cropland GHG emissions circa 2020 (2.4 Gt CO2eq yr-1) and to the assessed annual technical mitigation potential of these sources by 2050 (1.8 Gt CO2eq yr-1). For countries responsible for 99% of rice CH₄, 72% of nutrient N₂O and 50% of peatland emissions among those with an assessed mitigation potential, the variation of national emission estimates across input datasets exceeded the country's technical mitigation potential for the same source. This makes it extremely challenging to confidently monitor reductions in emissions from these sources. Activity dataset choice was the leading contributor to variance for every source (78-99% of ANOVA sum-of-squares), substantially exceeding climate, hydrology, or emission-factor zonation. The uncertainty carried a distinct spatial fingerprint, concentrated in identifiable sub-national hotspots: the Indo-Gangetic Plain for nutrient N₂O, monsoon-Asia rice basins for CH₄, and tropical peat-forest margins for peatland CO₂. These findings show an urgent need to harmonize and standardize agricultural activity datasets, because consistent input data are an essential prerequisite to reliably track national cropland mitigation.

title: Indigenous Rights in Climate Governance: A Comparative Qualitative Study of Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia
source: Journal of Contemporary Governance and Public Policy
summary: This article examines how human rights paradigms are integrated into climate policymaking through institutional and regulatory governance, focusing on grassroots realities in the Global South. Addressing literature dominated by bibliometric
content: This article examines how human rights paradigms are integrated into climate policymaking through institutional and regulatory governance, focusing on grassroots realities in the Global South. Addressing literature dominated by bibliometric meta-analyses and top-down normative studies, it adopts a qualitative comparative design covering Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia. Data are triangulated from key informant interviews, community observations, and legal discourse analysis. The findings reveal a persistent paradox: although international legal frameworks increasingly recognise procedural rights, market-based mitigation initiatives such as Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) may reproduce forms of carbon colonialism. This governance architecture can bypass Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC), as illustrated by the Kichwa experience in Peru’s Cordillera Azul National Park. Indigenous agency has nevertheless generated legal and institutional resistance, including the December 2024 Bellavista Mixed Court ruling, the Sarayaku people’s Kawsak Sacha declaration, Ecuador’s Yasuní referendum, and Colombia’s asymmetrical decentralisation under Decree 632 of 2018. The article also considers Inter-American Court of Human Rights Advisory Opinion OC-32/25 and highlights solastalgia as an often-overlooked psychological consequence of climate change. It concludes that formal rights recognition remains limited without power redistribution, direct territorial funding, and effective enforcement. The study is particularly relevant to SDGs 10, 13, 15, and 16, with implications for SDG 3.

title: Pyroplastics: A new potential threat to coastal environments in the Anthropocene
summary: Pyroplastics are thermally altered plastic debris formed through processes such as melting, deformation, charring, or partial combustion, commonly associated with fires in coastal environments. In recent years, pyroplastic have been found o
content: Pyroplastics are thermally altered plastic debris formed through processes such as melting, deformation, charring, or partial combustion, commonly associated with fires in coastal environments. In recent years, pyroplastic have been found on a global scale, both in marine sandy and pebble shore regions. In this article, we examine the global occurrence and distinctive characteristics of pyroplastics, together with their potential environmental fate and associated impacts. The quantity of pyroplastics that are discovered on coastal beaches (n = 11, 69%) is almost twice as high as the amount found on island beaches (n = 5, 31). Pyroplastic may fragment into secondary microplastic and contain potentially hazardous metals. The polymer types most frequently found in pyroplastic are polypropylene (n = 10, 26%), and polyethylene (n = 9, 23%). The heavy metals which are mostly occurred together within the pyroplastic are lead (Pb) and chromium (Cr). Most widely used spectrometer for the pyroplastic polymer analysis is Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) (n = 14, 78%). This review also highlights a governance gap, as current plastic pollution frameworks and beach monitoring systems rarely recognize pyroplastics and related plastic rock types as distinct categories requiring targeted waste management, monitoring, and policy responses. This study comprehensively presents the pyroplastic geological and environmental research implications with quantitative analysis of substantial published data, offering fundamental insights for future research planning.

title: Climate Change, Associated Risks and Environmental Damages in Mozambique: A Systematic Review
source: International Journal of Environmental Protection and Policy
summary: Climate change is one of the most significant environmental and societal challenges of the twenty-first century. Its effects are expressed through changes in temperature and precipitation patterns, the increasing frequency and intensity of
content: Climate change is one of the most significant environmental and societal challenges of the twenty-first century. Its effects are expressed through changes in temperature and precipitation patterns, the increasing frequency and intensity of extreme events, environmental degradation, and growing risks to human livelihoods and well-being. Mozambique is particularly vulnerable because of its exposure to floods, droughts, tropical cyclones, coastal erosion, and other climate-related hazards, as well as its limited adaptive capacity in many communities. This article aims to review the state of the art on climate change and associated environmental risks, with particular emphasis on studies conducted in Mozambique. It also seeks to identify the main theoretical approaches, research trends, and knowledge gaps in the analysis of climate variability, vulnerability, impacts, resilience, and adaptation. The study adopted a qualitative approach based on a narrative literature review of scientific articles, reports, and other relevant academic publications addressing climate change, climate variability, environmental risks, vulnerability, resilience, and Mozambique. The reviewed literature was analyzed thematically in order to identify the principal concerns, methodologies, and findings presented by previous studies. The review shows that the international literature has substantially advanced the understanding of the environmental and human consequences of climate change, particularly in relation to vulnerability, adaptation, resilience, and disaster risk. In Mozambique, however, most studies focus on the impacts of natural disasters, vulnerability assessments, resilience, adaptation strategies, and projected climate-change scenarios. Comparatively fewer studies provide robust statistical analyses of historical temperature and precipitation records to demonstrate observed climate anomalies and long-term climatic trends. This limitation reduces the empirical basis for distinguishing between climate variability and anthropogenic climate change at local and regional scales. The article concludes that future research in Mozambique should combine vulnerability and impact assessments with systematic analyses of observed climatic data, climate indices, and regional climate projections. Such an integrated approach would strengthen the scientific basis for environmental planning, risk reduction, adaptation policies, and sustainable territorial development.

title: Evaluation of Wheat Genotypes for Combined Heat and Drought Stress Tolerance
summary: A field experiment was carried out from November 2021 to April 2022 to assess the tolerance of five wheat genotypes to combined heat and drought stress. The study followed a split plot design with three replications. The main plot treatment
content: A field experiment was carried out from November 2021 to April 2022 to assess the tolerance of five wheat genotypes to combined heat and drought stress. The study followed a split plot design with three replications. The main plot treatment consisted of two growing conditions (normal condition and combined heat and drought condition) and the sub-plot treatments consisted of five wheat genotypes (BARI Gom 29, BARI Gom 30, BARI Gom 31, BWMRI Gom 3 and BAW 1290). Under stress, BARI Gom 30 and BAW 1290 showed comparatively smaller reduction in days to anthesis and plant height than under the normal condition. In the case of days to physiological maturity, number of spikes m−2 and grains spike−1, the lowest reduction was found in BWMRI Gom 3 under combined heat and drought conditions and spike length and spikelets spike−1 were the same both under normal and combined heat and drought conditions. In the case of BARI Gom 30 the number of spikes m−2 was increased in stress conditions more than normal conditions. The lowest reduction of 1000-grain weight was found in BARI Gom 30 and in case of grain yield and above ground biological yield reduction was less in BWMRI Gom 3 and BARI Gom 30 under stress conditions than normal. Better yield components such as number of spikes m−2 and grains spike−1 under stress conditions, contributed to enhanced combined heat and drought tolerance in BWMRI Gom 3 and BARI Gom 30 compared to BAW 1290, BARI Gom 31 and BARI Gom 29. Based on stress susceptibility index (SSI) for grain yield, the genotypes were ranked as BWMRI Gom 3 (0.75) > BARI Gom 30 (0.84) > BAW 1290 (0.93) > BARI Gom 31 (1.09) > BARI Gom 29 (1.34) where BWMRI Gom 3 and BARI Gom 30 was found most tolerant. Thus, BARI Gom 30 and BWMRI Gom 3 appear suitable for cultivation in heat- and drought-prone regions of Bangladesh. Bangladesh Agron. J. 2026, 29(1): 20-31

title: Frequent appearance of nucleation-mode particles in the marine atmosphere downwind of an urban area
summary: . An intensive field campaign was conducted during September 2024 in Poros, a Greek island 55 km south of Athens, Greece, to investigate the frequency of new particle formation (NPF), the characteristics of the formed particles and the spat
content: . An intensive field campaign was conducted during September 2024 in Poros, a Greek island 55 km south of Athens, Greece, to investigate the frequency of new particle formation (NPF), the characteristics of the formed particles and the spatial extent of the NPF events, as well as the possible factors controlling their formation. Poros is often downwind of the Attica region, with major urban and industrial sources, while the surrounding Saronic Gulf is a major shipping corridor. Simultaneous particle size distribution measurements were carried out in Poros and two background sites in Athens. In Poros, local NPF events were rare, only 2 out of 24 days. However, transported nucleation-mode particles (NMP) events were frequent (almost 70% of the days), with particles appearing at sizes of 10-25 nm. The observations suggest that these particles were of secondary origin and not primary particles emitted by ships plumes. Backward trajectory analysis linked these events to air masses from Attica, which typically spent 2-5 h over the Saronic Gulf before arriving in Poros. About one third of the transported events (5 out of 16) in Poros did not occur in Athens, indicating that the spatial scale on which new particles were formed was much less than the distance between the two sites and of the order of a few tens of km. Accounting for the transported events where horizontal transport was to some extent evident, the potential area in which the NPF takes place in the Saronic Gulf was estimated to be several tens of km (averaging 28 ± 19 km) to the north and west of Poros, where SO 2 emissions were elevated due to shipping and industrial activity in the broader area. However, considerable uncertainties prevent precise localization of the formation region. Our analysis suggests that marine areas with similar conditions as in our study, characterized by high OH levels, downwind of urban and industrial areas, can be hotspots for new particle formation, typically occurring on a spatial scale of a few tens of km.

title: Influence of LED spectral quality and natural growing conditions on flowering, yield, and fruit biochemical quality of okra (Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) Moench)
summary: Introduction Climate change poses significant challenges to open-field production of okra ( Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) Moench), a tropical vegetable crop of high nutritional and economic value. This study evaluated the effects of light-emi
content: Introduction Climate change poses significant challenges to open-field production of okra ( Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) Moench), a tropical vegetable crop of high nutritional and economic value. This study evaluated the effects of light-emitting diode (LED) spectral quality on reproductive development, fruit characteristics, yield, mineral composition, antioxidant activity, and total phenolic content of okra. Methods Plants were grown under blue (452 nm), red (659 nm), and combined red/blue (9:1; 657/447 nm) LED lighting at a photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD) of 400 µmol m −2 s −1 under a 10-h photoperiod and compared with greenhouse and outdoor conditions. Results The red/blue 9:1 (RB 9:1) treatment promoted earlier flowering, with anthesis occurring approximately 37 days after sowing, and showed the highest numerical fruit length and fresh fruit mass, as well as the highest yield per plant and estimated yield per hectare, the latter being approximately twice that of the other growing conditions. RB 9:1 showed the highest numerical concentrations of calcium, potassium, sulfur, copper, and zinc, while outdoor plants showed the highest numerical concentrations of iron and strontium and red light the highest numerical rubidium concentration. RB 9:1 showed the highest numerical antioxidant activity, although it was not significantly different from red or blue light. Blue light showed the highest numerical total phenolic content, with no significant differences among treatments. Discussion Overall, RB 9:1 showed promising potential for earlier reproductive development and fruit production under the tested conditions.

title: Updated Estimates of Radiocarbon‐Based Deep Ocean Circulation Age
summary: Abstract The deep ocean circulation age based on radiocarbon was last determined almost 20 years ago, when digital archiving was not standard practice. This work updates the circulation age while making two improvements by using new nutrien
content: Abstract The deep ocean circulation age based on radiocarbon was last determined almost 20 years ago, when digital archiving was not standard practice. This work updates the circulation age while making two improvements by using new nutrient data and modifying the calculation. The newly calculated circulation age is spatially more coherent and older in the deep North Pacific than before. The basin‐averaged circulation age for the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, and Southern Ocean is respectively 256, 930, 689, and 326 years. The study confirms the centennial timescale of the world oceans.

title: National‑Scale Soil Erosion Risk Mapping in Zambia Using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE)
summary: Soil erosion poses a significant threat to agriculture and land sustainability across sub-Saharan Africa. In this study, we assess the extent and spatial distribution of soil erosion in Zambia using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation
content: Soil erosion poses a significant threat to agriculture and land sustainability across sub-Saharan Africa. In this study, we assess the extent and spatial distribution of soil erosion in Zambia using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) model. This model incorporates environmental parameters, including rainfall erosivity (R), soil erodibility (K), slope length and steepness (LS), cover-management (C), and support practices (P) to estimate average annual soil loss across the landscape. To achieve this, we integrated a Digital Elevation Model (DEM), satellite-based precipitation data, global soil databases, and land cover maps within a GIS environment. Furthermore, high-resolution orthoimages were used to identify and digitize existing conservation practices (e.g., contour farming, terracing), to accurately assess the P-factor. Results showed that the majority of the country is characterized by very low erosion susceptibility. However, critical erosion hotspots were identified in areas lacking conservation measures, exceeding tolerable soil loss thresholds. The study results confirmed that areas implementing erosion control exhibited significantly reduced soil loss, highlighting the effectiveness of these land management strategies. The derived spatial erosion patterns provide valuable insights for prioritizing conservation measures and sustainable land use planning in Zambia.

title: DIFFERENT PHOSPHORUS-SOLUBILIZING BACTERIA COMPOSITION FOR LETTUCE CROPS: INTERSECTIONS OF AGRONOMIC EFFICIENCY, FAMILY FARMING, CIRCULAR ECONOMY, BRAZILIAN PUBLIC POLICIES AND SUSTAINABILITY INTERNATIONAL AGENDA
source: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável
summary: Phosphorus bioavailability is a major constraint in tropical agriculture, demanding alternatives that reduce environmental risks and promote sustainability. This study evaluated different compositions of phosphate-solubilizing bacteria (PSB
content: Phosphorus bioavailability is a major constraint in tropical agriculture, demanding alternatives that reduce environmental risks and promote sustainability. This study evaluated different compositions of phosphate-solubilizing bacteria (PSB) in lettuce cultivation, focusing on their socio-environmental implications. The bio-inputs acted as physiological sinks, converting phosphorus into plant biomass while mitigating environmental footprints and water eutrophication risks. Integrating industrial byproducts validated a circular economy model, offering a viable replacement for mineral fertilizers. From a social science and public policy perspective, democratizing access to these sustainable biotechnologies directly strengthens the socioeconomic resilience of family farming. By reducing economic vulnerability to global input markets, this technology connects biological soil management to Brazilian law and the international sustainability agenda. Aligning with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and climate justice frameworks, these regenerative practices promote a fair, inclusive, and legally supported agricultural transition.

title: Crossfeeding interactions in a minimal marine chitin-degrading community
summary: Abstract Communities of heterotrophic particle-associated marine bacteria contribute to oceanic carbon cycling through interspecies interactions that can influence polysaccharide degradation. While these interactions have been extensively s
content: Abstract Communities of heterotrophic particle-associated marine bacteria contribute to oceanic carbon cycling through interspecies interactions that can influence polysaccharide degradation. While these interactions have been extensively studied using single natural isolates or pairwise combinations thereof, their mechanistic relevance within multispecies communities remains unclear. To address this gap, we developed MCC4, a minimal chitin-degrading bacterial community consisting of two chitin degraders and two non-degrading isolates that represent globally prevalent marine bacterial taxa. We show that the community remains stable across ten growth-dilution cycles, establishing a reproducible model for controlled multi-isolate experiments. Using transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses combined with metabolite supplementation assays, we uncovered the underlying crossfeeding network. While one degrader drives chitin degradation, the other exploits chitin monomers and chitooligomers generated by the main degrader. The two non-degraders are sustained by consuming deacetylated chitin monomers, 2-carbon compounds, nucleotides, and branched-chain amino acids, likely released by degraders. Community assembly is driven by competitive scavenging abilities, potentially complemented by specific survival strategies such as increased motility and deployment of type VI secretion systems. Despite its simplicity, MCC4 captures dynamic microbial interactions characteristic of natural marine ecosystems. It offers a tractable, reproducible framework for investigating how environmental perturbations impact community function and testing ecological theories in particle-associated marine environments. Funding We gratefully acknowledge funding from the Simons Foundation Principles of Microbial Ecosystems (PriME) collaboration (542395 to U.S.).

title: Thresholds and spatial effects of urbanization on ecosystem service supply-demand relationships: a multiscale study of the Wuhan Metropolitan Area
summary: Rapid urbanization continues to reshape the supply–demand relationships of ecosystem services (ESs), posing increasing risks to regional sustainable development. Previous work has looked at the scale dependence and spatial heterogeneity of
content: Rapid urbanization continues to reshape the supply–demand relationships of ecosystem services (ESs), posing increasing risks to regional sustainable development. Previous work has looked at the scale dependence and spatial heterogeneity of urbanization and how they independently impact supply–demand relationships of ESs but they have not been considered jointly. This study investigated the nonlinear effects of urbanization drivers on ES supply–demand relationships in the Wuhan Metropolitan Area (WMA). The supply–demand relationships of grain production (GP), carbon sequestration (CS), and water yield (WY) were analyzed from 2000 to 2020 at 3 km grid, 5 km grid, and town scales using random forest (RF), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR). The results showed that (1) GP and WY exhibited slight deficits with increasing supply–demand imbalances, whereas CS remained in surplus but with a continuous decline. (2)RF and SHAP showed significant nonlinear responses to built-up land proportion (BUILT), population density (POP), and GDP density (GDP). The importance and response patterns of drivers also exhibited scale dependence. (3) The MGWR indicated that urbanization drivers generally exerted negative effects on the ecosystem service supply–demand ratio (ESDR), while their direction and magnitude exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity. Overall, the nonlinear, scale-dependent, and spatially heterogeneous effects of urbanization highlight the importance of incorporating critical thresholds and spatial variation into multiscale ecological management and sustainable urbanization.

title: Next-generation cotton improvement through integrated biosynthetic pathways, multi-omics, artificial intelligence and advanced breeding technologies
summary: Cotton ( Gossypium spp.) is a globally important fibre and oilseed crop whose productivity and quality are increasingly constrained by climate change, biotic stresses and the complex genetic architecture of key agronomic traits. Recent adva
content: Cotton ( Gossypium spp.) is a globally important fibre and oilseed crop whose productivity and quality are increasingly constrained by climate change, biotic stresses and the complex genetic architecture of key agronomic traits. Recent advances in genomics, high-throughput phenotyping and systems biology have transformed our understanding of cotton evolution, fibre development, stress adaptation and defence mechanisms. This review synthesizes current progress in cotton improvement through integrative approaches encompassing pan-genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and phenomics, with particular emphasis on fibre quality regulation, secondary metabolite-mediated insect resistance and abiotic stress tolerance. We highlight how polyploidy, structural variation, homoeolog expression bias and regulatory network rewiring underpin phenotypic diversity and environmental adaptability in cotton. Furthermore, we discuss the emerging roles of artificial intelligence and machine-learning models in genomic prediction, trait mapping and decision support for precision breeding. The review also examines translational innovations, including CRISPR-based genome editing, nano-enabled delivery systems and nano-formulated inputs for sustainable pest and nutrient management. By integrating multi-omics data with AI-driven analytics, we propose a next-generation framework for accelerating cotton breeding pipelines under changing agro-ecological conditions. Despite rapid progress in Genomics, Bioinformatics, and Plant Breeding, existing reviews lack a systems-level perspective that links data generation, predictive modeling, and targeted intervention. This review addresses this gap by conceptualizing these advances as components of an integrated, data-driven breeding pipeline. This review uniquely integrates multi-omics and AI-driven approaches into a unified framework for cotton improvement, highlighting existing gaps and future opportunities. By integrating genome editing, nano-enabled delivery systems, and predictive analytics, these approaches enhance selection accuracy, reduce generation intervals, and enable high-throughput screening, collectively improving breeding efficiency, reduces breeding cycles and field-level resilience.

title: Plant pathobiome and the hierarchy of keystone drivers in disease complexes
summary: As plant disease complexes are recognized as polymicrobial systems in which multiple pathogens interact within the same host, the concept of the monomicrobial paradigm, which originated from Koch’s postulates, is therefore insufficient to e
content: As plant disease complexes are recognized as polymicrobial systems in which multiple pathogens interact within the same host, the concept of the monomicrobial paradigm, which originated from Koch’s postulates, is therefore insufficient to explain the dynamics of many plant disease complexes. This review proposes that primary pathogens function as keystone drivers for disease complexes, and that secondary pathogens depend mainly on host modifications for colonization. The transformation of resistant plant tissues into permissive conditions by primary initiators occurs through breaching of structural barriers such as the cuticle and cell wall, suppression of plant immunity responses like pattern-triggered and effector-triggered immunity, and the generation of nutritional niches through the formation of feeding sites or metabolic manipulation. These means allow opportunistic or facultative pathogens to establish and to increase disease severity. We propose a hierarchical concept to distinguish obligate secondary pathogens, facultative secondary pathogens, and co-primary pathogens. The review also examines factors such as antagonistic interactions, priority effects, the influence of host microbiomes, and environmental conditions that may alter or challenge pathogen hierarchies. To address these complexities and improve disease prediction, diagnosis, and management, we advocate for the integration of multi-omics strategies, network-level analyses, and synthetic microbial communities (SynComs). Additionally, we stress the importance of considering temporal dynamics and climate extremes that can shift pathogen composition and disrupt established hierarchies over time.

title: Breaking Linear Scaling Relations for Regioselective Phenol Hydroxylation via SiC-Supported Dual-Atom Catalysts
summary: The electrochemical hydroxylation of phenol offers a sustainable route to valueadded dihydroxybenzene isomers, yet rational catalyst design remains limited by 2 poor regioselectivity and structural instability. This study investigates silic
content: The electrochemical hydroxylation of phenol offers a sustainable route to valueadded dihydroxybenzene isomers, yet rational catalyst design remains limited by 2 poor regioselectivity and structural instability. This study investigates silicon carbide (SiC) monoliths as exceptionally robust supports for dual-atom catalysts, utilizing density functional theory and operando ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to screen 45 bimetallic combinations. Mechanistic analysis reveals that phenol undergoes site-specific activation directly at the Si-lattice, dictating regioselectivity toward catechol (ortho-pathway) or hydroquinone (para-pathway). Crystal Orbital Hamilton Population analyses and energetic span modeling demonstrate that macroscopic turnover is strictly governed by dynamic orbital overlap and precise d-band alignment. The TiFe configuration optimally minimizes the energetic span for ortho-hydroxylation, while TiMn provide the most competitive pathways for para-hydroxylation. Two-dimensional microkinetic mapping confirms that optimizing surface binding thermodynamics and bimetallic electronics successfully circumvents traditional linear scaling relations. Furthermore, operando AIMD simulations at 298 K validate these models, confirming that aromatic 𝜋-electron disruption constitutes the kinetic bottleneck (0.70 eV) and highlighting the critical role of interfacial potassium cations in electrostatically shielding polarized radical transition states.

title: Effects of Iron-modified nano-biochar on wheat growth and salinity tolerance associated with Iron metabolism and phenylpropanoid pathway
summary: Soil salinity induces ionic toxicity and nutrient deficiencies, particularly iron (Fe) deficiency, severely limiting wheat productivity. While nanobiochar can mitigate salt stress, its effectiveness is often limited. We hypothesized that en
content: Soil salinity induces ionic toxicity and nutrient deficiencies, particularly iron (Fe) deficiency, severely limiting wheat productivity. While nanobiochar can mitigate salt stress, its effectiveness is often limited. We hypothesized that engineering nanobiochar with iron (FeBC) would provide a synergistic solution by simultaneously alleviating sodium (Na⁺) toxicity and improving Fe nutrition, thereby enhancing salinity tolerance in wheat. A pot experiment was conducted with spring wheat under six treatments: Control, simple nanobiochar (SBC, 1%), FeBC (1%), NaCl stress (100 mM), SBC+NaCl, and FeBC+NaCl. We analysed growth, photosynthetic parameters, ion homeostasis, oxidative stress markers, osmolyte accumulation, and the expression of key genes involved in ion transport and Fe metabolism. Salinity stress significantly suppressed plant growth, photosynthesis, and potassium (K⁺) uptake, while accelerating Na⁺ accumulation and oxidative damage. Although SBC provided partial alleviation, FeBC was markedly more effective, improving shoot fresh weight by 62% and restoring photosynthetic performance under salinity stress. Mechanistically, FeBC orchestrated ionic homeostasis by upregulating the expression of TaSOS1, TaNHX, and TaHAK5 . It uniquely mitigated Fe deficiency, which was associated with reversal of salinity-induced downregulation of key Fe-transporter genes ( TaYSL1, TaNRAMP3, TaFER5 ), resulting in a 75% increase in root Fe concentration. Furthermore, FeBC reduced oxidative stress and suppressed TaRBOHB expression, while enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities such as catalase (CAT); ascorbate peroxidase (APX) and peroxidase (POD), while simultaneously activating the phenylpropanoid pathway to boost proline and phenolic compound synthesis. Our findings indicate that Fe-modified nanobiochar is more effective in enhancing salinity tolerance in wheat than conventional biochar.

title: Metabolism-Informed Bioreactor Model for Transferring Knowledge from Fed-batch to Continuous Biomanufacturing
summary: Abstract Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells remain the dominant platform for monoclonal antibody (mAb) manufacturing, and rising demand is pushing the industry from fed-batch toward continuous operation. Continuous cultures promise sustained
content: Abstract Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells remain the dominant platform for monoclonal antibody (mAb) manufacturing, and rising demand is pushing the industry from fed-batch toward continuous operation. Continuous cultures promise sustained high cell densities and volumetric productivities, but their operation depends on reliable real-time monitoring, prediction and control. Limited intracellular observability and sparse extracellular measurements hinder this, leaving a persistent gap between mechanistic understanding and predictive deployment. Here we describe a metabolism-informed model for mAb production that embeds reactor- and intracellular-level mass balances directly within a learning architecture, while deliberately avoiding predefined kinetic rate laws and explicit steady-state assumptions. Because conservation relationships remain invariant across operating modes, this formulation provides a principled structural prior for cross-regime generalisation, positioning the model as a soft sensor for continuous bioprocesses: inferring unmeasured intracellular fluxes and one-step ahead forecasting extracellular concentrations to support process monitoring and control. Benchmarking two metabolic network sizes and three metabolic optimisation strategies, concentration predictions are indistinguishable across network sizes. Exchange flux fidelity is agnostic to solver choice, with network size mattering only for intracellular interpretability. Transferring the developed model from fed-batch to continuous operation with fine-tuning outperforming other transfer learning variants. This is consistent with the metabolic structure being invariant to mode of operation. Predicted fluxes reveal growth rate in fed-batch, rather than operating mode, as the dominant axis of metabolic variation, and identify potential regime-shift signals to guide experimental design for continuous culture characterisation. These results chart a route towards digital models sufficiently grounded in first-principles knowledge, yet adaptive for deployment under regime shifts.

title: Community structure and hidden phylogenetic diversity of marine fungi in the tropical Indian and western Pacific Oceans
summary: Abstract Background Marine fungi remain a poorly understood component of ocean ecosystems despite their potential roles in marine biogeochemical cycling. Here, we investigated fungal diversity, community structure, vertical stratification,
content: Abstract Background Marine fungi remain a poorly understood component of ocean ecosystems despite their potential roles in marine biogeochemical cycling. Here, we investigated fungal diversity, community structure, vertical stratification, and environmental drivers across the tropical Indian and western Pacific Oceans using long-read 28S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing of 113 samples from surface waters, mesopelagic and bathypelagic zones, and sediments. Results A total of 46,938 fungal OTUs were clustered, representing 35 phyla, 164 classes, 254 orders, 509 families, 940 genera, and 1,055 species. Ascomycota dominated fungal communities, followed by Basidiomycota, Chytridiomycota, Rozellomycota. Phylogenetic analyses revealed three deeply divergent fungal lineages distinct from currently recognized phyla. Pending further molecular and morphological validation, these lineages were provisionally designated as Candidate.Taichumycota, Candidate.Shizhenmycota, and Candidate.Xihemycota. Their distinct vertical stratification suggested potential ecological differentiation: Candidate.Taichumycota was restricted to surface waters, Candidate.Shizhenmycota was broadly distributed but enriched in surface communities, whereas Candidate.Xihemycota occurred across habitats and was particularly enriched in sediments. Both fungal taxonomic and functional compositions exhibited significant vertical differentiation across habitats ( p < 0.05), with undefined saprotrophic guilds enriched in sediments and pelagic communities displaying diverse trophic strategies. Surface fungal community composition was jointly shaped by geographic and environmental gradients, with longitude, phosphate, and salinity identified as major predictors. Together, these variables explained 18.6% of the variation in surface fungal community composition. Conclusions This study reveals extensive hidden diversity and complex ecological structuring of marine fungi in the tropical Indian and western Pacific Oceans. The discovery of deeply divergent fungal lineages and habitat-associated shifts in taxonomic and predicted functional composition highlights the underestimated evolutionary diversity and ecological differentiation of marine fungal communities.

title: Engineering acid-tolerant non-conventional yeast Pichia kudriavzevii E1 for butyric acid production
source: Mycology&#58 An International Journal on Fungal Biology
summary: Butyric acid is an important organic acid with diverse applications; however, microbial production is hampered by the scarcity of acid-tolerant hosts. Here, we established a cytosolic reverse β-oxidation pathway in the acid-tolerant non-con
content: Butyric acid is an important organic acid with diverse applications; however, microbial production is hampered by the scarcity of acid-tolerant hosts. Here, we established a cytosolic reverse β-oxidation pathway in the acid-tolerant non-conventional yeast Pichia kudriavzevii E1 for butyric acid production. Strategies to enhance cytosolic acetyl-CoA availability were evaluated, including glyoxylate cycle disruption, acetyl-CoA synthetase overexpression, mobilization of peroxisomal acetyl units, and cytosolic expression of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. Cytosolic expression of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex increased butyric acid production 1.7-fold, highlighting the importance of acetyl-CoA compartmentalization. Evaluation of pathway enzymes identified trans-enoyl-CoA reductase (Ter) as a potential rate-limiting enzyme. A previously uncharacterized Ter enzyme, designated LpTer, was identified from a strong-aroma Baijiu pit-mud metagenome. Optimizing LpTer copy number and cytosolic NADH utilization increased the butyric acid titer to 339.07 ± 8.30 mg/L, representing an approximately 68-fold improvement over the initial strain. This study represents the first systematic engineering of the acid-tolerant yeast P. kudriavzevii for de novo butyric acid production without pH adjustment through pathway optimization and enzyme mining.

title: Postponed Nitrogen Enhanced Waterlogged Summer Maize Soil Nutrients by Regulating Microbial Diversity and Network Complexity
summary: Waterlogging stress and low nitrogen use efficiency are important factors constraining summer maize production in the Huang-Huai-Hai region. However, how postponed nitrogen application modulates soil micro-ecological properties and mitigate
content: Waterlogging stress and low nitrogen use efficiency are important factors constraining summer maize production in the Huang-Huai-Hai region. However, how postponed nitrogen application modulates soil micro-ecological properties and mitigates yield loss in waterlogged summer maize fields by regulating soil microbial community diversity, co-occurrence networks, and community assembly processes remained rarely explored. In this study, summer maize at the three-leaf-one-heart stage was subjected to waterlogging for 3 (WL3), 6 (WL6), and 9 (WL9) days, and the treatment without artificial flooding was set as the control (CK). combined with three postponed nitrogen application ratios: N1 (70% basal fertilizer + 30% topdressing after stress relief), N2 (50% basal fertilizer + 30% topdressing after stress relief + 20% topdressing at the V12 stage), and N3 (30% basal fertilizer + 30% topdressing after stress relief + 40% topdressing at the V12 stage). Soil nutrients, microbial community diversity, network stability, and assembly processes were systematically analyzed. Results showed that N3 treatment increased the contents of soil total nitrogen, inorganic nitrogen, available phosphorus, alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen and available potassium after waterlogging stress; prolonging the waterlogging duration increased the alpha diversity of soil bacteria at the flowering stage of summer maize. Under WL9 treatment, compared with N1 treatment, N2 treatment significantly increased the alpha diversity of farmland soil at the maturity stage. Linear discriminant analysis Effect Size (LEfSe) analysis revealed that under WL9 treatment, N3 treatment enriched putative nitrogen-cycling functional bacterial taxa such as Nitrolancea and Defluviicoccus, as well as saprophytic fungi including Blastocladiales, Acrophialophora, and Epicoccum. Nitrate nitrogen and ammonium nitrogen were identified as key environmental factors driving bacterial and fungal community diversity and structure at the maturity stage. Under the WL9 treatment, compared with N1, the N2 and N3 treatments increased network complexity by 30.61% and 46.94%, respectively. The migration rate and migration-drift parameter of bacterial and fungal communities increased with the increase of postponed nitrogen application ratio under CK and WL3 treatments. Under waterlogging conditions, compared with N1 treatment, N3 treatment increased summer maize yield by 27.29%–33.75%. Overall, the postponed nitrogen application improved micro-ecology of summer maize under waterlogging conditions by enhancing soil nutrient status, enriching microorganisms, and increasing network stability. This provides a theoretical basis for waterlogging prevention and optimized nitrogen management in summer maize production in the Huang-Huai-Hai region.

title: Generating blue carbon credits through conservation of Posidonia oceanica: experience from the LIFE SeaForest project
summary: Introduction Posidonia oceanica meadows are key blue carbon ecosystems in the Mediterranean Sea, storing substantial carbon within biomass and underlying sediments. Unregulated recreational anchoring contributes to meadow degradation and ma
content: Introduction Posidonia oceanica meadows are key blue carbon ecosystems in the Mediterranean Sea, storing substantial carbon within biomass and underlying sediments. Unregulated recreational anchoring contributes to meadow degradation and may compromise the retention of previously stored carbon. The LIFE SeaForest project (LIFE17 CCM/IT/000121) aimed to reduce carbon losses associated with P. oceanica degradation through integrated management, monitoring, conservation, and restoration actions across three Mediterranean protected coastal areas. Methods A comprehensive ex-ante accounting framework was developed to estimate anchoring-related potential carbon-stock losses, expressed in CO 2 -equivalent units, under baseline (business-as-usual) and project scenarios. The methodology considered vessel-size classes and substrate categories associated with P. oceanica (rocky, sandy, and degraded dead matte substrates). Project actions included environmentally friendly mooring systems, sustainable anchoring management plans, and regulation of recreational boating through a dedicated digital user platform. Results Over the ten-year accounting period, cumulative Net Emission Reductions (NERs) exceeded 5,000 tCO 2 eq across the three project areas. This value represents net avoided potential carbon-stock loss, rather than directly quantified atmospheric CO 2 emissions, and identifies a potential SeaForest credit volume subject to monitoring, verification, and certification. Discussion The proposed framework represents one of the first structured ex-ante approaches for estimating potential blue carbon credits from conservation measures that reduce anchoring impacts in Mediterranean P. oceanica meadows. Although further validation and long-term monitoring are needed, the SeaForest approach provides a potentially replicable framework for blue carbon initiatives, sustainable coastal management, and climate-mitigation policies in the Mediterranean region.

title: Self-Organizing Maps in the Identification of Key Phenotypes of Ornamental Pepper Plants Under Contrasting Growing Conditions
summary: Abstract High temperatures can significantly affect plant growth, development, and physiology. The identification of genotypes with desirable morphological and physiological responses under contrasting growing conditions is therefore releva
content: Abstract High temperatures can significantly affect plant growth, development, and physiology. The identification of genotypes with desirable morphological and physiological responses under contrasting growing conditions is therefore relevant for ornamental pepper breeding. This study aimed to characterize the phenotypic responses of ten ornamental pepper ( Capsicum spp.) accessions grown under controlled (27.15 ± 1.16 °C; VPD = 2.1 ± 0.23 kPa) and high-temperature/high-VPD (39.03 ± 1.98 °C; VPD = 6.23 ± 0.85 kPa) greenhouse conditions using morphological, phenological, and physiological traits and self-organizing maps (SOMs). Differences in plant architecture and physiological responses were observed among accessions within each growth condition, while descriptive differences were also observed between conditions. In general, plant height and canopy diameter were lower under the high-temperature/high-VPD condition, while the magnitude of gas-exchange responses varied among accessions. SOM sensitivity analysis supported a 2 × 3 topology with six neurons for both conditions, based on the balance among training quality, topological preservation, and stability across 100 independent runs. Three superclasses were identified under each condition, although their composition and multivariate profiles differed between environments. CPCE 005 and CPCE 007 remained associated under both conditions and, under high-temperature/high-VPD, were characterized by compact plant architecture combined with higher relative values of gas-exchange traits. CPCE 014 showed a distinct multivariate profile under the contrasting conditions and formed an individual superclass. Overall, SOM analysis revealed a reorganization of the relationships among morphological and physiological traits between growing conditions and identified distinct accession-specific response patterns. These results highlight CPCE 005, CPCE 007, and CPCE 014 as promising accessions for further validation in breeding studies targeting ornamental peppers grown under high-temperature and high atmospheric evaporative demand.

title: Yeast-Based Platforms for Next-Generation Human Health Applications
summary: Yeast platforms are rapidly transitioning from traditional eukaryotic model organisms to versatile, programmable chassis for next-generation human health applications. This review systematically examines the translational evolution of conve
content: Yeast platforms are rapidly transitioning from traditional eukaryotic model organisms to versatile, programmable chassis for next-generation human health applications. This review systematically examines the translational evolution of conventional and non-conventional yeasts including Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Komagataella phaffii, Saccharomyces boulardii, and Yarrowia lipolytica and redefines them as scalable biomanufacturing factories and advanced living therapeutics. We highlight milestone advancements in synthetic biology toolkits that lower technical barriers, such as CRISPR-mediated multiplex editing, modular cloning frameworks, and high-throughput secretion screening. We focus on sophisticated glycoengineering strategies for humanized N-glycosylation, alongside data-driven paradigms that leverage artificial intelligence to predict gene expression and streamline strain design. In clinical domains, we detail the established success of yeast in producing subunit or virus-like particle vaccines (e.g. HBV and HPV) and therapeutic enzymes (e.g. ecallantide), alongside its emerging role as gut-adapted live biotherapeutic products (LBPs) engineered for in situ delivery and biosensing. Finally, we explore specialized non-conventional platforms, focusing on lipid- and acetyl-CoA-rich hosts for lipophilic drug discovery, and stress-tolerant systems optimized for economical, feedstock-flexible bioprocesses. In summary, this review underscores the integrated value of yeast systems across disease modeling, industrial manufacturing, and clinical intervention, charting future directions to address global health challenges.

title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
summary: Ammonium thiocyanate (NH4SCN) has been used extensively to improve the current extraction and device performance of quasi-two-dimensional perovskite solar cells. Whilst this additive has been shown to influence quasi-2D perovskite crystalli
content: Ammonium thiocyanate (NH4SCN) has been used extensively to improve the current extraction and device performance of quasi-two-dimensional perovskite solar cells. Whilst this additive has been shown to influence quasi-2D perovskite crystallisation, a detailed understanding of its mechanism has not yet been established. Through spectroscopic and structural studies, we demonstrate that NH4SCN enables quasi-2D perovskite phases to structurally template the dominant 3D phase. Contrary to previous reports, we suggest that the benefit of this additive comes from an improvement to the 3D perovskite structure, not from charges transferring through vertically oriented 2D perovskite layers. We show that this additive provides kinetic control over the quasi-2D phase formation, suppressing the unfavourable n = 1 perovskite phase and promoting the growth of high-n 2D scaffold phases by extending the nucleation window. This promotes the in-situ templated growth of MAPbI3. We provide robust structural analysis demonstrating highly (110)-ordered 3D perovskite, with the mechanism confirmed by close lattice matching between this phase and quasi-2D phases. Furthermore, we show that this structural control is cation dependent, requiring both close lattice matching between quasi-2D and 3D perovskite phases, and successful kinetic control of the relevant quasi-2D phases.

title: Distribution and rare earth element abundances of apatite in Bennu samples determined by synchrotron X‐ray fluorescence spectroscopy
summary: Abstract Apatite is often the most rare earth element (REE)‐enriched mineral in chondritic meteorites. REE enrichment and fractionation levels in apatite grains can give insight into the aqueous fluids in which they formed and the condition
content: Abstract Apatite is often the most rare earth element (REE)‐enriched mineral in chondritic meteorites. REE enrichment and fractionation levels in apatite grains can give insight into the aqueous fluids in which they formed and the conditions prevailing within the host body. In this study, we applied synchrotron X‐ray fluorescence (SXRF) spectroscopy to investigate the distribution and REE enrichments of 34 apatite grains in five rock fragments from asteroid (101955) Bennu, collected and brought to Earth by NASA's OSIRIS‐REx mission. We observe a strongly heterogeneous apatite distribution with frequent occurrence of clusters containing three to nine apatite grains. SXRF results reveal a wide grain‐to‐grain range of REE enrichment levels, at 15–900 times those of bulk CI chondrites. Of the 34 measured apatite grains, four are Mn‐enriched (Mn > 1.26 wt%) and these show the lowest REE concentrations (15–65 times CI). Little light/heavy REE fractionation is observed in the Bennu apatite grains, in contrast to the heavy REE enrichment observed in apatite grains in samples from asteroid Ryugu. Our results suggest fluid circulation in Bennu's parent asteroid involved apatite precipitation in cavities and local variations in water‐rock interaction leading to local changes in , and fluid chemistry. Given the dynamically evolving fluid conditions and the enhanced peripheral luminescence and oscillatory zoning observed in some apatite grains, an absence of REE fractionation during apatite formation appears unlikely. We postulate that, as fluid chemistry evolved to higher alkalinity and salinity, sequential complexation resulted in early incorporation of light REEs into precipitating apatite grains, subsequently balanced by later adsorption of heavy REEs.

title: Surface Conditioning for Zero-Shot Multivariate Correction in a Marine Biogeochemistry Emulator
summary: Bias correction in process-based models usually means iterative data assimilation with explicit covariance modelling. We propose a lightweight alternative based on a neural emulator of marine biogeochemistry (BGC), showing that the conditio
content: Bias correction in process-based models usually means iterative data assimilation with explicit covariance modelling. We propose a lightweight alternative based on a neural emulator of marine biogeochemistry (BGC), showing that the conditioning pathway of its autoencoder can serve as an observation injection point. The decoder is conditioned on surface variables via Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), originally designed to incorporate physical boundary forcings. We extend these inputs to include surface chlorophyll-a and replace the simulated field with satellite observations at inference time. The surface substitution propagates through the water column, improving agreement with depth-resolved observations at all depths, and spreads to other output variables in a pattern consistent with expected trophic relationships.

title: Textile‐Integrated Electrochemical Sensing Approaches for Monitoring Wound‐Relevant Biochemical Markers
summary: ABSTRACT Wearable electrochemical sensors offer promising opportunities for wound‐related biochemical assessment by enabling the detection of wound‐relevant biomarkers directly at the skin–wound interface. In this study, we present a textil
content: ABSTRACT Wearable electrochemical sensors offer promising opportunities for wound‐related biochemical assessment by enabling the detection of wound‐relevant biomarkers directly at the skin–wound interface. In this study, we present a textile‐integrated sensor platform for dual‐analyte response of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) and enzymatically quantified lactate, which are key indicators of oxidative stress and metabolic activity, respectively. The redox sensor was fabricated using platinum‐coated Shieldex working electrodes and Ag/AgCl reference electrodes, arranged in a coaxial winding yarn. Besides having the same type of reference electrode in the setup, the lactate sensor employed a gold‐based working electrode functionalized with a chitosan–PPD–lactate oxidase (LOx) multilayer along with a platinum‐based counter electrode. Electrochemical characterisation showed that the redox sensor exhibited consistent current–time response behaviour, approaching a quasi‐stabilised response level within approximately 180 s, and demonstrating a measurable response trend across a broad experimentally explored H 2 O 2 concentration range (from the micromolar to high millimolar range). The lactate sensor produced repeatable qualitative current increases of approximately 25% and 50% at 2 mM and 4 mM lactate, respectively, with response magnitude affected by pH and temperature. Biocompatibility testing confirmed no cytotoxic effects for gold‐ and platinum‐based electrodes, and only moderate effects for Ag/AgCl under prolonged incubation, supporting the suitability of the primary sensing elements for wound‐contact applications. Taken together, the results demonstrate proof‐of‐concept functionality under controlled laboratory conditions, while comprehensive analytical validation remains the subject of future work, which supports the potential of textile‐based electrochemical sensors for integration into next‐generation smart wound dressings.
