title: TECHNOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT OF CEMENT MATRIX DETERIORATION IN CONCRETE FLOORINGS OF CATTLE BUILDINGS UNDER MANURE EXPOSURE: A REVIEW
source: Journal of Chemical Technology and Metallurgy
summary: Concrete floorings in cattle buildings are operated in an environment where the load - bearing capacity of the material is related not only to compressive strength but also to the resistance of the cement matrix to manure, urine, moisture,
content: Concrete floorings in cattle buildings are operated in an environment where the load - bearing capacity of the material is related not only to compressive strength but also to the resistance of the cement matrix to manure, urine, moisture, organic acids, sulfate compounds, microbiological activity and mechanical abrasion. In this review, a technological assessment of the main mechanisms of concrete deterioration under contact with an aggressive livestock environment is provided and the requirements for suitable concrete and cement systems are summarized. Publications, standards and applied studies related to concrete floors, cement matrix, organic acids, sulfate attack, calcium leaching, microbiologically induced corrosion and innovative binder systems were analysed. The datashow that concrete durability in a livestock environment should be assessed through a set of indicators: compressive strength, water absorption, density, porosity, permeability, sulfate resistance, acid resistance, wear resistance and reinforcement protection. From a technological point of view, concretes with a low water - cement ratio, a dense structure, adequate compaction and curing, as well as sulfate - resistant, slag, pozzolanic or alkali - activated binder systems, are considered the most justified. The main limitation in the literature remains the lack of long - term field studies in real cattle buildings where chemical, biological and mechanical factors act simultaneously.

title: EXTRAFISCALIDADE DO IPVA E ELETROMOBILIDADE: ENTRE O INCENTIVO TRIBUTÁRIO E OS LIMITES DA (IN)VIABILIDADE PRÁTICA NO CONTEXTO BRASILEIRO
summary: A transição para uma economia de baixo carbono demanda a adoção de instrumentos jurídicos capazes de incentivar comportamentos ambientalmente sustentáveis, destacando-se, nesse contexto, a utilização da tributação com finalidade extrafiscal
content: A transição para uma economia de baixo carbono demanda a adoção de instrumentos jurídicos capazes de incentivar comportamentos ambientalmente sustentáveis, destacando-se, nesse contexto, a utilização da tributação com finalidade extrafiscal. O presente estudo analisa o Imposto sobre a Propriedade de Veículos Automotores (IPVA) como mecanismo de incentivo à eletromobilidade no Brasil, examinando sua compatibilidade com os objetivos constitucionais de proteção ambiental e mitigação das mudanças climáticas. A pesquisa possui abordagem qualitativa, natureza exploratória e descritivo-analítica, desenvolvida mediante pesquisa bibliográfica, documental e análise comparativa da legislação dos Estados e do Distrito Federal acerca dos regimes de isenção e redução de alíquotas aplicáveis aos veículos elétricos. Além da análise normativa, investigam-se os principais fatores que condicionam a efetividade desses incentivos, como os custos de aquisição dos veículos, a evolução tecnológica das baterias, os desafios relacionados à mineração e à reciclagem de minerais críticos, a infraestrutura de recarga e a influência da matriz energética sobre os benefícios ambientais da eletromobilidade. Os resultados demonstram que a extrafiscalidade do IPVA constitui importante instrumento de indução de políticas públicas voltadas à mobilidade sustentável, especialmente após a Emenda Constitucional nº 132/2023, que fortaleceu a dimensão ambiental do Sistema Tributário Nacional. Contudo, verifica-se que a concessão de benefícios fiscais, embora juridicamente legítima e ambientalmente relevante, não é suficiente para assegurar, de forma isolada, a expansão da eletromobilidade, exigindo integração com políticas energéticas, industriais, tecnológicas e de infraestrutura capazes de viabilizar uma transição sustentável e socialmente eficiente.

title: How climate-related events become climate governance problems: climate change attribution divergence as an interpretive mechanism
summary: Climate-related events are often viewed as potential catalysts for policy learning and changes in climate governance. Floods, droughts, heatwaves, wildfires, and other environmental changes can expose vulnerabilities in infrastructure, land
content: Climate-related events are often viewed as potential catalysts for policy learning and changes in climate governance. Floods, droughts, heatwaves, wildfires, and other environmental changes can expose vulnerabilities in infrastructure, land-use planning, and emergency preparedness, drawing attention to the need to reassess existing practices. However, events can be associated with different responses, proving that exposure and scientific information alone do not determine collective action. Governance responses depend not only on institutional, political, and socioeconomic conditions, but also on how actors interpret experienced environmental changes in relation to anthropogenic climate change. These subjective interpretations are distinct from scientific event attribution and vary in strength across actors. Differences in attribution may contribute to divergent problem definitions, shaping which issues are prioritised and the type, scale, and temporal orientation of adaptation, mitigation, and other governance responses. Building on empirical research documenting variation in climate change attribution strength across actors and contexts, this paper introduces climate change attribution divergence, defined as differences among actors in the strength with which experienced environmental events and impacts are attributed to anthropogenic climate change. While existing research has examined attribution primarily at the individual level, less attention has been given to how differences in attribution may matter within shared governance contexts. The paper develops a conceptual framework specifying how subjective attribution, variation in attribution strength, and problem definition are linked, and how attribution divergence may contribute to divergent governance responses. The framework offers an interpretive mechanism for understanding why environmental events may give rise to different governance pathways.

title: Replication Code for National Conditions Associated with Low Tourism Greenhouse Gas Intensity: Evidence From NCA, fsQCA, and Regression Across 50 Countries
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This repository provides the R analysis code and replication documentation for the manuscript entitled "National Conditions Associated with Low Tourism Greenhouse Gas Intensity: Evidence From NCA, fsQCA, and Regression Across 50 Countries."
content: This repository provides the R analysis code and replication documentation for the manuscript entitled "National Conditions Associated with Low Tourism Greenhouse Gas Intensity: Evidence From NCA, fsQCA, and Regression Across 50 Countries." The code implements necessary condition analysis (NCA), fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), HC3 robust regression, and associated robustness and sensitivity analyses. The README provides instructions for reproducing the analyses.

title: Adoption, Farmers’ Perceptions, and Constraints to Sustainable Improved Forage Technology Integration in Smallholder Agroforestry Systems in Dire Enchini District
summary: Improved forage production is important for increasing livestock productivity and supporting sustainable mixed crop–livestock systems. This study assessed the sustainability of innovative forage technologies within agroforestry practices Di
content: Improved forage production is important for increasing livestock productivity and supporting sustainable mixed crop–livestock systems. This study assessed the sustainability of innovative forage technologies within agroforestry practices Dire Enchini District by assessing local community perceptions, identifying determinants of adoption, and examining community-driven forage resource conservation. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 142 randomly selected households from four kebeles: Nanno Jedue, Bilo Abayi, Arfinjo Daga, and Waldo Hene. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the survey data. Nine major improved forage species were identified, with Desho grass (19.0%), Rhodes grass (16.7%), and Napier grass (14.3%) being the most frequently reported. Tree Lucerne (Tagasaste) and Oat–Vetch mixtures each accounted for 7.1%. The major constraints to improved forage adoption were limited access to improved planting materials (31.0%), inadequate institutional support, limited technical knowledge, poor soil fertility (14.3%), and land shortage (7.1%). Male farmers accounted for 85.7% of reported adopters, compared with 14.3% for female farmers. Most respondents (65%) reported a moderate level of experience with improved forage technologies, while only 10% reported a high level of experience. The findings indicate that improved forage production in the study area is constrained primarily by limited access to planting materials, technical knowledge, and institutional support. Strengthening farmer training, extension services, and local forage seed and planting-material multiplication through farmer training centers could support wider adoption and sustainable production of improved forage species suited to local agroecological conditions.

title: Emerging Sustainability Roles in the Accounting Profession: An Empirical Analysis of Identities, Responsibilities and Competencies
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Sustainability reporting and assurance requirements are reshaping accountants' professional profiles. Yet empirical evidence on how these accountability demands translate into specific role configurations remains limited. To addres
content: ABSTRACT Sustainability reporting and assurance requirements are reshaping accountants' professional profiles. Yet empirical evidence on how these accountability demands translate into specific role configurations remains limited. To address this gap, this study draws on role theory to examine how accountants' responsibilities and required competencies have evolved in response to sustainability reporting and assurance requirements, driven by the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), while building on traditional accounting expertise. Using a hybrid (inductive‐deductive) content analysis approach complemented by clustering techniques, we analysed 139 sustainability‐related accounting job advertisements collected in 2024 across 18 European Union countries. The findings reveal the emergence of complex roles and a broad set of competencies, suggesting that organizations are incorporating sustainability work mainly by retaining familiar professional identities while changing the responsibilities and competencies attached to them. The study advances our understanding of the evolving profiles and expertise of accountants in the context of sustainability reporting and assurance and provides insights for researchers, practitioners and professional accountancy organisations.

title: Household Resilience Dynamics Under Climate and Security‐Related Conflict Shocks: Evidence From Burkina Faso
summary: ABSTRACT This article examines household resilience to climate and security‐related conflict shocks in Burkina Faso and discusses its implications for environmental sustainability. Using the Harmonized Survey on Household Living Conditions
content: ABSTRACT This article examines household resilience to climate and security‐related conflict shocks in Burkina Faso and discusses its implications for environmental sustainability. Using the Harmonized Survey on Household Living Conditions (EHCVM 2018–2021) data (14,143 households), it builds a Resilience Capacity Index (RCI) through structural equation modeling (SEM), integrating absorptive, adaptive, and transformative capacities and estimates the association between shocks and resilience using a household fixed‐effects (least squares dummy variable [LSDV]) regression model. The mean RCI shows a modest improvement between 2018 and 2021, but persistent urban–rural gaps remain. Climate shocks and armed conflict are both associated with significantly lower resilience, with a stronger association for conflict. A positive interaction term indicates that the combined association of climate and conflict shocks is less negative than the sum of their separate associations. Resilience emerges as key to sustainable development, requiring integrated policies on adaptation, social protection, and livelihood diversification. These findings are consistent with the resilience‐sustainability nexus literature, suggesting that strengthening household resilience can help curb the distress‐driven depletion of natural resources and support more stable, sustainable development trajectories in fragile Sahelian settings.

title: Organic fertilization enhances carbon–water coordination and water use efficiency of greenhouse tomato under deficit irrigation
summary: Water scarcity poses a major challenge to sustainable agricultural production. Organic fertilization may mitigate the negative effects of water deficit by improving soil conditions and sustaining plant physiological activity; however, its p
content: Water scarcity poses a major challenge to sustainable agricultural production. Organic fertilization may mitigate the negative effects of water deficit by improving soil conditions and sustaining plant physiological activity; however, its physiological benefits under deficit irrigation in greenhouse tomato remain insufficiently quantified. This study evaluated the effects of fertilizer type and irrigation level on tomato growth, transpiration, gas exchange, yield, and yield-based water use efficiency across spring–summer and autumn–winter growing cycles. A factorial experiment included three fertilization treatments, namely no fertilizer (CK), chemical fertilizer (CF), and organic fertilizer (OF), under full irrigation (FI) and deficit irrigation (DI, 70% of FI). The results showed that deficit irrigation reduced daily transpiration, gas exchange, and yield; however, OF alleviated these reductions. Under DI, OF maintained greater plant height, stem diameter, and leaf area index than CF, approaching the level observed under fully irrigated CF. Although DI reduced daily and cumulative water use, OF sustained relatively high transpiration, net photosynthetic rate, and stomatal conductance, while stabilizing intercellular CO₂ concentration and delaying the decline in stomatal conductance under increasing leaf temperature. Consequently, DI combined with OF reduced yield losses to 3.9% and 8.8% relative to fully irrigated CF in the two seasons, while increasing yield-based water use efficiency by 16.4–22.1%. These findings indicate that organic fertilization enhances physiological resilience and promotes carbon–water coordination under moderate water deficit, thereby sustaining greenhouse tomato productivity and improving yield-based water use efficiency. Integrating organic fertilization with deficit irrigation may represent a promising strategy for improving water use efficiency in semi-arid greenhouse systems.

title: Humic acid urea mitigates N2O emissions from winter wheat in a rice–wheat rotation by regulating nitrifying and denitrifying microorganisms and key genes
summary: Maintaining winter wheat productivity while reducing nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions is critical for sustainable rice–wheat rotation systems in the Yangtze River Plain, China. Humic acid urea (HAU) may enhance wheat yield and mitigate N 2 O
content: Maintaining winter wheat productivity while reducing nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions is critical for sustainable rice–wheat rotation systems in the Yangtze River Plain, China. Humic acid urea (HAU) may enhance wheat yield and mitigate N 2 O emissions, but its field performance and underlying biological mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. A two-year field experiment was conducted during the winter wheat phase of a rice–wheat rotation system, with three treatments: a zero-nitrogen control (CK), conventional urea (U, 210 kg N ha −1 ), and HAU (210 kg N·ha −1 ). Winter wheat yield, aboveground nitrogen (N) uptake, N use efficiency (NUE), and N 2 O emissions were evaluated across two growing seasons; soil carbon and N pools, bacterial communities, and N-cycling genes were examined at the jointing stage during the 2023–2024 growing season. Compared with U, HAU increased winter wheat yield by 7.3–8.7%, aboveground N uptake by 4.4–4.9%, and NUE by 3.2–3.6 percentage points. Higher yield was associated with a greater number of effective spikes. HAU also reduced cumulative N 2 O emissions by 23.3–24.1% and greenhouse gas intensity by 28.0–29.1%. At jointing, HAU increased soil NH 4 + -N and microbial biomass N but decreased NO 3 – -N, labile organic carbon, and microbial biomass carbon. These changes coincided with lower abundances of ammonia-oxidizing bacteria and the amoA , nirK , and nirS genes, and a higher abundance of the N 2 O-reducing gene nosZ . Overall, HAU improved winter wheat productivity and NUE while mitigating N 2 O emissions, supporting its potential for lower-emission N management in rice–wheat rotations.

title: Vehicular Air Pollution and Its Control Measures
source: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
summary: Vehicular air pollution is a major environmental concern in urban areas. The growing number of cars, buses, trucks, motorcycles, and other vehicles has increased emissions of harmful substances into the atmosphere. Major vehicle-related emi
content: Vehicular air pollution is a major environmental concern in urban areas. The growing number of cars, buses, trucks, motorcycles, and other vehicles has increased emissions of harmful substances into the atmosphere. Major vehicle-related emissions include carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen oxides (NO), particulate matter (PM), hydrocarbons (HC), sulfur oxides (SO), and carbon dioxide (CO2). These emissions can affect human health, air quality, and the environment. This paper discusses the main sources and types of vehicular air pollution, its effects, and methods for controlling vehicle emissions.

title: Surface Subsidence as an Effective Indicator of Methane Emissions From Underground Coal Mines
summary: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from underground coal mining remain a major and uncertain anthropogenic source. This study tests whether surface subsidence, a direct consequence of underground mining, can serve as an indicator of CH 4 em
content: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from underground coal mining remain a major and uncertain anthropogenic source. This study tests whether surface subsidence, a direct consequence of underground mining, can serve as an indicator of CH 4 emissions. We use the Changzhi coal belt in Shanxi of China, a major emission hotspot, as a case study. Time‐series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar analysis of Sentinel‐1 SAR data (November 2019 to October 2024) revealed persistent subsidence across the region. Over a similar period, hyperspectral images from four satellite platforms (March 2019 to October 2024) detected 568 CH 4 plumes from 33 point sources. The two data sets showed strong spatial overlap. Annual subsidence volume was significantly negatively correlated with time‐averaged point‐source emissions ( r = −0.65 to −0.53, p < 0.01), indicating that subsidence, as a proxy for extracted coal volume, is a reliable indicator of cumulative emissions. Applying this hyperspectral‐calibrated relationship to areas with subsidence but no detected plumes yields total point‐source emissions of 0.288–0.508 Mt·a −1 , representing 13%–43% of regional inventory estimates. Hyperspectral satellites alone miss approximately 18%–32% of this total. Combining InSAR‐derived subsidence with hyperspectral plume observations thus provides a nearly all‐weather pathway for monitoring CH 4 emissions from underground coal mining.

title: ANÁLISE JURÍDICA DA LEI ESTADUAL Nº 11.578/2021 DO MARANHÃO EM FACE DA REGULAÇÃO DO MERCADO DE CARBONO BRASILEIRO
summary: A Lei nº 15.042, de 11 de dezembro de 2024, instituiu o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa (SBCE) e disciplinou, pela primeira vez em lei federal, a titularidade originária de créditos de carbono por catego
content: A Lei nº 15.042, de 11 de dezembro de 2024, instituiu o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa (SBCE) e disciplinou, pela primeira vez em lei federal, a titularidade originária de créditos de carbono por categoria territorial, os programas jurisdicionais de REDD+ e as condições de comercialização em territórios tradicionais. O Maranhão, contudo, já dispunha de marco próprio — a Lei Estadual nº 11.578/2021, regulamentada pelo Decreto nº 37.969/2022 —, o que exige verificar, dispositivo por dispositivo, a relação entre as duas ordens normativas. Este artigo analisa a compatibilidade jurídico-normativa entre esses diplomas quanto à titularidade e à repartição de benefícios decorrentes de créditos de carbono nas Áreas de Proteção Ambiental (APAs) estaduais da Baixada Maranhense, das Reentrâncias Maranhenses e de Upaon-Açu/Miritiba/Alto Preguiças. Adota-se pesquisa qualitativa, exploratória, documental e jurídico-comparativa, com apoio de análise espacial de dados secundários (MapBiomas, CNUC, SICAR e plataformas de povos e comunidades tradicionais), estruturada em oito categorias analíticas e em escala de classificação de cinco níveis. Os resultados indicam que a compatibilidade não é uniforme: há convergência quanto à arquitetura jurisdicional e às salvaguardas; complementaridade dependente de regulamentação quanto ao registro e à prevenção da dupla contagem; e incompatibilidade parcial, quando interpretadas de forma ampliativa, das regras estaduais de titularidade e de repartição negociada de benefícios. Conclui-se que a natureza jurídica da APA, composta por terras públicas e privadas, impede presumir titularidade estatal uniforme, impondo matriz fundiária por polígono e adequação regulamentar específica.

title: Biophysical factors associated with radiation use efficiency and productivity of Mimosa scabrella plantations for energy
summary: Abstract Forest plantations managed for biomass production play an important role in the transition toward renewable energy systems. However, the biophysical factors underlying biomass production and radiation use efficiency (RUE) in native
content: Abstract Forest plantations managed for biomass production play an important role in the transition toward renewable energy systems. However, the biophysical factors underlying biomass production and radiation use efficiency (RUE) in native tree species remain poorly understood. This study evaluated radiation use efficiency, biomass accumulation, radiation interception, and potential energy yield of Mimosa scabrella Benth. plantations established under different planting spacings in southern Brazil. A nine-year field experiment was conducted in a randomized complete block design with three replications and four planting spacings (2.0 × 1.0, 2.0 × 1.5, 3.0 × 1.0, and 3.0 × 1.5 m). Measurements were performed at 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 years to evaluate leaf area index (LAI), photosynthetically active radiation interception, biomass accumulation and partitioning, and RUE. The relationships among these variables were further investigated using principal component analysis based on treatment means for each spacing × age combination. Planting spacing affected stand development, radiation interception, biomass production, and energy yield. The densest spacing (2.0 × 1.0 m) exhibited the highest RUE (0.0021 kg MJ −1 ), aboveground biomass production (264 Mg ha −1 ), and potential energy yield (1,276.9 MWh ha −1 ), indicating greater biomass production per unit of intercepted radiation. Principal component analysis showed strong associations among LAI, radiation interception, RUE, and biomass accumulation, highlighting the role of canopy development in stand productivity. These findings contribute to understanding the biophysical factors associated with biomass production in M. scabrella plantations and provide a basis for evaluating planting spacing in forest systems intended for sustainable bioenergy production.

title: Embedding research in Living Labs: insights from a case comparison of knowledge co-production processes
summary: Abstract Increased focus on collaborative change-making in Living Labs creates a need to better understand how knowledge co-production enables experimental investigation of and engagement with sustainability challenges. Tracing how knowledg
content: Abstract Increased focus on collaborative change-making in Living Labs creates a need to better understand how knowledge co-production enables experimental investigation of and engagement with sustainability challenges. Tracing how knowledge co-production in Living Labs supports learning processes beyond local contexts is equally important. This study uses a multiple-step reflection process to compare four workshop series about improving water and landscape governance within Living Labs in Sweden, Germany, Finland, and Latvia. Drawing on reflective diaries, interviews with case leaders, and a joint workshop for data collection, we investigate how specific framings of these knowledge co-production processes affect actors’ commitment to join a workshop series. We also compare the roles of actor selection and process design for co-producing context-specific knowledge, nurturing shared understandings, and developing pathways forward. Our findings show that framing elements such as the sustainability problem addressed, links to collaborative structures or networks, and approach to long-term engagement determine actors’ commitment to join and participate in workshops. We argue that actor selection should strike a balance between overly similar interests and entrenched positions while ensuring breadth and depth of knowledge. Moving from understanding the problem towards developing pathways forward, providing guidance and direction while ensuring open-endedness, and centering activities for relating to others and place can support processes of connecting knowledges and developing feasible strategies with high implementation potential. We conclude that investing in reflective practice to transparently discuss processes and outcomes of knowledge co-production remains essential for both conceiving and conducting societally relevant research in Living Labs.

title: Photon-pairing-enhanced distributed spectroscopy sensing over 400 km optical fiber
summary: Single-photon detection enables sensitive measurements at ultra-low photon fluxes, supporting long-range sensing and imaging tasks. Photon-counting schemes reconstruct spectra by coherently accumulating interferograms, but phase fluctuation
content: Single-photon detection enables sensitive measurements at ultra-low photon fluxes, supporting long-range sensing and imaging tasks. Photon-counting schemes reconstruct spectra by coherently accumulating interferograms, but phase fluctuations between interfering beams pose challenges for distributed spectroscopy. Here, we introduce a photon-pairing scheme that exploits second-order correlations rather than relying on first-order interference, thereby removing the need for phase alignment of interferograms while enabling long integration times. Our approach enhances the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of reconstructed spectra, with SNR increasing linearly with photon count rate, in contrast to the square-root dependence of photon-counting techniques. We accurately reconstruct intensity spectra at an average receiving power of only 5.5 × 10−15 W per comb line over a 400 km fiber link in a distributed configuration, achieving an SNR of over 23.5 dB and demonstrating strong resilience to fiber-induced fluctuations. Our photon-pairing scheme holds strong potential for long-haul dual-comb spectroscopy and opens new avenues for frequency metrology, remote sensing, and quantum networking. Photon-pairing spectroscopy overcomes phase fluctuations to enable sensitive spectral measurements over 400 km of fibre. The study achieves spectral reconstruction at an ultra-low power of 5.5 × 10-15 W per comb line, advancing long-range sensing.

title: Scale-Dependent Degradation Kinetics and Reliability of Perovskite BIPV Modules under Semi-Arid Outdoor Conditions
source: Journal of Applied Technology Research and Innovation
summary: Perovskite photovoltaics are promising candidates for Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) applications, but their long-term outdoor stability is a critical challenge for large-scale deployment. This study investigates the degradation ki
content: Perovskite photovoltaics are promising candidates for Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) applications, but their long-term outdoor stability is a critical challenge for large-scale deployment. This study investigates the degradation kinetics and reliability behavior of scale-dependent perovskite BIPV modules under the real-world semi-arid environmental conditions in Peshawar, Pakistan. Two perovskite modules of active area 300 cm² (Module A) and 500 cm² (Module B) were monitored separately from October 2025 to January 2026 with an IoT enabled data acquisition system integrating INA219 sensors, ESP32 based monitoring and environmental sensing devices. We investigated the electrical performance, energy yield, conversion efficiency, degradation characteristics and reliability metrics at various irradiance, temperature and humidity conditions. The results indicate a progressive degradation for both modules, with a significantly higher performance deterioration for Module A (smaller area). The conversion efficiency of Module A decreased from 4.40% to 2.29% (loss of 47.9%), while the loss of Module B was comparatively smaller from 7.23% to 6.11% (loss of 15.5%). Module B contributed >70% of the total energy yield and 84.5% of the initial efficiency, while only 52.1% of the initial efficiency was retained for Module A. The efficiency decay behavior was well described by first-order degradation kinetics with degradation constants of 0.218/month and 0.056/month for Module A and B, respectively, indicating that the degradation rate of Module A was about 3.9 times faster. Reliability tests also showed increased stability of the larger module after prolonged outdoor exposure. Our findings provide direct evidence of the scale-dependent degradation and reliability performance of perovskite BIPV systems and highlight the enhanced resilience of larger-area modules for long-term utilization in semi-arid climatic environments.The results show that module size plays an important role in the outdoor stability of perovskite BIPV devices, where larger area modules are more resistant to environmental degradation for semi-arid climate conditions. This study provides one of the first climate-specific evaluation of scale-dependent perovskite BIPV degradation in Pakistan and useful insights for design, deployment and long-term optimization of perovskite-based building-integrated photovoltaic technologies.

title: Paradoxical agriculture as a conditional framework for balancing food production, climate action, ecosystem health and the sustainable development goals
summary: Abstract Improvements in agricultural production are possible without degrading ecological resources; however, the benefits that enable sustainable food security are often unequally distributed. This integrative and critical narrative revie
content: Abstract Improvements in agricultural production are possible without degrading ecological resources; however, the benefits that enable sustainable food security are often unequally distributed. This integrative and critical narrative review explores these tensions in relation to food security, water resources, resource use, climate change and terrestrial biodiversity. The evidence base comprises a synthesis of key publications from the initial bibliography, supplemented by focused verification and literature updates conducted on 15 September 2026 using publisher databases, scholarly literature and intergovernmental reports. Production benefits are qualitatively structured according to delayed costs, implications for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), intervention mechanisms and constraints. Three recurring issues arise: environmental costs and benefits are shifted off-farm, efficiency gains are mistaken for actual resource reductions and responsibility for transition costs and benefits remains unclear. Evidence supports several component practices, including diversification and improved resource management, but no single named sustainability approach has consistently achieved all desired outcomes. Land Maxing is examined as a proposed pathway linking restoration of degraded land with participatory domestication of culturally valued indigenous species and locally retained enterprise income; its components have empirical support, but the full pathway has not yet been evaluated against a comparator. The proposed framework reframes agricultural paradoxes as conditional and testable relationships rather than inevitable consequences of intensification. Its primary function is to provide a common framework for assessing mechanisms, distributional impacts and scale-dependent consequences. Study selection was purposive, evidence designs were heterogeneous and no pooled effect size was calculated due to methodological diversity. Successful transition requires locally relevant bundles of practices, credible ecological boundaries, secure rights and integrated assessment of production and welfare outcomes.

title: 5. Sınıf Sosyal Bilgiler Eğitiminde Küresel İklim Değişikliğine Karşılaştırmalı Bakış: Türkiye ve İsveç Örneği
summary: Bu makale, Türkiye ve İsveç’in sosyal bilgiler eğitiminde yer alan öğretim programları ve ders kitaplarında küresel iklim değişikliğinin temsiline ilişkin yaklaşımları karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemektedir. Çalışmada, iklim değişikliği tema
content: Bu makale, Türkiye ve İsveç’in sosyal bilgiler eğitiminde yer alan öğretim programları ve ders kitaplarında küresel iklim değişikliğinin temsiline ilişkin yaklaşımları karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemektedir. Çalışmada, iklim değişikliği teması çevresel, ekonomik, sosyal ve politik boyutlarda analiz edilmiş; iki ülkenin öğretim programları ve ders kitapları nitel doküman analizi yöntemiyle sistematik olarak değerlendirilmiştir. Bulgular, her iki ülkede de çevresel boyutun belirgin biçimde yer aldığını göstermektedir. Ancak İsveç’in sosyal bilgiler eğitimine yönelik öğretim programı ve ders kitaplarında diğer dört boyutun iklim adaleti, toplumsal eşitsizlik, politikalar ve uluslararası iş birliği gibi çok boyutlu temalarla makro düzeyde ve küresel ölçekli eleştirel bir perspektifle işlendiğini göstermektedir. Buna karşın, Türkiye’de iklim değişikliği çoğunlukla bireysel sorumluluk, yerel çevre sorunları ve mikro ölçekli uygulamalar üzerinden ele alınmakta; sosyal ve politik boyutlar daha sınırlı ve dolaylı biçimde temsil edilmektedir. Bununla birlikte, Türkiye Yüzyılı Maarif Modeli (TYMM) ile sürdürülebilirlik eğitimi alanında güçlü adımlar atıldığı ve öğretim programının daha bütüncül bir yapıya kavuşma yönünde gelişmekte olduğu da gözlemlenmektedir. Bu çalışma, küresel iklim değişikliği eğitimin yalnızca çevresel etkilerle sınırlı kalmaması; adalet, eşitlik, yönetişim ve kolektif sorumluluk gibi temalarla bütünleşik, çok boyutlu ve eylem odaklı bir öğrenme anlayışıyla yapılandırılması gerektiğini vurgulamaktadır. Sonuç olarak, İsveç’in bütüncül yaklaşımı, Türkiye’deki eğitim politikalarının geliştirilmesi için öneriler sunmaktadır.

title: Photocatalytic strategies for mitigating microplastic pollution and greenhouse gas emissions
summary: Microplastics contaminate water, soil, and air, and their persistence is linked to greenhouse gas emissions. Photocatalysis can break down these polymers via reactive oxygen species but particle shrinkage alone does not prove complete miner
content: Microplastics contaminate water, soil, and air, and their persistence is linked to greenhouse gas emissions. Photocatalysis can break down these polymers via reactive oxygen species but particle shrinkage alone does not prove complete mineralization. Recent photocatalytic systems are examined, including TiO 2 -based materials, S-scheme and Z-scheme heterojunctions, laddered architectures, metal-organic frameworks, and g-C 3 N 4 composites. These systems improve charge separation and visible-light harvesting, with some achieving high mineralization under optimized conditions. Verifying true breakdown requires TOC, LC-MS, and GC-MS because incomplete oxidation can produce toxic intermediates. Photocatalysis may also shorten plastic residence times and reduce methane and nitrous oxide emissions, though this depends on carbon fate, catalyst stability, energy inputs, and water chemistry. Combining photocatalysis with renewable energy and water treatment could offer a practical route to microplastic management, provided catalyst recovery, toxicity, and scale-up challenges are addressed.

title: Integrated use of remote sensing techniques and machine learning in assessing soil salinity: current approaches, methods, and future perspectives
source: Archives of Agronomy and Soil Science
summary: Soil salinity, driven by climate change and human activities, threatens global food security across over 412 million hectares, requiring precise monitoring. Traditional methods are accurate but costly and time-consuming. This review synthes
content: Soil salinity, driven by climate change and human activities, threatens global food security across over 412 million hectares, requiring precise monitoring. Traditional methods are accurate but costly and time-consuming. This review synthesizes recent advances integrating remote sensing (RS; UAVs, satellites, hyperspectral) with machine learning (ML; Random Forest, SVM, ANN) for soil salinity assessment. RS supplies large-scale temporal data, while ML captures complex non-linear relationships. Multi-sensor fusion (e.g. optical-radar) and ensemble ML improve accuracy (R2 up to 0.98). Yet limitations remain: reliance on surface data (0–20 cm), spectral interference from vegetation, small training datasets, and poor generalizability. Deep learning (DL) architectures (e.g. U-Net, FCNN) outperform traditional ML for specific tasks, including semantic segmentation of salinity classes (accuracy > 90%) and subsurface EC prediction (R2 up to 0.85). Future work must close the root-zone salinity gap using DL, time-series analysis, and proximal sensing. A Digital Soil Mapping framework incorporating climatic, topographic, and soil covariates is essential for robust, transferable models. Prioritizing large-scale validation and standardized methods will shift salinity assessment from mapping to predictive management, supporting sustainable agriculture and land restoration.

title: Sustainable Syngas Production From CO 2 ‐Assisted Gasification of Solid Wastes: A Simulation‐Based Approach to CO 2 Utilization
summary: ABSTRACT CO 2 ‐assisted gasification offers a potential route for waste valorization and CO 2 utilization, yet the suitability of chemically distinct wastes under comparable operating conditions remains insufficiently established. This stud
content: ABSTRACT CO 2 ‐assisted gasification offers a potential route for waste valorization and CO 2 utilization, yet the suitability of chemically distinct wastes under comparable operating conditions remains insufficiently established. This study compares wood residue (WR), rice straw (RS), poultry litter (PL), and high‐density polyethylene (HDPE) using an Aspen Plus equilibrium model. The effects of temperature (500°C–1000°C) and gasifying agent‐to‐waste (G/W) mass ratio (0.5–3.0) on syngas composition, H 2 /CO ratio, gas yield, lower heating value, cold gas efficiency, and net heat duty were evaluated. The feedstocks exhibited distinct thermodynamic responses. Biomass‐derived feedstocks generally showed improved gas‐phase performance with increasing temperature, whereas HDPE exhibited substantially higher gas yields and a distinct response to CO 2 availability. Contour‐based trade‐off analysis and constraint‐based screening were further applied to identify feedstock‐specific feasible operating regions. Within the predefined operating window of 700°C–900°C and G/W = 0.5–2.5, using H 2 /CO = 1–2 and CGE ≤ 100% as screening criteria, HDPE exhibited a broad feasible region, WR showed a highly restricted region, and no feasible regions were identified for PL and RS. These findings provide a systematic framework for preliminary feedstock and operating‐domain screening for CO 2 ‐assisted waste‐to‐syngas conversion.

content: The subsequent study aimed to determine the humus stock variations with diverse utilization of arable gray-brown soils in the arid subtropical zone.Based on the results, significant variations were prominent in humus stocks of gray-brown soils with diverse arable land uses under arid subtropical conditions.Climate change also considerably contributes to intensification of this process.Field and laboratory analyses revealed that the humus content in the topsoil ranges between 2.13% and 2.48%.The recording of lower humus levels appeared with cotton and maize crops, whereas relatively higher values were evident with alfalfa and winter wheat.The highest increase in humus content surfaced under alfalfa (0.26%), while the lowest increase was in the maize crop (0.05%).The input of plant residues varied, reaching 94 t/ha under alfalfa and 3.59 t/ha under vegetable crops (tomatoes).Over the last 15 years, mineralized humus under alfalfa reached 1.60 t/ha, while the lowest value (1.05 t/ha) emerged under vegetable crops.In the 0-30 cm soil layer, the humus stock balance was 28.58% for alfalfa and 2.60% for silage maize.Overall, a positive balance was notable with alfalfa, winter wheat, and grain maize, whereas a negative balance occurred for silage maize, cotton, and vegetable crops.

title: Developing a PBL-Based E-LKPD Integratung Local Temperature Data to Improve Global Warming Conceptual Understanding
summary: This study aims to develop and examine the effect of using a Problem-Based Learning (PBL)-based E-LKPD integrated with temperature pattern changes on students conceptual understanding of global warming material. The research uses the Resear
content: This study aims to develop and examine the effect of using a Problem-Based Learning (PBL)-based E-LKPD integrated with temperature pattern changes on students conceptual understanding of global warming material. The research uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the 4D model (define, design, develop, and disseminate), but is limited to the develop stage. The E-LKPD was implemented with 27 ninth-grade students at a public junior high school in Bengkulu City. The research instruments included observation sheets, student needs questionnaires, interviews, expert validation sheets, student response questionnaires, and conceptual understanding tests in the form of multiple-choice questions (pretest-posttest). Validation by three experts on the aspects of material, media, and language obtained an average score of 99% in the “very feasible” category. Pretest and posttest data were analyzed descriptively and quantitatively using the N-gain test. The average pretest score increased from 31.1 to 80.7 in the posttest. As many as 67% of students achieved a high N-gain category, 30% a medium category, and 3% a low category. Student responses obtained an average of 97% in the “very good” category. The results indicate that the PBL-based E-LKPD integrated with temperature pattern changes is feasible for use, effective in improving students conceptual understanding, and received positive responses from students.

title: Making the Implicit Explicit for Multilingual Learners: A Language-Based Framework for Literacy Development
source: Journal of International Crisis and Risk Communication Research
summary: Literacy is fundamentally an act of meaning-making that requires bridging micro-level linguistic choices with macro-level text structures across genres. Current literacy policies dominated by Science of Reading (SoR) mandates often overemph
content: Literacy is fundamentally an act of meaning-making that requires bridging micro-level linguistic choices with macro-level text structures across genres. Current literacy policies dominated by Science of Reading (SoR) mandates often overemphasize isolated, word-level foundational skills. This narrow focus creates a one-size-fits-all model that reduces reading to the level of individual words, not appropriate for multilingual learners (MLs) who require access to dense, specialized disciplinary discourse. This article proposes an intentional, language-based literacy framework designed to build high-challenge, high-support classrooms for MLs without lowering academic expectations. Integrating genre-based pedagogy through the Teaching and Learning Cycle (TLC) with the mode continuum, the framework employs mode shunting to intentionally bridge MLs’ existing linguistic repertoires with disciplinary academic registers. The approach makes implicit lexicogrammatical choices explicit across content area genres. Finally, the article operationalizes this pedagogy by introducing practical genre-mapping tables aligned with the four WIDA Key Language Uses (Narrate, Inform, Explain, Argue), providing educators with a concrete pathway to scaffold disciplinary literacy effectively.

title: From Theoretical Wood Availability to Mobilizable Bioenergy: A Constraint-Cascade Assessment on Monte Isola, Italy
summary: Forest bioenergy is often inferred from standing stock or biological growth, although only part of that resource becomes usable fuel after accounting for silvicultural, spatial, and operational constraints. We quantified this reduction on M
content: Forest bioenergy is often inferred from standing stock or biological growth, although only part of that resource becomes usable fuel after accounting for silvicultural, spatial, and operational constraints. We quantified this reduction on Monte Isola, a forested island in northern Italy, defining it as scenario-based technical potential rather than an estimate of immediately marketable supply. We combined a forest inventory of 14 plots selected by stratified random sampling (479 trees) with 58 quality-controlled increment-core observations sampled independently of the plots. These data supported a 15-year growth projection and a GIS analysis of accessibility. The baseline harvesting system was conventional ground-based tractor/skidder–winch extraction. Forest was classified as technically accessible if it lay within 100 m of usable roads or tracks and had a terrain slope of ≤40%. Cable-based extraction was excluded because no data were available on local cable-yarding deployment, anchor and landing configurations, or the feasibility of individual cable lines. Projected gross increment was 34,736 m3 over 15 years. After accounting for mortality, slope-constrained accessibility, 60% operational recovery, and 10% processing losses, 2901 m3 remained as processed wood-fuel equivalent, or 193 m3 year−1. The resulting baseline was 0.58 GWh year−1 or 49.6 TEP year−1. Bootstrapping with 5000 replicates propagated sampling uncertainty in cores and plots, yielding a 95% interval of 39.6–62.8 TEP year−1. Varying the ground-based slope limit from 30% to 50% produced a separate scenario range of 18.9–91.6 TEP year−1. The baseline theoretical energy equivalent represents 10.0% of a project-specific benchmark for residential diesel and LPG use. This benchmark was derived from 2015–2020 building energy records and 2020 housing and population assumptions, rather than contemporary fuel sales. Excluding the oak-rich forest type reduced the theoretical energy equivalent by 5.9%. This reduction is specific to the scenario and does not quantify a general penalty for cascading use, greenhouse gas mitigation, or ecological sustainability. Terrain-constrained accessibility and operational recovery dominated scenario sensitivity. These results provide a transparent basis for screening local forest bioenergy options while treating statistical uncertainty, operational scenarios, and ecological sustainability as separate questions.

title: บทบาทของภาษคารบอนตอการขบเคลอนเศรษฐกจสเขยวของไทย: การวเคราะหเชงนโยบายและผลกระทบตอความสามารถในการแขงขน
summary: The transition toward a green economy has led many countries to adopt carbon pricing measures. In Thailand, a carbon price of THB 200 per tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent () has been incorporated into the excise tax structure since 2025;
content: The transition toward a green economy has led many countries to adopt carbon pricing measures. In Thailand, a carbon price of THB 200 per tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent () has been incorporated into the excise tax structure since 2025; however, it does not yet cover all economic sectors. Meanwhile, the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) has been fully implemented since 1 January 2026, impacting key Thai exports, particularly cement and steel. This article analyzes carbon pricing options for Thailand and their implications for competitiveness by applying Pigouvian tax theory, the Porter Hypothesis, and the concept of carbon leakage, alongside a comparative analysis of policies in Sweden, British Columbia, the European Union, Germany, and India. The qualitative analysis indicates that setting a comparable carbon price could reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 2.4% by 2030, with a short-term GDP impact not exceeding 1.2%. This highlights the necessity for Thailand to develop a carbon pricing framework aligned with Article 9 of the EU CBAM to address both environmental and trade objectives. Furthermore, the authors analyze how recycling carbon pricing revenues can mitigate economic impacts and propose three key approaches: (1) developing a Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) system in accordance with international standards to support Article 9; (2) adjusting the carbon price trajectory to align with greenhouse gas reduction targets under NDC 3.0; and (3) developing quantitative or Computable General Equilibrium (CGE) models to evaluate impacts within the Thai context. Accordingly, the authors recommend that the Ministry of Finance and the Department of Climate Change and Environment accelerate the establishment of a forward carbon tax trajectory and subordinate legislation. This will facilitate revenue recycling and drive policy implementation across the proposed three-phase framework, ensuring clarity and practical feasibility.

title: Public attitudes toward speed safety camera enforcement and critical elements of support in British Columbia, Canada
summary: Background This study aimed to determine the views of British Columbia (B.C.) residents on acceptance and wider adoption of automated speed enforcement (ASE) in their province and local communities. The specific objectives of this study wer
content: Background This study aimed to determine the views of British Columbia (B.C.) residents on acceptance and wider adoption of automated speed enforcement (ASE) in their province and local communities. The specific objectives of this study were to determine 1) the proportion of B.C. residents who approve/disapprove of ASE; 2) the characteristics of people who approve/disapprove of ASE; and 3) the critical elements that would engender support for ASE. Methods A survey was developed and administration commissioned to a Canadian-based market research company in 2023. The survey was comprised of questions regarding demographic characteristics (including questions on age, education level, occupational status, household income, and residence community size); attitudes and behaviours reflecting traffic safety culture; attitudes toward ASE; attitudes toward 30 km/h default speed limits in residential areas; and driving characteristics. Results Of 2,104 B.C. residents participating in the survey, 53.1% approved or strongly approved of ASE. A majority of British Columbians in both the strong approver and approver groups for ASE indicated their agreement and increased support across all critical elements that engender support for ASE. The support statements which even strong ASE disapprovers favoured were a known grace allowance (e.g., 10 km/h over in a 100 km/h zone), visible signage, and camera locations being based on crash data. Conclusion This survey demonstrated a majority support for existing ASE in the province of B.C. and identified the programmatic elements that appear to be constructive in increasing the likelihood of expanding agreement and support amongst even those who disapprove of ASE most strongly.

title: Trends in measured and modeled lower stratospheric Antarctic vortex ozone over the past two decades
summary: Abstract. We analyze 2004 to 2023 winter/spring lower stratospheric Antarctic ozone data from the Aura Microwave Limb Sounder (MLS), along with similarly sampled profiles from two simulations from the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Mode
content: Abstract. We analyze 2004 to 2023 winter/spring lower stratospheric Antarctic ozone data from the Aura Microwave Limb Sounder (MLS), along with similarly sampled profiles from two simulations from the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model (WACCM) run with specified dynamics. One of these simulations uses fixed surface organic halogens from 1998 onward. The interannual variability in MLS vortex-average ozone is well matched by WACCM, although WACCM shows a smaller seasonal decrease. Probability density functions of vortex ozone profiles reveal slow increases in the smallest values; WACCM shows good agreement with MLS distribution shifts and simple linear trends. We also use multivariate linear regression with two periodic functions and a proxy for polar stratospheric clouds to derive trends in vortex-average ozone during September and October. Calculated trends are consistent with slow Antarctic vortex ozone recovery from the impact of ozone-depleting substances, with values between ~5 and 16 ppbv yr-1 in the 56–100 hPa layer. WACCM results agree well with those from MLS. The simulation with fixed surface organic halogens is consistent with zero trend. We also apply the Match technique, which follows MLS-observed parcels along trajectories to estimate vortex-average chemical ozone loss. Match estimates also show reductions in seasonal Antarctic ozone loss, although few of the Match results represent greater than two-sigma departures from zero. Our work confirms the emergence of ozone recovery, a key goal of the Aura mission, and underscores the importance of the 1987 Montreal Protocol and its Amendments in curtailing emissions of ozone-depleting substances.

title: Powering Ships, Cutting Carbon: The FuelSOME Approach to Multifuel SOFCs
summary: Abstract The maritime sector faces an accelerated decarbonization trajectory driven by the International Maritime Organization’s 2023 greenhouse-gas (GHG) strategy [1] and the European Union’s FuelEU Maritime regulation [2]. Against this re
content: Abstract The maritime sector faces an accelerated decarbonization trajectory driven by the International Maritime Organization’s 2023 greenhouse-gas (GHG) strategy [1] and the European Union’s FuelEU Maritime regulation [2]. Against this regulatory backdrop, the FuelSOME project develops and validates a multifuel solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) system tailored to ocean-going vessels [3]. The system targets efficient operation on ammonia, methanol and hydrogen—preferably sourced from renewable energy or waste streams [4] —supported by a fuel supply and quality framework and by techno-economic and life-cycle sustainability assessments (LCSA) [5]. This paper outlines the project rationale, system concept and interim progress, while situating FuelSOME in the scientific and industrial state of the art. Key activities include (i) screening fuel pathways and defining SOFC-grade fuel quality requirements, (ii) advancing stack-level tolerance and degradation management under multifuel operation [6], (iii) designing a flexible 6 kW SOFC architecture with harmonized balance-of-plant for multiple fuels [7], and (iv) implementing an integrated TEA/LCSA to compare against conventional marine propulsion [8]. Initial results indicate successful design and manufacturing of stack modules suitable for multifuel operation, component validation under varying atmospheres, and development of reforming/cracking units for ammonia and methanol [9]. Socio-environmental and economic assessments are progressing, with no major risks identified to date. The near-term objective is the laboratory validation of a 6 kW system with ≥50% electrical efficiency and ≥500 h operation under marine-relevant profiles. Collectively, these outcomes point to the technical feasibility and sustainability potential of multifuel SOFC systems as a pathway to deep decarbonization in deep-sea shipping [10]

title: Adsorption and separation of U(VI) by hafnium phosphate modified with phosphomuscle alcohol
source: Journal of Radioanalytical and Nuclear Chemistry
summary: Abstract During the advancement of the nuclear industry, substantial uranium-bearing wastewater is inevitably generated. Given the current scarcity of uranium resources, the separation and recovery of uranium hold great importance.At presen
content: Abstract During the advancement of the nuclear industry, substantial uranium-bearing wastewater is inevitably generated. Given the current scarcity of uranium resources, the separation and recovery of uranium hold great importance.At present, facing a shortage of uranium resources, it is of great significance for separating and recovering uranium. A novel hybrid adsorbent of hafnium phosphate (HfP) decorated with phosphomuscle alcohol (PA) (HfP-PA-x, where x represents the amount of PA) was prepared. The adsorption performance and separation mechanism of HfP-PA-x for U(VI) were explored systematically. Through FT-IR and XPS analysis, it was confirmed that PA was successfully loaded onto the surface of HfP. The adsorption experiments showed that the optimal dosage of PA and pH value was 10% and 5.0, respectively. The removal rate of 50 ppm U(VI) by HfP-PA-10% is close to 94.2% within 180 minutes, which is nearly 20% higher than the removal rate of unmodified HfP. XPS analysis indicate P-O and P = O played in a great role in removal of U(VI) in aqueous solution. This study provides new functional materials for the green separation and resource recovery of uranium in uranium containing wastewater.

title: Decarbonising road freight: A scoping review and conceptual framework for alternative fuel and powertrain selection
summary: The transition to alternative fuels and powertrains is a critical lever for road freight decarbonisation. However, these technologies present complex techno-economic and environmental trade-offs, creating a need for strategic decision suppo
content: The transition to alternative fuels and powertrains is a critical lever for road freight decarbonisation. However, these technologies present complex techno-economic and environmental trade-offs, creating a need for strategic decision support on which technologies to adopt. This systematic scoping review analyses studies that apply quantitative decision-making methods to evaluate and select alternative fuels and powertrains. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, an initial 6,372 articles published from 2015 onwards were identified through database searching. After screening and citation searching, 45 primary studies were included in the review. The analysis reveals that exact optimisation (n = 27) is predominantly used for fleet planning or transport and energy system transition modelling, whereas multi-criteria decision-making (n = 15) is primarily applied for strategic technology ranking and prioritisation. Metaheuristic approaches (n = 3) are largely reserved for highly complex or computationally difficult optimisation problems. The evidence base is concentrated in Europe and North America, limiting the transferability of evidence to the Global South. Multiple research and modelling gaps were also identified that affect comparability and practical usability. These include unspecified contextual boundaries, limited social impacts, narrow environmental modelling, and unspecified fuel production pathways. The primary contribution of this review is the Alternative Fuel and Powertrain Decision Framework (AFPDF). This conceptual framework combines recurring decision elements across the evidence base with modelling and reporting recommendations to structure the broader decision-making process, whilst addressing existing gaps. The AFPDF provides analysts with a transparent process for generating context-specific fuel and powertrain recommendations for road freight stakeholders, and reporting the assumptions on which those recommendations depend.

title: CO2 hydrogenation across the pressure gap over Ag/ZnO:Al2O3 catalysts
summary: Abstract The hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to value-added chemicals is a major challenge. Metal-oxide interfaces and surface structures play fundamental roles and govern the selectivity of this reaction; thus, catalysts must be investigat
content: Abstract The hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to value-added chemicals is a major challenge. Metal-oxide interfaces and surface structures play fundamental roles and govern the selectivity of this reaction; thus, catalysts must be investigated under relevant reaction conditions to identify structure-activity relationships and engineer more efficient materials. This work aims to elucidate mechanisms of carbon dioxide hydrogenation to methanol and side products by using operando characterization techniques within a pressure range of 1 mbar up to 15 bar. Bifunctional Ag/ZnO and Ag/ZnO:Al 2 O 3 catalysts are studied using multiple spectroscopic techniques combined with online product analysis. During catalyst activation in hydrogen, several restructuring processes of the catalyst occur at different pressures. Under carbon dioxide hydrogenation reaction conditions carbonate, formate and CH x surface intermediates show strong pressure-dependent abundances. Combining thermodynamics with in situ and operando investigations of pressure-dependent structures and intermediates allows assessing carbon dioxide hydrogenation through the pressure gap.

title: Designing a blockchain-enabled certification framework for food loss and waste reduction: a proof-of-concept in the fresh food supply chain
summary: Blockchain technology, supported by IoT, has proven essential for improving traceability in food supply chains, but its application to auditing and certifying food loss and waste (FLW) reduction remains largely unexplored. This paper addres
content: Blockchain technology, supported by IoT, has proven essential for improving traceability in food supply chains, but its application to auditing and certifying food loss and waste (FLW) reduction remains largely unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by proposing the architectural design, data models, and audit workflow of a permissioned blockchain-enabled tool developed within the EU H2020 FOODRUS project. Focused on the Spanish fresh vegetable supply chain pilot, the proposed framework integrates Hyperledger Fabric to establish a decentralized and immutable ledger for recording audit evidence and verifying compliance indicators. Rather than assessing long-term operational impact, this study demonstrates the baseline technical feasibility of automating FLW certification workflows through a deployed proof-of-concept prototype. The implementation highlights key architectural contributions, such as standardized data schemas and an integrated 7-stage audit lifecycle, while identifying primary deployment hurdles, notably stakeholder reluctance toward ERP data sharing. The findings confirm that while a permissioned blockchain design effectively secures audit record integrity, broader adoption hinges on establishing legally recognized FLW certification schemes and granular data-governance mechanisms.

title: Small Modular Electrochemical Containers for Decarbonization of AI Data Centers
summary: Abstract The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasing data-center electricity demand and reinforcing the near-term role of fossil-fuel power generation. Decarbonizing this infrastructure requires carbon capture systems tha
content: Abstract The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasing data-center electricity demand and reinforcing the near-term role of fossil-fuel power generation. Decarbonizing this infrastructure requires carbon capture systems that are efficient, compact, modular, and compatible with space-constrained data centers. Here, we evaluate Small Modular Electrochemical Containers (SMECs) as a deployment-oriented application of a two-stage, membraneless electrochemically mediated amine regeneration (EMAR) process. The design integrates CO2 absorption and electrochemical desorption within one gas-diffusion-electrode cell, eliminating absorber columns and ion-exchange membranes. Single-cell experiments were conducted under simulated natural-gas and coal-derived flue gas. Polarization mapping identified optimized operating conditions, which were then used in a 300-cycle, 50-h accelerated stability test with periodic polarity switching. The cell maintained repeatable voltage and CO2 absorption/desorption profiles, with absorption and desorption efficiencies of ∼90% under optimized conditions. The energetics ranged from 50–85 kJe/molCO2, and GC/IC analyses showed no detectable gaseous or liquid side products. The paper further includes theoretical modeling of SOx and NOx effects on the absorbent. In a case study for a 360 MW data-center power plant, the TEA showed that fewer than 20 SMEC units could achieve near-complete decarbonization, increasing the levelized electricity cost from about \$58/MWh to \$74/MWh.

title: The Public Health Implications of Online Food Delivery Platforms: A Narrative Review
summary: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarises current knowledge on the role of online food delivery (OFD) platforms in shaping dietary behaviours, sedentary behaviours and other related health outcomes. RECENT FINDINGS: OFD platforms predominan
content: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarises current knowledge on the role of online food delivery (OFD) platforms in shaping dietary behaviours, sedentary behaviours and other related health outcomes. RECENT FINDINGS: OFD platforms predominantly promote and facilitate access to energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods. Drivers such as convenience, time scarcity, and algorithmic personalisation reinforce unhealthy eating patterns by making less healthy options more visible and accessible. Evidence concerning sedentary behaviour remains sparse. A small number of studies suggest that OFD use may be displacing traditional food procurement behaviours resulting in reduced physical activity. OFD platforms further influence health through environmental, labour, and corporate activities. Despite their growing influence, OFD platforms remain largely unregulated within existing policy frameworks. There is an urgent need for interdisciplinary research, improved methodological rigour, regulatory change, and industry accountability to mitigate the health risks associated with OFD platforms and harness their potential for promoting healthier diets and related health behaviours.

title: Beyond brown adipose tissue: Avian thermogenesis without UCP1 – mechanisms, evidence gaps and implications for metabolic health and sustainable poultry production
summary: ABSTRACT Unlike mammals, birds lack canonical brown adipose tissue and the UCP1 gene, yet exhibit UCP1-independent non-shivering thermogenesis (NST). In vitro, embryonic chicken mesenchymal cells differentiate into avian brown adipocyte-lik
content: ABSTRACT Unlike mammals, birds lack canonical brown adipose tissue and the UCP1 gene, yet exhibit UCP1-independent non-shivering thermogenesis (NST). In vitro, embryonic chicken mesenchymal cells differentiate into avian brown adipocyte-like cells (ABALCs) with multilocular lipid droplets, elevated mitochondrial density, and upregulated PGC-1α and PPARγ, activating a transfected mouse UCP1 promoter despite endogenous UCP1 loss. In vivo, gradual cold acclimatization or triiodothyronine (T 3 ) induces beige-like adipocytes enriched in mitochondria within the subcutaneous neck depot (“neck warmer”), with increased avian uncoupling protein (avUCP), CIDEA, TBX1, and mitochondrial markers, while abdominal fat remains largely unresponsive. Skeletal muscle is the main site of NST, where SERCA/RyR-mediated calcium cycling and avUCP/ANT-associated mitochondrial uncoupling are candidate mechanisms; because avUCP is multifunctional (heat, redox and fuel handling), its expression is not by itself a read-out of heat output. Nutritional and microbial interventions—including polyunsaturated fatty acids, capsaicin, succinate, bile acids, and probiotics—have been associated with altered lipid metabolism and reduced visceral adiposity, although direct links to quantifiable heat production remain unestablished and non-thermogenic mechanisms (lipid digestion, hepatic lipogenesis, feed intake, inflammation) have not been excluded. Collectively, the evidence is consistent with, but does not yet prove, a conserved, multi-organ thermogenic metabolic network (TMN) in birds in which skeletal muscle predominates. Exploiting this latent capacity offers a conceptual framework for nutritional and management strategies to mitigate excessive fat deposition and enhance thermal resilience in commercial broilers, although the energetic trade-offs with growth and feed efficiency remain to be resolved. A structured roadmap integrating nutritional, microbial, environmental, and genetic approaches is proposed to test, and if validated to harness, the TMN for sustainable production.

title: A review of refuse-derived fuel utilisation as an industrial resource: The nigerian perspective
source: Journal of Infrastructure Policy and Development
summary: Municipal solid waste (MSW) generation in Nigeria has increased significantly due to rapid urbanisation, population growth, and changing consumption patterns, creating serious environmental and waste management challenges. Refuse-derived fu
content: Municipal solid waste (MSW) generation in Nigeria has increased significantly due to rapid urbanisation, population growth, and changing consumption patterns, creating serious environmental and waste management challenges. Refuse-derived fuel (RDF), which is produced from the combustible fraction of MSW, has emerged as a sustainable alternative fuel for industrial applications, particularly in cement manufacturing, steel production, and electricity generation. This review examines RDF production processes, industrial utilisation, and environmental implications, with an emphasis on the Nigerian context. It discusses the generation, composition, and management of MSW, highlighting how waste characteristics influence RDF quality and performance. The review further evaluates the current status of RDF utilisation in Nigeria, identifies key technical, economic, and policy barriers limiting its adoption, and explores opportunities for wider implementation. The findings indicate that Nigeria possesses substantial potential for RDF development owing to its abundant MSW resources and growing industrial energy demand. Strengthening waste segregation, supportive policies, and investment in processing infrastructure will be critical to advancing RDF utilisation and promoting a circular economy.

title: A Tracking Data-Based Evaluation of Truck Electrification Potential in Europe
summary: Abstract This research explores challenges of transitioning heavy-duty truck (HDT) fleets to electric power, using real-world telematics data. By combining energy consumption modeling with total cost of ownership (TCO) analysis, the study i
content: Abstract This research explores challenges of transitioning heavy-duty truck (HDT) fleets to electric power, using real-world telematics data. By combining energy consumption modeling with total cost of ownership (TCO) analysis, the study identifies when battery-electric trucks (BETs) can viably replace diesel and liquefied natural gas (LNG) vehicles. As expected, battery capacity is a major barrier to widespread electrification. However, adopting customized battery configurations and enabling intermediate charging can greatly expand electrification opportunities while lowering yearly operating expenses. In addition to the approach with detailed daily route information from telematics data, this contribution presents a procedure to estimate the electrification potential for HDT fleets based on usage metadata, such as the distribution of daily driven kilometers and fuel consumption. Results of this approach for close to 300 fleets with about 22,500 trucks are presented. Further analyses show that differentiated toll costs can play a major role in the economic competitiveness of BETs. The study offers recommendations for fleet managers and policymakers, highlighting the importance of the deployment of reliable charging networks and the design of supportive regulations to accelerate the shift toward electric freight transportation.

title: Reflections on Renewable Energies in BRICS+ Nations
summary: The urgency to address climate change on a global scale has never been greater. In recent decades, the international community has increasingly acknowledged the necessity for sustainable development, with energy transitions playing a critic
content: The urgency to address climate change on a global scale has never been greater. In recent decades, the international community has increasingly acknowledged the necessity for sustainable development, with energy transitions playing a critical role in alleviating the environmental effects of economic growth ( Schlaepfer & Lawler, 2023 ). From the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro to the Paris Agreement of 2016, the world has experienced a range of concerted initiatives aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and fostering cleaner, more sustainable energy systems. As countries work to align their development plans with climate change objectives, renewable energy has become a fundamental element of worldwide sustainability efforts.

title: Variation in rhizosphere microbial communities and nitrogen- and phosphorus-cycling functional genes among rubber plantations in Yunnan, China
summary: Introduction Rhizosphere microorganisms are important participants in soil nutrient transformation. However, variation in rhizosphere microbial community composition and nitrogen (N)- and phosphorus (P)-cycling functional gene profiles amon
content: Introduction Rhizosphere microorganisms are important participants in soil nutrient transformation. However, variation in rhizosphere microbial community composition and nitrogen (N)- and phosphorus (P)-cycling functional gene profiles among rubber plantations in Yunnan Province remains unclear. Methods Metagenomic sequencing was used to compare rhizosphere microbial community composition and N- and P-cycling functional gene profiles among the rubber plantations located in five major natural rubber-producing areas in Yunnan Province, China: Gengma (MD), Ximeng (XM), Mengla (ML), Jinghong (JH), and Jiangcheng (JC). Results Bacterial and fungal community composition and N- and P-cycling functional gene profiles differed significantly among the five rubber plantations. JC exhibited higher fungal diversity and richness, but its bacterial diversity was significantly lower than that in MD. The bacterial communities were dominated by Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota, and Actinomycetota, and the relative abundance of Acidobacteria was significantly enriched in JC compared to JH. Furthermore, Mucoromycota, Ascomycota, and Basidiomycota were the dominant phyla in the fungal community. At the functional level, compared to JC, key genes associated with N cycling were significantly enriched in ML, including N assimilation ( glnA , gltB , gltD ), dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium ( narG , narH , nirB ), nitrification ( nxrA , nxrB ), and denitrification ( napA , napB ). Furthermore, the nosZ gene was also significantly enriched in MD compared to JC. Regarding the P cycle, compared to JC, genes associated with high-affinity phosphate transporters ( pstA , pstB , pstC ) and polyphosphate degradation ( ndk ) were significantly enriched in MD, whereas the organic phosphorus mineralization-related gene phnX exhibited the opposite trend. Meanwhile, compared to MD, the polyphosphate degradation-related gene ppk2 was significantly enriched in ML, whereas the inorganic phosphorus solubilization-related gene pqqC exhibited the opposite pattern. Hierarchical partitioning identified soil pH, total phosphorus (TP), and total potassium (TK) as the primary factors significantly associated with variations in bacterial community composition and P-cycling functional gene profiles. Conclusion In summary, the composition of rhizosphere bacterial and fungal communities, as well as the functional gene profiles related to N and P cycling, differed significantly among the investigated rubber plantations. These variations were closely associated with soil physicochemical factors. These findings may provide a microbiological basis for further developing site-specific nutrient management strategies in rubber plantations.

title: Optimizing Tugboat Emissions within Port Areas Using Data Fusion
summary: Abstract Maritime transport is essential for global trade but remains a major source of greenhouse gas and air pollutant emissions, especially near ports and coastal communities. Tugboats, which play a crucial role in vessel manoeuvres, are
content: Abstract Maritime transport is essential for global trade but remains a major source of greenhouse gas and air pollutant emissions, especially near ports and coastal communities. Tugboats, which play a crucial role in vessel manoeuvres, are significant contributors but their emissions are poorly quantified due to the inadequacy of conventional estimation methods. This study develops a multidisciplinary approach to quantify and optimize tug-related emissions by integrating on-board field campaigns, interviews with tug crews, Automatic Identification System (AIS) data, and full-mission bridge simulation. Initial results from Spanish ports reveal that tugboats operate inefficiently, with more than half of their time spent below 25% engine load and extended waiting periods contributing to unnecessary fuel consumption.
