title: The End of Uniformity: Spatial, Climatic, and Toxicological Redefinitions of Air Quality
summary: Her research interests focus on air pollution and human health.Her group combines field measurements, laboratory experiments, and computational simulation to study oxidative potential, environmental persistent free radicals (EPFRs), and che
content: Her research interests focus on air pollution and human health.Her group combines field measurements, laboratory experiments, and computational simulation to study oxidative potential, environmental persistent free radicals (EPFRs), and chemical and cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) in particulate matter to understand the sources, reaction mechanisms, toxicity, and health effects of air pollutants.

title: Wide-bandgap Technologies in Electronic Power Circuits for Electrified Vehicles and Charging Infrastructures
summary: Abstract Wide-bandgap (WBG) semiconductors play a pivotal role in advancing the next generation of electric vehicles. Compared to conventional silicon-based semiconductors, WBG materials offer superior performance, enabling a faster transit
content: Abstract Wide-bandgap (WBG) semiconductors play a pivotal role in advancing the next generation of electric vehicles. Compared to conventional silicon-based semiconductors, WBG materials offer superior performance, enabling a faster transition toward sustainable mobility. To support this technological shift, several research initiatives have been launched. This paper focuses on a series of interconnected projects: starting with HiPERFORM in 2018, followed by HiEFFICIENT from 2020, and continuing with HiPower 5.0, which begins in 2025. These projects bring together stakeholders across the entire value chain – from semiconductor manufacturers to leading automotive OEMs. Their shared goal is to enhance the power density, efficiency, and reliability of WBG-based power electronics for applications in electric vehicles, maritime transport, and charging infrastructure. The paper highlights recent advancements in WBG materials such as Silicon Carbide (SiC) and Gallium Nitride (GaN), also considering emerging bidirectional WBG technologies enabling high power density and performance. In addition, these emerging materials offer significant benefits over traditional Silicon, including improved switching performance, higher operating temperatures, and increased power density. As a result, they contribute to reduced energy losses, smaller system sizes, and lighter components. To illustrate these developments, the paper presents selected technical solutions and benchmarks them against the current state of the art.

title: Mobilizing the seafood industry for climate action
summary: Abstract Large seafood companies face climate-related risks across their operations, with substantial economic and financial implications. Nevertheless, corporate reporting remains limited, with nearly half of the 100 largest companies prov
content: Abstract Large seafood companies face climate-related risks across their operations, with substantial economic and financial implications. Nevertheless, corporate reporting remains limited, with nearly half of the 100 largest companies providing no climate-related disclosures. Reporting, which can be an indicator of action and priorities, has focused primarily on mitigation, with little attention to adaptation. We consider these gaps and propose four priorities to support capacity and pathways for climate-resilient seafood operations.

title: Assessing net climate impacts and avoided impacts of sewage sludge management options: A case study of Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
summary: Wastewater treatment plants, which are essential for protecting water quality, can generate substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through biological treatment, energy consumption, and sludge management.This study applies life cycle and
content: Wastewater treatment plants, which are essential for protecting water quality, can generate substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through biological treatment, energy consumption, and sludge management.This study applies life cycle and avoided-impact assessments to quantify GHG emissions and evaluate mitigation options for the Central Wastewater Treatment Plant in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, using 2024 operational data.The functional unit was 1 m³ of treated wastewater.Four scenarios were evaluated: continued long-term sludge storage (S1), a 20% reduction in electricity consumption (S2), anaerobic digestion with combined heat and power (CHP) generation (S3), and controlled composting (S4).The baseline climate change impact was 1.2969 kg CO₂-eq/m³, corresponding to approximately 90,137 t CO₂-eq attributable to wastewater received in 2024, including cumulative sludgestorage emissions over an assumed four-year period.Direct emissions accounted for 81.71% of the total impact.CH₄ emissions from sludge storage and wastewater treatment collectively contributed 61.58%, whereas electricity consumption contributed 17.32%.S2 reduced the impact to 1.2520 kg CO₂-eq/m³, a 3.46% reduction relative to S1. S3 achieved the greatest modelled mitigation by avoiding baseline sludge-storage CH₄ emissions and substituting grid electricity and coal-based heat with recovered biogas energy.Its net impact was 0.6379 kg CO₂-eq/m³, a 50.81% reduction.In contrast, S4 increased the net impact to 1.4473 kg CO₂-eq/m³, an 11.60% increase, because emissions from composting and subsequent compost application outweighed avoided sludge-storage emissions and fertilizer-substitution credits.Under the modelled assumptions, AD with CHP showed the greatest mitigation potential among the evaluated options.These results provide quantitative evidence to inform sludge-management and climate-mitigation planning in Ulaanbaatar.

title: QUALITY OF LIFE OF RESIDENTS IN GAS FLARING COMMUNITY IN AKWA IBOM STATE, NIGER DELTA REGION, NIGERIA
source: International Journal of Renewable Energy and Environment
summary: Gas flaring remains a persistent environmental and public health issue in Nigeria’s Niger Delta, particularly in Akwa Ibom State, where crude oil extraction is widespread. This research compares the quality of life (QoL) of residents of a g
content: Gas flaring remains a persistent environmental and public health issue in Nigeria’s Niger Delta, particularly in Akwa Ibom State, where crude oil extraction is widespread. This research compares the quality of life (QoL) of residents of a gas flaring community (Mkpanak) and a non-gas flaring community (Okposo) in the Niger Delta region of Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. A cross-sectional, comparative survey was conducted. Multistage sampling was used to sample 389 respondents. The analysis was conducted using the four components of QoL: subjective wellbeing, objective wellbeing, psychological wellbeing and environmental quality. Data analysis involved descriptive statistics and comparative analysis. The results showed that many residents of Mkpanak indicated low environmental quality (86.7%), low objective wellbeing (29.1%) and low psychological wellbeing (13.3%). Comparatively, Okposo residents reported better environmental quality (61.7%), objective wellbeing (15.5%) and psychological wellbeing (6.7%). However, subjective wellbeing in Mkpanak (46.9%) was marginally better than in Okposo (43.0%), the difference in subjective wellbeing warrants further investigation into factors that may influence residents’ perceptions of quality of life. In conclusion the research highlights the negative impacts of gas flaring on various dimensions of wellbeing. It recommends policy action to implement environmental laws, enhance social infrastructure, and address health and livelihood needs. The study adds to the conversation on environmental justice and sustainable development in the extractive industry.

title: Carbon Credits for Belowground C Sequestration by Alders? A Review of Empirical Evidence and Underlying Processes
summary: Increasing belowground carbon sequestration through forest management has significant potential to mitigate rising atmospheric CO2 but is rarely used in C-credit systems. Difficulty in, and expense of, quantifying changes in soil C, along w
content: Increasing belowground carbon sequestration through forest management has significant potential to mitigate rising atmospheric CO2 but is rarely used in C-credit systems. Difficulty in, and expense of, quantifying changes in soil C, along with large but somewhat ambiguous results in trials, has hindered its use in C-credit systems. Growing N2-fixing trees, however, has been widely suggested to consistently increase soil C. We review evidence from empirical and ecosystem process studies to evaluate whether consistent belowground C sequestration is present in the most widely studied N2-fixing-tree genus Alnus (alder). We searched globally for studies that included measures of change in mineral-soil C, including chronosequence studies and field trials. We found studies that also compared alder effects against non-N2-fixing species, which link to additionality calculations (relative C sequestration). We found that: (1) the empirical evidence of positive soil-C accretion under alder is large and unidirectional for all studies; (2) ecosystem process studies provide multiple mechanisms that can explain the observations; and (3) both empirical and mechanistic evidence persist across a wide array of climate, soils, and disturbance regimes. We suggest that evidence is sufficiently consistent to establish an interim 0.5 Mg ha−1 yr−1 standard when considering C-credits, especially in decisions on whether to include alders to mitigate rising CO2.

title: Towards personalized and lifestyle-inspired soil management: lessons from the gut microbiome
summary: Abstract Soil microorganisms are key drivers of ecosystem functions supporting biodiversity, food production, and climate regulation. Restoring multiple ecosystem functions under intensive land-use and climate change requires steering micro
content: Abstract Soil microorganisms are key drivers of ecosystem functions supporting biodiversity, food production, and climate regulation. Restoring multiple ecosystem functions under intensive land-use and climate change requires steering microbiome composition. However, this remains challenging due to the high complexity of soils and the assembly rules of their microbiomes. As the extensively studied human gut microbiome has considerable similarities with the soil microbiome, we explore advances in steering the human gut microbiome composition to improve the steering of soil microbiomes.

title: Beyond net zero: Understanding the wider motivations and barriers to the adoption of greenhouse gas mitigation and sequestration measures amongst UK beef and sheep farms
summary: This paper draws on online survey responses from 111 UK beef and sheep farmers to provide an insight into engagement with the net zero greenhouse gas (GHG) target. First, we explore whether they consider the net zero target into their decis
content: This paper draws on online survey responses from 111 UK beef and sheep farmers to provide an insight into engagement with the net zero greenhouse gas (GHG) target. First, we explore whether they consider the net zero target into their decision-making , and second, identify the motivations, perceived barriers, and behavioural controls influencing adoption of GHG mitigation and sequestration practices . Most respondents believed net zero was achievable and expressed some knowledge of required actions. However, consideration of net zero in routine decision-making remained limited. Behaviour also varied by farm characteristics: hill, smaller farms, and those with direct processor or retailer supply contracts, or had completed a carbon audit were more likely to consider net zero in decisions. Many farmers had implemented, and expressed willingness to adopt mitigation measures, largely motivated by productivity and economic benefits. For sequestration, measures to enhance soil carbon were popular, while afforestation was not. Several distinct characteristics were associated with a greater willingness to adopt GHG mitigation and sequestration measures. These included larger farm size, lowland farms, cattle-based enterprises, and completion of a carbon audit. Awareness of the net zero target did not significantly influence willingness to adopt. Strikingly, the majority of respondents were not aware of any co-benefits of implementing GHG emission mitigation measures, despite numerous potential positive outcomes for farm businesses. We recommend that communication of these co-benefits are prioritised in future knowledge exchange, and policy/advisory strategies should avoid framing net zero at the sector-level as a singular goal and instead embed mitigation measures within broader strategies for resilient and profitable farming systems.

title: Performance and emission analysis of sustainable rice bran-Calophyllum-CNSL biodiesel blends in a conventional diesel engine
summary: Diesel engines are often run on blended fuels to evaluate the adaptability and alternative energy source with changing engine components. The study compares the engine performance and emission characteristics of diesel engines operating on
content: Diesel engines are often run on blended fuels to evaluate the adaptability and alternative energy source with changing engine components. The study compares the engine performance and emission characteristics of diesel engines operating on pure diesel and biodiesel blends. Tests were carried out on a single cylinder, four stroke, water cooled direct injection diesel engine at constant speed of 1500 rpm. The 10%, 20% and 30% bio-oils by volume (B10, B20 and B30) biodiesel blends were tested at different engine loads in comparison to regular diesel without any engine modifications. The diesel engine performance was evaluated by brake power (BP), brake specific fuel consumption (BSFC), total fuel consumption (TFC) and brake thermal efficiency (BTE). Also, emissions characteristics such as carbon dioxide (CO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx) and unburned hydrocarbons (UBHC) were measured. The results revealed that all the biodiesel blends had the same braking power for all the fuels with a maximum value of 4.26KW under all loads. Because biodiesel has a reduced calorific value, performances like TFC and BSFC improved with its presence; this impact was particularly noticeable for the B30 mix. Nevertheless, the B20 blend achieved a slight increase in TFC at medium and higher loads, leading to effective fuel use. Due to better combustion aided by the oxygenated fuel characteristic, B20 outperforms the other blends, obtaining a higher BTE of 30.2% than diesel at greater loads. Higher biodiesel concentration increased the UBHC emission since it had the maximum viscosity and decreased fuel volatility. All things considered, the B20 blend offers the best balance between thermal efficiency, emission characteristics, and fuel consumption.

title: Optimisation of ultrasound-assisted deep eutectic solvent extraction of carbohydrates and proteins from farmed brown seaweed (Saccharina latissima) using response surface methodology
summary: Seaweeds are emerging as versatile and promising sources of bioactive compounds with applications in food, feed, and nutraceuticals. This study explored ultrasound-assisted extraction using a deep eutectic solvent (choline chloride: lactic
content: Seaweeds are emerging as versatile and promising sources of bioactive compounds with applications in food, feed, and nutraceuticals. This study explored ultrasound-assisted extraction using a deep eutectic solvent (choline chloride: lactic acid) to enhance the co-extraction of proteins and soluble carbohydrates from Saccharina latissima . Extraction parameters, ultrasound amplitude (70–90%), sonication time (5–15 min), and solid-to-solvent ratio (3–7%) were optimised using response surface methodology with a Box-Behnken design. Total protein content (TPC) and total soluble carbohydrate content (TSC) were used as the two primary responses for model development and numerical optimisation, while protein recovery yield (PRY) and carbohydrate recovery yield (CRY) were calculated from the corresponding TPC and TSC values. The optimised conditions (88% amplitude, 12 min sonication, and 3% solid-to-solvent ratio) yielded a TPC of 50.98 mg BSAE/g of ethanol-pretreated and dried seaweed and a TSC of 431.09 mg GE/g of ethanol-pretreated and dried seaweed, corresponding to protein and carbohydrate recovery yields of 56.58% and 83.54%, respectively. The optimised condition was validated experimentally. The developed models for the two responses were highly significant (p < 0.0001), with coefficients of determination (R 2 ) exceeding 0.98. The optimised ultrasound-assisted deep eutectic solvent (US-DES) extraction approach significantly enhanced antioxidant capacity, achieving 73.46 ± 1.3% DPPH radical scavenging activity and 134.48 ± 1.67 µM TE/mL of extract for FRAP. Fucose content was maximally recovered under the same conditions (20.56 ± 0.46 mg/g of ethanol-pretreated and dried seaweed). FTIR and SEM analyses revealed changes in the biomass functional-group profiles and surface morphology following extraction. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of ultrasound-assisted DES extraction for recovering protein- and carbohydrate-rich fractions from S. latissima , with promising antioxidant capacity.

title: Decoupled ore and scrap trade networks constrain low-carbon metal supply
summary: Abstract Global supply chains for critical metals such as aluminium and copper are increasingly exposed to sustainability and geopolitical risks under the pressure of energy transition. In this paper we compare primary (ore) and secondary (
content: Abstract Global supply chains for critical metals such as aluminium and copper are increasingly exposed to sustainability and geopolitical risks under the pressure of energy transition. In this paper we compare primary (ore) and secondary (scrap) trade networks for the United States, European Union and China using multilayer network analysis. We focus on the years 2010-2023, a period that captures intensified demand for the two metals. Results identify a marked structural decoupling: around 40% of scrap-trading countries do not participate in ore trade. Further, while about 50% of ore trade links overlap with scrap networks, only some 10–15% of scrap connections overlap with ore trade. Despite strong alignment in trading partners, volumes of scrap and ore trade diverge substantially. The observed differences indicate that the two commodity streams use partly distinct international trading relationships. Major economies may compete for ore suppliers but remain interdependent in scrap trade, revealing a bifurcated system with uneven resilience. Strengthening integration between primary and secondary supply chains is therefore critical for achieving sustainable critical metal supply for the low-carbon energy transition and establishing resource-efficient metal systems.

title: Future-ready livestock systems: climate resilience, animal welfare and sustainable adaptation
summary: Climate change is increasingly challenging the sustainability, productivity, and welfare of livestock systems worldwide. Rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, water scarcity, changing precipitation patterns, and emerging disease risks di
content: Climate change is increasingly challenging the sustainability, productivity, and welfare of livestock systems worldwide. Rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, water scarcity, changing precipitation patterns, and emerging disease risks directly affect animal health, welfare, feed availability, reproductive performance, and farm profitability. These pressures are particularly pronounced in climate-sensitive regions such as the Mediterranean, where livestock production is closely linked to limited natural resources and highly variable environmental conditions. Strengthening the adaptive capacity of livestock systems therefore requires an integrated approach that simultaneously addresses animal welfare, environmental sustainability, technological innovation, and farm resilience. This paper examines key pathways for developing climate-resilient livestock systems by integrating animal-based, environmental, technological, and management strategies. Particular attention is given to climate-adapted breeds and genetic resources, heat-stress mitigation, improved animal health and welfare management, adaptive grazing, sustainable pasture and forage management, integrated crop–livestock systems, and efficient use of water and other natural resources. The potential of precision livestock farming, digital monitoring, sensor-based technologies, early-warning systems, and data-driven decision-support tools to anticipate climate-related risks and improve adaptive management is also considered. Beyond farm-level interventions, the paper highlights the importance of enabling mechanisms, including climate-risk assessment, financial instruments, farmer training, institutional support, and appropriate policy frameworks. Evidence and examples from different production environments are used to demonstrate how locally adapted solutions can enhance animal welfare and productivity while reducing environmental pressures and strengthening resilience to climatic shocks. The paper emphasizes that climate resilience should not be addressed solely as a productivity or environmental challenge but through a systems-based framework that recognizes the interconnections among animal welfare, ecological sustainability, technological innovation, and socio-economic viability. Building future-ready livestock systems will therefore require coordinated research, policy support, investment, and stakeholder engagement to translate climate adaptation strategies into practical and scalable solutions.

title: The E-Scooter Paradox: Governing Micromobility for Urban Sustainability. Environmental Impacts and Policy Implications from Hamburg’s Suburban Implementation
summary: Abstract Despite meeting sustainability criteria in theory, shared e-kick scooters face widespread criticism regarding their environmental benefits and urban integration. This study examines the potential of e-scooters as first - and last-m
content: Abstract Despite meeting sustainability criteria in theory, shared e-kick scooters face widespread criticism regarding their environmental benefits and urban integration. This study examines the potential of e-scooters as first - and last-mile connections in suburban areas through a demonstration project in Hamburg, Germany. Using vehicle data, user surveys, and life cycle assessment methodology, we analyzed 175,381 vehicle-kilometers across two suburban districts. Results show that 23% of trips were intermodal, with 26% replacing car trips. Under conservative assumptions, the deployment resulted in net additional emissions of 4,272 kg CO 2 e due to high embedded emissions from vehicle production. However, a sensitivity analysis reveals that achieving 37% car trip substitution or reducing LCA emissions to 42.6 g CO 2 e/km would result in net-zero emissions. The study demonstrates that improved vehicle durability, increased modal shift from private cars, and integration with public transport can enable e-scooters to contribute meaningfully to sustainable urban mobility systems, notably in sub-urban environments.

title: The Just Energy Transition Plan in BRICS+ Nations
summary: The concept of a “just energy transition” is fundamental to reshaping global energy systems in ways that are both sustainable and equitable. Grounded in the principles of social justice and environmental responsibility, a Just Energy Transi
content: The concept of a “just energy transition” is fundamental to reshaping global energy systems in ways that are both sustainable and equitable. Grounded in the principles of social justice and environmental responsibility, a Just Energy Transition aims to mitigate the adverse effects of climate change while ensuring that all socio-economic groups, particularly vulnerable and marginalized populations, benefit fairly from the shift to cleaner energy. For BRICS+ nations, an economic bloc comprising Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, with extended cooperation from countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates, and Saudi Arabia, energy transition has emerged as a strategic priority. While these countries are influential actors in the global economy, they each face unique challenges in formulating and implementing energy policies that simultaneously promote economic development, environmental sustainability, and social equity.

title: Mapping global organic soil disturbance and associated greenhouse gas emissions, 2001–2024
summary: Peatlands and other organic soils occupy a small fraction of the land surface but store a large share of global soil carbon, and drainage and fire in these systems are major, poorly mapped sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Remote s
content: Peatlands and other organic soils occupy a small fraction of the land surface but store a large share of global soil carbon, and drainage and fire in these systems are major, poorly mapped sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Remote sensing enables global monitoring of organic-soil disturbance, but few globally consistent systems link organic-soil extent, disturbance activity, and emissions at high spatial resolution. Here we develop a nominal 30 m (0.00025°) global framework that overlays an organic-soil extent map with multi-temporal land-cover, infrastructure, plantation, peat-extraction, and burned-area data to delineate disturbed organic soils. Using IPCC Wetlands Supplement (Tier 1) methods, we estimate CO 2 , CH 4 , N 2 O, and CO emissions over 2001–2024. The baseline uses an operational organic-soil extent from an ensemble probability layer, thresholded separately within tropical, boreal, and temperate IPCC climate domains. Because mapped organic-soil extent is a primary determinant of disturbed area and emissions, we interpret this baseline as a spatially explicit monitoring estimate rather than as a definitive global total. In the baseline configuration, disturbed organic soils emitted about 2.6 Gt CO 2 e yr − 1 (2.5–2.7 Gt CO 2 e yr − 1 across five inventory periods), with roughly three-quarters from drainage and one-quarter from fires. Emissions are heavily concentrated in a few countries and land uses, led by Indonesia and Russia, with the tropics contributing the largest share. The leading drained land-use sources are settlement/built-up pixels, oil palm, and forest inferred as drained from nearby infrastructure, followed by cropland on organic soils. For 2021–2024, alternative extent products yield 2.6–3.3 Gt CO 2 e yr − 1 , and jointly varying the classification threshold and Tier 1 emission factors—the two dominant sources of tested variation—spans an overall scenario envelope of approximately 0.7–4.5 Gt CO 2 e yr − 1 . These estimates should be read not as a correction to existing peatland-specific estimates but as complementary, more comprehensive monitoring of disturbed organic-soil systems under a harmonized, globally consistent framework. The resulting 30 m maps of organic-soil state, disturbance, and emissions show how multi-temporal Earth observation can be combined with GHG inventory methods to identify high-emitting hotspots and support inventories, nationally determined contributions, and peatland conservation and restoration planning.

title: A million data centre satellites will usher in a new era of space pollution
summary: The SpaceX filing for authorization to launch a million satellites to operate orbital data centres lacks details needed to evaluate the environmental risk posed by pollutant emissions from massive upscaling of launches and re-entries. First
content: The SpaceX filing for authorization to launch a million satellites to operate orbital data centres lacks details needed to evaluate the environmental risk posed by pollutant emissions from massive upscaling of launches and re-entries. First-order estimates of total launch emissions of all byproducts and of re-entry nitrogen oxides (NOx) suggest increases of 70- to 150-fold relative to contemporary emissions. An even greater 200- to 280-fold increase in re-entry mass is determined, but associated ablation emissions dominated by metals cannot be deduced, as even broad material composition of satellites is absent. Re-entry NOx from reusable and single-use objects is at least 6 times more than the natural meteoritic influx. At the launchpad, NOx emissions surpass other Earth-bound US sources subject to emissions controls, and methane venting rates rival large US oil and gas extraction basins. The unprecedented increase in anthropogenic chemicals stands to modify stratospheric aerosols, deplete ozone, alter climate, perturb mesospheric nitrogen, and degrade air quality. These risks should incite regulators to demand provision of information needed to calculate emissions and enable environmental impact assessments. Our estimates show that, at a minimum, information should include rocket specifications (propellant type, payload capacity, reusability, re-entry masses, heat shield material and percent ablated), satellite details (composition, mass, re-entry rates), and propulsion technology (fuel, usage rates). Greater knowledge of environmental harm resulting from impact assessments would steer research investment to address scientific gaps and spur technological innovation for more sustainable space operations.

title: Assessing European Road Transport Emissions and Mitigation Scenarios
summary: Abstract Road transport accounts for a large proportion of Europe’s air pollutant and greenhouse gas emissions. As EU policy increasingly targets the sector through drivetrain subsidies, emission regulations, and behavioural incentives, und
content: Abstract Road transport accounts for a large proportion of Europe’s air pollutant and greenhouse gas emissions. As EU policy increasingly targets the sector through drivetrain subsidies, emission regulations, and behavioural incentives, understanding the effects of these measures becomes essential. This study quantifies European road transport emissions and evaluates the effectiveness of mitigation pathways, including metrics for the emissions’ impact on climate and air quality. We present an integrated model chain combining a European travel demand model, a vehicle technology diffusion model, and a climate impact model. This framework allows for the simulation of a range of policy and technology scenarios, assessing both direct and systemic impacts on travel behaviour and emissions. By comparing technological solutions (e.g., electrification) and behavioural changes (e.g., modal shifts), it is possible to explore their relative and combined effects on long-term climate outcomes. The presented model chain is part of the larger service “Application Suite Emissions”, which also includes global and city-level applications. The results provide insights into how policy choices influence emissions and their climate impact, supporting decision-makers in designing effective and equitable transport decarbonization strategies.

title: Solvent-mediated synthesis and catalytic performance of oxalate gel-derived CuO/ZnO/Al2O3 catalysts for hydrogen production via methanol steam reforming
summary: Abstract The influence of solvent engineering during oxalate gel co-precipitation on the physicochemical properties and catalytic performance of CuO/ZnO/Al₂O₃ (CZA) catalysts for methanol steam reforming was systematically investigated. Cat
content: Abstract The influence of solvent engineering during oxalate gel co-precipitation on the physicochemical properties and catalytic performance of CuO/ZnO/Al₂O₃ (CZA) catalysts for methanol steam reforming was systematically investigated. Catalysts were synthesized using ethanol, ethylene glycol, diethylene glycol (DEG), triethylene glycol, and propylene glycol, followed by characterization using XRD, FESEM, EDX-mapping, FTIR, and BET analyses. Solvent selection markedly affected catalyst microstructure, phase dispersion, morphology, and specific surface area. Among the prepared catalysts, the DEG-derived sample exhibited the smallest CuO crystallites, the highest specific surface area, and the most homogeneous morphology, resulting in superior catalytic performance. It achieved approximately 51% methanol conversion at 160 °C and nearly complete conversion above 220 °C, while maintaining CO selectivity below 1.5% up to 300 °C and excellent stability over 24 h. These findings demonstrate that solvent engineering provides a simple and effective strategy for optimizing Cu-based catalysts for efficient hydrogen production via methanol steam reforming.

title: Towards Nature-Positive Transport: Embedding Biodiversity and Societal Considerations in Railways Infrastructure Planning and Policy
summary: Abstract The rail sector, with its capacity to drive intermodal integration, is well-positioned to lead the transition toward scalable and sustainable transport solutions across Europe in connection with other transport modes and sectors. D
content: Abstract The rail sector, with its capacity to drive intermodal integration, is well-positioned to lead the transition toward scalable and sustainable transport solutions across Europe in connection with other transport modes and sectors. Despite broad recognition of the importance of biodiversity-sensitive infrastructure in national and international frameworks, implementation remains limited [3]. Key barriers include fragmented regulatory frameworks, insufficient cross-sectoral coordination, and the inadequate incorporation of biodiversity considerations into infrastructure planning, construction and operation as highlighted by initiatives such as the BISON project. In response, this study—conducted within the EU-Rail SYMBIOSIS project—analyses the societal impacts, regulatory challenges, and interdependencies between rail and energy infrastructure in relation to biodiversity and climate objectives. Using a robust methodology based on literature review and stakeholder consultation, an inclusive framework is being developed to improve environmental and cumulative impact assessments and enhance environmental evaluation procedures across the infrastructure life cycle. The work also examines the alignment of EU policies with international environmental goals and investigates the consequences of the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive on biodiversity matters’ governance and accountability. Evidence-based recommendations are formulated to integrate biodiversity and climate priorities into procurement practices and regulatory mechanisms. The outcomes aim to support a more resilient, integrated, environmentally and socially responsible approach to transport infrastructure planning and implementation across Europe.

title: X‐Ray CT Analysis of Soil Pore Structure, Connectivity and Hydraulic Responses to Micro‐Nanobubble Aerated Drip Irrigation
summary: ABSTRACT Soil pore network architecture is fundamental to rhizosphere functioning. This study employed high‐resolution X‐ray computed tomography (CT) to quantify rhizosphere pore structure, spatial distribution, connectivity and hydraulic f
content: ABSTRACT Soil pore network architecture is fundamental to rhizosphere functioning. This study employed high‐resolution X‐ray computed tomography (CT) to quantify rhizosphere pore structure, spatial distribution, connectivity and hydraulic function in greenhouse tomato across two consecutive growing seasons (S1 and S2) under five micro‐nanobubble (MNB) aeration scheduling treatments: nonaerated control (CK), early aeration (AE), reproductive aeration (AR), late aeration (AL) and continuous aeration (AC). CT‐derived parameters included void ratio, pore morphology, nearest neighbour index (NNI), fractal dimension, absolute permeability and pore‐throat characteristics. AC produced the greatest improvements in the void ratio and pore area across both seasons. AR recorded the highest pore count in Season 1 (1.45 × 10 5 ) and NNI in Season 2 (6.9), indicating concentrated root–bubble interactions during peak oxygen demand. At the end of S1 and S2, the absolute permeability under AC was 8.6 and 18.9 μm 2 , respectively, compared with 4.3 and 0.7 μm 2 under CK. Because CT sampling was destructive and different soil blocks were collected at the end of each season, these values represent season‐specific cross‐sectional contrasts rather than longitudinal changes in the same soil core. Overall, growth‐stage MNB aeration was associated with distinct end‐of‐season rhizosphere pore‐network characteristics, supporting precision oxygen management in greenhouse SDI systems.

title: Policy Options to Reduce Emissions of L-Category Vehicles in the European Union and Expected Effects
summary: Abstract L-category vehicles, including mopeds, motorcycles, quadricycles, and all-terrain vehicles, represent a significant pollution source, particularly in urban areas. This study assesses the effectiveness of the following mitigation me
content: Abstract L-category vehicles, including mopeds, motorcycles, quadricycles, and all-terrain vehicles, represent a significant pollution source, particularly in urban areas. This study assesses the effectiveness of the following mitigation measures – introduction of Real Driving Emissions (RDE) testing, adoption of stricter World Motorcycle Test Cycle (WMTC) limits, enforcement of anti-tampering provisions, changes in the driving behavior, and acceleration of the fleet replacement. All of them are compared in parallel into two distinct baseline scenarios, a high and low electrification for the period 2025–2050, to quantify environmental benefits and support evidence-based policy decisions for L-category vehicles. The policies were simulated using fleet emission projection models and the assessment was based on existing and updated emission factors derived from emissions data collected through laboratory emission tests, on-road measurements and roadside tests. Results show that the introduction of RDE testing achieves the most substantial reductions in NOx and CO emissions, with declines exceeding 17% by 2050 compared to the baseline scenario, highlighting the significance of decreasing the gap between laboratory and real-world performance. The accelerated fleet replacement has its highest impact on HC emissions, whereas in other air pollutants, it shows significant impact as well. The remaining measures achieve consistent improvements across all pollutants.

title: Adapting Road Transport Decarbonization Strategies: A Comparative Study Between Spain, Norway, and the United Kingdom
summary: Abstract Transport is the second largest emitter of CO2, responsible for 23.8% of total emissions in Europe. Yet decarbonization in transport is progressing more slowly than in other sectors. This highlights the challenge of decarbonizing a
content: Abstract Transport is the second largest emitter of CO2, responsible for 23.8% of total emissions in Europe. Yet decarbonization in transport is progressing more slowly than in other sectors. This highlights the challenge of decarbonizing a sector deeply linked to economic growth, where options are constrained. Meeting the challenges requires more than high-level models and demands instead concrete, context-specific policy evaluations to meet the objectives of the Paris Agreement. This paper assesses how Norway, Spain, and the United Kingdom design and implement decarbonization pathways in road transport, with a focus on alternative fuel (AF) deployment for buses, light-duty vehicles (LDVs), and heavy-duty vehicles. Drawing on national policy reviews, Path2Zero project data, and an Ambition-Achievement framework, we compare policy targets with current fleet data to identify gaps and takeaways. Results show that Norway leads in both policy ambition and adoption, particularly its AF LDV share (30.4%), which is more than ten times Spain’s (2.2%), while the UK shows strong regulatory ambition but uneven results. Long-standing fiscal consistency, rather than regulatory targets alone, explains Norway’s leadership. These findings can be useful for policymakers and companies working toward transport decarbonization by 2050.

title: FOOD SAFETY, FOOD LOSS AND SUSTAINABLE CONSUMPTION: ADVANCING SDGS 2, 3 AND 12
source: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
summary: Food safety, food loss and waste, and sustainable consumption are interconnected challenges affecting global food security, public health and environmental sustainability. While food loss and waste reduce the quantity of food available for
content: Food safety, food loss and waste, and sustainable consumption are interconnected challenges affecting global food security, public health and environmental sustainability. While food loss and waste reduce the quantity of food available for human consumption and contribute to greenhouse gas emissions, unsafe food causes preventable illness, death and economic losses. This article examines the relationship among these issues through the lens of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2 (Zero Hunger), 3 (Good Health and Well-being) and 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). It adopts a descriptive and analytical research design based on secondary data from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), World Health Organization (WHO), United Nations Sustainable Development Goals reporting and the joint United Nations report The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World. The evidence indicates that approximately 13.3% of food was lost globally after harvest and before retail in 2023, while an estimated 1.05 billion tonnes of food were wasted at retail, food-service and household levels in 2022. Meanwhile, WHO’s 2026 estimates indicate that contaminated food caused approximately 866 million illnesses and 1.52 million deaths in 2021. These figures demonstrate the scale of food-system inefficiencies and foodborne disease, although they measure distinct phenomena and cannot establish a direct causal relationship between food waste and foodborne illness. The article argues that food-loss reduction must be accompanied by effective food-safety controls, appropriate storage and transport infrastructure, transparent supply chains, consumer awareness and evidence-based redistribution systems. It proposes an integrated food-systems approach that combines prevention, safety assurance, responsible consumption and accountable governance to support progress towards SDGs 2, 3 and 12.

title: Influence of Laser Beam Orientation on Weld Morphology, Microstructure, and Mechanical Performance of Similar and Dissimilar Dual-Phase Steels: A Comprehensive Review
summary: Abstract This review encompasses a comprehensive evaluation of the findings from various experimental works and computational data on welding dual-phase steel in similar and dissimilar configuration. It concentrates on the effect of the ori
content: Abstract This review encompasses a comprehensive evaluation of the findings from various experimental works and computational data on welding dual-phase steel in similar and dissimilar configuration. It concentrates on the effect of the orientation of laser beam on geometrical features of the weld joint, microstructure, defect occurrence, and mechanical behavior of dual-phase steel. These steels, characterised by a ferritic matrix with islands of martensite, are among the most preferred Advanced High-Strength Steels due to their exceptional strength, formability, and crashworthiness. The automotive industry uses laser-based processing for dual-phase (DP) steels because of their high precision, adaptability, and suitability for lightweight design specifications. Laser incidence angle is considered as crucial factors for establishing melting pool dynamics, penetration depth, heat input and, stress field, joint strength and hardness uniformity, and fatigue lifetime. Experimental investigations prove the efficiency of the application of tilting angle in the range of 5° to 15° degrees in achieving successful results in balancing welding with the lowest number of defects. Numerical techniques, help in acquiring thermal cycle, key hole stability, and phase transformation kinetics data. This study aims to highlights some of the unresolved research areas, industrial applications, and future prospects of laser beam orientation adaptation.

title: Operationalizing Climate Change Adaptation Literacy through Framework Development and National Population Evidence from Taiwan
summary: Abstract Climate change adaptation requires citizens to understand risks, navigate public institutions, and engage with feasible responses. We developed a climate change adaptation literacy framework comprising four domains and 16 subdimens
content: Abstract Climate change adaptation requires citizens to understand risks, navigate public institutions, and engage with feasible responses. We developed a climate change adaptation literacy framework comprising four domains and 16 subdimensions through literature synthesis, expert consultation, and pilot testing. A weighted national telephone survey assessed 2,527 adults in Taiwan in 2025. Only 11% correctly rejected a statement equating adaptation with emissions reduction, and 22% recognized the need to adjust policy for specific groups. Support for adaptation was high, while reported engagement with local resources and civic action was lower. Adjusted analyses showed higher conceptual and policy knowledge among respondents with more education. Younger adults had higher knowledge scores, and older groups reported more adaptive practice. These findings highlight priorities for clarifying concepts, differentiated protection, accessible local services, and practical participation. The framework provides a national baseline for evaluating communication and education on adaptation.

title: A reproducible factorial screening framework for energy and operational-carbon attribution in battery-electric underground mines
summary: Underground-mine electrification alters traction demand and ventilation requirements for diesel exhaust and heat, yet sequential reporting prevents consistent attribution. This study presents a reproducible 2 3 factorial screening framework
content: Underground-mine electrification alters traction demand and ventilation requirements for diesel exhaust and heat, yet sequential reporting prevents consistent attribution. This study presents a reproducible 2 3 factorial screening framework separating the effects of fleet type, ventilation control and operational coordination on annual final energy, operational greenhouse-gas emissions and purchased-energy expenditure. Eight deterministic scenarios represent an illustrative 1.20 Mt y −1 mine. Direct diesel and location-based electricity emissions were combined at a reference grid factor of 0.20 t CO 2 e MWh −1 . Compared with the diesel, fixed-ventilation, conventional-dispatch reference (18,767 MWh y −1 ; 4,488 t CO 2 e y −1 ), the battery-electric, dynamic-ventilation, coordinated case required 4,061 MWh y −1 and emitted 812 t CO 2 e y −1 , reductions of 78.4% and 81.9%. Mean final-energy effects were − 8,974 MWh y −1 for electrification, −5,268 for dynamic ventilation and − 494 for coordination; the fleet–ventilation interaction was − 735. A corrected like-for-like sensitivity applied the same grid factor to all scenarios and found no operational-carbon crossover over 0–0.80 t CO 2 e MWh −1 . At illustrative prices, expenditure fell 79.5%, excluding capital and production effects. The framework supports transparent screening; investment and safety decisions require site metering, ventilation-network verification and productivity validation.

title: Soil Moisture as a Key Regulator of Organic Carbon Stabilisation and CO2 Fluxes Across Agroecosystems: A Systematic Review
summary: Soil moisture plays a critical role in soil organic carbon (SOC) storage and stabilisation and carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions amid climatic variability and in different agroecosystems. However, the mechanisms that regulate organic matter de
content: Soil moisture plays a critical role in soil organic carbon (SOC) storage and stabilisation and carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions amid climatic variability and in different agroecosystems. However, the mechanisms that regulate organic matter decomposition, microbial activities, and root respiration with direct impacts on carbon (C) cycling remain incompletely synthesised. This review synthesises evidence showing how soil moisture regulates SOC stabilisation and CO2 fluxes, particulate organic C (POC) and mineral-associated organic C (MAOC) response and the role of rare microbes under drought. Findings from 87 peer-reviewed studies from Web of Science and Scopus between 2007 and 2026 confirm that soil moisture is a key regulator of C circulation. Additionally, moderate soil moisture of a 60–70% water-holding capacity (WHC) enhances SOC stocks and CO2 efflux peaks due to increased microbial activities and respiration. Extreme drying and rewetting cycles in rainfed soils trigger drastic CO2 emission pulses. However, under drought conditions, rare microbes can be utilised (for rhizosphere modification) to improve microbial biomass C (MBC), necromass C and MAOC formation, thereby enhancing sustainable agricultural production. This study confirms that CO2 efflux and SOC stabilisation primarily rely on soil moisture dynamics. Therefore, sustainable moisture conservation practices improve moisture retention and SOC stabilisation and reduce CO2 emissions, offering a viable pathway for mitigating the impacts of climate change footprints.

title: Promoting Sustainable Development in Nigeria through Deployment of Renewable Energy: an Analysis of the Legal Framework
summary: Renewable energy is an important pathway to promoting sustainable development in Nigeria through improved energy access, environmental protection, energy security and economic growth. Despite Nigeria abundant renewable energy resources, the
content: Renewable energy is an important pathway to promoting sustainable development in Nigeria through improved energy access, environmental protection, energy security and economic growth. Despite Nigeria abundant renewable energy resources, their deployment remains limited by legal, regulatory, and institutional challenges. This study examines the Nigerian legal framework governing renewable energy deployment and its effectiveness in promoting sustainable development. The study adopts a doctrinal methodology, analysing relevant constitutional provisions, statutes, government policies, regulatory guidelines, international instruments, case law, textbooks, journal articles, and comparative legal materials. The findings reveal that Nigeria’s existing legal framework, particularly, the Electricity Act 2023(as amended) provides a foundation for renewable energy deployment. However, the frameworks, especially the policies remain inadequate due to fragmented policies, overlapping institutional mandates, weak enforcement mechanism, insufficient fiscal incentives, and the absence of a clear, binding renewable energy targets. The study recommends the enactment of a comprehensive renewable energy Act to harmonise existing laws and policies, establish enforceable renewable energy target, clarify institutional responsibilities, strengthen regulatory oversight, and provide appropriate financial incentives. The study concludes that effective renewable energy deployment is essential to promoting sustainable development in Nigeria and requires comprehensive legal reform, and effective implementation and enforcement.

title: Alternative Fuels for Decarbonising Freight Transport: A System Dynamics Approach
summary: Abstract This system dynamics (SD) model evaluates the adoption of hydrogen, biofuels, and synthetic e-fuels to decarbonise freight transport across global corridors, supporting global climate-neutral goals. The model integrates quantitativ
content: Abstract This system dynamics (SD) model evaluates the adoption of hydrogen, biofuels, and synthetic e-fuels to decarbonise freight transport across global corridors, supporting global climate-neutral goals. The model integrates quantitative data from international freight pilots and global datasets (e.g., IEA, IRENA) with qualitative insights from stakeholders, including fleet operators, policymakers, and researchers. It simulates fuel adoption scenarios under varying policy, infrastructure, and market conditions, focusing on vehicle fleet, energy efficiency, carbon emissions reductions, and circular economy principles (e.g., biofuel production from organic waste). Key outputs include optimal policy levers (e.g., subsidies, carbon pricing) identified through sensitivity analysis and potential emission reductions of 30% by 2035 with targeted investments. The model provides a scalable decision-support tool for policymakers and industry, addressing barriers to alternative fuel adoption.

title: A critical systematic insight into alternate wetting and drying irrigation for a sustainable solution in paddy fields
summary: Growing global food demand amid dwindling water resources and climate change has shifted traditional rice cultivation systems to sustainable alternatives. Among these, alternate wetting and drying (AWD) irrigation has sustained prominent po
content: Growing global food demand amid dwindling water resources and climate change has shifted traditional rice cultivation systems to sustainable alternatives. Among these, alternate wetting and drying (AWD) irrigation has sustained prominent potential for environmental mitigation, water and agricultural productivity. This comprehensive systematic review integrates 463 peer‑reviewed studies (2004–2024), using a multi‑tool bibliometric and text‑mining framework to unravel two decades of scientific progress, dominant research trajectories, and persistent uncertainties surrounding AWD adoption. Keyword evolution, clustering, and topic modeling reveal a decisive shift from early investigations on soil aeration and aerobic rice toward contemporary emphases on water productivity, greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation, nutrient-use efficiency, and yield stability. Meta‑analysis of these modeled sustainability themes demonstrated that AWD significantly enhances water productivity (+0.18 ± 0.04 kg grain m −3 , P < 0.0001) while maintaining statistically comparable grain yields to continuous flooding (CF), despite substantial heterogeneity driven by soil type, drying intensity, cultivar choice, and nutrient management. AWD consistently reduces CH 4 emissions (-199.21 kg CH 4 ha −1 , P < 0.002) and lowers net global warming potential (-4.14 t CO 2 -eq ha −1 , P < 0.0002), but N 2 O responded a non-significant substantial contextual variability. However, AWD contextual synergies with zeolite, biochar, optimized N placement, and drought‑tolerant cultivars resulted in yield amplification, nutrient recovery, and GHG mitigation. Adoption caveats include labor-intensive monitoring and irrigation infrastructure requirements, socio-economic barriers, and geographic concentration of research in Asian regions. These gaps warrant regional‑specific AWD intensity calibration and decision-support tools development that account for local hydrological, climatic, and socio-economic realities.

title: Increased soil organic carbon in organically managed croplands: Evidence from on-farm monitoring in Bavaria (Germany)
summary: Organic farming is widely associated with environmental benefits and is commonly assumed to promote soil organic carbon (SOC). However, it remains unclear to what extent organic farming leads to higher SOC contents under practical farming c
content: Organic farming is widely associated with environmental benefits and is commonly assumed to promote soil organic carbon (SOC). However, it remains unclear to what extent organic farming leads to higher SOC contents under practical farming conditions. This study compares SOC contents and their temporal changes in organically and conventionally managed arable soils across Bavaria using data from the Bavarian Soil Organic Matter Monitoring Program. The dataset comprises 198 conventionally and 65 organically managed sites, all representing practical farming conditions, with repeated soil sampling after a ten-year period (initial sampling: 2001/2008; resampling: 2011/2018). SOC at resampling tended to be higher under organic management. A higher proportion of perennial grass-clover leys and other perennial forage crops and a lower share of root crops in organic crop rotations were identified as key drivers of SOC, which are intrinsic to organic agriculture but can be applied in any management system. Across all sites, SOC showed a non-significant decline of 0.74 % (16.19 to 16.07 g kg −1 ), while total nitrogen (Nt) increased significantly by 3.13 % (1.60 to 1.65 g kg −1 ). Organically managed sites exhibited a slight mean increase in SOC (+0.73 %), whereas conventionally managed sites showed a mean decrease (−1.14 %). Temporal SOC changes were further influenced by soil texture, with clay-rich soils showing slightly stronger declines or weaker increases. The increase in Nt, combined with contrasting SOC trends, resulted in a significant narrowing of the C:N-ratio across all sites (10.16 to 9.74; −4.13 %). The decline was stronger under conventional (10.14 to 9.69; −4.44 %) than organic management (10.22 to 9.95; −2.64 %). This shift may enhance SOC mineralization and increase the risk of future SOC losses. These findings highlight that results from experimental systems may not fully translate to practical farming conditions and underline the importance of long-term monitoring to develop effective, practice-oriented management strategies for maintaining or enhancing SOC stocks.

title: Value-based principles in sustainability reporting
summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles have become a dominant framework for evaluating corporate sustainability. However, despite the widespread adoption of ESG, issues such as greenwashing, inconsistent accountability, pers
content: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles have become a dominant framework for evaluating corporate sustainability. However, despite the widespread adoption of ESG, issues such as greenwashing, inconsistent accountability, persistent social and environmental injustices, and low trust remain unresolved. To address these gaps, this conceptual paper introduces a value-based ESG framework (V-ESG), which integrates 10 values—stewardship, accountability, leadership, transformation, compassion, justice, community wellbeing, integrity, trust and interconnectedness into ESG reporting. Through a multi-stakeholder engagement, we gathered diverse perspectives from selected participants from various sectors, including finance, energy, academia, policy, and social development to enhance the understanding process of this new reporting approach. An identification of recurring stakeholder perspectives and themes was conducted to prioritize core values, which were then mapped onto the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals to ensure alignment with global sustainability reporting framework. Additionally, a literature review reinforced the selection of values and development of measurement indicators for V-ESG implementation. The conceptual contribution suggests that values-driven sustainability may strengthen long-term institutional trust, corporate responsibility, and community impact. The framework could enhance traditional ESG by embedding ethical leadership, social justice, and governance transparency into sustainability strategies. By promoting a holistic, resilient, and adaptive approach, V-ESG could offer a robust alternative to traditional ESG, ensuring that businesses and investment practices not only comply with regulatory standards but also uphold ethical imperatives for a just and sustainable future. There is also a need to develop capacity of leaders and corporate teams in enhancing awareness and capability on V-ESG as a measurement tool for voluntary certification.

title: Transient polymer nanocomposites with programmable functions for zero-residue and self-regulating food applications
summary: The next generation of sustainable food materials must move beyond passive biodegradability toward systems that actively control their function, lifespan, and environmental fate. This review introduces the emerging concept of transient and
content: The next generation of sustainable food materials must move beyond passive biodegradability toward systems that actively control their function, lifespan, and environmental fate. This review introduces the emerging concept of transient and programmable polymer nanocomposites, a transformative class of materials designed to perform specific food-related functions, adapt to changing conditions, and subsequently disassemble into benign, zero-residue products. Unlike conventional biodegradable nanocomposites that degrade through uncontrolled environmental processes, transient systems enable triggerable and time-defined disintegration, providing precise control over material persistence and nanoparticle release. Similarly, the ability to modify material properties in response to stimuli can be extended to include feedback-driven control of antimicrobial, barrier, or antioxidant properties. The review provides an integrated perspective of the interaction between nano-polymer, function, degradation, and lifecycle sustainability. New materials are reviewed that include sustainable polymer, transient degradation chemistry, nano-enabled sensing, self-regulating release systems, and intelligent packaging. Special attention is paid to balancing function with safety, as well as circular economy. The future directions for these materials are the use of artificial intelligence as a tool, closed-loop packaging, and permanently floating nanocomposites are also explored. Through the introduction of the term "function-response-disappearance", we are addressing a gap in the literature on food nanotechnology, while describing a roadmap for safe, adaptive and zero-waste materials that can aid resilient and sustainable food systems.

title: Effect of MgO nanoparticle concentration on the engine performance, combustion, emissions, and tribological characteristics of dual-biodiesel–n-butanol blends
summary: Abstract This study investigates the effects of 5% n-butanol and green-synthesized MgO nanoparticles on the engine performance, combustion, emission, and tribological characteristics of dual-biodiesel-based fuel blends. MgO nanoparticles we
content: Abstract This study investigates the effects of 5% n-butanol and green-synthesized MgO nanoparticles on the engine performance, combustion, emission, and tribological characteristics of dual-biodiesel-based fuel blends. MgO nanoparticles were synthesized using guava leaf extract and characterized by SEM, TEM, FTIR, and XRD, confirming a flake-like morphology with particle sizes below 50 nm. The tested fuels included D100, A10PJ10D80, A10PJ10D75B5, and MgO-containing blends at 30, 60, and 90 ppm. Engine experiments were performed under different load conditions, while friction and wear behaviour were evaluated using a four-ball tribometer and SEM analysis. At full load, 5% n-butanol reduced BSFC from 0.328 to 0.322 kg/kWh and increased BTE from 30.4% to 30.5%, with concurrent reductions in CO, HC, and smoke opacity. Increasing MgO concentration further improved engine characteristics, with 90 ppm MgO achieving a BSFC of 0.305 kg/kWh and BTE of 32.4%, while CO, HC, and smoke opacity decreased to 0.0561%, 39.2 ppm, and 44.2 HSU, respectively. However, NO X increased from 910 to 975 ppm, indicating a trade-off associated with enhanced combustion intensity. Peak in-cylinder pressure and HRR increased to 70.9 bar and 39.4 J/deg, respectively. The optimum tribological response occurred at 60 ppm MgO, with COF and WSD decreasing to 0.0795 and 0.458 mm, corresponding to reductions of 14.97% and 18.94% relative to D100.

title: Leveraging the Business Canvas Modell for the Hungarian Biomethane Industry
summary: Abstract The global biogas and biomethane sectors are experiencing significant growth, driven by rising environmental concerns, international decarbonisation goals, and the broader transition to renewable energy sources. These developments
content: Abstract The global biogas and biomethane sectors are experiencing significant growth, driven by rising environmental concerns, international decarbonisation goals, and the broader transition to renewable energy sources. These developments have positioned these subsectors of the alternative fuel industry as the targets of strategic investment opportunities for multinational companies pursuing sustainable business models. Our paper seeks to identify and assess some of the critical factors that influence successful entry into the biogas and biomethane production markets, using the Business Model Canvas (BMC) as an analytical framework. Through a comprehensive, multidimensional approach, our research explores key partners, core activities, customer segments and value proposition characteristics of the application of BMC in the transport sector. Special emphasis is placed on aligning company capabilities with national energy strategies, including potential partnerships, and economic feasibility of the alternative fuel projects. Our study’s findings contribute to the growing number of publications on sustainable business strategies and the dynamics of renewable energy markets of alternative fuels. Furthermore, our research provides practical insights for industry practitioners, innovators, and policymakers involved in strategic decision-making within the biofuel sector. By leveraging the BMC model, this study offers the Hungarian use case for the rapidly evolving biogas and biomethane production industry.

title: Optimising Logistics for a Sustainable Hydrogen Economy: The DTI4HydroChains Framework
summary: Abstract Logistics is the strategic backbone of a scalable hydrogen economy. It links renewable resources, industrial clusters and export corridors while determining cost, reliability and investment feasibility. This paper introduces DTI4Hy
content: Abstract Logistics is the strategic backbone of a scalable hydrogen economy. It links renewable resources, industrial clusters and export corridors while determining cost, reliability and investment feasibility. This paper introduces DTI4HydroChains, a modular decision support framework that integrates techno-economic optimisation, scenario analysis and risk assessment to guide phased, multi-product infrastructure development. The framework is applied to a Finland-wide case study, informed by several months of exploratory research involving companies, technology developers and public sector actors. The analysis focuses on three near term value chains with strong market pull, biogenic CO 2 , e-methane and e-SAF, and examines how their logistics requirements shape feasible siting, transport and export configurations. Results highlight that (i) biogenic CO 2 aggregation is a central constraint on synthetic fuel scale up, (ii) early export ready infrastructure is essential given limited domestic demand, and (iii) flexible, multi-product assets reduce lock in risks under uncertain market development. The study provides actionable policy insights and discusses the transferability of the framework to other national contexts.

title: Global 0.1° Monthly Anthropogenic CO₂ Emissions Dataset with Near-Real-Time Updates
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset provides global monthly anthropogenic CO₂ emission estimates at a spatial resolution of 0.1° × 0.1°, with the latest update extending through September 2026. The dataset is designed to provide a valuable resource for assessing
content: This dataset provides global monthly anthropogenic CO₂ emission estimates at a spatial resolution of 0.1° × 0.1°, with the latest update extending through September 2026. The dataset is designed to provide a valuable resource for assessing the global carbon budget and the effectiveness of climate mitigation efforts. The estimates are generated using a deep learning–based framework that employs a convolutional neural network as its backbone and incorporates a mask fusion module to address spatially missing input data. The framework integrates satellite observations, meteorological reanalysis data, and temporal and spatial encoding features to estimate anthropogenic CO₂ emissions at a global scale. The data are provided in NetCDF format on a global 0.1° × 0.1° grid (1800 × 3600 cells) using the WGS84 geographic coordinate system. Each file contains monthly anthropogenic CO₂ emission estimates for all 12 months of a given year, expressed in tonnes month⁻¹ cell⁻¹. Files follow the naming convention ACO2_01deg_YYYY.nc, where YYYY denotes the corresponding year. The dataset is also updated regularly at doi: 10.12237/casearth.6a01788fe8a21d1686165027 A manuscript describing the methodology and dataset is in preparation.

title: Cymbopogon citrates a Biodegradable waste-derived biodiesel as a potential green fuel: Process Extraction and Utilization in Agricultural Diesel Engine
summary: This study investigates the use of two specific alcohols, octanol and deconal, alongside diesel and biodiesel derived from Cymbopogon citratus. Two ternary blends, labeled as D50-CC30-OCT20 and D50-CC30-DEC20, were formulated and analyzed t
content: This study investigates the use of two specific alcohols, octanol and deconal, alongside diesel and biodiesel derived from Cymbopogon citratus. Two ternary blends, labeled as D50-CC30-OCT20 and D50-CC30-DEC20, were formulated and analyzed to assess their engine performance compared to the D50-CC50 blend, pure diesel operation. Results indicate a decrease in peak cylinder pressure with the use of ternary blends. The maximum rate of heat release was observed to be higher in the octanol-containing blend. Furthermore, the deconal blend exhibited a 2.5% improvement in brake thermal efficiency (BTE) compared to octanol yet remained 3.5% lower than traditional diesel operation. Notably, the NOx emissions of the deconal blend were 4% lower compared to octanol. Overall, higher alcohol blends led to reduced smoke emissions compared to binary blends. Octanol, specifically, showed a 15% decrease in smoke opacity. However, the emissions of hydrocarbons (HC) and carbon monoxide (CO) increased with the use of greater alcohol blends. This research underscores the potential of 1-deconal as a viable fuel option for diesel engines running on biodiesel derived from Cymbopogon citratus oil sourced from biomass.

title: Economic and Reliability Assessment of Hybrid EV Charging Systems using Improved Coot Bird Optimisation on IEEE-33 Bus System
summary: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are crucial to the transition to sustainable transportation on a global scale due to their near-zero emissions and their ability to mitigate noise pollution. However, widespread adoption of EVs is hindered by the les
content: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are crucial to the transition to sustainable transportation on a global scale due to their near-zero emissions and their ability to mitigate noise pollution. However, widespread adoption of EVs is hindered by the less accessible and high cost of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS) for distant areas. This study addresses this issue through the development of a Hybrid Renewable Energy Sources (HRES)-based EVCS system connected to the IEEE 33 bus radial distribution network. The system incorporates a Renewable Energy System including Photovoltaic (PV) and Wind Turbine (WT), to decrease the cost of EV charging based on the renewable energy availability, and improve energy sustainability. To develop an optimized design and efficient hybrid system, this research introduces an Improved Coot Bird Optimization Algorithm (ICBOA). This improved metaheuristic algorithm quickly produces the best sizing and location for RES based on calculations intended to balance cost and reliability objectives. The reliability of the system is tested using standard reliability indices, which ensure some measure of operational stability and reliability in the energy provided. The simulation outcomes demonstrate that the proposed method has adequately reduced charging costs, improved overall reliability, and aided in achieving sustainability goals.

title: Paris in Strasbourg? The Role of International Environmental Law in the European Court of Human Rights’ Climate Change Jurisprudence
source: The European Convention on Human Rights Law Review
summary: Abstract This article analyses the European Court of Human Rights’ (ECtHR or the Court) approach to international environmental instruments in its first climate change cases, specifically in Verein KlimaSeniorinnen Schweiz and Others v Swit
content: Abstract This article analyses the European Court of Human Rights’ (ECtHR or the Court) approach to international environmental instruments in its first climate change cases, specifically in Verein KlimaSeniorinnen Schweiz and Others v Switzerland . It focuses on the ECtHR’s use of systemic integration and its living instrument doctrine to incorporate international environmental instruments, including the Paris Agreement, Aarhus Convention, and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, into its interpretation of the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). While respecting states’ discretion, the ECtHR links standing before the Court with Aarhus Convention criteria, and climate change mitigation obligations to ECHR rights, incorporating the Paris Agreements’ general goals like temperature limitation and greenhouse gas neutrality. However, the Court stops short of directly enforcing equity principles embedded in international environmental law. This article argues that the ECtHR’s balanced approach strengthens ECHR protections against climate harm, without overstepping its mandate into the domain of a quasi-environmental court.

title: Field-derived nitrous oxide emission factors for fertilised smallholder oil palm systems on mineral soils in South-East Asia
summary: Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions from fertilised oil palm (OP) systems remain poorly quantified despite their importance for regional greenhouse gas inventories and life-cycle assessments. This study measured N 2 O emissions following 18 fer
content: Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions from fertilised oil palm (OP) systems remain poorly quantified despite their importance for regional greenhouse gas inventories and life-cycle assessments. This study measured N 2 O emissions following 18 fertiliser application events across 12 smallholder OP farms in Indonesia and Malaysia between 2022 and 2025. Cumulative fertiliser-induced emissions were estimated over a 21-day measurement period and used to derive N 2 O emission factors (EFs) for individual fertilisation events. Individual EFs ranged from 0.01% to 1.43% of applied nitrogen fertiliser (mineral and organic). To place these measurements in a regional context, results were combined with published EFs from OP systems on mineral soils in Southeast Asia (SEA). Using log-normal statistical treatment to account for the highly skewed distribution of EFs, a regional mean EF of 0.82% of applied nitrogen was derived (95% confidence interval: 0.44–1.78%). Sensitivity analyses indicated that regional EF estimates varied according to study inclusion and analytical approach, with mean values ranging from 0.51% to 1.12% of applied nitrogen. While uncertainties remain and the observational study design does not allow the independent effects of site, year, fertiliser type and management to be disentangled, the derived EF is broadly consistent with the IPCC Tier 1 default value of 1% and represents a regional estimate based on the currently available field evidence. These results contribute to a limited empirical dataset for OP systems in SEA and provide a transparent evidence base for greenhouse gas inventories, life-cycle assessments, and future evaluations of mitigation opportunities within the sector.
