title: Trade Globalization and Environmental Sustainability: Sectoral Heterogeneity and Moderation Evidence From OECD Countries
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental degradation, particularly rising CO 2 emissions, has become a prominent global policy concern owing to its threat to climate stability, ecological viability, and long‐term economic prosperity. Social factors such as p
content: ABSTRACT Environmental degradation, particularly rising CO 2 emissions, has become a prominent global policy concern owing to its threat to climate stability, ecological viability, and long‐term economic prosperity. Social factors such as population shifts, income, industrial activity, financial development, and technological dissemination influence CO 2 emissions in addition to globalization. This study utilized an extended STIRPAT framework to analyze trade globalization and CO 2 emissions in 32 OECD economies from 2005 to 2023. FMOLS, DOLS, and panel quantile regression with country‐cluster bootstrap inference complement a country fixed‐effects model with Driscoll‐Kraay standard errors. The study examines the dimensions of globalization, sectoral linkages, and moderations. Trade globalization positively affects emissions in the baseline and both long‐run estimators, but its coefficients are insignificant across conditional quantiles. The share of the working‐age population, industrial value added, and domestic credit to the private sector increase emissions, whereas internet use decreases them. Economic and interpersonal globalization also boosts emissions. Sectoral estimations link industrial value added to higher emissions and service value added to lower emissions. Industry and agriculture boost trade‐emissions, but manufacturing and services weaken it, according to the interaction estimates. These findings emphasize the importance of sectoral mix in trade globalization environmental assessments. They advocate integrating sector‐specific environmental measures, cleaner production, and technology dissemination into trade policy to balance international economic integration with OECD emissions‐reduction objectives.

title: Nutritional values, phytochemical profiles and enteric methane mitigation potential of West African indigenous forage species for sustainable ruminant livestock production systems
summary: Manipulating feed rations with forages containing specific natural phytochemicals that reduce enteric methane emissions is a sustainable strategy for cattle farming. This study aimed to select forages based on their secondary metabolites, n
content: Manipulating feed rations with forages containing specific natural phytochemicals that reduce enteric methane emissions is a sustainable strategy for cattle farming. This study aimed to select forages based on their secondary metabolites, nutritional value and methane production. A total of fifteen forage species identified by cattle farmers were studied. Phytochemical parameters were measured in line with the European Pharmacopoeia method. In vitro fermentation with bovine rumen juice was used to assess digestibility and methane production. Results showed that species with high tannin content: Acacia sieberiana (2.002%), Khaya senegalensis (1.939%) and Detarium microcarpum (1.665%) had the lowest digestibility values of Organic Matter Digestibility (OMD ranging from 30.0 to 47.1%) and metabolizable energy values (1281.6 to 1952.4 kcal/kg DM). These low energy values were also coupled with low methane production (185.0 to 282 mL CH 4 /kg DM). Furthermore, despite their high tannin contents, Anogeissus leiocarpa (4.556%) and Isoberlinia doka (2.486%) recorded good digestibility, good energy values, and moderate methane production. However, species that are poor in tannins and rich in nitrogen, such as Blighia sapida , Leucaena leucocephala , and Faidherbia albida , have high digestibility values (43.1% − 62.8%) and metabolizable energy above 2200 kcal/kg DM. Blighia sapida , in particular, stands out with an exceptional dMO content of 62.8% and an energy value of 2657.6 kcal/kg DM, combined with values of 0.93 UFL and 0.88 UFV. However, this performance resulted in the highest methane production (505 mL CH₄/kg DM). Species with moderate levels of secondary metabolites, such as Piliostigma thonningii , Daniellia oliveri , Combretum collinum , Annona senegalensis and Diospyros mespiliformis , have average digestibility (53.3%) and energy values ranging from 1868.3 to 2206.4 kcal/kgDM. These plants offer a good compromise between digestibility and methane production through the balanced presence of polyphenols and flavonoids. This study definitively demonstrates that the rational management of secondary metabolites in ruminant feed is a promising way to combine zootechnical performance with a more responsible environmental footprint. This research is the first study in Benin that provides data and tables to guide cattle farmers in ecofeed rations formulation.

title: Fe(II) and Cu(II)-Mediated Enhancement of Biogas Yield and BioMethane Content in Cow Dung - Chicken Manure Co-Digestion: A Kinetic Study
summary: Abstract Trace metal supplementation is an exciting, low-cost approach to enhancing anaerobic digestion (AD) performance, yet the concentration-dependent effects of individual metals on co-digestion kinetics and biogas quality has remained
content: Abstract Trace metal supplementation is an exciting, low-cost approach to enhancing anaerobic digestion (AD) performance, yet the concentration-dependent effects of individual metals on co-digestion kinetics and biogas quality has remained incompletely resolved for heterogeneous livestock-waste mixtures. This study investigated the impacts of Fe(II) and Cu(II) supplementation at concentration of 0.02, 0.05, and 0.10 mM as FeSO₄·7H₂O and CuCl₂·2H₂O) on the anaerobic co-digestion of cow dung (CD) and chicken manure (CM) at a 50:50 ratio, in terms of both digestion kinetics and biogas compositional quality over a 50-day hydraulic retention time. Physicochemical characterization of the CD and CM was conducted by standard protocols. The result proved that compositionally, CM was richer than CD in nitrogen, protein, and macro-minerals, whereas CD contributed majorly a carbon-dominant, fibrous fraction. Across all bioreactors, cumulative biogas yield followed a clear biphasic (diauxic) trajectory, which was accurately described by a two-phase logistic model (R² = 0.992–0.999).This pattern reveals sequential use of readily degradable soluble organics, followed by the refractory lignocellulosic materials. Fe(II) displayed a typical hormetic dose - response, and 0.05 mM demonstrated the best performance (29.90 dm³ cumulative biogas, which 21.16% above control; 75.34% CH₄) while 0.10 mM turned out to be inhibitory, with only 23.51 dm³ (with 63.27% CH₄, lower than control). In contrast, Cu(II) produced a monotonically positive response in all the tested range, with 0.10 mM producing the overall highest cumulative yield (30.25 dm³, 22.56% above control) and biomethane content (76.79%), alongside near-complete suppression of sulfurous off-gas, consistent with copper-mediated sulfide precipitation. Furthermore, gas chromatographic analysis revealed a concurrent increase in residual hydrogen under high-dose Cu(II), suggesting possible a partial uncoupling of hydrogenotrophic and acetoclastic methanogenic pathways. These findings demonstrate that micro-dosing of Fe(II) (0.05 mM) or Cu(II) (0.10 mM) can enhance both the yield and quality of biogas substantially from CD/CM co-digestion, while highlighting that effective trace-metal concentrations are strongly substrate- and matrix-dependent, underscoring the value of two-phase kinetic modelling for optimizing metal-amended anaerobic digestion systems.

title: Multifaceted dynamics of health expenditure in the European Union: macroeconomic, environmental, social and medical determinants
summary: This study explores the impact of a multidimensional mix of factors—macroeconomic, environmental, social and medical on the annual variation of the current health expenditure as a share of GDP of the European Union countries between 2000 an
content: This study explores the impact of a multidimensional mix of factors—macroeconomic, environmental, social and medical on the annual variation of the current health expenditure as a share of GDP of the European Union countries between 2000 and 2022. A comprehensive investigation was conducted through static and dynamic panel regression techniques to ascertain the extent to which spending on health is influenced by economic growth, CO2 emissions, life expectancy, urbanization, hospital beds and physicians. The results show a negative association between GDP growth and the health expenditure to GDP ratio, which a decomposition analysis suggests largely reflects a mechanical denominator effect, while the residual, non-mechanical relationship between economic growth and health spending appearing positive. Furthermore, the analysis identifies a negative association between annual variations in CO2 emissions and health spending dynamics, which may reflect interactions between environmental policies and healthcare financing. Concurrently, positive annual variations in life expectancy growth signal a marginal decrease in health expenditure variations, reflecting enhanced preventive strategies. Urbanization increases the burden on healthcare spending primarily by intensifying service demand. Hospital beds and physicians exert upward pressure on the health sector’s direct costs. The findings indicate several determinants that can inform public policies aimed at achieving an efficient and sustainable level of health expenditure.

title: Interfacial Vacancy Engineering in CdS–CeO 2 S‐Scheme Heterojunctions for Efficient Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution and Wastewater Remediation
summary: ABSTRACT A hydrothermal–calcination route combined with an in situ oil‐bath deposition process was designed to construct CdS nanoparticle‐decorated CeO 2 nanorod heterostructures. The intimate interfacial contact between the two components,
content: ABSTRACT A hydrothermal–calcination route combined with an in situ oil‐bath deposition process was designed to construct CdS nanoparticle‐decorated CeO 2 nanorod heterostructures. The intimate interfacial contact between the two components, along with the presence of sulfur vacancies in the CdS lattice, was corroborated by x‐ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, high‐resolution transmission electron microscopy, and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. The resulting heterostructure, with an optimal composition, shows substantially improved photocatalytic performance in visible‐light‐driven H 2 generation and the decomposition of various organic contaminants, including dyes, antibiotics, and phenolic derivatives. A suite of characterization techniques—including photoluminescence spectroscopy, transient photocurrent measurements, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and radical quenching assays—was employed to probe the charge dynamics. The results reveal that the S scheme charge transfer mechanism, working in concert with vacancy engineering, facilitates charge‐carrier separation and migration while retaining the robust redox capacity inherent to both semiconductors. Collectively, these findings establish defect engineered CdS/CeO 2 heterojunctions as a versatile and promising candidate for simultaneous solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion and water purification.

title: Highest possible ambition: an introductory guide to the assessment of national climate plans under Article 4.3 of the Paris Agreement
summary: The Paris Agreement requires countries to formulate Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) towards reaching the global temperature goal of limiting warming well below 2°C while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C relative to pre-indus
content: The Paris Agreement requires countries to formulate Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) towards reaching the global temperature goal of limiting warming well below 2°C while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C relative to pre-industrial levels. At present, countries’ emission reduction plans fall collectively short of what is required to meet this goal. Ensuring that forthcoming NDCs reflect countries’ ‘highest possible ambition’, as expected under the Paris Agreement, is therefore essential. This briefing introduces a new framework designed to translate the legal expectation of ‘highest possible ambition’ into a practical, evidence-based approach for both designing and assessing national climate pledges.

title: Soil carbon storage and stability controlled by site properties more than forest management in a humid boreal forest
source: Soil Science Society of America Journal
summary: Abstract Soils of managed boreal forests are a significant carbon (C) reservoir, and maintaining or increasing their ability to store C could play an important role for climate change mitigation. We investigated the effects of forest loggin
content: Abstract Soils of managed boreal forests are a significant carbon (C) reservoir, and maintaining or increasing their ability to store C could play an important role for climate change mitigation. We investigated the effects of forest logging through clearcut and partial cut compared to forest conservation on total soil C stocks, particulate organic matter, and mineral‐associated organic matter (MAOM) physical fractions down to 55 cm in the mineral soil in a humid boreal balsam fir forest of Eastern Canada. We analyzed the variables that best explained the observed variations in soil C stocks, including topographic variables, deadwood, and soil physicochemical properties. Our results showed that harvesting treatments had no significant effect on soil C stocks for the entire soil profile. The variables that contributed most to explaining variations in soil C stocks for the FH horizons were exchangeable manganese, C stocks in buried wood, aboveground woody debris and mosses, slope inclination, and pH; pH, metal oxide, and rock content for mineral horizon C stocks; and pH, metal oxide content, and exchangeable iron for the MAOM fraction of mineral horizons. This study highlighted the complex and indirect role of deadwood and the significant influence of local site and soil properties (mainly metal oxide content) on soil C stocks in managed boreal forests.

title: Cross-Resolution Surrogate Modeling for CCUS-EOR Digital Twins Using 4DFNO Coupled with a Denoising Hamiltonian Network
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract Repeated compositional simulation is costly when Carbon Dioxide-Enhanced Oil Recovery (CO2-EOR) is deployed within carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) workflows that evaluate many geological realizations, assimilate pro
content: Abstract Repeated compositional simulation is costly when Carbon Dioxide-Enhanced Oil Recovery (CO2-EOR) is deployed within carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) workflows that evaluate many geological realizations, assimilate production data, or compare grid resolutions. The proposed framework, termed DHN-4DFNO, couples a four-dimensional Fourier neural operator (4DFNO) with a Denoising Hamiltonian Network (DHN) to predict pressure, oil saturation, and CO2 molar fraction over (t,z,x,y). The 4DFNO provides the global spatiotemporal state fields, while DHN encodes the 4DFNO feature-field response into time-indexed latent variables q and p, applies block-wise denoising Hamiltonian relations conditioned by a trajectory code z, and uses the scaled latent refinement in a 4DFNO-feature residual branch. The training objective combines supervised prediction and coarse-field losses with a Hamiltonian block loss. An optional simulator-exported component residual-label branch is retained in the implementation, but its particle swarm optimization (PSO)-selected weight is zero in the reported model. It therefore contributes neither loss nor gradient during final training. Tests use 1,500 compact compositional CO2-EOR numerical simulations with latent permeability-field variance parameter 0.2. The fixed random split gives 1,350 final-training cases and a 150-case evaluation partition reserved from final model fitting. For representative evaluation case 214, field-specific structural similarity index (SSIM) values are 0.9228-0.9994 over 370 reporting records, and DHN-4DFNO reduces pressure mean squared error (MSE) from 0.6322 to 0.3632 and CO2 molar-fraction MSE from 7.56E−3 to 2.45E−3. The trained framework is also evaluated from the native 40 × 40 × 3 setting to an 80 × 80 × 3 target grid without retraining, where the target-grid reference states are generated by rerunning the compositional simulator after horizontal interpolation of the rock-property fields. The surrogate supports rapid state forecasting, response screening, permeability data assimilation, CO2 storage-accounting post-processing, and net present value (NPV) evaluation.

title: Moving CO2 Liquefaction Offshore: Technology Selection for Scalable Floating CCS Hubs
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) is expected to play a critical role in achieving global decarbonization targets, requiring the development of scalable and economically viable CO2 transportation infrastructure. While pipeline-based
content: Abstract Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) is expected to play a critical role in achieving global decarbonization targets, requiring the development of scalable and economically viable CO2 transportation infrastructure. While pipeline-based CCS hubs have traditionally been regarded as the preferred solution for transporting captured CO2 to geological storage sites, their deployment is often constrained by high upfront capital investment, lengthy permitting processes, interface risks between project stakeholders, and limited flexibility for phased capacity expansion. Marine transportation of liquefied carbon dioxide (LCO2) has therefore emerged as an attractive alternative, particularly for connecting multiple emitters to offshore storage sites. This study proposes a nearshore Floating Liquefaction and Storage Unit (FLSU) as a shared midstream infrastructure solution that relocates CO2 liquefaction, temporary storage and marine loading from conventional onshore terminals onto a floating facility. The concept combines short gathering pipelines with marine transportation to reduce dependence on dedicated long-distance CO2 export pipelines while enabling phased CCS development and shared infrastructure utilization. Five CO2 liquefaction process configurations representing three refrigeration concepts were evaluated using steady-state process simulations. The configurations included propane Joule-Thomson (JT), ammonia JT, propane-CO2 cascade, ammonia-CO2 cascade, and CO2 self-refrigeration. All configurations were assessed under a common low-pressure storage design basis using thermodynamic performance indicators together with engineering and offshore suitability criteria including process complexity, equipment count, refrigerant inventory, safety and scalability. Although ammonia JT demonstrated the lowest specific energy consumption under the selected operating conditions, technology selection for a floating installation cannot be based solely on thermodynamic performance. CO2 self-refrigeration provided the most balanced solution by eliminating external refrigerants, reducing process complexity, minimizing major process equipment, and offering superior suitability for modular offshore deployment while maintaining competitive energy performance. The selected concept was subsequently evaluated for both low-pressure and medium-pressure transportation strategies, demonstrating its applicability across a range of CCS shipping scenarios. The study presents a structured technology selection framework that integrates thermodynamic analysis with offshore engineering considerations and CCS value-chain requirements. Rather than proposing a new liquefaction cycle, the work demonstrates how appropriate technology selection can enable scalable floating CCS infrastructure, providing a practical pathway toward flexible and phased CO2 transportation networks.

title: Towards Cost-Effective CCS-EOR: Multi-Scale Evaluation of Impure CO2 Injection Using an Integrated Compositional Simulation Framework
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract Carbon dioxide enhanced oil recovery (CO2-EOR) has emerged as a key technology for extending the productive life of mature oil reservoirs while simultaneously enabling geological carbon storage, making it an important component of
content: Abstract Carbon dioxide enhanced oil recovery (CO2-EOR) has emerged as a key technology for extending the productive life of mature oil reservoirs while simultaneously enabling geological carbon storage, making it an important component of carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) strategies. In practical field applications, however, injected CO2 streams are rarely pure and often contain impurities such as nitrogen (N2), methane (CH4), and hydrogen sulfide (H2S), originating from carbon capture processes, transportation, recycling operations, or source-dependent gas compositions. These impurities significantly influence phase behavior, minimum miscibility pressure (MMP), fluid properties, and multiphase displacement mechanisms, thereby affecting both oil recovery and long-term CO2 storage performance. Despite their practical importance, the combined effects of single and mixed impurities remain insufficiently understood, particularly under realistic reservoir conditions. This study presents an integrated compositional simulation framework to systematically evaluate the impact of impure CO2 streams on enhanced oil recovery and carbon storage efficiency. The workflow combines numerical slim-tube simulations for miscibility evaluation, a large ensemble of two-dimensional (2D) compositional reservoir simulations for impurity screening, and high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) field-scale compositional simulations for validation under realistic geological heterogeneity. The results demonstrate that inert impurities, including N2 and CH4, consistently increase MMP, reduce oil swelling, accelerate gas breakthrough, and consequently decrease displacement efficiency and ultimate oil recovery. In contrast, moderate concentrations of H2S improve miscibility, reduce MMP, and partially compensate for the adverse effects introduced by inert gases. Mixed-impurity systems exhibit strongly nonlinear behavior, indicating that reservoir performance cannot be reliably predicted by extrapolating single-impurity trends alone. The optimization identifies impurity compositions capable of achieving recovery factors comparable to those of pure CO2 injection while maintaining favorable CO2 storage performance. Furthermore, field-scale simulations confirm that impurity-tolerant injection strategies identified during the screening stage remain effective under realistic heterogeneous reservoir conditions, providing balanced improvements in sweep efficiency, and long-term CO2 retention. Therefore, the proposed integrated workflow offers a scalable and computationally efficient methodology for the design and optimization of impurity-aware CO2-EOR projects.

title: Challenges in Ductile Fracture Control for Dense Phase CO2 Pipelines: Toughness Demands, Impurity Sensitivity, and Commissioning Risk
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract Carbon dioxide has several use cases in the oil and gas industry, such as enhanced oil recovery (EOR), carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) and, more recently, transporting carbon dioxide from emitters into a shared indus
content: Abstract Carbon dioxide has several use cases in the oil and gas industry, such as enhanced oil recovery (EOR), carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) and, more recently, transporting carbon dioxide from emitters into a shared industrial cluster or hub network. As a result, dense phase CO2 pipelines are rapidly becoming more common, with infrastructure scaling globally. Transporting dense phase CO2 through a pipeline comes with the critical design requirement to mitigate the risk of ductile fracture propagation through a fracture control plan. This paper aims to demonstrate how to design a dense phase CO2 pipeline against ductile fracture propagation, which is a high risk and uncontrollable failure event caused by the inadvertent depressurization and phase change of dense phase CO2. This necessitates identifying the charpy V-notch (CVN) energy requirements based on operating conditions and whether these toughness demands can reliably be achieved by pipe manufacturers. The approach centers around thermodynamic modeling of a given CO2 composition, which can contain several impurities that shift the phase envelope. To do this, all credible operating scenarios from a pressure and temperature perspective must identified including details related to the startup/commissioning, normal operating modes and during maintenance events such as pigging. Rapid depressurization events, such as a failure, are then thermodynamically modeled to predict the point at which the temperature and pressure cross the saturation line or saturation envelope, which is where dense phase CO2 begins to flash and undergo a phase change. During a phase change the pipeline cannot depressurize quickly enough relative to the velocity of the fracture, which allows the fracture to propagate axially along the pipeline, increasing the potential severity and damage of a rupture. The methodologies described in DNV RP-F104[1] and ISO 27913-2016[5] allow a designer to specify a CVN energy to resist this propagation, which is to be specified at the onset of pipeline design and procurement. The DNV RP F104 methodology is supported by full scale CO2 burst/propagation tests covering a limited range of pipe diameters and wall thicknesses, while the methodology in ISO 27913-2016 Annex D is based on the Battelle two-curve method. In the case of the DNV RP F104 methodology, if the subject dataset falls outside the bounds of the test data, it is recommended to complete a full scale fracture propagation test to widen the test data and determine if different diameters and wall thicknesses exhibit similar arrest-propagation behaviour as derived from the full scale test results. Impurities in the gas stream have a significant influence on the maximum saturation pressure, which directly drives the CVN energy requirement. Impurities such as nitrogen, which is commonly used in commissioning activities, can drastically influence the CVN requirement and may become challenging to achieve reliably in pip

title: Stratigraphy-Aware Patch-Transformer for Well Logs Reconstruction Applied to Geomechanics and Reservoir Analytics Workflows
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract High-quality well logs are essential inputs to reservoir characterization, carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS), and geomechanics workflows, but complete well logs are rarely available over the full depth interval. Conve
content: Abstract High-quality well logs are essential inputs to reservoir characterization, carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS), and geomechanics workflows, but complete well logs are rarely available over the full depth interval. Conventional empirical backfills such as Gardner-type density–velocity relations and lithology-specific velocity transforms are useful when their assumptions are satisfied, yet they require expert selection and may not preserve formation-dependent relationships. This paper presents a stratigraphy-aware, patch-based Transformer for reconstructing missing multivariate well logs. The workflow combines data conditioning, explicit missingness masks, learned stratigraphic embeddings, overlapping depth patches, and self-attention that jointly models depth-wise continuity and cross-log dependencies. The model is evaluated on the GeoLink and Taranaki public-scale datasets, whose basin settings, formation composition, acquisition conditions, and missingness profiles differ substantially. Against an XGBoost baseline, the proposed model reduces mean absolute error (MAE) on GeoLink by 31% for gamma ray, 29% for bulk density, 13% for neutron porosity, and 24% for compressional slowness. On Taranaki, reductions are 3%, 11%, 6%, and 17%, respectively. Experiments show that most of the performance gain is attributable to stratigraphic conditioning and patch-wise context. Results in physical units give approximately 0.0391 g/cm3 MAE for bulk density over 1.95–2.95 g/cm3 and 5.4698 us/ft for compressional slowness over 40–240 us/ft on GeoLink. On a field-scale Barents Sea case, the same workflow reduces the error of the classical Gardner and Greenberg–Castagna backfills by 76% for bulk density and 84% for compressional slowness on intervals where both curves are measured. The reconstructed curves provide a rapid, internally consistent input set for downstream reservoir and wellbore-stability analytics.

title: Roadmap for inferring metabolic regulation using multiomics, machine learning, and genome-scale modeling
summary: Machine learning and genome-scale metabolic modeling have accelerated the discovery of metabolic-regulatory relationships in model microbes and mammalian cells. This review provides a roadmap for integrating omics with computational methods
content: Machine learning and genome-scale metabolic modeling have accelerated the discovery of metabolic-regulatory relationships in model microbes and mammalian cells. This review provides a roadmap for integrating omics with computational methods for studying systems-level transcriptional, post-translational, and allosteric regulation. Developing methods to infer and integrate multiple regulatory mechanisms simultaneously is essential for discovering novel modes of metabolic regulation and precise engineering of metabolic networks.

title: A metabolic flux efficiency model reveals mitochondrial triage: H2S reallocates carbon skeletons to match cysteine under cyanide stress in rice
summary: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) achieves comparable growth recovery to cysteine (Cys) in rice under cyanide (CN - ) stress, despite Cys being the direct substrate for CN - detoxification and driving a substantially higher assimilation rate via β-c
content: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) achieves comparable growth recovery to cysteine (Cys) in rice under cyanide (CN - ) stress, despite Cys being the direct substrate for CN - detoxification and driving a substantially higher assimilation rate via β-cyanoalanine synthase (β-CAS). This paradox implies a fundamental trade-off between immediate detoxification and long-term resilience. Here, we profiled tissue-resolved metabolomics of the TCA cycle intermediates oxaloacetate (OAA) and α-ketoglutarate (α-KG), and their cognate aspartate (Asp)- and glutamate (Glu)-family amino acids, the branches most intimately linked to CN - assimilation, together with transcriptional analysis of their biosynthetic genes. We then developed a Metabolic Flux Efficiency ( MFE ) model, a proof-of-concept framework that integrates these data to estimate relative flux efficiency within the TCA–amino acid (AA) cycle. H 2 S is proposed to execute a mitochondrial triage strategy, depleting root nitrogen reserves (Asn and Gln reduced by 92% and 67%) to liberate carbon skeletons, while boosting root α-KG (+93%) to sustain anaplerotic TCA cycle flux. The calibrated MFE model (Asp family: α = 0.39, β = 1.52; Glu family: α = 0.37, β = 1.64) suggests that metabolic conversion dominates over transcription in governing flux under CN - stress, and predicts that H 2 S redirects flow away from primary nitrogen assimilation (Glu→Gln) toward energy-generating cycles (Orn→Cit). This pattern is consistent with recovery being governed not by nitrogen abundance but by dynamic reallocation of carbon skeletons from storage to biosynthetic and anaplerotic routes. By redefining the mitochondrion as a metabolic regulatory hub that prioritizes reconstruction over mere survival, our work provides a quantitative framework for interpreting metabolic trade-offs and a conceptual basis for engineering stress-resilient crops.

title: Umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes ameliorate parathyroid ischemic injury via inhibition of the neutrophil cytosolic factor 4-nuclear factor kappa B pathway
summary: BACKGROUNDPost-surgical hypoparathyroidism results primarily from mechanical injury to parathyroid tissue or vascular injury during thyroid surgery, leading to glandular ischemia and dysfunction.Patients characteristically exhibit severe hy
content: BACKGROUNDPost-surgical hypoparathyroidism results primarily from mechanical injury to parathyroid tissue or vascular injury during thyroid surgery, leading to glandular ischemia and dysfunction.Patients characteristically exhibit severe hypocalcemia and significantly reduced parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion.The conventional management strategy involves prolonged high-dose supplementation with calcium and active vitamin D. While this approach partially ameliorates hypocalcemia, it cannot substitute for the physiological actions of PTH, especially PTH-mediated calcium reabsorption in the kidney.Therefore, chronic high-dose calcium therapy commonly results in hypercalciuria, substantially elevating the risk of renal dysfunction, kidney stones, and ectopic calcification.Restoration of parathyroid function following surgical injury represents a critical clinical challenge. AIMTo investigate the effect of umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (UCMSC-Exo) on rabbit parathyroid injury and to elucidate the mechanism. METHODSWe established a rabbit parathyroid ischemia model by ligating the superior thyroid artery branches supplying both parathyroid glands.UCMSC-Exo was injected into the capsule of the parathyroid gland to evaluate the levels of serum PTH and calcium, the histological changes of the parathyroid gland, cell apoptosis and proliferation.Additionally, we studied the effect of UCMSC-Exo on hypoxia-induced damage to rabbit parathyroid cells.Subsequently, rabbit parathyroid tissues were analyzed to elucidate the mechanism by which UCMSC-Exo improves parathyroid injury.4 / 33 RESULTSThe results showed that UCMSC-Exo treatment significantly restored PTH and serum calcium levels, alleviated the histological damage of the parathyroid gland, inhibited mitochondrial dysfunction, inhibited cell apoptosis, and promoted cell proliferation.Moreover, in vitro experiments demonstrated that UCMSC-Exo could inhibit the generation of reactive oxygen species in hypoxia-induced parathyroid cells, inhibit cell apoptosis, and promote cell proliferation.Through sequencing and western blot, we found that UCMSC-Exo exerted its protective effect by inhibiting the neutrophil cytosolic factor 4-nuclear factor kappa B signaling pathway. CONCLUSIONThese findings indicate that local subcapsular injection of UCMSC-Exo has beneficial effects on improving rabbit parathyroid injury and is a promising therapeutic strategy for preventing parathyroid dysfunction after thyroid surgery.

title: When are Two‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks Good Electrodes for Lithium Ion Batteries? A Data‐Driven Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are emerging as sustainable organic electrode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries. Despite more than a decade of research, existing heuristics for designing electroactive COFs
content: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are emerging as sustainable organic electrode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries. Despite more than a decade of research, existing heuristics for designing electroactive COFs lack generality, and the suitability of these materials as alternatives to conventional electrodes remains poorly resolved. Here, we map structure–electrode–function relationships across 1099 experimentally synthesized 2D COFs from the CoRE COF database by developing a data‐driven framework integrating density‐functional theory computations with machine learning models and establishing atomic‐level design rules governing electrode behavior. We uncover that cathode‐like character originates from dense, multidentate nitrogen and oxygen rich coordination pockets at pore walls, characteristic of imide, acylhydrazones, keto–amine linkages, and π‐macrocycles, whereas anode‐like behavior is encoded by spatially separated redox sites and π‐rich interlayer galleries that sustain weak, reversible Li + intercalation. Sequential voltage, capacity, and conductivity‐based screening across the database yields 14 anode and 14 cathode candidates. We show that the known chemical space of 2D COFs cannot outperform inorganic electrodes in terms of operating voltages. However, strategic pairing of 2D anode|cathode pairs within an all‐organic lithium battery architecture delivers full‐cell voltages exceeding 2 V with capacities above 200 mAh g −1 on both electrodes, surpassing small organic molecules and polymer counterparts.

title: Reclamation of degraded saline-alkali soils of the northwestern region of India through microbial amendments
summary: Salt-affected soils of semi-arid northern India severely limit ecosystem functioning and agroforestry productivity through elevated salinity, low organic carbon, restricted phosphorus availability, and alkaline pH. Eleven amendment treatmen
content: Salt-affected soils of semi-arid northern India severely limit ecosystem functioning and agroforestry productivity through elevated salinity, low organic carbon, restricted phosphorus availability, and alkaline pH. Eleven amendment treatments comprising enriched charcoal (Ench) and enriched soil (EnS) substrates co-inoculated with four indigenously characterised plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR: Klebsiella aerogenes , Lysinibacillus acetophenoni , Pseudomonas stutzeri , and Pseudomonas mosselii ) were evaluated across three soil depth intervals (0–30, 30–60, and 60–90 cm) in a randomised split-plot design at three sites (Hisar, Karnal, Bhiwani) in Haryana. Soil pH, electrical conductivity (EC), organic carbon (OC), available nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) were analysed using split-plot linear mixed-effects models (LMMs). Ten amendments significantly reduced EC, with nine achieving significant reductions across all three depth intervals and the largest reductions reaching 0.31 dS m⁻ 1 (67% of baseline) at the surface. Eight treatments increased OC significantly at 0–30 cm (83–109% above baseline); only T11 (EnS + four-strain consortium) extended this effect to 60–90 cm (+ 0.262%, p = 0.014). Multiple treatments significantly increased phosphorus availability at all three depths. pH, N, and K were unresponsive within the study period. Marginal R 2 values ranged from 0.074 to 0.569 across the six soil properties, while conditional R 2 values ranged from 0.634 to 0.881 for models with estimable random-effect variance, indicating that the hierarchical model structure accounted for substantial additional variation beyond treatment and depth. A PCA-derived Soil Quality Index showed the highest mean SQI for T2 (Ench + K. aerogenes ) and T5 (Ench + P. mosselii ), whereas T9 (EnS + P. stutzeri ) showed the lowest coefficient of variation across the three soil-depth intervals. These responses indicate that selected organic-microbial amendments have potential to improve specific dimensions of soil quality under the conditions tested, while their persistence and broader applicability require validation across additional seasons and sites.

title: Ex Vivo Normothermic Machine Perfusion of Declined Kidneys: A Pilot Study of Perfusion Dynamics, Necroptosis Pathway Activation and Clinical Translation
summary: BACKGROUND: Ex vivo normothermic machine perfusion (EV NMP) enables functional assessment and reconditioning of marginal donor kidneys. This pilot study aimed to establish an EV NMP platform, characterise perfusion parameters and cell death
content: BACKGROUND: Ex vivo normothermic machine perfusion (EV NMP) enables functional assessment and reconditioning of marginal donor kidneys. This pilot study aimed to establish an EV NMP platform, characterise perfusion parameters and cell death pathways and facilitate clinical translation. METHODS: Six kidneys declined for transplantation underwent 2 h of EV NMP with a red blood cell-based perfusate. Perfusion dynamics, biochemistry and urine output were monitored. Histological injury was graded using the Remuzzi scoring system. Immunohistochemistry evaluated necroptosis (RIPK1, RIPK3, MLKL, pMLKL) and apoptosis (cleaved caspase-3, caspase-8). RESULTS: All kidneys produced urine and achieved Remuzzi scores ≤ 3. Renal vascular resistance declined 78% over the perfusion period. Perfusate creatinine and potassium decreased significantly (reduction 69.7 μmol/L, 95% CI [22.4, 117.0], p = 0.006 and 2.4 mmol/L, 95% CI [0.4, 4.4], p = 0.021, respectively). Necroptosis markers were prominent within tubular epithelium; pMLKL positivity in 18.5% of proximal tubules at baseline indicated active necroptotic signalling prior to perfusion. Apoptotic markers were comparatively sparse. A marginal DCDD kidney declined by all allocated transplant units was assessed using EV NMP and accepted for transplantation. The recipient experienced delayed graft function resolving within 1 week and mixed rejection at 6 months that responded to treatment, with maintained graft function at 2-year follow-up (serum creatinine 159 μmol/L). CONCLUSION: EV NMP is feasible and clinically translatable within a kidney transplant programme. Prominent baseline necroptotic signalling, reflected by pMLKL burden at commencement of perfusion, identifies the RIPK3-MLKL axis as a rational therapeutic target during ex vivo organ reconditioning, warranting investigation in prospective trials.

title: Digital traceability in construction: A systematic review on RFID, IoT, and blockchain integration
summary: Digital traceability is now a strategic imperative in construction, where materials, equipment, documents, and responsibilities traverse organizational and geographic boundaries. This review synthesizes evidence on three technology families
content: Digital traceability is now a strategic imperative in construction, where materials, equipment, documents, and responsibilities traverse organizational and geographic boundaries. This review synthesizes evidence on three technology families that anchor end-to-end traceability: radio-frequency identification (RFID) for persistent identity and events, the Internet of Things (IoT) for continuous sensing and telemetry, and blockchain for tamper-evident logging and automation. Using a PRISMA-informed search and evidence-synthesis approach, we synthesize a 2023–2025 evidence base and complement it with a 2020–2025 bibliometric overview of publication trends across RFID, IoT, and blockchain research. Findings indicate a layered architecture: RFID stabilizes identity, IoT furnishes state and context, and blockchain supplies integrity, ordering, and automation, with hybrid models emerging as the practical route to verifiable custody, proactive operations, and secure documentation. Constraints related to interoperability and identifier management, integration performance and scalability, telemetry security and privacy, governance and legal recognition, and scaling economics explain why many deployments remain pilot-bound. We contribute a cross-technology comparison, canonical dataflow patterns for hybrid architectures, and a forward agenda prioritizing identifier/ontology standards, privacy-preserving assurance, consortium governance, and rigorous longitudinal evaluation. Overall, sector-scale adoption will occur when identity, sensing, and assurance are engineered and governed in concert, not as parallel solutions.

title: Evaluating Thermal Resistance in Cryogenic LNG Cargo Containment Systems: A Case Study of The Tangguh–FSRU Jawa Satu Transport Route
source: Journal of Emerging Supply Chain Clean Energy and Process Engineering
summary: This study evaluated the thermal resistance performance of spherical cryogenic storage tanks on liquefied natural gas carriers operating between the Tangguh refinery and the Jawa Satu Floating Storage Regasification Unit to address the oper
content: This study evaluated the thermal resistance performance of spherical cryogenic storage tanks on liquefied natural gas carriers operating between the Tangguh refinery and the Jawa Satu Floating Storage Regasification Unit to address the operational challenge of cargo shrinkage. The natural evaporation of cryogenic fluids during maritime transportation represented a physical loss of energy supply and caused a significant financial burden on the national energy supply chain. To measure the thermal efficiency of the tanks, the theoretical heat transfer rate and the theoretical daily boil-off rate were calculated based on the thermal resistance of the composite wall structure. These theoretical baselines were then compared with actual volume shrinkage data from voyage reports to determine the efficiency deviation and the subsequent economic loss. The analytical model demonstrated that the theoretical heat transfer rate penetrating the storage system was 116.9 kW, which corresponded to an expected daily boil-off rate of 0.17%/day. However, the field performance data revealed an actual daily boil-off rate of 0.35%/day. This comparison identified a performance inefficiency deviation of 0.18%/day, which was attributed to the degradation of the insulation materials. Consequently, this thermal inefficiency caused a commercial energy supply failure of 31,351.46 MMBtu that evaporated during the voyage. This energy loss translated to a financial deficit of $194,108.77 for a single voyage cycle, highlighting the critical necessity for strict insulation maintenance.

title: Short‐term surface soil responses to compost rate during peach orchard establishment on sandy Ultisols
source: Soil Science Society of America Journal
summary: Abstract Compost amendment can improve soil health, but rate‐dependent responses in sandy orchard soils remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated the short‐term effects of compost application on soil physical, chemical, and
content: Abstract Compost amendment can improve soil health, but rate‐dependent responses in sandy orchard soils remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated the short‐term effects of compost application on soil physical, chemical, and biological properties during the first 2 years of peach ( Prunus persica (L.) Batsch) orchard establishment on a sandy Ultisol at Clemson University's Musser Fruit Research Center in South Carolina. Compost was incorporated into soils before planting at rates of 25.6 (1x treatment) and 51.2 Mg ha −1 (2x treatment) in 2019, followed by annual spring surface applications at rates of 8.5 and 17.0 Mg ha −1 for the 1x and 2x treatments, respectively. A no‐compost control (CT) was included for comparison. Surface soil (0–15 cm) was sampled in spring and fall of 2020 and 2021. Compost increased soil moisture, pH, permanganate oxidizable carbon (C), potentially mineralizable nitrogen (N), extracellular enzyme activities associated with C, N, and phosphorus (P) cycling, and total C and N by the end of the study. In contrast, compost did not increase extractable inorganic N and P. Across most short‐term biological indicators, the increase from CT to 1x was more consistent than the increase from 1x to 2x, indicating limited additional functional gains at the higher compost rate. Overall, compost enhanced surface soil moisture, organic matter accumulation, and biologically mediated nutrient cycling more than short‐term inorganic nutrient pools under this fertilized orchard establishment system. These results suggest that moderate compost input may capture much of the near‐term surface soil functional benefit during peach orchard establishment on sandy Ultisols, although long‐term studies with deeper sampling, tree performance measurements, and economic analysis are needed to identify optimal compost rates for sustainable orchard production.

title: Evaluation of 1-octadecyl-3-methylimidazolium bromide for enhanced oil recovery: interfacial behavior and pore-scale displacement in a glass micromodel
summary: The efficiency of conventional surfactants in chemical enhanced oil recovery (EOR) is often limited by high salinity, elevated temperatures, and adsorption-related chemical losses, particularly in carbonate reservoirs. These limitations hav
content: The efficiency of conventional surfactants in chemical enhanced oil recovery (EOR) is often limited by high salinity, elevated temperatures, and adsorption-related chemical losses, particularly in carbonate reservoirs. These limitations have motivated the investigation of alternative surface-active agents with favorable interfacial performance under challenging conditions. In this study, the interfacial and pore-scale displacement performance of the ionic liquid 1-octadecyl-3-methylimidazolium bromide ([C18mim][Br]) was investigated through a combination of interfacial tension (IFT) measurements and flooding experiments in a heterogeneous glass micromodel. A systematic experimental program was conducted to evaluate the effects of ionic liquid concentration, salinity, and temperature on oil–water interfacial behavior and displacement efficiency. The ionic liquid reduced the oil–water IFT from approximately 89 mN/m to below 2 mN/m as the [C18mim][Br] concentration was increased from 0 to 200 ppm, corresponding to a reduction greater than 97%. A pronounced salinity-dependent interfacial response was observed, with an IFT value of approximately 0.36 mN/m at 22,500 ppm NaCl and a nominal ionic-liquid concentration of 50 ppm in the salinity-focused experiments. Micromodel flooding experiments further showed that injection of a nominal 10 ppm [C18mim][Br] solution increased the final recovery factor to approximately 58% relative to conventional water flooding under the tested micromodel conditions. Temperature elevation also improved the observed displacement performance, with recovery increasing from 36.8% at 25 °C to 48.1% at 60 °C. The results further demonstrated that the lowest IFT condition did not necessarily correspond to the highest oil recovery, indicating that pore-scale displacement performance depends on coupled interfacial and flow-related mechanisms. Overall, the findings indicate that [C18mim][Br] provides strong interfacial modification and favorable pore-scale displacement performance at the tested concentrations under the controlled experimental conditions investigated. However, the present study did not quantify ionic-liquid adsorption or retention on carbonate minerals, glass surfaces, or within porous media, and therefore the reported concentrations should not be interpreted as field dosage or as evidence of low chemical consumption at reservoir scale. Accordingly, the results should be regarded as a pore-scale screening assessment that provides a basis for further carbonate-specific validation rather than direct evidence of carbonate-reservoir applicability.

title: Utilization of support vector-based techniques for prediction of compressive strength for graphene oxide based self- compacting concrete
summary: In the present work, the machine learning methods were used to develop the predictive models for the Compressive Strength (CS) of the graphene oxide-enhanced self-compacting concrete. The models were built and analysed using a comprehensive
content: In the present work, the machine learning methods were used to develop the predictive models for the Compressive Strength (CS) of the graphene oxide-enhanced self-compacting concrete. The models were built and analysed using a comprehensive database of 76 samples extracted from the literature. The model uses water content, ground granulated blast furnace slag, fly ash, fine aggregates, coarse aggregates, superplasticizer and cement quantity as input parameters and concrete CS as output. The predictive modelling methods used are linear regression, genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization, support vector regression, grey wolf optimization, differential evolution and manta rays foraging optimization. The model efficiency was assessed on the basis of seven parameters, namely, coefficient of correlation (CC), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), normalized root mean square error, Willmott’s index, Nash Sutcliffe efficiency and coefficient of determination. The results showed that the support vector regression differential equation had the highest accuracy and lowest error to predict CS. The maximum CC obtained were 0.990 and 0.960 for training and testing datasets respectively. The error values for training and testing datasets are SVR DE achieved CC values of 0.995 and 0.958, RMSE values of 1.785 and 3.947 MPa, MAE values of 0.874 and 2.899 MPa, NRMSE values of 0.023 and 0.088, WI values of 0.997 and 0.978, and NSE values of 0.990 and 0.911 respectively.

title: Molecular alloying of titanium–oxo clusters for linker-free S-scheme interfaces
summary: Abstract Heterojunction engineering is one of the most effective strategies for enhancing charge separation and improving the performance of photo-functional materials. However, such heterojunction functionality has been almost exclusively
content: Abstract Heterojunction engineering is one of the most effective strategies for enhancing charge separation and improving the performance of photo-functional materials. However, such heterojunction functionality has been almost exclusively realized in extended solids, and how to translate this concept into atomically precise molecular systems remains an open question. Here, we employ two isostructural yet electronically distinct titanium-oxo clusters, Ti 12 Mn 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 and Ti 12 Cr 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 (denoted as TiMn and TiCr, respectively; Bz denotes C 6 H 5 CO 2 ), as modular nanosized building blocks to construct molecular alloys that form eutectic molecular alloys across the entire compositional range. Free from covalent or ionic linkages, TiMn and TiCr achieve spontaneous Fermi-level equilibration solely through intimate intermolecular packing, thereby establishing an S-scheme junction at the molecular scale. This markedly enhances charge-carrier separation, carrier lifetime, and interfacial charge-transport kinetics, leading to substantially increased photocurrents, accelerated reactive oxygen species generation, and significantly improved elimination of representative waterborne micropollutants. The emergent functionality originates from local electronic complementarity and low-resistance intermolecular charge-transport channels facilitated by ligand π–π interactions, whereas long-range crystalline order is not essential. Our findings suggest a convenient approach for developing nanocluster-level functional donor–acceptor systems without relying on extended frameworks or on covalent fusion between the building units.

title: Refined Ann Predictions for Reiner–Rivlin Fluid With Dispersed Hybrid Nanoparticles Around an Isothermal Porous Cone
source: ZAMM ‐ Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics / Zeitschrift für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik
summary: ABSTRACT This study presents numerical solutions for the steady non‐Newtonian Reiner–Rivlin viscous flow around an isothermal vertical permeable porous cone with a linearly variable surface temperature of degree . The research investigates
content: ABSTRACT This study presents numerical solutions for the steady non‐Newtonian Reiner–Rivlin viscous flow around an isothermal vertical permeable porous cone with a linearly variable surface temperature of degree . The research investigates the role of hybrid nanomaterials, which consist of multiple magnetic nano‐sized particles dispersed in the base fluid, in enhancing heat and mass transfer characteristics. The governing coupled, nonlinear equations were formulated and solved using a finite difference method, leading to the identification of critical phenomena governing the flow and thermal behavior. Results reveal that the Reiner–Rivlin factor significantly enhances the velocity and its gradient , showcasing the pronounced non‐Newtonian effects. Similarly, the temperature gradient exhibits substantial variations under different physical parameter conditions, highlighting the intricate interplay between viscous forces and thermal conductivity. The study also emphasizes the influence of key parameters such as the Hartmann number, Prandtl number, and Darcy number on the flow dynamics, shedding light on their individual and combined effects. To augment the numerical analysis, an artificial neural network (ANN) model was employed to predict the values of with remarkable accuracy. The ANN model demonstrated excellent agreement with numerical computations, validating its efficacy in forecasting complex fluid behaviors. This integration of ANN with numerical techniques not only enhances predictive capabilities but also underscores the potential for machine learning in solving challenging fluid mechanics problems. These findings provide valuable insights for applications in engineering, thermal management, and material science, paving the way for optimized designs in industrial and environmental systems.

title: Towards a hydrogen economy: A comprehensive review of the full hydrogen value chain
summary: As countries pursue deep decarbonization and energy system transformation, hydrogen (H 2 ) is emerging as a critical enabler for hard-to-abate sectors and large-scale energy storage. However, realizing a sustainable and scalable H 2 economy
content: As countries pursue deep decarbonization and energy system transformation, hydrogen (H 2 ) is emerging as a critical enabler for hard-to-abate sectors and large-scale energy storage. However, realizing a sustainable and scalable H 2 economy requires a holistic understanding of the entire H 2 value chain, encompassing production, storage, transportation, and end-use. This review paper provides a comprehensive assessment of the key technologies, infrastructure challenges, and policy frameworks that influence the development of a low-carbon H 2 ecosystem. The paper examines two primary production pathways: green H 2 , which is produced through water electrolysis powered by renewable electricity, and blue H 2 , which is derived from fossil fuels with carbon capture and storage. Their techno-economic characteristics, scalability, and regional applicability are compared based on recent literature and policy developments. In terms of storage and transportation, various options such as compressed H 2 , cryogenic liquid H 2 , ammonia, and liquid organic hydrogen carriers are analyzed for their efficiency and economic feasibility. On the utilization side, the paper explores both the direct use of H 2 in fuel cells and industrial processes, and its indirect use in the synthesis of e-fuels such as methanol and ammonia. The review emphasizes the importance of integrated system-level approaches that connect all stages of the value chain, supported by modeling of supply-demand dynamics, infrastructure optimization, innovation in H 2 carriers, and industrial deployment. Ultimately, this paper suggests that approaching H 2 technologies as part of an integrated system, rather than as isolated components, is the key to ensuring the sustainability and viability of the H 2 economy.

title: Seasonal climate modulates water and nitrogen use efficiency and biodiversity contributions to yield stability in cereal/legume forage intercropping
summary: Increasing climatic variability and water scarcity threaten forage yield stability, yet how cereal/legume intercropping stabilizes yields under contrasting seasonal conditions remains unclear. A 4-year-long field experiment (2022–2025) was
content: Increasing climatic variability and water scarcity threaten forage yield stability, yet how cereal/legume intercropping stabilizes yields under contrasting seasonal conditions remains unclear. A 4-year-long field experiment (2022–2025) was conducted with five cropping systems, including oat ( Avena sativa L.) monoculture (SO), common vetch ( Vicia sativa L.) monoculture (SC), oat/common vetch intercropping (OC), hairy vetch ( Vicia villosa L.) monoculture (SH), and oat/hairy vetch intercropping (OH), under spring and summer sowing seasons. Forage productivity and yield stability were evaluated, and the relative contributions of water productivity (WP), nitrogen use efficiency (NUE), and biodiversity effects to yield stability were quantified. Compared with monocultures, intercropping improved forage productivity and resource use efficiency while reducing CV by 23.6%, indicating greater yield stability. OC showed the strongest overall performance, increasing DMY by 87.4% and CPY by 51.1% relative to the mean of the corresponding monocultures, while achieving the highest WP DMY (32.9 kg ha −1 mm −1 ) and nitrogen uptake (179.3 kg ha −1 ). Summer sowing further enhanced productivity and stability, particularly in intercropping systems. The dominant drivers of yield stability shifted from water productivity under spring sowing to biodiversity effects under summer sowing, with complementarity and selection effects becoming increasingly important. Variance partitioning revealed that shared effects among complementarity effects, selection effects, water productivity, and NUE accounted for more than 80% of the explained variation in yield stability. Overall, the findings support the proposed hypotheses that intercropping can enhance forage yield stability and that the relative importance of its underlying mechanisms varies with sowing season conditions.

title: Mid infrared spectroscopy and machine learning for predicting soil properties in Inceptisols of the Indo Gangetic plain
summary: Mid-infrared (MIR) spectroscopy offers the potential for rapid soil assessment, particularly when predictions are adequately evaluated against laboratory measurements set. In this study, we compared partial least squares regression (PLSR),
content: Mid-infrared (MIR) spectroscopy offers the potential for rapid soil assessment, particularly when predictions are adequately evaluated against laboratory measurements set. In this study, we compared partial least squares regression (PLSR), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) regression to predict ten physical and chemical properties of Inceptisols from Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar in the Indo-Gangetic plains of India. A total of 450 surface soil samples were collected from arable land at 0–15 cm depth, and the property-specific datasets used for modeling include 434–447 observations after removing outliers and samples affected by measurement or sampling errors. Laboratory MIR spectra were related to particle size distribution, gravimetric water retention at field capacity (FC) and permanent wilting point (PWP), soil organic carbon (SOC), pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and available P and K. Approximately 70% of the observations were used for calibration and 30% for held-out validation. Overall, PLSR performed best for most properties. In validation, PLSR yielded R² = 0.84 and RMSE = 2.89% for clay, 0.75 and 3.28% for silt, 0.71 and 4.14% for sand, 0.74 and 1.52% for PWP, and 0.70 and 2.37% for FC. PLSR also predicted SOC with R² = 0.72 and RMSE = 0.11%, and pH with R² = 0.73 and RMSE = 0.46 pH units. SVM achieved slightly higher R² values for EC and available K, although predictions of EC and extractable nutrients remained weak. These findings support using MIR spectroscopy as a screening tool for selected soil properties within the calibration domain; however, the validation analysis does not demonstrate transferability to new regions, instruments, or field measurement conditions.

title: A coastal beach seed bank shows high diversity, but low similarity to the adjacent forest vegetation in an Amazonia Marine Extractive Reserve
summary: Abstract Marine Extractive Reserves (RESEX-Mar) play a fundamental role in conserving Amazoniana coastal biodiversity, maintaining ecosystem services, and supporting the livelihoods of traditional communities. However, the relationship betw
content: Abstract Marine Extractive Reserves (RESEX-Mar) play a fundamental role in conserving Amazoniana coastal biodiversity, maintaining ecosystem services, and supporting the livelihoods of traditional communities. However, the relationship between seed taxonomy and adjacent vegetation remains poorly understood. This study evaluated whether the taxonomic composition of seeds deposited on the beaches of the RESEX-Mar in the municipality of Soure, Brazilian Amazon, reflects the composition and diversity of the adjacent vegetation. A floristic inventory was conducted on the main beaches of the reserve, while seeds were manually collected from the sand during low tide. The vegetation comprised of 20 species distributed across 16 families, with dominance of Rhizophora sp. and a predominance of arboreal habit (50 – 56% of individuals). A total of 786 seeds were recorded, representing 21 plant families, 64 identified species, and 46 morphospecies, exhibiting substantially higher diversity than the vegetation (Shannon 3.90 – 4.13 for seed taxonomy versus 0.79 – 2.29 for vegetation) and high evenness (Pielou ≥ 0.95). Mean seed density did not differ statistically among beaches. The divergence between seeds and vegetation indicated a strong influence of external dispersal, likely shaped by hydrochory. The results demonstrate the genetic potential of the seed bank, characterized as an important propagule reservoir for the ecological restoration of coastal ecosystems. Therefore, it was observed that seed composition does not fully reflect the adjacent vegetation but reinforces the role of Amazoniana coastal ecosystems as biodiversity source areas, highlighting the need for conservation strategies that consider ecological connectivity, monitoring of natural regeneration, and sustainable management of tourism use.

title: Technological approach to invasive species: the role of remote sensing and predictive modelling
summary: Remote sensing, predictive modelling and machine learning are increasingly central to detecting and monitoring invasive plant species across broad and heterogeneous landscapes. This review synthesises 25 years of remote sensing-based invasi
content: Remote sensing, predictive modelling and machine learning are increasingly central to detecting and monitoring invasive plant species across broad and heterogeneous landscapes. This review synthesises 25 years of remote sensing-based invasive plant species research (2000-2025) to determine how sensor selection, analytical methods and reporting practices have evolved. Records from Web of Science and Scopus were screened using defined eligibility criteria and coded by platform, sensor, species, region, method, impact category, accuracy reporting and linkage with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Bibliometric keyword analysis was used to examine thematic structure and emerging research directions. The evidence shows rapid publication growth after 2015, continued dominance of satellite data, increasing use of uncrewed aerial systems, light detection and ranging, synthetic aperture radar and machine learning classifiers and persistent geographic imbalance. Of 166 retained studies, 149 provided extractable impact information and 76 reported overall accuracy values. The literature indicates a shift from descriptive mapping toward integrated monitoring, risk assessment and decision support frameworks for biodiversity conservation, restoration planning and invasive plant management.

title: Thermoresponsive Self‐Healing Carbon Nanotube‐Reinforced Dual‐Network Hydrogels for Wearable Sensors and Information Concealment
summary: ABSTRACT The development of multifunctional hydrogels combining mechanical robustness, autonomous self‐healing, electrical conductivity, and stimuli responsiveness remains challenging. Here, we report a thermoresponsive, self‐healing dual‐n
content: ABSTRACT The development of multifunctional hydrogels combining mechanical robustness, autonomous self‐healing, electrical conductivity, and stimuli responsiveness remains challenging. Here, we report a thermoresponsive, self‐healing dual‐network hydrogel reinforced with carbon nanotubes (CNTs), integrating reversible dynamic crosslinking, ionic liquid‐mediated phase transitions, and electrical conductivity. The hydrogel combines a borate–poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) network with a gelatin/oxidized dextran framework linked through dynamic imine bonds. A phosphonium‐based ionic liquid introduces tunable lower critical solution temperature (LCST)‐type behavior, while CNTs provide mechanical reinforcement and additional conductive pathways. The resulting hydrogels exhibit rapid gelation (<30 s), autonomous self‐healing, stretchability exceeding 1000% strain, and reversible optical switching near 45°C. Their stable, strain‐dependent electrical responses are consistent with contributions from both ionic transport and CNT‐mediated conduction, without compromising thermoresponsivity or dynamic bond exchange. These combined properties enable reliable human motion monitoring, handwriting recognition, Morse code communication, and thermally gated information concealment. This work demonstrates a versatile strategy for integrating dynamic polymer networks with conductive nanomaterials, offering promising opportunities for mechanically resilient wearable electronics, adaptive human–machine interfaces, and thermally programmable information systems.

title: Deciphering leaf morpho-biochemical and mineral diversity in strawberry tree (Arbutus andrachne L.) genotypes through multivariate statistical approaches
summary: Strawberry tree ( Arbutus andrachne L.) leaves represent a sustainable source of bioactive compounds and mineral nutrients with considerable potential for pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and functional food applications. However, comprehensi
content: Strawberry tree ( Arbutus andrachne L.) leaves represent a sustainable source of bioactive compounds and mineral nutrients with considerable potential for pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and functional food applications. However, comprehensive information integrating leaf morphology, biochemical characteristics, mineral composition, and multivariate statistical analyses remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the leaf morpho-biochemical and mineral diversity of 30 naturally growing strawberry tree genotypes collected from Hatay, Türkiye, and to identify phenotypically promising plant materials for future evaluation in breeding, domestication, and industrial leaf biomass production. The evaluated variables were analyzed using Pearson correlation analysis, principal component analysis (PCA), hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), heat map analysis (HMA), and multiple regression analysis (MRA). Leaf width, leaf length, petiole length, and petiole thickness ranged from 24.92 (‘ST-2’) to 54.28 mm (‘ST-5’), 45.48 (‘ST-28’) to 91.74 mm (‘ST-12’), 8.14 (‘ST-10’) to 23.14 mm (‘ST-29’), and 0.78 (‘ST-28’) to 1.72 mm (‘ST-16’), respectively. Total phenolic content, total flavonoid content, and antioxidant activity ranged from 53.95 (‘ST-13’) to 74.89 mg GAE 100 g⁻¹ FW (‘ST-2’), 13.59 (‘ST-26’) to 35.12 mg CAE 100 g⁻¹ FW (‘ST-7’), and 32.00% (‘ST-17’) to 64.50% (‘ST-13’), respectively. Calcium was the predominant mineral element, ranging from 5327.22 mg kg⁻¹ DW (‘ST-10’) to 27352.35 mg kg⁻¹ DW (‘ST-28’), followed by phosphorus and potassium. Pearson correlation analysis revealed strong positive associations among leaf morphological traits and among most mineral elements, whereas MRA showed that leaf width was primarily explained by leaf length ( R² = 0.95). In contrast, magnesium was identified as a significant predictor of phenolic and flavonoid contents, while both magnesium and potassium were significant predictors of antioxidant activity. PCA extracted six principal components, jointly explaining 79.62% of the total variation, confirming substantial multidimensional diversity among genotypes. Collectively, the results identified ‘ST-5’ and ‘ST-12’ for superior leaf morphology, ‘ST-2’, ‘ST-7’, and ‘ST-13’ for outstanding bioactive properties, and ‘ST-28’ for exceptional calcium accumulation as phenotypically promising plant materials for further evaluation in breeding, conservation, domestication, and sustainable industrial utilization of strawberry tree leaf biomass.

title: Temperature Field Optical Detection and Reconstruction: Methods, Principles and Applications
summary: ABSTRACT The temperature field constitutes a core parameter for thermal‐process analysis and equipment optimization. Traditional contact‐based temperature‐field measurement techniques suffer from flow‐field interference and single‐point‐det
content: ABSTRACT The temperature field constitutes a core parameter for thermal‐process analysis and equipment optimization. Traditional contact‐based temperature‐field measurement techniques suffer from flow‐field interference and single‐point‐detection limitations and cannot satisfy high‐precision measurement requirements within complex high‐temperature environments. This paper systematically reviews the physical principles, detection methods, and reconstruction algorithms of non‐contact optical temperature measurement and temperature field reconstruction. The physical principles include radiation temperature measurement, passive spectral temperature measurement, interference deflection temperature measurement, and optical fiber temperature measurement. The detection methods are divided into passive radiation detection and active laser illumination detection, and their system architectures and application scenarios are analyzed respectively. Optical fiber temperature measurement is classified as contact‐based optical measurement due to the need for physical connection or thermal coupling with the measured object, serving as a supplement to noncontact technologies. The reconstruction algorithms are summarized from classical analytical methods to iterative regularization methods. Finally, issues such as the contradiction of spatial and temporal resolution, multi‐source interference, and the trade‐off between 3D reconstruction accuracy and real‐time performance are discussed, and future development trends are presented, including multimodal fusion, AI‐driven end‐to‐end reconstruction, and system integration.

title: Wireless monolithic flexible zinc-ion battery–pressure sensor enabled by a tough anti-freezing hydrogel electrolyte
summary: Developing wearable sensors that integrate self-powering capability, reliable static and dynamic pressure detection, and miniaturized wireless signal processing remains a formidable challenge. Here, we propose a material–device–system co-de
content: Developing wearable sensors that integrate self-powering capability, reliable static and dynamic pressure detection, and miniaturized wireless signal processing remains a formidable challenge. Here, we propose a material–device–system co-design strategy to construct an untethered, all-weather, monolithic flexible zinc-ion battery–pressure sensor enabled by a tough anti-freezing hydrogel, a co-anode architecture, and a miniaturized wireless module. At the material level, a tough, anti-freezing PAM/CMCS-DMSO-Zn hydrogel serves as the core. It combines a low freezing point, superior toughness, fatigue resistance, and high ionic conductivity, enabling a dual role as an active pressure-sensing layer and a stable battery electrolyte. At the device level, a nylon-mesh-spaced co-anode architecture isolates the hydrogel from the Zn anode at rest, establishing a zero-output state that eliminates standby power. Upon loading, interfacial impedance modulation ensures static and dynamic pressure detection with rapid response and recovery times of 20 and 30 ms, respectively. At the system level, integrating the device with a custom printed circuit board creates an end-to-end microsystem for signal acquisition, processing, and wireless transmission, which we successfully validated across diverse harsh conditions. Ultimately, this co-design bridges hydrogel chemistry under extreme conditions with self-powered wearable electronics, providing a versatile paradigm for all-weather, wireless IoT sensing nodes.

title: Lensless Wide‐Field Microscopy: Toward Next‐Generation Chemical Bioimaging
summary: Lensless imaging offers a new route to substantially alleviate the shackle of space-bandwidth-product (SBP) on conventional optical microscopes, thus high resolution and wide field-of-view (FOV) can be more easily achieved simultaneously. A
content: Lensless imaging offers a new route to substantially alleviate the shackle of space-bandwidth-product (SBP) on conventional optical microscopes, thus high resolution and wide field-of-view (FOV) can be more easily achieved simultaneously. A series of lensless imaging methods have taken their place in chemical bioimaging due to their advantages of wide FOV and low cost. This review discusses the development of sensor-proximal contact, incoherent, holographic, and ptychographic imaging and evaluates their applications across cellular phenotyping, particle and molecular sensing, as well as tissue and in vivo imaging. Particular emphasis is placed on interfacial chemical strategies involving affinity reagents, responsive materials, luminescent reactions, and engineered probes. These approaches convert nanoscale chemical events, which cannot be directly resolved by lensless systems, into amplified and spatially resolved optical signals. By combining chemical signal transduction with large-area imaging, lensless platforms can detect individual cells, particles, and molecular events while simultaneously capturing their temporal dynamics, spatial organization, and collective evolution. This chemistry-centered minireview highlights future opportunities for extracting multiscale spatiotemporal information from complex chemical and biological systems.

title: Comparative Spectroscopic Study of Poly(vinylidenefluoride‐ co ‐hexafluoropropylene)/Graphene Oxide Films and Fiber Mats
summary: ABSTRACT Poly(vinylidenefluoride‐ co ‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‐HFP) and graphene oxide (GO) were utilized to produce four types of samples: PVDF‐HFP films, PVDF‐HFP/GO films, PVDF‐HFP fiber mats and PVDF‐HFP/GO fiber mats. The so‐obtained
content: ABSTRACT Poly(vinylidenefluoride‐ co ‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‐HFP) and graphene oxide (GO) were utilized to produce four types of samples: PVDF‐HFP films, PVDF‐HFP/GO films, PVDF‐HFP fiber mats and PVDF‐HFP/GO fiber mats. The so‐obtained samples were characterized at room temperature by dielectric and Raman spectroscopies and the deduced results were compared with each other. Since the PVDF‐HFP/GO films were found to be electrically conductive, they were not included in the comparative dielectric characterization.
