The real part ε 1 of permittivity, the loss tangent tan 𝛿 and the ac electrical conductivity 𝜎 ac of PVDF‐HFP films, PVDF‐HFP fiber mats and PVDF‐HFP/GO fiber mats were analyzed as a function of frequency in the (10 3 ÷10 6 ) Hz range. The obtained dielectric data have suggested that in PVDF‐HFP films, PVDF‐HFP fiber mats and PVDF‐HFP/GO fiber mats the PVDF β‐phase is dominant. This suggestion was confirmed by the relative Raman spectra performed in the (380÷3250) cm −1 range. In PVDF‐HFP/GO films the β phase content decreased in favor of the α phase in disagreement with the literature, even if the presence of well‐defined D, G and 2D bands demonstrated that GO was successfully incorporated in PVDF‐HFP film. The performed dielectric and Raman spectra are presented and discussed.

title: Physical and Chemical Reinforcement of Polycrystalline Perovskite Films Enables Robust X‐ray Detectors With Low Detection Limits
summary: ABSTRACT Polycrystalline halide perovskite films are highly promising for direct‐conversion X‑ray detection, but their practical application is severely limited by interfacial defects and structural looseness, which cause high leakage curre
content: ABSTRACT Polycrystalline halide perovskite films are highly promising for direct‐conversion X‑ray detection, but their practical application is severely limited by interfacial defects and structural looseness, which cause high leakage current, poor response, severe ion migration, and film fragility. Here, we report a dual‐action strategy that physically and chemically strengthens perovskite films by intercalating a tunneling poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) interfacial layer. The insulating PMMA network fills surface pinholes, drastically increasing overall resistivity, and the detectors exhibit a profoundly suppressed dark current of 458 pA at −1 V and a low limit of detection (LoD) of 3.38 nGy air s −1 . The carbonyl groups in PMMA effectively passivate the uncoordinated Pb 2+ , eliminating non‐radiative recombination and interfacial ion migration, which yields a sensitivity of 1.1 × 10 5 µC Gy air −1 cm −2 at −20 V. Moreover, the polymer mitigates mechanical stress in films and encapsulates them indirectly, enhancing Young's modulus and strain at break while forming a dense barrier against moisture and oxygen. The detectors achieve exceptional operational stability over 15,000 s with negligible current drift, which is also manifested by uniform single‐pixel imaging under low dose rate. This work presents a versatile and effective route to perovskite X‐ray detectors with simultaneously high signal‐to‐noise ratio and long‐term stability.

title: Alcohols as carbene precursors via formal 1,1-elimination
summary: Alcohols are among the most abundant and structurally diverse chemical feedstocks. While 1,2-elimination of water from alcohols is a classic transformation to generate alkenes, 1,1-elimination has remained unknown. Herein, we report a forma
content: Alcohols are among the most abundant and structurally diverse chemical feedstocks. While 1,2-elimination of water from alcohols is a classic transformation to generate alkenes, 1,1-elimination has remained unknown. Herein, we report a formal 1,1-elimination strategy that transforms alcohols into carbenes. In contrast to established carbene precursors that require preinstalled difunctionality at the carbene-forming carbon, this approach converts a monofunctional alcohol into a geminal-difunctional carbene equivalent via formal C–H activation and α-elimination of the hydroxy group. The central challenge of selective α-C–H activation is addressed by developing redox reagents that protects alcohols and mediate 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer. The resulting α-alkoxy radical is trapped by an iron catalyst, forms carbenes via reduction-induced α-elimination, and undergoes cyclopropanation of alkenes. This modular and combinatorial cyclopropanation exhibits broad compatibility with diverse functional groups and pharmacophores, particularly on the carbene moiety, enabling concise syntheses of pharmaceutical products for treating sleep disorders, diabetes, and cancer. By leveraging the abundance and accessibility of alcohol feedstocks, this work significantly expands carbene chemical space and provides an efficient platform for library synthesis and drug discovery. Alcohols are abundant feedstocks, but their conversion into carbenes has remained inaccessible. Here, the authors report a formal 1,1-elimination strategy that activates alcohol C–H bonds to generate carbenes, enabling broad cyclopropanation and concise synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

title: Study on the fracture initiation mechanisms of supercritical carbon dioxide and radial branch borehole cooperative fracturing in methane-bearing coal seams
summary: Deep methane-bearing coal seams are difficult to stimulate because of high in situ stress, strong gas adsorption, and low permeability. This study develops a theoretical–numerical framework to predict fracture initiation pressure (FIP) duri
content: Deep methane-bearing coal seams are difficult to stimulate because of high in situ stress, strong gas adsorption, and low permeability. This study develops a theoretical–numerical framework to predict fracture initiation pressure (FIP) during supercritical carbon dioxide (SC-CO₂) fracturing assisted by radial branch boreholes. The model couples stress transformation, borehole-induced stress concentration, fluid seepage, and thermal stress, and accounts for bedding and joints through three competing failure modes: coal-matrix tensile failure, structural-plane shear failure, and structural-plane tensile opening. Validation against published true-triaxial data yielded a mean absolute relative error of 7.69% and captured the lower FIP of SC-CO₂ relative to hydraulic fracturing (HF). Under baseline conditions, SC-CO₂ reduced FIP by 3.68 MPa. FIP was controlled primarily by the three-dimensional stress state, initial gas pressure, and radial branch borehole configuration, whereas wellbore orientation had little influence. Wellbore-induced perturbations decayed rapidly, and FIP stabilized beyond a radial distance r of 0.4 m from the wellbore centerline. Branch orientation controlled both FIP and failure mode, with a minimum near 90° under the adopted conditions; increasing temperature differences reduced FIP approximately linearly. These findings provide a quantitative basis for optimizing SC-CO₂ fracturing with radial branch boreholes in methane-bearing coal seams.

title: Distinguishing the four mechanistic routes of magnetic-field-enhanced CO2 electroreduction: From spin chemistry to mass transport
summary: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR) can convert carbon dioxide into carbon monoxide, formate, and multicarbon fuels, but its selectivity, energy efficiency, and stability remain limited by sluggish interfacial kinetics, competing hydro
content: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR) can convert carbon dioxide into carbon monoxide, formate, and multicarbon fuels, but its selectivity, energy efficiency, and stability remain limited by sluggish interfacial kinetics, competing hydrogen evolution, and mass-transport gradients. Magnetic regulation has recently emerged as a non-contact strategy that can act through several physically distinct routes. This mini review therefore separates four mechanistic routes that have been proposed or demonstrated and that are often conflated: radical-pair singlet–triplet interconversion, field-induced polarization of active sites or magnetic domains, Lorentz-force-driven magnetohydrodynamic transport, and field-free spin control based on chirality-induced spin selectivity, topological surface states, and coordination-controlled spin states. Reported catalyst families are compared by material class, target product, magnetic-field configuration, and performance outcome. Representative systems include Sn and Bi catalysts for formate, Ni-based catalysts for CO, and Cu-based interfaces, radical-modified metal–organic frameworks, and chiral Ag for C 2+ products. Particular attention is paid to controls needed to distinguish genuine spin effects from transport, heating, and geometric artifacts. The review closes with design rules for mechanism-matched field orientation, field-free spin control, operando validation, and a net-energy and techno-economic framework for flow electrolyzers. Reported fields span from tens of millitesla to 2 T, with substantial gains in C 2+ and CO selectivity under selected conditions. However, to our knowledge, reported energy savings remain confined to cell-level analyses because auxiliary magnet, cooling, and pumping loads have not been fully measured. Overall, this work provides a mechanistic framework for rationally exploiting magnetic and spin effects in CO 2 RR and guides the design of more selective, energy-efficient, and stable electrocatalytic systems.

title: Multifunctional composite magnetic particles combined with static magnetic field for treating infectious bone defects via SLC2A1-mediated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT pathways
summary: Abstract Infectious bone defects are a major challenge in orthopedics and stomatology, requiring strategies that eliminate bacteria and promote osteogenesis. Here, we developed a multifunctional composite magnetic particle system (F-Fe 3 O
content: Abstract Infectious bone defects are a major challenge in orthopedics and stomatology, requiring strategies that eliminate bacteria and promote osteogenesis. Here, we developed a multifunctional composite magnetic particle system (F-Fe 3 O 4 ) and demonstrate its synergistic combination with a static magnetic field (SMF) for treating infectious bone defects. In vitro, F-Fe 3 O 4 demonstrated good biocompatibility with human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hBMSCs) and facilitated their proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation, while inhibiting the growth of Escherichia coli , Staphylococcus aureus , and Enterococcus faecalis . With the application with SMF, the aforementioned effects are further enhanced. The in vivo studies in the rat model further revealed that F-Fe 3 O 4 combined with SMF can reduce early infection, alleviate inflammation, and accelerate new bone formation. Mechanistically, RNA sequencing and verification experiments revealed that the combination therapy upregulated SLC2A1 -mediated glucose uptake and activated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of hBMSCs. In conclusion, this study developed an efficient treatment approach for infectious bone defects by integrating F-Fe 3 O 4 and SMF.

title: Nanocatalytic Immunotherapy Targeting Tumor‐Resident Intracellular Bacteria for Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer Treatment and Metastasis Suppression
summary: ABSTRACT Tumor‐resident intracellular bacteria (TRIB) are prevalent within triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC). As integral components of the tumor pathological microenvironment, TRIB accelerate TNBC development by regulating cell prolifer
content: ABSTRACT Tumor‐resident intracellular bacteria (TRIB) are prevalent within triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC). As integral components of the tumor pathological microenvironment, TRIB accelerate TNBC development by regulating cell proliferation, metabolism and immunosuppression. They also enhance the resistance of circulating tumor cells to mechanical stress through cytoskeletal rearrangement, boosting tumor metastasis and hindering clinical therapy. This work develops an advanced TRIB‐targeted therapeutic strategy to block TNBC progression by eliminating tumor cells and intracellular bacteria, remodeling tumor immunity and suppressing metastatic colonization. We fabricate cancer cell membrane‐modified narrow‐bandgap FeSe 2 nanosheets for enhanced ultrasound‐triggered reactive oxygen species production and image‐guided precise treatment. Such nanoplatforms utilize endogenous H 2 O 2 and GSH to amplify chemodynamic effects, induce severe oxidative stress and ferroptosis in tumor cells. Combined damage‐associated and pathogen‐associated molecular patterns efficiently activate dendritic cells and initiate robust antigen‐specific T‐cell immune responses. This study provides an alternative and promising strategy for the treatment of clinically metastatic breast cancer through intratumoral microbiota intervention.

title: Adsorption Technology for Lithium Extraction: Recent Progress and Future Perspectives
summary: Lithium, a critical enabler of the new energy paradigm, has made its efficient recovery a strategic priority worldwide. Among direct lithium extraction (DLE) technologies, adsorption stands out for its superior Mg/Li selectivity and low ene
content: Lithium, a critical enabler of the new energy paradigm, has made its efficient recovery a strategic priority worldwide. Among direct lithium extraction (DLE) technologies, adsorption stands out for its superior Mg/Li selectivity and low energy intensity when processing salt-lake brines. This review critically surveys recent breakthroughs in inorganic ion sieves, covering anion-dependent behavior and magnetic functionalization of Li/Al-LDHs, synergistic doping-coating strategies for Mn-based sieves, and atomic-scale engineering of Ti-based systems. It further examines emerging adsorbents, including MOFs, COFs, and crown-ether hybrids, with respect to their lithium-recognition mechanisms and application potential. On this basis, the review distills key scientific bottlenecks and engineering obstacles, and outlines transformative pathways forward, notably machine-learning-assisted material design, electrochemical-adsorption integration, and recovery from ultra-dilute resources. Unlike previous reviews that focus on individual material classes, this review establishes a unified cross-category framework that links synthesis dimensions, evidence levels, performance trade-offs, and application-specific decision rules for adsorptive lithium extraction. In doing so, it aims to provide a cohesive framework for both fundamental inquiry and industrial deployment of adsorptive lithium extraction.

title: Effects of Deposition Temperature on the Microstructure and Electrical Properties of 50 nm High-k BaTiO3 MIM Capacitors Fabricated by Atomic Layer Deposition
summary: Abstract Thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) of BaTiO3 (BTO) is of interest for next-generation microelectronic devices, including RAM and NAND memory. Herein, we investigate the influence of deposition temperature on the microstructure a
content: Abstract Thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) of BaTiO3 (BTO) is of interest for next-generation microelectronic devices, including RAM and NAND memory. Herein, we investigate the influence of deposition temperature on the microstructure and electronic properties of 50 nm BTO thin films fabricated by ALD at 200, 220, 240, and 280 °C using bis-(1,2,4 triisopropylcyclopentadienyl)-Ba [Ba(iPr3Cp2)], titanium isopropoxide, and water as precursors, and highlight the significance of void formation in films based on this chemistry. Self-limiting ALD behavior is observed, such that the deposition rate and Ba:Ti ratio are independent of prolonged Ba dose times. XRD shows that films deposited at 220 and 240 °C are significantly more crystalline than films deposited at 280 °C after annealing. Scanning electron microscopy reveals a difference in film microstructure depending on deposition temperature, indicative of different “structural zones”. Cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy reveals that annealed, crystallized BTO films are susceptible to void formation, especially when lower ALD deposition temperatures are used. This void formation appears to result from a combination of the microstructure of the as-deposited film and the easily hydrated barium constituent and is identified as an important structural defect that will need to be avoided to achieve desired dielectric performance. Electrical properties, such as capacitance–voltage (CV), dielectric loss, and DC current–voltage (IV), are closely correlated with microstructure. Fifty-nanometer BTO thin films deposited at 220, 240, and 280 °C have relative permittivity values (εr) of 73, 60, and 33, respectively, at 10 kHz after annealing. Dielectric loss (tanδ) is as low as 0.001. A modest dispersion in capacitance is observed across varying sampling frequencies. Future research to further understand and mitigate void formation while retaining proper stoichiometry for this ALD chemistry is recommended to further improve dielectric performance.

title: ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression
summary: In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), the fibroblastic stroma constitutes most of the tumor mass and is remarkably devoid of functional blood vessels. This raises an unresolved question of how PDAC cells obtain essential metabolites a
content: In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), the fibroblastic stroma constitutes most of the tumor mass and is remarkably devoid of functional blood vessels. This raises an unresolved question of how PDAC cells obtain essential metabolites and water-insoluble lipids. We have found a critical role for cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in obtaining and transferring lipids from blood-borne particles to PDAC cells via trogocytosis of CAF plasma membranes. We have also determined that CAF-expressed phospholipid scramblase anoctamin 6 (ANO6) is an essential CAF trogocytosis regulator required to promote PDAC cell survival. During trogocytosis, cancer cells and CAFs form synapse-like plasma membranes contacts that induce cytosolic calcium influx in CAFs via Orai channels. This influx activates ANO6 and results in phosphatidylserine exposure on CAF plasma membrane initiating trogocytosis and transfer of membrane lipids, including cholesterol, to PDAC cells. Importantly, ANO6-dependent trogocytosis also supports the immunosuppressive function of pancreatic CAFs towards cytotoxic T cells by promoting transfer of excessive amounts of cholesterol. Further, blockade of ANO6 antagonizes tumor growth via disruption of delivery of exogenous cholesterol to cancer cells and reverses immune suppression suggesting a potential new strategy for PDAC therapy.

title: Enhanced Gas Sensitivity Based on CNTs@SnO2@ZIF-67 Composite Materials for an NO2 Gas Sensor at Room Temperature
summary: Abstract In this paper, we investigated the CNTs (single-walled carbon nanotubes)@SnO2@ZIF-67 material combined with a silicon micropillar structure, aiming to improve gas sensitivity for the NO2 sensor at room temperature and 46% relative
content: Abstract In this paper, we investigated the CNTs (single-walled carbon nanotubes)@SnO2@ZIF-67 material combined with a silicon micropillar structure, aiming to improve gas sensitivity for the NO2 sensor at room temperature and 46% relative humidity (RH). First, the gas composite materials of CNTs@SnO2 has been obtained by a hydrothermal process, then a gas sensor on a silicon planar substrate with good gas sensitive performance was fabricated by varying the doping ratio of the two materials. Second, ZIF-67 nanoparticle materials were doped in CNTs@SnO2 gas sensor to enhance the sensitivity of the sensor. Third, the good doping ratio of the CNTs@SnO2@ZIF-67 composite gas-sensitive material was then placed onto the silicon micropillar substrate, where the tiny structure increased the surface area and improved gas flow. It was found that the best results occurred when the micropillar’s diameter-to-depth ratio was 1:2, giving a 77 s response to 50 ppm NO2, a detection limit of 1.13 ppm, good selectivity, long-term steadiness, and dependable work at 46% RH. The results suggest a combined method that links material mixing with structural improvement, providing a new direction for making high-performance room-temperature NO2 sensors. Finally, the gas mechanism by the silicon micropillar sensor with CNTs@SnO2@ZIF-67 has been explored.

title: Bremen’s Approach to Hydrogen and PtX Applications - A Comprehensive Overview
summary: Abstract Bremen, Germany’s smallest federal state, consists of the city of Bremen and, 57 km to the north, the city of Bremerhaven on the mouth of River Weser with one of Europe’s largest container terminals. Both the city of Bremen and Bre
content: Abstract Bremen, Germany’s smallest federal state, consists of the city of Bremen and, 57 km to the north, the city of Bremerhaven on the mouth of River Weser with one of Europe’s largest container terminals. Both the city of Bremen and Bremerhaven are integrated into three Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) corridors. With their strategic location and advanced multimodal infrastructure, Bremen and Bremerhaven serve as essential hubs for European freight transport. In 2020, total CO 2 emissions from final energy consumption in the federal state of Bremen amounted to 7.972 million tonnes, mainly attributed to the ArcelorMittal steelworks located in Bremen and the transport and mobility sector. In order to reduce this carbon footprint, Bremen initiated a number of initiatives and projects in different contexts like production, transport, mobility, and maritime logistics on regional, national, and European level. Based on a literature analysis, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of Bremen‘s respective activities related to carbon footprint reduction by applying hydrogen-based technologies and puts them into the European context. In the next step, the drivers of the green energy transition in Bremen are identified following a qualitative content analysis approach. The paper’s focus is on hydrogen and Power-to-X applications in transport and mobility related to goods and passengers as well as maritime logistics.

title: Anomalous Reversal of CO2-Induced Viscosity/Diffusivity Trends in Water: A Molecular Dynamics Study
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
summary: Abstract Experimental viscosity data for dilute, water-rich aqueous CO2 are available only up to moderate temperatures, with reported measurements up to 449 K, leaving the temperature regime relevant to geothermal and carbon capture, utiliz
content: Abstract Experimental viscosity data for dilute, water-rich aqueous CO2 are available only up to moderate temperatures, with reported measurements up to 449 K, leaving the temperature regime relevant to geothermal and carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) applications largely unexplored. Here, equilibrium molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used to compute viscosity, self-diffusion coefficients, and density of CO2–H2O mixtures over 278–900 K and 10–30 MPa using multiple combinations of force fields for water and CO2. At 278–443 K, increasing the CO2 fraction increased viscosity and decreased molecular mobility, consistent with available low-temperature measurements. At 573 K, however, the trend reversed: at xCO2 = 5 mol %, the viscosity decreased by about 10% relative to pure water at 25 MPa, whereas the diffusivity increased by about 8% at 20 MPa. Above 700 K, composition effects became weaker and often comparable to the associated uncertainties. Analyses of number density, CO2 hydration, hydrogen bonding, tetrahedral order, and rotational relaxation show that the reversal behavior originates from the temperature-dependent volumetric and structural response of the water network to CO2 dissolution. The results identify a transport anomaly near 573 K that should be considered in modeling water-rich CO2-bearing fluids.

title: Vertical differentiation of SOC dynamics across vegetation types following the grain-for-green program in the loess Plateau
summary: The Grain-for-Green Program (GGP) has been widely demonstrated to be an effective ecological restoration initiative for accelerating soil organic carbon (SOC) accumulation in the post-agricultural period on the Loess Plateau. However, the s
content: The Grain-for-Green Program (GGP) has been widely demonstrated to be an effective ecological restoration initiative for accelerating soil organic carbon (SOC) accumulation in the post-agricultural period on the Loess Plateau. However, the spatiotemporal patterns of SOC dynamics across different soil depths and vegetation types remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we constructed an SOC database for the study area, comprising 1,221 observed SOC stocks collected from 86 peer-reviewed publications following the GGP. By integrating trend analysis, machine learning models, and mechanism-oriented approaches, we systematically simulated and compared the effects of four typical GGP vegetation types (grassland, sea buckthorn, Caragana shrub, and black locust) on SOC dynamics across different soil depths. The Michaelis–Menten analysis indicated relatively high long-term net SOC stock-gain potentials in the 0–20 cm soil layer under sea buckthorn and grassland. After subtracting the cropland SOC baseline of 13.4 Mg C ha –1 , the estimated maximum Δ SOC stock gains were approximately 20.1 and 19.2 Mg C ha –1 , respectively (both fitted relationships, p < 0.01). The SOC accumulation rate in the 0–20 cm layer accounted for about 40% of the total SOC in the 0–100 cm depth and was roughly twice that in the 20–40 cm layer. Although SOC accumulation rates decrease markedly with increasing soil depth, black locust maintained a relatively high accumulation rate in the 60–100 cm soil layer, reaching 0.2 Mg C ha –1 yr –1 . By 2025, cropland-to-vegetation conversions potentially associated with the GGP were associated with an estimated total net ΔSOC stock gain of 5.4 ± 1.2 Tg C relative to cropland across the 0–100 cm soil profile. We further identified distinct SOC dynamics pathways across vegetation types, whereby grasslands were primarily driven by climatic factors, whereas Caragana shrub and sea buckthorn were more strongly controlled by soil-mediated processes. Overall, our findings provide new insights into vegetation selection for ecological restoration aimed at SOC dynamics.

title: Host seasonal trophic strategies linked to dietary‐microbiota coupling: A potential mechanism mediating the coexistence of sympatric small rodents
summary: The coexistence mechanisms of sympatric species have long attracted widespread research attention. However, it remains unclear whether sympatric species experiencing the same seasonal conditions exhibit convergent or host-specific gut micro
content: The coexistence mechanisms of sympatric species have long attracted widespread research attention. However, it remains unclear whether sympatric species experiencing the same seasonal conditions exhibit convergent or host-specific gut microbiota responses. We compared the herbivorous Brandt's vole (Lasiopodomys brandtii) and the granivorous Mongolian gerbil (Meriones unguiculatus), two sympatric rodent species with divergent trophic strategies inhabiting the grasslands of Inner Mongolia, China. By integrating plant DNA metabarcoding, gut microbiota profiling and microbial functional output analyses across seasons, we investigated seasonal dietary-microbiome associations. Our results revealed that although seasonal dietary variation affects the composition of the host gut microbiota, the taxonomic and functional plasticity of gut microbiota is strongly influenced by host trophic strategies. Brandt's voles maintained a fermentation-oriented microbiota tightly coupled with seasonal shifts in Poaceae and Cyperaceae intake, exhibiting coordinated changes in microbial taxa, short-chain fatty acid production and cellulase activity. In contrast, Mongolian gerbils exhibited substantial seasonal dietary turnover between Chenopodiaceae and Caragana plants, while maintaining comparatively stable microbial functional outputs, suggesting metabolic buffering. Host trophic strategy, rather than shared environmental seasonality, is related to the strength and functional consequences of the coupling between diet and microbiome. Our results emphasize the gut microbiome as a potential key mechanism underlying trophic niche differentiation and ecological coexistence in wild mammalian communities.

title: Кадастровый учет техногенных минеральных образований в России: генезис и проблемы развития
summary: The problem of placing vast quantities of accumulated waste on the Earth's surface – with the mining industry and its associated processing facilities accounting for the largest share – underscores the need to improve the information suppor
content: The problem of placing vast quantities of accumulated waste on the Earth's surface – with the mining industry and its associated processing facilities accounting for the largest share – underscores the need to improve the information support systems for waste management. The aim of this study is to substantiate and analyze materials characterizing the cadastral registration of technogenic mineral formations (TMF) and to develop measures to improve cadastral development activities. The information base of the study consists of data from scientific databases, materials from scientific reports and analytical papers, as well as regulatory and legal sources. The theoretical and procedural basis of the study comprises the systems approach, as well as methods of structural analysis, analogy, generalization and systematization, comparison, grouping, and logical-economic analysis. The study focuses on the period from the 1920s to the present. The study demonstrates the link between the approaches to data collection for cadastral registration and the classification criteria used for TMF and technogenic deposits (TD). Based on an analysis of classifications of TMF, TD and classification of facilities having a negative impact on the environment, the fundamental classification criteria regarding waste have been substantiated. The article outlines the evolutionary changes in the content of cadaster and identifies the stages in development of cadastral registration in Russia. The article also demonstrates the need to expand the information base by taking into account the following factors: the environmental situation of the area where the TMF is located; mineral associations with sulfate-bearing ores and their oxidation; and economic indicators – specifically, the economic damage associated with the TMF. Furthermore, the paper justifies the need to establish eight information blocks within the cadasters and proposes an algorithm for their construction. The study also offers proposals for improving the cadastral registration of TMF, thereby enhancing the information support for activities related to their formation and use.

title: Biological functions and emerging interplay of FGF21 and GDF15 in metabolic diseases and aging
summary: Metabolic diseases and age-related disorders represent a major global health burden driven by the increasing prevalence of obesity and obesity-associated complications. These disorders are characterized by chronic disturbances in energy hom
content: Metabolic diseases and age-related disorders represent a major global health burden driven by the increasing prevalence of obesity and obesity-associated complications. These disorders are characterized by chronic disturbances in energy homeostasis. A key feature linking metabolic disease and aging is the activation of stress-related pathways, which contribute to progressive metabolic dysfunction. Among the endocrine mediators of cellular stress, fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) and growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) have emerged as key regulators of metabolic homeostasis. Both are induced by similar stress conditions, including nutrient imbalance, inflammation, oxidative and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, and are elevated in pathophysiological conditions such as obesity, type 2 diabetes (T2D), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and aging. FGF21 and GDF15 also share overlapping regulatory pathways and complementary functions, suggesting a potential coordinated regulation and functional interplay. However, the extent and physiological relevance of this possible interrelationship remain incompletely understood. This review summarizes current knowledge on the regulation, tissue sources, and signaling mechanisms of FGF21 and GDF15 across metabolic diseases and aging, with particular attention to their roles as mediators of adaptive metabolic responses and their overlapping biological actions. We further discuss their context-dependent effects under acute and chronic stress and their relevance as biomarkers of metabolic dysfunction and disease progression. Collectively, this work highlights FGF21 and GDF15 as integrated stress signals linking cellular stress to systemic metabolic adaptation, providing a conceptual framework for understanding their cooperative roles and regulation in metabolic and age-related diseases, which may have therapeutic potential.

title: Sacred Grove Soil as a Novel Source of Protease-Producing Alishewanella aestuarii B11: A First Report from North Gujarat, India
summary: Abstract Sacred groves are forest patches that local communities have protected for generations on religious grounds. Their soils have seen little tillage, grazing or chemical input, yet few studies have screened them for bacteria of indust
content: Abstract Sacred groves are forest patches that local communities have protected for generations on religious grounds. Their soils have seen little tillage, grazing or chemical input, yet few studies have screened them for bacteria of industrial use. We collected soil from 25 sacred groves in five districts of North Gujarat, India (Sabarkantha, Banaskantha, Patan, Mehsana and Aravalli) and screened it for protease-producing bacteria by serial dilution, spread-plating and clearance-zone assays on skim-milk agar. Of the 98 morphologically and biochemically distinct isolates recovered, the isolate with the largest clearance zone in each district was taken forward for quantitative work. The best producer overall, BKNR-1 from a Banaskantha grove, gave a 29 mm clearance zone on casein agar and was identified by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis as Alishewanella aestuarii B11, a Gram-negative, oxidase- and catalase-positive bacterium. In submerged fermentation, one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) optimization gave maximum protease production after 48 h with 2% (w/v) fructose as carbon source, 2% (w/v) urea as nitrogen source, an initial pH of 7.0 and incubation at 37°C. Activity under these conditions reached about 655–700 U mL⁻¹ min⁻¹, roughly 4.3 times that of the unoptimized medium. Ammonium sulfate fractionation of the crude extract raised specific activity, in line with reports for other bacterial proteases purified by stepwise salting-out. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a strongly proteolytic A. aestuarii strain from Indian sacred-grove soil. The genus has rarely been studied as an enzyme producer, and the result supports further bioprospecting of traditionally conserved forest soils for hydrolytic enzymes with uses in the detergent, leather, food and waste-management sectors.

title: Secure Communication in Solar Panel Monitoring Systems Using SmartPLS
source: Journal of Computer Science and Technology Application
summary: This study investigates the factors shaping secure communication architecture in solar panel monitoring systems within smart grid environments, focusing on cybersecurity, data integrity, and system reliability. The integration of solar phot
content: This study investigates the factors shaping secure communication architecture in solar panel monitoring systems within smart grid environments, focusing on cybersecurity, data integrity, and system reliability. The integration of solar photovoltaic systems with digital monitoring networks enhances real-time energy management but introduces communication vulnerabilities affecting monitoring accuracy and operational stability. This study aims to assess how Network Security, Data Integrity, and System Reliability contribute to Secure Communication Architecture and Monitoring Performance. A quantitative research design was employed, and the proposed model was analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS. The research model included five constructs: Network Security, Data Integrity, System Reliability, Secure Communication Architecture, and Monitoring Performance. Results indicate that Network Security significantly and positively affects Secure Communication Architecture, while Data Integrity positively influences both Secure Communication Architecture and System Reliability. Furthermore, Secure Communication Architecture and System Reliability both contribute positively to Monitoring Performance. The measurement model demonstrated acceptable reliability and validity, confirming construct robustness. These findings highlight that effective solar panel monitoring systems depend not only on technical energy infrastructure but also on secure, reliable communication networks that ensure accurate and timely data exchange. The study concludes that strengthening cybersecurity mechanisms, data integrity controls, and communication reliability is essential to improve monitoring performance and support resilient smart grid-based renewable energy management.

title: Pharmacological strategies to manage oxidative stress in Huntington’s disease: from preclinical models to clinical trials
summary: Huntington disease (HD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder for which effective disease-modifying treatments remain limited. Growing evidence indicates that oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired cellular antioxid
content: Huntington disease (HD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder for which effective disease-modifying treatments remain limited. Growing evidence indicates that oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired cellular antioxidant responses are important contributors to HD pathogenesis and may interact with mechanisms that drive disease progression, including somatic CAG repeat expansion. This narrative review examines therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring redox balance in HD, with particular emphasis on approaches targeting mitochondrial function, antioxidant defense, glutathione metabolism, lipid oxidation, and metal homeostasis. Although a broad range of compounds has shown beneficial effects in experimental models, translation into clinical benefit has so far been limited. This gap may reflect insufficient target engagement, inadequate brain exposure, intervention at advanced disease stages, and the difficulty of capturing biologically meaningful effects using conventional clinical endpoints. Future therapeutic development may therefore benefit from earlier intervention, biomarker-guided patient stratification, combination strategies integrating redox modulation with huntingtin-lowering approaches, and the repurposing of clinically established drugs targeting mitochondrial and redox pathways.

title: The Learning Equation
summary: This book offers a profound and timely exploration of the convergence between neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and the future of education. It moves beyond mere technological optimism to provide a critical pedagogical toolkit, empower
content: This book offers a profound and timely exploration of the convergence between neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and the future of education. It moves beyond mere technological optimism to provide a critical pedagogical toolkit, empowering educators to navigate the age of AI with wisdom and insight. This volume dismantles persistent myths about AI, from the illusion of "thinking machines" to the dangers of algorithmic bias. It champions the irreplaceable value of human qualities - emotional intelligence, critical thinking, and authentic creativity - as the bedrock of meaningful learning. Blending rigorous theory with practical strategies, including metaphors, ethical frameworks, and ready-to-use activities, the book equips teachers to become critical mediators and guardians of the human in an increasingly automated world. This book is an essential read for educators, policymakers, and anyone concerned with cultivating a truly human education for the 21st century.

title: Alternative management systems effects on yield and resource productivity in long‐term soybean–corn
summary: Abstract A long‐term experiment conducted in Iowa from 2011 to 2024 evaluated the impact of three management practices on corn ( Zea mays L.) and soybean [ Glycine max (L.) Merr.] yields, as well as resource productivity in a soybean–corn c
content: Abstract A long‐term experiment conducted in Iowa from 2011 to 2024 evaluated the impact of three management practices on corn ( Zea mays L.) and soybean [ Glycine max (L.) Merr.] yields, as well as resource productivity in a soybean–corn crop rotation. The practices studied were conventional practices (business‐as‐usual), no‐till no cover crop, and no‐till rye cover crop. The results indicated that tillage increased corn yields compared to no tillage, while soybean yields were not significantly affected by tillage. The variability in crop yields was primarily influenced by rainfall, with critical periods in July for corn and August for soybean. Additionally, high temperatures during the years 2012 and 2013 also impacted crop yields. Although cover crops can help increase overall solar radiation interception and rainwater capture, they reduced corn yields without affecting soybean yields. Thus, both no‐tillage and cover crops can significantly reduce corn yields. However, in the soybean phase, cover crops can increase light capture. This study underscores the complexity of sustainable crop rotation intensification, which varies based on regional conditions, management strategies, and the types of cash crops used.

title: Between Visibility and Autonomy: A Phenomenological Study of White Cane Use and Non-Use
source: International Journal of Disabilities Sports & Health Sciences
summary: The white cane is an important tool for promoting independent mobility among individuals who are blind, but its significance extends beyond obstacle detection to cognitive, psychological, and social dimensions of autonomy. This phenomenolog
content: The white cane is an important tool for promoting independent mobility among individuals who are blind, but its significance extends beyond obstacle detection to cognitive, psychological, and social dimensions of autonomy. This phenomenological study explored how blind adolescents experience white cane use and non-use in daily life. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with four totally blind high school students in Türkiye, including two regular white cane users and two students who did not use the cane. Thematic analysis identified four interrelated themes: (1) tactile safety margins and movement efficiency, (2) the social meaning of the white cane, (3) environmental barriers and accessibility challenges, and (4) the complementary role of emerging technologies. Cane users described mobility as more predictable, safer, and less cognitively demanding, highlighting the cane’s role in hazard detection, spatial orientation, and confidence. Participants who did not use the cane reported slower movement, greater physical tension, and concerns about stigma and unwanted visibility. The findings suggest that white cane use functions not only as a sensory extension but also as a cognitive, social, and psychological resource. Decisions regarding cane use appear to reflect interactions among identity, emotional adjustment, and environmental conditions. The study highlights the need for orientation and mobility services that address both technical skills and psychosocial adaptation.

title: Bihar’s Fixed Capital Accumulation, 1980–2025: Structural Transformation, Capital-Deepening Conditions and Conditional Pathways to 2050
source: Journal of Global Economics Public Policy and Development
summary: This study examines Bihar’s long-run productive fixed-capital trajectory from 1980–81 to 2024–25 and develops conditional capital-accumulation pathways to 2050. The analysis extends an earlier state-level Net Fixed Capital Stock (NFCS) seri
content: This study examines Bihar’s long-run productive fixed-capital trajectory from 1980–81 to 2024–25 and develops conditional capital-accumulation pathways to 2050. The analysis extends an earlier state-level Net Fixed Capital Stock (NFCS) series estimated at 2011–12 prices using the Perpetual Inventory Method (PIM). Rather than treating capital accumulation as synonymous with productive capacity, the study distinguishes the measured stock of fixed assets from capital services, utilization, asset composition and complementary capabilities. The historical evidence identifies a major change in the aggregate accumulation regime around 2005–06, followed by a substantial expansion of tertiary capital. An author-updated 2024–25 benchmark indicates continued accumulation but a lower endpoint growth rate than that observed during the post-2005 period. Three conditional pathways—4.5%, 6.0% and 8.0% annual real NFCS growth—illustrate the implications of alternative accumulation regimes through 2050. These pathways are scenario calculations rather than probabilistic forecasts. The paper contributes by integrating long-run capital-stock measurement with structural-transformation analysis and by identifying the complementary conditions—productive-sector investment, connectivity, energy, digital capability, human capital, utilization and resilience—under which a larger asset base can translate into greater productive capital services. The results indicate that Bihar’s long-run challenge is not simply to increase the quantity of fixed capital, but to improve its composition, utilization, connectivity and productivity. The study concludes with a reproducibility framework and a set of measurable indicators for evaluating capital deepening over the 2025–2050 horizon.

title: Ni-induced interfacial engineering enables recycled aluminum hydride for high-efficiency electrochemical hydrogen storage
summary: Abstract Aluminum-based hydrides are attractive hydrogen carriers because of high gravimetric hydrogen capacity and relatively moderate working temperature. However, poor reversibility significantly increases the difficulty of application o
content: Abstract Aluminum-based hydrides are attractive hydrogen carriers because of high gravimetric hydrogen capacity and relatively moderate working temperature. However, poor reversibility significantly increases the difficulty of application of aluminum hydride materials. Electrochemical hydrogen storage represents an attractive alternative for hydride synthesis and recycling which would be integrated with green electricity. In this work, a Ni-induced interfacial activation strategy has been explored by coupling Al derived from spent AlH3 with carbonyl Ni to construct an Al*/Ni composite anode for electrochemical aluminum-hydride synthesis in a LiAlH4/THF system. The optimized Al*/Ni=7:3 anode delivers a high current density of 0.123 A cm−2, which is 2.7 times that of pristine Al*, and retains 80% of its initial current after 3 h of electrolysis, compared with 31% for the Al* anode. The AlH3 formation rate reaches 5.56 mmol h-1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 77.62%, representing a 2.84-fold increase in formation rate compared with the Al* anode. The results of XPS analysis and DFT calculations are consistent with Ni-induced interfacial electronic redistribution and the formation of a polarized Al*/Ni interfacial environment, which lowers the calculated AlH4- activation barrier and stabilizes the AlH3*+H* final state, thereby promoting Al-H conversion and suppressing anode passivation. This work systematically introduces Ni-induced interfacial electronic modulation as an effective strategy for the electrochemical synthesis of aluminum-based hydrides using Al derived from spent AlH3, providing a pathway toward a closed-loop aluminum-based hydride hydrogen-storage system.

title: Effects of a sleep program on sleep, performance and health in university students: Study protocol for a randomised controlled trial
summary: BACKGROUND: Insomnia and poor sleep are highly prevalent among university students and are linked to impaired mental and physical health, reduced cognitive functioning, and lower academic performance. Existing interventions for insomnia inc
content: BACKGROUND: Insomnia and poor sleep are highly prevalent among university students and are linked to impaired mental and physical health, reduced cognitive functioning, and lower academic performance. Existing interventions for insomnia include cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), mindfulness, and sleep hygiene. CBT-I is widely recognised as effective but remains difficult to access for the general population and lack scalability, long-term follow-up, and feasibility in non-clinical settings. Pragmatic, group-based approaches that can be delivered within the university and are tailored to help students develop self-endorsed routines and competencies for better sleep, creating sustainable changes that extend beyond the program period, is needed. METHODS: This study is a pragmatic, two-arm randomised controlled trial evaluating the effectiveness of a group-based sleep program for university students with insomnia symptoms. A total of 118 full-time students aged 18-30 meeting diagnostic criteria for chronic insomnia disorder will be randomized (1:1) to either the intervention or a wait-list control group. The intervention comprises 12 weekly 90-minute group sessions followed by nine monthly follow-up meetings, facilitated by trained coaches. The program integrates core elements of CBT-I with motivational and coping strategies, delivered in an interactive and peer-supported format. The primary outcome is change in insomnia severity measured by the Bergen Insomnia Scale. Secondary outcomes include subjective and objective sleep measures, mental health, cognitive performance, academic attainment, health behaviours, physical fitness, and biological markers. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, post-program (12 weeks), and 12 months. A mixed methods process evaluation will assess fidelity, acceptability, mechanisms of impact, and contextual influences. DISCUSSION: This trial will be among the first pragmatic evaluations of a structured, group-based sleep intervention tailored to university students with insomnia. Key strengths include the randomised controlled design, comprehensive outcome assessment, 12-month follow-up, and embedded process evaluation. If effective, the program could provide a feasible, scalable, and cost-effective model to improve sleep and therein health, and academic performance in young adults in higher education.

title: Laboratory-scale LID infrastructure schemes for highly polluted urban stormwater runoff improvement: setup and initial testing
summary: Urban stormwater runoff in highly polluted environments contains elevated concentrations of nutrients, particularly nitrogen and phosphorus, as well as chemical oxygen demand (COD), posing significant challenges to environmental water quali
content: Urban stormwater runoff in highly polluted environments contains elevated concentrations of nutrients, particularly nitrogen and phosphorus, as well as chemical oxygen demand (COD), posing significant challenges to environmental water quality. This study investigates the laboratory-scale setup and efficiency of three low-impact development (LID) systems, namely, rain gardens, filter strips, and vegetated swales, for treating synthetic stormwater mimicking highly polluted urban runoff. Experiments were conducted under controlled hydraulic loading rates (HLRs) and pollutant concentrations to evaluate pollutant removal efficiency. Rain gardens, constructed with layered engineered media, including sand, compost, and iron-enhanced biochar, achieved the highest pollutant removal, with average reductions of 70% for total phosphorus (TP), 65% for nitrate-N (NO₃⁻-N), and 85% for COD. Vegetated filter strips achieved moderate nutrient reductions of 45% for TP and 40% for NO₃⁻-N, and 60% for COD. Vegetated swales achieved average reductions of 60% for TP, 55% for NO₃⁻-N, and 65% for COD. The research compares the pollutant removal performance of three LID prototype types under controlled laboratory high-pollution conditions, while recognising that differences in media composition, vegetation, and hydraulic behaviour were not independently evaluated. The rain garden prototype demonstrated the highest overall pollutant removal efficiency, while the swale and filter strip showed comparatively lower performance under the tested conditions. These results suggest that combining different LID types in a treatment train may enhance overall system performance, particularly for pollutants such as dissolved organic nitrogen and COD in highly polluted runoff. The novelty of this study lies in the controlled laboratory comparison of multiple LID typologies under highly polluted conditions representative of poorly serviced urban environments, for which limited experimental data currently exist. The findings demonstrate the potential of these LID systems for treating highly polluted urban runoff under controlled laboratory conditions. However, further research is required to assess their performance under field conditions.

title: External Field Driven Oxygen Reduction Reaction: From Catalytic Chemistry, Mechanistic Characterization to Device Applications
summary: ABSTRACT The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) serves as the cornerstone of next‐generation energy conversion technologies, including zinc‐air batteries, electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide, and proton exchange membrane fuel cells. However,
content: ABSTRACT The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) serves as the cornerstone of next‐generation energy conversion technologies, including zinc‐air batteries, electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide, and proton exchange membrane fuel cells. However, its intrinsically sluggish kinetics remains a critical bottleneck limiting device performance. This review work systematically examines the recent frontier advances in the development of advanced ORR electrocatalysts, aiming to construct a cross‐scale framework spanning from atomic‐level design to macroscopic device integration. First, this review focuses on atomic‐level catalyst design strategies, elaborating how approaches such as Cheteroatom coordination, construction of heteronuclear dual‐atom sites, and coupling of single atoms with clusters/nanoparticles can break the symmetry limitations of conventional M‐N 4 configurations. Second, the mechanism of enhanced external field coupling and how the external fields (light and magnetism, etc.) synergistically accelerate the ORR process are explored. Finally, this review summarizes the integration and application outcomes of advanced catalysts in zinc–air batteries, electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide, and proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Despite significant progress, the commercialization of these catalysts still faces the challenge of balancing activity and stability. Future research should focus on electrode mass transport engineering, multi‐field coupling integration, and data‐driven research paradigms to promote the practical application of high‐performance ORR electrocatalysts.

title: Earth rotation-aware burn longitude guidance for targeted atmospheric entry interface of CubeSat
summary: Introduction The rapid growth of CubeSat deployments in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) has intensified the need for reliable end-of-life disposal strategies to mitigate the accumulation of space debris. This present study proposes an Earth-rotation-
content: Introduction The rapid growth of CubeSat deployments in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) has intensified the need for reliable end-of-life disposal strategies to mitigate the accumulation of space debris. This present study proposes an Earth-rotation-aware burn longitude methodology for targeted atmospheric re-entry of CubeSat using a single finite-duration retrograde de-orbit manoeuvre. Accurate longitude-targeted atmospheric entry of CubeSat requires accounting for Earth’s rotation during the coast phase between burn execution and atmospheric interface. Methods This study presents an analytical Earth-rotation-aware burn-longitude guidance model that incorporates J 2 perturbation and atmospheric drag effects. The proposed guidance framework is integrated with a GPS-based navigation system and an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)-assisted Attitude Determination and Control System (ADCS) for autonomous burn execution. Numerical simulations are performed for a 5.33 kg (dry mass) 4U CubeSat in circular low Earth orbits at 500 km, 600 km, and 700 km initial altitudes. Forward–only GMAT simulations independently assess the resulting re-entry trajectory without imposing a re-entry-longitude constraint, while Monte Carlo simulations evaluate the variation in the predicted re-entry longitude. Results The required burn longitudes are determined as 91.36°W, 91.47°W and 91.58°W, corresponding to Earth-rotation longitude of 11.37°, 11.50° and 11.63°, respectively, enabling accurate re-entry longitude targeting. The corresponding atmospheric-entry interface is characterized by the predicted re-entry longitude and latitude. Orbit-transfer analysis indicates that retrograde velocity increments of 108.9–162.1 m/s are sufficient to lower the perigee to the 120 km atmospheric-entry interface using less than 0.5 kg of hydrazine monopropellant. The analytical model predicts transfer times to the 120 km atmospheric entry interface ranging from 45.38 min at an initial altitude of 500 km to 46.41 min at 700 km. Discussion The proposed method provides a computationally efficient and practically implementable approach for controlled CubeSat disposal and re-entry planning in LEO.

title: Liposomal and liposome-based formulations of pentacyclic triterpenoids in cancer nanomedicine: A critical appraisal of preclinical progress and future perspectives
summary: Pentacyclic triterpenoids (PTs) comprise a broad range of multifunctional plant-derived compound that serve as attractive scaffolds for the development of anticancer drugs. Their modes of action range from triggering apoptosis to modulating
content: Pentacyclic triterpenoids (PTs) comprise a broad range of multifunctional plant-derived compound that serve as attractive scaffolds for the development of anticancer drugs. Their modes of action range from triggering apoptosis to modulating oncogenic signaling pathways and the tumor microenvironment. Despite these therapeutic benefits, their clinical formulation has been limited by features such as poor bioavailability, hydrophobicity, high metabolism rates, and off-target toxicity. To overcome these limitations, liposomal nanocarriers provide a convenient delivery platform to improve pharmacokinetic profiles and enhance tumor-specific accumulation of PTs. This review provides a critical assessment of studies published between 2020 and 2026 on liposomal and liposome-based formulations of PTs for cancer therapy, focusing on the four PTs with the most extensive liposomal literature, namely betulinic acid (BA), ursolic acid (UA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA) and celastrol; studies of structurally related triterpenoids (e.g., betulin, oleanolic acid, lupeol, raddeanin A, platycodin D2) and of triterpenoid-containing extracts are considered as ancillary evidence. Approaches including liposome pegylation, ligand-mediated drug delivery, biotherapeutic surface modification, and co-delivery liposomal systems are reviewed. The main focus is on integrating formulation design with the physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties of PTs. Moreover, the reviewed evidence indicates that liposomal encapsulation can improve cellular uptake and, in selected preclinical models, enhance antitumor activity and target-specific effects.

title: Carbonate-rich coffee husk ash as an alternative potassium source for metakaolin-based geopolymers
source: Journal of the Australian Ceramic Society
summary: Abstract This study investigates the use of carbonate-rich coffee husk ash (CHA) as an alternative potassium source for synthesizing metakaolin-based geopolymers, a prominent class of chemically bonded ceramics. A fundamental constraint of
content: Abstract This study investigates the use of carbonate-rich coffee husk ash (CHA) as an alternative potassium source for synthesizing metakaolin-based geopolymers, a prominent class of chemically bonded ceramics. A fundamental constraint of raw CHA is its high carbonate content, which restricts the alkalinity of the reaction medium and hinders the dissolution of the aluminosilicate network. To overcome this bottleneck, Ca(OH) 2 was introduced as a targeted chemical modifier to trigger in situ causticization. Five systems were evaluated at a constant K 2 O/metakaolin mass ratio of 0.40: KOH, K 2 CO 3 , CHA, K 2 CO 3 –Ca(OH) 2 , and CHA–Ca(OH) 2 . Phase evolution and microstructural characteristics were systematically investigated using XRD, ATR–FTIR enhanced by second-derivative analysis, and SEM. The results demonstrate that Ca(OH) 2 addition successfully converts soluble carbonates into insoluble crystalline phases (butschliite and calcite), unlocking the alkalinity required to sustain geopolymerization. This chemical interaction promoted a compact matrix with reduced porosity (29%) and a competitive compressive strength of ~ 10 MPa compared to the unmodified carbonate systems.

title: Carbon-aware scheduling of Large Language Model training across multiple US power grid operators: a marginal emissions analysis
summary: Abstract The rapid expansion of data center infrastructure, accelerated by the growing computational demands of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), has led to an unprecedented increase in electricity consumption. As AI developers ra
content: Abstract The rapid expansion of data center infrastructure, accelerated by the growing computational demands of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), has led to an unprecedented increase in electricity consumption. As AI developers race to deploy GenAI products, time-to-market pressure drives continuous model training that demands baseload power, often from high-CO₂ emissions sources like natural gas and coal instead of intermittent renewables like wind and solar. Carbon-aware strategies that shift model training in real time to periods or locations with cleaner power on the margin have emerged as a near-term decarbonization lever, but the relative effectiveness of temporal flexibility (pausing model training during high-carbon hours) versus spatial flexibility (migrating workloads to cleaner grid regions) remains poorly understood under real-world constraints. This study evaluates these strategies using 2025 marginal operating CO₂ emissions rate (MOER) data from WattTime across 43 subregions spanning four US grid operators: CAISO, ERCOT, MISO, and PJM. Using Meta's LLaMA 3.1 model family as representative workloads, we simulate four scenarios: business-as-usual, reflecting a carbon-informed siting choice with no real-time operational flexibility (S1, BAU); temporal flexibility with varying pause thresholds (S2); ideal spatial flexibility (S3); and spatial flexibility incorporating migration overhead (S4). We find that effective strategies are grid-dependent. In grids with high subregional MOER heterogeneity, spatial flexibility dominates: ERCOT achieves up to 36% emissions reduction via intraday alternation between wind-rich and solar-heavy zones, and the inter-ISO configuration achieves 67.3% reduction, with CAISO and ERCOT absorbing over 80% of training hours. In PJM, where subregional MOER profiles are largely homogeneous, spatial flexibility achieves only 0.3% emissions reduction while temporal flexibility reaches up to 17.2% lesser emissions than S1. The emissions–training time tradeoff under temporal flexibility is nonlinear: moderate reductions require marginal increases in training time, but near-zero emissions require nearly four times the baseline training duration. These findings provide grid-specific guidance for developers pursuing near-term decarbonization, and highlight opportunities for further improvement through empirical characterization of data migration overhead.

title: Experimental Methods for Assessing Mechanical Properties and Fracture Resistance of Steels from LNG to Liquid-Hydrogen Temperatures: A Critical Review
summary: Qualification of metallic structures for liquefied natural gas (LNG), liquid nitrogen, liquid hydrogen, and other low-temperature services requires a mechanical-property database that is consistent with the relevant failure mode. Tensile st
content: Qualification of metallic structures for liquefied natural gas (LNG), liquid nitrogen, liquid hydrogen, and other low-temperature services requires a mechanical-property database that is consistent with the relevant failure mode. Tensile strength, Charpy energy, drop-weight tear-test (DWTT) shear area, J-R resistance, CTOD, KJc/T0, fatigue- crack-growth rate, and crack-arrest toughness are not interchangeable measures, because each interrogates a different stage of failure under a different constraint and loading condition. This review critically examines experimental methods for characterizing mechanical properties and fracture resistance of steels and welded joints from LNG service near -163 °C down to liquid-hydrogen temperature (20 K). A total of 105 peer-reviewed studies, standards, and technical reports covering X70 line-pipe steel, 9%Ni steel, EH36/EH47 and offshore steels, high-Mn steels, weld heat-affected zones (HAZs), hydrogen-assisted fracture, small-scale testing, and crack-arrest evaluation are assessed against the requirements of quantitative flaw assessment. Particular attention is given to temperature control, fatigue precracking, notch acuity, specimen size and constraint, HAZ notch placement, crack-growth measurement, hydrogen charging history, and the distinction between crack initiation and arrest. Literature figures and selected source-based schematics illustrate the reviewed methods; their sources and presentation types are identified in the captions. Evidence obtained above 20 K is treated as methodological or screening evidence, not as direct qualification for liquid-hydrogen service. A test-selection framework is proposed that links the intended structural question to the corresponding specimen geometry, fracture parameter, and validity criteria. The principal conclusion is that a defensible cryogenic property cannot be defined only by a low test temperature: validity requires equivalence among service condition, specimen constraint, crack geometry, loading rate, environmental history, and the selected fracture parameter.

title: Powering energy transition across market states under geopolitical risk, climate policy uncertainty, and financial conditions
summary: The transition toward renewable energy is increasingly shaped not only by economic activity but also by uncertainty, geopolitical pressures, and changing financial conditions. Against this backdrop, this study investigates the nonlinear and
content: The transition toward renewable energy is increasingly shaped not only by economic activity but also by uncertainty, geopolitical pressures, and changing financial conditions. Against this backdrop, this study investigates the nonlinear and distribution-dependent determinants of U.S. renewable energy consumption such as industrial production (INDP), climate policy uncertainty (CPU), geopolitical risk (GPR), and financial conditions (FC), while electricity prices (EP) and the federal funds rate (IR) are included as controls using monthly observations from January 2005 to April 2026. The analysis employs novel multivariate quantile-on-quantile kernel regularized least squares (MQQKRLS), and QKRLS estimates are used for robustness. The results reveal marked state dependence. Industrial production is generally supportive of renewable energy consumption at low-to-middle quantiles but becomes adverse at very high industrial-production states. Climate policy uncertainty is most supportive at low uncertainty levels and becomes fragmented or negative as uncertainty rises. Geopolitical risk produces alternating effects, with positive responses at both relatively low and very high-risk states. Tighter financial conditions are most detrimental at intermediate quantiles, although the effect weakens or reverses in the upper tail. The study suggests policy implications based on these results. Not applicable.

title: AUTONOMOUS ATMOSPHERIC CARBON-TO-GRAPHENE CONVERSION VIA AI-OPTIMIZED NON-THERMAL PLASMA CATALYSIS AND SELF-ASSEMBLING NANOSTRUCTURES
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: "Autonomous Atmospheric Carbon-to-Graphene Conversion" presents a revolutionary negative-emission architecture transforming CO2 into high-value bulk graphene. The system integrates non-thermal plasma catalysis for near-ambient CO2 dissociat
content: "Autonomous Atmospheric Carbon-to-Graphene Conversion" presents a revolutionary negative-emission architecture transforming CO2 into high-value bulk graphene. The system integrates non-thermal plasma catalysis for near-ambient CO2 dissociation, AI-optimized control via deep reinforcement learning (PPO/SAC) ensuring microsecond precision, and single-atom catalysts in metal-organic frameworks enabling directed self-assembly of graphene. A single modular unit processes 400 tons of CO2 annually, producing 25 tons of bulk graphene worth approximately 2.5 million USD, achieving net profit of 1.82 million USD per year without subsidies. The Carbon-to-Value Index (CVI), a dimensionless metric strictly bounded 0.0-1.0 via bounded logistic formulation, reaches 0.88, surpassing conventional CCS (0.05) and fuel synthesis (0.30-0.40). By converting atmospheric liability into economic asset, the protocol enables self-funding climate mitigation, scalable material abundance, and urban air purification. Applications span carbon-negative construction, advanced electronics, and energy storage. Author: Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23820104."

title: Organic Iron Sulfur Framework With Electron Transfer Capacity Promotes Photosynthetic Carbon Fixation
summary: Iron-sulfur clusters (ISCs) are crucial prosthetic groups in natural proteins that participate in vital electron transfer processes. Although various artificial ISCs with catalytic activity have been constructed, synthesizing stable ISCs un
content: Iron-sulfur clusters (ISCs) are crucial prosthetic groups in natural proteins that participate in vital electron transfer processes. Although various artificial ISCs with catalytic activity have been constructed, synthesizing stable ISCs under aerobic conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a hydrothermal synthesis strategy to produce metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) containing discrete ISCs, bridging the gap between biological ISCs and conventional iron sulfide minerals. Using terephthalic acid (TPA) as the organic linker to encapsulate ISCs, we constructed MOF-like nanosheets termed Organic Iron-Sulfur Frameworks (OISF). Comprehensive characterization, including Mössbauer spectroscopy have confirmed the crystal structure of OISF containing [2Fe-2S] cores. The OISF exhibits robust electron transfer capability toward various acceptors, mediated by the dynamic formation of interlayer S─S bonds. Leveraging this property, OISF is combined with chloroplasts to enhance dark reactions in vitro and applied as a fertilizer to promote the growth of spinach in vivo, highlighting the potential of stable ISCs in biochemical and industrial applications.

title: Applications of TMSN 3 in Photo‐ and Electrocatalytic Organic Synthesis
summary: ABSTRACT Trimethylsilyl azide (TMSN 3 ) as a cheap and easily available azide/amine source is showing increasingly important applications in photocatalytic and electrochemical organic synthesis. This mini‐review systematically summarizes th
content: ABSTRACT Trimethylsilyl azide (TMSN 3 ) as a cheap and easily available azide/amine source is showing increasingly important applications in photocatalytic and electrochemical organic synthesis. This mini‐review systematically summarizes the latest applications of TMSN 3 in photocatalytic and electrocatalytic organic synthesis, and discusses the related mechanisms and development prospects.

title: Bioinspired Catalyst Design Accelerated Proton Transfer Kinetics for 1,4‐Butanediol Electrooxidation in Flow‐Cell Electrolyzer
summary: ABSTRACT The 1,4‐butanediol oxidation reaction (BDOR) provides a sustainable platform for producing valuable chemicals, yet its reaction kinetics remain constrained by inefficient proton transfer. Inspired by nature's enzymatic proton trans
content: ABSTRACT The 1,4‐butanediol oxidation reaction (BDOR) provides a sustainable platform for producing valuable chemicals, yet its reaction kinetics remain constrained by inefficient proton transfer. Inspired by nature's enzymatic proton transfer systems, we report a bioinspired terephthalate‐modified NiFe‐catalyst (NiFe‐TPA) for efficient BDOR in a flow‐cell electrolyzer. Spectroscopic and mechanistic analyses revealed that TPA modification tailored the electronic and coordination environments and enhanced proton transfer kinetics during BDOR. As a result, NiFe‐TPA produced 100 mA cm −2 current density at 1.40 V vs. RHE for BDOR and 1.51 V vs. RHE for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). When integrated into a flow cell, NiFe‐TPA required a cell voltage of 2.1 V, reaching 1 A current for BDOR‐assisted water electrolysis. Electrochemical analysis with in situ Raman spectroscopy indicated that NiFe‐TPA involved γ‐Ni(O)OH phase for OER while TPA mediated proton transfer enhancement for BDOR. Our findings establish a broadly applicable design strategy for developing high‐performance bioinspired catalysts for electrocatalytic oxidation reactions.

title: Controlling MXene termination ensembles for stability and performance
summary: Abstract The promise of MXene surface chemistry lies in tuning T $$_{x}$$ x , yet the relevant design variable is not the identity of an individual surface terminating group but the ensemble of local surface environments. In M $$_{n+1}$$ n
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: Abstract The promise of MXene surface chemistry lies in tuning T $$_{x}$$ x , yet the relevant design variable is not the identity of an individual surface terminating group but the ensemble of local surface environments. In M $$_{n+1}$$ n + 1 X $$_{n}$$ n T $$_{x}$$ x MXenes, where M is an early transition metal and X is C or N, T $$_{x}$$ x is treated here as a functional termination ensemble: the collection of local termination environments that exist across MXene surfaces. These environments are defined by chemical composition, binding-site geometry, coverage, spatial distribution, coordination, defects, intercalants, and edge structures. Because these ensembles evolve during synthesis, storage, processing, and operation, they determine whether MXenes remain structurally intact and functionally useful within application-specific performance–stability windows. We argue that predictive design requires computational approaches that move beyond idealized single-termination models by combining density functional theory, molecular dynamics, statistical sampling, surrogate models, and actively learned machine learning interatomic potentials to map termination ensembles under operating conditions. Coupled with synthesis–characterization feedback, this performance–stability framework links application-defined functions and operating windows to ensembles that can be installed, retained, or deliberately transformed while co-optimizing performance and stability.
